One day, because Mañjuśrī suddenly gave rise to views of the Buddha and views of the Dharma, he was brought by the World-Honored One’s majestic spiritual power toward the two Iron Ring Mountains.
Wuyun Feng asked: "Where are these two Iron Ring Mountains? Do you understand? Even now, there are people..."
To give rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma—Wuyun offered two bowls of boiled tea. Now tell me, was this a reward for him or a punishment?
Baizhang Yuan said: "At that time, the World-Honored One lacked the marks of a great man.
Now, if someone here at Chengtian gives rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma, I would never dare let them disturb it. Why is this so?"
"Once the snow has completely melted, spring will naturally arrive.
Wuzu Yan said, "Wuzu possesses great compassion," and then he clapped his hands and said, "Mañjuśrī, how do you do?
Will you dare to do this again hereafter? After a long silence, he said to himself, "Once bitten by a snake, one fears the grass."
Seeing the well-rope cut, Master Lin said, "The ancient's application was biased and incomplete; it had a beginning but no end. Here in my lineage, the family tradition is different:
even if one does not give rise to views of Buddha or Dharma, one must still be banished to the two Iron Ring Mountains. Why?
Therefore, when there is reward, they are rewarded together; when there is punishment, they are punished together.

Baohua Ren said: "Although the three great elders—the Five Patriarchs, including Juefan Xingxiu, Baiyun Shouduan, and Wuzu Fayan—claimed to uphold and establish the fundamental principles of the school,"
For now, you have not yet penetrated the final word. Cao Shan, however, was not like this.

If anyone here were to give rise to a view of Buddha or a view of Dharma, he would allot half a monastery to each of them. Why? Because a single palm does not ring out; it is only when both palms strike together that there is a resounding *glop-glop*.
Kaixian Jin said: "It is not that Mañjuśrī did not suffer this banishment; yet, at such a time as this, tell me, was Qiyun able to escape the two Iron Ring Mountains?
Heh! A cold wind blows over the great earth on the first day of the sixth month, and frost settles upon the tiled roofs of every house."
Bodhitrengyun said: "The World-Honored One wields sovereign authority beyond the threshold and fully maintains the true command.

Were it not for Mañjuśrī, it would be most difficult to accept. Should anyone nowadays give rise to views of Buddha or views of Dharma, this mountain monk is willing to relinquish his four elements to serve as a meditation seat as an offering."
Because Devadatta slandered the Buddha, the World-Honored One’s physical body sank into the earth as a result.
He then sent Ānanda to inquire whether he was at peace within the hells. Devadatta replied, "I am here as happily as if in the third dhyāna heaven.
The World-Honored One further ordered him to ask, "Do you intend to seek release? Devadatta said, "I shall emerge as soon as the World-Honored One arrives. Ānanda said:

"The Buddha is the guide of the three realms; how could he have any portion [of karma] leading to entry into hell? Devadatta said, "If the Buddha has no portion for entering hell, how could I have any portion for escaping from hell?"
Cuiyan Zhen said: "The words of the Master come from the Master’s own mouth.
Jingshan Daokai said: "Since there is no part that comes out, and no part that goes in, what do you call Śākyamuni?
What do you call Devadatta? And what do you call hell? Do you understand this thoroughly?"
Ma! Carrying his own flask, he went to buy village wine; putting on his robe, he returned to act as host.
Tianning Qi said: "Miaoxi’s critique in this manner is like confusing 'diao' with 'dao' or 'yu' with 'lu'; it is all askew.
Little do they realize that Śākyamuni is Śākyamuni, Devadatta is Devadatta, and hell is hell—each maintains its own distinct character."
There is no way to engage with it. A night of falling flower-rain; the entire city is filled with the fragrance of flowing water.
Fulong Chang said: "To remain undaunted in the face of peril is the mark of a true great man."
Wanfeng Zang said: "Since he is the Teacher of the Three Realms, why does he have no portion of entering hell?
Anan must receive it directly before he can attain it.
Baohua Ren said: "The World-Honored One has bait on the hook; he is accustomed to catching golden-scaled fish. Devadatta holds fast to the seal.
This is a display of self-importance throughout his entire body. It is truly laughable that Ānanda was so lacking in spirit.

Had he possessed the mettle of a true monk at that time, when [the Buddha] said, "How could I possibly have the lot to escape from hell? he should have immediately replied, "I take it you are slandering the World-Honored One."
Even if Devadatta possessed supernatural skills reaching the heavens, they would only result in his total disintegration and dissolution like ice melting away.
Bayan Fu said: "How strange! At first glance, Ānanda seems merely to be acting as a messenger for another;
little did he know that one gourd has brought ruin upon both families."

At the assembly on Vulture Peak, there were five hundred bhikṣus who had attained the four dhyānas and possessed the five supernormal powers, yet they had not yet realized the patience of the Dharma (dharmakṣānti).
By means of their supernormal power of knowledge of past lives, each of them individually beheld their own past transgressions, such as killing their fathers and mothers and other grave offenses.
Within their own minds, each harbored doubts and was unable to enter into or realize the profound Dharma. Thereupon—
Mañjuśrī, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, then grasped a sharp sword in his hand and pressed it against the World-Honored One. The World-Honored One said to Mañjuśrī: "Stop, stop!
You should not commit an act of rebellion. Do not harm me. If I am to be harmed, let it be for the sake of goodness that I am harmed."
"Mañjuśrī, from the very beginning you have been without a self or a person; it is only because of the internal mind that you perceive a self and a person.
When the internal mind arises, the 'self' is inevitably harmed, and this is precisely what is called 'harm.

Thereupon, the five hundred bhikṣus realized for themselves that their original mind is like a dream and like an illusion. Within dreams and illusions, there is no self or person, nor even that which can produce or that which is produced."
Then his biological parents, with one voice and in unison, praised him, saying: "Mañjuśrī, Great Sage of Wisdom, you have profoundly penetrated the very source of the Dharma.
Though you held a sharp sword in your hand and pressed it against the body of the Tathāgata, the sword and the Buddha are likewise the same:
they are of one mark and not two. Being without marks and without arising, how could there be killing therein?"
Tiantong Jie said: "To act for others, one must act with thoroughness; to kill, one must see blood.

Although Mañjuśrī exhausted the strength of his wrists, he still did not know where this sword came from. This has brought misfortune upon Śākyamuni, who, though possessing a mouth all over his body, could not provide a clear explanation.
That five hundred bhikṣus attained enlightenment in such a manner—entering hell is like an arrow shot."
He shoots. Suddenly, as if he had trampled the great ocean and toppled Mount Sumeru, Yunmen’s fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking Indra on the nose.
A carp from the Eastern Sea receives a blow of the staff, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin.
And what about this? After a long silence, he says: "Since I first performed the Three Platforms dance, every beat has been..."
This is always a song.

Wanfeng Zang said: "If I were the World-Honored One, I would wait for Mañjuśrī to arrive and strike him dead with a single blow of my staff, so as to spare the bhikṣu from circling around and striking him in a state of signlessness and non-arising."
Nanshan Baoyun said: "The World-Honored One was so pressed by Mañjuśrī that he was compelled to cast out all his accumulated 'stale wares' with full sincerity.

Had it not been for the five hundred bhikṣus who were skillful at 'loosening the wrist,' even if Mañjuśrī possessed hands all over his body, he could not have gathered them back up. Nevertheless, under the gate of Gautama, this is so."
[He] attained it. Within the gate of the patch-robed monks (śramaṇas), not even a single speck is of any use.
Chongxian Qi said: "The World-Honored One abandoned himself to follow others; his compassion was far too excessive.
Mañjuśrī held the authority in his hand yet had not yet attained freedom; he brought misfortune upon five hundred bhikṣus, whose skulls were shattered to pieces regarding the profoundly deep Dharma."
When have you ever dreamed of this? If one is under the gate of the Patriarchs, one must directly cause blood to splash against the Brahma Heaven. Has it not been said:
"If you would act for others, you must act with thoroughness"?

Once, when a non-Buddhist asked the World-Honored One, "I do not ask about words of existence, nor do I ask about words of non-existence," the World-Honored One remained silent for a long time. The non-Buddhist...

He sighed and said, "The World-Honored One, with great kindness and great compassion, has cleared away the clouds of my delusion and enabled me to enter [the Way]. He then prostrated himself and departed.
Ānanda then addressed the World-Honored One, saying, "What principle did this non-Buddhist perceive that he sighed in praise and departed?
The World-Honored One replied, "It is like a fine horse that, upon seeing the shadow of a whip, immediately gallops forward."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "The Great and Small World-Honored Ones were both led away by Ānanda with a single document.

Fayen Yi, when asked for instruction by a monk, said: "When an outsider questioned the World-Honored One, asking neither about speech nor about silence—before the sound had even ceased, Fayen suddenly held him back, saying: 'Stop! Stop! You intend to go toward the World-Honored One’s long silence.'"
At the assembly at Nanquan, the monks attained awakening through this.
Xuedou Xian said, "Failing to distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox is like being struck by the shadow of a whip.

He further said, "O Zen adepts, once the clouds of delusion have cleared, you will certainly see the Buddha. Do you permit him to be considered a fellow student? If you all understand this together, then..."

"The patriarchs of the world all become companions of externalists. If each were not to provide a seal of certification, then the monks of this eastern land would not equal the externalists of the western heavens.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "The Great and Small World-Honored Ones were smeared right in the face by the externalists. As for those externalists..."
[The monk] said, "I thought I could enter [the Way], yet I have not even dreamed of it. Since I have never dreamed of it, why did I suddenly awaken?
Yangqi Hui said, "Since the World-Honored One abandoned himself to follow others, the non-Buddhists then celebrated the feast."
Tianyi Weishan Zhe said: "The outsider harbors a precious mirror, which the World-Honored One personally held high;
this caused the myriad phenomena to manifest with brilliant clarity. Furthermore, Ānanda struck the golden bell once more, so that the fourfold assembly heard it together."
"Nevertheless, although it is thus, it is much like two dragons playing with a pearl; it only serves to increase the majesty and ferocity of the wise.

Yunju Qi said: 'Where is the point of awakening for the non-Buddhists? Among the assembly, some say that the World-Honored One’s long silence is precisely the place where the whip is raised. Can you understand it in this way?"
Zhaojue Qin said: "The non-Buddhists struck the orthodox because of their own perversity; the World-Honored One looked at the tower and struck the tower;
Ānanda observed from the side and was not skillful, leading the World-Honored One to become mired in the mud and water.

According to my own view, as soon as he says, 'I do not ask about having words, nor do I ask about having no words,' I would strike him with his voice still ringing. As for when Ānanda asked the outsider—"
"What realization is there to be attained in the Way? He then struck him with a harmonious sound. "Why? To kill a person, one must have the sword that kills;
to bring a person to life, one must have the blade that brings to life."
Jingshan Hongdao, having finished citing the words of Xuedou, said: "The heterodox and the orthodox are divided; the orthodox arises from the shadow of the whip.
Tianning Weiqi said: "If you wish to know where the heterodox and the orthodox do not divide, who is the outsider and who is the World-Honored One?"
Do you wish to distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox? The World-Honored One is the World-Honored One; the non-Buddhists are the non-Buddhists.
This is Tianning’s way of seeing things; let the various quarters criticize and disparage it as they please.
The *Śòuchāng Jīng* says: "This matter may be called an echo transmitted through an empty valley, heard by those practicing in a vacant hall.
As for the World-Honored One’s long silence and Zhaojue’s bestowal of the staff—were they the same or different? If you can discern this, then even non-Buddhists become Buddhas;
if it is not yet so, then the Buddha is but a non-Buddhist. Do you understand? The soaring dragon and the dancing phoenix are truly marvelous!
Strange! It would not have passed the "azure-eyed" scrutiny of the Hu-seng (barbarian monk).
After Xingshan finished citing the words of Xuedou and Miaoxi, he said: "He has just been critiqued within the shadow of the whip.
Tell me, setting aside the shadow of the whip, how would you speak this one sentence? After a long silence, he said: "Thirty years from now, this..."
These words were widely circulated.

Foyan Cong said, "The World-Honored One remained silent for a long time—filling the ditches and blocking the ravines; thus, the non-Buddhists were able to enter. It is like applying moxa to a scar from a burn;
let each be given a pair of straw sandals, so as to leave the whole world in doubt. Today, if someone were to ask: [text continues]
When asked whether he would speak of existence or non-existence, the mountain monk simply held up one finger. Tell me, is this the same as the World-Honored One, or is it different?
Gounan said: "Xuedou speaking thus may indeed be called clearly distinguishing between the Chinese and the barbarians; nevertheless, the clouds of delusion..."
Even after it was opened, he still did not see the Buddha. Where could these patch-robed monks and heterodox outsiders be squatting or standing?

If you can penetrate this point here, I grant that you are a fellow student. Nanjian asked: "How incredibly clumsy and negligent was that Gautama! Had I been there at that time," he said, "I would have..."
He and Huo overturned the seat. Nevertheless, though it was thus, those who understood him were few, while those who laughed at him were many.
Baoen Xian said: "Fayan said, 'Dwelling, dwelling! Do you intend to understand this at the place where the World-Honored One remained silent for a long time?'"
I wish to ask: do you not realize it in the place of long silence? In what place do you realize it? He replied, "Do you know yet? [The Master continued:
"As for this monk’s place of awakening and the place of awakening of the non-Buddhists (tīrthikas)—are they the same or different? If you say they are the same..."

It is evident that the masters revered by the world are all but companions to external paths. If you say they are distinct, then the patch-robed monks of this land are not as good as the non-Buddhists of the Western Heavens.
If you can distinguish between the black and the white here, I grant that your studies are complete.
Bai Zhang Le said: "To deploy strategy within the tent and decide victory a thousand miles away—this was not lacking in the World-Honored One.
But as for the outsider who attained enlightenment so suddenly, what principle did he ultimately perceive? Do not say it was at the moment when the World-Honored One remained silent for a long time!
I know full well that you have misunderstood it here."
Qixia Chengyun said: "The outsider sets up a question, yet it does not transcend the perspective of an outsider.
The World-Honored One remains seated; this may be called the magnanimity of a great man who has not lost the heart of an infant.
Ānanda still chatters on—truly, one cannot help but let out a cold laugh. Nevertheless, were it not for the wild geese arriving last night, how could one see the sea?"
The Gate of Autumn.

Master Furi Zhe said: "Although the two venerable masters Xuedou and Miaoxi swallowed up the Buddhas and patriarchs in their spirit and shook the world with their fame through ancient and modern times, even so, when one examines them closely, they would not escape thirty blows—not even a single blow would be spared. Why is this? Not...
They mistakenly distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox based on the mere shadow of the whip.
Chongxian Qi said: "The World-Honored One not only deceived others, but deceived himself as well; he was cornered by Ānanda with a single pressure."

Setting aside for a moment those who have reached the point of standing before donkeys and behind horses, even as for the non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*) who claim to have attained awakening—have they truly realized it?
Fayun said: "The clever Pāpīyas turns back at a single push; the learned Ānanda fails three times."
[The Master] turned back. Even if one were to catch a glimpse of the whip’s shadow, it would still be like marking the boat to seek a lost sword.
Because King Prasenajit asked the World-Honored One: "In ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya), is there conventional truth (saṃvṛti-satya)?
If you say there is not, then wisdom should not be dual; if you say there is, then wisdom should not be singular. What is the meaning of this duality and unity? The World-Honored One...
The Honored One said: "Great King, in the past, during the time of the Buddha Dragon Light, you once asked about this meaning.
Now I have nothing to say, and you have nothing to hear. This state of neither speaking nor hearing is called 'one meaning' and 'two meanings.'"
Cuiyan Zhen said: "King Prasenajit was skilled at questioning but unskilled at answering; the World-Honored One was skilled at answering but unskilled at questioning.
One was deficient in principle; the other was deficient in fact. Had Cuiyan seen this at that time..."
"Lighting a fire to see how thick the skin of this yellow-faced old fellow is," said Jianfu Huai.
"Gentlemen, the Great King asked clearly and the World-Honored One answered clearly; guest and host were distinct.
How can you speak of a principle that is neither spoken nor heard?"
Yuan of Yufan said: "How thick is the skin of this 'Yellow-Faced Old Man'? He may only deceive worldly folk;
you have thoroughly deceived him right before his eyes. According to my judgment, I shall take the Celestial Crown and the Dragon-Robed Imperial Garment and dress the World-Honored One in them;
I shall take the Gold-Threaded Kāṣāya and clothe King Prasenajit in it. Right then—
At such a time, to call him the World-Honored One is also to call him King Bimbisāra; to call him King Bimbisāra is also to call him the World-Honored One.
Tell me, how can this be resolved? The plum blossoms, together with the moon, deliver spring; their jade-like radiance and pure fragrance enter the chamber.
Baon Xian said: "Although the World-Honored One gave an excellent answer, he brought King Bimbisāra down into the waters of death.
A skillful means (sūpanaya) is not like this: when asked about the meaning of 'one' or 'two,' what is that meaning? [The Master] raised his whisk and said:"
If you call it a whisk, you fall into the trap of contact; if you do not call it a whisk, you turn your back on it. After all, what would you call it?

As soon as he hesitated, [the Master] gave him a shout, causing King Bimbisāra to pass through directly. Not only did this avoid falling into the categories of "one" or "two," but it also brought lifelong joy and liberation.
Lingyan said: "Buddha after Buddha hands it over; Patriarch after Patriarch transmits it. It is like a seal impressing water; it is like space merging with space.
Although its patterns and colors are fully manifest, fundamentally no trace remains.

Unless one possesses the eye that transcends the ordinary, one cannot avoid remaining stuck in the state of neither speaking nor hearing. Or, if someone were to ask about the first or second [case] of Guoqing—

What is the meaning of this? To him [the Master] simply replied: "The waves of the four seas are stilled and the dragon sleeps soundly; the clouds of the nine heavens are clear and the crane flies high.
Once, when a non-Buddhist asked the World-Honored One, "What Dharma did you preach yesterday? the World-Honored One said, "Yesterday I preached the Dharma of Samādhi. [The non-Buddhist] asked...
"What Dharma do you teach today? The World-Honored One replied, "Today I teach the indeterminate Dharma. [The interlocutor] asked, "Yesterday you taught the determinate Dharma;
why do you teach the indeterminate Dharma today? The World-Honored One said, "Yesterday was determinate; today it is indeterminate."
Wuzu Keqin said: "How could the World-Honored One take the property of another and use it as his own? Yangshan Huizhong said:
"The World-Honored One was much like someone who, while looking at a building, strikes the building itself. Daming Daowei said: "I do not think so. Suppose he were asked:
'Yesterday you spoke of the fixed Dharma; today why do you speak of the unfixed Dharma? He would simply say: 'This is not within your realm.'"
Jianfu Huaiyun said: "The Old Man with the Yellow Face was cornered by a heterodox practitioner; his escape was merely coincidental.
Even so, right and wrong have not yet been distinguished. If anyone can discern this, I grant that they possess the eye at the crown of their head."
The Longhua School says: "The Yellow-Faced Gautama follows the heterodox and pursues evil.
Although the non-Buddhists have echoes within their words, alas, they lack sinews in their eyes. If Longhua were here, he would give them all a thorough beating at once."
A certain heterodox teacher asked the Blessed One, "Are all phenomena eternal? The Blessed One did not answer. He asked again, "Are all phenomena impermanent?
The Blessed One likewise did not answer. The teacher said, "Since the Blessed One possesses all-encompassing wisdom, why do you not answer me?
The Blessed One replied, "The questions you have posed are all mere conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*)."
Gao Feng said, "When those of heterodox learning speak, it is like the silence of a mute; when the World-Honored One speaks, it is like thunder.
To see this clearly here is precisely to increase frivolous proliferation. Why? Listen closely, listen closely!"

The World-Honored One, because the brahmin Kāla had exercised his supernatural power to bring two stalks of *saṃyuktaka* and *pīlu* flowers, held aloft in his left and right hands as an offering, summoned the rishi.
The rishi responded, "Yes. The World-Honored One said, "Put them down."
Zhì then set down the flower in his left hand. The World-Honored One called out again, "Ascetic, put it down.
Zhì then set down the flower in his right hand. The World-Honored One called out once more, "Ascetic, put it down.
Zhì said, "World-Honored One, now both my hands are empty; what else do you command me to put down? The World-Honored One replied, "I am not commanding you."
Relinquish those flowers. You should relinquish the six external objects, the six internal faculties, and the six intermediate consciousnesses all at once.
There is no place from which to relinquish them; this is your way of escaping birth and death. Resolve to awaken to the patience of non-arising beneath these words.
Jingshan Xiu said: "The Buddha is the Great Master of the Three Realms, yet he still fell within the calculations of conscious mind;
he deserves twenty blows of the staff. Although the Brahmacārin attained awakening, he likewise has not escaped the calculations of conscious mind;
he too deserves twenty blows of the staff. When Beishan makes such a critical judgment, tell me: is there fault or no fault? Xiao He established the laws.
Qixia Chengyun said: "The Great Master of the Three Realms should not have brought out the things of the inner chambers;
he was instead seen through by the Brahmin. If it were Shouchang, when [the monk] said, "Now both my hands are empty—what more do you want me to put down?
he would have struck him with a severe blow and driven him out. Why? Have you not heard it said: "To kill a man, one must use a sharp blade"?
The sword that kills people. To bring people to life, one must use the sword that brings people to life.
While the World-Honored One was seated, he saw two men carrying a pig past him and asked, "What is this? The two men replied:
The Buddha possesses all-encompassing wisdom, yet the piglet did not recognize it. The World-Honored One said, "One must ask about one's transgressions.
Taeyang and Hyunbyeol both remarked, "Had it not been for the World-Honored One asking, we would have ended up forgetting."
The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* says: "The gentleman completes the beauty of others.
Wanfeng Zang said: "When Yi stepped forward, the World-Honored One had already fallen."
Wanshou Fan said: "The World-Honored One did not ask this out of mere knowledge; he was accustomed to creating waves upon level ground.
Even if these two men were truly heroic and outstanding, they should have stepped forward with their hands joined in *añjali* as soon as the question was posed and said:"
"What kind of mental activity do you have, Old Gautama? I dare say the World-Honored One has a mouth like a mute.
Zifu Lu said, "The gentleman is moved by profit.
Huangmei Jue said, "Old Gautama kills without cause; at that time, when asked such a question, he was caught by the two men."
He laughed heartily and said, "The Archer-Pig has gone away! But how about this?
Chongxian Qi cited the words of Taizhao Shouchang and concluded: "These two old fellows have both come to judge others by their own standards.
They fail to realize that the Yellow-Faced Old Man [the Buddha] always gives before he takes."
Baiyan Fu said: "The elders of this world, so venerable and dignified, are searching for fish and shrimp upon level ground.
Were it not for these two 'Meng-ba-langs,' look at how you would have dealt with such behavior."
When the World-Honored One was at the assembly on Vulture Peak, he held up a flower to show the multitude. At that time, among the hundreds of thousands of people and devas, all remained silent;

only the Venerable Kāśyapa broke into a smile. The World-Honored One said, "I possess the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa, the subtle and wonderful Dharma-gate of the true mark which is formless.
It does not rely on words and letters; it is a separate transmission outside the teachings. [He then] entrusted it to...
He instructed Mahākāśyapa.
Baizhang Yuan said: "Kāśyapa was skilled at observing the winds and clouds and discerning their complexions.
Even so, did he still feel his crown heavy?"
Huanglong Xin said: "To pass straight through the skull is already to have exchanged one's eyes.
When facing the brink of peril, there is no need to alarm others; where else could one see the Old Man Śākyamuni?"
Yunfeng Yue was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the gesture of holding up the flower at Vulture Peak?
Yunfeng said, "Once a word has been spoken, even four horses cannot overtake it. "Then what is the meaning of Kāśyapa’s smile? Yunfeng said, "The mouth is the gateway to calamity."
Shitoku Kō said: "A scorched brick strikes one who is frozen through to the marrow; a red-eyed man bumps into a firebrand. Kōfū Myō said:
"The World-Honored One supports the head; Kāśyapa supports the tail. Even until now, it has not been lifted up. Is there no one to lend a hand?
He then made a gesture with both hands as if supporting something and said: "It remains just as it is."

[The Master] listened. Jingshan Xiu said: "When the World-Honored One held up the flower, it was because 'when one is poor, one's ambitions are short-sighted. When Kāśyapa smiled, it was because 'when a horse is thin, its hair is long.
To say, 'I have the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, which I entrust to Mahākāśyapa,' is also an empty fist."
Deceiving the young child.
Wushi Dao said: "At that time, it was fortunate that there was only Kāśyapa alone.

Even if hundreds of thousands of people and devas had all broken into smiles, tell me, to whom would the World-Honored One have entrusted the treasury of the true Dharma-eye and the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa?"
"Who is it? Holding up the whisk, he said, "Is there anyone here who can break into a smile?
Striking the desk, he said, "Familiar faces fill the world, but how many can truly know the heart?"
Shilin then said: "Today, this unworthy descendant wishes to question the Old Man with the Yellow Face:
'From where did you obtain these two things? As soon as he attempts to open his mouth, I shall give him a shout."
Xuedou Yun raised his hand in the gesture of holding up a flower and said, "Is there anyone among you who can laugh at this?

If there is, one may truly say that whether ancient or modern, such a person is worthy of being called a hero. If there is not, then these teeth are but a set of bones, and the lips are but two pieces of skin;
their opening and closing are entirely under one's own control—why do you not realize this for yourself? He let out a shout.

Tiantong Muan said: "Setting aside for a moment the fact that the patriarchs and ancestors of old have not been fully understood, leading to a calamity that has reached their descendants even until now—tell me, was there an entrustment at Vulture Peak or not?
If you say there was an entrustment, you bury the golden-colored dhūta; if you say there was no entrustment, you betray Śākyamuni Buddha. I ask you all: what do you say?"
He uttered a phrase that transcends the ordinary way of birth. After a long silence, he let out a shout and said: "The thousand sages do not know where they have gone;
the sky-relying long sword strikes one with its chilling cold."
Jin-su Yuan said: "Although Kāśyapa distinguished the melody by shifting the strings, alas, an iron yoke has already been placed upon his neck.
Is there anyone who can avoid this fault? Even if there were such a person, they would still be nothing more than a muddled fellow."
Fengxue said with joy: "The World-Honored One possesses the hand that subdues dragons; Kāśyapa has the mechanism that traps tigers.
Although father may conceal things for his son and son may conceal things for his father, nevertheless, not even a single point can be hidden from the hundreds of thousands of devas and humans."

Yun’an Yue said: “If I were Kāśyapa, when I saw him say, ‘I have the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye’ (and so forth), I would have laughed once more. Look at how this old man with the yellow face manages his reconciliation.”
Chongxian Qiyun said: "One person spreads false rumors to incite the masses; another seizes upon empty echoes.
Both are but skulls seeing ghosts before them. It is a pity that at that assembly, none were true men of character, which has led to this point where the chase for the deer continues unabated."
Wufeng Fu said, "From my perspective, this is not at all as good as a million humans and devas in a cold place, their eyes fixed with unblinking intensity, doing nothing but looking.
But tell me, what are they looking at? Look at these two fellows:
under the bright sun and clear sky, they have opened their eyes only to wet their beds."
Chongqing once said: "The World-Honored One was a pile of bones on level ground; Kāśyapa opened his eyes and stumbled.
This has brought trouble upon the descendants of later generations, who mistake a tortoise for a turtle. "O Great Assembly!
For me to offer such a critique is merely a waste of lips and tongue. Aha-ha! A gust of golden wind blows, sweeping away the leaves before the courtyard."

Chong Hwa-neng said: "When the World-Honored One held up the flower, he was like a doting father who does not realize his child’s ugliness. Mahākāśyapa’s smile was like driving a spike through one's brain and into a vat of glue. Baeryam Pu said: "Old Gautama has grown branches where there were none; Mahākāśyapa followed the heterodox and pursued the evil. Huang... [text fragment]... said: "He has already fallen into the pit of the three poisons. Master Yunmen said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. The former was like a man with a head of gold, the latter like a man with a head of iron. Master Fayan said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of iron. Master Dongshan said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of gold. Master Xuedou said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of iron. Master Yuanwu said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of gold. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of gold. Master Wuzu said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of gold. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of gold. Master Dahui said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of gold. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of gold. Master Juefan said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of gold. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of gold. Master Yuanwu said: "The World-Honored One held up the flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of gold. It is like a man with a head of iron meeting a man with a head of iron. It is like a man with a head of gold meeting a man with a head of gold. As for Baiyun himself, he too deserved twenty-nine blows; I shall leave one blow for all of you.
If there is anyone among you who can discern the sting of this, not only will you not have brought shame upon the former sages, but you will also truly see Baiyun. Otherwise—"
"Not so. When eating porridge or rice in the hall, you must chew thoroughly; do not simply swallow it whole. Zhigui of Haiyun said, "Alas!
Coming from the West across the sea, he sought only to find one or two [true practitioners]. Who cared about taking the wrong for the right?
If Haishangze were here, as soon as he saw him bowing, he would have given him a kick. It was not [a matter of mere expediency]."
This serves solely to reveal the eyes of the patch-robed monks (*śramaṇera*), and also spares future generations from hiding behind the place of prostration.
Baoshou Xin said: "This toothless old barbarian woman chatters away; she is like someone chewing food to feed an infant.
What use is there in her? If it were I, Elder Xin, I would wait for that pack of black lacquer jars to present themselves."
No matter what they say or how they act, I shall strike each of them with a blow to the head.

This will not only cause them to sever their own entanglements once and for all, but ensure that each one becomes thoroughly enlightened and rolling in wisdom. Furthermore, it will spare future generations from falling into the trap of clinging to the mere skin and marrow of the teachings.

The Second Patriarch, Grand Master Huìkě (successor of Bodhidharma), was once asked by Sengcān: "I, your disciple, am afflicted with a chronic wind-ailment; I pray that you, O Upādhyāya, will absolve me of my transgressions.
The Patriarch said, "Bring forth your transgressions so that I may absolve them for you. After a long while, Cān said, "I have searched for my transgressions, but they are utterly unobtainable.
The Patriarch said, "I have finished absolving your transgressions for you. You should now abide in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṃgha. Cān said, "As I now behold the Upādhyāya..."
"Although I already know what the Sangha is, I do not yet understand what is meant by 'Buddha' and 'Dharma. The Patriarch said, "This mind is the Buddha;

this mind is the Dharma. Dharma and Buddha are non-dual; the Jewel of the Sangha is likewise so. Daoquan said, "Today I have finally realized that the nature of sin is neither within, nor without, nor in between.
It is just like this mind: the Buddha-Dharma is non-dual. The Patriarch held him in high esteem.
Langya Huijue said: "It is still lacking; what about the one who says 'it exists'?
Liangshan Huiquan, at the point where the offense cannot be found after searching for it, asked: "Where has the nature of the offense gone?
He further said: "Not only is the nature of the offense not to be found, but even the seeker is not seen to exist."

Yunju Qi said: "The Second Patriarch regarded him with deep esteem. Now tell me, did he approve of his understanding of the Buddha-dharma, or did he approve of his ability to expound principles? Tanyuan Ning said:
"Everyone says that Master Ke obtained the method for settling the mind from the First Patriarch and succeeded in carrying on the Western [tradition]."
The Master said: "Look at how he responds; not even a hair’s breadth of worldly vulgarity has ever been altered.
Furthermore, there was one who merely echoes empty sounds who said, 'If one's mind is such, then the Buddha-dharma is non-dual.
To bury such fellows all together in a single pit—what fault would there be in that?"
The Third Patriarch, Master Sengcan (succeeded by Huik'e), in his *Inscription on Faith in Mind*, said: "The six dusts are not evil; they are identical to perfect enlightenment.
Xuedou Xian said: "This staff is a 'dust. What fault is there? Since there is no fault, one ought to discern the host. Therefore it is said:
'Upon a heap of refuse, the sixteen-foot golden body appears. For now, set this aside. Red...

Upon this lump of flesh, it stands upright like a thousand fathoms. Yet, he lets it pass once more. Even if one were to face him from all eight directions and four quarters, one should strike him right along with his staff.
Gu Nanmen said: "Although Xuedou’s staff is well able to act as a master for the Patriarchs, nevertheless—"
It is in the place where the heel has not yet touched the ground.
The Third Patriarch’s *Inscription on Faith* says: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult;
it only dislikes discrimination. Baoen Xiu said: "When the Third Patriarch spoke the word 'dislikes,' he had already begun with hatred and attachment himself. Yet he then said..."
Do not harbor likes or dislikes; be thoroughly and clearly enlightened. How could this possibly be like raising one's voice in an attempt to stop an echo?
Everyone, step back and turn toward yourselves; try to examine this closely.
Deshan Huibie said: "The Ultimate Way is most difficult; it requires discernment. If there is neither aversion nor attachment, how could one fail to see its clarity?
Fuchuan Yi said: "The Patriarch has opened it wide with eight characters and entrusted it to us with both hands. Although it is direct..."
"Quick! Indeed, it is direct and straightforward. Yet, alas, there are many errors. If you wish to see the Patriarch face-to-face, I shall provide you with another path.
He then said: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes picking and choosing. Simply do not harbor hatred or attachment, and it will be transparently clear.
After a long silence, he said: "Investigate! (Chán).
The Sixth Patriarch, Zen Master Huineng of Caoxi in Nanhua (the successor of the Fifth Patriarch Ren), was staying in the corridors of Faxing Temple in Nanhai.
One evening, as the wind blew the temple banner, two monks engaged in a debate. One said, "It is the banner that moves. The other said, "It is the wind that moves.
As they could not resolve their dispute, the Patriarch said, "It is neither the wind moving nor the banner moving; it is you, O virtuous ones, who move."
His mind was moved.
Xuefeng Yun said, "The great patriarchs have a dragon's head but a snake's tail; they deserve twenty blows.
While Fu the Elder was standing in attendance, he unconsciously gnashed his teeth. Xuefeng said, "When I spoke thus, the old monk also deserves twenty blows."
"Ten blows! Baofu Zhan said, "The heart of a thief is naturally apprehensive; this too is like Xiao He establishing the laws.
Baling Jian said, "The Patriarch said, 'It is not the wind moving, nor the banner moving. Since it is neither wind nor banner, where do you place it?
If there is anyone who can act as the Patriarch's advocate, come forth and meet with Baling."
Xuedou Xian said: "The wind moves, the banner moves. Since they are both wind and banner, where do you place them?
If there is anyone who can act as a host for Baling, come forth and meet with Xuedou.
Huanglong Xin said: "It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. To one with clear eyes, nothing can be concealed for even a single moment.
It is your own mind that moves. Now, slow down! Where did you see the Patriarch?
He then cast down his whisk and said, "Look!"
Letan Qing said: "It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. A person of keen intelligence should, like one letting go over a precipice, immediately take this up.
To look back and ahead only gives rise to further confusion. 'It is you, O worthy one, whose mind moves.
Is there anyone now who can act as the master for the Patriarch? Come forth and meet the old monk. Tiantong Hua said: [The same].
"One blind man leading a crowd of blind men; they pull one another into a fiery pit.
After Jingshan Daoyuan finished citing the words of Xuefeng, he said: "Do you wish to recognize Elder Fu? When the rhinoceros gazes at the moon, patterns grow upon its horn.
Do you wish to recognize Xuefeng? When the elephant is struck by thunder, flowers enter its tusks."
Zhongfeng Ben said: "Tasting a single morsel from the cauldron allows one to fully know all its flavors. 'It is not the wind that moves, nor the banner;
it is the mind of the noble one that moves'—this may indeed be called tasting a single morsel from the cauldron. It causes people to involuntarily feel nausea and vomit."
Tianning Qi said: "O virtuous practitioners of Chan! 'The wind moves, the banner moves, the mind moves'—I have already removed these for you.
Where, then, will you see the Patriarch?"
Jingshan Xiu said, "The great and small patriarchs have wrongly provided annotations for people; they deserve thirty blows of the staff.
Longchi Chuan said, "It is not the wind moving, it is not the banner moving, nor is it the mind moving.
A monk asked, 'Ultimately, what is it that moves? Chuan called to the monk. As the monk approached, Chuan struck him with his palm and said:"
"I allow you to know, but I do not allow you to understand. With another slap of his hand, he said, "Go!
Longchi Wei remarked, "I have forty painful blows of the staff: twenty for striking the two monks who were not right to say 'the wind moves, the banner moves';
ten blows for striking Caoxi, who was not right to say 'the mind moves'; and ten blows reserved for striking someone else."
At that time, a monk stepped forward intending to ask a question. [The Master] gave him a sharp strike across the back and said:
"One accustomed to fishing for whales and sea monsters in the vast depths now sighs over the frog's stride, stumbling in the mud and sand."

Nengren Jian said: "Throughout ancient and modern times, how many people have failed to recognize that these two monks were not merely drifting through circumstances, but were instead settled in a 'black mountain ghost cave' where they made their living?
Today, I shall overturn this nest for all of you: thirty blows if the wind moves; thirty blows if the banner moves."
"The mind has moved—thirty blows! A monk standing nearby said, "What about you, Master? Guàn then looked at his attendant and said, "Recognize this monk," and immediately returned to his quarters.
Jin-su Yuan said: "Do you know where the Patriarch has gone? At the beginning of the letter, he instructs his mother to be diligent in her rest;
at the end of the letter, he instructs his mother not to doze off. The single phrase in between does not form a coherent text; it is boundless longing, tears like falling blossoms."
Oufeng Chengyun said: "Whether it is the wind that moves or the banner that moves—each of these two monks has their own point of view.
'Neither the wind moves nor the banner moves'—the Patriarch’s slip was no small matter. 'It is your mind that moves'—I would gladly give you thirty blows.
Why? At this Cool Spring, rewards and punishments are clear; let the various quarters judge as they will."
Dajue Sheng said: "The great and small patriarchs have foul mouths; whenever pressed, they speak only of mind and nature.
I dare guarantee they have not yet reached the ultimate. Today, Dajue shall clearly reveal it for you: 'It is not the wind moving, nor the banner moving, nor the mind moving.
If you can utter a phrase that transcends the body, you shall be worthy of receiving offerings from devas and humans."
Baiyan Fu said: "The great and small patriarchs of that time simply stated, 'It is not the wind moving, it is not the banner moving,' and that was all.
This sufficiently leaves people with doubt. Yet they then said, 'It is the mind of the benevolent one that moves.
Under the scrutiny of a thousand ages, how could they avoid being criticized? [Turning to his left and right, he said: Is there anyone here who can speak on behalf of the patriarchs?"
"Qi? What is it? Even if one were to say, "It is not the movement of the mind," one still deserves thirty strokes with a broom.
Wufeng Fu said, "The Sixth Patriarch is like a village schoolmaster lecturing on the *Zhongyong* and *Daxue* to a group of young children."
To move toward sincerity and correctness and to cultivate oneself thoroughly is enough to make people nod off without end. Why not say instead: "In spring, stroll upon the fragrant grass;
in summer, admire the green lotuses"? This would truly bring a smile to one's face.
The Sixth Patriarch had a verse that said: Steadfastly, I do not cultivate good; Leisurely, I do not commit evil. In stillness, I sever seeing and hearing;
In vast openness, my mind is free from attachment.

The *Shouchang Jing* says: "Stolidly not cultivating goodness— One smashes through empty space; how many fragments are there? Leisurely not committing evil— One turns around and topples the Palace of the Empty King.
In profound stillness, seeing and hearing are severed; The ten directions and the entire dharma-realm share a single gate of compassion.
Vast and expansive, the mind has no attachments; Startled, the gnat soars up to swallow the Five Peaks. Is this meaning not so?
Are they similar? Alas! The long river flows eastward day and night; the waters of the sea have never increased nor diminished from of old.
When Yongjia arrived at the Sixth Patriarch’s place, he circumambulated the meditation seat three times, struck his monk’s staff once, and stood there upright.
The Patriarch said, "A śramaṇa possesses the three thousand dignified demeanors and eighty thousand subtle practices. Great Virtue, from what direction have you come?"
Dazhu Huiyong gave rise to great conceit. [Later,] Yong said, "The matter of birth and death is great; impermanence is swift. The Patriarch said, "Why do you not realize non-arising?
Why do you not understand that there is no swiftness? Yong said, "Realizing it is non-arising; understanding it is fundamentally without swiftness.

The Patriarch said, "So it is, so it is. Only then did Yong assume the full ceremonial demeanor to pay his respects. After a short while, he took his leave. The Patriarch said, "Is your departure too swift? Yong—

[Daoyi] said, "Fundamentally, it is not moving; how could there be speed? The Patriarch asked, "Who knows that it is not moving? Yong said, "It is you, O Benevolent One, who gives rise to discrimination.
The Patriarch said, "You have deeply grasped the meaning of non-arising. Yong said, "If there is non-arising, how can there be 'meaning'?"
The Patriarch said, "If there is no intention, who is it that makes distinctions? Yong replied, "Distinction itself is not intention. The Patriarch sighed in admiration and said, "Excellent!
Stay for one night.
Xuedou Xian, citing the passage regarding "giving rise to great arrogance," let out a shout and said, "At that time, Yongjia..."

The one who could deliver a shout at the bottom would have avoided the fault of having a dragon’s head but a snake’s tail. Furthermore, standing where he stood upright, I would speak on behalf of the Patriarch, saying:
"Before you reached Caoxi, I would have given you thirty blows!"
Fushan [Yuan] said: "The initial practice has not reached its destination;
the final conclusion is excessive. Ruiyan Yun said: "Yongjia received echoes from empty space; the Patriarch took what was wrong and made it right.
Xuedou is like scraping hair off a tortoise's back; Fushan is like adding horns to a horse's head. Circling the meditation seat three times, his eyes are like copper bells.
I entreated him to stay for one night; his head was like a wooden ladle. The pine wind and river moon are known by few.
A Persian from the South Sea produced the "White Radiance" (Bai Ze).
Because Wōluán had composed a verse, the Sixth Patriarch said: "Wōluán has skillful means; he can sever a hundred thoughts. When facing objects..."
"When the mind does not arise, Bodhi grows day by day. The Patriarch then spoke differently: "Huìnéng has no skillful means; I do not sever the hundred thoughts.
When encountering objects, the mind arises in response; How then can Bodhi grow?"
Tiantong Jue said: "The sunflower turns toward the sun; the willow catkins follow the wind. Gushan Xian said:
"The Sixth Patriarch administered this medicinal dharma to save Wulun; if one clings to it as being real, one is mistaken."
"Even to become a servant to the Wheel of Reclining has not yet been attained," Bao-shou Xin said.
"As soon as 'Qian' (the hexagram of Heaven) is spoken of in three lines, 'Kun' (the hexagram of Earth) immediately appears in six breaks.
Tell me, how can one bring a single hexagram to completion? If you wish to know where the lines and images are clearly revealed, they lie right upon King Wen’s palm."
Observation.
A monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, "Who can attain the essential meaning of the Yellow Plum [Patriarch]? The Patriarch replied, "One who understands the Dharma of the Buddha can attain it.
The monk asked, "Does the Master yourself attain it? The Patriarch said, "I do not attain it. The monk asked, "Why does the Master not attain it? The Patriarch—
[The monk] said, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "If you understand it, there are two heads; if you do not understand it, there are three heads.
How then can you find a way to emerge?"
Jingshan Daowu said: "Do you see the Patriarch? If you do not see him, Jingshan shall point him out for you.

The banana tree—banana tree—has leaves, yet they have vanished. Suddenly, a gale arises, just like the one that blew through the thirty-six courtyards of the East Corridor at the Great Xiangguosi Temple in the Eastern Capital, where it shattered the wall-corner of Master Wang."
"The Kāṣāya. Ultimately, how is it? "Return to the hall and drink tea. Tianning Qi said: "A staff strikes the head of a stone man;
*bò bò*, he discusses the actual matter."
Yunju Zhuang said: "Setting aside for a moment whether one has attained or not, or whether one understands or not, why has the life-essence of the Patriarch fallen into the hands of this monk?"
Qinghua said, "Although this monk is skilled at one blow after another, he lacks courage.

If he were a man who has long experienced the battlefields of the monastic world, as soon as [the master] said, 'I do not understand the Buddha-dharma,' he would have overturned the meditation seat. Would that not have brought glory to his predecessors and inspired those who follow?"
Chongxian Qiyun said: "Now tell me, when the Patriarch answered in such a manner, did he grasp the essential meaning of Huangmei or not?
Do you wish to understand? A white horse with a purple-gold saddle, ridden out for all the world to see;
one asks, 'Whose son is this?'—a scholar who has attained office."
Lingxi Yu said: "Thirty blows for one who understands the Buddha-dharma; thirty blows for one who does not understand the Buddha-dharma.
Ultimately, who can grasp the essential meaning of Huangmei? The beautiful maiden has already returned to the celestial void;
the simpleton still crouches by the fire."
One day the Sixth Patriarch said to his disciples, "I wish to return to Xinzhou; you should quickly prepare our boats.
The disciples asked, "Master, when you depart from here, when will you return? The Patriarch replied, "Leaves fall and return to their root; when I come, I shall have no mouth."
Fayun Xiu said, "Not only was there no mouth when he came, but there were also no nostrils when he went.
Baizhang Yuan said, "The Patriarch may truly be called one who is skilled at borrowing a hand to perform a fist-punch.
There are some fellows who often say, "The words are still in our ears," yet they fail to see that it is said: "Ziqi has gone and does not return; how lamentable this vast expanse! Not so!
"Who knows the heavens and the earth? Who, moreover, is the one who knows sound?
Wuzu Yan said: "The Patriarch speaking thus still lacks enlightenment. [A side remark:
The Patriarch appears in the margin.

The Fourth Patriarch had a collateral successor, Chan Master Faron of Niutou (the Dharma heir of the Fourth Patriarch Xinxing). Once, when the Fourth Patriarch arrived at the mountain and entered the rear hermitage, he saw a tiger and made a gesture of fear.
Faron said, "The Master still has this remaining. The Patriarch asked, "What is this? Faron—
Upon hearing these words, he attained realization.
Xuedou Xian, acting on behalf of Yuanrong, merely made a gesture of fear. He also said, "It would have been better to let it pass.
Dayang Huiqie, when asked by a monk, "What was it like before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? replied, "The hairs on my body stand on end."
Seeing this, what happened next? Sweat broke out on his forehead.
Yunmen Cheng said: "The Fourth Patriarch saw the tiger and immediately made a gesture of fear. A hundred-foot fishing line drops straight down."
"The Master still has this one remaining. "Caught on the first cast! "What is this? [The Master] further pressed him with a phrase about being "pressed by the wind.
Yuanrong attained realization upon these words. Those who enter through the gate do not necessarily possess the family treasure.
If it were a lion cub that turns back to look over its shoulder, even the Fourth Patriarch would have to face danger.

Chan Master Xuān Guó Xuántǐng (46th generation, successor of Wéi of Niútóu) was once asked by a monk: "The Great Master Wǔzǔ Rěn spoke of 'the arising of reality through conditions' (*tathatā-pratītyasamutpāda*);
what is the meaning of this? The Master remained silent. At that time, Xuān Guó was standing in attendance beside him and said:
When the Venerable Zhengxing raised a single thought to ask a question, it was an *pratītyasamutpāda* (dependent origination) within true nature.

Upon hearing the Master’s words, he attained great enlightenment. Jingshan Daokai said: "Before the single thought had even arisen, it cannot be that there was no dependent origination. At that time, a monk asked:
"Before the single thought had arisen, what could one call 'dependent origination'? Miaoxi said: "I simply want this too."
When you speak in this way, Tianning Qi says:
"The Kunlun slave wears iron trousers; he strikes once and walks one step. Lingyan Chu says:
"Father and son climb the mountain, each exerting their own effort. Everyone says that Huangmei has attained it.

"Low, level, and high"—yet they fail to realize that the foothills are far too perilous. This monk looks only toward advancing upon the ten-thousand-fathom cliff, unaware that his body is already in the Imperial Capital.
Regarding Chan: in Miaoxi’s school, one person "is not reached when pointed at," while another "reaches it when pointed at.
I, this mountain monk, shall never reveal the secret; those with eyes, look beneath your own feet.
Wenfeng Yu’s *Separate Record of Miaoxi* states: "The stolen goods are still here.
This refers to Chan Master Xuansu of Helin in Runzhou (a successor of the Fourth Patriarch of Niutou, Weizhong). When a monk knocked on the door, Helin asked, "Who is it?
The monk replied, "It is a monk. Helin said, "Not only a monk; even if a Buddha were to come, he would not be admitted. The monk asked, "Why would a Buddha come?"
“Do not cling. Lin said, “There is no place for you to rest.
Baoshou then remarked, “Heli said this as if he were standing atop a towering mountain peak;
little did he know that this monk had already been pushed into a ten-thousand-fathom abyss long ago. Is there anyone who can examine this?
"Can anyone point this out? If there is one who can come forward and meet it with Xuefeng’s staff...
Chan Master Guishan Daoyin (47th generation, successor of Helin Su) of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou once received a letter sent by Mazu.
In the letter, Mazu had drawn a circle. Upon opening the seal and seeing it, Daoyin placed a dot within the circle.
The reply was sealed and returned. When National Teacher Zhong heard of this, he said, "Master Qin is still being deluded by Master Ma.
Baofu Zhan asked, "In what way was Master Qin deluded by Master Ma? Furthermore, how can one avoid being deluded?"

Xuedou Xian said: "Setting aside for a moment the fact that Jingshan was deluded, suppose he had presented this to the National Teacher—what other stratagem could he have employed to avoid being deluded?
An old master remarked: "At that time, he should have simply sat there and left it at that."
There is also a way to simply draw a line across it; if you act like this, you are merely lacking a sense of shame.
Daring to claim that the teachers of the world all possess the vajra-eye and perform vast supernatural transformations—can they truly avoid this?
Xuedou’s insight is something I wish for everyone to know together: at that very moment when Master Ma drew the line, he was already [caught].
This has caused confusion.
Guishan Zhe said, "Do you all recognize Mazu and Jingshan? A single drop of ink forms dragons in two places.
National Teacher Daqin was still deluded by Master Mazu; this can truly be called "the same wind blowing over a thousand miles. Not so.
Jiandao held a "Night-Bright" talisman in his hand; how many knew it was dawn? Jingshan Hongdao said:
"Master Mazu’s [time] was the bitter cold of mid-winter; Master Qin’s was the gradual heat of early summer.
Although the cold and heat differ, both did not miss their proper seasons. Why then did National Teacher Zhong say that Master Qin still..."
"Deceived by Master Ma. Do you understand this thoroughly? "The lotus leaf moves though there is no wind; there must be fish swimming beneath. Tianning Qi said:
"A drop of ink is placed within the perfect circle; sun and moon lose their light, and heaven and earth fall into darkness.
At first he was not deceived by Master Qin; it was Master Ma who first deceived himself, bringing disgrace upon the venerable Nanyang as well—a scene of utter chaos."
After a long silence, he said: "Throughout my life, I have laid open my liver and gall to others; though we know one another, it is as if we were strangers.

Baoning Miao said: "A drunkard supports those who are sober; who provides the strength for rising and falling? Nevertheless, even when the National Teacher extends his hand, it is still a clumsy affair."
Jingshan Xiu said: "Mazu stirs up waves where there is no wind; Guoyi follows the heterodox and pursues the evil.
Although they are skilled at playing with the vital spirit, they cannot avoid both suffering defeat. This causes National Teacher Zhong and Master Daoqin to still be deluded by Master Ma.
Do you all know where the point lies? The magpie cries atop the tree; its intent is in the hemp."
Yeli. Yunju Zhuang said:
"The arrow-points meet directly; seizing and relinquishing according to the occasion—this belongs only to Mazu Guoyi.
He suddenly picked up his staff, called to the assembly, and said: "As for National Teacher Daoyou’s words, even he was still surpassed by Master Mazu."
"Delusion! Ultimately, what is the point? [Zhaozhou] struck his staff once. Gounan said: "Gounan has thirty blows: one for Master Ma not responding to himself;
two for Master Qin not being deluded; three for Xuedou not judging it as delusion; and there is yet one more blow."
He spoke candidly and revealed the truth to the various people.
Chongxian remarked, "Master Ma’s greetings were perfunctory; Master Qin’s characters were full of twists and turns.
Although their exchange was without error, it only served to make the path appear more circuitous. All say that even National Teacher Zhong was still constrained by Master Qin.
Master Ma is deluded; he does not realize that "after three transcriptions, a character for 'crow' becomes 'horse'.
Bayan Fu said: "Mazu and Jingshan lack the marks of a great man; set them aside.
National Teacher Huizhong is skilled at blaming others but ignorant of blaming himself—he deserves thirty blows of the black staff. After a long silence, he looked to his left and right and said:
"Today is fortunately without anyone.
West Mountain Yin said: "Master Qin is busy and has no time for cursive script; Master Ma’s family is poor and cannot afford white rice.
Although there is this coming and going, it is merely according to the abundance or scarcity of one's household. Now tell me, what did National Teacher Zhong do?
"How is it? [Zhaozhou] said, "The words of the master come from the master’s own mouth.
Once, Guoyi was asked by Zhizang, whom Mazu had sent, "In the twelve hours of the day, what do you take as the object of perception?
Guoyi replied, "Wait until you have returned, and I will give you a message. Zhizang said, "I am returning right now. Guoyi said, "Deliver this message to Mazu."
As for the Way, you must go and ask Caoxi. Yunju Zhuang said:
"Mazu was much like one who buries his troops and engages in a feint; Guoyi may truly be called one who produces a stratagem when encountering change.
Although this monk was skilled at conveying messages, he was nonetheless wearying and without merit. He then suddenly took up his staff and drew a line.
One stroke says: "The third-tier waves are high and the fish transforms into a dragon; yet the deluded person still scoops water from the night pond.
Once, when National Teacher Yitong was seated in the palace of Emperor Daizong of the Tang dynasty, he rose as the Emperor’s carriage approached.
The Emperor asked, "Why does the Master rise? Yitong replied, "How can you, a donor (*dānapati*), perceive me, a poor monk, within the four modes of deportment?"
Regarding this, Jingshan Daokai said: "If one does not look within the four modes of deportment, how then can one see Guoyi?
Baoshou Fang said: "Guoyi and Miaoxi each saw only one side; neither was able to escape the criticism of later generations."

Let us set that aside for now. Xuefeng asks you all today: since you cannot see [it] within walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, yet you cannot see it outside of walking, standing, sitting, or reclining either—after all, where do you see it?
If you can find your footing here and plant your feet securely, I will allow you to walk hand-in-hand with the ancients.
Not so. In the four modes of daily conduct (*catur-īryāpatha*), there is great failure.
When the attendant Huītong was about to take his leave from Chan Master Dàolín of Fènglín Níokō in Hángzhōu (who was the successor of Jìngshān Qīn), Dàolín asked him where he was going.
Huītong said, "I am going to various places to study the Buddha-dharma. Dàolín said, "As for the Buddha-dharma, it is right here."
Tong asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma here in this monastery? Lin picked up a tuft of cloth from his body, blew upon it, and showed it to him. Tong attained realization.
Daguixiu said: "It is a pity that this monk takes the sounds and colors from another's lips to define his entire life;
he does not realize that his own radiance covers heaven and earth."
Shendeng Yin finished presenting the public case. He then took a tuft of cloth from his own body and showed it to the assembly.
Following this, he blew upon it and said, "Do you understand? Hereafter, do not let me down."
Jingshan Daokai said, "Even if Guishan were to pass such a critique, he has not yet seen Bird Nest [Nianfo] in his dreams.
Tianning Qisong said, "If the attendant had been able to shout at the very moment the feather was picked up, there would have been no need for the various quarters to scrutinize it.
For me to speak thus is also to increase affliction through involvement in idle matters."
Tianbao Zhen said: "Niaoke acting this way is like a parent who loves their child so much they fail to see their ugliness.
He deserves thirty blows of the staff. Why? Gold has its own price; why must one sell it mixed with sand?"
The Fifth Patriarch’s collateral successor, Chan Master Junji of Songshan (who inherited from Wusan Paozhuoduo), was asked by a monk, "What is one who practices good?
The Master said, "Carrying a cangue and wearing shackles. The monk asked, "What is one who commits evil? The Master said, "Practicing dhyāna and entering samādhi. The monk asked again:
"Someone of shallow capacity requests the Master to point directly," he said. Yunmen replied, "If you ask me about evil, evil does not follow from good;
if you ask me about good, good does not follow from evil. After a long silence, the monk remained silent. Yunmen asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
Yunmen said, "The evil person has no thought of good; the good person has no thought of evil. Therefore it is said that good and evil are like floating clouds—arising and ceasing together."
There was no place [for doubt]. The monk attained awakening upon these words. Later, when Pokuo Duowen heard this case cited, he said:
"This man has realized that all dharmas are unborn. Jianfu Hui said: "In front, the official will not allow even a needle; behind, private carriages and horses pass through freely. If...
"You have been able to discern it; I grant you the eye of the investigation of dharmas (*dharmapravicaya*).
Zhaojue Qinqin said: "When investigating goodness, from where does goodness come? When investigating evil, from where does evil arise?
If one can clearly see this ground, one will know that all phenomena are unborn. Someone asked Chongning, "What is the Great [Reality]?"
A person who practices the Way cultivates dhyāna and enters samādhi; how about a person who commits great evil, bearing a cangue and wearing shackles?
Tell me, are they the same as or different from [the one at] Songshan?
Jingshan Hongzhi said, "Alas, how can one avoid forming deluded thoughts before the skull?
Wushi Daoyuan said, "At Shixi’s place, it is not like this. If someone asks, 'What is one who is a great practitioner?
I tell them: 'Lying across the body, facing the universe. If someone asks, 'What is one who performs great deeds? [He] says: "Red... (The text here appears to be truncated).
"Mountains of knives upon one's feet. Now tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different? After a long silence, he said:
"If this body can be free from all hindrances, what prevents worldly affairs from being as tangled as hemp?"
The *Shouchang Jing* says: "The evil person has no goodness; the good person has no evil. Suddenly, one knows where to return beyond words;
turning back, one does not fall into cause and effect. The monk attained great enlightenment. What did he awaken to? The lion cub snaps the golden tether.
To speak of this according to reality, neither is free from fault. Ultimately, where does the fault lie? Ten thousand loads of idle clouds gather.
Azure cliffs: let them be stirred by wind and thunder as they please, yet they gather back in.
The Sixth Patriarch, from whom the Chan Master Shenhui of Heze in Luojing (the successor of Dajian Huineng) emerged, received news from his hometown that his parents had passed away. [Shen]ze—
He then entered the hall and struck the wooden gavel, saying, "Both my parents have passed away; I request the assembly to recite the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
As soon as the assembly had gathered, Zé struck the gavel again and said, "I have troubled the assembly."
Baoshou Fang said, "Although Heze (Zhaozhou) was great and small in his letting go, it was perilous; in his gathering back, he was too hasty.
To think that one has yet to repay the ground where one's two parents were raised is not yet sufficient. Xuefeng, however, was not like this.

Today, if there were someone who had forgotten to repay their two parents, he would enter the hall and strike the gavel, saying: "Both parents have passed away; I ask the assembly to beat the Dharma drum."
He beats the drum; with his left hand he strikes the gong and with his right he dances. At the crossroads, he startles the leaping tiger.
Looking at the assembly, he says: "Tsk! Get out of the way, get out of the way! Do not come to block my path to the goal."
