*Anthology of Ancient Cases from the Chan School*, Volume Six.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Dharma Heir of Baiyan at Guhang.
△ Side Lineages of the Patriarchs (2):

National Teacher Huizhong of Nanyang (61st Successor of Dajian Huineng), a Side Lineage of the Sixth Patriarch. Because the Tripitaka Master Mahakarṇa from the Western Heaven arrived at the capital, he claimed for himself—
He had attained the supernormal power of knowing others' minds. Emperor Suzong ordered the Master to test him. When the Tripiṭaka Master saw him, he bowed and stood up to his right.
The Master asked, "Have you attained the supernormal power of knowing others' minds? The Tripiṭaka Master replied, "I dare not say so. The Master said, "Tell me, where am I right now?
The Tripiṭaka Master said, "The Master is the teacher of the entire nation; why are you going to Western Sichuan to watch the boat races?"
After a long silence, the Master asked again, "Tell me, where is the old monk right now? Zang replied, "The Master is the teacher of the entire nation;
how can you be watching monkeys being played with at Tianjin Bridge? After another long silence, the Master asked again.
"You say, 'Where is the old monk right now? Zang was at a loss for an answer. The Master rebuked him, saying, "You wild fox spirit!
Where is your power of knowing others' minds? Zang had no reply.
Xuansha Bei questioned him, saying, "Do you say that you saw the National Teacher on those two previous occasions?
Xuedou said, "A failure! A failure!
Baoci then questioned him, saying, "You saw him on the first two occasions; why did you not see him later? Tell me, what is the benefit?"
"Where is the harm? Zhaozhou Shen subsequently had a monk ask: "The Great-Ear Tripitaka Master failed to see the National Teacher for the third time;
I wonder where the National Teacher was? Zhaozhou said, "He was inside the Tripitaka Master's nostrils. Later, a monk asked Xuansha:
"Sandō was inside National Teacher Sanzang’s nostrils; why then could he not see them? Sandō replied, "It was precisely because they were too close.
Tsui-yen Chi said, "But did Sanzang himself see the National Teacher’s nostrils?"
Baizhang Yuan said: "The National Teacher is inside the nostrils of the Tripitaka Master; how could he be difficult to see?
One simply does not realize that he is inside the eyes of the Tripitaka Master.
Tiantong Ju said: "Setting aside for a moment the fact that the Tripitaka Master did not see the National Teacher, tell me: did the National Teacher even know himself?"

Do you know where it falls? If you say you know for yourself, then the hundred birds will carry flowers and the devas will present offerings without a day’s rest. But tell me: at this very moment, where does it fall?
Gao Feng said, "The entire lifetime of skillful means of both the Great and Small National Teachers was completely exposed by this barbarian monk.
Nevertheless, it is fortunate that they encountered a sagely sovereign who served as their witness."
Baoneng Xiu said: "If it were within the eyes, what would be difficult to see?
Yet you do not realize that the Tripitaka Master was the National Teacher throughout his entire being. Nevertheless, he too spoke only half of it.
To speak it in its entirety, the National Teacher had already met the Tripitaka Master long before the latter departed for the Western Heaven."
Tiantong Wu said: "If one were to ask now, 'Why do they not see within the eyes of the Tripitaka?
I would reply: 'It is not within your realm.
Baoshou Xin said: "To see the National Teacher is easy; to see the Tripitaka is difficult. Why? Because [people] only know..."
The Tripitaka Master did not understand where the National Teacher had gone; he simply failed to realize that he himself had been scrutinized and exposed by the National Teacher.
But tell me, where exactly was the point at which he was scrutinized and exposed?
Seong-san Hap said: "Tell me, where was the National Preceptor during his third visit?
Only one who can apply a single eye here may truly be called a monk of no-affairs."
Fengshan began by saying, "The Great and Small National Masters were once thoroughly deluded by the Tripitaka Master.
Fuchuan Zong said, "Everyone says the Tripitaka Master did not know where the National Master was;
little do they realize that the National Master’s nostrils were actually in the hands of the Tripitaka Master. It was simply that at that time, he still lacked one move. Wait until he says..."
"Where is he right now? [The Master] merely clapped his hands and laughed loudly. He was surely unable to distinguish [the truth] as a National Teacher of a whole nation.
Puzhi Zhen said: "Great or small, the National Teacher was driven by the Tripitaka Master until he had no place left to hide. And so it is.

"Set it aside. As for why he could not see [the staff] on the third occasion, the mountain monk says that not only did the Tripitaka Master fail to grasp it, but I dare guarantee that even National Teacher himself did not know its ultimate location. Thereupon, he laughed heartily.
The National Teacher called to his attendant. The attendant responded. Thus he called three times and the attendant responded three times.
The Master said, "I thought I was failing you; who would have known that you were failing me?"
Zhaozhou Shen said, "It is like a person writing characters in the dark; though the characters themselves do not form a complete text, their traces are already manifest.
Xuedou then gave a shout. Yufan Yu said, "This one shout has both guest and host; it has both illumination and function.
Jingshan Guangzhao said, "This one shout lies within the realm of the National Teacher’s attendant; it lies within the realm of Zhaozhou. [He] followed along...
After the final shout, Yufan Yu said, "In a quarrel, you might as well have your say.
Touzi Tong also said, "Why do you suppress and coerce others? Xuedou said, "A dodger of the root."
Xuansha Shibei said, "It is actually the attendant who understands. Xuedou said, "This stops the prisoner and fosters wisdom.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "What is it that I have wronged you? If you can understand this, it too is groundless.
Xuedou said, "So, he does not understand after all. Yunmen then asked again, "What is it that the attendant has wronged?"
"Even if one were to grind one's bones and crush one's body, one would still not have repaid the National Teacher for his kindness. Xuedou said, "Endless, endless.
Fayan Wenyi, when asked by a monk, "What was the National Teacher’s intention in calling for his attendant? Fayan said, "Go now;
come back at another time. Yunju Xi said, "When Fayan spoke thus, did he clarify the National Teacher’s meaning or not?"
Master Ming expressed his intent. Xuedou said, "He cannot deceive me.
Xinghua Jiang said, "One blind man leads a crowd of blind men. Xuedou said, "Truly blind. When someone asked [this], Xuedou struck him.
He did this so that those from all quarters might examine it.
Baoci then asked the monk, "Where is the meeting place of the attendant? The monk said, "If one does not understand, how could one possibly respond in such a way?
Baoci then said, "You have little understanding. He further said, "If you can see into this, you will recognize Xuansha."
Cuiyan Zhi said: "The National Teacher and his attendant were both lacking in understanding.
How do you understand it now? Xuedou Xian said: "The National Teacher called three times; 'pointing' did not reach him. The attendant responded three times;
'reaching' did not point to him. He further said: "I thought I was failing you, but it was actually you who failed me. You have deceived Xuedou!"
It cannot be pinpointed.
Yunju Xi asked, "Tell me, did the attendant understand? If he understood, National Teacher said, 'You have failed me.
If he did not understand, Xuansha said, 'In fact, it was the attendant who understood. So, how is this to be resolved?"

A discussion. Tiantong Jue said: "Within the way of benevolence and righteousness, and within the relationship between teacher and disciple, if one calls out again and the other responds again, this concerns the real and not the unreal.
Now tell me: is there a failure of duty or not? 'Pure jade has no flaw; carved patterns ruin its virtue.'"
Fushan said, "The National Teacher was like gouging a sore on healthy flesh; Yunmen was like applying moxa to a healed scar.
Xuedou was much like one who follows the heterodox and pursues the evil; he did not realize that the nostrils were entirely in the hands of the attendant.
Baoning Mocheng said, "The two of them were truly blind; each was merely playing with a lump of mud.
Duanyan Yun said, "In the monastic communities, they deliberate upon this: when the National Teacher called out three times, he vomited forth his heart and liver;
when the attendant responded three times, he took full responsibility. This is certainly so, yet it is simply that the National Teacher said, 'I thought I was alone.'"
"If you betray me, who will know it? You have betrayed me. Again, how is this so?
If one says there is no betrayal for either, one obscures Yunmen. If one says there is betrayal for both, one wrongs Xuedou.
If it is neither of these, Fushan further says, "The nostrils are all in the hands of the attendant. Here, Ruiyan reveals a message.
This too must be scrutinized from all perspectives. It is easy to distinguish flour from snow, but difficult to discern soot within ink.
Nantang wished to say: when the National Teacher called his attendant three times and the attendant responded three times, it could be said that "the form is straight and the shadow is upright.
Yet, when he said, "I thought I was failing you, but it is actually you who are failing me," one immediately perceives the distinction.
"Not down. But tell me, where does the error lie?
Xigyan Bao laughed heartily and said, "All you Zen practitioners, do you know the point at which this laughter falls?
If you know it, the National Teacher will be reduced to nothingness like melting ice or crumbling walls. If you do not know it, the attendant remains as solid as a four-sided prism."
"Ground! Do you understand thoroughly yet? Once the first yang has passed, the vernal message arrives; on the night of the last month of winter, the cold plum blossoms through the snow. Yuan-an says:
When I, this old monk, am at leisure, I also call for the attendant, and the attendant responds.
When the attendant holds up a cup and passes a goblet, I receive them with my hands as they come. Thus, neither I nor the attendant bear any debt to one another."
To speak candidly: "After the wind and rain have swept through the peach blossoms along the road, where can a horse's hoof avoid the remaining petals?
Nanjian asked, "The Elder Miaoxi was not met at the front of the village nor overtaken at the back of the inn;
he wished to see the National Teacher’s attendant for sixty kalpas across three lifetimes."
Baoshou newly says: "The National Teacher called three times; it was like a pearl rolling on a tray. The attendant responded three times; it was like a tray rolling a pearl.
Ultimately, where does the failure lie? A Persian blows an iron flute; its melody issues from the azure heights."
Hexu Qian said: "The National Teacher called thus; the attendant responded thus.
This may be called 'the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching,' where the needle and the awl meet in perfect accord. Yet, where did he fail the National Teacher?
The woman has already returned to the void of the heavens, while the fool still crouches by the fire."
Xuefeng said: "Three times he called, and three times there was a response; drinking from the cup in a state of intoxication.
Yunmen and Xuedou were like those who draw snakes and add feet—realizing it directly is also groundless."
The National Teacher was once asked by Emperor Suzong, "What is the samādhi of non-contention? The Master replied, "Donor, you are walking upon the crown of Vairocana.
The Emperor asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Do not mistake it for your own pure *dharmakāya*."
Jingshan Daowu said: "Do you all wish to see the National Teacher? He is right within your own eyes. Even with eyes open, you miss him;
even with eyes closed, you miss him. Since he is right within your eyes, why do you miss him?"
Even though Miaoxi spoke thus, he too missed the mark by no small measure.
When National Teacher Huizhong arrived before Emperor Suzong at the palace, he pointed to a stone lion and said, "Your Majesty, this stone lion is extraordinary;
please provide a turning word for it. The Emperor replied, "I am unable to provide a turning word; I request that you, Master, provide one. The Master—

He said, "This mountain monk has committed a transgression. Later, Danyuan asked, "Does the Emperor understand? The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment whether the Emperor understands, how do you understand it?"
Xuansha Shibei said, "The Great State Preceptor was thoroughly exposed by his attendant.
Baoshou Xin said, "If it were not a true lion, how could it roar so skillfully? Nevertheless, tell me: did the State Preceptor roar skillfully?
Did Emperor Suzong roar skillfully? Or did Danyuan roar skillfully? Please provide a turning word for each.
If one were to say that the disciple could not descend and thus requested the Master to descend, how would you bring this to a conclusion? Alas!
It is difficult to be a ruler and not easy to be a minister.
The National Teacher asked Nanquan, upon his arrival, "Where have you come from? Nanquan replied, "From Jiangxi.
The Master said, "Have you brought the portrait of Master Ma with you? Nanquan said, "This very one here. The Master said, "What about the one behind him? Nanquan then fell silent.
Changqing Ling said, "It is very much like not knowing.
Baofu Zhan spoke differently, saying, "How could you possibly not have arrived here, Master?
Yunju Xi said, "Both of these venerable elders were merely supporting him from behind; as for Nanquan, he simply ceased [speaking]."
"Supporting those in front and supporting those behind.
Tianjie Shengyun said: "Nanquan builds a high tower at the bottom of the well; the National Teacher peers over his shoulder inside a lacquer bucket.
Beyond this, these pairs and trios—supporting those in front and supporting those behind—are precisely like picking up horse dung in Yangzhou. Yet...
He went to Suzhou to sell blended incense.

When National Teacher [Huai-jang] encountered Dan-xia coming to pay his respects, as soon as Dan-xia unfolded his sitting mat, the Master said, "Not necessary, not necessary. Dan-xia then stepped back three paces.
The Master said, "So it is, so it is. Xiang stepped forward three paces. The Master said, "Not so, not so. Xiang circled the meditation seat once and departed.
The Master said, "The time since the Sage has passed; people are mostly indolent. Thirty years from now, it will be difficult even to find a single person like this."
Baofu Zhan said, "Danxia was so intent on reaching his destination that he did not realize he had become exhausted.
Guishan Zhe said, "Danxia may be said to harbor a supreme treasure; when it meets a wise person, its brilliance increases.
The Great Gate of the National Teacher is wide open; those who ascend it must be the right kind of person. Is there anyone present now who can act for Danxia?"
"Is there anyone here? Come forth and meet with Dayue! Is there anyone? If you are not a guest from Longmen, take care not to suffer a black mark on your forehead.
Letan Zhun said: "The traveler's road is as vast as the heavens; the nobleman's gate is as deep as the sea. This was explained by Deng Mitian Shi.
The gatekeeper must be the right person; in receiving a distinguished guest, one should possess the magnanimity of Lord Mengchang.
If it is not so, then the paths of host and guest will diverge like heaven and earth, and they will remain as incompatible as clouds and mud.
Daguang Guo said: "Danxia’s one advance and one retreat won him a victory in the dark;
National Teacher’s overturning the east and beating the west cannot help but draw laughter from onlookers."
Zhaojue Qin said: "When guest and host meet, they wish to unfold [the ceremony] but do not; withdrawing and then advancing, their prostrations become mere flattery.
Fortunately, the Old Man of Nanyang is old but not senile."
Dongshan Guanzhi said: "A bright mirror stands upon its stand: when a Hu comes, a Hu appears; when a Han comes, a Han appears. A great bell hangs upon its frame:
struck with force, it rings loudly; struck softly, it rings faintly. One contraction and one expansion; one capture and one release.

This may be called the perfection of both illumination and function, where practice and teaching reach their full realization. Furthermore, as the National Teacher said: 'The time since the Sage departed is remote; many people [are deluded].'"
"Laxity! After thirty years, it will be difficult to find even a single person. Ultimately, is this praise or blame?
Chongxian Qi said, "The National Teacher is like a drum placed before the hall; it is difficult for anyone to strike it. Danxia’s three notes from Yuyang are of a natural spirit.
Among the assembly, everyone says the guest and host are in harmonious accord, yet they are actually not in harmony at all—though one has attained it."
Changrong had his two feet cut off.
Yunxi Ting said, "The two elders have both yielding and seizing; recognize the fault and recognize the rest. They are not ashamed to meet once again.
Even so, Huang Shigong relied on meeting Zi Lang; had it been Han Gaozu, he would not have escaped suffering [the same fate].
He spoke with arrogance and insulted him.
When Danxia came to visit the National Teacher while he was asleep, he asked the attendant, "Is the National Teacher here? The attendant replied, "He is indeed here;
it is simply that he does not see guests. Danxia said, "How very remote and distant! The attendant said, "Do not speak of the Venerable One [in such a way]."

Even with the Buddha-eye, one cannot see it. Xie said, "The dragon begets a dragon; the phoenix begets a phoenix. When the Master woke from his sleep, the attendant reported the previous conversation to him.

The Master then struck the attendant twenty blows and expelled him from the monastery. Hearing this, Xie sighed and said: [Note: The original text contains a fragmentary quote regarding Xie's reaction. A complete rendering of the full context would require the subsequent portion of the narrative.]
It was no mistake that he became the National Teacher of Nanyang.
Tiantong Huihua said: "The attendant eating the staff and leaving the monastery is an event that occurs but once in a thousand years.
Yet how could Guizong avoid having his eyes burn with envy? Although Danxia was indeed a master of the craft, what could he do when he fell into the National Teacher’s net? All [of you], listen!
Can people still discern this? If not, it is like one who still grips a golden whip and asks a traveler returning home: "In the deep of night, who walks with you along the Imperial Street?
Jingshan Rong said: "The National Teacher was fortunately already sleeping soundly; it was the attendant who spread his family's disgrace. It was not for no reason...
Dana said, "How could one see the National Teacher’s roar? He then asked the assembly, "Since the National Teacher was right here, why did he not see the guest?
If you can see through this point, not only will you know that Danyuan missed the mark, but you will also see for yourself the path by which one emerges from the self.
Nevertheless, do not let your idle scholarly interpretations bury the Patriarchal Way.
"Master Xinxin.
Tianqichao said, "Danxia knew only the one but not the two; the attendant knew only the two but not the one.
Both should have received twenty blows of the staff. It is a pity they were let off. Now tell me, what about the National Teacher?"
"Where are the Master’s eyes? [The Master] replied, "Wait until you have finished eating this staff, and then I will tell you.
Tongxuan Qi said, "The attendant was staring with wide eyes while speaking in his sleep; he caused the National Teacher to lose his peace of mind over food and rest.
Although Danxia understood how to bury a person right where they stood, he failed to consider that bystanders would see through him. Is there anyone who knows that attendant?"
"Is this the one who ate the staff, the one who was startled by Danxia? Try and say it.
Xiqia Cheng said, "The National Teacher cast his body across the world beyond, eating his fill and sleeping soundly; he relied on having an attendant to receive guests.
Yet when a distinguished guest arrived, he could not avoid being respectful yet lacking in courtesy. Had it not been for the National Teacher's wisdom..."

The mirror hangs high; it nearly had its brilliance scraped away by Danxia. Yet, though Danxia was a masterful hand, he could not avoid the guest’s failure to realize that his efforts were merely troubling the host.
Nanshan Baoyun said: "Although the attendant’s eyes were high and keen, Danxia’s discernment was not skillful.

Had it not been for the National Teacher’s ability to distinguish the melody from a single string and shift the pivot of the occasion, he would have inevitably incurred the scrutiny of others. Nevertheless, even so, this is a calamity arising from within one's own household."
Fengshan began by saying: "The gate bears the character 'Phoenix' (Feng), yet within its phrases lies a hidden mechanism.
To expand the family tradition and teach one's children with righteous integrity—this can truly be called a 'pierced-less flute meeting felt clappers. Nevertheless, tell me:
did Danxia ever actually meet the National Teacher?"
Lingfeng said, "Lingyun: Danxia sang wildly in the emerald caves; the National Teacher was utterly intoxicated in the jade pitcher.
Had it not been for the attendant’s feigned innocence, how could one have seen the greatness of his meritorious service?"
Baiyan Fu said: "This fellow Danxia harbored ill intent. Had it not been for Nanyang’s mirror that illuminates demons, the National Teacher would have nearly been ruined by his attendant.
Yet, although the attendant received the blow of the staff, he remained unhurt;
only Danxia’s entire frame of bones and joints still aches to this day."
Qianlu Huiyun said: "The movement of benefit is for the gentleman. Let us set aside Danxia’s case for now;
it is like drawing a bow when a bandit passes by—the National Teacher merely boasts of his skill at archery. When examined closely, what spirit is there in that?
It is not even as good as Meng Bala’s single cold arrow hitting two targets, which is somewhat more effective."

The National Teacher was once discussing the meaning of the teachings with the Imperial Attendant Zilin. As the Master ascended the seat, the Attendant said, "I request the Master to establish a thesis;
I shall refute it. The Master replied, "The thesis has already been established. The Attendant asked, "What is that thesis? The Master said, "Indeed, you do not see it."
"This is not the realm of ordinary people. He then descended from his seat.
Guangyin Biaoyun remarked: "A skilled warrior leads others into battle rather than being led by them. One like Zilin has only a vanguard but no rearguard.
Had he been a true man of the Way at that time, he would have waited until the establishment of the thesis was complete, and then—"
To speak candidly, this old man who understands the Way makes his living within a ghost cave; he is certain to prevail by taking advantage of the enemy's form.
Even if the troops of another land were numerous, what benefit would they bring to victory?
The National Teacher asked Attendant Zilin, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from south of the city.
The Master said, "What color is the grass south of the city? He replied, "It is yellow. The Master then asked the boy, "Boy, what color is the grass south of the city? The boy replied, "It is yellow.
The Master said, "This very boy could also be granted purple robes before the imperial curtain and discuss the profound mysteries in the presence of the Emperor."
Taisu Zhe said: "The National Teacher asked in such a manner; the Palace Attendant and the boy answered in such a manner.
Tell me, was there any point of advantage or disadvantage? If you can discern this, I grant that you have personally seen the National Teacher; if you cannot discern it, [you have not]."
The grass south of the city remains yellow as before.
Jingshan Daokai said, "Do you say that the National Teacher’s 'muddy and watery' teaching of 'householder Chan' is permissible?
Haimen Yong said, "Although the National Teacher was accustomed to treating the noble as base, when scrutinized, it is still just grass."
"Rolling in the nest.
Because the National Teacher was commenting on the *Suyāma-sūtra* for the Imperial Attendant, the Master said, "In commenting on a sutra, one must first understand the Buddha’s intent.
The Attendant replied, "If one does not understand the Buddha’s intent, how can one comment on a sutra? The Master ordered his attendant to bring a bowl of water. Within the water...
He placed seven grains of rice on it and set a single chopstick across the face of the bowl. He asked Daofeng, "What is the meaning of this? Feng was speechless.
The Master said, "I do not yet understand even the intention of this old monk; how much less could I grasp the intention of the Buddha?"
Guishan Lingyou said: "The Palace Attendant has a beginning but lacks an end; he had an action but no merit. At that time, as soon as he saw the question, 'What is the meaning?
he should have simply said: 'Originally, there was no need to bring it out. He could have kicked it over and walked away.
Even if National Teacher Huairang possessed a mouth made of his entire body, there would have been no place for him to speak."
The National Teacher asked the Attendant, "What is the practice you have cultivated, Venerable Sir? He replied, "I lecture on the *Qinglong* commentary.
The Master said, "Is this commentary on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*? He replied, "It is. The Master said, "What are the first two characters of the sūtra text called?
[The Attendant] replied, "'Thus' (*evam*). The Master said, "What is that? The Attendant was speechless.
Mingzhao Qian, acting on behalf of the attendant, said: "The Vulture Peak of old, today seen in person.
Guo of Mt. Mushi said: "I want to ask Mingzhao: 'The Vulture Peak of old, today seen in person'—what, after all, is this?
At that time, had someone been able to apply a single squeeze, even if Mingzhao were to have been thorough...

The Heavenly Offering.
One day, while crossing a bridge on a donkey, the Chan Master Yushan of Chaling stepped on the plank and fell. Suddenly, he attained great enlightenment.
He spoke a verse, saying: "I possess a divine pearl; for a long time it has been locked away by the dust of worldly toil. This morning the dust is cleared and its light shines forth."
"Shattering the ten thousand peaks of mountains and rivers.

"The sun has been smashed to pieces by a single blow of the hammer. He looked around left and right and said, "Is there anyone who does not feel this bitterness?
He leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.

Fubei said, "If you have some further excellence, feel free to bring it forth. The old woman folded her hands and wept, saying, "In the midst of heaven, even more grievous suffering is added!

Fubei was silent. The old woman said, "Your words do not distinguish between the biased and the correct; your principle does not recognize the inverted and the crooked. To act as a teacher for others..."

When the old woman heard this, she laughed and said, "Master Wang still lacks a certain skillful means.

[Daowu] was at a loss. The old woman asked, "Do you understand? Daowu stood there with his palms joined. The old woman said, "Dead Zen monks are as numerous as hemp and millet.
Daowu reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "If I had seen that stinking old woman, I would have questioned her until she was speechless.
Daowu asked, "I do not know how the Master would have questioned her. Zhaozhou then struck him. Daowu said, "Why did you strike me instead?"
Jiazhou said, "This fellow is a dead-end Zen monk. If I do not strike him, when shall I wait for the right time? He struck him with his staff and drove him out.
When the old woman heard of this, she said, "Zhaozhou deserves a blow from my own staff. Later, a monk reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou wept and said, "How tragic! How painful!
When the old woman heard this, she joined her palms and sighed, "Zhaozhou’s eye of wisdom pierces through the four worlds."
The State Governor asked a monk, "What is the Eye of Zhaozhou? The old woman then raised her fist. The monk returned and reported this to Zhaozhou.
Zhaozhou then composed a verse, saying: "When the occasion arises, he presents it face-to-face; Face-to-face, he acts with the swiftness of the occasion. I tell you, Laywoman Lingxing!"
"What gain or loss is there in this sound of weeping? Vappa replied with a verse: "The Master has already understood the sound of weeping; having understood it, who else could know?
At that time, in the kingdom of Magadha, how many would have lost the opportune moment before their eyes?"

Yingshan Yun said: "Ling Xingpo possessed a strategy that transcended the ordinary; even Zhaozhou and Nanquan would have yielded her a step.

An elder who had heard of this previously remarked, "Reverend, do not speak so hastily! If one speaks of the true cause, there is not even a single character.
Having finished speaking, he tapped his teeth and said, "Just now, I spoke without cause; it was not right to speak in such a manner.
An old practitioner by the neighboring wall heard this and said, "What a fine pot of soup, ruined by a single mouse dropping!"
Baoci then raised the point, saying: "Tell me, is this a word of praise or a word of refusal?
If it is praise, he also says that rat-dung has defiled it; if it is a refusal, what fault is there in that old master?"
Xuedou Xian said, "In whose household are there not one or two grains in the cauldron?
Jingshan Xiuzhen said, "This monk creates trouble where there is none; I, the old monk, prescribe medicine according to the illness.
The thread goes out and the silk comes in, yet the needle-point remains hidden. Yet, alas, he has still not realized the final phrase. As for that old master next door..."
"So it is. But how about this? 'The Three Platforms must be urged forward by everyone together.
After Fengri Yue finished citing Xuedou’s words, he said: "These three fellows were all merely following in the footsteps of others;
they have not yet emerged from the thicket of entanglements. If it had been I, Fengri, when that monk asked such a question, I would have [responded] with his very voice."
He then struck him and drove him out through the mountain gate. If there were blood beneath his skin, he would surely have found another livelihood;
this would have spared us from such a state of mutual neglect and futility.
Benjue Wei said: "The way those two old masters acted was much like a tortoise dragging its tail.

Furthermore, there was a fellow who 'peered through a hole in the wall to steal light' who went on to add a point to an arrowhead. But tell me, where exactly is the spot defiled by the two mouse droppings?"
There was an elderly master who wrote the character for "mind" (心) above his door, on his window, and on his wall.

Fayan Yi said: "Above the door, one should simply write the character for 'door' (門); on the window, one should simply write the character for 'window' (牕); on the wall, one should simply write the character for 'wall' (壁)."
Xuánjué then said: "Do not write the character 'gate' on the gate; do not write the character 'window' on the window;
do not write the character 'wall' on the wall. Why? Because the meaning of these characters is already manifest."
Longtang Zhi said: "On the gate, one writes the character for 'window'; on the window, one writes the character for 'wall'; on the wall, one writes the character for 'gate. Why is this so?
The stream from the eastern ravine flows into the western ravine; clouds rise from the southern mountain and drift over the northern mountain."
Baiyan Fu said: "The Elder committed the slander of contradiction; Fayan committed the slander of superimposition; Xuangjue committed the slander of denial;
and Longtang committed the slander of frivolous proliferation. These four fellows have all been convicted by this mountain monk according to their own confessions.
Is there anyone here who still feels dissatisfied? Come forth and try to argue a case!"
An elder said, "The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years to seek out those who understand him. If you understand it in this way, the day will come when you eat iron rods.
Another elder said, "The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years; how can you not feel ashamed?
If you understand it in such a manner, you must buy straw sandals and travel on foot for another thirty years."
Langya Huijue said: "Since that is not so, tell me: what was the meaning of the Patriarch’s wall-gazing? After a long silence, he said:
"If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma."
Tiantong Jie said: "The two old masters were merely knocking on bricks and beating tiles; Langya was like an old hand painting a tiger that turned out to be a wildcat.
Do you all wish to see the intent behind the Patriarch’s wall-gazing? A bottomless pit is difficult to fill."
An elder said, "This plot of land has been entrusted to you for a long time; I shall stand here waiting for you to grasp it.
Fayan Yi said, "I, this mountain monk, now sit here waiting for you to grasp it—is there any principle in that?"
There is none. Which one is close and which one is distant? Try to judge for yourself.
Zhaojue Qin said: "This field of land has been entrusted to me for a long time. Today, before the assembly, I shall offer a celebration and confession."
Huìyún said, "The three elders have cast their bodies across for the sake of sentient beings with such great compassion;
yet how can they withstand these winds and waves, which seem difficult to reconcile? The mountain monk, however, says it is not so: this plot of land has been entrusted to me for a long time.
"I am weary and wish to go to sleep," [he said].
Shishuang Zun said, "This patch of ground has been entrusted to you for a long time. Why then do none of you tread upon it?
It is precisely because it is too clear that it causes what is attained to be delayed."

An ancient worthy was once asked by a monk: "When the first yang returns, the days grow longer by one thread; I wonder, how much does the Buddha-dharma grow? The worthy replied: "It grows by one thread.
Furthermore, another monk asked an ancient worthy: "When the first yang returns, the days grow longer by one thread;
I wonder, how much does the Buddha-dharma grow? The worthy replied: "One thread grows."
Jianfu Can said: "Traveling the mountain path together as one, each person perceives the wind and smoke differently before their eyes.
Gaoping Miao said: "Attacking the nest to seize the prey is the essential hammer and tongs of those two elders;
if you speak of the length or brevity of the Buddha-dharma, you have not yet seen it even in a dream. Today, should someone suddenly ask about the length of the West Peak’s Buddha-dharma—
"How much? [To this] he simply said, "Ten thousand east and west, eight thousand south and north.
Xiangtian Xian remarked, "Although these two elders possess the skillful means to patch up empty space, their red thread has not yet been severed;
they merely make their living by calculating lengths and distances. How could their distance from the Buddha-Dharma be less than ten thousand [miles]?"
"Eight thousand. If I were this mountain monk, I would not say it so. When the first yang returns and the days grow by one thread, I wonder how much the Buddha-dharma grows?
To him I would simply say: "Do not compare the length of the jade thread; you should instead take up the golden needle and look at what is embroidered."
An ancient worthy said: "The Buddha-dharma is vast indeed; it is simply a toothache. Jingshan Hongzhi said:
"I told you not to travel the path beneath the mountain; now you truly hear the heart-rending cry of the ape."
The Dharma-Cloud of the Supreme Dharma: "If one were Tao Yuanming, one would simply knit one's brows and return home.
An ancient worthy said: "That which is long is the long Dharmakāya; that which is short is the short Dharmakāya."
Tiantong Jue said: "Tell me, what does the Śūnyatā-deva call when he speaks of the Dharma-body? After a long silence, he said:
'Do you understand? One must not shorten the ducks or cut off the cranes, nor level the mountains or fill the valleys.'"
There was a practitioner who followed a Dharma Master into the Buddha hall. He spat toward the Buddha. The Dharma Master said, "Practitioner, you lack propriety;
why do you spit at the Buddha? The practitioner replied, "I have come from a place where there is no Buddha to spit upon this one. The Dharma Master had no words.
Guishan Lingyou said: "The benevolent person is actually the non-benevolent person; the non-benevolent person is actually the benevolent person.
Yangshan Huiji, acting on behalf of the Dharma Master, simply spat at the practitioner. If the practitioner had something to say, he would have told him:
"Bring me back to the place where there is no practitioner."
Zifu’s attendant struck on behalf of the Dharma Master. He further said, "This only saves half.
Bairyak Pu remarked, "It is not that the Dharma Master is without words—it is like unrefined gold and uncut jade—but it is simply that a clear mirror is rarely encountered."
There were two monks who lived in hermitages; they did not meet for many days. One day they encountered each other.

The master of the upper hermitage asked, "It has been a long time since we last saw one another; where have you been? The master of the lower hermitage replied, "I have been in my hermitage building a seamless stupa.
The master of the upper hermitage said, "I also wish to build one. Please lend me the model of your stupa so that I may see it. The master of the lower hermitage said, "Why do you not..."
"You spoke too early; it has just been borrowed by someone.
Fayen Yizheng asked, "Tell me, was it his style that was borrowed, or was it not his style?
The attendant Shouyibao of Caoxi, upon the arrival of a monk, held up the robe and said, "This is the one from Mount Dayu."
[The monk] could not lift up his head. The monk asked, "Why is it then in the hands of the Senior Monk? The attendant was speechless.

Yunmen Wenyan said, "Neither has reached a resolution. He further spoke on behalf of the attendant at that point of silence, saying, "Hearing from afar is not as good as arriving in person. He also said, "This is a lion cub."
Baiyan Fu said: "When a robe-and-bowl attendant or a monk is confronted with a single, piercing pressure, it causes sweat to flow down the spine.
One knows from this that the mouth is the gateway to calamity. At that moment, when [the master] asks, 'Why is it in the hands of the senior monk?
you should simply lower your voice and say, 'Reverend, you may well have doubts. This will surely ensure that the monk has no choice but to kneel."
There was a laywoman who had supported a mountain hermit for twenty years, constantly employing a young woman to attend to him.
One day, she ordered the woman to hold the hermit firmly and asked, "At such a moment as this, how is it? The hermit replied, "A withered tree leans against a cold cliff;
throughout the three winters, there is no warmth. When the woman returned and reported this to the laywoman, the laywoman said, "For twenty years, I have only provided support..."
Having raised this worldly fellow, she then sent him away and burned down the hut.
Tiantong Jie said: "This old woman’s inner chamber is deep and secure, her defenses impenetrable;
yet she has gone so far as to scatter flowers upon withered wood and ignite flames within a cold cliff. This monk stands alone and remote, accustomed to plunging into surging waves."
Sitting idly, he cuts off the surging tide; in the end, his body is not even moistened by a single drop of water.
If one examines this closely, there are undoubtedly two people involved in being shackled and bound. As for the Buddha-dharma, you have not even dreamed of it yet.
Nanjian asked, "The weak exploiting the strong and the strong relying on the powerful has been so throughout ancient and modern times.
A long skirt peddling prettiness makes it difficult for heretical teachings to be supported. In years past, I myself had my eyes changed by an old woman.
You, monk, claim you missed the mark with that woman; yet, if one examines this closely, it was actually the woman who missed the mark with you. He clapped his hands and laughed heartily.
He laughed loudly and said, "Thirty years from now, I shall explain it through for all of you. Kōngtóng Cíyún remarked:
"Among the assembly, some say the Hermitage Master has not yet attained realization; the old woman is a skilled practitioner.

To propagate the Dharma in such a manner, one sees only the sharpness of the tip of the awl, yet one fails to realize that the old woman does not know the place where the Hermitage Master finds his true enjoyment. As for the Hermitage Master..."
Not knowing the old woman’s point of action, the Master struck both the pair of astonished attendants with twenty blows each. Why?
Because here at Lion Rock, rewards and punishments are clearly distinguished.
Longhua Ti said: "Although this old woman possesses the eyes and hands of a master throughout her entire body, it is ultimately but the 'old woman’s Chan.
Only this monk enters fire without smoke and enters water without drowning; he instantly causes all the old woman’s hundreds of thousands of wiles to melt away like ice and crumble like rubble."
Dongta Xi said: "The hermitage master’s wall is several *ren* high, its joints and passages impassable.

The old woman secretly crossed the layered barriers, wishing to explore the springtime colors within the inner gate. Had this not been a truly extraordinary occurrence, how could one have seen such a dark meeting with a bright entry?"
Tianbao Zhenyun said: "Everyone says the old woman had great skill and insight; yet upon closer inspection, she was completely outwitted by this monk.
Although this monk was sent out the door, he was nonetheless difficult even for the Buddha-eye to perceive."
Fengshan began by saying: "The mountain is high and the stream flows clear; the more sublime the melody, the fewer those who can harmonize with it.
Boya and Ziqi were no ordinary acquaintances. Setting aside the old woman for a moment, do you recognize the master of the hermitage’s phrase for turning about?
His boundless elegance he has no desire to display, so as to avoid being pointed out by others as a 'fine young man'."
Xidun Chao said: "Of those who have traditionally commented on this case, many have supported the old woman while disparaging the monk.

They failed to realize that with a single utterance, the old woman—a mere worldly person—reviled all the people in the world, while the monk, by being driven away, caused all the people in the world to fall into ruin."
Dayu Zhe said: "The old woman has the stratagem of burning her boat, yet she lacks the capacity to smash her cauldron.
This monk possesses the scheme of retreating, yet he especially lacks the strength to break through the pass. Both fail to escape being scrutinized by others.
Nevertheless, while it is easy to see the old woman, it is difficult to see this monk."
Baiyan Fu said: "In the midst of clarity, he sits with his tongue out; this still belongs to the old woman. To withdraw the horizontal bone from within the darkness, one must be this monk.
Although the sharp awl and the square chisel each excel in their own way, if one examines them closely, they are both merely salt smugglers."

On the road to Linyang, there was an old woman who made her living selling cakes. When Deshan Jian first left the roads of Sichuan and passed through Linyang, he went to her to buy some cakes for his mid-morning meal.
The woman pointed to his carrying pole and asked, "What texts are on the head of the venerable monk's burden?

Deshan replied, "The *Qinglong Shuchao* (Commentary on the Diamond Sutra). The woman asked, "Which sutra does this commentary explain? Deshan said, "The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. The woman said, "I..."
There is a question: if you can answer it, I will give you refreshments; if you cannot answer, please go elsewhere to buy some.
The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* says: "The past mind is unattainable; the present mind is unattainable; the future mind is unattainable."
"I do not know which mind the Elder was pointing to," said Shanshan.
He remained silent. Tiantong Wu remarked: "If I were Deshan, I would simply say, 'I am hungry; pick out the largest ones and bring them here quickly.
Once they were brought, I would shoulder them and walk away immediately. This would surely leave that old woman in a state of total doubt."
[The Master] went out.
Xi-cheng said, "If I were Zhou Jingang, when [the Master] asked, 'I do not yet know which mind the Venerable is pointing to,' I would simply have replied, 'Today the mountain monk is weary.
Had he been able to utter those words at that moment, he would have been taught a lesson."
This old woman was so flustered that she failed to serve the refreshments properly.
Long ago, there was a man riding a donkey who asked a group of monks, "Where are you going? The monks replied, "To the site of enlightenment (the *bodhimaṇḍa*).

The man said, "Where is not the site of enlightenment? He struck one of the monks with his fist and said, "This fellow has no sense! You are riding a donkey right in the midst of the site of enlightenment!"
[The Master] did not descend from his seat. The man remained silent.
Baoren Xiu said, "Everyone says this fellow has a head but no tail; he can do it, but he cannot face it.

What they fail to realize is that this monk’s earlier words do not match his later ones. Since one knows that every lifting and placing of the feet [is the Way], [how could there be such a discrepancy?]
The Site of Enlightenment. Why do you not realize that riding a donkey or mounting a horse is nothing other than the work of a Buddha?
Wansong wishes to settle this unresolved case; let me further pass judgment on these flowers: "Eating a fist—what a lackluster fellow!

Maoguang and Du the Chan monk were already lacking in self-discipline; how could they have allowed themselves to miss the mark? The Site of Enlightenment has but one; the Buddha-dharma is fundamentally not many.
"Leave this for the *ācārya* to explain. Huǒn said, "Oṃ sarva.
Longtángzhù remarked, "This monk is far too coarse; he has been beating people indiscriminately within the ritual precinct."
A donor entered the monastery to distribute the annual offerings to the community of monks. The administrative monk said, "Place one portion before the Holy Monk (the Buddha statue).
The donor asked, "How many years of seniority does the Holy Monk have? The administrative monk had no reply.
Fayan Yi said in his place: "One knows it when the heart's intention is fulfilled.
Baoning Yong said: "I only fear that the donor’s resources may fall short.
Tianning Qi said in his place: "The alms bowl has no bottom."
Baoshou then spoke on behalf of the administrator, saying: "If that were so, the assembly would not receive a single word today.
A monk living in a hermitage in Guangnan encountered a great king while out hunting. An official informed the abbot, "The Great King is coming; please rise."
The monk said, "It is not only when Your Majesty comes that I do not rise; even when the Buddha comes, I do not rise.
The King then asked, "Is the Buddha not your teacher? The monk replied, "He is. The King said, "If so, why do you not rise upon seeing your teacher? The monk was speechless.
Fayan Yi’s successor said: "It is not yet sufficient to repay his kindness.
Tianning Qi said: "If you wish to observe the master, first observe the disciple.
Bairyak Pu’s successor spoke on behalf of the monk, saying: "If the son is not revered, the father will not be honored."
Hexu Qian said: "Today I have gone out for a small matter and encountered a great event.
There was an elder whose house a monk came to beg from, only to be bitten by his dog.

The elder then pointed to the *kāṣāya* the monk was wearing and said, 'I have heard that even if a dragon wears but a single thread, a *garuḍa* will not swallow it; yet you, Great Master, are fully clad in the Dharma robes.'"
"Why was he bitten by a dog? The monk remained silent. Baohua Ren spoke on behalf of the monk, saying:
"Before examining the earth upon the mountain peak, one first observes the master beneath the eaves."
The layman Han [surname unknown] was invited by the assembly to serve as the presiding mourner for the funeral rites of Sanping, following his passing.

Han then covered a bronze gong with a handkerchief, placed a single sword across it, and set it before the reliquary shrine, saying, "If you can speak the Way, you shall be the presiding mourner. The assembly remained silent, unable to respond.
Han immediately kicked over the cooking cauldron and wailed, "Heaven! Heaven! My former master is gone far away!
Luoshan Xian said, "Alas! How extraordinary, how extraordinary! The six hundred or so disciples under Sanping have all been swallowed up by this worldly fellow.
Had Old Teacher Chen been present at that time, he would have simply covered [the corpse] with three feet of cloth."
He turned his head away and held a sharp-edged sword askew across his shoulder. Raising the funeral curtain, he sat upon the dais.
Observe this man of the Han family: whether he wishes to act as the presiding mourner or not, he cannot do so.
To advance, there must be propriety; to retreat, there must be propriety.
△ At Caoxi, two branches emerged simultaneously:
Chan Master Xingxiu Qingyuan of Jizhou (the successor of Dajian Huineng) sent a letter to National Teacher Nanyue Huairang, entrusting him with the message:
"When you return, I have a 'pickaxe' for you to dwell in the mountains. Xingxiu arrived at Nanyue...
Yue had not yet seen the letter when he asked, "When one does not admire the various sages and does not prize one's own spirit, what then?

Yue said, "Your question is too high, my son. Why not ask about things below? Xian replied, "I would rather suffer in the depths of saṃsāra for eternal kalpas than seek liberation through the various sages.
He then returned home. Yuan asked, "Why have you returned so quickly? Did your letter reach? Xian said, "The letter reached."
This was also not permitted; his letter did not reach him either. On the day he departed, he received the Master’s promise of a "pickaxe.
He requested it now. "Please, bend down one foot," [the Master said]. Baizhang then prostrated.
Xuansha Shibei said, "The great and small Stoneheads were pushed over by Nanyue; to this day they cannot be raised.
Xuedou Xian said, "Stonehead was already passed over while carrying a wooden board," and he further said, "Great and small Nanyue did not know how to maintain the command."
Cuiyan Zhi said: "When Master Si extended his feet and Shitou prostrated, he simply could not find an axe.
But tell me, what did he use afterwards?"

Huanglong Nan said: "Although Shitou was indeed skilled at traveling far and wide without disgracing the ancestral style, he was too hasty in displaying his brilliance and failed to realize he had lost the vital point.
Since he had already lost the vital point, why did he receive the axe upon his return?"
Dongyuan Jing said: "Both of these two great elders have points where they let things pass. When it is said, 'Not admiring the sages, not esteeming one's own spirit'—how is this so?
Why did Nanyue not give him a blow across the spine? Your question is too high; why not ask from below?
Shitou would have done well to give him a shout right in the face."

Gounan said: "What a pity about that dull axe! All you venerable seniors, since Shitou had already seen Nanyue, why did Qingyuan ask him and he reply, 'Even a letter cannot convey it, nor can a message reach it'? Do you understand?"
The golden rooster pecks through the lapis lazuli shell; the jade hare pushes open the gates of the azure sea.
Tianmu’s Vinaya says: "This crude axe—if it were not for Stonehead to take it up, it would be too difficult."
Baoshang said, "Stonehead can truly be called one who, when the feathered dispatches flew in haste, did not disgrace his mission;
yet he should not have coveted that other man’s adze.
Yuedi Zhi said, "He was asked for an adze; why then did he dangle a foot? Since he did not comply with the others...
The Sage seeks liberation. How can you simply prostrate? Thereupon, he shook his sleeves and said: "Look! Look!
An adze has split heaven and earth into an eight-cornered millstone; the golden crow and jade hare have been chased down.
Where would the blind tortoise and the lame turtle know of this?"
Qingyuan went to visit the Sixth Patriarch and asked, "What should one do to immediately avoid falling into stages? The Patriarch said, "What have you been doing?
Qingyuan replied, "I do not even practice the Noble Truths. The Patriarch asked, "In what stage do you fall? Qingyuan said: [I fall into no stage.]
"If one does not even practice the Noble Truths, what hierarchy could there be? Master Zu deeply esteemed him.
Dongyuan Jing said, "If I were the Sixth Patriarch, when asked 'What should one attend to? I would immediately avoid falling into any hierarchy.
He then shouted, "This dung-carrier! What are you doing here? If he were Qingyuan, when [asked the same question]...
When asked, "What have you been doing? he clapped his hands and said, "This old fellow is still talking in his sleep.
Did this not cause the path of Caoxi to possess a unique splendor?
Lingyan Chu said: "If even the Noble Truths are not established, what levels or stages could there be?
Zhaozhou was used to drinking tea; Caoshan loved to drink wine. A pair of ancient sages—two people sharing a single hand.
*Du!* Cast off the clothes of marriage; block the mouth of the primordial void. The mud ox knows how to let out a lion’s roar."
Baiyan Fu said: "When the mundane and the sagely are swept away into emptiness, not even a speck of dust remains.
It is as chillingly majestic as a verdant cliff or an autumn precipice, utterly beyond reach or veneration. Were it not for the unicorn among the many-horned beasts, how could one achieve this?
I can only regret that Ge Liao of Lingnan let the matter pass at that time. He said, 'If even the Holy Truth (āryasatya) does not exist, what grades or stages could there be? How excellent!"
Striking the right desk with his staff, he said, "For now, place it by the side where you stand. When the old fellow from Qingyuan arrives here, he will surely have a different way of life.
When a monk asked Qingyuan, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Qingyuan looked at the monk and said, "The price of rice in Luling."
"What is the price?

Boshanlai replied, "The price of rice, high or low. The verdant hues of Huancui encircle the wondrous peaks; swallowing and spitting forth the elegance of Luling, it refines the lunar splendor within the jade trees.
One must know that the Great Function is boundless and responds whenever there is resonance. As for discussing Qingyuan—
As for this Buddha-dharma, even after sixty kalpas across three lifetimes, one has not yet seen it in a dream.
Cuiyan Zhe said: "Do you Zen adepts still recognize where Old Man Qingyuan stands?
One sees only the imperial wind forming a single expanse; one knows not where the boundaries of territory lie."
Qingyuan asked Shitou, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Caoxi. Qingyuan said, "What have you brought back?
He replied, "Even before reaching Caoxi, I was not lacking anything. Qingyuan said, "If that is so, what was the use of going to Caoxi?
He replied, "If I had not gone to Caoxi, how would I have known that I was not lacking anything?"
Lingyan Chu held up his staff and said: "The 'Shang Daren' (The Great Man of Shang) knows propriety. You young students, tell me: where does the essential point lie?
He struck the ground once and said: "From this point on, he will not return; yet were he to return, he would find it.
Who could compete for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes?"
Qingyuan was originally a student of Heze Shenhui. Once, Qingyuan asked him, "Where have you come from? Shenhui replied, "From Caoxi.
Qingyuan asked, "What is the essential meaning of Caoxi? Shenhui stood up straightening his body. Qingyuan said, "You still carry some rubble with you.
Shenhui asked, "Does the Master not have some genuine gold here to give to people? Qingyuan said, "Even if there were, where would you put it?"
Xuansha Bei said, "As expected.
Yunju Xi said, "As for Xuansha saying 'as expected,' is it true gold or is it rubble?
Cuoyan Zhi said, "'True gold' and 'rubble' are both erroneous expressions; what would you call them now?"
Tiansheng Tai said: "Qingyuan was so struck by Heze’s single question that he broke into a sweat on his forehead and felt his mouth go dry with gum-like stickiness.
As for Chan Master Huairang of Nanyue in Hengzhou (a successor of Dajian Huineng), when he visited the Sixth Patriarch, the Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from? Huairang replied:
At Mount Song, the Patriarch asked, "What thing comes thus? Fengyue had no reply. He then spent eight years until, suddenly, he attained realization.
He said to the Patriarch, "I have a point of understanding. The Patriarch asked, "How so? Fengyue replied, "To describe it as a single thing is not correct.
The Patriarch asked, "Is there still need for cultivation and realization? Fengyue said, "Cultivation and realization are not absent; however, [it is] defilement..."
"If you are defiled, you may not [enter]. The Patriarch said, "This very non-defilement is what all Buddhas protect and keep in mind.
Since you are thus, I am also thus."
Baiyan Fu said: "To respond in such a manner requires one who has personally reached that other shore, having penetrated to the very top and bottom;
otherwise, it would be utterly impossible to utter a single word. It was therefore fitting that the 'Horse Colt' (Mazu) should emerge from beneath his feet and trample the whole world underfoot.
Yet, had the Sixth Patriarch at that time been able to strike him once more with a heavy blow behind the head,"
That the flourishing of descendants does not end with this day alone—saying "it is thus, it is thus"—is this not the strategic method of the Patriarch?
Mazu said: "Nanyue’s saying that 'to resemble even a single thing is not correct'—how about that, Sixth Patriarch?"
The Master said, "I am also like this. How thick-skinned you are!
Nanyue was once asked by a monk, "When a mirror is used to cast an image, once the image has been formed, I wonder where the light has gone?"
Yue said, "As for the Venerable One, what were your features like when you were a child? He replied, "But once the image was completed, why could it no longer reflect things?
Yue said, "Even though it cannot reflect things, not even a single point can be hidden from it."
Fayan Yi said, "Which one of these, Great Virtue, is a cast image?
Baoshou Fang replied, "Whether large or small, the commentaries on Mount Nanyue are not easy to interpret. Xuefeng said, "It is not so here."
When a mirror casts an image, once the image has been formed, where does the light go? Wait until his eyes flicker with movement, and then strike him across the spine. △ Qingyi.

Chan Master Xituan of Shitou on Mount Nanyue (a successor of Qingyuan Xingsi) was once asked by Yaoshan: "I, Huian, have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
However, I have heard that in the South they point directly to the human mind for the realization of Buddhahood; I truly do not yet understand this clearly.
I humbly hope that the Venerable Master will compassionately provide me with instruction. Shitou said: "It is not so, nor is it otherwise."
"Not so. Neither 'so' nor 'not so'—neither is acceptable. What do you say? Shanshan remained silent for a moment.
Mazu said, "Your karmic conditions do not lie here. There is Master Ma in Jiangxi; go there, and he will explain it for you.
When Shanshan arrived there, he questioned him as before. Mazu said, "Sometimes I teach them by raising an eyebrow or blinking an eye; sometimes..."

"It is not that I teach him to raise his eyebrows or blink his eyes; sometimes it is that I teach him to raise his eyebrows and blink his eyes, and sometimes it is that I teach him to raise his eyebrows and blink his eyes which is not so.
How do you understand this, my son? At these words, Shansheng attained realization and prostrated himself.
The Patriarch asked, "Son, what principle have you seen that you prostrate yourself? Mountan said, "I am like Wenyi at Shitou, like a mosquito on an iron ox.
The Patriarch said, "Since it is so for you, you should maintain this well."
Fayun Xiu said: "Shitou’s 'iron hammer without a hole' is truly excellent; it is almost as if he could not entrust [the Dharma] to him.
Although Yaoshan went beyond the Yangtze River and attained enlightenment, alas, he still stumbled on level ground.
What support or aid was there for him? Let those with eyes try to discern this."
Wuzu Yan said: "Among the assembly, some deliberate thus: 'To say "this very mind is Buddha" is not permissible; to say "this very mind is not Buddha" is also not permissible.
If one acts like this, how can they dare to call themselves a Chan guest? Little do they realize that the ancients were both civil and martial, possessing both strategy and tactics.
I, this mountain monk, wish for all of you to know my own perspective as well; I see only the waves."
The waves surge; the sea dragon palace is not seen.
Guishan Zhi said: "What do you mean by saying that when he was at Shitou, he was like a mosquito on an iron ox?
Even now, how has he ever managed to let anything out?"
Guishan Lingyou said: "The first arrow is still tolerable; the second arrow pierces the person deeply. Yaoshan continued:
"Even if you were to attain enlightenment in such a way, you would still fall into the 'second moon'."
Jingshan Daokai said: "What a fine point for discussion! Who could bring it up? Even if one were to bring it up perfectly, I would not yet dare grant my approval.
Xiangyan Bao said: "At that time, Mazu should not have let him go; when he prostrated himself, he should have given him his own staff."
"Distributing fodder. What does this mean? It means that even an iron ox must break into a sweat all over its body before it will do so.
The *Stonehead’s Accordance with the Truth* (*Shitou Cantong qi*) says: "Reciprocity and non-reciprocity."
When a monk asked Yunmen Wenyan, "What is mutual interpenetration? Yunmen pointed to the head of his meditation platform and said, "One must not call this the head of the platform.
The monk asked, "What is non-interpenetration? Yunmen replied, "This very thing is the head of the platform."
Tiantong Jue said: "Shitou’s tongue has no bone; Yunmen’s eyes have sinews. For a thousand ages, his reputation and fame have shone brightly.
If you now wish to walk hand in hand with him, you must first be thus before you can understand 'not being thus.
Only then will there be no further connection. Do you understand this? In my youth, I once broke through the ranks of dragons and snakes."
"In my old age, I listen once more to the songs of young children.
Baoshou Xin said, "To respond in such a manner is much like Xu Liu carrying a single plank—each sees only one side.
But tell me, where does Shitou’s intent lie? "The moon shines upon a thousand crags in stillness; the mountain stream flows deep through ten thousand ravines."

Shitou gave this instruction: "Words and activities have no connection [to the truth]. At that time, Yaoshan came forward and said, "Even to attain a state where there are neither words nor activities has likewise no connection.
Shitou said, "In this place, not even a needle can penetrate. Yaoshan said, "In this place, it is like planting flowers upon a stone."
Baiyan Fu said: "These two old fellows are much like the Sea Dragon King and Śakra competing in wealth;
it is as if the four great continents and the three mountains and five peaks all at once flash with brilliant jewel-light, causing the sun and moon to lose their radiance."
"Here, would you dare to utter even a single word? At that moment, a monk stepped forward.
Baoyun shook his hand and said, "Do not bury the patriarchs' mind with your idle scholarly learning. Get out!"

△ To the south, on the west bank, was Chan Master Daoyi of Mazu (successor to Nan-yueh Huai-jang). When he first began to guide his disciples, Nan-yueh sent a monk to observe him.
Waiting for the time when [Mazu] ascended the hall, the monk stepped forward and asked, "How is it? Mazu replied, "Since the beginning of the chaos."
For thirty years, he had never lacked salt or sauce. When the monk returned and related this to Nanyue, Nanyue approved of it.
Jingshan Daokai said, "Yunmen was not like that: when he dreamed of an inauspicious omen at night, he wrote 'Great Auspiciousness' over his gate."
Tianning Qisong said: "When the Great Master Mazu said, 'For thirty years I have never lacked salt and sauce,' he had already consumed a great deal of salt and sauce himself!

If I were the Great Master, as soon as I saw this monk come forward, I would immediately step down from my meditation seat, seize him, and give him a severe beating, so that he might return and report it to Nanyue, thereby manifesting [the truth]."
The lineage of this master has a clear basis; his own eyes are distinct and clear. You may take it for certain that he will cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven.
Having finished citing the words of Miaoxi, he said: "Now tell me, are Jingshan and Mazu the same or different?
Why, upon a black-lacquered screen, does one further write the poem by Lu Tong on the lunar eclipse?"
Fulong Chang said: "A donkey’s back is fit for nothing but flies.
The *Shouchang Jing* says: "When Mazu spoke thus, I, the old monk, would not have it so.
Since that time of chaos, thirty years have passed without a grain of salt or sauce. "Assembly, tell me: how far apart was he from Mazu?"
"What? Da jue said, "As for 'The meaning emerges in a bountiful year,' this belongs to Mazu; yet it cannot avoid bringing trouble upon Nan-yueh, who remains hanging over his heart."
A monk asked Mazu, “Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations, I ask you, Master, to point directly to the meaning of the West.
Mazu said, “I am weary today and cannot explain it for you. Go ask Zhizang. The monk went to ask Zhizang. Zhizang said, “Why do you not ask the Master?
The monk replied, “The Master told me to come ask you. Zhizang said, “I have a headache today; I cannot speak.”
"I can explain it for you. [The monk] asked, "Go ask Elder Hai. The monk asked Hai, and Hai said, "When I arrived here, I did not understand.
The monk then reported this to the Patriarch (Nanyue Huairang). The Patriarch said, "Zangtou’s head is white; Hai’s head is black."
Taisu Zhe said: "This monk asked in such a manner, and Master Ma answered in such a manner—transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations.
Yet Brother Haizang did not know this at all. Do you understand? Have you not heard it said: 'The colt tramples the people of the world to death'?"
Wuzu Yan said: "As for the place where Master Mazu was ashamed and at a loss, he could only say, 'The head of the cangue is white, the head of the sea is black.
This too is Fenghou Mr. Xian; he knows the first but not the second.
This monk carries a load of bewilderment and exchanges it for a lack of peace and joy. If his eyes were like shooting stars, how much more [would there be]!"
When a person loses their money, they meet with calamity.
Gaofeng Miaoyun said: "The lineage of Master Ma [Huai] and his son is not merely one where the Buddha’s mouth harbors a serpent’s heart;
they are also well-versed in the *Liùtão* and *Sānlüè*. Had this monk not possessed the strategic brilliance of Zhuge Kongming, he would surely have lost his life."

Baoneng Xiu said: "These three old fellows have similar mentalities. If you understand this by way of being 'beyond the four propositions' and 'transcending the hundred negations,' I would rather bury you in the same pit as this monk."
The *Longchi Chuan* says: "The three great elders were brought to such chaos and disorder by this foot-picking fellow that, even to this day, father and son remain at odds.
Is there anyone who can broker a reconciliation? Having said this, he threw his staff into the abbot’s quarters.
Baoshan Zhenyun said, "I am accustomed to being a 'white-handed' thief, yet I alone admire the Master of Ma and his son.
Seeing a thief and catching a thief—what a pity they did not encounter a true adept! Nevertheless, is there anyone who can recognize this monk?"
At Kōngtóng, the Cloud of Compassion—both the Great and Small Māzú and their entire lineage—have had their very lives and natures entirely placed in the hands of this monk.
Is there anyone who knows where this monk has landed?
Jiaoshan Chengyun said: "In both ancient and modern times, one must concede that this monk was a master at 'stealing in broad daylight. Why?
Because although Master Ma’s school possessed the solidity of copper walls and iron fortresses, he plundered it all away in a single morning."
Jin-su Yuan said: "This monk poses a question with a mechanism that is exceedingly steep and perilous.
Were it not for Master Ma and his son, one would surely find no way out. Nevertheless, do you feel that every single skull has been struck by an arrow?"
Zifu Guang said: "Tsk! This blind fellow who bumps into a pillar deserves thirty blows. Nevertheless, Master Mazu and his disciples are not without fault.
Why? Have you not heard it said: 'If an arrow is fired and does not hit the mark, the archer is no true master'?"

Lingyan said: "To remain unstartled amidst a great smelting furnace and unafraid when facing great chaos—were it not for one who has mastered the great constants of the world and grasped the transformative nurturance of Heaven and Earth, they would still be unable to calculate from within their tent and secure victory a thousand *li* away.
How, then, could one dare hope for 'sincere reverence' such that the world is at peace? The Ma family, father and son, were like those who..."
When ten thousand heroic soldiers were in their great battle formation, the entire army was bound and surrendered at his mere cough or spittle. By what artifice was this brought about?
Let you clever monks try to determine this for yourselves.
Baiyan Fu said: "Entering the water without disturbing the waves; entering the forest without moving the grass—this is the skill of Master Ma and his son, both emerging from a single gate.
Nevertheless, neither could entirely avoid being sneered at behind their backs by this monk."
A monk drew four lines before Mazu—making the top line long and the bottom three lines short—and said, "You must not say that one line is long and three lines are short.
Outside of these four lines, please, Master, give me your answer.
Mazu then drew a single line on the ground and said, "Do not speak of long or short; my answer to you is complete."
Nanyang Zhong said, "Why not ask the old monk?
Guishan Guo said, "Borrowing a mother-in-law’s robe to bow for her birthday.
Gaofeng Miao said, "After three transcriptions, the characters *wu* and *yan* become *ma*. Xifeng could no longer restrain his impatience and specifically...
[The Master] corrected this for the sake of all people. After a long silence, he called to his attendant and said, "Take this clearly to heart.
Gushan Xian remarked, "This monk’s formulation of a question is truly extraordinary. If it were a teacher of the present day, they would have already struck him with a staff.
Mazu, however, was not like that; he simply drew a line upon the ground—this may indeed be called [the ultimate]."
"To offer wood and peach in return for jade and precious gems. This monk has gone out small and encountered the great.
Yet the Patriarch said, "I cannot speak of long or short; I have already answered you. This is like chewing food to feed an infant.
When Master Mazu was asked by Master Pang, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion?
Mazu replied, "I will tell you when you can drink up all the waters of the West River in a single gulp."
Yuwang observed and said: "Master Mazu only knew that it was easy to open one's mouth; he did not realize his tongue was long.
Had he been asked by Yuwang at that time, he should simply have said: 'Wait until empty space falls to the ground,' and naturally he would have surpassed him."
Why is this? A carriage does not push sideways, and there is no principle for making a crooked judgment.
Master Nengren’s mirror says: "When the Great Master Mazu answered the question in such a manner, it was very much like not knowing where the point of the question originated."
This has caused Master Pang to be drowned in stagnant water. When Dayan speaks thus, tell me: what is his intention?
He does not seek to strike the grass; he simply wishes to startle the snake.

Shitai Ren said: "This man from the Pang family is much like a destitute scholar who, having happened upon a single copper coin at a crossroads, immediately boasts of his wealth to anyone he meets. It is clear that his worldly airs have not yet been eliminated."
Master Ma was like a reckless young gentleman of the gentry lineages throughout the ages; he spent gold as if it were soil and his teeth did not keep his words from leaking out.
He would answer whatever came to mind, for in his old age he had not yet disciplined his nature. Suppose someone were to ask him about Xingguo:
"Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as companions? Simply answer him:
"The donors who have prepared this vegetarian feast today are all guests upon the road to Shanyin. This merely leaves him with no time to respond.
Why is this so? He plants his staff and says: "The traveler by the river is heartbroken; he is not a native of his own hometown."
Once, while Mazu was accompanied by Baizhang, Nanquan, and Xitang as they enjoyed the moon, Mazu asked, "At this very moment, how is it?
