When meeting water, I drink the water; when meeting grass, I eat the grass. How could I know the conduct of a beast?"
Fahua Ju said: "Furthermore, what is 'walking among those of different species'? A stone ox constantly lies in the mist of the three springs;
a wooden horse occasionally neighs by the spring of an autumn night."
When a monk asked Yunmen Cheng, "What is it like to walk among those of different species? Cheng said, "Strike me lightly!
Strike me lightly! The monk said, "I understand. Cheng asked, "How do you understand? The monk then brayed like a donkey.
Tancheng said, "To depart and rest.
Yuanwu Yun said: "It is like the earth upholding a mountain, unaware of the mountain’s towering loftiness;
it is like a stone containing jade, unaware of the jade’s flawlessness. Thus did Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū shift his seat and attain perfect enlightenment, just as did Sudhana."
Seeing Dechun from a distant peak, the monk said: "Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it;
if you speak of it, horns will immediately sprout. Why do you utter such words? *Cluck!* "Old fellow Meng, you have gone off in that way again!"
Huìyún said: "Nánquán has already walked through the wild weeds, and Guīzōng has entered the deep village;
I do not know how the teachers and monks of these times advance or retreat. Even if one were to go in such a manner, it would still be like a blind donkey following a great crowd."
Nanquan ascended the hall and said, "Last night at the third watch, Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra gave rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma;

I have given each of them twenty blows and expelled them from the monastery. At that time, Zhaozhou stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "Whom does the Master’s staff intend for to eat [the blows]?
Nanquan replied, "Where is the fault of Old Wang? Zhaozhou then bowed and withdrew.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "I have deeply received the Master’s compassion; I have found peace and security under the Master’s robes and bowl.
He further spoke on his behalf, saying, "To eliminate a pest for the sake of the assembly."
Baoci then raised the point, saying: "Tell me, does Zhaozhou’s prostration signify his approval of Nanquan, or his disapproval of Nanquan?
Jia Shan Ling said: "Nanquan displayed his brilliance for a time, yet he could not help but raise a mound on level ground;
though Zhaozhou acted with direct immediacy, he did not realize his forehead had struck the earth."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Nanquan moved the strings; Zhaozhou played a different tune. How painful for the blue heavens!
Hanshan and Shide—if it were Chongning, it would not be so. Last night, the lanterns and the pillars gave rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma."
Each was given twenty blows and sent back to their original positions. Should there be someone who steps forward and says, "Whom does the Master intend for this stick to strike?
one should simply reply to him, "Guest and host both fall."
Gao Feng said, "Although Master Nanquan possessed the eye atop his head and was clear in his judgments of merit and demerit, even so, when scrutinized, he was merely driving a stake into empty space.
If it were not for Zhaozhou’s subsequent remark, I do not know how one would have reached a resolution.
Gao Feng, however, is not like this: if someone suddenly gives rise to views of Buddha or views of Dharma, he simply says to them—"
Excellent, excellent! When the time arrives, the principle will manifest of itself.
Dizang Xue said: "Nanquan stirs up waves where there is no wind; Zhaozhou has a needle within his cotton.
If you attempt to deliberate upon this as a matter of the Buddha-dharma, it will ensure that you enter hell as swiftly as an arrow.
Chongxian Qiyun said: "Nanquan exerted himself to the utmost for the sake of the assembly, yet the calamity arose from his own household.

Although Zhaozhou was indeed a thief who recognized a thief, he could not avoid being accused of 'stealing the sheep while witnessing his father do it. Nevertheless, even when the world is at peace, do not say that there is nothing to attend to."
Once, while Nanquan, Luzu, Guizong, and Shanshan were drinking tea together, Luzu picked up his tea bowl and said, "This existed even before the world was formed.
Nanquan said, "People today recognize only this, but do not recognize the world."
Xuanzong said, "Yes. Fayan Quan said, "Does the Senior Brother not hold this same view? Xuanzong then picked up his tea bowl and said, "Could you say anything before the world was yet formed?
Fayan made a gesture of slapping him with his palm; Xuanzong made a gesture of catching the blow with his face.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Luzu sifts dust and raises clouds; Nanquan mixes mud and blends water; Guizong stirs up fire and scatters ashes;
Shan Shan sits and watches success and failure. Do you understand? When arrowheads meet, they do not yield to one another;
four people together lift a single cup."

Once, Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Please speak, Master, regarding that which transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations. Nanquan immediately descended from his seat and returned to his quarters.
Zhaozhou said, "This old fellow usually talks incessantly, but today, having been questioned by me, he is left with nothing to say.
An attendant remarked, "It would not be right to say the Master has no words. Zhaozhou gave him a slap and said, "Don't talk nonsense!"
"This slap is surely for Master Wang to eat.
Baiyan Fu said, "This fellow Zhaozhou is much like a ball fresh from a red furnace; if you offend him, he will shatter your face.
How magnificent he is within the ranks of the claws and fangs! Yet, in the end, it all does not escape Master Wang."
The Master draws a circle. But tell me, where is Master Wáng’s circle?
Once, when a monk asked Nánquán, "When you return to your quarters, what will you point to as the guide? Nánquán said, "Last night at the third watch, I lost my ox;
at dawn, having risen, I have lost my fire."
Longxiang Xun said: "The great and small Nanquan were like mixing mud with water. Zhongfeng, however, was not so.
If someone were to ask, 'Master, when you return to your quarters, what will you point to as guidance? he would immediately reply, 'Today the staff has opened its seal.'"
Tianjie Shengyun said, "In that case, it is not easy to serve as an abbot. Although so, it must be Master Wang who can do it.
Furong Jiao said, "Nanquan took his three hundred and sixty bones and eighty-four thousand pores..."
At one time, [the teaching] was entirely laid out before this monk. Yet, alas, this monk was like a mosquito on an iron ox—nowhere to enter or take hold.
Longyuan, however, was not so. If someone were to ask, "Master, when you return to your quarters, what will you use as a guide?
he would say: "When hungry, eat; when thirsty, drink; when idle, sit; when weary, sleep."
Once Nanquan went to a manor estate. The master of the estate had prepared a reception in advance. Nanquan said, "I, this old monk, usually enter and exit without letting others know.
How is it that you have made these preparations in advance? The master replied, "Last night the local deity informed me that the Master would come today.
Nanquan said, "Master Wang’s cultivation of practice lacks strength; he has been seen by ghosts and spirits. His attendant...
Someone then asked, "Since you are a great spiritual friend (mahā-kalyāṇamitra), why were you seen by ghosts and spirits?
Nanquan said, "Offer another portion of rice before the local deity."
Baoci then said, "Where is the place for serving another portion of rice before the local deity?
Because of this, Shengying remarked, "Master Wang, having been questioned by this monk, could not help but continue making his living inside a ghost cave."
Yunju Xizheng said: "The first portion of rice before the local deity—does this reward him or punish him?
It is simply that when the local deity looks upon it, he sees whether it is Nanquan or not Nanquan."
Tiantong Jue said: "At that time, when I saw the host speak in such a manner, I immediately seized him and said, 'I will not let you go.
Why? Have you not heard it said: 'He who comes to speak of right and wrong is himself a person of right and wrong'?"
Baoneng Xiu said: "Although Tiantong understands how to catch ghosts and sell them, he cannot avoid being disturbed by the ghosts on his estate.

I, this mountain monk, am not like that. If I see the master of the estate say, 'Last night the local deity reported [this],' I simply snap my fingers three times and say: *Oṃ durlu durlu dīve svāhā*."
Nanquan ascended the hall and said, "Wang Laoshi is selling himself; is there anyone who will buy him? A monk came forward and said, "I will buy him.
Nanquan said, "Neither at a high price nor at a low price—how will you buy him? The monk was speechless.
Zhaozhou Shen said, "Next year, I shall sew a robe of hemp cloth for the Master.
Wolong Qiu said, "The Master belongs to me.
Heshan Yin Daide said, "What kind of principle is this?"
Xuedou Xian said, "Although these masters compete to buy it, they still do not understand how to yield the strategic move.
But tell me, would Nanquan have consented? Xuedou also intends to offer a price, straightway leaving Nanquan with no way to advance and no path to retreat.
After a long silence, he said, "The Master cannot be accommodated elsewhere."
Yunju Zhuang said: "If I were this monk, when he asked, 'I will neither act as noble nor as base;
how would you buy me? I would have immediately replied, 'The nose-rope is in the hands of so-and-so.
Even if Master Wang had some other superior skill, he would have had no choice but to swallow his indignation in silence."
Xiaoyan Bao said: "Today this mountain monk offers a brand-new price, so that this old fellow can neither belong to another nor belong to himself.
When he says, 'It is neither expensive nor cheap; how will you buy it?
simply say, 'Please, Master, return to your quarters for a moment of tea.'"
Yuanwu Keqin said: "Xuedou can only serve as Nanquan’s slave. But as for this—where there is no door to advance and no path to retreat—can Xuedou even be tolerated?"
Gunanmen said: "When the various elders handle and present the matter in this way, do they truly accord with Nanquan’s intent?
They fail to realize that the old fellow Nanquan was judging others by his own standard; it was only out of compassion that he spoke these words that 'descend into the weeds.'"
At that time, when the monk waited for [the Master] to say, "If it is neither noble nor base, how would you buy it?
he simply said, "In that case, I and the Master shall share the price equally. Having thus revealed his own skillful means, he did not fail the Master’s single act of Dharma-giving.
Do you understand? Once the music-master Ziqi has departed and does not return, the vast expanse of the world is truly lamentable. Not so.
"I know those between heaven and earth; I know who that 'knower' is.
Baoyan Fu said: "The various masters of antiquity and today have exhausted their essence and spent all their thought, yet none of them were not intent on becoming the protagonist for Master Wang.
Little did they realize that while the price has been paid, the contract has not yet been placed in hand."
[The monk] said, "It is so. [Zhaozhou] asked, "In that case, how is it ultimately? At that time, when Master Wudao was selling himself—was there anyone who bought him?
He should have replied, "I am going out of the prefecture tomorrow to meet with guests; I trouble the Master to go on ahead."
Tianmu’s Vinaya says: "Master Wang merely seeks someone whose price is equivalent; he does not realize that his slaves and servants will bring calamity upon themselves for all eternity.
Because Layman Lu asked Nanquan, "In my home, I have raised a gosling in a jar; it has now grown—"
Daiyu said, "I wish to get this goose out, yet I must not break the jar, nor may I harm the goose.
I wonder, Master, what skillful means do you have? Nanquan called out, "Grand Master! Daiyu responded, "Yes? Nanquan said, "It is out."
Gao Feng said, "Nanquan’s clumsy hands and eyes lack intimacy; even if he were to produce something, it would still be dead merchandise.
If it were Gao Feng, he would simply say to him, 'Sir, have you ever shown this to anyone?
As soon as the other attempts to respond, he would strike him with a flurry of blows. This was not merely to strip this fellow of his 'hawk-odor' robe; it was because..."
It would cause every single monk in the world to untie their adhesions and cast off their bonds, finding lifelong joy and liberation.
Yingshan Yun said: "The Great Official has established this point of inquiry; it is indeed clever.

Yet, had he not encountered the Old Master Wang, the bottle would have been broken and the gander killed. But tell me, what is it like after he has called them out? Ten-thousand-li eagles fly together to the far distance."
The cranes of a thousand years fly together.
Nanquan and Dongshan went with Mazu to pay their respects to National Teacher Zhong.
On the road, Nanquan drew a circle and said, "If you can speak the Way, then you may go. Dongshan sat down right inside the circle. Mazu performed a woman’s bow. Nanquan said:
"If it is so, then one does not go. Zong asked, "What kind of mental activity is this? Quan then called out to each other and turned back, no longer going to pay their respects.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "If I had seen them at that time, I would have given each of them a blow of my staff, just to ensure peace throughout the world."
Yunju Xi said: "Recently, one was about to pay respects to the National Teacher; why did Nanquan instead call him back?
Tell me, what was the intention of the ancients?"
Baoci then raised the question: "As for Nanquan speaking in such a manner, was it an affirmative statement or a non-affirmative one?
Wuzu Yan said: "The three men are the Samādhi of the Wisdom Torch and the Samādhi of the King of Adornment."
Jianfu Xingyun said: "Among these three, there are those who can see the National Teacher and those who cannot.
If anyone can discern this, I grant that you possess the 'eye on the crown of the head.'"
Nanhuang Bing said: "Discerning the melody when the strings are moved belongs to Magu Guizong; seizing the drum and capturing the flag is especially appropriate for the old fellow Nanquan.
It reaches the point where those who travel together do not walk in step, and where one sides with principle rather than kin.
Where the white clouds end, there is the green mountain; the traveler is further beyond the green mountain."
Tiantong Jue said: "If I had been there at that time, I would have immediately wiped away the circle.
Not only would this have smashed Nanquan’s old nest, it would have left Guizong with nowhere to stand. Magu would have been unable to display his wits.
When Nanquan said, 'In that case, I shall not go,' it was indeed so, indeed so."
Tianbao Shu said: "The three great elders display such skillful means on the road; yet, as for seeing the National Teacher, it will not happen even in a donkey’s year.
Zhongfeng Ben said: "Nanquan draws lines in the earth to make a prison; Guizong falls into pits and ravines; Magu [bows]."
Yet they lack propriety. To examine them closely: one person’s eyes look down upon the four seas with utter emptiness; another’s tongue reaches up to support the Brahma Heaven;
and another enters hell as swiftly as a flying arrow.
Daweilun said: "These three fellows devised a ruse to withdraw midway, thinking they had gained the upper hand.
Yet, in the final analysis, a thousand explanations are not equal to a single seeing."
Xiaoyan Bao said: "Before the three men had even set foot on the road, their nostrils were already in the hands of National Teacher Zhong.
Even when they reached the midpoint of the journey, they were seen to be merely playing with the 'fragrance of rice gruel.'"
Xiuyun of Qingshan said: "Although these three great elders were born from the same root, they did not die upon the same branch;

each has his own path of departure. Yet, among these three men, there is one who is worthy to serve as a teacher and model. If anyone can discern him, I grant that you possess the eye that discriminates the Dharma."
New clouds appear in the sky. One person buys a hat to fit his head; another takes a mistake as a success;
another looks at the tower and strikes the tower; yet there is one more person whose forehead breaks into a sweat.
Baoguangyuan said: "As for these three fellows who play with lumps of mud, it is certainly impossible for them to see the National Teacher.
Yet when the Old Master called out to them, they immediately turned back. Now tell me, what was the meaning of this?"
When Nanquan was staying in a hermitage, a monk arrived. Nanquan said to him, "I am going up the mountain to do some work;

when it is time for the meal, please cook rice and eat it yourself, then send a portion back. The monk cooked the rice, ate it, and then smashed all the cooking utensils at once before lying down on his bed.
Nanquan waited for him to return and did not come, so he went back to the hermitage. Seeing the monk lying there, Nanquan also lay down beside him.
He lay down on his side, and the monk then rose and departed. Later, Quan said, "When I previously lived in a hermitage, there was a very clever practitioner;
even until now, I have not seen him again."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said, "This too is a poor man thinking of his old debts.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "These two fellows have not reached the village in front nor the inn behind."
Gao Feng said, "Although Nanquan was indeed solidly grounded at every step, he could not avoid following others in their rising and falling.
Even if this monk were capable of eating his fill and sleeping soundly, he would certainly not know that rice is made from grain.
If there be even a single word of falsehood in Gao Feng’s announcement, may I fall forever into the Hell of the Tongue-Tearing Plow."
Tongxuan Qi said: "This monk travels on pilgrimage in such a manner that even in the year of the donkey he will find no place to stay.
Nanquan receives him in such a way that he is truly a man of immeasurable capacity; yet, alas, both parties are not without their mutual frustration."
Yuan'an Yu said: "It is a pity that this monk has vanished without a trace. At that time, his dignified bearing was truly lovely.
After Nanquan passed away, one longs for a gentleman; seeing him so late, it is too late. Why did he not, upon coming down the mountain at that moment, dig a pit and bury this monk?
Would that not have settled the matter once and for all? At that time, there was a monk who said: [He would have been buried alive.]
The old man said, "Listen! Give him a hot stick and drive him out through the mountain gate.
Chengshan Jia said, "Nanquan, under a clear sky and bright day, there are not a few thieves.
Although this monk’s skills are excellent, alas, he has plunged deep into the net of another's house."
Yun’an Yue said: "Although Nanquan possessed the mechanism for trapping a tiger, he nonetheless did not exhaustively perfect his skill.
Had I been there at that time, upon seeing him smash the cooking utensils and sleep soundly on his pillow, I would have simply laughed loudly, 'He-he!'"
"I shall certainly kill this man with doubt.
Nanquan sent a letter to Zhunyu, saying: "Principle changes according to phenomena; vastness is not external. When phenomena accord with principle, they are harmonized."
A monk asked, "What is 'the silent solitude that is not internal'? After Daosheng finished writing his letter, he asked Zhuyu, "What is 'the vast expanse that is not external'?

Zhuyu said, "To ask one and receive a hundred answers is no hindrance. The monk then asked, "What is 'the silent solitude that is not internal'? Zhuyu said, "To perceive through forms and sounds is not the mark of a skilled hand.
The monk further asked Changsha, "What is 'the vast expanse that is not external'? Changsha stared at him with wide-open eyes.
"How is it that 'solitude is not within'? Sha closed his eyes and stared at him. The monk asked again, "How is it that 'vastness is not without'?
Zhaozhou made the gesture of eating a meal. "How is it that 'solitude is not within'? Zhaozhou made the gesture of wiping his mouth with his hand.
Upon hearing this, Shishuang said, "These three men are not falsely claiming to be my disciples."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Although Nanquan had the karmic conditions for raising these sons, alas, he loved his children so much that he failed to notice their ugliness.
He did not realize that among these three men, one has eyes but no feet, one has feet but no eyes, and one has neither feet nor eyes.
Nevertheless, all three could serve as teachers to Nanquan. Why is this so?"
This is clear in both principle and fact.
Nanquan ascended the hall and said: "Master Wang has raised a water buffalo since childhood. If I intend to pasture it on the east bank of the stream..."

One cannot avoid infringing upon the water and grass belonging to another king; if one intends to graze on the west bank of the stream, one still cannot avoid infringing upon the water and grass belonging to another king.
It would be better to accept things as they are, bit by bit, for in doing so, nothing at all is seen.
Yunmen Wenyan said: "Tell me, does the ox enter within or does it enter without?
Even if you can explain clearly where it enters, I still wish to ask you: where is the ox to be found?"
Guishan Zhe said, "Yunmen only knows how to seek out the ox, but he does not know how to pierce its nostrils.
He took up his staff and said, "The nostrils of the Buddhas of the three periods and all the old monks under heaven have all been pierced at once by this mountain monk’s staff.
Now tell me, where are the nostrils of this mountain monk? After a long silence, he said, "To slander another—"
"Add offense to offense.
Changqing Ling said, "Tell me, does Nanquan act for others before him or after him?
Xuedou Xian said, "He pierces them through both at once."

Yunfeng Yue said: "What need is there to speak of 'a mere trifle'? The entire universe—earth and sky, form and emptiness, light and darkness, the sentient and the insentient—is all here within this mountain monk. If one lets go, there is a place to follow conditions;
if one holds fast, there is no door for escape. Now tell me: is letting go better, or is holding fast better?"
Zhaojue Qin said: "Harmonizing with light and following things, mingling with the dust of the world;

not striking against sharp edges, yet possessing mastery over gathering and releasing—this is Nanquan’s fundamental fodder. Since my youth, I have raised a water buffalo. Sometimes it stands alone on a solitary peak;
sometimes it moves freely through the bustling marketplace. Regardless of whether it is east of the stream or west of the stream, it always..."
"Breaking the dust, piercing the bullseye. But tell me, where is it right now? Try looking with your own eyes. Tiantong Jie said:
"Nanquan set up the mold and drew the pattern; Changqing sifted through the sand to pick out gold;
Yunmen’s nostrils were already pierced; Xuedou handed down the verdict based on the facts. He held up his staff and said: "There is yet another one—where is he?"
"Where is it? he asked, and then cast down his staff.
Lingyin Yue said, "The Old Teacher Wang has indeed emptied his guts and turned over his belly, yet I have not seen him change the customs or transform the ways.
This mountain monk, however, has raised but a single donkey, which has been falling to the east and staggering to the west all along, following the times."
The sun travels more than a thousand li in a day, yet when it is twisted, it does not move even an inch. Tell me, how far is this from the water buffalo of Master Wang?
After a long silence, he said: "The fisherman dances his oars; the rustic old man sings his song."
Tiantong Jue said: "Nanquan’s 'Herding the Ox' may indeed be called extraordinary;
it is simply that at every point there is no way to block or guard against it. Why is this so? It is because he accepts whatever comes his way."
Baoneng Xiu said: "Nanquan’s water buffalo has no nostrils; how will you, you lot, thread it through?
Therefore, the Elder Shengmo said: "Identical with all things in every respect, yet nowhere can it be contained.
But tell me, after one has accepted a little according to one's lot, what then? Even the weeds and chaff worry about being weeded out.
Regarding the place where the hooves, horns, skin, and hair are pursued for profit, Gu Nanmen said:
"Nanquan only knew how to seek people while falling into the weeds; alas, he recklessly produced horns and head.
This led all the great masters to roll about in the weeds. Without attaining a state of absolute purity, do you still see Nanquan?"
"Is it at the place where the spring is cast aside? To offer this body and mind to every dust mote and land—this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.
Yúán of Yú'ān said: "Now tell me, does this still belong to the east stream or the west stream?
Only if this ox would neither chew a single blade of grass nor drink a single drop of water could it be so. Even if one were to lead it away to another realm..."
"Outside the world, can one still emerge from the king's territory and soil? I beg Master Wang to settle this for us.
While Nanquan was inspecting the hall, he led an ox into the hall. The Head Seat patted the ox’s back once with his hand.
Nanquan then ceased speaking. Zhaozhou then placed two bundles of straw before the Head Seat.
Guoqing Ying said: "Zhaozhou and Nanquan were very much like those who sell Yangzhou goods from within their own house; for the Head Seat to act in such a manner is truly 'knowing the rites'!"
A monk asked Nanquan, "Why did the hundred birds carry flowers to offer to Niutou before he had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
Nanquan said, "Because he was treading the steps of the Buddha at every step. The monk asked, "Why did they not come after he had seen him?
Nanquan said, "Even if they had not come, they would still have been one thread's breadth inferior to Old Wang."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "Nanquan only understands climbing higher step by step; he does not understand letting go from the void.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is 'climbing higher step by step'? Yunmen said, "The World of Fragrant Accumulation.
The monk asked, "What is 'letting go from the void'? Yunmen said, "Filling the ditches and blocking the ravines."
When Nanquan saw Deng Yinfeng approaching, he pointed to a water pitcher and said, "The pitcher is an object;
you must not touch the object. Bring me some water. Yinfeng took the pitcher and poured water before Nanquan, whereupon Nanquan ceased speaking.
Guizong Chang said, "Deng Yinfeng was also pouring it out in confusion.
Shengfafa said, "Deng Yinfeng still lacks one more blow. Nanquan said, "I will stop now;
Boya and Ziqi were no ordinary acquaintances. Now, as for Guizong speaking thus, tell me: does he approve of him?
This was not an acceptance of the other.
Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying, "In Jiangxi, Mazu says 'this very mind is Buddha. I, Old Man Wang, do not speak thus.
It is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing. In speaking thus, is there any fault? Zhaozhou came forward and bowed.
Having prostrated, he departed. A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What was the meaning of the Senior Monk's departure after his prostration?
Zhaozhou said, "You should ask the Master instead. The monk then asked Nanquan, "What was the meaning of the Senior Monk Shen's [Zhaozhou's] departure just now?"
Quan said, "He indeed grasped the old monk’s meaning.
Huanglong Xin said, "When the ancients spoke thus, it was like looking at a leopard through a tube; one sees but a single spot."
Even if one enters a forest without stirring the grass or enters water without disturbing the waves, it is still like riding a horse across the edge of ice.
If you possess the hand of one who shoots down a vulture, why not rub an itch on the head of a snake? Those who have passed through the barrier, try to discern this!
After a long silence, he said: "The embroidered mandarin ducks emerge from the golden needle."
Jingshan Daokai said: "Though these two old fellows are adept at moving their fingers inside their boots, they fail to realize that the bystander is the one who looks ugly.
Tianning Weiqing said: "Nanquan and Zhaozhou were both brought to account by this monk in a single indictment."
A monk once asked Nanquan, "Before one's parents were born, where was the nose?
Nanquan replied, "After one's parents are born, where is the nose?"
Guoqing Ying said: "When going, his nostrils reach the heavens; when coming, his feet tread upon solid ground.
Why then does he seek someone’s permission? After a long silence, he said: "Were it not for Yang Deyi, who would have seen Ma Xiangru?"
While Nanquan was gazing at the moon, a monk said, "When will I come to be like this?
Nanquan replied, "I, Old Teacher Wang, also came this way twenty years ago. The monk then asked, "What is it now? Nanquan immediately returned to his quarters.
Tiantong Jue said: "Setting aside for a moment what was before twenty years ago, how about after twenty years?
Do you still know where Old Wang’s footsteps lie? There is no spirit-bed in the inner chamber; the whole family does not wear mourning."
Zimei said, "Zhou Yun, here at Leping, we do not care whether it is twenty years before or twenty years after.
But what about this very night of the fifteenth day of the eighth month? After a long silence, he said, "Better to cut out one's tongue."
One must not violate the national taboo [of the master’s name].
One day Nanquan did not go to the hall. The attendant said, "Please, Master, come to the hall.
Nanquan said, "This old monk has already eaten his fill of oil-cakes at the manor today. The attendant said, "The Master has not gone out. Nanquan said, "You do not understand."
The attendant went to inquire of the master of the estate. Just as he was coming out, he suddenly saw the master of the estate, who said, "Thank you, Venerable Monk, for visiting our estate.
Jingshan Gao remarked: "The Venerable Monk did not attend the hall; the master of the estate thanked him for the honor of his visit. One character entering the gate of officialdom—"

Beneath Nanquan Mountain there was a master of a hermitage. Someone said to him, "The Master Nanquan has recently appeared in the world. Why..."
He did not go to pay his respects. The Master said, "It is not only Nanquan; even if a thousand Buddhas were to appear in the world, I would still not go.
When Nanquan heard this, he ordered Zhaozhou to go and investigate him. Upon seeing the Master, Zhaozhou immediately prostrated himself. The Master paid no attention.
Zhaozhou moved from west to east and then from east to west, yet the Master still paid him no heed. Zhaozhou said, "The grass-robber has been utterly defeated," and then dragged him down.
Lianzi then returned and related this to Linquan. Linquan said, "I have always suspected this fellow.
The next day, Linquan took a novice monk with him, carrying a bottle of tea and three cups, and went to the hermitage. He threw them onto the ground and said, "Yesterday's!
Yesterday's! The Master asked, "What was it about yesterday? Linquan struck the novice on the back once.
The one below said, "You’ve deceived me! You’ve deceived me! and brushed his sleeves, turning back immediately.
Xuedou Xian said, "Great as they were, Nanquan and Zhaozhou were both exposed by this fellow with a shoulder-board."
Taisuī Zhe said, "The hermitage master sits watching for success or failure; how great are Nanquan and Zhaozhou, yet they meet with a fall upon the pure ground!
Zhikai Heo said, "It is so, but the hermitage master only knows how to hold fast to the boundaries; he cannot share in life."
They died together. At that time, Zhaozhou prostrated himself and simply said, "This thief—I know you.
He waited for him to go from east to west or from west to east, and then he would have dragged his staff and driven him out.
Let us see what other skill Zhaozhou had.
Ou-feng Cheng said: "Tell me, where is it that the 'board-carrying fellow' (the one who carries a wooden board) exposes the flaws of Nanquan and Zhaozhou?
If one were a monk with clear eyes, it would not be difficult to expose the flaws of Xuedou right here."

Qinglong said: "The two venerable masters, Panshan and Ciming, seem much like those who borrow the prestige of a noble house to falsely inflate their reputation;
as for the path above, they still could not bring it forth. Today, Bianshan intends to present it face-to-face to you all. He then threw down his staff and said, "Look! Look!"
Jinxian Can said: "The two great elders, Panshan and Ciming— one with a tight throat and lips,
the other with wide teeth and tongue— though each established their own school, viewed from the perspective of the true eye, neither has yet trodden the upward path."

Fochuan’s commentary states: "While the various masters of past and present have not lacked merit in their manner of upholding the Dharma, if one wishes to penetrate the path that transcends all, one must wait until the year of the donkey."
Guangjiao Yuyu said: "The path that goes beyond is sixty kalpas for three lifetimes.
Haimen Yongyun said: "Originally there is a single, straight great road; yet it is pointed out by these many ancient sages, whereby it instead becomes circuitous.
This causes those who are utterly exhausted to lose their way from the place of treasure."—Haimen.
"How can we simply sit by idly? Today I shall cause each and every one of them to return home along the very path they have traveled.
Thereupon, he suddenly overturned the meditation seat and went straight back to the abbot’s quarters.
Panshan addressed the assembly: "The moon of the mind is solitary and perfect; its light swallows the myriad phenomena. The light does not illuminate objects, nor do objects exist.
When both light and objects are forgotten, what is it then?"
Dongshan Liangjie said, "If the luminous realm has not yet been forgotten, what else could it be?
Yunmen Wenyan said, "Even if you were to act in such a way, you would still be halfway; this is not yet the path of total transcendence.
He asked, "What is the path of total transcendence? After a long silence, he said, "Tiantai Huading."
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "A white egret descends to the field—a thousand points of snow; a yellow oriole perches on a tree—a single branch of blossoms.
Qinghua Yuan shook his staff and gave a shout, saying: "When a character is transcribed three times, the 'crow' becomes a 'horse.'"
Xuedou said this and that. These two fellows are much like Xu Liu carrying a single plank—seeing only one side.
Each deserves twenty blows of the staff. If you wish to uphold the matter handed down from of old, then proceed with caution.
"East is the bright mirror; when light and object are both forgotten, what is it then? He lets out a shout and says, "What is this?
When light and object have not yet been forgotten, what is it then? He then raises his whisk and says, "What do you call this thing?
Again, he lets out a shout.

Baoshan ascended the hall and said, "Virtuous Chan practitioners, you may study the Way within this: it is like the earth supporting a mountain, yet not knowing that the mountain is fundamentally solitary and steep;
or like a stone containing jade, yet not knowing that the jade is inherently flawless. If you can act in this manner, you are truly a renunciant."
Xuedou Xian said: "Walking three thousand miles by day and eight hundred by night—this is what I habitually employ;
set that aside for a moment. In what place do you all perceive Panshan?"
Jingshan Hongdao said: "If one can do so, it is like pressing on the eyes until flowers appear.
Cuiyan Zhongzhe said: "For you all, it is easy to see Panshan, but difficult to see Jingshan."
Lingyan said, "With eyes open, it is right; with eyes closed, it is right. Where is there that is not Panshan?
After a long silence, he gave a shout and said, "Drowsy fellows! Are you awake yet?"
Panshan addressed the assembly: "O virtuous practitioners of Chan! It is like casting a sword through the air: one need not deliberate over whether it reaches its mark or not.

This is because the wheel of emptiness leaves no trace and the edge of the blade remains unimpaired. If you can thus maintain a mind-moment after mind-moment that is free from knowing, then the whole mind is the Buddha, and the whole Buddha is the person.
When there is no distinction between person and Buddha, only then have you attained the Way."
Jingshan Hongzhi, under the phrase "In mind after mind there is no knowing," said: "Tsk! Tsk! Within the treasury of our King, there is no such blade.
Yufan Yuanwu said: "If one speaks of a patch-robed monk of true substance, there truly is no such blade; if one speaks of true substance..."

"Monks, there truly is such a sword. A monk laughed derisively from the side and said, "Have you not seen Panshan say that those who study the Way exhaust their bodies like a monkey grasping at a reflection in water? Yunmen said, "Tsk! I knew you were sitting in a ghost cave."
As Panshan was about to pass away, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Is there anyone who can capture my true likeness?
The assembly presented the portraits they had produced, but none were satisfactory. At that time, Puhua stepped forward and said, "I have captured it.
Panshan asked, "Why do you not present it to this old monk? Puhua then performed a backflip and departed. Panshan remarked, "This fellow will later go completely mad."
He was away when he suddenly passed away.
Baofu Zhan said, "Puhua’s antics were no small matter; Panshan’s ugliness and clumsiness were even more so.
Changlu Liao shook his body and said, "What joy! What joy! If one did not possess the eye that pierces through heaven and earth, [one would not understand this].
"Kong! How can one see the unrefined gold and raw jade? He spoke again: "I, this mountain monk, have modeled a copy after the likeness of Puhua.
Tonight I shall unfold it so that the great assembly may gaze upon it. Thereupon, he performed a somersault and returned to the hall.
Qixia Chengyun said: "If this were Master Linji, not even a single one of thirty blows would have been spared.
Fortunately, we encountered Panshan, who let him off. But tell me, where did that blow land?
If you say 'right across the spine,' I shall know you are striking blindly and acting recklessly."
Guoqing Ying said: "Tut, tut, tut! One person transmits what is empty; ten thousand people transmit it as real.
When Panshan first went to study, one day he went out the gate and saw someone performing a funeral.
The cantor shook his bell and sang: 'The red wheel is certain to sink to the west; I do not know where the soul has gone. Beneath the curtain, the filial son wailed: 'Alas, alas!'"
Shanhu’s body and mind suddenly leaped with joy. He returned and related this to Mazu, who gave his seal of approval. Yunju Zhuang said:
"One who acts as a teacher of men must possess the eye that penetrates the barrier; he must distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, and examine the capacity of those who come to him.
For instance, Panshan took that which is 'brightly manifest and spiritually alert' to be the ultimate principle. Master Mazu, from [the beginning]..."
To grant such approval would surely be to betray the former sages and deceive future generations.
If there were such a person here among my monks, they would certainly have a different way of life. But tell me, what kind of life is it?
"The embroidered mandarin ducks are for you to behold; I do not hand the golden needle over to anyone."
Chan Master Magu Baoche of Puzhou (the second successor of Mazu in the South) went to Linji and asked, "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Mahākaruṇika, which one is the true eye?
Linji grabbed him and said, "Regarding the thousand hands and eyes of Mahākaruṇika, what is the true eye?"
"Quick way! Quick way! Gu shouted as he pulled Jie down from his meditation seat and sat back down himself. Jie asked after him, saying, "I hope you have been well.
Gu hesitated, whereupon Jie gave a shout. Gu pulled Jie down from the meditation seat and sat back down again; Gu then went out.
Master Shengying said, "Virtuous practitioners of Zen, these two venerable masters were like this. Now tell me, what was their intention? People today all speak of 'illumination' and 'function.
What kind of bowl are they illuminating? Everyone only knows how to mount their own horse to pursue the thief, or take up their own sword to kill the thief.
These two men, however, were able to seize the thief’s horse and capture the thief. He seized [the meaning].
"The thief's sword kills the thief. Although it is thus, Linji gained the advantage, yet he lost the advantage.

Yangshan Qin said, "When these two great elders engage in such vigorous debate, although hundreds and thousands of hands and eyes are revealed all at once, how can they avoid being both blind men? Tell me, is there anyone who can discern this?"
"Dima! Xie! Tianning Qi said:
"The two elders, guest and host, exchanging roles and wielding power and restraint, are truly worth observing—like a fierce flame burning through the sky or a sudden thunderclap shaking the earth.
Nevertheless, what connection does this have with the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion?"
"Only the surging waves are seen; the Dragon Palace of the Sea is nowhere to be found. An Guocong said:
"Striking the joints and knocking at the gates, charging through towers and leaping over hearths; pushing and prodding one another, their mastery of seizing and releasing transcends the crowd.
One must admit these two elders were skilled hands. But if we speak of the True Eye of Great Compassion, they have not even dreamed of it for donkey-years."
Magu went to Zhangjing’s quarters; he circumambulated the meditation seat three times, struck his monk’s staff once, and stood there upright.
Zhangjing said, "So it is, so it is. He then went to Nanquan; he circumambulated the meditation seat three times, struck his monk’s staff once, and stood there upright.
Jianquan said, "It is not so, it is not so. Guishan said, "Zhangjing says it is so; why does the Master say it is not?
Jianquan said, "Zhangjing is indeed right, but you are not. This is turned by the power of the wind; in the end, it returns to decay."

Baofu Zhan said in his parting words: "He simply shook his mendicant's staff once and departed. He further commented:
"Zhangjing and Nanquan may be called one right and one wrong. He also said: "Magu’s [chant] was faintly like a melody just fit to hear, yet it was blown by the wind into another tune."
Yunju Xi said: "Zhangjing did not necessarily say it was right; Nanquan did not necessarily say it was wrong. He further said:
"At that time, it would have been perfectly appropriate for Magu simply to take his staff and walk out."
Xuedou Xian, acting on behalf of Magu, said "Wrong" to both the "is" and the "is not.
Yangqi Fanghui said, "Zhangjing’s 'is' falls within Magu’s trap; Nanquan’s 'is not' [falls within it as well]."
They, too, have fallen into Mazu’s trap. Daowei was not like this:

suppose someone were to take up his staff, circumambulate the meditation seat three times, snap the staff once, and stand there with a sudden, resolute presence; one should simply say to him, "If you had not yet reached this state, I would give you thirty blows."
Letan Qingyun said: "Even if Zhangjing says 'it is,' he deserves thirty blows of the staff.
Even if Nanquan says 'it is not,' he also deserves thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because whether it 'is' or 'is not,' the wondrous meaning is fully revealed;
both Zhangjing and Nanquan have suffered a defeat."
Shengmo Guang said: "This 'is' cannot be 'is'; this 'non-is' is truly not 'non-is. This 'is' and 'non-is' have no master; all myriad virtues return to the same source.
While the owl and the cock struggle in vain through day and night with their fragmented distinctions, I lack even three inches [of tongue], yet the turtle can call out to the tortoise.
Kāśyapa did not consent; let him do as he pleases, knitting his brows."
Tianning Qisong said: "Circumambulating the meditation seat and shaking the mendicant's staff are the constant rituals for paying respects.
Why is it that Zhangjing says 'yes' while Nanquan says 'no'? Bitter gourds are bitter from root to tip; sweet melons are sweet from stem to blossom."
Qixia Chengyun said: "If you do not enter the tiger’s den, how can you get the tiger’s cub? Some say that Magu had his eyesight stolen by Nanquan;
what they fail to realize is that Nanquan was nearly crushed by Magu, almost as if he were about to break open Caizhou.
Xuedou’s two instances of "mistakes" only managed to save half of it.
Boshan Lai said: "Zhangjing says it is so; Xuedou says it is wrong; Nanquan says it is not so.
What room is there for such talk? Only Magu’s staff has a bit more substance."
One day Magu was sitting inside his curtain, covering his head with a handkerchief. When Master Piyun came, he entered, saw him, and immediately made a sound of wailing.
After a long while, he went out onto the Dharma Hall, circled the meditation seat once, and re-entered.
He pulled back the curtain and saw that Magu had removed the handkerchief and was sitting there. He then said, "To find life within death—there is not one in ten thousand. Magu [nodded].
He then descended from his seat, took his place, and drew out his sitting mat. Yun approached him, seized him by the collar, and said, "Dead before, alive after—do you still find this agreeable?
Gu said, "It is agreeable; what can you do, Master? Yun pushed him aside and said, "I knew that your former words did not accord with your latter ones."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Entering the temple, one looks at the plaque; seeing the surface, one knows the interior.
Having long been accustomed to being a distinguished guest amidst the clouds, he takes the tail for the head and takes the head for the tail. Under Magu Mengchang’s gate, observe his responses:

it was not that he did not know [the ultimate], but rather because his application of effort was too deep. At that time, had he waited until [the Master] said, 'To find life within death is ten thousandfold...'"
Not one [word] was spoken in between. He sighed, "Alas! Alas! Why? Because he had received an ox from one person and returned a horse to another.
While Magu was fanning himself, a monk asked, "The nature of wind is eternally abiding; it is all-pervasive. Why, Master, do you..."
[The monk] then shook his fan. Gu said, "You only know that the nature of wind is ever-present; you do not yet know that it is all-pervasive.
The monk asked, "What is the principle of its being all-pervasive? Gu then shook his fan. The monk bowed. Gu said, "Useless monk!
Even if you were to wear a thousand [fans], what benefit would there be?"
Zhaojue Qin said: "This monk’s single performance was worth watching; it is a pity he had a beginning but no end.
Had it not been for Magu being a master of the Way, he would have surely let him off the hook. I dare ask you all: where did this monk fail?
How many people are there who can discern the upward-opening aperture?"
Guo of Mount Gui said: "This monk only knew how to bow his forehead to the ground; he did not realize he had missed the mark right before his own face.
Had the order been carried out at that moment, where else would one have to search for Magu?"

Chan Master Ruhui of Dongsi Temple in Tanzhou (the first-generation successor of Mazu, the third in the Southern Lineage) was visited by Yangshan, who came to attend upon him. The Master asked, "Where are you from?
Yangshan replied, "I am a man from Guangnan. The Master said, "I have heard that there is a 'Taming Pearl' in Guangnan; is this true?"
Mount Yunmen said, “It is this. Baizhang asked, “What about this pearl? Yunmen said, “In the dark moon it is hidden; in the bright moon it appears.
Baizhang asked, “Can you bring it back here? Yunmen said, “I can bring it back. Baizhang said, “Why then do you not present it to this old monk?
Yunmen joined his palms, stepped forward, and said, “Yesterday when I arrived at Mount Mui, I was also asked for this pearl, and I was left with nothing to say in response.”
There was room for further argument. The Temple Master said, "A true lion cub; you are well able to roar.
Zhaojue Qin said, "Dongshan asked for but a single grain, while Yangshan poured out an entire basket."
Tianning Qi said: "Although Yangshan was indeed a lion cub, how could he bear to sell the 'Bright Pearl that Subdues the Sea' for a mere pea?
For all eternity, he will be scrutinized by others. Today, this mountain monk sides with principle rather than kin;
even if Dongsi himself were to arrive, he must first pass the examination before receiving a blow."
Dongshan Ying said: "Yangshan treasures this within his chest; let him be a skilled merchant and sell it.
It is a pity that Dongsi was dazzled by the radiance of that pearl, which left him with a dragon's head but a snake's tail.
If I were Dongsi, I would simply call my attendant and say, 'Quickly bring the dustpan and broom!'"
Baiyan Fu said: "Zhenghai’s bright pearl is indeed held firmly in Mount Yang’s grasp;
yet he cannot avoid being dragged down by it and defiled by others. At that time, when asked whether it could still be recovered, one should have replied:
'I have already cast it onto a heap of refuse. If he had further said, 'A true lion cub is truly capable...'"
He let out a roar and, covering his ears with his hands, went straight out. It is certain that he could not wait for the East Temple to arrange its bright windows.

Zen Master Zhizang of Xitang in Qianzhou (a successor in the third generation of the Southern Lineage and first generation of Mazu’s lineage) said during a communal work period: "Cause and effect are clearly manifest."
"What can be done? What can be done? At that moment, a monk came forward and propped up the floor with his hand.

The Hall Master asked, "What are you doing? The monk replied, "Save me! Save me! The Hall Master said, "Everyone, this monk is still somewhat better than others. The monk then shook out his sleeves and walked away.
The Hall Master remarked, "A worm within the lion’s body eats the lion’s own flesh."
Zhaojue Qin said: "The West Hall [monk] Dongming has grasped the essential principles; from beginning to end, he has fully upheld the orthodox command.
This monk acts like a beast among humans, yet he is like a dragon’s head with a snake’s tail. I dare ask the assembly: when cause and effect are clearly manifest, how do you speak this one phrase?
If it is so, the Dragon Girl suddenly attains Buddhahood; if it is not, Shanxing falls into the abyss."
Once, when Minister Li Ao asked a monk at Xitang, "What teachings did Master Mazu have?
the monk replied, "The Master sometimes said 'this very mind is Buddha,' and sometimes he said 'neither mind nor Buddha. Li Ao remarked, "He has passed entirely to that side."
One day he asked Daokai of the Hall, "What instructions did Master Mazu have? Daokai called out, "Li Ao! Li Ao responded.
Daokai said, "The drums and horns are sounding."
As Anzhang said: "Everyone says that Lord Li was the one who interrogated the monk, yet they fail to realize that Lord Li suffered a defeat right before that monk's eyes.

Furthermore, when he went to the West Hall to seek a resolution, he was pressed by the West Hall master until he had no way to turn his body. Is there anyone present now who can turn his body for him?"

"Come forth and meet with the staff of Ruan. As soon as the monk stepped out, Xiang suddenly said, "If you are not one who plays in the tide, do not enter the surging waves," and he immediately descended from his seat.
A monk asked Xitang, "When there is a question and an answer, the roles of host and guest are clearly distinguished; but what about when there is neither question nor answer?
Xitang said, "I am afraid it will rot right where it stands."

Changqing Ling was asked by a monk who cited a precedent: "When there is a question and an answer, the roles of guest and host are clearly defined. But when there is neither question nor answer, what then?
Changqing said, "Everyone says they will retire from office; yet among those beneath the forest trees, I have never seen a single person."
Xuedou Xian said, "Why not give him his proper fodder?
Nantang Yu said, "These two ancient Buddhas answered the dialogue in such a way that their fragrance may flow for a thousand ages;
yet, if one wishes to completely block the throats of the patch-robed monks, it still does not suffice. Tonight, if someone asks Lingyan: [what would you say?]
Question: When there is questioning and answering, the roles of host and guest are distinct. But how is it when there is neither question nor answer? Response: I tell you:
"The winter solstice to Cold Food Festival is one hundred and five days; the Lantern Festival is fixed for the fifteenth day of the first month."
Baiyan Fu said: "In this place there are no ten taels of gold; the common folk sell three sheng of wine.
Of whom are these two elders speaking? Xuedou said: "Why not give them their proper fodder? This too is merely covering one's ears while stealing a bell;
neither has reached the point of total eradication. [The Master] picks up his staff and says: "If someone here were to ask a question, there would be a question and an answer—host and guest."
It is clear. When there is neither question nor answer, how is it? [The Master] threw down his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Chan Master Changjing Huaiyun of Jingzhao (the third in the lineage of Mazu in the South) was sent by Baizhang with a monk to test him.
While waiting for Huaiyun to ascend the hall, the monk spread out his sitting cloth, bowed, and stood up; he then took one of Huaiyun’s sandals and brushed the dust off it with his sleeve.
Changjing turned it upside down and said, "The old monk has committed a transgression.

Huanglong Xin remarked, "Even if Baizhang had exhausted all his supernatural powers, they would not have been enough to dissolve Changjing’s statement that 'the old monk has committed a transgression.
Had he done so, [Baizhang's pride] would have melted away like ice and crumbled like a fortress."
Gushan Gui said: "Huanglong Mengbailang still lacks one move. He only knows that Baizhang displayed his supernatural powers;
he does not know that Baizhang’s skill was completely exhausted. He only knows that Zhangjing spoke of the old monk’s transgression;
he does not know that Zhangjing accepted the charge immediately. Do you understand? It may still be tolerable for a snake to swallow a shrimp, but furthermore—"

There was a centipede behind him. Chan Master Lingmo of Wuxie Mountain in Wuzhou (the second-generation successor of Mazu) went to visit Shitou and asked: "If our words accord with one another, I shall stay; if they do not, I shall depart. Shitou remained seated as usual. Lingmo then turned to leave. Shitou called out after him, "Dharma-heir! Lingmo stopped and turned back. Shitou said: "The centipede behind you has already been stepped on by you. Lingmo looked back and saw it; he bowed and departed. Later, he stayed at the mountain for many years. One day, while walking about, he suddenly leaped up and shouted, "Wu-xie! At that moment, he attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse: "Before my parents gave birth to me, I had already attained the Way. After my parents gave birth to me, I realized the Way once more. The Way is originally not difficult; It is simply that people overcomplicate it. He then returned to the mountain and lived there until his death. His dharma heirs were numerous, including the famous masters of the Five Houses. Among them, the most eminent was Master Xuefeng Yicun. Master Xuefeng was originally from Fuzhou; his secular surname was Lin. He first visited Baizhang, then Mazu, and finally stayed with Shitou. One day, while sitting in meditation, he suddenly heard the sound of a stone striking bamboo and attained great enlightenment. He then went to see Lingmo, who asked him, "Where have you come from? Xuefeng replied, "From the place where the Way is realized. Lingmo said, "What is the Way? Xuefeng said, "When I was just now sitting in meditation, I heard the sound of a stone striking bamboo. Lingmo said, "That is merely the sound of a stone striking bamboo. Xuefeng said, "Master, why do you deny the Way? Lingmo said, "How can you say that? You have fallen into a pit of doubt. Xuefeng was startled and left. That night, he went to the master's room and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Lingmo said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Xuefeng was greatly enlightened upon hearing this. He later resided at Xuefeng Mountain, where he gathered a large assembly. His dharma heirs included the famous masters Yunmen Wenyan and Deshan Xuanjian. Master Yunmen was originally from Quanzhou; his secular surname was Chen. He first visited Dongshan, then Caoshan, and finally stayed with Xuefeng. One day, while sweeping the grounds, he suddenly heard the sound of a tile striking a bamboo and attained great enlightenment. He then went to see Xuefeng, who asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Yunmen said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Xuefeng said, "You have already seen it. Yunmen said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "You have already seen it. Yunmen then bowed and withdrew. Later, he resided at Yunmen Mountain, where he gathered a large assembly. His dharma heirs included the famous masters Fayan Wenyi and Yangshan Huiji. Master Yangshan was originally from Hongzhou; his secular surname was Li. He first visited Guishan, then Nanquan, and finally stayed with Yunmen. One day, while sitting in meditation, he suddenly heard the sound of a bell and attained great enlightenment. He then went to see Yunmen, who asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Yangshan said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Yunmen said, "You have already seen it. Yangshan said, "I have already seen it. Yunmen said, "You have already seen it. Yangshan then bowed and withdrew. Later, he resided at Yangshan Mountain, where he gathered a large assembly. His dharma heirs included the famous masters Linji Yixuan and Huangbo Xiyun. Master Linji was originally from Fenzhou; his secular surname was Ji. He first visited Huangbo, then Nanquan, and finally stayed with Yangshan. One day, while sitting in meditation, he suddenly heard the sound of a dog barking and attained great enlightenment. He then went to see Yangshan, who asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Linji said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Yangshan said, "You have already seen it. Linji said, "I have already seen it. Yangshan said, "You have already seen it. Linji then bowed and withdrew. Later, he resided at Linji Temple, where he gathered a large assembly. His dharma heirs included the famous masters Danyuan Yingzhen and Xuefeng Yicun. Master Danyuan was originally from Fuzhou; his secular surname was Lin. He first visited Baizhang, then Mazu, and finally stayed with Linji. One day, while sitting in meditation, he suddenly heard the sound of a bird chirping and attained great enlightenment. He then went to see Linji, who asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Danyuan said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Linji said, "You have already seen it. Danyuan said, "I have already seen it. Linji said, "You have already seen it. Danyuan then bowed and withdrew. Later, he resided at Danyuan Mountain, where he gathered a large assembly. His dharma heirs included the famous masters Xuefeng Yicun and Yunju Daoying. Master Yunju was originally from Fuzhou; his secular surname was Lin. He first visited Baizhang, then Mazu, and finally stayed with Danyuan. One day, while sitting in meditation, he suddenly heard the sound of a wind chime and attained great enlightenment. He then went to see Danyuan, who asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Yunju said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Danyuan said, "You have already seen it. Yunju said, "I have already seen it. Danyuan said, "You have already seen it. Yunju then bowed and withdrew. Later, he resided at Yunju Mountain, where he gathered a large assembly. His dharma heirs included the famous masters Fayan Wenyi and Yangshan Huiji. Thus, the lineage of the Southern School flourished, spreading throughout the land like a forest of cypress trees. Each master, through their own realization, transmitted the Dharma, ensuring that the true teaching would never perish. This is the essence of the Zen tradition: direct pointing to the human mind, seeing into one's own nature, and attaining Buddhahood. It is not a matter of intellectual speculation or scriptural study, but of personal experience and realization. As the ancients said: "A single word, and the whole universe is revealed; a single phrase, and all dharmas are exhausted. This is the spirit of the Zen school, which continues to inspire practitioners to this day.
Xie turned his head back. Daohou said, "From birth until death, it is only this very thing. Why do you turn your head and look back?
At these words, Xie attained great enlightenment; he then snapped his staff in two and settled there.
Dongshan Jia said, "At that time, had it not been for our late teacher Wuxie, it would have been very difficult to uphold [the Dharma].
Nevertheless, even so, there was still a journey yet to be traversed."
Changqing Ling said, "Perilous.
Baoci then questioned him, saying, "Where is it that he still traverses the path? Tell me, what was Dongshan’s intention?"
Yunfeng Yue said: "Big and small Stonehead cannot sit still and cannot hold on. They are like those fellows who carry a single board;
having let them go, they immediately call them back. Having been deluded by him for a while, they say, 'I have attained enlightenment here.
When will such people ever see a dream [of truth]?"
Tangshan Xing said: "If Wuye had left immediately at that time, he would have cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven.
But because he was called back by others, he was not a little muddled. Even if one were to snap his staff in two, it would still be like drawing a bow after the thief has fled.
Now, let gain and loss, right and wrong, be all cut off at once. I dare ask the assembly: [What about] Shitou?"
As he sat, [Master] En asked, "What was the meaning of this?
Dizang En said, "At that time, Wuxie should have simply gone away like that; he should not have come back like this.
Chan Master Baizhang Weizheng of Hongzhou (the second successor of Mazu in the South) asked Nanquan, "Do the spiritual friends of all quarters still..."
"Is there no teaching that does not resemble a person? He replied, "There is. Baizhang asked, "What is this teaching that does not resemble a person?
He replied, "It is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing. Baizhang said, "If that is so, then you have described it as resembling a person.
He replied, "I am indeed like that; but what about you, Master? Baizhang said, "Neither am I."
"Good friend, how could one know whether there is a teaching that is spoken or not? The monk said, "I do not understand; I pray the Master will explain it.
The Master said, "I have already explained it to you to my utmost."
Taisuī Zhe said: "Baizhang only knew how to look forward and did not know how to look back.

At that time, had he waited for the other to say, 'I do not understand,' and simply replied, 'I, the old monk, also do not understand,' then Baizhang would have established himself as a master not only for Nanquan, but as a master for all people under heaven."
Tianqishen said: "These two fellows, when they grasp the head they lose the tail, and when they grasp the tail they lose the head;

they provoke the laughter and derision of those everywhere. Since there is a Dharma that cannot be spoken, tell me: does it still permit you to engage in the question-and-answer exchange between host and guest?
Even if you were able to scrutinize it thoroughly, you would find yourself with no way to advance or retreat. To boast further of its subtlety is only to become increasingly intolerable."
"What do you all do when you arrive here? "Please each return to the hall; take care.
One day, while Baizhang was on the road, he encountered an imperial messenger who invited him to a meal. By chance, a donkey brayed. The messenger said, "Dhūta," and Baizhang raised his head.
The messenger then pointed at the donkey, and Baizhang pointed back at the messenger. The messenger was speechless.
Baofu Zhan said, "Bazhang celebrated with a feast.
Fayan Yi spoke differently, saying, "Just make the bray of a donkey.
Zhiti Ai said, "When one family has business, a hundred families are busy."
Chan Master Daoheng of Mingxi in Liuzhou (the second-generation successor of Mazu in the South) once said: "I have a great illness that cannot be cured by worldly physicians.
Later, when a monk asked Caoshan Benji, "The ancients said, 'I have a great illness that cannot be cured by worldly physicians. I do not know—"
"What kind of illness is this? Shanshan said, "It is the illness that cannot be gathered together. [The monk] asked, "Do all sentient beings also have this illness?
Shanshan said, "Everyone has it. [The monk] asked, "Does the Master also have this illness? Shanshan said, "I do."
Shan said, "I am precisely seeking the place where it arises, but I cannot find it. [The monk] asked, "Why then do all sentient beings not fall ill?
Shan said, "If all sentient beings were to fall ill, they would no longer be sentient beings. [The monk] asked, "I wonder, do the Buddhas also have this illness?
Shan said, "They do. [The monk] asked, "Since they have it, why do they not fall ill? Shan said, "It is because they are awake."
Xing. Yufan Yu added: "I have a great illness that can be cured by one thing. Tell me, what is this thing?
If you can bring it forth, you may be considered a fellow student with me at Xiaoxi."
Chan Master Zongyin of Sanjiaoshan in Tanzhou (the second-generation successor of Mazu Daoyi) ascended the hall and said:
"If one discusses this matter, by the time you even blink your eyebrows, you have already missed it. At that moment, Magu asked: "I do not ask about blinking the eyebrows."
"What is this matter? Jue said, "You have missed it. Gu then overturned the meditation seat, and Jue struck him.
Baofu Zhan said, "Jue was like drawing a bow after the thief has already fled."
Xuedou Xian said, "These two fellows have heads but no tails. Before their eyebrows have even blinked, how can you say they have missed this matter?
Later, a monk asked, "Why do the eyebrows not blink? Xuedou struck him.
Zhaojue Qin said: "To call this 'this matter' is already like gouging a sore on top of healthy flesh;
how much more so to say that as soon as one raises one's eyebrows, one has already missed it. Mazu and Xuedou are indeed like drawing a bow after the thief has fled, but there is yet another.
Suddenly seizing his staff, he descended from the seat.
The *Tianbao Shu* says: "When these two great elders exchange verses in this manner, it is no less than thunderclaps and rolling lightning, rocks splitting and cliffs collapsing.
Yet, as for this matter, there are ten thousand miles of white clouds."
Nantang Yu said: "Although the two elders' methods of granting and revoking are worth observing, alas, they both wounded their own blades and committed a blunder with their hands.
In my place, I have never from the beginning raised this matter; nor have any of you ever so much as blinked an eyelash."

In the interim, there is certainly neither error nor non-error. Since none of you have overturned the meditation seat, I, this mountain monk, shall likewise not strike you across the back with my staff.
Naturally, the sound accords with the resonance, and the form being straight, the shadow is upright.
Not only are the host and attendants mutually fused, but even humans and devas rejoice. Striking the whisk, he says: "The waters return to the great ocean; the waves..."
The waves subside; when clouds reach Cangwu, the atmosphere is tranquil.
Tianjie Shengyun said, "This is a thief recognizing a thief; it does not hinder one from contending for the initiative.
When Magu saw Sanjiao making such a statement, he should have overturned the meditation seat; how could he have tolerated being asked about this matter further? Sanjiao saw Magu...
If Guo had asked in this manner, it would have been well to strike him across the back with a staff. How could he have endured further saying, "You missed it"?

Although there is both illumination and function, they cannot avoid falling into the trap of secondary branches. Xuedou wished to seize the initiative; having hooked the monk out, he struck him immediately.

This is not without illumination and function occurring simultaneously. Yet, as for the heavens covering and the earth supporting, the mountains high and the waters deep—this is another matter entirely.
There must be something else that does not blink its eyebrows.
Gu Nanmen said, "If there were no triangular eyebrows, Xuedou would have struck him with two blows.
If someone asks this very question now, strike them across the back; what eyebrows are they looking for?
Guangjiao Yu said: "These two elders are much like a hungry hawk dividing meat or a fierce tiger snatching food;

though they compete for the price and offer their compensation, they cannot avoid being laughed at by onlookers. Today, when this mountain monk beats the drum and ascends the seat, everyone comes crowding forward, yet none dare so much as touch him.
Without the use of weapons, you may take it for granted that all will be bathed in wind and rain."
The world is at peace. Within this, there is a constant testing and pressing. If one says it was missed, one deceives ordinary people;
if one says it was not missed, after all, what can be called "this matter"? (He gives a shout and descends from his seat.)

Baiyan Fu said: "These two fellows are flustered and frantic; they may succeed in creating a bustle at their gate, but as for this matter, it is not merely a matter of ten thousand miles of white clouds."
Chan Master Hong’en of Zhongyí in Dǐngzhōu (the second successor of Nán II Mázǔ) was once asked by Yǎngshān, “How can one come to see the nature of Buddhahood?
Zhongyí said, “I will give you a simile: suppose there is a room with six windows and a monkey inside.
Outside, a person calls ‘Sìngsīng’ from the eastern window, and the monkey responds. This happens at all six windows.”
They both called out and both responded. Yangshan bowed in thanks and rose, saying, "I have just received the Master’s parable;
there is nothing I do not understand. However, there is one further matter: as for the inner monkey falling asleep while the outer monkey wishes to see it, what then?
The Master took Yangshan’s hand on the rope-bench and danced with him, saying, "The *xingxing* has already met you; this is the parable."
It is like a tiny gnat building a nest upon the eye-lashes of a mosquito, standing at a crossroads and crying out:
"The land is vast and the people are few; those who meet one another are rare."
Xinxiang Xian said: "Do you people want to see these two elders? I shall give you a parable. Zhongyi was much like a goldsmith.
Yangshan brought a piece of gold to have the goldsmith appraise its value, and the goldsmith offered his full price in return.
Just as they were about to finalize the transaction, the seller added extra weight to the scale. The goldsmith..."
Although Anxi was pleased, he could not help but harbor a secret suspicion in his heart. Why? If it were not a spy, it must certainly be stolen goods.
Yunju Xi said: "At that time, if Zhongyi had not obtained that single phrase from Yangshan, where [could he have been]?"
There was Zhongyi Chaoshou Chou, who said:
"Is there anyone who can definitively grasp this principle? If one cannot definitively grasp it, one is merely a person fiddling with their own spirit;
where, then, does the meaning of Buddha-nature lie?"
Baoci then said, "If it were not for Yangshan, how could one have seen Zhongyi?
But tell me, where exactly was it that Yangshan saw Zhongyi?"
Dongta Ming said, "The Great and Small Yings have mistakenly employed these names and phrases; they call it 'Buddha-nature,' and they also call it a 'monkey.
Then, clapping his hands and laughing 'he-he,' he asked, 'What kind of talk is this?'"
Baoneng Xiu said: "Entering the startling waves to catch a fish to one's heart's content—this is not without merit for Zhongyi.

A golden-winged garuḍa entering the sea takes the dragon directly and swallows it—this is due to Yangshan. But I, this mountain monk, am not like that. How can one realize the meaning of 'seeing Buddha-nature'?
He then slapped him across the mouth, saying: "This avoids being mired in mud and water. He further said: "If I were Yangshan, upon seeing [him]..."
He spoke thus by way of analogy. He merely performed a prostration and said, "I thank the Master for his instruction.

But tell me, how would you settle the case regarding the man from Zhongyi? Xiqia Cheng said, "Zhongyi speaks while his eyes are closed; Yangshan speaks while his eyes are open. Ultimately, these two..."
Neither understood them. If this were the meaning of Buddha-nature, even after sixty kalpas of three lifetimes, they would not have so much as glimpsed it in a dream.
Cuiyan Zhe said, "Zhaozhou was able to take what is near as an analogy; Zhongyi may indeed be called benevolent.
Yet, alas, having been pressed once by Yangshan, he could not avoid becoming flustered and confused. Cuiyan was not like this—how can one come to clearly see the Buddha?"
"Nature! [I] strike his spine with a blow! Why? To avoid letting the ape fall prey to drowsiness; it would weary the six gates with incessant calling.
Zifu Guang said:
"A fine steed carrying salt cannot be appreciated or discerned unless it is Bole; a Lu'er horse drawing a carriage [requires the same]."

"A skilled charioteer like Xu Wangliang is required to control [the horse]. While that may be true for a horse, what would one do to manage it when encountering a wind-roaring fierce tiger or a lion cub that leaps back at you?
He then made a parrying gesture with his hand and said, "Tell me, where would you strike this?"

Lushi said, "Please, Master, tell me. Xiaoyao struck him across the mouth with his whisk. Lushi shook out his sleeves and departed.
He emerged and summoned the assembly from afar, saying: "O Great Assembly! It is truly a matter of fixing one's eyes upon the crown of the head;
yet even so, you fail to discern him. Zhaojue Qin said: "Although this old monk has no eyes upon the crown of my head, I can still verify that his bones have been exposed.
How is this to be seen? 'The venomous snake in the ancient tomb wears horns upon its head; the fierce tiger of the South Mountain has a tail like a *ṭa-śa*.'"
Master Shuilao of Hongzhou (the second successor of Mazu Nanquan) asked Mazu, “What is the very intent of the West?
Mazu said, “Prostrate yourself. As Shuilao was about to bow, Mazu stepped on his chest and knocked him down. Suddenly, Shuilao attained awakening;
he rose, clapped his hands, and laughed heartily, saying, “How extraordinary! How extraordinary! Hundreds of thousands of samādhis and immeasurable wondrous [teachings]!”
The meaning is simply this: one must recognize the source upon the tip of a single hair. After his formal retirement, he would often say to the assembly:
"Ever since I was kicked by Mazu, I have laughed without ceasing until this very day."
Langya Jue said, "Great assembly, do you say that Shuilao had ever attained awakening or not?
Tiantong Jue said, "Master Mazu should not have let him go. When he rose up and spoke thus, he should simply have been asked, 'From where did this single hair-tip come?
