Gushan Puyun said: "The 'Great' and 'Small' Shaolun were much like beggars seeing small profits.

Bairyak Fu said: "It is a pity that Master Ma had the sword that kills people but lacked the blade that gives life, causing the 'Great' and 'Small' Shaolun to fall prostrate upon the tip of a single hair. But how can one remove this for them?"
"A single hair-tip. After a long silence, he said, "At that time, it would have been better to give him another two kicks.
The Monk Wugu of Quzhou (a successor of Mazu Daoyi in the second generation of the Southern Lineage) was visited by the two senior monks Xuanshao and Ershang.
Wugu asked, "Where did you two Zen travelers set out from? Xuanshao replied, "Jiangxi. Wugu then struck him. Xuanshao said, "I have long known that the Master possesses..."
"This is the essential point. Baizhang said, "Since you do not understand, let the monk behind you answer.
When Shao attempted to step forward, Baizhang struck him as well, saying, "I knew there would be no difference between those in the same pit. Go to the meditation hall."
Xuedou Xian said: "The eyes of a master must be like this—like a golden-winged bird cleaving the sea to seize and swallow the dragon directly.
There are some fellows whose eyes cannot distinguish east from west and who do not even know when their staffs are upside down;
they merely go on talking about 'illumination and function occurring simultaneously' or 'person and environment being both seized. What fault would there be in killing ten thousand of them?"
Taisu Zhe said: "Wujiu was much like Guli displaying the majesty of cleaving Mount Taihua;
it was as if a blue dragon unfurled its power to seize the pearl from the black dragon. It left heaven and earth shorn of luster and the sun and moon hidden in their brilliance.
He then took up his staff and said: "Do you all recognize Wujiu? If you do, then with your Mohe sword held crosswise, you alone shall stand within the world."
"According to [the precedent], if you still do not understand it, the eyes upon the tip of the staff are as clear as the sun.
He struck the meditation staff and descended from his seat. Baizhang said: "Among the assembly, some discuss this, saying: 'The staff was in Wujou’s hands;
what difficulty is there in using strength to overwhelm weakness? Alas! Such a perspective as this will be difficult even for water to digest. Therefore it is said:"
The supreme flavor of *amṛta* (ghee) is prized by the world, yet when encountered by such people as these, it turns instead into a poisonous drug. Do you recognize the *vibhītaka* tree?
Grasping the Mohe sword crosswise, he maintains the full authority of the True Command; throughout the realm of Great Peace, he beheads the deluded and the stubborn.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Xuedou may indeed be called one who clearly distinguishes between past and present, and discerns the heterodox from the orthodox.
Nevertheless, while he has seen where Wugou lets go, he has not yet clarified where Wugou holds fast. Do you wish to know where Wugou holds fast?
It is such that even Śākyamuni and Maitreya would still serve as his messengers, and dare not look upon him with a direct eye."
[Zhaozhou] said, "If one were to act strictly according to the command, everyone in the entire world would have to receive a blow of the staff.
Tianmu Li said, "Everyone says that Wujou’s application [of the teaching] was like a 'burning-tail' thunderclap;
they do not realize that their very lives and natures had already fallen into the hands of the monk, like a defeated general who has cast aside his spear and scattered across the field."
Yunju Zhuang said: "A precipice on level ground; a flat plain in a solitary, towering place.
Everywhere people know only that Wujou possessed the means to transcend the school and surpass the standard, yet they do not know Wujou’s thoroughgoing, grandmotherly heart.
Do you wish to recognize this grandmotherly heart? Striking the head of a stone man with a staff—*bò bò*—he speaks only of actual reality."
Kaixian Jin said: "Xuedou was a great master of the school; he clearly distinguished between the ancient and the modern.

Yuan-an Meng said: "Wujiao simply carries out his orders, leaving Maitreya and Śākyamuni standing downwind.
I ask you, two Zen guests: do you accept this? If you accept it, you blind the eyes of all people in the world;
if you do not accept it, you blind Wujiao’s own eyes. Or perhaps one might say: whether accepted or not, it is all gathered up together."
"This is a blind donkey chasing after a great crowd.
Baoguang said, "The old fellow Wujiao is like a divine arrow circling a tree;
with a thunderbolt covering his head, he leaves all people throughout the great earth speechless at the edge of their blades, with no place to evade. But tell me, what eye does he possess?"
With his staff, he struck them all at once, dispersing them.
An-guo Cong said: "This monk cut through the waves and breached the barriers, disregarding even peril and death; he truly possesses the spirit and bearing of a Chan monk.
Although Wu-jou exercised sovereign authority beyond the frontier, when scrutinized, his very life and soul fell into the hands of this monk."
[The Master] held it in his hand. Fengshan said, "Wujiao’s staff has eyes; beneath its feet there is no partiality.

He is accustomed to using the 'white-thief' technique, yet he should not bend others to his will when they are without fault. Nevertheless, he knows only how to exhaust the law; who cares whether there is [fault] or not?"
Min Gujing’s *Qiyun* says: "The wujiao and chima blades are held in one's grasp; killing or enlivening is decided according to the occasion.
Even if you possessed three heads and six arms, upon reaching this point, there would be none who did not look over the precipice and retreat. Nevertheless, one cannot avoid being caught by this."
The monk was thoroughly exposed.
Ziguoxiu said, "Wujiao exhausted his methods but failed to manage the people. Xuedou, too, was merely following the red ink to fill in the black.

"The place where Wujou lets go. Do you wish to know the place where Wujou lets go? He brandishes his staff and strikes it repeatedly, saying:

Nantang Yu said: "Wujiao sat facing the doorway, his true command just being put into practice;

This is indeed so. Let those with eyes discern it. Yuyan Meng said:

Lie! This is why it is called attaining great mastery. If you were to arrange even a single blow, in the end there would be no point of convergence;

Although it is thus, there is still one move left unplayed.

Baiyan Fu said: "The Great Master Mazu refused to act merely according to the command; it was solely because he was moved by the interests of the 'gentlemen' (junzi).

Nevertheless, if such a monk were to come to one's door today, the various quarters must surely have their own strengths; otherwise, [it would be] all..."
This was a case of following in the footsteps of the ancients.
One day, while on the road, Monk Baoling (the second successor of Nanquan and the first successor of Mazu) encountered Layman Pang.
He asked, "Have you ever shared with anyone that phrase by which you attained realization at Mount Nanyue? The Layman replied, "I have. Baoling asked, "To whom did you share it?"
The scholar pointed to himself with his hand and said, "I am Pang Gong. Huileng said, "This is truly the Wondrous Virtue who was born from emptiness;
words of praise are insufficient. The scholar then asked Huileng, "Who can know the phrase by which you have attained power? Huileng donned his bamboo hat and departed.
The scholar said, "Excellent as a guide for the road. Ling did not look back again.
Jingshan Daokai said, "If this matter had not been addressed by Master Pang, it would have nearly been misquoted to others."
Even so, the hundred spirits were still one move behind Old Pang. Why?
At that time, had he not obtained this broken straw hat to cover his skull, what face would he have had to see Old Pang?
Tianning Qi said: "Bailing wears his hat and sets off; this 'sentence of gaining power' can indeed be called clearly presented.
Why did the Elder Miaoxi say, 'What face does Bailing have to see that Pang?
This too is a case of supporting the strong rather than the weak. If someone were to act as a patron for Miaoxi, how would you ask it?"
"A phrase that brings forth power. Speak quickly! Speak quickly! If you hesitate even for a moment, I shall strike you across the spine with my staff.
Tiantong Wu said: "Were Bailin not at Jingshan, even if he had worn his straw rain hat until it was worn through, he would have had no way to show his head."
Baoguang said: "Although Baoling and Master Pang each firmly maintain their own domains, they do not realize that an onlooker perceives their ugliness.

According to my view, however, it was actually Master Pang who was pinned down by Baoling at the end, and remains so to this day."
There is nowhere to find a decisive resolution; let those with the eye of discernment examine it.
Chan Master Yinshan of Longshan in Tanzhou (the second of the Southern Lineage, a successor of Mazu) lived as a mountain hermit.

Once, when Dongshan and his senior teacher Mi were passing by the foot of the mountain, they saw vegetable leaves floating down a stream. Dongshan said, "This is a deep mountain where no one dwells; why are there vegetable leaves flowing along?"

[Zhao] Liufu asked, "Is there a practitioner of the Way living here? They then cleared away the brush and traveled upstream for five or seven li, where they saw a man of emaciated form and unusual appearance.
They approached him to exchange greetings. The hermit said, "There are no paths on this mountain; from where have you *śrāmaṇeras* come?

Duan said, "Setting aside the matter of the pathless state for a moment, from where did you, the master of the mountain, enter? The hermit said, "I do not come from among the wandering clouds and waters. Duan—
Dongshan asked, "Master of the Mountain, how long have you been living on this mountain? Yinyuan said, "I do not involve myself with spring and autumn.

Dongshan said, "The Master of the Mountain has lived here first; this mountain has existed since before. Yinyuan said, "I do not know. Dongshan asked, "Why do you not know? Yinyuan said, "I did not come from the realm of humans or devas.
Dongshan asked, "What principle did the Master of the Mountain realize that he was able to dwell on this mountain? Yinyuan said, "I see..."
Two clay oxen fight and enter the sea; until this very day, there has been no news. Dongshan first assumed his formal demeanor and paid his respects, then asked:
"What is the guest within the host? Yunyan said: "Green mountains shroud white clouds. Dongshan asked:
"What is the host within the host? Yunyan said: "Never leaving the door for all one's years. Dongshan asked: "How far apart are guest and host? Yunyan said: [Silence].
On the waters of the Yangtze River, waves arose. [Dongshan] asked, "When host and guest meet, what words are spoken?
Yunyan replied, "The clear breeze brushes the white moon. Dongshan took his leave. Yunyan then said: "I have lived for long in this three-bay thatched hut;

A single divine light shines through ten thousand tranquil realms. Do not bring right and wrong to judge me; In this floating life, artificial analysis is irrelevant. Thereupon, he burned down the hermitage.
Delving even deeper into the peaks and ridges, Tiantong Jue said:
"The Host is like clouds concealing the crown of the head; the Guest is like snow pressing down upon the brow ridge. Departure is the limited jurisdiction of the gatekeeper;
speech is the resonance of jade and metal. Now, tell me: how do these four lines compare with the [verse on] "Hiding"?
Whether the mountains are the same or different—let those with the discerning eye among the monastic communities try to distinguish them.
Thus, when Chan Master Chuan (the second successor of Mazu) was picking tea, Layman Pang asked: "The Dharma-realm admits no body."
"Did the Master see me on my way back? Zhaozhou said, "It was not I, the old monk, who answered your question.
The scholar said, "To have a question and an answer is merely the ordinary way of things. Zhaozhou then went to pick tea, paying no heed.

The scholar said, "Do not take offense that I just now asked so casually. Zhaozhou still did not look back. The scholar shouted, "You ill-mannered old fellow! Wait until I recount everything to [Master] Baizhang!"
A man with clear eyes—Zhaozhou threw down his tea basket and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Xuedou Xian said: "Zhaozhou only knew how to hold fast to the borders; he could not live and die together [with them].

Zhaojue Qin said: "Twice he did not look back; he cast aside his basket and returned home. But tell me, where does the ultimate meaning lie?
Do you understand? A bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip; a sweet melon is sweet from stem to fruit. This old man of Zequan has experienced much."
Baoning Mochun said: "Though Zequan recognized the formation of the battle array, he did not know how to subdue the enemy.

he would have seen what Pang Gong would have done."
Gunanmen said: "How extraordinary is Master Pang! Although he was a layman, he established a point of inquiry and was able to hold firm to his boundaries.

"Cloud" refers to one who hides his head but exposes his tail. Had he hesitated for a moment, [the Master] would have simply taken up the tea tray and struck him.

Not only would this have cut off the old fellow’s entanglements, but it would also have shown that those within our own circle of the square robe and round crown possess their own distinct excellence.
Yuan'an Yu said: "Thus, Old Man [Zhaozhou] held fast the secure barrier, allowing not even a drop of water to pass;
one could say his head was straight and his tail was straight. Master Pang sought powder in the snow and looked for soot upon ink;
he exhausted his own mind and broke the mouths of others. Fortunately, he escaped being pursued by Old Man Zhaozhou."
Fengshan began by saying: "When Master Pang charged straight through the fray, the Pass of Qin was already gone from his sight.
Had it not been so, [Zhao] Chuan would have lowered his banners, ceased beating his drums, reduced his cooking fires, and concealed his sharpness—until he finally broke through the city of Caizhou."
The layman Pang Yun of Xiangzhou (the second of the Southern Lineage; successor of Mazu) asked Mazu: "The person who is not oblivious to their original nature—please, Master, cast your eyes high.
Mazu looked straight down at him. The layman said: "This single stringless lute—only you, Master, can play it wondrously.
Mazu looked straight up at him. The layman then prostrated himself. As Mazu returned to his quarters, the layman followed behind him and said: "Just now, my cleverness led to a failure."
"Clumsy. Yunfeng Yue said: "Tell me, is it the guest who turns cleverness into clumsiness, or is it the host who turns cleverness into clumsiness?
Is there anyone who can discern this? If you can discern it, thirty blows—each blow will not spare even one."
[The monk] said, “I have. If you cannot discern this, there will be new branches next year; the spring breeze will continue to trouble them without end.
Langya Huijue said, “He committed a theft all night long, yet he did not realize it was dawn.”
Zhihai Yi said: "Of these two old fellows, one has opened his mouth and cannot close it; the other has closed his mouth and cannot open it.

Jingshan Daowu said: "It is not that Master Mazu failed to look up and look down; it is simply that he obscured the person of original nature.

"Even so, it still does not accord with the original body. Have you not heard the saying: 'A grain of pepper in a toad's mouth'?

"This is a lute with its strings broken. He took up his staff and said, "It is not that I am letting Master Mada pass;

When Pang Gong paid his respects, Mazu immediately returned to his quarters. Is there anyone here who can discern this?

Regarding "Discourse on Non-arising":

Human beings do not inquire as to how many thousands of autumns have passed; they merely perceive that heaven and earth are as large as a grain of millet.

Wealth and nobility, glory and splendor—these are but the "hu" and "ya" (interjections) within the vast void. Only the green mountains facing one's door remain, which are originally a single scroll of painting.
Thus, with a whisk, he draws a stroke across the air.
*Anthology of the Ancestral School’s Excerpts from Ancient Cases*,
Scroll 12 and Scroll 13. Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu,
Successor to the Patriarch at Bairyam in Ancient Hangzhou.

Chan Master Yushan Weiyan of Yuzhou (a successor of Shitou Xiqian). For a long time he did not ascend the seat [to preach]. The head of the monastery said, "The assembly has long been longing for your Dharma instruction;
we request that the Master preach the Dharma. Yushan ordered the bell to be struck. When the assembly had gathered, Yushan ascended the seat. At that moment—

After a long while, he descended from his seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters. The head of the monastery followed him and said, "Master, you previously promised to preach the Dharma for the assembly;
why did you not deign to offer even a single word? The Mountain replied, "The sutras have masters of the sutras; the treatises have masters of the treatises.
How can you blame the old monk?"
Xuedou Xian said: "What a pity that Old Man Yaoshan took a tumble on level ground; all the people in the world cannot lift him up.
Langya Jue said: "Yaoshan’s descent from the seat was not without cause for doubt, yet as soon as the Hall Master gave him a squeeze, he lost it."
"Turn back one eye. Cuiyan Zhi said:
"When Yaoshan descended from his seat, the monastery director initially resented that he did not preach the Dharma for the assembly;
this can truly be called 'misleading the three armies.'"
Jianfu Huiyun said: "Does Yaoshan see the head monk? Does the head monk see Yaoshan?
Thirty years from now, when you encounter a master of literary composition, do not fail in your citation."
Kaifeng Ning said: "Yaoshan was careful at the beginning and guarded against the end; his Buddha-eye is difficult to peer into.
When the Abbot met him on a narrow path, he carelessly let the opportunity slip away.
Xuedou Zong said: "Holding hands beyond the Kalpa of Wei-yin—who would be willing to return together? He cast [it] down at the crossroads."
"Gold! How much have we missed? I dare ask you all: tell me, did Yaoshan ever speak [these words] or not?
If you say he spoke them, you slander Yaoshan; if you say he did not speak them, you betray Yaoshan.
Tell me, ultimately where does this person reside? After a long silence, he said: "One must know that beyond the clouds, atop a thousand peaks, there is something else."
"The numinous pines are cold with the rain.
Regarding this, Dahui Zonggao, while at his station below the seat, added the comment: "There is no small amount of entanglement.
Regarding the phrase "How can one blame the old monk?", he added the comment: "It makes people laugh to death!"
Tiantong Jie said: "Cuiyan possesses only one eye; he simply does not realize that when Yaoshan returned to his quarters, it was truly putting his entire army to labor.
Zifu Xian said: "Yaoshan ultimately returning to his quarters is like being a good person, yet he was merely slighted by him."
A slight pinch, and one immediately forgets what came before and loses track of what follows.
Zhongfeng Ben said: "Yaoshan did not ascend the hall for a long time, and when he finally did, he could not utter a single word before the assembly.
One might think, 'I thought, I thought,' until at the very end he says: 'The sutras have masters of sutras; the treatises have masters of treatises. Ah, so that was it all along!"

Boshanlai said: "When one engages with sentient beings, emotional attachments are cast aside; yet even this state of detachment becomes a burden. When giving and taking provoke one another, do not be surprised by it.

Furthermore, who would have known that those seeking to hear the cries of the autumn crickets would find them so chaotic, or that one of pure character would be vexed by ornate colors? It was because he was pressed by the head of the monastery."
"Directly, it is reduced to a hundred fragments.
After Gu Nanmen cited the words of Cuiyan and Mian, he said: "Although these two elders exerted their full strength to support [the tradition], they possessed only a single eye.
Little did they know that the Master of the Medicine Mountain Courtyard alone was directing strategy from within the tent."
"A single person decides victory a thousand *li* away. Nevertheless, Yaoshan only knows how to go that way; he does not know how to come this way.
If it were I, returning to my quarters and seeing the courtyard master ask such a question, I would simply say to him:
"The subsequent text is long; it shall be entrusted to a later day."
Qixia Chengyun said: "Yaoshan has a fine melody; its tonal resonance is truly resonant and clear.

Yet, without cause, he was buffeted by a gust of wind from the monastery superintendent, which left the *gong* and *shang* notes all thrown into disarray. Nevertheless, even so, it is still superior to the idle lute strings of ordinary households."
Qinghua said: "How strange is this old fellow Yaoshan! He is accustomed to picking up the holeless flute and blowing it specifically at the beginning of the kalpa.
Thus, while its pure sound pervades the world, alas, those who can truly appreciate it are few."
Longhua Ti said: "The head monk was merely rushing along the road, unaware that he had taken the wrong path.
Yaoshan sought someone to enter the weeds; he was thoroughly soaked through with mud and water.
If I were Yaoshan, I would have waited for him to ask why he did not utter a single word, and then simply said, 'I took you for a man. Had he hesitated, I would have struck him out with my staff."
Longtang Fu said: "Yaoshan employs a mechanism beyond the ordinary; he looses an arrow before the wind.
He is far too prone to relying on his wealth to deceive the poor, causing the monastery steward to greedily gaze at the moon in the sky while losing the pearl in his own palm. Here, it is not so.
If the Prior were to seek instruction for the sake of the assembly, this mountain monk would have no objection to stringing together pearls and joining jade, weaving a fine robe."

A palindrome. Revealing it spontaneously as it arises, he directly causes each person to realize their point of return in that very moment, sparing the superintendent from having to follow up with questions later.
"Tell me, what kind of Dharma is being spoken? After a long silence, he said: "The night is cold; having stood for a long time, I hope you will take care of yourself."
Xishan Yin said: "Yaoshan secretly threaded the golden needle; the Abbot darkly pierced the jade thread.
Although it is said that the brocade seams are layered upon one another, when scrutinized, the points where the cross-patterns meet cannot avoid being fatally exposed."
Lianfu Ce remarked, "It often happens that people say Yaoshan lost track of what came before and after, failing to avoid the charge of bowing to the ancients.
Little do they realize that Yaoshan was like a divine dragon protecting its tail or a lion losing its tracks;
he did not merely humble the monastery steward at that time, but also changed the eyes of countless people throughout past and present."
Baiyan Fu said: "Yaoshan, long ago before the beginning of kalpas, cast down a vast net across the heavens, intending to capture the golden k'un fish that carries Mount Tai to repay his ancient vow.
Instead, he ran straight into a three-legged toad; having untied the net, the frustration remains only within his belly.
Upon careful examination, it is clear that, in sum, the attendant failed to exert his strength. Attendant.
Had he possessed strength at that moment, when the abbot was about to extend his request, he would have simply shouted the abbot out.
Would Mount Yaoshan not then have been "head straight and tail straight"?

A monk once asked Youshan, "I have a doubt; I pray that the Master will resolve it for me. Youshan replied, "Wait until the time for the formal assembly, and I shall resolve your doubt for you, lay brother.
That evening, when the assembly had gathered for the evening discourse, Youshan said, "Today you wished to have your doubts resolved; where is the elder who sought this?
The monk stepped forward from the assembly and stood there. Youshan descended from his meditation seat, seized him by the collar, and said, "Assembly, this monk has—"
Suspecting [that he was still confused], he gave him a shove and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Baoci then pressed him, saying: "Tell me, did you resolve his doubt for him or not? If you say you resolved his doubt, then where exactly was the resolution?
If you say you did not resolve his doubt, how can you account for his coming to the hall for the evening sermon?"
Cuiyan Zhi said: "When Yaoshan resolves doubts in such a manner, he is merely adding mud to the earth.
Nevertheless, this monk must not fail to repay Yaoshan."
Yunju Yuan said, "Big and small Yaoshan were both exposed by this monk.
Yuan'an Yu said, "This is nectar; this is poison. It is a sword that kills; it is a blade that gives life."

Baiyan Fu said: "To sink thirty thousand *hu* of fragrant bait into the vast depths, yet the object of one's aim is not the bream or the carp—yet the old man Yaoshan exerts such effort for the sake of a field frog or a well minnow.
Is this truly the way of a skilled practitioner?"
While Zun Bunan was bathing the Buddha statue, Yaoshan said, "This one you are bathing—you can bathe this, but can you bathe that one?
Zun said, "Bring me that one. Yaoshan then ceased speaking.
Changqing Ling said, "A false dharma is difficult to support.
Baoci then questioned him, saying, "Tell me, when Changqing spoke thus, was he acting as a guest or as the host?
The assembly calls this 'the words for bathing the Buddha,' and it is also called 'the inclusive statement. Tell me, is it perfect or not?"
Huanglong Nan said: "As for these two venerable masters, one emerges and one enters; their victory or defeat has not yet been seen.
Thirty years hence, do not err in citing this. Zhaojue Qin said:
"Yaoshan’s question was obscured by a heavy barrier; Old Zun’s answer struck twice with a single blow."
Indeed. One must not merely cling to a single path. When asked, "Chongning, can that which is washed by bathing be washed?
he picked up his ladle and said to him, "How is it?"

Tianbao Shu said: "If I, this old monk, had seen Yaoshan speak in such a manner at that time, I would have immediately taken a ladle of water and poured it over his head, causing him to melt away like ice dissolving."
Qingshan Xiu said: "Yaoshan provided a lateral path to guide beginners by looking down upon them with compassion.
But when Puna took up the task of benevolence, he did not yield; with a single pressure, the matter was finished.

If I were Yaoshan, I would have waited for him to say, 'Bring that thing here,' and then snatched the ladle away and poured it over his head. Why? Because the water of concentration is full and serene; bathe in this stainlessness."
Ren’u Yan’an said, “What a fine ‘resting’! How could Yaoshan not have been capable of it? It is like the coarse, superficial, obscure, and short-sighted types of the present day;
their approach to the fundamental principle is incorrect. When asked, ‘Bring forth that which you will use,’ they immediately strike or shout, or even overturn [the table].”
He overturned the bathtub and made a great mess; truly, he has no sense of shame.
I say that if Yaoshan does not leave at once, I shall seize him and cast him into the vast ocean of the Eastern Sea, ensuring he never again bathes in such a "mind-like" or "intention-like" manner.
"I shall wait for Maitreya’s descent to ask him further. Bring that one here," said [Baizhang].
Qixia Cheng said, "Tell me, did Yaoshan know that 'one' or not?
If he knew it, why did he stop as soon as Pouna pressed him? Is there anyone here who can open a single eye on this point?"
Mao. Baoyan Fu said: "If I were a patch-robed monk, could you bathe this one after you have finished bathing that one?
He then threw away the ladle and poured out the scented water. Nevertheless, when Yaoshan retired, what did he do?
"How so? A monk asked Yaoshan, "In the level fields and shallow grass, the deer and roe form a herd. How does one shoot the king of the deer among them?
Yaoshan said, "Watch the arrow! The monk threw himself down and fell. Yaoshan called to his attendant, "Drag this dead man out! The monk then [arose].
He ran off. Mount Nung said, "What limit is there for this fellow who plays with lumps of mud?
Xuedou Xian said, "Though this monk is alive at three steps, he must die at five."
Yunju Yuan said: "Yaoshan’s bow, capable of launching a thousand-jin arrow, was not meant for a mere field mouse to trigger its mechanism.
This monk left the gate with an arrow in his side; once dead, he shall never live again."
Jingci Chang said: "This monk has chased a monkey into a bustling marketplace; Yaoshan rides a fierce tiger straight up a high mountain.
If you deliberate upon them as two separate instances, you will ultimately be subject to scrutiny."
Yuan'an Yu said: "This monk set up a question-head that was not easy to encounter. But when he loosed his arrow, it turned out to be a dead deer.
Perhaps by some stroke of luck he drank nectar elsewhere and was reborn, so as not to lose his status as the primordial ancestor, King Weyin.
Then, aiming at the empty sky, he drew a bow and said: 'Look at the arrow!'"
Gounan said: "This monk hides his body in the weeds and sets up a question; from beginning to end, he is able to bear it.
Yaoshan’s single arrow hits the mark, yet for all that, the monk who shot him does not die."
Qixia Chengyun said: "To transcend the multitude, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to overcome the victor, one must be a lion cub.
This monk exerted his full strength to soar upward, yet he could not escape beneath Yaoshan’s legs. How can he be called a lion cub or a man of heroic spirit?
Yaoshan said, "Drag out this dead man! What other words could have been spoken here to achieve such a result?
"You cannot avoid being surpassed by one who excels the ranks of his enemies; try to explain it!

Baoyan Fu said, "Although this monk is fully armored and his advances and retreats follow a method, how can he withstand the old general Yaoshan’s courageous pursuit and relentless chase? Where is there for you to drag your heels? The attendant dragged him out.
"This dead man! [Yunmen] then rose from his seat, clapped his hands, and laughed heartily, saying, "This old fellow has been thoroughly exposed today.
If this monk were capable of such a thing, even Yaoshan would have had no choice but to surrender here."
Yaoshan said to Yunyan, "Call the śrāmaṇera here for me. Yunyan asked, "What do you want to have him do, Master?
Yaoshan replied, "I have a broken-legged cauldron that I want him to carry up and down.
Yunyan said, "In that case, I shall lend you a hand. Yaoshan then stopped.
Guishan Zhe said, "If Old Man Yaoshan had not encountered Yunyan, his broken-legged cauldron would have become a discarded vessel.
I, Daopei, wish for everyone to join hands to save this broken-legged cauldron. Why is this?"
Furthermore, let us strive so that the ancient style does not fall into ruin.
Tiantong Huayan said: "Yaoshan knew the head; Yunyan knew the tail. Although the head and tail corresponded to one another, they still did not know shame."

Tianning Qisong said: "When one's insight is equal to that of the teacher, the teacher’s virtue is diminished by half; only when one's insight surpasses that of the teacher is one fit to receive the transmission.

Yunyan at that time was also lacking one move. Had he waited for [Deshan] to say, "I have a broken-legged cauldron," and then asked him to lift it up and carry it down, he would have withdrawn his body and departed immediately.
Only after the snow has fallen does one know the resilience of the pine and cypress; only when affairs are difficult is one truly tested.
Regarding the "seeing the mind of the Great Man," Nengrenjian (鑑) said:

"Everyone says that Yaoshan and his son 'knew the tail by nodding their heads,' but when one examines this closely, it is all nothing more than washing clods of earth in the mud. What connection does it have [to the truth]?"
Baiyan Fu said: "To serve one's ruler with the utmost loyalty, not wavering even unto death—this is the constant principle of a minister.
As for leading the ruler to a height above Yao and Shun, there is yet another way to speak of it.
Without learning Yunyan’s way of speaking, try to present another approach."
Guangyin Biao says: "One who is not the son of a man worth a thousand pieces of gold cannot manage a capital of a thousand pieces of gold.
Yaoshan was old and solitary; had it not been for Yunyan knowing his innermost heart, nearly an act of ungrateful ingratitude would have occurred."
Clapping his hands, he said: "To be able to refrain from altering the way of one's father for three years may be called filial piety.
Yaoshan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Hunan. Yaoshan said, "Is the water in Lake Dongting full yet? The monk said, "It is not.
Yaoshan said, "It has been raining so much for so long; why is it not full? The monk was speechless.
Yunyan Cheng, acting on behalf of the monk, said, "It is profoundly still.
Daowu Zhi offered an alternative response, "It is full.
Dongshan Jia said, "In what kalpa has it ever increased or decreased?"
Yunmen Wenyan said, "It is right here.
Once, while Yaoshan was reading a scripture, Li Ao, the Regional Inspector of Langzhou, arrived. Yaoshan remained silent and did not look at him at all.
Li Ao then said, "Seeing you in person is not as good as hearing of your reputation," and he brushed his sleeves and left. Yaoshan called out, "Li Ao! Li Ao turned his head back, and Yaoshan—
He said, "How can you, Provincial Governor, hold my ears in high esteem while disparaging my eyes? Hsiao turned around, bowed in thanks, and asked, "What is the Way?
The Mountain Master pointed upward with his finger and then pointed downward, saying, "Do you understand? Hsiao replied, "I do not understand.
The Mountain Master said, "Clouds in the blue sky; water in the pitcher. Hsiao joyfully prostrated himself and presented a verse, saying: "Refined is my physical form..."
The crane’s form: beneath a thousand pine trees, two cases of scripture. When I came to ask about the Way, there was no further talk:
“Clouds are in the blue sky; water is in the pitcher. Songyin said, “It is not so here. If you were to ask Longfeng today, ‘What is [the meaning]?’”
"Only say: 'When the state is correct, the mind of Heaven is harmonious; when the officials are pure, the people are naturally at peace.
Now tell me: is there any distinction between the Way and Yaoshan? Relying on my staff, I descend from the seat."
One day, while Yaoshan was sitting in meditation, Shitou saw him and asked, "What are you doing here? Yaoshan replied, "I am doing nothing at all.
Shitou said, "If that is so, then you are just sitting idly. Yaoshan said, "To sit idly is itself an act."
Shitou said, "You say you do not practice; for what do you not practice? Shanshan replied, "Even the thousand sages do not recognize it.
Bairyak Pu said, "Great indeed was Yaoshan; he did not dwell in a monastery nor reside on a cold cliff.
This single patch of secure and secret ground cannot be seen even by the thousand eyes of Mahākāruṇika. Thus, for the sake of the old man Shitou and others..."
A single, sudden pressure—truly like the untying of a pearl pouch—is it not a state of profound stability?
Once, while Yaoshan was reading a scripture, a monk asked, "Master, you usually do not permit others to read scriptures;
why then do you read them yourself? Yaoshan replied, "I am merely trying to cover my eyes. The monk asked, "May I learn from the Master? Yaoshan said: [The text ends here.]
"If you look at it, even ox-hide must be pierced through.
Changqing Ling said, "What fault is there in the eyes?
Baoci then asked, "Tell me, does Changqing understand Yaoshan’s meaning, or does he not understand Yaoshan’s meaning?"
Xuedou Zong said: "The true mind is unmoving; the ocean of teachings is clear and bright.
When its function is realized as suchness, the sky of meaning shines brilliantly. At this very moment, tell me: is this the scripture or the eye?

If you can see through to the bottom here, there is no further need to follow the lines of the text or chase after delusions while losing the truth. If it is not yet so, even if you pierce through ox-hide, it is still..."
"It is well. How many people know that skulls lie strewn across the wilds?
At Yueshan’s evening assembly, he did not light the lamps, but instead delivered this statement: 'I have a phrase; I shall tell it to you when a hornless ox gives birth to a calf.
At that time, a monk came forward and said, 'A hornless ox has given birth to a calf,' to which [Yueshan] replied, 'It is simply that you, Master, do not..."
Dowshan called out, "Attendant, bring the lamp! The monk then withdrew his body and entered the assembly.
Because Yunyan had raised this matter, Dongshan Shoujie said, "This monk actually understands; it is simply that he refuses to prostrate."
Qingliang Qin said: "At that time, do not ask for the lamp; simply ask him whether the one born is a male calf or a female calf.
He further provided the following response on his behalf: "They are twins."
Touzi said, "Qingyuan, tell me: where is this monk’s point of meeting? If you can say it, you may clear this monk's grievance;
if you cannot say it, you will be deceived by Yaoshan."
Fushan Yuan said: "I have a single phrase; I will speak it when a tongueless person asks. Zhaojue Qin said:
"Yaoshan’s casting of his line was intended for the *kūn* and *jing* fish; this monk swallowed the hook as the three thousand waves surged.
Dongshan’s True Eye shares the same breeze from a thousand miles away; Fadeng readjusted his banners and spears and donned his armor once more."
Although it is thus, I, this mountain monk, am not like that. I have a single phrase that I have already spoken for all people since before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranirghoṣa.
If someone asks whether it accords with the side of light or the side of darkness, I simply answer them:
"When the dragon obtains water, his spirit increases; when the tiger encounters mountain terrain, his fierce majesty grows."
Huanglong Zhen said: "Do you understand? It is like a person writing characters in the dark; though the characters do not form a complete text, the traces of the brushstrokes are already manifest.
Now that the traces are manifest, why does one not see them when a lamp is lit? It is not said that 'the thief is a petty person whose cleverness surpasses that of a gentleman'?"
Yunju Zhuang said: "Big or small, Yaoshan’s head is a dragon, but his tail is a snake. This monk only knows how to grasp at the moon, unaware of the depth of the water.
Great assembly, this is like a bull giving birth to a calf! I tell you, monks: bring me a single phrase as an answer!"
Dongshan Ying said: "Yaoshan wanted this story to circulate; he straightened what was crooked and bent what was straight. This monk looked for a hole to drive a wedge into;
such a favorable opportunity is hard to encounter. Look closely: everyone has failed to resolve it.
Dongshan also has a single phrase—wait until the pillar gives birth to a child, and I will tell you. Or perhaps a monk stepped forward and said, 'The pillar has given birth to a child.'"
It was simply that the Master did not speak. He merely said, "I already knew you were making your living in a ghost cave. Tianjing Xin said:
"Yaoshan produced a mechanism upon a mechanism; this monk produced a cleverness upon a cleverness. This is the battle array of Dongshan."

Later, when the banner was unfurled, it had not yet returned even half of what had been lost to others. If it were not for the Dharma-lamp, how could one see that the merit of the "sweat-soaked horses" was so great?
After all, how is it so? If you do not sleep on the same bed, how can you know there is a hole in the lining of the quilt?
One finger points to the clouds. Since Yaoshan and this monk have already been clearly critiqued by the venerable elders of all quarters, let us set that aside for now.
I wish to ask you, my brothers: ultimately, what do you call "one phrase"?
Do not rely on patterns or imitations; speak otherwise. Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
Once, when a dharma master went to the home of the lay practitioner Gan-zhi, Gan asked, "Where have you come from?

The master replied, "From Mount Yaoshan. Gan asked, "Have you brought some medicine with you? The master asked back, "What illness does the lay practitioner have? Gan then gave him two ingots of silver.
Having received the silver, the master returned immediately to submit his report. Yaoshan asked, "Why did you return so quickly? The master related the previous conversation.
Mountan said, "You have been robbed; return it to him quickly. The host then returned it. Gan said, "So there was someone on the mountain peak all along.
He then added more gold and gave it as a gift.
Tongan Xian said, "Had I known the practitioner would ask in this manner, I would never have said that Yaoshan had come.
Xuefeng Kong said, "The old fellow Yaoshan was himself timid. Had it been Xuefeng, he would have simply accepted him.
Why? It would have left this fellow Ganzhi to harbor doubts for thirty years."
Baoshou Fang said: "Although Yaoshan discerned the wind coming from afar, how could he have known that the practitioner had a talisman behind his elbow?
Not only did this monk fall victim to the thief, but Yaoshan fell victim to the thief even more severely.

Had it been I, when the host had finished presenting the story, I would have immediately ordered the administrative officer to take him into the storehouse and record on the register: 'On such-and-such a day, Ganji was taken into custody.'"
The practitioner bought two ingots of silver for medicine. "See how the practitioner's life has fallen into the hands of this mountain monk," [said] Tiantong Wan.
"Ganqi used a shrimp to fish for a turtle; the fundraiser greedily took the bait and forgot the hook.
Yaoshan lost his sheep and only then repaired the fence; gain and loss cannot help but be half-and-half. Tong'an said, "Had I known the practitioner was like this earlier..."
If he had asked this, Guishan would never have said, "Yaoshan has come. Although there was a plan to enter the earth, there was no scheme to pierce the heavens.
Had Guangrun acted as the master of offerings, he would have simply let out a shout and departed at that moment; one can be certain that the attendant would have harbored doubts for half his life.
Bodhidharma’s dense clouds: for the sake of another's single grain of rice, one loses six months' worth of provisions. The patron died on the spot and has not been able to live since.
If it were I, the mountain monk, when asked whether I had brought medicine back with me, I would simply say, "What kind of mental state is this?
If the practitioner were to offer a silver ingot, I would say, "Good! But the poor monk has never [accepted such things] from of old."
"It did not pass through my hands; the layman must have sent it himself for it to be accepted. It is a pity that this monk’s eyes and brows were not sharp enough;

he brought trouble upon those two elders. Although Yaoshan was a thief who recognized thieves, he ought not to have let this monk go free, thereby causing him to run errands incessantly and bringing disgrace upon the lineage."
Kongtong’s clouds of compassion and the Great and Small Yaoshans were far too mired in the mud and water.
At that time, had they waited for the messenger-monk to submit his petition and present the case, they should have immediately provided him with fodder suited to his own nature;
not only would this have allowed the messenger-monk to find a distinct livelihood in the future, but it would also have left the lay practitioner Ganji thoroughly perplexed.
Longtang Zhu said: "If I were to act as the master of the ritual, I would wait for him to offer two ingots of silver. Then, extending my hand, I would say:
'The practitioner must take another two or three doses before he is finished. Thus, I could ensure that he would empty his entire purse in offering;
his very life-force would remain in my hands."
Baiyan Fu said: "Ganzhi thought, 'Originally there was someone on the mountain peak,' and so he added more gold to give as alms.
The old fellow Yaoshan suffered a total loss here. Among all the elders of antiquity and today, there is not a single one who understands the point of profit and loss.
If I were Yaoshan, upon hearing the fundraiser recount Ganzhi’s words in this manner—"
He simply dealt thirty painful blows to the Patriarch and cast him out through the mountain gate.

Zen Master Tianran of Danxia in Dengzhou (a successor of Qingyuan Xingsi and Shitou Xiqian), while passing by Huilin Temple during a freezing cold spell, took a wooden Buddha and used it as fuel for his fire.
The temple steward scolded him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha? Danxia struck back with his staff.
Hui said, "I shall burn these to obtain the *śarīra*. Huayan said, "Wooden Buddhas—how could they have *śarīra*?
Hui said, "Since there are no *śarīra*, please bring two more statues to burn. Thereafter, the eyebrows and beard of the monastery master fell off.
Touzi Qingyun said, "I do not know how to be a guest; I trouble the host.
Daining Kuan was asked by a monk, "Why did the eyebrows and whiskers of the temple steward fall off when Danxia burned the wooden Buddha?
Kuan replied, "A thief does not strike a poor family."
Baoning Yong said: "Setting aside for a moment the fact that the abbot’s eyebrows and beard fell out, does Danxia’s eyebrow still remain?
If you can see this, you will be a fellow student of the ancient Buddhas; if you do not see it, you must strictly avoid denying cause and effect."
Baofeng Wen said: "When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, the head monk’s eyebrows and beard fell off. He suddenly took up his staff and said, "This is not a wooden Buddha.
Throwing down the staff, he said, "Who dares to burn you? If you intend to act, your eyebrows and beard will fall;
but if you do not intend to act, what then? He called out loudly, "Attendant, pick up the staff!"

Shimen Cong said, "Huangbo’s demonstration was indeed extraordinary; yet, as soon as he was pressed by this monk, he lost one of his eyes.
Cuiyan Zhen said, "Everywhere it is said that Huangbo sat upon this monk, and it is also said that Huangbo was [pressed] by him..."

This assembly has hitherto merely provided a superficial analysis without delving deeper; they fail to realize that a misty leopard, though its fur is lush, never lowers itself to eat, and a bird in the courtyard nurtures its courage only to wait for the moment to startle others.
Fachang Yu said, "I want one who has no Chan to serve as National Teacher.
Jingshan Gao said, "Tell me, is this a sentence of clarified butter or a sentence of poison?"

Tiantong Wu said: "Huangbo was much like one who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. At that time, when [Nanquan] asked, 'What would you do if someone were presiding over disciples and leading a community elsewhere?
why did he not strike him immediately upon the sound of these words? Had he hesitated even for a moment, Huangbo would have struck him out with a continuous series of blows."
Kaixian Jin said: "Huangbo was one whose eyes looked down upon the four seas with utter emptiness.
Why, then, did he see his resolve shatter like tiles and melt like ice when pressed by a mere patch-robed monk? Tell me, what was Huangbo’s intention? Do you wish to understand?
Three cups of wine on the face of a noble lord; a single branch of flowers tucked into a beauty’s hair."
Yuan'an Yu said: "Huangbo, for a moment, took that Eye of the True Dharma and gouged it blind, cutting off all access at the vital pass;
yet he was crushed to pieces by this fellow who eats dregs of wine."
Dongshan Ying said, "Although Huangbo’s eyes covered heaven and earth and his breath swallowed the entire world, he was nonetheless far too noisy and clamorous.
Is there anyone who knows where Huangbo lost ground? After a long silence, he said, 'Danger!'"
Zifu Guang said: "Huangbo’s words here bring tears to his eyes and pain to his bowels. Those who do not understand take them to be a means of outshining all other quarters [of the Chan school].
If that were so, it would be a profound injustice to the ancients. From my limited perspective, I shall briefly reveal a single facet of this.
After a long silence, he said: 'A short song is chanted softly; it cannot be prolonged.'"
Fayun once said: "The old fellow Huangbo was much like one who relies on his power to bully others, forcing the virtuous into lowliness.
As soon as he was pressed by this monk, his eyes went wide with panic and his mouth became a muddle. Nevertheless, even so..."
Do you still know where the ancients fell? "Accustomed to fishing for whales and sea monsters in the vast depths, yet sighing over the frog’s stride as it rolls in the mud.
When Baizhang asked Huangbo, "Where have you come from? Huangbo replied, "I have been gathering mushrooms at Mount Daxiong."
As he approached, Baizhang asked, "Do you see the tiger? Huangbo then let out a tiger's roar. Baizhang raised his axe and made a gesture as if to strike;
Huangbo then gave him a slap. Baizhang laughed heartily and returned to the hall. Addressing the assembly, he said, "There is a great tiger at the foot of Mount Daxiong.
You all must watch out for it. Today, the old fellow Baizhang has seen it with his own eyes."
They encountered a single word.
Yangshan Ji said, "Baizhang only knew how to ride the tiger's head; he did not know how to grasp the tiger's tail.
Wuzu Jie said, "Baizhang was much like a thief whose heart is filled with trepidation; Huangbo is simply unable to forget what he is most familiar with."
Yunju Zhuang said: "When teacher and disciple attain one another, it is like a needle meeting its eye; their spiritual sparks are exchanged, and illumination and function proceed in tandem.
It is like two dragons contending for a pearl—seizing the clouds and grasping the mist without stirring a ripple—or two tigers vying for food."
"Capturing alive without harming a single life. Some say, "Baizhang lacked the means to trap a tiger; Huangbo possessed the capacity to surpass his master.
To argue in such a manner is like driving a stake through one's own brain and plunging it into a vat of glue. [The Master] draws a stroke with his whisk and says:
"He splits open the towering, celestial beauty of Mount Hua; he releases the Yellow River, pure to its very depths."

Baiyan Fu said: "Everyone says this fellow has picked out a three-legged toad from amidst the weeds and is then parading it about for show at the crossroads; how could this be the discernment of a great man?
However, according to my own view as a mountain monk, I can only believe half of what he says."
Fahen Mi said: "Observe how this father and son meet fist with fist and kick with kick;
it is much like a tiger pouncing and a dragon leaping, leaving no one able to grasp or imitate them. Furthermore, when he ascended the hall to address the assembly, what a kind heart!
Examining this from beginning to end, it is entirely a case of having a head but no tail.
When Huangbo was serving as the Head Seat under Nanquan, one day at the time of the midday meal, he took up his bowl and sat upon Nanquan’s seat.
When Jue entered the hall, he saw him and asked, "In what year did you begin your practice? Baizhang replied, "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja.
Jue said, "That is still just the descendant of Old Master Wang; go down! Baizhang then took his bowl and passed to the second seat.
Guishan Lingyou said, "Huangbo was very much like one who perishes by deceiving the enemy. Yangshan Huiji said, "Not so;
you must know that Huangbo possessed the mechanism for trapping tigers. Guishan said, "Your insight has grown this far!"
Xuedou Xian said: "It is a pity that Old Master Wang saw only the sharpness of the tip of the awl.

Had I been Nanquan at that time, as soon as he said, 'Before King Wei-yin,' I would have immediately taken the second seat, leaving this fellow Huangbo unable to rise for the rest of his life. Nevertheless, one must still rescue Nanquan."
Yunfeng Yue said: "The monastic communities all say that Huangbo possesses the mechanism for trapping tigers and Nanquan possesses the function of killing tigers.
To speak in such a manner is truly a pity! Little do they realize that this old thief has years but no virtue;
even his eating and sitting do not accord with his true nature. If one were to approach the gate of Yunfeng..."
To say that even before the time of King Weyinwang there were teachers greater than the King is to deserve a beating and be driven out.
Jingshan Huiyuan said:
"Why wait to ask him how many years he has been practicing the Way? As soon as you enter the hall and see him presiding over the assembly..."
Taking his place, he then held up his bowl and sat in the second seat. Even if Huangbo possessed the "trap for tigers" device, where could he have applied it?
Baohua Ren said: "There is gathering and there is releasing; host and guest exchange roles. Indeed, Huangbo was a master craftsman. Not...
"To merely ride the tiger's head while also knowing how to grasp its tail—Nanquan was truly a master at this. Guishan said, "To deceive the enemy is to invite ruin;
it is like pouring oil onto a fire. Yangshan said, "One must know that Huangbo possessed the mechanism for trapping a tiger;
it is much like placing a torch in a cold spot. These four elders each demarcated their own territory and claimed their own domain.
Venerable ones, when fully upheld, all are fully upheld; when deficient, all are deficient.
Today, this mountain monk has bound the father and son of Miu and Yang, along with the uncle and nephew of Nanquan, into a single bundle and cast it before you all.
Furthermore, is there anyone who would speak out on behalf of the four great elders?

Yuyan Yuan said: "Master Wang is advanced in years; why does he not retire from his position, thereby causing his descendants of later generations to defecate upon his head? What kind of principle is this?"
Lingyin Li said: "The mountain monk’s duties as abbot are many and complex; I have no leisure to engage in the entanglements of various disciples.
I shall simply place these two fellows beneath my words to serve as a commentary. Is there anyone here today who can occupy the mountain monk’s seat?
If there is, let the mountain monk present his bowl and return to the abbot’s quarters; let us see how he comports himself."
Sha! Shouchang Cun said: "These two great elders were like kindred spirits responding to one another; it was much like burying troops to engage in combat.
Examining this closely, it was certainly not done with good intentions."
Xidun (Westward Retreat) leaped beyond, saying, "If one overreaches at Mt. Mui, one perishes by deceiving the enemy. Having finished speaking, he said, "Mt.
Mui’s words seem to have missed the mark regarding Huangbo; yet little did he know that this fellow from Mt. Mui was accustomed to casting his hook. It is as the saying goes:
'Borrowing another's fragrant bait to cast into the blue sea, drawing forth the giant k'un-fish and the turtle onto the straight hook. Yangshan said that Huangbo had fallen into a trap."
"The tiger’s mechanism. This remark seems to suggest that his wisdom surpassed that of his teacher.

Upon closer inspection, it is like taking clear water and offering it as a sacrifice to the tide god. The son of Guishan saw things so profoundly that everyone thought he had deeply affirmed Yangshan;
unconsciously, they praised him with their whole mouths. They did not realize that Guishan’s handiwork was even more swift and decisive, for he acted right then and there.
Yangshan’s pivotal occasion was itself enacted through Yangshan’s own person.
Later patriarchs frequently administered this medicinal head to people's mouths, yet they often missed the mark right before their faces. Some have asked:
"Why did Yangshan have no further words at that time? To which one should reply: "Go back and study for thirty more years."
Because Baizhang asked Huangbo, "Dharma-heir Yun, it is no easy matter to clear the fields," Huangbo replied, "I am performing my duties along with the assembly.
Baizhang said, "It must be troublesome for you to apply your Way-power. Huangbo said, "How would I dare refuse such toil? Baizhang asked, "How much field have you cleared?
Huangbo took his mattock and struck the ground three times. Baizhang then gave a shout; Huangbo covered his ears and departed.
Taisu Zhe said: "Huangbo’s cultivation of the fields was not a labor spent in vain; Baizhang’s tenure as abbot did not result in empty commands.
Langya Jue said: "Baizhang’s single shout can truly be called casting a line into a ten-thousand-fathom abyss; Huangbo..."
[He] covered his ears. [Thus he] stood alone atop the peaks of a thousand mountains.
While Huangbo was traveling on pilgrimage at Kaiyuan Temple in Hongzhou, he happened to meet Prime Minister Pei Xiu.
Seeing a portrait on the wall, the Prime Minister asked the temple steward, "What image is that on the wall? The steward replied, "It is the true likeness of a high monk. The Prime Minister said:
"The true countenance may be beheld; where is the eminent monk? The abbot had no reply. The Duke asked, "Is there a Chan master here? The abbot said, "Recently a monk has joined this temple;
he bears much resemblance to a Chan practitioner. The Duke then requested an audience and repeated his previous words, asking, "The true countenance may be beheld;
where is the eminent monk? Baizhang called out in a loud voice, "Pei Xiu! The Duke responded, "Yes. Baizhang said: [The rest of the dialogue follows].
"In what place did the Duke understand the meaning beneath the words?
Jingshan Daoyuan said: "Lord Pei took the wrong for the right; he cast off all root and dust. Huangbo bestowed compassion spontaneously, without expending a thought or effort.
It was like the earth supporting a mountain, unaware of the mountain's towering loftiness; it was like a stone containing jade."
One does not know that jade is without flaw. Nevertheless, Huangbo possesses only the "sword that kills" and lacks the "sword that gives life.
Today, if Grand Councilor Dazai were to ask Yunmen, "The true image of the High Monk may be beheld;
where is he? Yunmen would likewise summon the Councilor. If the Councilor responds with an "Amen," Yunmen would immediately say to him: "Now..."
In the hall on that day, there was a special expression of gratitude for the offerings.
Tianning Qi said, "Minister Pei, where is the Way-superior monk? This clearly changes one's very eyes.
Huangbo further called out, "Prime Minister!"—firmly attaching a handle to a bowl. Old Miaoxi has given people a mistaken commentary.
He stepped forward and said, "It is like the earth supporting a mountain without knowing the mountain's towering loftiness, or like a stone containing jade without knowing the jade's flawlessness.
You have missed it. Tianning, however, was not like this. He also called out, "Minister!
When the Minister responded, Tianning struck him across the back with his staff, lest this fellow be drowned in the stagnant waters of death.
Boshan Fenyun said: "Although Huangbo fanned the fire with the wind, he did not exert much effort;
yet when one examines him closely, he possesses only the sword that kills, but lacks the sword that gives life."
Once Huangbo was traveling to Tiantai when he encountered a monk on the road who appeared to be an old acquaintance. He gazed at him intently; the monk’s gaze pierced others.

They traveled together until they reached a mountain stream where the water had suddenly swollen. Huangbo planted his staff and stood there. The monk urged him to cross with him, but Huangbo said, "If you wish to cross, brother, cross by yourself.
The monk then lifted his robes and stepped across the waves as if walking on level ground. Looking back, he called out, "Come across! Come across!"
Huangbo said, "Tsk! You self-satisfied fellow! I should have known to chop off your shins long ago. The monk sighed and said, "Truly a vessel for the Mahāyāna Dharma; I am not his equal."
Huìyún said: "Huangbo had the courage but lacked the heart to let this monk go. When he saw him crossing over, he should have said to him, 'You only know how to go like that;
you do not know how to come like this. Had he waited for the monk to cross back, he would have taken up his staff and struck him soundly."
One day Huangbo clenched his fist and said, "All the old monks of the world are right here. If I let out a single thread of opportunity, they will run wild in every direction;
if I do not let them pass, it takes no more than this one squeeze. A monk then asked, "What is it like when you let out a single thread?
Huangbo replied, "Running wild in every direction. The monk asked, "And what about when you do not let them pass? Huangbo replied, "It takes no more than this one squeeze."
"What is it like at that time? Baizhang replied, "Universal.
Yunmen Wenyan, when asked by a monk, "What is the sevenfold freedom and eightfold ease? said, "The old monk thinks of his own old age. "What is 'universal'?
Yunmen said, "The light of heaven shines back. "What is 'the light of heaven shining back'? Yunmen said— [text ends].
"Yun-gu’s Beak is little known by few.
Huangbo addressed the assembly: "Since Master Bodhidharma arrived in this land, he has spoken only of the One Mind and transmitted only the One Dharma."
One transmits the Buddha through the Buddha, not through other Buddhas; one transmits the Dharma through the Dharma, not by speaking of other dharmas.
The Dharma is the ineffable Dharma; the Buddha is the ungraspable Buddha. The Buddha is precisely the fundamentally pure mind.
Ruigan Yun said: "Huangbo was merely breathing out through the nostrils of Master Bodhidharma; he thought there was no one to examine him.
This mountain monk is not suppressing his majestic brilliance, but simply wishes for domestic peace and household tranquility."
Huangbo was once invited by Minister Pei Xiu, who presented him with a statue and knelt before him, requesting, "I beg the Master to bestow a name upon it. Huangbo called out, "Pei Xiu!
The official responded, "Yes. Huangbo said, "I have finished bestowing the name upon you. The official then prostrated himself and said, "Thank you, Master, for bestowing the name."
Xuedou Xian, acting on behalf of Baizhang Huaihu at that time, simply gave a shout.
Jingshan Daokai said, "Lord Pei and Huangbo may truly be described as water entering water, or gold exchanging for gold.
Nevertheless, when examined closely, there is still no lack of leakage. Today, if Minister Cai were to present one...
When the Honored Image requested Yunmen to bestow a name upon it, Yunmen immediately said, "The Pure Dharmakāya Vairocana Buddha.
If one says, "Thank you, Master, for bestowing the name," Yunmen further said, "Going downhill, do not run; such a swift opportunity is difficult to encounter."
Tianning Qisong said: "When Lord Pei held up the image and Huangbo bestowed its name, it was like a Confucian teacher instructing a new bride—it was truly laughable.

One could laugh for thirty years. Since Miaoxi could not cut off the flow of conceptualization, he could not avoid following the worldly pattern of inversion; he simply called it the 'Pure Dharmakāya Vairocana.'"
The Buddha [enjoined the use of] *zhū* wood; the people of the Zhou used cypress; the people of the Yin used chestnut.
Because Huangbo was asked by Nanquan, "Regarding the equal cultivation of concentration and wisdom (*samādhi* and *prajñā*) to clearly perceive the Buddha-nature—how is this principle?

Huangbo replied, "Only when, throughout the twelve periods of the day, one does not rely upon or depend on a single thing can it be achieved. Nanquan said, "Is this not precisely your own realization, Elder?"
Baizhang said, "I dare not. Nanquan said, "Setting aside the payment for the gruel and water for a moment, who will repay the cost of the straw sandals? Baizhang then withdrew.
Yunfeng Yue said, "If one does not sleep on the same bed, how can one know that the lining of the quilt is worn through?"
Jingshan Hongdao said: "When meeting a swordsman on the road, you must present your sword; if you are not a poet, do not offer your poem.
Tianning Weiqi said: "This is gaining the advantage, yet it is also losing the advantage."
Yuan'an Meng said: "I, this old monk, am not like that. Nanquan returned the money for the rice gruel; Huangbo paid back the money for the straw sandals.
Have you not seen it said: 'The thief is a petty person whose cunning surpasses that of a gentleman'?"

When Huangbo encountered six newly arrived monks, five of them prostrated themselves. One monk held up his sitting mat and drew a circle. Huangbo said, "I have heard there is a very fierce hunting dog here.
The monk replied, "It comes seeking the sound of the antelope. Huangbo said, "The antelope makes no sound; where would you go to seek it?
The monk said, "It comes seeking the tracks of the antelope. Huangbo said, "The antelope leaves no tracks; where would you go to find them?"
The monk asked, "I have been searching. Huangbo said, "The antelope leaves no tracks; tell me how you search.

The monk said, "If that is so, then it is a dead antelope. Huangbo then ceased speaking. The next day, he ascended the seat and said, "Yesterday’s monk who was searching for the antelope, come forward!
The monk came out. Huangbo said, "Yesterday’s case was not yet settled. I, the old monk, stopped speaking. How did you proceed?"
Sheng remained silent. Baizhang said, "I thought you were a monk of true substance; it turns out you are merely a scholar-monk.
He struck him with his staff and drove him out.
Xuedou Xian said: "As for sounds and traces being non-existent, where would a hunting dog go to seek them out?

Is it by cutting off all sounds and traces that one encounters Huangbo? O Zen practitioners, if you wish to clarify the mechanism of 'falling into the tiger's trap,' you must also be a patch-robed monk of the true lineage."
Gunanmen said: "At Huangbo’s hook there is bait; this monk followed the hook straight up.
Although that is so, since he has become a hunting dog, why is it that even when a langur monkey arrives right before him, he does not recognize it?
If he were a true man, when Huangbo said, "The langur is silent—go find it," he would have immediately seized him and said, "This old fellow was originally just..."
To be here like this—then you have at least a whiff of the true spirit of a monk. Even if Huangbo possessed the trap for ensnaring tigers, where else could he possibly set it?
Longhua Ti said: "Xuedou has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake; he brings Huangbo down into the pit of fame and traces.

At that time, if that monk had been a son of the Dharma in his true sense, when Huangbo said, 'The wild sheep leaves no sound for you to seek,' he should have simply replied, 'No need to examine further,' and then swept his sleeves and departed. Even if Huangbo were to manifest his whole being..."
"This is the eye. [Baizhang] could not discern his intent.
Baofu Da said, "To answer in such a manner is very much like being under the influence of wine. Where has the one who then confronted Linji gone?
It leaves people with nothing but doubt. He then said, "The public case from yesterday is not yet settled; I, the old monk..."
"Stop! What do you make of this? You are a man who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. I should give this monk a formal indictment for his conduct.
Chan Master Changqing Da'an of Fuzhou (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan and Baizhang Huaihai) resided at Dayang Mountain and was known as Lanyan. While in his room, he would frequently ask monks:
"There is a phrase, there is no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. What is the meaning of this? When Shushan Ren heard of this, he went specifically...

He entered the mountain range to seek further instruction. He encountered Mazu Daoyi while he was plastering a wall. He asked, "The saying that 'having a phrase or not having a phrase is like a vine leaning against a tree'—is this not the Master’s own words?
Mazu replied, "It is. Duanzhou Shan said, "If suddenly the tree falls and the vine withers, where do the phrases return?"
Dongshan Qing set down his mud-tray and laughed heartily as he returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Deshan Shan followed behind him and said, "I have traveled three thousand *li* selling my straw mat, coming specifically for this matter. Why does the Master deceive me?
Qing called to his attendant, "Bring two hundred coins and give them to this elder. He then instructed him, saying, "In the future, there will be the 'One-Eyed Dragon' (Yunyan Tansheng)."
You have already pointed it out. Later, when Guishan reached Mingzhao, he brought up the previous conversation.

Mingzhao said, "Daguang can truly be called 'head straight and tail straight,' yet he simply did not meet a true connoisseur; even Guishan did not reach accord. Guishan then asked again, "When the tree falls and the vines wither, where does the phrase return?
Mingzhao said, "It makes Guishan’s laughter all the more fresh. At these words, Guishan attained great enlightenment and said:
It turns out that in his smile, Guishan originally held a blade.
After Kaifeng Ning had finished speaking the words "a phrase with no phrase," he remained silent for a long while and said: "Do you understand?
Deep autumn rain fills the curtains of a thousand homes; the setting sun brings the wind of a flute to the towers."
Tianmu Li said: "A phrase and no-phrase are like a vine leaning against a tree; they cut off all distinctions, yet a venomous snake lies across the path.
When the tree falls and the vine withers, where does the phrase return? This old monk could not resolve this for five years."
Baoneng Xiu said: "If Wansong had been asked at that time, 'The phrase with a line and the phrase without a line—like a vine leaning against a tree;
when the tree falls and the vine withers, where does the phrase return? he would simply have replied, 'The azure heavens! The azure heavens! Why? Have you not heard it said:
'Spring is proceeding with the ordinances of winter'?"
Gao Feng said: "A phrase, no phrase—the golden crow swallows the jade hare. Like a vine leaning against a tree; a mangy horse tied to a withered post.
When the tree falls, the vine withers; burned all winter long, it is not yet exhausted. Where do these phrases return?
A stone tiger crouches in the path. Ha! Ha! Great laughter! A dragon’s head and a snake’s tail—knocked down into the mire. A sharp blade does not cut."
"A person without fault. He then asked, "Tell me, where does the error of Guishan lie? Thereupon, he laughed heartily and descended from his seat.
Chan Master Huanzhong of Daci in Hangzhou (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan) ascended the hall and said: "I, this mountain monk, cannot answer questions; I can only recognize the illness.
At that time, a monk stepped forward, and Huanzhong immediately returned to his quarters.
Baoci then pressed him, saying: "Tell me, does Great Compassion recognize the illness or not? Is this monk who has come forth an illness or not?
If you say he is an illness, then his daily walking and staying cannot all be the illness.
If you say he is not an illness, then what is he when he comes forth?"
Xuedou Xian said: "In general, to uphold the lineage of the School, one must discern right from wrong. Now, Daci recognized the illness but did not answer the monk's question;
at that time, a monk came forward and immediately returned to the abbot’s quarters. Xuedou recognized the illness but did not answer the question."

There was a monk who came forward; [the Master] struck him across the back with his staff. Those from various regions who recognized this as a "sickness" (a pedagogical device) did not engage in dialogue.
There was another monk who came forward; he certainly possessed some special capacity, for he dared to provoke him. "The Son of Heaven of the Great Tang has only three [monks]."
Huanglong Nan said, "It is a pity he was let off. At that time, had I seen him come out, I would have struck him across the back with my staff.
Had I waited for him to realize where the blow came from, he might have avoided being scrutinized by others for a thousand ages.
Today, Huanglong recognizes the illness and understands how to respond. Suppose a man were to come out and overturn the meditation seat—[what then?]"
How would you handle this? All you venerable seniors, please offer a turning phrase on my behalf and see.
Cuiyan Zhi said: "As soon as this monk stepped out, Daci immediately returned to his quarters; there was no principle involved at all."
"What place is the locus of the sickness of consciousness? Now you must also examine this closely.
Tiantong Jue said: "Both Daci and Xuedou were masters; yet, while they looked ahead, they did not watch their steps.
Suppose there were someone who did not distinguish between good and bad, nor inquire about east and west, who came forth—then...
He overturned the meditation seat. Even if you possess the full functioning of the great capacity, I fear that when it comes to putting it into practice, you will not be able to manage it.
At such a moment as this, is there anyone who possesses the eye that recognizes the illness?
Baoning Mocheng said, "Great Compassion is well suited for compounding medicine according to the prescription, yet it is difficult to administer the medicine to one's own illness.
Nantang Yu said, "Xuedou may cause his fragrance to flow through the ages, but he has not yet reached the point of total eradication.
According to my own view, you must strike him and drag him out. Why? Because the great ocean does not harbor a corpse.
Yuan'an Yu said: "If it were not for this monk, how could one see the national master? But tell me, what illness does this monk have?
I say it is precisely this questioning. Do you accept it?"
Gunan said: "Gunan also cannot answer the question; he can only recognize the illness. When a monk stepped forward, Gunan simply said:
"A disease of the vital organs (gao-huang) cannot be cured by medical treatment. "The great assembly has already been moved and touched," [he added]. "If you can properly take this up..."
This is indeed counted among the thousand Buddhas.
Tiantong Muan said: "There are only three Emperors of the Great Tang. Xuedou is far too brazen to point this out himself;
the various quarters must surely have their own superior insights. It is better for a needle to remain inside a cloth bag than to poke its head out.
"Hand! Although this is so, once one has seen the meaning, it is not unbrave to act accordingly. Now, this mountain monk also recognizes the illness and does not answer questions;
should a monk come forward, I simply let out a great laugh. If this were the standard practice of other quarters, there would surely be many 'guests from Jiangnan' in the assembly."
Baoshou Xin says: "Daci and Xuedou not only diagnose the illness of consciousness, but also commandeer its remedy.
Even if you had Lu Ban or Bian Que, you would have to fold your hands and surrender. Nevertheless, if the illness has reached the vital organs (gao-huang), how will you treat it?
'Blind seven, blind eight.'"
Longhua Ti said: "Bianshan also did not answer the question; he merely recognized the illness.
He waited for a monk to come forward and simply told him, 'Do not move earth on the head of the Tai-sui. As soon as the monk hesitated, he struck him with a staff and drove him out."
Baiyan Fu said: "The Dragon Gate rises ten thousand fathoms high, and the snow-white waves reach the heavens.
Unless one possesses the skill to seize the mist and clutch the clouds, those who arrive here will inevitably return with their foreheads marked. Nevertheless, do you recognize this monk?"
Daciyan said: "Old man Xingkong, although letting him go was perilous, bringing him back was too hasty.
Upon careful examination, he has been completely accounted for by this monk in a single statement."

Xishan Yin said: "This mountain monk does not recognize illness; I simply answer the question. When a monk comes forward, I say: 'Today this mountain monk has a toothache. Daci asked Zhaozhou, "What is the essence of prajñā? Zhaozhou replied, "Prajñā—what is its essence? Daci said, "Prajñā—what is its essence? Zhaozhou replied, "The essence of prajñā is the essence of prajñā. Daci said, "If so, what is the essence of the essence of prajñā? Zhaozhou said, "The essence of the essence of prajñā is the essence of the essence of prajñā. Daci said, "If so, what is the essence of the essence of the essence of prajñā? Zhaozhou said, "The essence of the essence of the essence of prajñā is the essence of the essence of the essence of prajñā. Daci said, "If so, what is the essence of the essence of the essence of the essence of prajñā? Zhaozhou said, "The essence of the essence of the essence of the essence of prajñā is the essence of the essence of the essence of the essence of prajñā.
