How can one avoid this fault? You people, do you wish to understand? I return Venerable Zhaozhou’s meal to you."
"The porridge is not yet finished. [Yunmen] picked it up; this monk has already finished eating his porridge. Xuedou gives you a staff;
go back to the hall. Yungfeng Yue said: "Yunmen speaking in such a manner is very much like growing a beard for a eunuch or painting patterns on a snake."
[The Master] said, "It is sufficient. The mountain monk, however, does not think so. For this monk to have awakened in such a manner is like being shot by an arrow straight into hell.

Huanglong Xin said, "Although Yunmen and Xuedou were skilled at uprooting the strong to support the weak and abandoning the wealthy to follow the poor, they nonetheless could not establish a home or found a state.
He then asked the monk, "Did you eat porridge this morning and wash your bowl?"
"Now, as for this delusion and this awakening," the monk bowed and rose. Longmen Yuan called him forward and said, "I have a fly-whisk;
I give it to you. Return to the hall.
Longmen Yuan then said, "The mountain monk has finished eating his congee today; he has finished washing his bowl. It is simply..."
They do not awaken. Since they are good spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), why do they not awaken? Do you understand? How could one call a bell a jar?
One would never point to a deer and call it a horse. A good person is difficult to offend; mercury has no counterfeit.
If you suddenly see through it in a moment of clarity, you can be certain that everything will be laid down at once.
Kaifuning said: "Great assembly, tell me: where was this monk’s place of awakening? Do you understand thoroughly?
'Various shades of cloud emerge from the mountain peak; a single tone of spring water falls before the railing.'"
Jingshan Daowu said: "Yunmen is much like the Asura King who shakes the great cities of the three realms and the ocean of all afflictions.

He then shouted, "What is this 'sleeping talk'? He further said: "Although Yunfeng was skilled at drawing a golden arrow from behind his back and turning his body to draw the horned bow, what could he do? He simply missed Yunmen. He also said: "Zhaozhou..."
Had this monk not encountered Yunmen, he would have suffered a lifelong grievance.
Nowadays, there is a certain kind of blind fellow everywhere who invariably interprets this as the "story of washing the alms bowl."
Tianning Qi said: "Good sirs, it is easy to see Yunmen; it is difficult to see Miaoxi.
Where does the confusion lie? The sword has long since been lost, yet you are still marking the boat."

Yunju Zhuang said: "Zhaozhou uses a wedge to extract a wedge; Yunmen looks at the tower and strikes the tower. This monk has attained awakening—does he have any point where he was thoroughly scrutinized or not?
After a long silence, he said: 'The wind does not whistle through the branches; the rain does not break up the clods of earth.'"
Gunanmen said: "Stop! Stop! Xuedou only knows that Yunmen was like drawing legs on a snake that has none;
he himself could not avoid being like a sacred tortoise dragging its tail. But if you were to set all this aside at once, what then? Blind!"
Yuan'an Yu said: "Zhaozhou squats inside a jar of scorpions; Yunmen sits and lies within a pit of snakes;
Yunfeng plays amidst a den of tigers. The scorpions cannot sting, the snakes cannot poison, and the tigers cannot deploy their claws and fangs.
Truly, they are masters of the subtle hand! According to my own judgment, even Zhaozhou has no way to wash it away."
The "Bowl" Anecdote. Even if Yunmen possessed the brush of a master painting a snake, where could he possibly add feet?
It was Yunfeng who entered hell; this monk entered hell. [The Master] strikes the desk once and says:
"Today, I take the radiant countenances and the wondrous functions of the spiritual powers of these three great elders and present them before you all. You lacquer buckets!"
"How regrettable! If you attempt to deliberate upon this as if it were the Buddha-dharma, you will enter hell like an arrow shot from a bow. He let out a shout and said:
"Amidst the purple and emerald mists and vapors of ten thousand mountains, their varying shades and shifting depths cannot be captured in a painting."
Dongmingji said: "Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao, Chen, Si, Wu, Wei—within this, those who know the sound have no taboos.
A-he-he! Do you understand yet? Whether at the top of the feet or beneath them, one acts with total freedom. What is there of value in the wind and moon of Chang’an?"
Qinghuo said, "One drags his skirt to the ground; the other's trousers are even longer.
Although this monk has attained awakening, he will only ever master the affairs of servants and maids."
Furiji said: "Great Wisdom has picked up and examined this in many directions across all quarters, and he has provided numerous annotations.
Yet, not a single person has ever clearly explained it through and through. Today, Miaoxi shall explain it clearly for you all:
having finished eating rice gruel, one washes the bowl. Tell me, has he ever pointed it out? Black beans have been so from the beginning."
It is well to blend the sauce. A bhikṣuṇī is certainly a śramaṇerī. This old fellow Dàhuì has teeth like a forest of swords and a mouth like a blood-basin;
it turns out he was always right here. As for the story of washing the alms bowl, how could it ever have been explained?
Tonight, Longan will spare no effort to speak clearly for all of you: after eating porridge, wash the alms bowl;
a gourd hangs on the eastern wall of Zhaozhou; having grasped the nose, one is struck for losing one’s mouth;
Bodhidharma was not an old scrawny beard.

Benjue’s *Weiyuan lu* says: "The Great and Small Zhaozhou are both drumming up the stench of rice and gruel. Even if this monk had attained enlightenment, it would still be like thrusting one's head into a vat of glue.
When Zhaozhou arrived at Huangbo, Huangbo saw him coming and immediately closed the door to his quarters; Zhaozhou then held a torch before the Dharma hall.
Inside the hall, someone cried out, "Save us from the fire! Save us from the fire! Huangbo opened the door, seized him, and said, "Speak! Speak! Zhaozhou replied, "The thief has already fled;
drawing the bow afterward. Baofu Zhan said, "Huangbo has a head but no tail; Zhaozhou has a tail but no head."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "Huangbo only knows how to buy cheap; he does not know how to sell dear. Zhaozhou turned misfortune into fortune.
Xuedou Xian said: "Truly laughable! One could laugh for thirty years. Suppose a monk were to suddenly ask:"
"What are you laughing at? Laughing at 'drawing the bow after the thief has fled.
Nantang wanted to say: 'Beating the wooden clappers at the double gates'—Huangbo was being overly defensive.
'Biting the arrowhead and breaking through the pass'—Zhaozhou was habitually seizing the advantage. Although neither harmed the other, they have broken Xuedou’s nostrils."
Gunanmen said: "Xuedou’s laugh is indeed fine; it is simply that he did not fail to follow the conversational thread of Zhaozhou.
After all, what is it? Thief! Thief!"
Yunxi Ting said: "One opens the door to let the thief in; another ties up his topknot and goes to the yamen.
This provokes the laughter of the yellow-mouthed children until their lips and skin are split."
Zhaozhou was discussing the meaning of the teachings with his attendant Wenyuan, saying, "We shall compete on the basis of inferiority, not superiority; the winner shall lose a sesame cake.
Wenyuan said, "I ask the Master to state your thesis. Zhaozhou said, "I am a donkey. Wenyuan said, "I am a donkey's stomach."
Zhaozhou said, "I am donkey dung. Yuan said, "I am a worm in the dung. Zhaozhou asked, "What are you doing there?
Yuan said, "I am spending the summer retreat there. Zhaozhou said, "Bring me that sesame cake!"
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said, "Calamity does not come alone.
Langya Huijue said, "Zhaozhou Wenyuan was like Xiao He establishing the penal code.
Jingshan Hongzheng Daokai said, "Wenyuan spent the summer retreat amidst donkey dung; a flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech. Zhao— [text fragment] —.
The Governor greedily sought a small profit and won only this "Hu-bing" (barley cake). Even upon close inspection, it turns out he was a man from Puzhou who delivered a thief.
Ultimately, how is it? A king of geese chooses its milk; it is simply not of the same class as a duck.
Tiantong Jue said: "The high is so lofty it cannot be pointed out; the low is so deep it cannot be reached. The eyes compete for the first prize;
the tally is won by tying a knot. Tianning Qi said:
"At that time, Wenyuan should have waited for Zhaozhou to say, 'I am a donkey,' and then [acted]."
Dàoshū had already lost the sesame cake. The old man reached for the cake, snatched it from his hand, and walked away.
Bǎohuā Rèn said: "Wényuǎn won within a loss; he was defeated in the light but victorious in the dark. Zhàozhōu won within a loss; he was victorious in the light but defeated in the dark.
As soon as one wins, one loses; as soon as one loses, one wins. Calculated thus, there is no share of the sesame cake at all. Now..."
I pick this up for everyone to see: to move even slightly toward it is to become a laughingstock.
*Duḥ!* Yanjiao Le said: "Zhaozhou only knew how to hurry along the path, failing to notice he had taken the wrong road;
although Wenyuan lost the fruit-cake, he nonetheless gained an unacknowledged advantage. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, let those with eyes discern it.
While traveling, Zhaozhou encountered an old woman on the road. He asked her, "Where are you going? The woman replied, "I am going to steal Zhaozhou’s bamboo shoots.
Zhaozhou said, "What will you do if you suddenly encounter Zhaozhou? The woman then gave him a slap. Zhaozhou then desisted.
Xuedou Xian said, "A fine slap! Even if you were to give him two more slaps, there would still be no place for examination.
Wuzu Yan said, "Zhaozhou has already ceased; how will you discuss this? Baoyun revealed a message.
This is known to all you honorable and eminent ones. Although the old woman exercised her rightful authority, she failed to reach a resolution in her lifetime.

Zhaozhou was struck twice with her palms, yet he bit down on his teeth with unyielding resolve. It can be said that the old woman’s path forward was as light as a single leaf, while Zhaozhou’s lofty reputation remains as heavy as a mountain for a thousand ages.
Nantang Yu said: "I thought the barbarian must have a red beard; yet there is a barbarian with a red beard.
Longchi Chuan said: "Tell me, when Zhaozhou said 'Stop,' did he approve of him or not?"
Gounan said, "Today Zhaozhou has gone out a little way and encountered a great calamity.
Nanshan Bao said, "Both of these fellows have fallen so gravely ill that even acupuncture and medicine can do nothing to save them.
If anyone can examine this and see through it, I will grant them that they possess one eye."
Yuanzhao Sen said: "Do you still recognize this old fellow Zhaozhou? Clouds drift like threads; the wind carries the cotton-wool.
Tell those traveling on the road: do not go up the mountain peak."
Ou-feng Cheng said: "The thief is a petty person, yet his cunning surpasses that of a gentleman.
Bai-yan Fu said: "This old woman not only stole the bamboo shoots, but also took the bamboo back with her;
one could say her 'theft-of-heaven' skill is no less than that of Shi-zhi. Yet, as for Zhaozhou’s 'resting,' how could it merely be a theft of heaven?"
Thus it was said.
One day, Zhaozhou lay prostrate in the snow and cried out, "Save me! Save me! A monk went over and lay down beside him;
Zhaozhou then got up and left.
Cuiyan Zhi said: "This monk is within Zhaozhou’s circle; is there anyone who can get out? Tiantong Hua said:
"This monk is like an insect gnawing through wood; he does not realize that Zhaozhou’s realm is worlds apart.
There are some blind fellows who immediately say, "The Master supports the strong and does not support the weak," yet they do not know that within the treasury of our King—
"There is no such sword. [He] let out a shout. Shengfafa said:
"This monk only knows how to save others; he does not know how to save himself.
When Zhaozhou arrived at Daowu, as soon as he entered the hall, Daowu said, "Nanquan’s single arrow is coming! Zhaozhou said, "Watch!"
Dowu said, "It missed. Zhaozhou said, "It hit. (Some editions read "ju yu" [holy basil] instead; this is incorrect. Here we follow the *Huiyuan*.
Xuedou Xian said, "Both were adepts. In fact, both Dowu and Zhaozhou were not adepts at all.
"The tips of arrows do not meet; even if they were shot and hit simultaneously, one would still be nothing more than a mere archer at a target.
Baoci then said, "Now tell me, when these two great elders met, was there any superiority or inferiority between them?
If you can discern this, I will grant that you have found an entrance into the very midst of it."
The Ancient Southern Gate says: Zhaozhou and Daowu bared their fangs and claws; they were not mistaken in being of the same lineage. Nevertheless, as Xuedou said:
"Even if they were to shoot simultaneously, they are still nothing but marksmen. Does he approve of them, or does he disapprove? Do you understand?

A master displays his mastery within the hands of a master; in the heart of a red heart— *Note: The phrase "紅心心裏" (hóng xīn xīn lǐ) is a classical Zen expression indicating the direct, unmediated realization of the truth.*
[He] struck the meditation seat once with his hand. Mingzhao supplemented this by saying:
"A fine hand displaying its skill before another fine hand—Vzhou was certainly not lacking in this. However, for a true master, there is no 'beak-picking' (the hen pecking and the chick picking).
If they are simultaneous, both are lost. So, how would you handle it?"
Zhaozhou, seeing a monk sweeping the floor, asked him, "Sweeping like this, is it ever truly clean? The monk replied, "The more I sweep, the more there is.
Zhaozhou said, "Is there no one who brushes away the dust? The monk asked, "Who is it that brushes away the dust? Zhaozhou looked at him and said, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. Zhaozhou said, "Go ask Yunju. Later, the monk asked Yunju, "What is it that brushes away the dust?"
"Regarding 'dust'—the one who sits there is a blind fellow.
Ancient Tang said, "The two elders failed to cut it off when they ought to have; this monk thus sweeps on and on until it becomes more and more. I, this mountain monk, am not like that.
When he asks, "Who is the one who brushes away the dust? I would immediately snatch the broom from him and give him a thorough beating.
"Sudden. Why is it so? Has it not been said: "If one is to act for others, one must act with thoroughness"?
When Zhaozhou saw Attendant Wenyuan bowing to the Buddha in the Buddha Hall, Zhaozhou struck him once with his staff and asked, "What are you doing?
Wenyuan replied, "Bowing to the Buddha is also a good thing. Zhaozhou said, "A good thing is not as good as having nothing at all."
Zhongfeng Ben says: Wenyuan said, "To prostrate to the Buddha is also a good thing; it does not hinder one's dullness.
Zhaozhou said, "A good thing is not as good as having none at all. The conversation has already fallen into error. Do you wish to know the old man Zhaozhou’s words as they apply everywhere?
Wait until his skull is smashed open, and then I shall tell you.
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? Zhaozhou said, "No.
The monk said, "From the Buddhas above down to the ants below, all possess Buddha-nature. Why then does the dog lack it?

Zhaozhou replied, "It is because he still possesses the consciousness of karmic activity (*karmavijñāna*). Later, another monk asked Zhaozhou, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? Zhaozhou said, "Yes. The monk...
[The Master] said: "Since it exists, why has it entered this skin-bag? Dongshan said: "Because it knows and yet deliberately commits the offense. Cuiyan Zhi said:
"To speak of existence and to speak of non-existence are two colors and one match. What about now?"
Gao Feng said: "The Great and Small Zhaozhou brought forth a single grain of *bādara* (barberry) seed, which churns up the entrails of the patch-robed monks.
Even those who might manage to swallow or spit it out cannot avoid losing their lives. Why? Because it is urgent!"

Boshan came forward and said: "Whether the Way exists or does not exist, the sharp blade is held crosswise. All people throughout the great earth have their share in seeking life at the hands of Zhaozhou;
only those who do not step over the stone bridge are not included within this limit. Why is that?"
"Though a sharp blade is swift, it does not slay the innocent.
Yungan Yuan said, "This monk is like a pig-seller from Liaodong who has obtained a white-necked pig and considers it a rare treasure;
yet upon arriving in Huainan, he finds himself utterly ashamed and without ground to stand on. That old fellow Zhaozhou is truly excellent."
He resembles a fine-bearded gentleman who is accustomed to wielding a trailing blade; his stratagems do not emerge from ordinary schemes.
If it were I, a mountain monk, it would not be so. Should someone ask, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? I would simply say to them, "A scabby dog swallows a frog."
Baiyan Fu said: "When this fellow Zhaozhou casually utters a single word, it may be a 'resuscitating incense' that raises the dead and returns life in an instant;
yet it may also be 'poisoned wine' that causes one to lose their body and forfeit their life in a mere moment.
But tell me, why can it be so beneficial and so perilous? After a long silence, he said: 'It is because he possesses the efficacious talisman behind his elbow.'"
Zhaozhou once said, "People of the present day must act within the 'different species' before they can succeed.
Zhaozhou asked, "I do not ask about the 'different'; what is the 'species'? Nanquan pressed both hands to the ground. Zhaozhou stepped forward and kicked him over.
He went back to the Nirvana Hall and cried out, "Regret! Regret! Master Quan had an attendant ask him, "Regret for what?
Xiangzhou said, "I regret not having given him another two kicks."
Baiyan Fu said: "When at the end of the road, one does not know how to turn; when the blade reaches its sharpest point, one lacks the skill to evade.
These are all men who have fallen and died. Nanquan and his son may indeed be said to be skilled at turning and skilled at evading;
yet, if one examines them closely, they still lack one move. Tell me, where is it that they lack this one?"
Regarding the "point of application," Tianjing Xin said: "Nanquan was short of one move compared to Zhaozhou; Zhaozhou lost one turn to Nanquan. How do you understand this?
"A thousand-year-old scrap of paper is good for compounding medicine."
Zhaozhou addressed the assembly: "Tonight, this old monk shall provide answers. Let anyone who can ask a question bring one forward.
At that time, a monk came out and bowed. Zhaozhou said, "I intended to throw a brick to draw forth a jade gem, yet instead I have drawn forth nothing but a cinder block."
Baoshou Zhaoyun said, "If one does not truly hit the tiger, one's efforts are in vain and the feathers are lost.
Fayen Yi raised this question to Jue Tiezui, asking, "What is the meaning of this? Jue said, "It is like the state appointing a general."
He then asked, "Who can go? When someone came forward and said, "I, [Name], can go," he must say, "You cannot go.
The student then says, "I understand."
Baoci then said, "Where does it become a brick? Within the monastic community, they say that as soon as one comes out, one becomes a brick.
Yet, in our daily coming and going, walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, we cannot all be bricks.
Tell me, when this monk came out, did he possess the eye of discernment or not?"
Guangxiao Jueyin was asked by Changqing: "When that monk had just come out and prostrated, why did you immediately treat him as a brick?
Guangxiao said, "Just now, someone over there asked the same thing. Changqing asked, "What did you say to him?
Guangxiao replied, "I told him that 'recently one throws a brick to draw out a jade,' yet instead, he drew out a brick."
Master Xuedou Xian said: "A person of keen intelligence, upon hearing a single mention, immediately knows where it lands.
Even so, let us let go of Jue’s iron beak. Now, the words of a master of the school do not issue forth in vain; whoever comes forward must surely be an adept."
For what reason does one throw a brick to draw out the tile? O virtuous practitioners of Chan, do you wish to know Zhaozhou?
No one has recognized his past labors on the battlefield; he simply wishes to reassert his merit that covers the age.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Everywhere it is said that Zhaozhou attained a mechanism that transcends the crowd; his provisional arrangements for a single occasion were indeed free and at ease.
Yet this monk, wishing to strike the rhythm and knock open the barrier, failed to manage his hands and feet within the flash of lightning.
Zhaojue’s iron-beaked [wit] is able to draw near analogies, so as not to let the ancestral wind fall; Fayen possesses a mirror that penetrates all quarters."
As soon as [the words] were uttered, he knew where they would land. I dare ask you all: since he was a master of the school, why did he throw a brick and only manage to draw out a mere cinder-block?
Bayan Fu said: "Master Jue misused his terminology; Fayan followed the words and gave rise to conceptual interpretations. Let this matter rest for now.
This was a matter of principle. Zhaozhou used his influence to deceive people; he must not have let this monk off.
Had that monk come forward at that time and immediately overturned the meditation seat, let us see what kind of final judgment he would have received.
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "What is the man-eating lion? Zhaozhou replied, "Take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha; do not bite the old monk."
Tianning Qisong said: "This monk is merely a dung-eating dog. Why? As soon as Zhaozhou saw him, he immediately spat out his excrement and rushed toward the scavenger's den."
Once, a monk asked Zhaozhou, "The ultimate Way is without difficulty; it only dislikes discrimination. Is this the nest of people of this age?
Zhaozhou said, "Someone once asked me this, and for five years I could not properly respond."
Xuedou Xian said: "If one cannot turn the words of recognition, one is already dead; twenty blows are well-deserved.
These blows must have their due recipient; if you cannot discern this, let this story circulate widely for now."
Gunan says: Zhaozhou’s response clearly discerned the wind coming from afar.
Xuedou said, "If you cannot turn the words of recognition, it would be better to die; he too deserves twenty blows. Gunan says, "Endlessly, endlessly.
He further says, "This blow must have its place of delivery. If you cannot discern this, let this story circulate widely for now. Gunan.
"I say: 'Blind! If anyone can discern this, they will surely stride alone through the crimson heavens.
Yuyan Meng said, "Even the ancient Buddha Zhaozhou could not speak for five years;
how much more so for others? You all simply go on opening your mouths recklessly. At that time, a monk standing nearby laughed at him. I then struck him three times.
The commentary says: "Present this for a person with clear eyes to examine.
When Zhaozhou arrived at Baizhang, Baizhang asked, "Where have you recently come from? Zhaozhou said, "From Nanquan.
Baizhang asked, "What sayings or phrases has Nanquan spoken lately? Zhaozhou said, "Those who have not yet attained must remain profoundly still. Baizhang then gave a shout, and Zhaozhou bowed.
Feeling intimidated, Zhaozhou said, "How wonderful, such profound stillness. Thereupon, he performed a dance and departed.
Langya Huijue remarked, "The old man Zhaozhou has secured his claws and fangs from within the lion’s den."
Zhaojue Qin said: "When masters of the Way meet, neither can grasp the other; they are left in a state of blank stillness.
Advancing or retreating, one cannot mold them nor fashion them. One does not travel the great highway, but wanders through the weeds."
Tiantong Muan said: "The thief is a petty person whose cunning surpasses that of a gentleman.
Yet between these two types of thieves, there is one who is a true thief and one who is a mere bandit. If you can definitively distinguish them, I will grant that you are a man of substance."
"Not so. You must wear [the robe] as a thief.
Zhaozhou asked the Dharma Master, "What sutra are you lecturing on? The Master replied, "The *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*. Zhaozhou said, "May I ask about a passage of its meaning?
The Master said, "Yes. Zhaozhou kicked once into the air with his foot and blew upon it, saying, "What is this?"
Yi said, "This meaning does not exist in the sutras. Zhou said, "You empty-headed liar! This is the meaning of the five hundred strongmen lifting the stone;
you simply do not recognize it."
The Elder spoke on behalf of the Dharma Master, saying: "The Abbot deceives me and deceives the assembly.
Xuedou Xian offered a different version, saying: "The Abbot is well-practiced at seizing the opportunity.
Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Where have you set out from? The monk replied, "Xuefeng. Zhaozhou said, "What words or phrases did Xuefeng use to instruct people?"
Tudu said, "Ordinarily it is said that the ten directions of the world are the single eye of the śramaṇa.
Where, then, do you all void your excrement? Daowu said, "If you, Master, ever turn back, please send along a spade."
Langya Jue said: "Among the assembly, some say that if one says, 'I am sending a spade to bury Xuefeng,' then if one says, 'I am sending a bowl,' it is used for holding porridge and rice.
Such wild interpretations are merely dreaming; how can they be discussed?
This is not the hand of Monk You; it is merely a vain claim to have studied painting."
Qinghua said, "It is a pity that at that time he did not encounter a true master.
Had I been the mountain monk there, when the guest-monk returned, I would have sent him a spade.
If he asked why I did not send it, I would have replied: 'The Master cannot do without this here.'"
Zhaozhou arrived at Yunju. Yunju said, "Old man, old man, why do you not seek a place to stay?
Zhaozhou replied, "Where is the place where Zhen finds his dwelling? Yunju said, "In front of the mountain there is the site of an old temple.
Zhaozhou said, "Venerable Sir, you may take it for yourself. He then went to Zhunyu. Zhunyu said, "Old man, old man, why do you not seek a place to stay? Zhaozhou—
Yangshan asked, "Where is the place where Xuanzhen Shenyi resides? Yangju replied, "Even though you are old and venerable, you do not even know your own dwelling place.
Yangzhou said, "For thirty years I have been riding a horse, but today I have been thrown by a donkey."
Yunju Xi said: "Where was it that Zhaozhou was struck by the donkey? Weishan Zhe said:
"Yunju and Zhuyou treat others as they treat themselves; yet how could Zhaozhou have entered into such artifice?
Nevertheless, were it not for the power of snow and frost, who would know the integrity of the pine and cypress?"
Daguai Tai said: "The two elders only knew how to hold fast and did not know how to let go; Zhaozhou only knew how to let go and did not know how to hold fast.
Examining them closely, they have not achieved full perfection. But as for the phrase 'releasing both and gathering both at once'—how would you say it?
In the end, water must flow toward the sea; in the final analysis, clouds must seek the mountain to return."
Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Have you ever studied the Lotus Sūtra? The monk replied, "I have.

Zhaozhou said, "Wearing patched robes in a secluded place, falsely calling oneself an *āraṇyaka* (forest-dweller), you deceive the people of the world. How do you understand this? The monk prepared to prostrate himself.
Zhaozhou said, "Did you come wearing these patched robes? The monk replied, "I came wearing them. Zhaozhou said, "Do not delude me. The monk asked, "How then can one attain [liberation]?"
Zhaozhou said, "Do not take my words.
Xuedou Xian said, "Big or small, Zhaozhou has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. If you all can discern this, then you will see through Zhaozhou;
if you cannot discern it, each of you should simply tuck up your robes and do not be deluded by Cui Feng.
"Excellent.
Gunan said: 'Xuedou is like seeing a snake produced on a rope; he blinds his own eyes and deludes himself. Now let me ask you all:
when Zhaozhou asked in such a manner and this monk answered in such a manner, was it this monk who deluded Zhaozhou?"
In Zhaozhou, the Master was deluding this monk. Had he wished not to delude him at that time, when the monk asked, "Have you come wearing your patched robe?
he should have simply said, "Not even a speck of dust can enter the eyes of the Master."
While Zhaozhou was drawing water on the well-house, he saw Nanquan passing by; he then climbed onto a pillar with his feet dangling and cried out, "Save me!
Save me! Nanquan went up the ladder and struck him, saying, "One, two, three, four, five.

When people are equal, they do not speak; when water is level, it does not flow. Do you understand? Where the favor received is deepest, one should repay it first."
[The monk] retreats. When the state of realization is profound, it is best to simply rest. Tianning Qi said:
"Exhausting this monk’s spiritual powers, he still cannot leap over Zhaozhou’s barrier. A true man of great character should make a decisive choice before the assembly;
before the bowstring snaps and the arrows are spent, one should simply fold one's hands and surrender. Why not put on [the armor]?"
A single turning word: instruct him to submit his surrender. But tell me, what kind of word could he possibly apply?
Qingshan Xiu said: "This monk’s formulation of the question is quite extraordinary.
If one says he has not yet realized it, how would he dare enter the tiger’s lair and stroke the tiger’s whiskers? If one says he has realized it, how could he be willing to let it rest like this?"
A government official once asked Zhaozhou, "Does the Master enter hell? Zhaozhou replied, "I shall enter it at the very end.
The official asked, "Why would a great teacher of wisdom enter hell? Zhaozhou said, "If I do not enter, who will transform and guide you?"
Fuyan Rong said: "The old fellow Zhaozhou’s methods were unlike others; not only did he drag people down when entering the water, but he was also able to seize the banner from their very faces.
Nevertheless, he could not avoid being exposed by the pillar."
A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "What is the crown-mark of Vairocana? Zhaozhou replied, "Since I left home as a youth, I have never suffered from blurred vision.
Tiantong Huo said, "Zhaozhou’s words are biased and one-sided. If someone were to ask me, 'What is the crown-mark of Vairocana?'"
This is the crown-protrusion (uṣṇīṣa) of Vairocana; it simply corresponds to the great being as great and the small being as small.
Tiantong Jie said: "If you see it within Zhaozhou’s words, you will sit dead the world over;
if you see it within Ying’an’s words, you will run dead the world over. Huazang, however, is not like this.

Suddenly someone asked, "What is the crown-protrusion (uṣṇīṣa) of Vairocana? Zhaozhou replied to him simply, "A common brick. "What is the nature that is indestructible? Zhaozhou replied, "The four great elements and the five aggregates.
Zhaojue Qin said, "A thousand-fathom deep pool is clear to its very bottom.
Regarding this, a monk asked Zhaozhou, "Among the three bodies, which is the original body? Zhaozhou replied, "None is missing; none is superfluous."
Yishan Nu said: "When Great and Little Zhaozhou were pressed by others, they were unable to respond with any distinction.
Now, if someone were to ask Yishan, 'Among the three bodies, which one is the original body? I would immediately rise, join my palms, and stand there.
Waiting for their eyes to flicker and move, I would strike them across the spine."
Once, a scholar asked Zhaozhou, "Is it true that the Buddha does not go against the wishes of sentient beings? Zhaozhou said, "Yes.
The scholar said, "May I beg for the staff in your hand, Master? Zhaozhou said, "A gentleman does not take away what another cherishes.
The scholar said, "I am no gentleman. Zhaozhou said, "Neither am I a Buddha."

Yishan Nu said: "The ancient Buddha Zhaozhou was free in both bestowing and taking away; were it not for one of extraordinary capacity, one could not avoid running headlong into the thicket of right and wrong."
Haimen said, "The ancient Buddha Zhaozhou has teeth but no virtue. Why did he not perfect the excellence of another at that time?
Had it been Haimen, I would have handed it to him with both hands. When [Zhaozhou] was about to receive it, I would have struck him across the back.
Not only would this have caused him to break into a profuse sweat and find lifelong joy in the moment, but it would also have inspired future generations."
The Buddha’s disciples know the functional activity of us patch-robed monks.

One night, while Master Jingcen (also known as Changsha Zhaoxian), a successor of Nanquan Puyuan, was gazing at the moon with Yangshan, Yangshan said, “Everyone possesses this very thing, yet they cannot put it to use. Jingcen replied, “That is precisely why I ask you to use it. Yangshan—
Yunmen said, "How will you employ it? Ceng struck him across the chest with a kick, knocking him down. Yangshan rose up and said, "Ha!
You are like a great tiger right before my eyes."
Changqing Ling said: "In the former case, both were masters; in the latter, both were not masters. He then added separately:
"A false dharma is difficult to support.
Baofu Zhan said: "What a fine moon! It is simply that too much effort was exerted; it has been trampled to pieces by him."
This forms two parts. Everyone says that Zen Da-chong is extraordinary; one must know, however, that Yangshan possesses the mechanism for trapping tigers.
Deshan Mi said, "I would like to give him another kick."
Langya Jue said: "Though Li Ling was a skilled hand, how could he avoid falling into the barbarian camp?
Jingshan Daokai said: "The 'Little Śākyamuni' possessed the mechanism for trapping tigers; yet the great beast has no teeth.

That single kick at the time—how could it have been a mere casual act? To suddenly fall to the ground was no accident. Is there anyone among the assembly who can distinguish the black from the white?"
"Did those two elders manage to get out? After a long silence, he said, "Even if they did, it would still be like swinging a staff at the moon.
Tianning Qi said, "The two elders revealed themselves in such a manner; within the gateway of transformation and edification, this is truly worth beholding.
But as for this matter, I suspect there is no connection whatsoever."
Longxiang Yun said: "One person opens the gate to invite the enemy; another buries his troops to engage in combat.
If this is what you mean by 'this matter,' you have not yet seen it even in your dreams."
Baokung Fayun said: "Little Śākyamuni does not know how to be a guest; he troubles his host.
It is precisely because I am borrowing your strength that I provide you with your rightful fodder. Even a fierce tiger with horns would be made to retreat three thousand li."
Fahen Mi said: "It is commonly said that little Śākyamuni was pinned down by Big Tiger Cen;
yet they fail to realize that Big Tiger Cen was pinned down by little Śākyamuni and remains seated there to this day, unable to rise.
Is there anyone here now who can make him rise? Return my tiger to me!"

Once, because a scholar was reading the *Sutra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas*, Changsha asked him, "I see the names of the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, but I do not know in what lands they dwell, nor whether they still transform sentient beings. Changsha called out, "Scholar! The scholar responded, "Yes?
Changsha said, "After Cui Hao inscribed his poem on the Yellow Crane Tower, have you, scholar, ever inscribed one yourself? He replied, "I have never inscribed one."
Changsha said, "I shall take the opportunity to compose a fine poem.
Baizhang Huaihai replied, "If one were truly such a man, upon hearing Changsha speak thus, he would simply say: 'As for the Yellow Crane Tower, it is not difficult to compose a poem about it.
But I wonder, in what land do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas dwell? If one could deliver this [verse],..."
This single pressure not only cuts off the tongue of Changsha, but its fame is also inscribed in the annals of history. Zhaojue Qin said:
"A sword suddenly cleaves one's face—who can discern this? A sword cleaves the face and strikes the chest—how many can truly take responsibility for it?
If you can see Changsha’s horizontal [sword] at the place where rushing currents cross a whetstone blade and swift flames pass through the wind," [you will understand].

When the self departs as an object, it does not require even a single squeeze. Should one follow the verbal explanations and enter into a mere formal report, it would be like asking about the east and answering about the west—twisting the pivot of the discourse. For now, let us rejoice that there is no connection.
But ultimately, what is the definitive point of Changsha? Do you understand? It is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life.

Qingshan Xiu said: "Although Changsha possessed both the 'knife that kills' and the 'sword that gives life,' he was not without the fault of beginning like a dragon's head but ending like a snake's tail.
If I were the mountain monk, it would not be so; as soon as his question had not yet ended, I would have called out, 'Scholar!'"
He was about to agree when Yunmen suddenly asked, "In which land do you reside?
Yunmen said, "It is a pity that hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have been buried by Master Changsha inside a single Yellow Crane Tower.
Can this be called providing an annotation? One must not speak of dreams before a fool."
The heavens are filled with clouds; Mount Cen’s great tiger scatters food across the great earth. Wherever there is a drop of blood upon its skin and fur, it can become a lineage of ambrosia.
Nevertheless, even so, this is not the case when honoring one's ancestors. Wait and ask the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas;
you will see only their names, for it is uncertain in which lands they dwell. Simply call out, "Scholar," and wait for the response. Then—
"Head toward the Way! You have such good fortune; you will hit the bullseye and become the top graduate at the first attempt.
Cuiyan Zhe said, "Although the Ancient Buddha of Changsha was skilled at responding to the occasion, alas, the scholar was still in a hurry and failed to appreciate the magnificent scenery of He Lou.
If someone were to ask Cuiyan today about the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas—"

Examine carefully in which land he dwells; it is simply that from the Jade Green Palace toward the Way, the flowing sounds are vast and grand, and the purple-gold light surges forth, dripping with sweat.
Zimei said, "Changsha’s response in this manner can truly be called picking up what was placed upon the crowns of a thousand Buddhas. Ten thousand...
Although it is pointed out that the Buddha-land exists within [the mind], this too is merely using the hand to perform a fist—a teaching established in reliance upon others.
Zimei was not like this. When asked, "I do not yet know in which Buddha-land you dwell," he simply replied, "Have you eaten today?
When the questioner said, "I have not," he then said, "If you have not eaten, then you do not need a stomach."
"Alas! O Great Assembly, tell me: how far is this from Changsha? To see it and not seize it, to think of it a thousand miles away.
Changsha addressed the assembly: "If I were to exclusively proclaim the Dharma of the School, the grass before the Dharma Hall would have grown ten feet deep."
The Fourth Patriarch Zhe said, "Such a proclamation does not yet accord with the essential teaching of our school. I, this mountain monk, am not like that;

I would simply make the entire earth devoid of even an inch of soil, and furthermore, I would give him thirty blows of the staff. Why is this so? Because the whale swallows the ocean until it is dry."
"Exposing the coral branches.

Dajue Sheng said, "How could it stop at the grass being ten feet deep? If this mountain monk were to proclaim the Dharma of the School, it would surely result in all the people of the world incessantly slandering me.
Nevertheless, without entering the waves that startle the world, it is difficult to encounter [the pearl]."
Regarding "The Fish that Delights in Pleasure," Baiyan Fuzheng said: "Changsha spoke thus; tell me, what was his intention?
Was his intention to enter the marketplace and lower his hand, or was his intention to dwell alone on a solitary peak? If you can discern this, I grant you my approval."
He sees with the same eye as Changsha and hears with the same ear; he cannot distinguish between them.
You call yourself a Zen guest within this nine-bay meditation hall—there will come a day when this dark-faced old man beats you on your ghostly buttocks.
A monk asked Changsha, "After Nanquan passed away, where did he go? Changsha said, "He became a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? Changsha said, "If you want to ride him, ride him; if you want to dismount, dismount."
Jingshan Daowu said: "If someone were to ask Yunmen today, 'Where has the elder Yuanwu gone after his passing?
I would tell them: 'He has entered the Great Avīci Hell. I do not know what the underlying meaning of this is.
[There he] drinks molten copper and swallows hot iron balls. If one were further to ask, 'Can he still be saved? [I would say] he cannot be saved. Why? Because...
"What cannot be saved? This is the daily meal of this old fellow. Tianning Qi said:
"If one wishes to repay virtue and requite kindness, one must be a 'rebellious' descendant of Changsha and Miaoxi to achieve it.
Nevertheless, the two rows of tears upon the coral pillow are half from thinking of you and half from resenting you."
A monk asked Changsha, "How can one turn the mountains, rivers, and the land back into oneself?
Changsha said, "How can one turn oneself into the mountains, rivers, and the land? The monk said, "I do not understand. Changsha said, "Under the walls of Hunan, it is good for raising the people;
rice is cheap and firewood is plentiful, sufficient for all our neighbors. The monk was speechless. Changsha then presented this verse: Who asks?
Mountains and rivers turn; toward whom do mountains and rivers turn? Perfect penetration has no two sides; the nature of phenomena originally has no place of return.
Zhaojue Qin said: "If you receive one ox from another person, you must return one horse to that person."
Tiantong Jue said: "Although host and guest alternate with one another, for now the mud and water remain undifferentiated.
Suddenly, when the nose is twisted around, neither 'it is so' nor 'it is not so' will do. Furthermore, what should be done? Now the royal decree is somewhat strict;
it does not permit encroaching on others' paths or seizing their markets."
Suiyan Yun said: "This monk carried a load of blinding darkness and exchanged it for a load of turbid mud. Nevertheless..."
If it were not for the geese arriving at night, how could one perceive the autumn at the sea-gate?
Qingshan Xiu said: "Even if you could turn the mountains, rivers, and the great earth back into yourself, you would still be burying your own spiritual brilliance.
Furthermore, even if you could turn yourself into the mountains, rivers, and the great earth, you would still be turning your back [on reality]."
To perceive the union with sensory objects—none of it is like that. Tell me, does it turn, or does it not turn?
One day, Changsha ordered a monk to ask his fellow practitioner, Master Hui, saying: "After you saw Nanquan, what was it like?
Hui remained silent. [Changsha] said: "Before you had seen Nanquan, how did you act? Hui replied: "It cannot be."
There is yet another [case]. Monk Hui cited it for Master Sha. Sha said: "The person who does not move atop the hundred-foot pole—though they have gained entry, it is not yet the ultimate reality.
Advancing further from the hundred-foot pole, one manifests the entire body throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
The monk then asked: "As for that hundred-foot pole, how does one advance? Sha said: "Mountains of Langzhou, waters of Lishou."
He said, "I do not understand. The Monk said, "The four seas and five lakes are within the imperial transformation.
Linji Yixuan said, "If you wish to see Changsha, you must take another step forward. If someone were to ask, "What is this one step?
I would wait until I could leisurely entangle you in a web of complications.
Baoning Qian said, "Miaoxi says that one must see Changsha and take another step forward. Baoning, however, is not like this;
he says one must recognize Changsha and take another step backward. Ultimately, how is it? 'Change the bones and wash the intestines, then reorganize;
though your whole body is eyes, you must still investigate.'"
Boshanlai said: "Master Hui sits and kills the Dharma-body, failing to allow passage for either ordinary beings or sages.
Old Cen [Zhaozhou] further battles for the essence beyond the blue sky and outside the clouds. The white ox gongs and rams in every direction; even a dead cat knows how to play."
"To restore sight to the blind and open the ears of the deaf. Does Master Hui still recognize pain and itchiness?
Tiantong Muan said: "The two great elders, Jingshan and Baoning—one in front, one behind.
When examined closely, they have not yet come to rest. To truly know Changsha, you must overturn the flagpole."
Why is it so? The pure pitcher is shattered; not a single thing remains. The cuckoo cries upon a branch of falling blossoms.
Because of this, Changsha instructed San-sheng to ask the Senior Monk Xiu, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing?
Sha said, "When Shitou was a novice, he studied under the Sixth Patriarch. Xiu said, "I am not asking about Shitou seeing the Sixth Patriarch."
"Where has Nanquan gone after his passing? Zhaozhou said, "I will have him go searching for himself.
Xiu said, "Although you, Master, possess a thousand-foot cold pine, you lack a sprouting bamboo shoot from a stone. Zhaozhou remained silent.
Xiu said, "Thank you, Master, for your answer," and Zhaozhou again remained silent. Upon returning, Xiu recounted this to Sansheng. Sansheng said, "If it is truly thus, it is still superior."
Linji took seven steps. Although this was so, [Zhao]zhou said, "I shall wait to test him further.
The next day, Zhaozhou went up to the hall and asked, "I heard the Master’s response yesterday regarding Nanquan’s passing; it may truly be called 'illuminating the past and surpassing the future.'"
Rarely heard in either ancient or modern times. Sha also remained silent.
Zhaojue Qin said: "How extraordinary! How extraordinary! Changsha painted a tiger, yet it turned out to be a wildcat.
Once Nanquan departed, there has been no news; he leaves travelers to engage in idle disputes."
Nanjian asked, "How would you all resolve this koan? As for Changsha’s three instances of silence—how do you understand them?
If you can understand, provide me with a turning phrase for each one.
He then added a verse, saying: "The first is Nanquan’s words on passing away; They illuminate the past and transcend the future, ancient and rare."
Now it is rare. A tiger without teeth is indeed distinct; it is not easy to know unless one has personally encountered it.
When Changsha returned from traveling the mountains, he arrived at the gate. The Head Seat asked, "Where have you come from, Master?

Changsha said, "I have come from traveling the mountains. The Head Seat asked, "To what places did you go? Changsha said, "First I followed the fragrant grasses away, and then I returned following the falling blossoms."
The Head Seat said, "It is very much like the spirit of spring. Shishuang said, "It is even better than autumn dew dripping on lotuses.
Xuedou Xian said, "Thank you for answering the Master’s question.
Baoshou Fang said, "If the Head Seat had been a true man, he should have waited when [Shishuang] said, 'Just as it begins from the fragrant grasses to go...'"
Furthermore, as he was returning following the falling flowers, it would have been well to say: "Venerable Master, this time your mountain journey was no easy matter;
what course of action will this fellow take next?
Once, when Changsha was visited by Minister Zhu, he called out, "Minister! The minister responded, "Yes. Changsha said, "It is not the Minister."
The monk wrote down his own name and said, "It is not that one can depart from this very moment of responding; is there another, second master?
Yunmen said, "Can you call a Minister of State 'the Most Honored One'? The monk said, "If that is so, then at the time when there is no responding at all—is that not my master?
Yunmen said, "Not only at the time of responding or not responding; since beginningless kalpas, it has been thus."

This is the very root of birth and death. He then pointed this out with a verse: "Those who study the Way do not recognize the Real, Simply because they have long been attached to the conscious spirit.
The source of birth and death throughout immeasurable kalpas— Fools call this the 'Original Person.'"
Jingshan Daowei said: "The one responding right now is certainly not the original person; then what do you call the original person?
After a long silence, he said: "For me to speak thus is merely like trying to treat a dead horse."

Liran Guang said: "To distinguish gold from ore requires a master craftsman; Changsha was such a master. Although Miaoxi’s method was direct and straightforward, it was nonetheless unable to cure the fatal ailment of the *gao-huang* [the incurable disease of the heart and back].
Today there are a certain kind of people who cannot distinguish between a slave and a lord, nor can they tell beans from wheat;
they are unable to emerge from the nest of conceptual thought or the field of the five aggregates (*pañca-skandha*). They all say: 'How could there be...'"
The second person said, "Alas, alas! If it is thus, when Old Man Yan calculates the price of the rice, do not say you were not warned.
Changsha, because of this, was asked by the official Haoyue: "An ancient worthy said, 'When one has realized it, karmic obstructions are originally empty; before realization...'"
"One must repay one's karmic debts from former lives. [The Master asked,] "As for the Venerable Siṃha and the Great Master, the Second Patriarch—why did they instead go to repay their debts?
The monk said, "Virtuous One, you do not recognize that all is originally empty. [The Master asked,] "What is meant by 'originally empty'? The monk said, "Karmic obstructions are it."
Baiyan Fu said: "The jade is split to release the linked rings; the pearl is threaded through the nine bends. One must allow Changsha to be the masterful hand here.
Yet, even if one possesses the nostrils of an over-limit monk, if one discusses the fodder of one's own fundamental portion, it is still lacking.

Had he been struck with a blow right to the head at that moment when asked, 'What is the original emptiness? then he would have been honored as supreme for a thousand ages. Furthermore, how could this be otherwise?
It is merely to stop the tiger.
Chan Master Zhuyou of Ezhou (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan of the Southern School) ascended the hall, held up a piece of bamboo, and said:
"Is there anyone who can drive this peg into empty space? At that time, the senior monk Lingxu stepped forward from the assembly and said: "Empty space is..."
Jiufeng Yuyuan struck him with a wooden stake. Ling said, "Do not strike me in error. Yuyuan threw down the bamboo and returned to his quarters.
Yunmen Wenyan remarked, "Adding a point to an arrowhead. A monk asked, "Master, why did you just say that?"
The Gatekeeper said, "Beating the bell to thank the echo; one gets a toad that comes out.
Xuedou Xian said, "If you want this story to spread widely, you must strike him and drive him out."
Fayun Xiu said: "Zhuyou only knows how to look forward; this monk cannot look back.
If one examines them closely, both must receive blows of the staff."
Qixian Shi said: "Tell me, when that monk came out and spoke in such a manner, did he possess the eye of discernment or not?
Zuyou struck him on the spot. But tell me, where did he strike him? Try to examine this."
Nantang Yu said: "Zhunyu drove a stake into the air; Lingxu encountered a stake in barren ground. Xuedou takes no account of the fact that when one exhausts the law, there are no subjects left;
he simply wishes for the words to be transmitted through the ages. Yet, if one examines this closely, they are all nothing but a crew of charlatans who dabble in the void.
Tiantong Wu said: "When Zhuyou struck that monk at the time, was he actually wrong or not? If he was wrong, why did he return to the abbot’s quarters?
If he was not wrong, why did he return to the abbot’s quarters? Try to decide this for me. He added: "It would kill you with doubt."
Baiyan Fu said: "In general, when gathering and releasing are handled with propriety, among them the *jūyū* (evodia) is particularly lovely.
While that is so, at that time, because that monk knew that Master Jiuzhi’s words were pure and his conduct was pure, what would have happened had he been turbid?"
Zhuyou, following Zhaozhou as he held his staff, went up the Dharma Hall from east to west. Zhuyou asked, "What are you doing?
Zhaozhou replied, "Probing the water. Zhuyou said, "There isn't even a single drop here; what is there to probe? Zhaozhou leaned his staff against the wall and went down.

Taisu Zhe said: "Zhaozhou was skilled at probing the waters without disturbing the waves; yet even though there was not so much as a single drop from Zhunü, he could not help but be caught in the trap."
Langya Jue said: "When power fails, the servant deceives the master; when years decline, the ghost toys with man. Tiantong Hua said:
"There is not even a single drop of zhuyu, yet the white waves overflow the heavens. Zhaozhou leaned his staff against the wall, avoiding the clear ripples.
Although these two elders shared the same death and the same life, how could I, this mountain monk, ever consent?
Let it pass.
Li’an Wang said: "The walls and moats of Zhuyou are not secure; Zhaozhou’s probe-stick is too short.
Examining this closely, neither of them has reached a final resolution.
Chan Master Lizong of Zihu in Quzhou (a successor of Nanyuan Yuan of the third Nan lineage) posted a sign at his gate that read: "At Zihu there is a dog;
it takes people's heads from above, takes people's hearts from the middle, and takes people's feet from below. To hesitate is to lose one's life.
Two monks from Linji’s assembly came to visit; as soon as they lifted the curtain, Lizong shouted, "Watch out for the dog!"
The monk turned his head. Lake immediately returned to the abbot’s quarters. Xuedou Xian said: "Everyone in the assembly says that this monk took a bite. Indeed, he took it;
yet how can one say the monk is finished? I ask you all: if the dog of Zihu kills whoever takes a bite, why did this monk [not die]?"
It is so. If there were no monk with universal insight to save him, even if Zihu had appeared in the world and bitten to death hundreds of thousands of beings, what benefit would that have been?
Had I seen him at that time, I would have first cut down his signboard and then entered the hall;
when that old fellow shouted, "Watch out for the dog! I would have let loose a great tawny tiger for him. It is like this...
"Do you all wish to see it now? The sun is already late; let us return to the hall.
Shending Yin said, "The ancient masters' presentation of a single causal occasion was truly no trivial matter.
Tell me, at such a moment as that, what words could have been uttered? Had Shending been there at the time, he would have immediately shouted, "This beast!"
He appeared to be born; then he said he was dying; then he made a gesture of retreating.
Tiantong Huihua said: "Although this old fellow is accustomed to gaining the upper hand, what can he do? He cannot bring himself to bite this monk to death."
Furthermore, tell me: where does the point of benefit or harm lie?
Tianbao Shu said: "If one were a true man, he would trample the placard to pieces and enter directly for an audience.
When the other says, 'Look at the dog,' he would seize him and say, 'Beast! Beast! leaving Zihu with no way to advance or retreat."
It cannot be done. First, one must not neglect Linji; second, one must not betray oneself.
Wanfeng Wei said: "Upon entering the gate, a single shout—head straight and tail straight. To deliberate or reflect is to lose one's very life.
So, how can one enter the gateway of that house?"
Bai Zhang Le said: "If one does not enter the tiger’s den, how can one obtain the tiger’s cub?
At that time, the two monks waited for his shout and said, "Look out for the dog! Then they grabbed him by the chest and held him, saying, "You beast, don't poke your head out!
When he attempted to employ some artifice, they shook their sleeves and departed. Is this not exhilarating?
One night, Zihu cried out before the Sangha hall, "Thief! Thief! The assembly was all startled.
A monk came out from within the hall, and Zihu seized him, saying, "Venerable Karmadāna, I have caught him! I have caught him! The monk said, "It is not he."
"This is so-and-so. Hu said, "It is indeed so; it is simply that you are unwilling to take responsibility for it.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Zihu was merely fitting a hat to a head."
Guo of Mount Gui said, "Zihu’s approach is much like pressing a cow’s head down to make it eat grass.
Sheng of Tianjie remarked, "Big as Zihu may be, he leaves the dragon’s head with a snake’s tail.
If it were Chongxian, upon hearing "It is not so," he would have immediately pushed him over and said, "Do you still want to steal from the old monk?"
When Liu Tiemo arrived, Zihu asked him, "I have long heard of Liu Tiemo; is it really you? Tiemo replied, "I dare not say so.
Zihu said, "Turn left? Turn right? Tiemo said, "Do not be topsy-turvy, Master. Zihu then struck him.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Zihu’s staff-head has eyes, simply because the authority is in his hand. Tiemo’s skin beneath the fur has blood;
he owes it to his carrying the bamboo pole with him wherever he goes. Although the weak may overcome the strong, one must still ensure the words remain."
Chan Master Tanzhao of Baima in Jingzhou (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan of the Southern School) used to say constantly, "How joyful! How joyful!
Yet when the time of his death arrived, he cried out, "Suffering! Suffering! He also said, "King Yama has come to take me away.
The temple administrator asked, "When you were thrown into the water by the Military Commissioner, your countenance did not change; why is it that now you act like this?"
Dizang then picked up the pillow and said, "Tell me, was it so at that time, or is it so now? The head of the monastery had no reply.
Dizang then threw down the pillow.
Fayan Yi was the abbot of Daichuan at that time; he simply covered his ears and walked out.
Qingliang Qin said, "At that moment, it would have been better to snatch the pillow and hurl it straight at his face."
Yunfeng Yue said, "Bitter, bitter! It was so then; it is so now. He snatched away the pillow and presented it, saying, "The King of Yama is right here!"
Daguizhi said: "The ultimate compassionate heart. Tianbao Shu said:
"The white horse dies and returns to life; the monastery director lives and returns to death. At the third watch, one passes beyond the Iron Ring Mountains."

When the sun was exactly at its meridian, Baiyan Fu said, "The head is straight and the tail is straight; even with the white horse, it is still lacking. The head monk asked, "How can you be like this now?
Yet he continued to cry out in a loud voice, "Alas! Alas! King Yama is coming to take me!"
It is so. "Not hindering the world from being killed by doubt," yet he pointlessly raised his pillow and spoke at length—wherein is there anything extraordinary?
Chan Master Yiduan of Xiangyan in Dengzhou (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan) ascended the hall and said: "Words are slander; silence is [slander]."
"Deception! There is something further beyond the silence of speech. This old monk’s mouth is too narrow; I cannot explain it for you. He then descended from his seat.
Lingyin Yue said, "When Xiangyan spoke thus, was he speaking or not? After a long pause, he said, "Go drink tea."
Tianmu Li said: "If one were to shed tears frequently according to the teachings, even the vast ocean would have to dry up.
Benjue Wei said: "Xiangyan’s tongue dragged across the ground; Songyuan mistakenly added a footnote.
Qingfu simply sat on the ground watching Yangzhou.
When Master Rizi (the successor of Nanshan Nanquan Yuan) was visited by Yaxi for an audience, Rizi made a gesture of rising.
Yaxi said, "This old mountain ghost still sees me here. Rizi said, "A transgression, a transgression! Just now I failed to respond properly.
As Yaxi was about to offer further words, Rizi gave a shout. Yaxi said, "When facing a great battle array, it is indeed difficult to resist. Rizi said, "Right, right. Yaxi—
He said, "Not so, not so. Zhaozhou Shen remarked, "Pity these two fellows; they do not recognize the phrase for turning the body.
Tianning Hui said, "Zhaozhou does not know good from bad; he recklessly judges the ancients. He fails to realize that these two..."
A certain fellow: where he gained advantage, he lost it; consequently, in the end, he became a dragon’s head with a snake’s tail.
O Zen adepts, tell me: where exactly was it that he had a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail? Examine this for yourselves.
