△ Third in the Southern Lineage: Chan Master Yunji Shizu of Zhongnan Mountain (Third in the Southern Lineage; successor of Nanquan Puyuan).

He asked Nanquan, "The *maṇi* jewel is not recognized by people, yet it is personally held within the *tathāgatagarbha*. What is this *garbha*? Nanquan said, "That which comes and goes with you is it."
The Patriarch asked, "What about one who neither comes nor goes? Quan said, "That too is a concealment. The Patriarch asked, "What is the pearl? Quan called out, "Master!
The Patriarch responded, "Yes. Quan said, "Go. You do not understand my words. From this point on, the Patriarch gained faith and entered [the Way].
Xuedou Xian, when addressing those who come and go, says: "A fellow of the weeds. When addressing those who do not come and go, he also says:
"Adding frost to snow. When asked, "What is the pearl? he replies: "Dangerous! He further says:
"To perform tricks atop a hundred-foot pole is not the work of a master hand; one must have an eye here where host and guest interact."
He was able to penetrate deeply into the tiger’s den. Had it not been so, even if the Master had attained enlightenment, it would have been like a dragon’s head with a snake’s tail.
Baizhang Yuan said: "This monk possesses a *maṇi* jewel; it may truly be called a treasure rarely seen in this world. Great indeed!
How pitiable! It nearly fell into a ten-thousand-fathom deep pit. Fortunately, it was personally rescued by the old master Nanquan.
But tell me, where is this pearl now? He then said: "The sea god knows its nobility but not its price;
it remains for humanity to illuminate the dark night."
Jingyin Cheng said: "Nanquan’s responses to the occasion were worthy of observation for their ability to both grant and revoke.
Yet, when scrutinized, he ultimately failed to point out where the pearl was. Even if one says, 'You do not understand my words,' this is precisely the concealment.
After all, where is the pearl? Is it that the sea god knows its value but does not know its price? This is [the case]. (The text ends here.)
"Come, new bride Chan; there is no need to bring it forth. [He] struck the meditation seat and said:
"The pearl and the casket have been smashed to pieces by this old monk’s single blow. What more do you all seek here for a bowl? He struck once more.
Zhaojue Qinyun said: "Nanquan’s single period of teaching involved the deployment of his hand; there was indeed no lack of gathering and releasing, capturing and letting go.
Yet, fundamentally, the matter of the 'Upward Direction' has not yet been seen. For instance, if the entire earth is the Tathāgatagarbha, where would you place the pearl?
If the entire earth is the maṇi jewel, what do you call the 'garbha'? If you can clearly understand this, there is turning."
Regarding his physical presence, I grant you one eye.
Regarding Nantang’s desire, he said: "Nanquan entered the grass to seek out people. Setting aside for a moment Xuedou’s act of casting his body across a tiger’s den, [consider this].
Furthermore, tell me: when the Master attained enlightenment, by whose power did he ultimately receive it? If you can apply the eye here, you will see that both head and tail are straight.
Gu Nanmen said: "Nanquan uses far too many words. When asked, 'What is the Tathāgatagarbha? he should have simply said..."
He said, "Do not seek it elsewhere. What is the pearl? It has been smashed to pieces by a single blow—truly a masterful hand! Do you all understand?
Lian-an Guang said, "Nanquan exhausted his own mind to break the mouths of others; as for this mountain monk..."
Not so. When asked, "What is the treasury? he replied, "Brocade wrapping a special stone. When asked, "What is the pearl? he replied, "Iron encasing a lump of clay.
Lu Xuan, the Grand Master and Governor of Xuanchuan (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan), asked Nanquan: "The Great Compassionate Bodhisattva uses such [power]..."
"What is the use of so many hands and eyes? Nanquan said, "It is like a state employing a high official; what would one do with such a person?
Xuedou Xian commented on Nanquan, saying, "He did not equal the question posed by the High Official."
Baoning Yong said separately: "This is not at all out of place.
When the Grand Master came to offer condolences following Nanquan’s passing, the monastery director asked the Grand Master, "Why do you not weep for the late Master?"
The Great Officer said, "If the Abbot can explain the Way, I shall weep. The Abbot had no reply.
Changqing Ling said, "Now tell me, should he have wept or not?
The Lay Practitioner Ganji of Chizhou (a successor of Nanyuan Yuan of Nan-san) entered Nanquan’s hall to provide a vegetarian feast. At that time, Huangbo was serving as the Head Seat.
Zhizhe requested a gift of wealth. Huangbo said, "The two gifts of wealth and Dharma are equal and without distinction.
Zhizhe said, "If you speak thus, how can you deserve my offering? He then carried the money out. A short while later, he re-entered and said, "Please accept a gift of wealth.
Huangbo replied, "The two gifts of wealth and Dharma are equal and without distinction. Thereupon, Zhizhe made the offering.
Cuiyan Zhen said: "The practitioner Ganqi is a clever fellow who has caught the master off guard; as for Huangbo bestowing wealth, when was he ever truly awakened to it?
Yunju Yuan said: "Big and small Huangbo both had one eye changed by Ganqi."
Jingshan Daowu said, "In a class of their own, they follow the heterodox and pursue evil; yet Yunju Luohan is slightly better.
Lingyin Yuanzhao said, "They are all merely covering their ears while stealing the bell. They do not realize that Ganqi knows how to withdraw and how to let go.
The Head Seat was thoroughly alert: the clouds have gathered and the rain has cleared, the vast sky is wide open; a pair of mandarin ducks cannot be captured in a painting.
Yuyan Meng said: "Cuiyan and Dahui observed the winds and knew the changes, exercising restraint with skillful means; it was simply that..."
One sees the sharpness of the awl’s point but not the squareness of the chisel’s head. Huangbo maneuvers from within the tent to secure victory a thousand miles away;
the Practitioner charges the front lines twice, once lifting and once pressing down—truly, he exhausts his own mind to break the other's mouth with laughter.
Only Old Man Nanquan, however, is able to sit and observe the outcome.
Lingyan Zhu said: "Although Cuoyan may raise with one hand and press down with the other, his elbows and arms never extend beyond his body.
While it is true that the Head Seat finds it difficult to forget what he is well-versed in, he cannot avoid being stuck in a single way without change.

The practitioner may be said to grant or withhold according to the occasion, yet he excessively seeks merit and hopes for emulation; how can this compare to the vegetarian feast prepared by the five lay practitioners of Liangxi?"
He distributes the alms. He does not boast or take credit; he simply wishes for everyone to be satisfied and that is all.
Qinglong said, "Huangbo is much like one who delays a prisoner to foster his own cleverness; the almsgiver is also like a poor man selling his wealth.
Although both are masters of their craft, when examined closely, they are not without flaws. As for this mountain monk:
Acting as Huangbo, he waited for the attendant to request alms; then, seizing whatever came to hand, he flung it directly at his face.
Although the attendant’s entire body was eyes, he was taught that he could not possibly manage to react in time.
Mingzhao’s Supplementary Commentary says: "The practitioner requested the performance of the almsgiving twice; one was a good intention and the other was not.
Huangbo’s responses were identical in both instances. Why did the practitioner accept one and reject the other?"
Ganqi opened his reception hall. Someone asked, "It is not easy for a practitioner to attend to guests. Ganqi said, "It is like feeding a donkey or feeding a horse.
Langya Huijue said, "Quickly bring the food!"
Wuzu Yan said, "I wish that the practitioner would remain as he is today.
Gao Feng Miao said, "Although Master Langya’s words are beautiful, they are merely a hurried fabrication;
they are not fit for offering. Master Wuzu did not discern the wind coming from afar; it is a pity that he served nothing but a bowl of plain leek soup."
I have consumed much salt and vinegar. It is like feeding a donkey or a horse; I simply tell them that this leftover soup and rancid rice need not be carried out.
But tell me, O assembly: are you the same as the ancients, or are you different? You must be able to determine this.
"He consumed ten thousand taels of gold daily. Otherwise, even when drinking water, one must guard against choking.
The Monk Puhua of Zhenzhou (dharma successor of Nanshan Panshan Ji) habitually entered the marketplace shaking a rattle, saying:

"If it comes from the bright side, strike the bright side; if it comes from the dark side, strike the dark side; if it comes from the four quarters and eight directions, strike with a whirlwind; if it comes from empty space, strike in succession!"
Jiada. One day, Linji had a monk seize him and said, "If no one comes in this manner at all, what then?
Huahua pushed him away and said, "Tomorrow there is a vegetarian feast at Beici Monastery. When the monk returned and reported this to Linji, Linji said, "I have always suspected this fellow."
Wuzu Yan said: "If I were Wuzu, it would not be so. If someone asked, 'What is it like when one does not come in this way at all?
I would strike them with a shout. They would surely say, 'Wuzu uses blind censure and blind blows,' and I want you to say exactly that.
Why? So that you may freely present this to all quarters."
Yunmen Xinchun said, "When Master Puhua was acting so strangely, he was pinched on the nostrils by Linji until he was left in tenfold agony.
Had it not been for his evasion at the Great Compassion Temple, who would have seen Puhua again?"
Fuyan Rong said: "Puhua brings such trouble upon others; there is no way to heaven above and no door to enter the earth below.
Tell me, where exactly does it lie? Linji said, 'I have always suspected this fellow;
perhaps he does not have good intentions either.'"

Xuedou said this and that. Although Puhua’s response was thus—transcending the present and surpassing the past such that it leaves people in awe and unable to reach its heights—if one examines it closely, it still has not managed to completely block the throats of the monks.
Today someone asked the mountain monk, "What is it like when one does not come in this way at all? I simply told him, "Valley, valley;
solitary valley, solitary valley.
Once, when Puhua was sitting in the monks' hall together with the two elders, He'ang and Muta, they were engaged in conversation.
The discussion states: Puhua was a man who daily in the streets and markets acted like one driven by wind or madness.
When it was time for formal deliberation, and everyone was debating whether he was ordinary or a sage, Puhua suddenly entered from outside. Linji asked him, "Are you ordinary or a sage?
Puhua replied, "You tell me first, am I ordinary or a sage? Linji then gave a shout. Puhua pointed his finger and said, "At Heyang, there is a new..."
"His wife and children! A wooden pagoda and the grandmother’s Zen! Linji, that little brat, yet he possesses a single eye.
Huizhao said, "That thief! Changhua said, "Thief! Thief! and immediately went out.
Shoushan Nian said, "These two thieves—one is the primary thief. Now tell me, which one is the primary thief?
He then spoke on their behalf, saying, "Liu Benzi."
Puhua and Linji were together at a donor’s house for a meal. Linji asked, “A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru.
Is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or is it simply the natural way of things?
Puhua suddenly kicked over the dining table. Linji said, “How crude! Puhua replied, “What kind of place is this that you speak of ‘crude’ and ‘refined’? Linji—
"Go rest. The next day, they again attended a meal at the house of the same donor. Linji asked, "How does today’s offering compare to yesterday's?
Yunhua once again kicked over the rice table. Linji said, "You are too crude. Yunhua replied, "Blind fellow! What 'crude' or 'refined' is there to speak of in the Buddha-dharma?
Linji then stuck out his tongue.
Xuedou Xian said: "These two old thieves have not even finished their meal; they deserve thirty blows of the staff.
Though the blows are dealt, who is the actual thief?"
Nantang Jing said: "These two venerable masters were like two dragons contending for a pearl; they seized the clouds and grasped the mist without stirring a ripple.
They were like two tigers contending for food; they captured the living and seized the raw without harming a creature's life. Here, should someone ask:"
"A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Is this the wondrous function of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*), or is it simply the natural way of things?
To this, I say: "With a single punch, the Yellow Crane Tower is toppled; with one kick, the Parrot Isle is overturned.
When there is spirit, spirit is added; where there is no elegance, there is elegance nonetheless."
Nanhuabing said: "Linji’s face-to-face guidance and Puhua’s total response in kind were such that the turtle-nosed snake of the South Mountain swallowed the carp of the Eastern Sea;
the iron ox of Shanyu gored the great elephant of Jiazhou to the ground."
"Why is it so? When meeting, one does not dismount; each hastens toward their own future. Zhaojue Qin said:
"If refined gold is not tempered a hundred times, how can its brilliance be seen? If a supreme treasure is not offered at its true value, how can one distinguish the genuine from the counterfeit?
It was not for Linji that he could not test Puhua; it was not for Puhua that [Linji] could not..."
He opposed Linji, which is like water entering water or gold being matched with gold.
Nevertheless, if one lets it pass, both are masters; if one scrutinizes it, both suffer loss. Those who possess the eye of discernment should try to examine this.
Tiantong Hua said: "One emerges and one submerges; one goes and one returns.

To snatch food from the mouth of a fierce tiger or to scratch an itch on the head of a venomous snake—yet even so, it does not yet measure up to the affairs of a Great Man. These two elders have their names resounding through the universe."
Its value was high in that era. How could this mountain monk prudently keep my three inches [of mouth] shut?
If I let both pass, it would be because they were feigning the real; if I let neither pass, it would be because their deception was too extreme.
If you all treat this as a matter for deliberation within the Buddha-dharma, the school of Bodhidharma will be swept away to its very foundations.
Nantang Yu said: "If Xuedou speaks in such a manner, he too deserves twenty blows. But tell me, where does his fault lie?
Have you not heard it said: 'When the real thief has fled, the patrolmen eat the blows'?"
Xiu of Qing Shan said: "These two venerable elders—one possessed the hand that seizes the dragon; the other attained the mechanism that traps the tiger.
They may truly be called masters meeting as peers. But tell me, who is the one who traps the tiger? Who is the one who seizes the dragon?"
Those who possess the eye of discernment should attempt to distinguish and examine this.
Gu Nanmen said: "When these two fellows encounter each other head-on, one fist comes and the other leg responds;
were they not karmic enemies, they would not have gathered together. I dare ask the assembly: Linji’s single staff was habitually used for striking both horizontally and vertically.
Having arrived here, why then do you stick out your tongue? Do you see these two old fellows? "At evening on the parting pavilion, a single sound of the Hsiang flute;
you head for Hsiang-hsiang, I head for Ch'in."
Qixia Chengyun said: "Linji’s two attempts to provoke him were intended solely to test Puhua;
yet Puhua was a man carrying a wooden board who, though pinched on the nose twice by Linji, remained entirely unaware."
Xuedou speaks thus; he has thoroughly scrutinized [the matter]. Those who today attain a single pivot—do they still recognize Linji’s baring his tongue?
Huiyun Sheng said: "Puhua upturned the celestial gate; Linji turned the terrestrial axis. As for their deeds, they were not [mere acts of] doing.
Fangjunqiao said, "Looking at them with a straight eye, both are blind men; I shall give each of you thirty blows of the staff.
Suddenly, a man said, "Whom does Huiyun’s staff intend for me to eat? Huineng struck him, saying, "Dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish; a patch-robed monk is difficult to deceive."

Chan Master Liangsui of Shouzhou (a successor in the third generation of the Mazu lineage, who inherited from Magu Cheshan) went to visit Magu. Upon seeing him approaching, Magu took up a hoe and went out to weed the grass. When Liang arrived at the place where Magu was weeding, Magu paid him no attention at all and returned directly to his quarters, closing the door behind him. On the following day, Liang went again; Magu closed the door once more. Liang then knocked on the gate. Magu asked, “Who is it? As Liang was about to state his name, Magu said: “Who is there knocking? Liang replied, “I am Liang. Magu said, “Go away; I have no room for you here. Liang said, “Master, please do not speak thus. Magu said, “If you can call forth the sound of the hoe striking the ground, I will let you enter. Liang struck the ground with the hoe three times. Magu said, “You have indeed attained the Way. Liang bowed and departed. Later, when Liang was teaching at Shouzhou, he remarked: “When I first visited Magu, I was like a man who has lost his way in a vast wilderness. I did not know where to turn. It was only after I had been there for some time that I finally found my bearings. Magu heard of this and sent a messenger to say: “I have always known that you would eventually reach this point. Upon hearing this, Liang sighed and said: “Had I not met Magu, I would have remained a man of shallow learning all my life. Magu then sent another message: “I have always known that you would eventually reach this point. Liang sighed again and said: “Had I not met Magu, I would have remained a man of shallow learning all my life. Magu then sent yet another message: “I have always known that you would eventually reach this point. Liang sighed once more and said: “Had I not met Magu, I would have remained a man of shallow learning all my life. Magu then sent a final message: “I have always known that you would eventually reach this point. Suddenly he attained awakening and immediately said, "Preceptor, do not deceive me, Liangsui.
Had I not come to pay my respects to you, Preceptor, I would have been led astray by the sutras and treatises for the rest of my life. Gu then opened the door and met him.
Upon returning to his lecture hall, he said to the assembly, "What all of you know, Liangsui knows entirely; what Liangsui knows, none of you know."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "There are waves that go against the current. He also asked, "What is the place where Liangsu knows?
Donglin Yan said, "What is the place where Liangsu knows? This is like a cormorant speaking to a crane.
Lingyin Yue said: "To act for others, one must be thorough; it is like biting into raw iron, riding against the current, or driving a stake into empty space.

Chan Master Jinzhou Cao (a successor of Nan San Zhangjing Yun) invited Master Mi to a vegetarian feast. He did not arrange seating positions. When Master Mi arrived, he [proceeded to] unfold [his sitting mat].
As they were performing prostrations on their sitting mats, Shouzhu descended from his meditation seat. Mi then took the seat of Shouzhu, while Shouzhu withdrew to sit upon the floor.
When the meal was finished, Mi departed. An attendant remarked, "The Master is revered by all people; today your seat has been usurped by another.
Shouzhu replied, "If he comes back after three days, I shall accept him as my successor. Three days later, Mi indeed returned.
He said: "The other day I encountered bandits.
Jingqing Fu was then asked by a monk: "Master Mi said, 'The other day I encountered bandits. What was the meaning of this? Jingqing replied:
"I saw only the sharpness of the awl's point; I did not see the squareness of the chisel's head."
Yuan-an Yu said: "At that time, as soon as Master Mi arrived, he sat down on the ground. This left Jinzhou with no way to ascend to heaven and no door to enter the earth.

He sat straight through until the appearance of Ruci Tathāgata, saying, 'If I were to come again at that time, I would meet him face-to-face. Then, with his hand, he struck his forehead and said, 'A cat!'"
Baon Xian said: "Jinzhou lost his position; Mihú encountered bandits. The scale-hook was struck with a nail; it was simply pulled straight.

It is a pity that the attendant lacked wit. Had he been a true man, when Master Mí said, 'The other day I encountered bandits,' he should have asked, 'What did you lose, Master? Had he been able to utter such words at that time, not only—"
Master Mi was filled with admiration. This allowed Jinzhou to withdraw from the position he held.
The Master of Bimokya Cliff on Mount Wutai (successor to Nansan Yongtae-tan) constantly carried a wooden pitchfork; whenever he saw a monk approaching, [he would strike him with it].
As soon as [Huitang] had prostrated, he crossed his arms over [Huitang’s] neck and said, "Which demon-spirit taught you to leave the household life?
Which demon-spirit taught you to travel on pilgrimage? If you can speak, you shall die under my cross-arms; if you cannot speak, you shall die under my cross-arms.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! When Heshan Tong heard of this, he went to see him. Before he had even prostrated, he threw himself into [Huitang’s] embrace. Huitang then patted Tong.
He struck his back three times, clapped his hands, and said, "Elder brother, you have deceived me for three thousand li; you have deceived me for three thousand li!
Baofu Zhan said, "To hesitate when one ought to act decisively only brings about further chaos."
Shoushan Nian said: "A thousand hearings are not equal to one seeing.
Fayen Yi, at Sudo, addressed the monks of the following generation, saying: "Beg for your lives! Beg for your lives!"
Fadeng bowed respectfully; when the monk merely extended his neck to indicate [the pole], Baoci then spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "Old man, you might as well lay down your pole.
Wuzu Jie said, "If I had been there at that time, I would have snatched the pole away, thrust it over his neck, and pinned him down. He then added, "... (The text ends here).
Hold up a torch and see how thick his skin is!
Mingzhao Qian said: "At that time, when I saw him about to speak but had not yet spoken, I first gave him a blow with my staff."
Langya Huijue said: "The sound of thunder is great, yet there are no raindrops at all.
Chan Master Jieling of Shanglin in Hunan (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan and Youtai of Yongtai) first visited Mount Guiyang.
Guishan asked, "What have you come for, Venerable Sir? Jieling replied, "My armor is fully equipped. Guishan said, "Take it all off before you come to meet me."
Lin said, "I have taken it off. Miu shouted, "The thief has not yet been beaten; why take it off? Lin had no reply.
Yangshan spoke on his behalf, saying, "Please, Master, ask those around you to step aside. Miu pointed with his finger and said, "Yes, yes.
Later, when Lin went to visit Yongtai, Yongtai finally explained the meaning of this to him.
Yuan'an Meng said: "Tell me, did Daolin awaken to the meaning of Guishan, or did he awaken to the meaning of Yangshan?
If he awakened from Guishan, where is his armor? If he awakened from Yangshan, let me ask:
has Yangshan ever even cast it aside? If it is not any of these, then you must realize it for yourself and cast it off."
"What do you reject? The monk said, "How can you, Master, judge others by your own standards?
Yuan pointed his finger and said, "Yes, yes. △ Qing III.
Chan Master Zongzhi Daowu of Tanzhou (a successor of Yaoshan Yan in the Qing lineage) left Yaoshan to visit Nanquan.
Nanquan asked, "What is your name, Reverend? Daowu replied, "Zongzhi. Nanquan said, "When wisdom does not reach, how do you establish the principle?
Daowu said, "One must strictly avoid speaking of it. Nanquan said, "Truly, if one speaks of it, horns will grow. Three days later, Daowu was with Yun...
Yanguan was behind the rack threading a needle. When Nanquan saw him, he asked, "Dharma Master Zhi, you said the other day that where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking;
if one speaks, horns will grow. How, then, should one conduct oneself? Yanguan immediately withdrew his body and entered the Sangha hall, while Nanquan returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Wulei Quan said: "The way the predecessors spoke in this manner is much like a sick bird perching on reeds;
they utterly lack the wisdom of transformation. Here, it is not so: where wisdom does not reach is precisely where one should speak. Rain falls upon the flowers of the crags."
The wind arises at the corner of the hall; diagnosis and treatment are administered according to the occasion. Giving medicine to suit the ailment, one observes the aperture and drives in the wedge.
Untangling the sticky and removing the bonds, the celestial horse thrusts open the Great Gate of Bestowal; heaven and earth tremble, and the stars and constellations fall.
Daowu, because Yunyan was unwell, asked him, "When you leave this leaking shell, where will we meet?
Yunyan replied, "We shall meet in the place of neither birth nor extinction. Daowu said, "Why do you not say that we shall not seek to meet even in a place that is neither born nor extinguished?"
Xuedou Xian said, "Attendant, remember this one question for me.
Zhaojue Qin offered a different response: "Where would you not encounter him?
Yunju Zhuang said, "In the place that is neither arising nor ceasing, nor not arising nor ceasing—there is nowhere at all to meet."
[The Master] said: "If someone asks, 'Yunju, having cast off the shell and the leaky vessel, where do you meet them?
simply say to him, 'Where would we not meet? Then, suddenly picking up the staff, he draws a line and descends from his seat."
Baiyan Fu said: "These two fellows usually utter every word and speak every phrase like iron caltrops—dare anyone chew them up?
Why is it that here they act like a master of commentaries? Is there anyone who knows their hidden intent?
Even if there were, you must take care not to split the discourse into two parts."
Daowu pointed to a hibiscus flower and asked a monk, "How is this like that? The monk replied, "It makes the hairs on my body stand on end.
Daowu said, "Ultimately, how is it? The monk said, "One from under Daowu’s gate. Daowu said, "The Great King of Ten Li."
Zhaojue Qin said: "To cast lacquer into lacquer is like verifying a shadow to know its form.

If you do not understand the coming from the orthodox and the coming from the deviant, how can you comprehend the bright casting itself into the dark harmony? Do you understand yet? A shrimp leaps up to the Brahma Heaven; an earthworm suddenly crosses the Eastern Sea."
Jingshan Ce said: "If one does not open the doors and windows, how can one know the light of the bright moon?
If one does not launch upon the celestial raft, how can one behold the majesty of the Milky Way? Daowu used a wedge to extract a wedge; this monk used wisdom to shatter wisdom.
Although they met by chance on the road, they could not avoid displaying their three heads and six arms. Do you understand? It is because he loves that young man.
It is turned instead into "The White-headed Old Man.
Daowu addressed the assembly: "Exaltedness does not lie on the highest peak; wealth does not lie at Fuyan; joy does not lie in heaven;
suffering does not lie in hell."
Jingshan Daokai said: "The high is at the summit; the wealthy are at Fuyan; the joyful are in heaven; the suffering are in hell. Nantang Yu said:
"One person looks from a very high place and finds it insufficient; another person looks from a very low place and finds it level."

This is more than sufficient for those within the gate of proclaiming the teaching; it is enough to behold its splendor. Yet, beneath the gate of the patch-robed monks (śramaṇas), there is still a lack of awakening.
As for original enlightenment (mūla-bodhi), how can it be described? Simply take rice and place it in the bowl of no-mind; someone will naturally come forward with a broken-legged cauldron.
Nengren Jian said: "The two great elders each obtained a single *zuoju* (seating mat) of land, and thus they demarcated boundaries and established territories.
Yet, as for the affairs within the gate of the patch-robed monks (*nanseng*), this still does not quite reach it. As for how it is here at Beihua, it is simply this:
'The patched robe covers the head, and all matters cease; at this time, the mountain monk understands nothing at all.'"
When Yunyan was about to pass away, Daowu sent a letter to bid him farewell.
Upon finishing the letter, Daowu said to his senior master Dongsan Mi, "Yunyan did not realize [the Way]. I regret that I did not speak to him at that time.
Nevertheless, even so, he did not fail to be a true son of Yaoshan."
Baoci then questioned him, saying, "When the ancients spoke thus, did they still know it was so?
Yunyan at that time did not understand; where was it that he did not understand?"
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Daowu and Yunyan did not know there was [something more]. I regret that I did not speak to them at the time.
Even so, when they spoke thus, did Daowu still know there was [something more] or not?"

Chan Master Tansheng of Yunyan in Tanzhou (a successor of Yaoshan Yan in the Third Generation of the Qingyuan lineage) was once asked by Yaoshan, "I have heard that you are skilled at performing the lion dance;
is this true? Yunyan replied, "It is. Yaoshan asked, "How many times have you performed it? Yunyan said, "I have performed it six times.
Yaoshan said, "I too am skilled at performing it. Yunyan asked, "How many times has the Master performed it? Yaoshan replied, "I have performed it only once."
Yan said, "One is six; six is one. Later, Yan went to Mt. Wei. Wei asked, "I have heard that you, Elder, were playing with lions at Yaoshan—is this true?
Yan said, "It is. Wei said, "When playing for a long time, there must be a time to set it aside.
Yan said, "If I wish to play, I play; if I wish to set it aside, I set it aside. Wei asked, "At the moment of setting it aside, where is the lion? Yan said, "Set aside."
"Set it down! Fanchang Yu said, "What a fine lion! It simply has a head but no tail.
Had I been there when Miaoshan said 'set it down,' I would have immediately let loose the golden lion crouching on the ground."
Mao: "This directly leaves Moshan with no way to hide his body.
Letan Zhun said: "Yaoshan and Yunyan have frustrated people to death; these two fathers and sons dangle one lion, yet they cannot even bring it forth.
If it were Upasaka Zhun, he would simply have to dangle it himself. He then picked up his staff and said:
The great assembly raised their eyes in expectation. Yunyan then cast it down and said, "As for this message within, how many people can truly know it?
Xiqia Cheng said, "Yunyan claimed he understood how to handle the six flakes of snow; yet when he reached Dayue’s 'one flake,' he could not even manage it.
Had he been able to let out a single roar at that time, I would have had to teach Dayue to retreat three thousand paces."
Dongshan said, "Although Yunyan was skilled at concealing his sharp edge, he should not have tucked the golden-haired lion into its den.
If it were I, when asked 'Where is the lion? I would simply strike him across the face."

"Zhǎng! You fellows who claim to manage Dàyuè have not yet learned how to avoid [this trap]. Today, with the assembly of humans and devas gathered in full, I shall perform a display for everyone to see.
He then suddenly seized his staff, let out a shout, and said: "With one roar, all beasts tremble;
let alone the fragrant elephants, they must all bolt in flight."
Yunyan asked a monk, "Is your father still alive? The monk replied, "He is. Yunyan said, "How old is he? The monk said, "He is eighty years old.
Yunyan said, "You have a father who is not eighty years old; do you know him? The monk said, "Is it this very one who has come here?"
Yan said, "One who comes in such a manner is still a descendant.
Dongshan Jia said, "Even one who does not come in such a manner is likewise a descendant."
Guishan Lingyou said: "It cannot be so, nor can it not be so. Ultimately, what is it? After a long silence, he said:
"From the beginning there has been no fixed order; there is no need for forced arrangement."
Bai Zhang Le said: "To recognize the father is easy; to recognize the sons and grandsons is difficult. In recent years, our household affairs have become extremely desolate;
from a thousand miles away, I look anxiously for news, yet it is rare."
While Yunyan was sweeping the floor, Daowu said, "You are being far too busy. Yunyan replied, "You must know that there is one who is not busy.
Daowu said, "If that is so, then there is a second moon. Yunyan held up the handle of his broom and asked, "Which moon is this? Daowu then desisted.
Xuansha Shibei said, "This is precisely the second moon.
Changqing Xuanleng asked Xuansha, "When he turns the broom handle upside down and strikes you right in the face, what then?
Xuansha withdrew without speaking.
Luoshan Xian said: "Alas! These two fellows do not recognize good from evil. This fellow Yunyan has had his hands and feet bound for how long now since he died!"
Yunmen Wenyan said, "The slave sees the maidservant being diligent.
Weishan Zhe said, "Using diligence to compensate for clumsiness.
Baofu Zhuan said, "Yunyan is much like pushing a cart through the mud; every step is laborious."
Xuedou Xian, regarding the phrase "If it were so, there would be a second moon," remarked separately:
"It was only right that he let it pass. Guishan Xing said: "Daowu creates a mound on level ground; Yunyan swings his arm while walking.
Xuansha said: "That is precisely the second moon. How thick is his skin? Now tell me, what was the intention behind Yunyan holding up the broom?
"How is it? A perfect ten-scored diamond drill—spread out before the gate, for whom is it sold?
Tianning Qi said: "Yunyan sets up his broom; Daowu stops and leaves. Both are merely the 'second moon.
Which one is not so troubled? This night, the single orb is full; where is its pure light not present?"
Baoneng Xiu said: "This lot of fellows all claim that Yunyan was unable to use his broom to strike through the tangled vines;
they fail to realize, however, that there are thorns within the mire."
Boshan Lai said: "To discern reality amidst a heap of dung and weeds, one must cast one's body across the handle of a broom.
Who cares whether it is the second month or the third? Use what is appropriate when the time comes. Xuansha and Yunmen have thorns within their words; these are both rewards and punishments.
Do not complain of the cold of frost and dew; they add a fine, fragrant scent."
Qingshan Xiu said: "If I were Daowu, when asked 'In which month was that person? I would simply say, 'Just so.
This would ensure he has no place to set his broom."
Gushan Xian said: "Xuansha and Changqing were a breed of fellows whose collective voices could melt gold.
It was not that they did not understand Yunyan’s meaning; they simply wanted him to act according to the mandate.
It is not that those under Xuefeng were wrong, but under Yaoshan, one is still ten thousand miles away."
Yunyan was once asked by Daowu, "Regarding the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, which one is the true eye?
Yunyan said, "It is like a person feeling for their pillow at night with their back turned. Daowu said, "I understand. Yunyan asked, "How do you understand it?
Daowu said, "The whole body is hands and eyes. Yunyan said, "To speak thus is to speak far too much; you have only spoken to eight-tenths of the truth. Daowu said, "Master..."
"What about your elder brother? Yan said, "His entire body is hands and eyes.

Baiyan Fu remarked, "Although these two great elders have eyebrows that resemble one another and nostrils that are faintly alike, they nonetheless do not fail to possess the True Eye of Great Compassion. As for Baoshou, however, it is not so. Today there is..."
Question: "Among the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye? [The Master] points toward him and says, "Blind!
If he were to say, "I understand," I would ask him: "Why is it that within Yunmen’s pavilion one does not see what lies beyond Tanggong Ridge?
If he hesitates even for a moment, I would strike him a heavy blow and drive him out. Why? Is it not said: "Pervasive"?
The body is hands and eyes.
Once, when Yunyan returned from visiting the Stone Chamber with the temple steward, Yunyan asked him, "When you went in there, why did you come back so quickly?
The steward had no reply. Dongshan spoke on his behalf, saying, "Someone has already occupied it there. Yunyan said:
"Why do you go away again? Shanshan said, "I cannot let human feelings be severed.
Tiantong Jue said: "Lowering the head, one loses the needle; opening the eyes, one picks up the thread. The thread has no end to measure;
the needle has no eye through which to pass. Reaching this point, even the *luan* glue needed to mend a broken string requires Dongshan himself."
[Daowu] said, "Yes. Yunyan addressed the assembly: "There is a man's son who, when questioned, has nothing he cannot explain.
Dongshan stepped forward and asked, "How many scriptures and commentaries are there in his house? Yunyan replied, "Not even a single character. Dongshan said, "How..."
"You have attained such vast knowledge," [Zhao]shan said. Yanguan replied, "Day and night I have never slept. Shan asked, "May I ask you about one matter?
Yanguan said, "If I could speak it, I would not speak it."
Tianning Qi said: "The Way can be spoken, yet it is not spoken. How do you understand this? 'I have always regretted that when spring departs there is no place to find it;
I did not know it had turned back and entered right here.'"
Yunyan asked a monk, "What have you been doing? The monk replied, "I have been talking on a stone. Yunyan said, "Does the stone nod its head too?
The monk was speechless. Yunyan provided the answer for him, saying, "It nods its head before you even speak."
Dongshan Yingdeng spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "How fortunate that the Master provides this testimony.
Chengguo Xingdeng spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "What is the use of making him nod his head?
He added, "If that monk had been able to utter a single word at that moment, it would have guaranteed that the old fellow Yunyan would have had no choice but to retire."
Chan Master Chuanzi Decheng of Huating in Xiuzhou (a successor of Yaoshan Yanzhao of Qingzhou): When Jia Shan came to visit him, the Master asked, "What monastery do you reside at, Virtuous One?
Jia Shan said, "I do not reside in a monastery; where I reside is unlike [ordinary places]. The Master asked, "If it is unlike anything, what is it that resembles [it]?
Jia Shan said, "It is not a phenomenon of the present moment. The Master asked, "Where did you learn this? Jia Shan said, "Not from anywhere."

Regarding everything that reaches the ears and eyes, the Master said: "A single phrase that hits the mark is a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas. The Master further said: "The fishing line hangs a thousand feet;
the intent lies in the deep pool. It is three inches away from the hook—why do you not speak? When Shan was about to open his mouth, [the Master struck him].
Zizhou struck him once, knocking him into the water. As soon as Shanshan climbed onto the boat, Zizhou said, "Speak! Speak!
Shanshan was about to open his mouth when Zizhou struck him again. At that moment, Shanshan attained great enlightenment and nodded his head three times.

Zizhou said, "The silk line on the tip of the rod is for you to handle; its meaning is distinct from the clear waves. Shanshan then asked, "Regarding casting the line and throwing the hook—what is your intention, Master?"

The Master said, "Silk suspended over green water; floating, it conveys the meaning of both existence and non-existence. Shanshan said, "The words carry the profound yet there is no path; the tongue speaks, yet there is nothing spoken.
The Master said, "Having fished through the waves of the river, only then is the golden-scaled fish encountered. Shanshan then covered his ears.
The Master said, "So it is, so it is. He then instructed him, saying: "In the future, you must leave no trace where there is a place to hide the body;
do not hide the body where there is no trace. For twenty years at Yaoshan, I have clarified only this matter.
Now that you have attained it, do not dwell in cities, prefectures, or villages hereafter. Instead, seek it within the depths of the mountains, by the side of your spade."
One person followed half a step behind the other; they did not let the succession be broken. When Shanshan was about to depart, he looked back again and again.
The Master (Zi) then called out to the *ācārya*. Shanshan turned his head. The Master raised his oar and said, "Did you think there was something else?
Thereupon, he overturned the boat and vanished into the water.
Changlu Liao said: "The oars are turned and the head is steered; the Milky Way and stars shine forth. The boatman steps upon it and the heavens and earth turn pitch black.
Holding up his whisk, he said: "This is that which is dry, white, and utterly pure on the side of the spade.
Do you know that which cannot hide its traces even where there are no tracks?"
Baiyan Fu said: "Nowadays, there are many who can provide answers that hit the mark; yet how could they all be like Jia Shan, who abandoned his followers upon seeing Chuanzi?
And how could they be like Chuanzi, who used the tongs and hammer of his teaching to receive Jia Shan?"
These two men were truly a match for one another in all of antiquity. Yet the Boatman said, "For twenty years at Yaoshan, I have sought nothing but this matter.
Now tell me, what matter is this? A monk stepped forward from the assembly, raised his sitting cloth, and asked, "Is it not this very thing?
Yunyan suddenly seized his staff and said, "Do not mistake the cry of a crane for the sound of a wild goose!"
The oriole sings. [Zhaozhou] went straight out through the Dharma Hall.
Chuanzi had a verse that said: "For thirty years I have roamed the seas; The water is clear, the fish appear, yet they do not swallow the hook.
When the fishing rods are worn out, I plant new bamboo; Without calculating the labor, I find rest as soon as it is convenient."
Baizhang Xue said: "Though the Great and Small Chuans were seeking people by descending into the weeds, they were far too clamorous.
Bianshan is not like this. For decades I have wandered upon these mountains; the grass is deep, the forests are dense, and the herds of beasts are thick.
At ease, I cast down a net that covers the heavens; there are golden-maned lions, and there are also monkeys. But tell me, can a monkey serve as [a true successor]?"
"What is the use? To perform an ordinary somersault and provoke the onlookers to laugh incessantly.
He then looked left and right and said, "Is there no golden-maned lion here? Come forth and display your teeth and claws!"
When Chan Master Huisheng of Pishu in Xuanzhou (a successor of Yaoshan Yan of Qingyuan) was lying down, Daowu came to visit him.
Finding Sheng in bed, Daowu approached and pulled the blanket over him. Sheng asked, "What are you doing? Daowu said, "Covering you.
Sheng asked, "Are you lying down or sitting up? Daowu said, "It is neither of these two. Sheng said, "But what about the fact that you have covered me? Daowu then...
"Ho! Zhaojue Qin said: "Bashu lies down and rises; Daowu covers him over. With one shout right at the head, the proclamation is overturned and revealed."
Taisuī Zhìyún said: "Meeting without avoiding; here we play for a while. He gave a shout and said:
"Turning heaven over and overturning the earth!
Bǎoshòu Fāng said: "These two fellows, pushing and prodding one another, refuse to let go; they do not fail in their [dharma] duty."
This is the clashing and striking between host and guest. It occurs at the very end;
when Daowu let out a shout, why did Bishu immediately stop? If you can see this scene here, I will grant that you have met Bishu face-to-face.
Chan Master Mingzhe of Boyan in Ezhou (successor of Yaoshan Yan of Qingzhou): When Dongshan and his senior teacher, Master Mi, visited him, Boyan asked, "Where have you two venerable monks come from?
Dongshan replied, "From Hunan. Boyan asked, "What is the surname of the Military Inspector?"
Baizhang said, "He cannot have a surname. Yangshan asked, "What is his name? Baizhang said, "He cannot have a name. Yangshan asked, "Does he still attend to administrative affairs?
Baizhang said, "There is naturally a hall and a screen for him. Yangshan asked, "Does he still come and go? Baizhang said, "He does not come and go.

Yangshan said, "How can it be that he does not come and go? Yangshan then shook out his sleeves and departed. The next day, Baizhang entered the hall and summoned the two head monks, saying, "Yesterday..."
The old monk said, "I have not found a single turning word that accords with yours, Dharma brother. I have been restless all night. I now ask you, Senior, to offer another turning word.
If it satisfies my mind, I shall open the rice gruel and stay with you for the summer retreat. Dongshan said, "Then I request the Master to ask the question.
Baizhang asked, "How is it when there is no coming or going? Dongshan said, "It is too noble. Baizhang then [laughed].
They opened the gruel together to pass the summer retreat.
Zhaojue Qin said: "The interplay of the Correct and the Deviant requires only perfect integration; responding directly to the immediate occasion honors only the noble.
Dongshan acted according to the capacity of his audience, while Boyan followed the principle of what was most appropriate. Even so, it depends on Jiang.
In this matter, you must develop a distinct eye of discernment before you can succeed. At that time, when he says, "I do not understand the name," you should immediately press him, saying:
"He does not understand you, and you do not understand him. I ask you: what words should be spoken here?
Is there anyone who can speak them? If there were someone who could, even I, this mountain monk, would not open my mouth.
"Congee. He simply handed over a whisk made of tortoise hair. "If you cannot say anything, study for another thirty years.
Tiantong Jie said: "Brightly cast, it meets in the dark; brilliant on all eight sides. Without striking the head-on, there is a path to turn back.
This is sufficient to behold the splendor under the Caodong school. As for the descendants of Linji, even if their staffs were broken, they would not have accepted this."
At that time, when he saw the Way, [Zhaozhou] did not inquire about his surname; he struck him a blow across the spine.
If one can turn the body here, it is not merely a matter of extending the offering of gruel, but is also an arrangement beneath the bright window. Is there such a person? Is there?
He gave a shout and said, "A lacquer bucket! Go to the hall! Tiantong Jue said:
"To maintain the gate, one naturally relies on those who come from the side. With solemnity in respectful silence, who would dare look him straight in the eye?

He employs expedients through borrowed function and maintains the position by shifting his station. Distributing authority to the left and right, he does not violate the singular path of supreme dignity."
Do you still know the place of honor? The precious palace is empty, with no one to stand in attendance; by not planting the *wutong* tree, one avoids the arrival of the phoenix.
Tianning Qi said: "If you wish to understand the single path of the honorable, Baoen does not open his two flaps of skin. You!
"Where are all you people groping? Baoshou Xinyou said:
'If you were Xinzuo, as soon as he said, "He is too noble," you should spit right in his face. Is there anyone here who would not be indignant? Come forth and act as the host for Dongshan!"* *Note:

This passage is a classic Chan encounter dialogue (gong'an) concerning the relationship between Dongshan Liangjie and his teacher Baoshou Xinyou. The text challenges the listener to demonstrate authentic, unmediated action rather than intellectualizing the situation.*
One day at mealtime, Layman Gao of Lǐzhōu (a successor of Yǎn of Yàoshān, recorded in Volume Three of the *Qīngyán*) saw Yàoshān beating the drum himself.
Gao then entered the hall dancing while holding his alms bowl. Yàoshān immediately threw down the mallet and asked, "Which chorus is this?
Gao replied, "This is the second chorus. Yàoshān asked, "What is the first chorus? Gao went to the rice bucket, scooped up a ladleful of rice, and departed.
Guangyin Biao remarked: "These two old fellows sing and respond to one another like this, as if they were oblivious to everyone else.
Had Mukan been there at that time, he would have kicked over both the rice tubs at once; let us see what he would have done next."
The novice Gao built a hut on the southern slope of Mount Yao. One day he came to pay his respects; it happened to be raining.
Mount Yao asked him, "Have you come? Gao replied, "Yes. The Mountain said, "It is quite soaked. Gao said, "One does not strike this broken drum. Yunyan said, "There is no hide;
what drum would one strike? Daowu said, "There is no drum; what hide would one strike? The Mountain said: [The text ends here.]
"What a magnificent performance today!
said Qinglong. "This lot of deluded fellows only know how to sell salt while ignoring the scale.
Had I been there at that time, I would have simply said, "Magnificent! But do not strike this broken drum and flute. What more need be said?
What a fine melody! It is like a puppet show on a stage where the director cannot finish the performance in time.
Baokong Fachuang said: "Yaoshan, father and son, have been drilling and hacking aimlessly into this single plot of ground."
Suddenly, there comes forth a man of impetuous temperament who strikes him with a single blow, and one sees the ice melt and the fortress crumble.
Yunxi Ting said: "Although Yuyan and Daowu were skilled at playing the stringless lute and singing the tuneless song, their nostrils nonetheless remained entirely in the hands of the novice."
When the novice Gao first visited Yaoshan, Yaoshan asked, "Where have you come from? Gao replied, "I have come from Nanyue. Yaoshan asked, "Where are you going?
Gao said, "I am going to Jiangling to receive the precepts. Yaoshan asked, "What do you hope to gain by receiving the precepts? Gao replied, "I hope to escape birth and death.
Yaoshan said, "There is a person who does not receive the precepts and yet has no birth and death to escape. Do you know who this is?"
"Do you understand? Gao asked. Daoshan replied, "If that is so, then what use are the Buddha's precepts? Gao said, "This śrāmaṇera still has some teeth left.
Gao then prostrated and withdrew, never again ascending to receive the precepts.
Yunju Xian said: "When High Sāmanera was pointed out by that single word, he immediately knew his place of return.

He was like a king of geese selecting milk from water, or a golden-winged garuḍa soaring through the sky; he truly possessed great spirit. Nevertheless, if one were always to act in this way, one would destroy one's own descendants.
Here at Yunju, we do not know how to play with the head of a dead snake; we simply administer medicine according to the illness."
Today, using the ten-branch method, I entrust the black-lacquered robe and bowl before the assembly of humans and devas with both hands.
Why? Because the waves of Caoxi are like those of the sea; countless ordinary people are submerged and lost.
Longyuan Faying said, "This fellow had his eyes plucked out by Yaoshan; do you still not know who that person was?
Changshan Liang said, "He defiles the pure tradition of the lineage and corrupts the children of the family—old Yaoshan!"
Han was already unable to evade his responsibility. As for Lord Gao, he did not plan for the peace of the state, but valued only the honor of a marquisate;
how, then, could this not be a betrayal of the sovereign’s intent toward the altars of soil and grain?
Xianfeng concluded by saying: "To skillfully cast fragrant bait and set a silken trap may be called fishing and hunting;
to be able to raise the red banner and capture a string of cities is truly to possess courage and valor. This is what is meant by 'Father and Son' at Yaoshan. It is indeed so.
Yet, as for the saying that there is one person who does not receive the precepts and has no birth-and-death from which to be exempted—tell me, who is this person?"

Master Youke Xuan said, "In this matter, it is not so. If someone were to say, 'There is a person who does not receive the precepts and yet cannot escape birth and death,' one should simply spit in their face.

At that time, had High Seat Gao been able to employ such a move, not only would he have manifested his own natural, majestic bearing, but he would also have caused Old Man Yaoshan to cut out his own tongue.

△ Qing-3: Chan Master Longtan Chongxin of Lizhou (Successor of Tianhuang Wu of Qing-3). Because Deshan came to visit him, he went straight up to the Dharma Hall.
He said, "I have long heard of Dragon Pond. But now that I have arrived, neither the pond nor the dragon appears.
The pond raised its body and said, "Son, you have truly reached Dragon Pond. Deshan was speechless and subsequently took up residence there.
Xuedou Xian said, "Taking error for error.
Yunfeng Yue said, "The great Deshan was pickled to death in a jar of leeks.
Huanglong Xin said, "When Xuedou speaks thus, is it Deshan who takes error for error, or Longtan?"
"Follow the error by correcting it. A monk who recognizes good and ill fortune must know where to go; those who have not yet passed through the barrier should likewise discern this.
Do you understand thoroughly? Even if you manage to plant and cultivate it, it will not be timber for a great beam.
Tiantong Wu said: "Since it is already a pool, yet the dragon is neither seen nor manifested—why then do you say 'the son has arrived in person'?
This is much like trying to fit a square block into a round hole. You gentlemen, tell me: where do you see his arrival in person?
Try to judge for yourselves."
Gounan said: "The old fellow of Longtan committed a robbery upon the person itself.
It is a pity that Deshan’s teeth were like a forest of swords and his mouth like a blood-basin; he drove him into a snare and a pitfall, yet [Deshan] did not know how to avoid it.
Now tell me, where does the point of profit and loss lie?"
Qixia Chengyun said: "Longtan uses shrimp to fish for carp; Deshan mistakes a servant for his master.
These two old fellows deserve thirty solid blows each. Someone asked: "Setting aside Deshan for a moment, where does Longtan’s fault lie?"
One who is heading toward the Way should not bewitch the men and women of others’ households.
Chan Master Wuxue Cuiwei of Jingzhao (a successor of Qingxi Danxia Ran) was asked by Longya: "Since arriving at the Dharma seat of the Master..."
Every time he went up to consult [the Master], he did not receive even a single teaching or instruction. What was his intention?
Cui said, "What is it that you find lacking? Ya again asked Dongshan. Dongshan replied, "How can you blame me, old monk?"
Fayan Yi remarked, "The Patriarch has arrived.
Xuedou Xian said, "These two old fellows have been thoroughly exposed by this monk; only Fayan was a fellow student with him.
Had he been under Xuedou's gate, they would have been beaten with a staff and driven out."
Yunju Qi said: "Do these three venerable elders have any distinction between near and far? If they do, which one is near?
If there is no distinction between near and far, where are their eyes?"
Cuiwei went to Qingping to inquire: "What is the great meaning of the West? Cuiwei said, "I will tell you when there is no one here.
After a long silence, Qingping said, "There is no one; please, Master, speak. Cuiwei descended from his meditation seat and led Qingping into the bamboo grove.
Qingping spoke again, "There is no one; please, Master, speak. Cuiwei pointed to the bamboo and said, "This..."
"The pole is so long; how can that pole be so short? At these words, Ping attained realization.
Tiantong Muan said: "To seek realization before Cuiwei had even dropped his excrement is already the 'second head.
As for those who claim to have awakened within the bamboo garden, they are truly at the 'eighth head. After all, what is it? [He] looked around."
The assembly said, "Eh! This was almost enough to have broken Caizhou.
Regarding Chan Master Xingkong of Xiaoyi in Jizhou (the third generation of Qingzhou, successor to Danxia Ran): once, as a monk was visiting him, Xiaoyi extended his hand to show it to him.
The monk stepped forward and then retreated. Huaiyi said, "Both your parents have passed away, yet you show not even a hint of grief.
The monk laughed loudly. Huaiyi said, "In a moment, I shall offer my condolences for your master. The monk performed a handstand and left. Huaiyi cried out, "Heaven! Heaven!"
Zhaojue Qin said: "Stretching out both hands, one sees only the sharpness of the awl's tip; advancing forward or retreating backward, one does not see the sharp-pointed awl.
Hehe! A great laugh—within the laughter there is a blade. He cries out to the blue heavens—his bow is broken and his arrows are spent."
Tell me, after all, what is it? After a long silence, he said: "If one does not cross together upon the bridge, how can one believe that the bridge flows while the water does not?
Master Xian Tian (successor of Qingji Dachuang) was approached by a monk who prepared to prostrate. Tian said, "Wild fox! What do you see?"
As soon as he had finished speaking, [Tianlin] bowed. [Xuefeng] said, "Old bald slave, what have you seen that you ask such a question? Tianlin said, "Alas! Alas!
Today, Xiantian has forgotten what came before and lost what followed. [Xuefeng] said, "Nevertheless, when one attains the moment, one does not compensate for what was lost."
The deity said, "Is it not so? The monk asked, "Who would accept this? The deity laughed heartily and said, "Far, far indeed!
The monk looked around and departed. Peakong Miao said:
"In one question and one answer, there is host and guest; all say that both are masters of the craft. If..."
According to my own examination, this monk is still somewhat acceptable; Xiantian, however, is laughable to the point of death.
Yangshan Ding said, "Everyone says these two fellows meet arrow-point to arrow-point and respond with fists and kicks, but according to Yangshan’s own examination, they are worlds apart."
Baiyan Fu said: "The dragon of the great marsh and the tiger of the deep forest—when they encounter one another head-on, it is not that the wind does not howl and the clouds do not roll up;
yet, alas, the pure customs of antiquity have been shattered like tiles."

When the immortal Tianyin visited to pay his respects, a monk from Silla had just spread out his sitting mat when the immortal seized him and said, "Before you departed from your own country, bring me a single phrase.
The monk was speechless. The immortal then pushed him out and said, "He asked him for one phrase, yet he spoke two."
Baoshou Fang said: "This monk was left speechless. While it is not without merit that he has built a mountain nine fathoms high, alas, at the very end he lacks the final basket of earth.
Had he been a man whose beginning and end were in harmony, when the master asked him a question, he would have replied with two;
he could have simply said, 'I regret having come so far,' and thus brought the matter to a conclusion."
Xiantian said, "This fellow has the capacity to open the East Gate wide.
Guangyin Biao asked, "Tell me, where are these two lines of this monk's Way? Try to analyze them."
If you can analyze it out, the Immortal has been seen through by you; if you cannot analyze it out, you have failed the Immortal’s labor.
Chan Master Sanping Yizhong (successor of Qingzai Dadian) asked Dadian: "Do not point east and speak of the west."
"Please, Master, point it out directly. Mazu said, "A stone man crouching at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou.
Huangbo said, "That is still pointing east while talking about west. Mazu said, "If one is a phoenix chick, one does not seek it there. Huangbo bowed.
Mazu said, "Had you not had the subsequent phrase, the preceding talk would have been difficult to complete."
Zhaojue Qin said: "This thorough, compassionate heart does not seek elsewhere. Father and son must meet in accord;
otherwise, one enters the weeds for no reason.
When Sanping ascended the seat, a Daoist stepped forth from the assembly, walking from east to west, while another monk followed from the west.
As they passed to the east, Baizhang Pingshan said, "The Daoist just now actually had some insight; the monk, however, has not yet attained it.

The Daoist came forward, prostrated, and said, "I thank the Master for guiding me. Pingshan struck him. The monk came forward, prostrated, and said, "I beg the Master for instruction. Pingshan struck him as well.
He again summoned the assembly, saying, "How would you settle these two cases? Is there anyone who can settle them?
He asked this three times, but the assembly remained silent. Baizhang said, "Since no one can settle them, I shall settle them for you.
Thereupon, he threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
Taisu Zhe said, "Had it not been for the old fellow Sanping, [Zhaozhou] would have nearly used intellectual reasoning to sever [the matter].
Did you not see Shigong say, 'For thirty years, with one bow and two arrows, I have only managed to shoot half a sage'? Indeed."
Sanping had a verse that says: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing; There is no further sound or form to present to you.
If one understands this point, there is nothing at all; Why should essence and function be divided or not?"
Tiantong Jue said: "Directly meeting, there is no point of contact. The six doors are not closed; the four crossroads are traceless.
The entire world is radiance; the whole body has no front or back. At such a time as this, what is it?
When the shuttle-head is unattached to the warp and weft, the patterns flow freely and the meaning is naturally distinct."
Master Bensheng (successor of Qingyuan Sandian) addressed the assembly. Holding up his staff, he said: "If I raise it, you immediately apply intellectual reasoning to the moment before it was raised.
If I do not raise it, you immediately exercise your own mastery over the moment it is raised.
Tell me, in what place does this old monk act for the sake of others? At that time, a monk came forward and said: "I dare not give rise to false thoughts."

[The Master] said, "This is a 'joint' (a difficult point). The monk said, "I know, O *ācārya*, that you do not treat me with partiality. [The Master] said, "Where it is low, leveling it leaves something remaining;
where it is high, observing it reveals a deficiency. The monk said, "A joint arises upon a joint. The monk was speechless. The Master said:
"Covering one's nose while stealing fragrance—this only invites criminal liability.
Xuedou Xian said, "This monk is indeed skilled at critical inquiry, yet alas, his bow is broken and his arrows exhausted.
None compare to our own Master Bensheng, a true adept of the school; when he raises [his hand], heaven turns and earth revolves—one must simply fold one's hands in submission."
Surrender! When you let go, it is like grass bowing before the wind; you will surely be able to preserve your whole being and distance yourself from harm.

But do you see the place where your original birth functions as a human being? Again, he took up his staff and said: "Peace is originally brought about by the generals, yet they are not permitted to witness that peace."
Gunanmen said: "Both Bensheng and Xuedou were accomplished masters who exerted their full strength for the sake of others.
Yet, how regrettable that they were burdened by too many complications! It would have been better if this monk had cut them off all at once. Why? Have you not heard it said:
'Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on it long ago, yet until this very day he has not attained the wondrous'? [He] threw down his staff and said: 'It is.'"
What? Xuedou said directly: "Although this monk possesses the spirit of a patch-robed monk, how can he be blamed for lacking the strategy to 'pull at the tiger's whiskers'?
Had he broken the staff in hand at that moment, not only would the monk’s fangs and claws have been revealed, but it would also have spared [the Master] from [this predicament]."
Xuedou creates further complications upon what is already complex.
Chan Master Shandao of Shishi in Tanzhou (a successor of Qingyuan Xingsi and Changzhi Kuang) would, whenever he saw a monk approach, simply raise his staff and say:
"All Buddhas of the three periods of time arise entirely from this. Few could respond with true resonance. When Changsha heard of this, he said:
"If I were to see him, I would immediately have him set down his staff and deliver another message.
When Sansheng responded with these words, Shishuang recognized them as the speech of Changsha. Hearing that Sansheng had missed the mark, Xingshan went personally to Stone Chamber (Shishi).
Upon seeing Xingshan arrive, Shishuang hid himself in the rice-hulling room to hull rice. Xingshan said, "It is no easy matter for an attendant to receive guests. I am poor..."
Xuedou said, "The Way is difficult to digest. Xiangshi said, "Bring it here in a bowl that pierces the heart; take it away in a platter that has no bottom.
What do you mean by 'difficult to digest'? At this, Xiangxiu ceased.
Zhaojue Qin said: "The stone chamber sets forth a question that is indeed solitary and lofty. Were it not for Changsha, how could one have found the opportune moment?
Although it is thus, one only knows 'it is thus,' but does not know 'it is not thus. He then raised his staff and said:"
The Buddhas of the past were not like this; the Buddhas of the present are not like this; the Buddhas of the future will not be like this.
Even if you were to say, "I have set down my staff," I would know that you are merely a person who parrots the words of others.
When the vital energy arises, bring forth a single phrase!
Tianning Qi, acting on behalf of Xingshan, said: "How can you take the property of the Sangha and put it under your robes and bowl to use?
Ba’en Xu said: "One is a cotton-wrapped stone; the other is an iron-bound lump of clay.
To let go is the *gui* and *zhang* jade vessels of the temple; to hold fast is the swallow and sparrow within the hall. He took up his staff and said: "Thus!"
Nor is it so. Not being thus is also not so. Letting go and not letting go are both not so. [He] strikes the meditation staff and says:
"A sky-reaching long sword, its coldness overwhelms people."
In the flourishing era of Huiyun, Xingshan said: "Above all, do not let your belly burst.
**Nan IV. Muzhou Longxing Daoming Chen Zunsu** (Nan IV. Successor of Huangbo Yun). Because a monk asked: "I respectfully bow to Śākyamuni..."
"How should one prostrate before Maitreya? The Master said, "Yesterday someone asked this; I chased him out.
The monk said, "I fear that I am not sincere enough, Master. The Master said, "The staff is not here; I will give you thirty blows with the handle of a broom for now."
Xuedou Xian said, "Muzhou only had the heart to receive the jade; he lacked the intention to cede the city.
Nantang Jing said, "For a monk, it is no extra effort to bow high to Śākyamuni and not prostrate to Maitreya."
One must also possess the essential tongs and hammer to be able to distinguish the true from the false. Why is this?

To emerge from the crowd, one must be a spirit-like child; to oppose and overcome others, one must be a lion’s cub. If one lacks such an eye for selecting Buddhas, even a thousand years would be of no avail.
Xichan Xu said: "If you wish to uphold the Great Dharma and proclaim the School of the Patriarchs, this old fellow is nearly there.
Do you all wish to see Muzhou? A sword leaves its precious scabbard because of injustice;
medicine comes from the golden jar to save the sick."
Nantang Yu said: "Xuedou’s critique in this manner deeply wrongs the ancients.
I, this mountain monk, say that although Muzhou set the whole dish out on the platter, he simply met with few who could appreciate him."
Gunanmen said: "Xuedou saw only one side; he did not realize that the old fellow Muzhou assigns office according to capacity, taking an ox from one person and returning a horse to another."
Longhua Ti said: "Xuedou saw only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but failed to see the squareness of its handle.
He did not realize that Muzhou was much like a golden-winged garuda cleaving the sea to seize and swallow the dragon directly.
Even so, he could not avoid being seen through by this monk."
Muzhou asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From over there, sir. Muzhou said, "I am at fault. The monk said, "The Master knows that, so it is fine.
Muzhou said, "A fellow carrying a cangue through the legal proceedings! He then struck him across the back.
Yunfeng Yue said: "Why did Muzhou use such elaborate words? 'Pointing there,' he would have struck him across the back immediately.
Muzhou addressed the assembly: "I saw that Baizhang did not know good from bad. As soon as the congregation had gathered, he struck them all down at once with his staff.
He then called out, 'The assembly! When they turned their heads, he said, 'What is this? There was no way for them to engage in conversation with him."
As soon as the assembly had gathered, Master Huangbo struck them all at once with his staff. He then called out to the assembly;
when they turned their heads, he said: "The moon is like a drawn bow—little rain and much wind. It is still somewhat better than that."
Xuedou Xian said, "Saying 'it is still somewhat better'—this is simply not yet it. According to Xuedou’s *Zhongji*, he would have struck them all down at once and left it at that.

If there were someone with an unperforated iron hammer who could exert their full strength for the sake of the assembly and skillfully shoulder this burden, they could encompass past and present and hold fast heaven and earth. Then, suddenly picking up his staff, he said: "Let go!"
After one turn, Langya Jue said, "If you enter the great waves, you must be a man who can play in the tide.
Lingyin Yue said, "The more one looks, the more it appears contradictory. These several fellows have come out to set up nets and snares. However—
Wading in the shallow waters to catch shrimp and clams, one exhausts one’s own mind and cracks open the mouths of others.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Baizhang brandishing his staff to call the dog cannot avoid being met with mutual glaring resentment;
Huangbo’s fragrant bait on the hook causes those who swallow it to lose their bodies and lives; Muzhou raising this up before the assembly is like providing a ladder for a thief to pass over."
Xuedou wanted people to shoulder [the burden]; he stirred up waves where there was no wind. Today, Chongning does not act in this way at all.
Everyone, please return to the hall. Gounmen said:
"Muzhou borrowed a sword to kill a man; Xuedou detained the prisoner to increase his wisdom. Although it is for this purpose...

Everyone exert your utmost strength! Yet, Baizhang and Huangbo were not at all left out. Do you understand? Carrying his staff slung across his shoulder, he pays no heed to others and strides straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks.
Muzhou asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk gave a shout. Muzhou said, "The old monk has been shouted at by you.
The monk shouted again. Muzhou said, "After three shouts and four shouts, what then? The monk was speechless. Muzhou struck him and said, "This fellow is a hollow swindler!"
Letan Qing said, "This monk only knows how to look forward and cannot look back. To travel on pilgrimage in such a manner is to bring people to utter frustration.

The Essential Principle of the Child: I dare ask all of you, how would you handle this monk? Would you bid him "take care" and let him go?
Or would you wait for him to come back after three days? Or would you have him pass from east to west? Or would you remain silent for a long while?
Or would you wave your sleeves and leave the hall? Or would you circumambulate his seat three times?
Is it performing the prostration of a woman? Or is it raising the eyebrows, winking the eyes, pointing a finger, or clenching a fist?
Or is it overturning the Dharma seat and shouting to disperse the assembly? All that has been done thus far is merely playing with the vital spirit.
Ultimately, how will you produce the single hand and eye to establish the fundamental tenet together with this mountain monk? Do you understand? A crane.
There are nine gorges where wings cannot soar; there are no horses that can vainly chase the wind for a thousand *li*.
An ancient inscription at the South Gate says: "The orthodox lineage of Hebei is like lightning striking;
yet Ke Fu Puhua, instead of fighting on the field, raises his army from behind the lines. This was intended to strip Linji of his attainment. Today, this mountain monk..."

I wish to establish the school of Linji at this mountain. Should there be a monk who, seeing the righteousness, acts with valor and enters directly with a single blade, coming forward and saying, "What did the Master say? I would strike him across the back with my staff.
Or should there be a second monk who comes forward and says, "Master, why did you just strike that monk? I— [the mountain monk] —[would strike him as well].
The monk also received a blow across his back. Tell me, how far apart was he from Linji? Suddenly picking up his staff, he said:
"The eye upon the tip of the staff is as bright as the sun; if you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire."
Foji said: "To wield authority beyond the threshold and to hold the sovereign command within the realm—this is not without Linji.

Yet, as for establishing the school of Huangbo, there is still a great distance to go. Why is this? Since it is the establishment of a school’s fundamental tenets, why is it that only two people are required to bring it to completion?
Reverend Shi respectfully received the imperial decree to establish [the lineage] here at Tian."

Regarding the essential meaning of the Patriarchs’ school: we have already relied upon the Sagely Son of Heaven extending a single hand. But as for the great assembly present here now, how shall they bring it to completion?
He strikes the meditation staff and says: "Together we prop up this gate that reaches to the heavens; the Dharma-ocean is vast as the myriad nations come as guests."
Yanjiao Le said: "Linji let loose his power of killing and giving life throughout the world, wielding authority beyond the frontier gates.

He was truly one whose spirit intimidated the masses and whose bearing stood alone. While it is not that he lacked the establishment of a school’s fundamental tenets, if one examines him closely, it is like drawing one's bow after the thief has already fled."
Linji addressed the assembly: "Those who seek the Dharma do not shrink from losing body or life.
At the place of my former teacher, I asked three times about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma; on each occasion, I was struck with a blow like a whisk made of mugwort.
If I were to think of another blow now, who would be willing to deal it? At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I will deal it. Linji took up his staff.
Linji took his staff and gave it to him; as the monks were about to intervene, Linji struck them.
Xuedou Xian said, "Linji was perilous in letting go, yet too hasty in gathering back.
Wuzu Ji said, "Linji is much like a poor man thinking of his old debts."
Xuedou Zong said: "Tell me, is the staff Linji uses today the same as the staff he received from Huangbo back then, or is it different?
If you say they are the same, you fail Huangbo. If you say they are different, you wrong Linji."
"If someone were to come forth with their full capacity, tell me, in whose sphere would they be? He then picked up his staff and said, "Step back! Step back!
Lingyin Yue picked up his staff and said, "Linji acts according to the mandate, yet he does not realize he has brought disgrace upon Huangbo."
Xuedou exerts all his strength carrying a wooden board, yet he sees only one side.
Tell me, where does the crux of Jianfu lie? [He] throws down his staff.
Jingshan Xiu said: "Linji is truly like a poor man thinking of old debts; this monk is just like a starving dog eating a tangled rope.
Xuedou said: "Linji’s letting go was perilous, and his pulling back was too fast. 'Intoxicated by me in the day of falling blossoms;
borrowing from within his strings and pipes.'"
Nantang Yu said: "What is he saying? 'To let go is perilous; to pull back is too fast.

Although one knows that Linji possesses the trap-for-tigers mechanism, this monk has not yet attained the eye for penetrating the barrier. Wait until he says, 'I must think it over once more,' and who will strike the blow?
Then you should overturn the meditation seat. This would not only block the throat of this old fellow, but moreover—"
"There is a path for those of noble origin.
Fu Long said: "Regarding the two venerable masters Xuedou and Lingyin—one has both ears deaf, and the other has one eye blind.
Not only do they fail Linji, but they also bring ruin to their own descendants. Wuming now...
One day, seeing an injustice on the road, he thought, "I must clear this man's grievance. After a long silence, he said, "Do not touch it;
if you touch it, I will break your donkey's back!"

Tongxuan Qi said: "If Linji, though holding the rank of a high minister, did not forget his days as a wandering mendicant, this monk is like a son of humble station who attempts to pose as a guest at the gate of a noble house."
Baoguang said: "The Great Master Linji’s 'buying high and selling low' was nothing short of reckless.
This monk stood firm in his principles and charged into battle, regardless of losing his body or life. As for his saying, 'It is like a broom made of mugwort,' what was his meaning?
Her cloud-like hair is not yet combed; the fragrance seeps through the dew-drenched flower branches."
Qinghuo said, "This monk is also like a newborn calf that does not fear tigers.
Had he been a man who acted with courage upon seeing what was right, he would have snatched the staff back then and there; where else would Linji be?"
Longhua Ti said: "Linji luring people into breaking the law was certainly no good hand. Although this monk received the blows, he was simply not satisfied.
