Dongta Xi said: "Great and small Linji—if it were not for this monk, you would have almost ended up in a state of total embarrassment. Although...
However, if I were that monk, I would wait for him to say, "Think it over again," and then ask, "Who will deal the blow?
Immediately, I would drag him down from the meditation seat and give him a severe beating. Let us see how he would manage to settle the matter.
Wufeng Fu said: "Although the ways in which Great and Small Linji acted may be called 'head straight and tail straight,' one cannot help but note that their nostrils were in the hands of this monk."
When a monk approached, Linji raised his whisk; the monk bowed, and Linji struck him. Another monk approached, and Linji raised his whisk;
the monk paid no heed, and Linji likewise struck him. Yet another monk approached, and Linji raised his whisk;
the monk said, "I thank the Master for this instruction," and Linji likewise struck him.
Yunmen Wenyan spoke on his behalf, saying: "It is simply fitting for this old fellow. Dajue said: "He has attained it, indeed;
yet he still has not seen the pivotal function of Linji. Yufan Yu said: "There is guest and host, there is illumination and function; therein, a single blow transcends all Buddhas."
A single blow is the crown of the ancestral patriarchs; a single blow supports heaven and props up the earth.
If anyone can discern this, I grant them the status of a descendant of Linji. A monk standing by said, "Old man, what kind of place is this?
Dividing first and dividing later, discussing Buddhas and discussing patriarchs! Baizhang then struck him and drove him out.
Once, while Linji was working together with the community in clearing the ground with a hoe, he saw Huangbo approaching and stood holding his hoe upright.

Huangbo asked, "Is this fellow tired? Linji replied, "The hoe hasn't even been lifted; what is there to be tired about? Huangbo struck him. Linji caught the staff and gave it a shove, knocking Huangbo over.
Huangbo then called for the *vina* (chant leader), saying, "Help me up! As the *vina* helped him up, Huangbo said, "How can you [behave like this], Master?"

"How can this madman be so impolite? Baizhang then gave Weinan a slap. Linji suddenly struck the ground with his staff and said, "Everywhere else they perform cremation; here I come to be buried alive."
Yangshan Ji said: "The real thief has fled; the officer who seized the loot eats the staff.
Wuwei Zhe said: "Huangbo falls to the ground; the rector helps him up. A cremation that is a living burial—the pure wind has not yet ceased."
Sanyao Songyun said: "A true dog does not steal oil; a rooster runs off clutching a lamp. Tongxuan Qiyun said:
"Linji’s receiving the staff was indeed swift; Huangbo’s taking the fall was truly sweet.
Yet, one who takes another's place in punishment cannot evade their responsibility. For Linji to speak in such a manner is to deceive people beyond measure."
Baiyan Fu said: "When a fire breaks out at the city gate, the disaster reaches the fish in the pond. There are many such instances; let us set them aside for now.
Generally speaking, when a family is wealthy, the children become arrogant—a situation truly difficult to manage with reason and propriety.
Is there anyone who can lend a hand to Huangbo? As soon as a monk stepped forward, Baiyan said, "Are you planning to act arrogantly? and struck him directly.
He emerged from the abbot’s quarters.
While Linji was planting pine trees, Huangbo asked, "What are you doing planting so many pines in the deep mountains?
Linji replied, "First, to provide a scenic setting for the mountain gate; second, to serve as a landmark for future generations. Having said this, he struck the ground with his hoe.
Huangbo struck the ground three times. Baizhang said, "Even so, you have already received thirty blows from me.
Linji then struck the ground three times and let out a sigh. Huangbo said, "My school will flourish greatly in the world through you."
Taisuī Zhe said: "Linji’s doing so is much like tripping and falling on level ground. Nevertheless, only by remaining unchanging in the face of peril can one be called a man of stature.
Huangbo said: "That my lineage has reached you and flourishes greatly in the world—this too is out of a father's fondness for his son, such that he does not notice his child's ugliness."
Tiantong Hua said: "Yellow Peak said, 'Even though it is so, you have already received thirty blows from me.
The conditions for raising a child must indeed be such as this. Although Linji’s true command was carried out, it is a pity that he willingly allowed himself to be buried alive by the mattock.
Today, Ying’an strips off his mask to meet you all. He then suddenly picked up [the whisk].
He struck his staff once and said: "To startle the multitude, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to overcome the victor, one must be a lion’s cub.
Linji ascended the hall and said: "Upon this ball of red flesh, there is a true person of no rank who is constantly present at the gates of the faces of all people."
Coming and going. Let those who have not yet seen the evidence look here. At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "What is the true person of no station?
Linji descended from his meditation seat, grabbed him, and said, "Speak! Speak! As the monk hesitated, Linji pushed him away and said, "What is this 'true person of no station'?
It is nothing but a dried-up shit-stick! He then returned to his quarters.
Xuefeng Yun said, "Linji is much like a thief who steals in broad daylight.
Xuedou Xian said, "A skilled thief is unknown even to ghosts and spirits. Since he has been seen through by Xuefeng, Linji was not a master hand.
He then called to the assembly, saying, "Today, Xuedou has exchanged the eyes of you all!"
If you do not believe this, each of you return to your quarters and investigate for yourselves.
Langya Huijue said: "Linji may truly be said to have crossed over the edge of an ice floe and attained his whole body upon the blade of a nine-edged sword."
Tianning Qisong said: "If Linji had not uttered his later words, he would have been captured when Caizhou was taken.
Nevertheless, unless a household possesses the Baitai talisman, such a monster will certainly not appear."

Yangshan Qian said: "Setting aside for a moment the fact that Linji was like a golden-winged bird cleaving the sea to seize and swallow the dragon directly—when this monk was seized by Linji, did he ultimately have words or not? 'When you see the moon, cease looking at the finger;
when you return home, stop asking about the path.'"
Longxiang said: "When two blades meet point-to-point, the arrow of Gouji does not miss its mark;
only when the plaster is ready to be carved can the axe of Master Ying be wielded. Linji’s usual demeanor was like that of a king, yet he played the games of a lowly servant;
had it not been for this, the Way of the Dharma would have been halted by a great wind. Today, Longxiang plays the part of death."
The horse-doctor: the "true person of no rank" bumps into and strikes against things; even when brought forward as evidence, it remains a mistake.
Now tell me: is it Linji who is wrong, or Longxiang? Let the people of the world speculate as they will.
The Pivot of the Celestial Jewel says: "The person of no station is a dry dung pellet. Linji was not yet a 'white-handed thief.
For a thousand ages it flies like a long white silk ribbon, a single line breaking the color of the green mountains."
Wushan Dao said: "Linji possessed the skill to seize dragons and the mechanism to trap tigers;
yet how could he have expected this monk to see right through him? Nevertheless, when that monk asked, 'What is the Unranked True Person?'—it was nothing but a piece of dried dung.
But what about it? He struck his staff and said: "Yellow chrysanthemums bloom across the earth; the entire world is spread with gold."
Nantang Yu said: "The sword that kills and the sword that gives life are the standard of conduct from antiquity and the essential pivot of the present age.
With the eyes of a dragon and the gaze of a hawk, one look pierces through everything;
thus, one may drive the plowman’s ox to make his crops flourish, or seize the food of the starving man to ensure he never again suffers from hunger and emptiness. It is precisely as described above."

When a general confronts the enemy on the battlefield, he shatters their ranks, beats his drums, and tears down their banners. Without the use of a single blade, corpses lie strewn for ten thousand *li*.
He ensures that the four barbarian tribes bring tribute and the eight regions submit to his rule. Is this not the achievement of a great man accomplishing the deeds of a great man?
If this were not so, do not come with right and wrong to judge me; the frivolous speculations of this floating life will not penetrate [the truth].
Related. Gu Nanmen said: "Often it is said that Master Linji was a 'white-handed thief. But tell me, what did he ever steal?
Xuedou said: "Since he was seen through by Xuefeng, where exactly was he seen through?"
"Regarding 'breaking through the place': although I, Guannan, do not today match the ancients in skillful stealth, I shall nevertheless explain it clearly for you all.
Thereupon, he dragged his staff and struck everyone down at once, dispersing them.
Jin-su Yuan said: "Linji’s letting go is perilous; his bringing back is too swift. If you recognize it, the 'true person of no station' enters and exits through the gate of the face.
If you do not recognize it, the 'true person of no station' likewise enters and exits through the gate of the face.
Setting aside for a moment whether you recognize it or not, how would you speak of the 'dry dung pellet'?"
Lingyin Li said: "Dahui speaking in this manner is much like Śakra Devendra restoring the great city of the three realms;
he has already cut off the vital thoroughfare without needing to brandish his mace or manifest his awesome power. Do you understand?"
[The Master] gave a shout and said: "If one does not look at the stubborn rock, how can one swallow the golden arrowhead?

How could one recognize the General’s heart in shooting the tiger? Longhuati said: "If this monk had been a true man back then, as soon as Linji stepped down from his meditation seat, he would have let out a thunderous shout.
This would have taught that fellow that there was no path forward and no room to retreat. Although...
However, Linji let this one matter pass for now. Xuefeng and Xuedou have passed it down to each other as a secret; it cannot simply be let go.
Thereupon, he suddenly seized his staff and struck everyone, dispersing them all at once.
Zifu Guang said: "Regarding this passage, I do not take its letting go, but I alone take its gathering in. What does this mean?
It is because he possesses a sword that, had it not been wielded at the precise moment for severance, would have invited chaos."
Chongqing once said: "Linji’s compassionate heart was revealed bit by bit, yet he could not avoid piling up bones on level ground. At that time, it was fortunate that there was this monk;
had it been a true man, when Linji said, 'What is the Unlocalized True Person? he would have replied, 'A dry piece of dung.'"
He then struck him across the face with his palm and said, "This fellow has wrongly applied a name; take it for granted that Linji will have cause to retreat.
Xidun Chao said, "Master Linji spent his entire life plucking tiger whiskers and twisting dragon horns; why is it that today..."
This is merely providing a footnote for others. Had I been there at that time, I would have clapped my hands and laughed loudly, saying:
"What desperate haste is this old fellow in? He has confessed before he was even asked!"
Baiyan Fu said: "Whether Great Linji or Small Linji let go or pull back, they are most swift.
It is simply like a gourd rolling and turning upon the surface of the water; where is there for you to grasp or conceive?
Nevertheless, as for that 'True Person Without Rank,' he can only serve as a lowly servant."
Caoshan Yong said: "Linji’s breast harbors strategic maneuvers; his ability to withdraw and advance at will makes him truly a master.
Although this monk pushed open the door and entered directly, disregarding danger and death, it is a pity that he has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake.
At that moment, had I been there, once I had him cornered, I would have given him a slap. Even if Linji possessed the mechanism for trapping a tiger, it would still have been so."
"You must retreat three thousand li.
Haimen Guang said: "Master Linji, great as he was, on one hand adds flowers to brocade, and on the other hand pulls out the nails from behind the head.
As for the 'True Man of No Station,' he has not yet arrived."
Xidu Jinzheng said: "Since he is the 'true person of no station,' why is he upon this ball of raw flesh?
Try to examine this!
Linji asked the monastery steward, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from selling yellow millet in the prefectural city. Linji said, "Selling..."
Ji asked, "Can it all be sold? The host replied, "It can all be sold. Ji struck the ground with his staff, making a single line, and said, "Can that which is here also be sold?
The host gave a shout. Ji struck him. Just then, the head cook arrived. Ji recounted the previous conversation.
The cook said, "The Abbot has not understood the Master's meaning. Ji asked, "And what about you? The cook bowed. Ji struck him as well.
Yellow Dragon Nan said: "When the Abbot lets out a shout, one must not let him pass. When the Steward prostrates, letting him pass is unacceptable.
Linji was strict in his commands; Guizong was lenient. Thirty years later, someone will explain this through."
Huanglong Xin said: "The kitchen steward’s prostration has fault but no merit; the abbot’s single shout has merit but no fault.
Since it has merit, why was he struck? The eyes upon the staff are as clear as the sun;
if you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire."

Tiantong Hua said: "Although these two venerable masters exerted great effort in upholding the essential principles, when examined closely, they could not avoid merely clinging to the grass and perching upon the wood.
Little did they know that the Great and Small Linji had their homes destroyed and their dwellings scattered by those two fellows."
Xichan Xu said: "The Head of the Monastery lets out a shout like lightning rolling and thunder crashing, mountains crumbling and the earth splitting apart.
The Steward bows in prostration as clouds gather and disperse, the moon brightens and the wind clears. Even so, why are they both struck with such severe blows?
Have you not heard it said: 'As soon as the Sleeping Dragon stirs, the Vermilion Phoenix soars away'?"
Baoneng Xiu said: "The head of the monastery was struck with a staff; in rewarding merit, one does not avoid an enemy. The master of offerings received grace;
in executing punishment, how could one choose between one's own flesh and blood? Tiantong Wu said: "Master Linji could not deceive him by even a single point. But where is [the deception]?"
At a point where one cannot deceive another, he took up his staff and said, "The eyes upon the tip of the staff are as clear as the sun;
if you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire. He then cast it down.

Guangjiao Yu said, "Although the head of the monastery and the chief cook have exerted every effort to carry on the burden, alas, at that time Linji only allowed half of the command to be carried out.
Had the command been fully implemented, how could there be a 'today' as we know it?
Have any of you ever seen this in a dream? He then took up his staff and struck them all down at once, dispersing them.
Huìyún said, "When the head of the monastery shouted, the cook prostrated; each had their own point of view.
Yet why did Linjì let neither of them off? Gold is naturally gold; how could one be willing to sell it mixed with sand?
Linji ascended the hall and said: "There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home; there is another person who leaves home yet is not on the road.
Which of these two is worthy of receiving the offerings of devas and humans?"
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "The thief’s identity has already been revealed.
Yunyan Tancheng said: "Recognize the meaning at the tip of the hook; do not fixate on the zero-point of the scale.
Jingshan added: "Linji’s insight was biased and one-sided; as expected, he possessed only a single eye. I, this mountain monk, [say]: [He was right].

Yesterday I arrived at Changguo to visit various officials and clerks. Going from east to west and from west to east, hurrying and bustling about, I spent the entire day only on the road. How, then, can one say that I did not leave my home?

Since returning these past days, I have joined my palms at the mountain gate, burned incense in the Buddha hall, passed through the monks' hall, and entered the kitchen and storehouse—all of these are [the home].
Regarding one's own home, how can you say "not departing from the road"? Members of the monastic community must speak according to reality;
if one does not speak according to reality, they are called a person of empty, deceptive speech—how could such a person receive the offerings of devas and humans?
Longjiao’s announcement was itself a minor deception. Now, for a single word of plain reality: [the answer follows].
"How would you say it? He then said: "From the beginning, I have never sung songs of empty deception; I hold fire to burn the mountains and gather marsh snails.
On the tips of white *nang* trees are fish-fans; on the rapids of rushing waters, birds build their nests.
Good brother! With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat once.
Yunju Zhuang said: "Whether one has left home or not left home, whether one is on the road or not on the road—let that be set aside for now.
This mountain monk says that throughout the entire great earth there is but one person worthy of receiving the offerings of devas and humans.
Do you all recognize that one person? He struck the whisk and said: "Do not let them open their eyes; the hawk has already passed."
Xinluo (Shinra) said, "Tianjie Shengyun, that little servant speaks like this; he still wants to eat some thistle!
Tiantong Mien said, "Master Linji has dropped his talk. Is there anyone who can examine it thoroughly?"
"Ma! If you can discern this, I grant that you have attained the same realization as him; you shall be worthy of receiving offerings from devas and humans.

If you have not yet reached this state, [the Master] lets out a shout and says: 'Do not bring matters of right and wrong to judge me; the worldly life’s forced interpretations have nothing to do with me.'"
An old master came to visit Linji, who said, "Is bowing the same as not bowing?
Linji then gave a shout. The old master bowed. Linji said, "What a fine grass-thief! The old master said, "Thief! Thief! and went out. Linji said, "Do not say there is nothing to it.
At that time, the Head Seat was standing nearby. Linji asked him, "Is there any fault here? He replied, "There is. Linji—
Yangshan said, "Is it the guest's fault or the host's fault? Yangshan said, "Both have faults. Jie asked, "Where does the fault lie?
The monk then went out. Jie said, "Do not say that there is nothing to it."
Nanquan Yuan said, "Official horses trampling one another.
Baoning Yong said, "This whole lot of bandits; among them there are both primary bandits and secondary bandits.
Now tell me, which is the primary bandit and which is the secondary? Can you discern this? It is easy to plead guilty, but the stolen goods—"
Difficult to discern. Huguo Yuan said: "The old master thrusts his body against the white blade; Linji’s merit is not in vain.
The Head Seat does not know how to observe from the sidelines; he brings upon himself a coating of mud and water. Even so, tell me: before this, there was nothing."
Compared to this state of "nothingness" that follows, how vast is the difference? Herein, the black and white are clearly distinguished.
Not only have you pierced the nostrils of Linji, but I grant that your eye-sight pierces through the four quarters of the world. If this is not yet so, do not say that "nothingness" is good.
Once, when Linji entered the kitchen with Huangbo, he asked the rice steward, "What are you doing? The steward replied, "I am sorting the rice for the assembly.
Huangbo asked, "How much do they eat in one day? He replied, "Two *shí* and five *dǔ*. Huangbo said, "Is that not too much? He replied, "I fear it may still be too little."
Huangbo struck him. The head cook reported this to Linji. Linji said, "That old fellow has already been cross-examined by you.
He then went to see Huangbo. Huangbo recounted the previous conversation. Linji said, "The head cook does not understand; please, Master, provide a turn of phrase on his behalf.
Huangbo said, "Just bring it up. Linji said, "Is that not too much? Huangbo said, "Tomorrow you shall eat another meal. Linji said, "To speak..."
"I will eat it right now instead of tomorrow. He then gave Baso a slap.
Baso said, "This madman has come here again to pull at the tiger's whiskers. Linji let out a shout and went out.
Guishan Lingyou said, "Only by raising a child does one come to know a father's compassion.
Yangshan Huiji said, "Huangbo was much like someone who lured a thief to ruin his own house.
Baoshou Yuanfang said, "This fellow Linji is accustomed to taking advantage of the situation; he is much like a son who becomes arrogant because his family is wealthy. This is precisely [the point].
Look at this: the tradition of the ancient Buddhas goes far beyond merely sweeping away the dust.
When Linji addressed the assembly, he said: "If you wish to be no different from the Buddhas and Patriarchs, simply do not seek outside.

The light of the pure mind in a single thought-moment is the Dharma-body Buddha within your own house; the light of the non-discriminating mind in a single thought-moment is [the Reward-body Buddha] within your own house..."
The Reward Body Buddha (Sambhogakāya) is the light of the non-discriminating mind in a single thought-moment; this is the Transformation Body Buddha (Nirmāṇakāya) within your own house.
These three bodies are none other than you, the person listening to the Dharma right now before your eyes. It is simply because you do not seek outward that such a function exists.
Shilin said: "The Great and the Small Linji were originally just people playing with light and shadow.
Had I seen them at that time, I would have given a shout to arrest them and overturned their meditation seat.
Not only would I have cut off their tongues, but I would also have spared future descendants from making their living within light and shadow."

Baiyan Fu said: "Everyone claims that the Linji school exclusively emphasizes directness and incisiveness, disparaging any other approach that involves language as being merely 'frivolous' or 'entangling.
If they were to read this statement by the Great Master, what would they think?
Although Shilin was able to conceal his father's faults for the sake of his son, he too knew only one side and remained ignorant of the rest."
The second point: One must realize that the Great Master was a master of eloquent speech; his vast and expansive waves were like the great ocean, containing everything within them.
How could those of small capacity—those who have only eaten a single meal from a pint of rice—ever hope to comprehend him?
Linji said, "Sometimes I use my shout not as a shout.
Shilin then remarked, "When a character is transcribed three times, the 'crow' becomes a 'horse. This old monk uses his shout only as a shout;
he sells stinking meat and rotten pickles to those who want them. Whether there is a fault or no fault, you all try to judge for yourselves."
"Look! [The Master] gave a shout.
Linji said, "One shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function operate simultaneously.
Zhaojue Qin gave a shout and said, "Now tell me: is it the guest or the host? Is it illumination or function? Do you understand?
"Sima! The momentum of a thousand peaks ceases at the edge of the mountain; the roar of ten thousand streams vanishes upon reaching the sea.
Chengshan let out a great shout and said, "Tell me, is this the guest or the host? Among the assembly, some said, "The guest and host are clearly distinct.
I would ask them, "What is this state of being clearly distinct? Before they could even deliberate, he would strike them across the spine.
A blow! Why? Because it is not seen that "illumination and function proceed simultaneously.
When Linji heard Deshan address the assembly, saying, "If you can speak it, thirty blows;
if you cannot speak it, thirty blows," he said to Luopu, "Go ask him why, even if one can speak it, there are thirty blows. Wait for him...
He struck him. Baizhang caught the staff and gave it a shove, watching to see what would happen.
Baofu asked as instructed. Deshan struck him; Baofu caught the staff and gave it a shove. Deshan then returned to his quarters and shut the door.
Baofu went back and reported this to Linji. Linji said, "I have always suspected this fellow. Nevertheless, do you recognize Deshan?"
Shanmo. As Pu hesitated, Linji struck him.
Yunju Qi said, "As for Linji’s statement, 'I have always suspected this fellow,' was that an expression of approval or disapproval?
Or is there some other underlying principle? Try to judge it."
Baiyan Fu said: "This red-tailed carp not only missed Deshan, it also missed Linji.
If I were Fu the Elder, I would have waited for Deshan to return to his quarters and close the door;
then, I would have written the character 'Seal' on the door. Upon his return, when Linji asks, 'Do you recognize Deshan? I would have answered him."
He then let out a thunderous shout, shook his sleeves, and departed. Nevertheless, do you know that both Linji and Deshan were entirely accounted for by Luopu?
When Linji’s two head monks met and simultaneously let out a shout, a monk asked, "Is there still a distinction between guest and host?
Linji replied, "Guest and host are perfectly distinct."
Guanghui Lian said: "When the two head seats of the hall meet and both let out a shout at the same time, tell me, do you see any guest or host here?
If you say there is, you are just a blind man; if you say there is not, you are also a blind man.
To say neither 'is' nor 'is not' is ten thousand miles from Yaizhou. If you can speak to this point, it would be well worth giving [you a blow]."
"Thirty blows! If you cannot say it, I shall likewise give you thirty blows.
"How can a patch-robed monk, having reached this point, find a way out of the mountain monk’s circle? After a long silence, he said, "Alas!
A frog and an earthworm leap up to the Thirty-three Heavens and crash into Mount Sumeru, shattering it into a hundred fragments. He then took up his staff and said, "A whole troupe!"
"A holeless iron hammer. Retreat quickly! Retreat quickly! Cheng Tianzong said:
"Linji’s words here have chased all the monks under heaven to their deaths. I, however, would not do so.
At that time, when asked whether there was still guest and host, I would simply say: 'A pair of holeless iron hammers.'"
Daguang Zhiyun said: "What is the principle of guest and host being clearly distinct?

If you can understand it, it is like a pair of solitary wild geese soaring high from the ground; if you have not yet realized it, it is like a pair of mandarin ducks standing alone by the edge of a pond."
Tiantong Jue said: "The sword that kills and the sword that gives life were in the hands of Linji.

Nevertheless, at that moment, when he said, 'Host and guest are clearly distinct,' and then let out a thunderous shout, even if one were to exert the greatest supernatural powers, one could only achieve resonance with the same sound."
Yuanwu Keqin said: "Try to examine this: which house is the guest and which is the host?
Where do guest and host interchange? If you say there is no guest or host, yet guest and host are clearly manifest before you.
If you say there is a guest and a host, then at the moment of a single shout, where are they divided? He struck his staff once and gave a shout.
He shouted, saying: "In my place here, there is both guest and host, and both illumination and function.
If you can discern this, you may be considered a fellow student of the two head seat monks. Is there such a one? Is there? Otherwise, I, the mountain monk, shall speak for myself."
He let out another shout, threw down his staff, and walked away.
Yun’an Yue said: “At that moment, if that monk had seen the Way clearly, with host and guest distinct, he should have overturned the meditation seat.
Even if Linji were to employ a different tactical maneuver, he would still fall short by two or three steps.”
As Linji was approaching his death, he said to the assembly, "After I have passed away, you must not let my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye be extinguished.
Sansheng stepped forward and said, "How would we dare let the Master's Treasury of the True Dharma Eye be extinguished?

Linji asked, "If someone asks you this in the future, what will you say to him? Sansheng then gave a shout. Linji said, "Who would have known that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would be directed toward..."
"Extinguish it at the side of the blind donkey. Guishan Xiu said:
"The ancients would rather die than wait for [the successor] to come. Why, then, was the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye extinguished at the side of a blind donkey?
Linji’s strategic maneuvers were swift; Sansheng, moreover, was in a great hurry. Because of this, the father..."
The Patriarch’s intent was forgotten, which ultimately caused later generations to lose heart. Had he not encountered the flowing water, he surely would have had to pass by other mountains.
Zhongfeng Ben said: "To take another's wealth as one's own and to treat the public highway as private favor—Zhijian’s mind was indeed excessive.
At that time, when Sanxing saw him say, "I cannot speak," [he remarked], "Then extinguish my treasury of the true Dharma eye!"
To simply cover his foul mouth would still leave something to be desired; thus he said, "How would I dare extinguish it? Alas!
To compare the Sage with the Savior is not merely a matter of being excessive—it is quite beyond that.
Baonenglun remarked: "As for the three sages shouting in such a manner—can the treasury of the true Dharma eye be glimpsed or not?
Is it seen through or not? Everyone, try looking up with a tilted brow and see!"
Boshanlai said: "To drive the plow and seize the food, one must be Huo-tuo; to mend the net and spread the wind, one must rely on San-sheng.
Yet, if you wish to transmit and uphold the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, proceed with caution."
Yunyan said: "Linji’s question was solitary and perilous; Sansheng’s answer was transcendent and absolute.
Yet, when scrutinized, this old fellow Linji was simply like a parent who, out of affection for their child, fails to notice their ugliness."
Linji asked Luopu, "Of the two from the past—one who employs the staff and one who employs the shout—which is more intimate?
Lupu said, "Neither is intimate. Linji asked, "What is the point of intimacy? Lupu shouted again. Linji then struck him.
Yangshan Qin said, "Although these two great elders were like the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching, they had not yet mastered the phrase for turning around.
If someone were to ask me, 'What is the phrase for turning around? I would look at my attendant and say, 'Remember this well.'"
When Linji ascended the hall, a monk stepped forward. Linji immediately shouted; the monk also shouted and then bowed.
Linji then struck him. Cuiyan Zhi said: "Linji was coarse-minded; it was fortunate that this monk was there.
If it had been a patch-robed monk of the present day, what would have happened?"
Dongchan Guanzhi said: "Linji does nothing; were he to act, ten thousand apertures would roar in fury.
This monk has seized the whirlwind and ascended ninety thousand li. Alas!
Yunju Zhuang said: "It is like the water jelly that has no eyes; in seeking food, it must rely upon the shrimp.
A monk with clear eyes can discern this without hindrance.
Once, a monk asked Linji, "What is the 'blow-off hair sword'? Linji said, "A disaster! A disaster! The monk bowed.
Ji then struck him.
Baeryam Poojeung said: "This monk’s prostration—was it a good intention or not?
Linji’s strike—was it a 'wind-blown sword' or a 'hair-cutting blade'? If you wish to be a true descendant in this lineage, you must look here."
"One must not be careless.
When Linji saw a monk approaching, he held up his whisk; the monk bowed, and Linji struck him.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "This monk’s reason was difficult to vindicate, yet he died without being mourned. But how do you understand this?"
"Now, how would you provide relief for this monk? Linji gave a small lecture:
"Sometimes I take away the person but not the environment; sometimes I take away the environment but not the person;
sometimes I take away both the person and the environment; and sometimes I take away neither the person nor the environment."
Zhongfeng Ben said: "Sometimes he takes away the person—wrong. Sometimes he takes away the object—wrong. Sometimes he takes away both person and object—wrong.
Sometimes he takes away neither person nor object—wrong. When the Great Master Linji reached this point, he locked up their throats.
Is there anyone who can speak out for him? One must by all means avoid taking a mistake and making it a further mistake."
Linji said, "In my place here, this is the living meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West; at all times, whatever is needed is used immediately.
Then Shilin took up his whisk, shook it, and showed it to the assembly, saying, "In my place here, this too is living. What is needed...
To use it, simply use it. At all times, tell me: is this the same as or different from Linji?
Striking once with the whisk, he then threw it down and said, "Linji still lacks one more move."
Che-xi Chong held up his staff and said, "In my place, everything is used as the occasion demands;
whether it be life or death, there is no deliberation. Nevertheless," he said, drawing a circle with his staff, "Linji and Tianru could not both get out of this."
Linji asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Dingzhou. Linji raised his staff; as the monk hesitated, Linji struck him. The monk did not accept this.
Linji said, "In the future, you will encounter those with clear eyes. Later, the monk went to visit Sansheng.
As soon as he brought up the previous conversation, Sansheng struck him. The monk hesitated; Sansheng struck him again.
Tiantong Hua said: "If Linji and Sansheng had possessed a turning phrase at that time, the descendants of later generations would not have been reduced to mere dust.
He suddenly picked up his staff and said, "There is yet another; where does it go? He struck the ground once with the staff.
Yuan'an Yu said: "The spring flows through the bamboo above; the water lies beneath the bamboo. Flowers bloom on the east side of the ravine;
the west side is red. Guangjiao Yu said: "Everyone everywhere says this monk lacks vigor.
If Linji had raised his staff and directly overturned the meditation seat and left, he would not only have cut off Linji's tongue, but could also have been the equal of Sansheng."
"Zan! Little do you realize that Linji and his father were both seen through by this monk.
Linji said: 'If you can realize the first phrase, you are fit to be a teacher of Buddhas and patriarchs. If you can realize the second phrase, you are fit to be a teacher of gods and men.
If you can realize the third phrase, you will not even be able to save yourself.'"
Tianbao Shu gave a shout and said: "Tell me, which phrase is it? If you call it the first phrase, you cannot save yourself.
If you call it the second phrase, you are ten thousand li from Yezhou. If you call it the third phrase, Dingguang beckons from afar at Jindi, and Zhiyi nods his head in secret at Jiangling."
Shishuang Zun said: "Shishuang also has three phrases. To realize the first phrase: 'A flake of snow flies from a red furnace.
To realize the second phrase: 'A single sword settles the dust. To realize the third phrase: 'I take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha.
Let those with the eye of discernment try to distinguish them."
Linji went up to Huangbo during the midsummer retreat. Seeing Huangbo reading a sutra, Linji said, "I thought you were a person of substance;
it turns out you are just an old monk who eats black beans. He stayed for several days and then took his leave. Huangbo said, "You arrived after the summer retreat had begun."
"Why do you not stay until the end of summer? Nanquan said, "I, Yixuan, have come for a moment to pay my respects to the Master.
Baizhang then struck him and drove him away. After traveling several *li*, Nanquan had doubts about this matter and returned. On the first day after the end of summer, he took his leave of Huangbo.
Huangbo asked, "Where are you going? Nanquan replied, "If it is not Henan, I shall go back to Hebei. Huangbo raised his staff; Nanquan seized it and held him back.
He then gave Baizhang a slap on the face. Baizhang laughed heartily and called to his attendant, saying, "Bring the meditation board and desk of our late master, Baizhang.
Nanquan Jie said, "Attendant, bring some fire. Baizhang replied, "Not so. You simply take it away."
"From now on, he will sit and cut off the tongues of all people under heaven.
Jiaoshan Ti said, "Guest and host are clearly distinct; teacher and disciple are in accord. A light question receives a heavy answer, not falling into ordinary sentiment.
Entrusting him with the meditation board and desk is precisely for the purpose of cutting off the tongues of all people under heaven—this is truly compassion."
The child does not perceive its own ugliness; even if one were to demand that it be burned by fire, it would never seek rebirth elsewhere. Do you understand?
With a grandmother’s urgent heart, I laugh aloud. Let others say what they will of my faults or virtues.
Linji addressed the assembly: "Sometimes my single shout is like the Vajra King’s precious sword;
sometimes my single shout is like a crouching lion; sometimes my single shout is like a probing pole or a blade of grass;
sometimes my single shout does not function as a shout. How do you understand this? A monk hesitated, and Linji immediately shouted.
Tianning Qi gave a shout and said: "Tell me, where does this one shout land?
Is it the precious sword of the Vajra King? Is it the lion crouching on the ground? Is it the probing pole and shadow-grass?
Or is it that this one shout is not used as a single shout? Try to discern it! If you cannot discern it, report [your failure]."
I have bestowed upon you this commentary. The Vajra King’s Sword can be verified before one's very eyes; if you hesitate or deliberate, you will fall into a pit or a chasm.
The Lion Crouching on the Ground is right here and now. Smash the skull and pull out the teeth. Is the probing pole and the shadow-grass good or not?
Sometimes support with the left hand, sometimes push over with the right hand; at times, let out a shout.
It is not used as a shout. Daowei and Linji do nothing but talk in their dreams. To understand it in such a way still leaves one short of a shout.
[Linji] lets out a shout. Kaixian Jin said: "When this monk hesitated, Linji immediately shouted. Was this not the Vajra King’s Precious Sword?"
Is it a crouching lion? Is it a probing pole and a shadowy blade of grass? Or is it a single shout that does not function as a single shout?
If you can distinguish the black from the white here, then weighing the Buddhas and Patriarchs and commanding humans and devas will not be difficult.
If this is not yet so, I, this mountain monk, shall point it out for you further. (He lets out a shout.)
Dongming struck once and said: "Tell me, is this the Vajra King’s Precious Sword?
Is it the Lion Crouching on the Ground? Is it the Probe and Shadow Grass? Or is it the case that a single shout does not function as a single shout?
If you can distinguish the black from the white within this, I grant that you possess the eye of a seeker. If this is not yet so, time passes swiftly."
"The matter of birth and death is urgent; you must grasp it immediately. He then let out another shout.

Once, when Linji was being visited by a Dharma Master, he asked, "What sutras and śāstras do you study? The Master replied, "I am a man of shallow learning, but I have roughly studied the *Śata-dharmaka-śāstra* (Treatise on the Hundred Dharmas).
Linji said, "There is one person who has clearly realized the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, and there is [another]..."

A man asked whether the teachings of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the scriptures could be understood as being the same or different. The Master said, "If they can be understood, they are the same;
if they cannot be understood, they are different. The attendant Luopu said, "What place is this, to speak of 'same' and 'different'?
Jie returned the question to Luopu, saying, "And what about you? Luopu then gave a shout. As Jie was seeing off the presiding teacher back home, he [the Master] remarked on the exchange.
He then asked, "Was it you who just now shouted at the old monk? Lupu replied, "Yes. Linji struck him.
Guangyin Biao remarked, "Luopu may be said to have nearly completed a nine-fathom task, yet failed by one basketful.
At that time, had he waited for the question, "Was it you who shouted at the old monk? and simply replied, "The sword has long since departed," he would have taught Old Linji a lesson.
Han Kuomu waited for him with expectant eyes.
Ping Shan Qian said, "If I were Luopo, when he asked, 'Is this you shouting at the old monk?
I would have snapped my fingers three times. Not only would this have cut off that fellow's throat, but it would also have provided a way out for myself."
*Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School*,
Scroll Twenty *Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School*,
Scroll Twenty-One Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Successor of the Patriarch Baiyan of Ancient Hangzhou.
△ Fourth in the Southern Lineage:
Chan Master Wushi Lingguan of Fuzhou (Successor of Huangbo Yun of the Southern Lineage). While he was pulling noodles, a monk came for an audience.
Lingguan pulled the noodles and showed them to him; the monk then departed. That evening, Lingguan asked his junior attendant, "Where is the newly arrived monk from today? The junior attendant...
Yangshan said, "I would have gone at that very moment. Shishuang said, "It is so, it is so; yet you have only attained a single peg.
Xuedou Xian said, "Old Guan is much like one who loses his money and then suffers for it."
Baoci then questioned him, saying, "Where is it that one peg is missing?
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Old Guandao claimed he had obtained only one peg; this is much like treating the worthy as common."
Dongchan Guanzhi said: "In general, these monks resemble this one; the entrustment at Vulture Peak has indeed been passed on.
Yet why did Old Guanzhi say he 'only obtained a single fragment'? Do you wish to understand? If you do not pay the proper price, how can you distinguish between the true and the false?"
Wushi usually kept his door bolted, and few people ever saw him. One day, Xuefeng came and knocked on the door. Wushi asked, "Who is it? Xuefeng replied, "The phoenix chick.
Wushi asked, "What are you doing here? Xuefeng said, "I have come to devour the old hermit. Wushi immediately opened the door, grabbed him, and said, "Speak!
Speak! Xuefeng hesitated, and Wushi pushed him away and shut the door. After Xuefeng established his own monastery, he addressed the assembly, saying, "I..."
If at that time you had been able to enter Old Guan’s gate, where would you fellows—who are nothing but wine-dregs eaters—have sought it?
Mingzhao Xian, on behalf of Xuefeng, said as soon as he saw the gate open: "To move is to perish. He then further represented Old Guan.
It is said: "How extraordinary! How extraordinary!
An old master remarked: "Xuefeng merely has these words; at that time one could not enter, and even now one cannot enter."
Xuedou Xian said: "What connection does this ingrate have? At that time, he could not enter;
how could it have been intended for him to enter? Now that he has failed to find his way, he brings disgrace upon Xuefeng, who was likewise under the gate of our late master Guan."
Baoshou Fang said, "To see Wushi is easy; to see Xuefeng is difficult.

Gounan Men said, "These three venerable seniors may indeed have ascended to the Hall of Old Contemplation and entered the Chamber of Old Contemplation, yet they still remain outside the gate. Why? Because the story remains."
Baoneng Xiu said: "If I were Xuefeng, as soon as I saw him grab hold [of the monk] and say 'Speak! Speak!
Speak!', I would immediately say, 'Why is this fellow flustered and at a loss? I would ensure that Old Guan could neither advance nor retreat."
Nevertheless, one must also rescue the "Old Contemplation" (Lao Guan).
Zifu Lu asked: "Tell me, when Xuefeng spoke thus, did he enter the gate of Old Contemplation or not?
If he had entered it, why would he have spoken like this? If he had not entered it, how could he have dared to speak like this?"
"What do you say?
Shengfafa said, "Xuefeng lost his money in the eastern sea, yet he goes to the banks of the Jinniu Lake to fish it out;
he deserves thirty blows of the staff."
Baiyan Fu said: "The mechanism of his lightning-flash is as formidable as a towering wall. Wushi is indeed a person worthy of admiration.

It is a pity that he rarely encounters a true master. Had Baiyan been Xuefeng at that time, he would have waited for [Wushi] to open the door, then suddenly let out a shout right over his head, and finally brushed his sleeves and departed.
At such a point, even if Wushi possessed the skill to seize a tiger, what could he do?"
There was no choice but to lower the flag from the high tree. How magnificent is the phoenix!
When a monk asked Wushi, "What is the Dharmakāya Lord Vairocana? Guanyin said, "If I were to tell you, it would be something else entirely.
The monk reported this to Dongshan, who remarked, "A fine koan; it simply lacks a follow-up question."
"Why do you not ask why he did not speak? The monk went forward and asked, "Why did he not speak?
Shishuo said, "If I say I did not speak, it would silence my mouth; if I say I spoke, it would stammer my tongue.
The monk returned and related this to Dongshan, who deeply approved.
Qingshan Xiu said: "Although Dongshan recognized the opportune moment, he was just like someone leading a small child into the marketplace.
Let us set aside for now the fact that this monk merely followed in another's footsteps; as for the old man Wushi, his skillful means were likewise not few."
Baoneng Xiu said: "Observing how the old man answered, it was indeed fine, yet it still lacked vigor.
If it had been me, when asked 'Why do you not speak?', I would have struck him down from his mouth.

Not only would Dongshan have dared not look him straight in the eye, but it would also have caused this monk to cast off all views and hearing, sparing him the need to pass on words and transmit phrases."
Baiyan Fu said: "Do you know that the very lives of these two men are entirely in the hands of this monk?
Those with eyes upon the crown of their heads should try to discern this."
Chan Master Dàsuì Fǎzhēn of Yìzhōu (the successor of Nánshī Chángqìng Ān) asked a monk who was taking his leave, "Where are you going?
The monk replied, "I am going to Mount Éméi to pay homage to Púxián. Dàsuì held up his whisk and said, "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are both right here."
Sengyi drew a circle, tossed it behind him, and then prostrated. Da sui called out, "Attendant, fetch a cup of tea for this monk.
Baofu Zhan said, "If Da sui had not spoken those subsequent words, he would have been laughing at this patch-robed monk."
Yunmen Wenyan said separately: "In the Western Heaven, they cut off heads and severed arms; here, you must go out and experience it for yourself.
Wuzu Huiji said: "Da sui—without going through one matter, one does not grow one wisdom."
Xuedou Xian said: "The sword that kills, the sword that gives life—let those with eyes discern it.
Wuishan Xiu said: "Dasui’s tea is not of the same category as Zhaozhou’s tea. Since it is not of the same category as Zhaozhou’s tea, those who obtain it are few.
This monk has obtained it; tell me, what excellence does he possess? Yet, it is not something unrighteous..."
"Wealth is to me like floating clouds.
Tian Tong Jue said: "He who understands the Dharma has cause for fear; he who deceives his enemy perishes. To select milk from water, one must be a king of geese."
Tiantong Wu said: "This monk was on the verge of completing a mountain nine *ren* high, yet he failed to add even a single basketful of earth.
At that moment, I intended to call for an attendant to give him tea; why did he not simply respond, 'It is not even necessary'?"
A monk asked Dashi: "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder: does this [reality] perish or not? Dashui said, "It perishes.
The monk said, "If that is so, then it follows along with it. Dashui said, "It follows along with it. Another monk asked Longji Xiu:
"When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder: does this [reality] perish or not? Xiu said, "No."
"Is it destroyed? he asked. Wuxiu replied, "Why is it not destroyed?
Longji said, "Wuxiu, 'it is destroyed' obstructs and stifles people; 'it is not destroyed' also obstructs and stifles people."
Daowu Zhen said: "Of these two old masters, one’s Way is ruined and the other’s Way is not ruined. Now tell me, which one has his Way ruined and which one has his Way not ruined?
Do you understand? Whether ruined or not ruined, both are neither internal nor external;
they do not differ by so much as a hair’s breadth. They are constantly face-to-face."
Huanglong Qing said: "Although these two venerable masters were impartial in their responses, those who follow in their shadow and echo their words will immediately give rise to dualistic views.
It is not so with Taiping. Suppose someone were to ask: 'When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder whether this [reality] is destroyed or not?
To such a person, I would say: 'As for whether it is destroyed or not destroyed, let that be for now.'"
Set it aside. Do you still recognize this? Suddenly called back from an autumn night’s dream, one raises the head and sees only the moon suspended in the sky.
Boshan Lai said: "Dasuī and Longji share the same root in life and death; in responding to beings and guiding capacities, they act according to their own household's abundance."
Frugality. One phrase pierces flowers and breaks willows as the ice melts at a wild ferry;
another phrase wears mist and robes in clouds as cold ashes flare into flame. Ultimately, is this thing ruined or not? Examine!
Yangshan’s Peak said: "Although these two great elders employ their spiritual mechanisms with such mastery, they cannot avoid being laughed at by bystanders.
But tell me, what is there to laugh at? Each of them sees only one side."
Daisuizhen quoted a poem by Guanhui that says: "When Zen practitioners meet, they merely snap their fingers;
how many can truly know this mind? He then raised this to ask Guanhui, "What is this mind? Guanhui had no reply.
Gui-zong Rou stepped forward to speak for Xiu, saying: "How many people are there who know?
Bao-shou Fang stepped forward to speak for Xiu and simply snapped his fingers once.
Chan Master Ling-shu Zhi-sheng Ru-min (a successor of Chang-qing An in the fourth generation of the Southern Lineage) was once visited by a nun who delivered a ceramic bowl to him.
Shou then lifted her up and asked, "Where did this one come from? The nun replied, "She came from Dingzhou.
Shou then struck her down and broke her; the nun had no response.
Qingliang Qin remarked, "He does not contradict this.
Baofu Zhan said, "He who deceives his enemy perishes.
Yunmen Cheng spoke on his behalf, saying, "Old and decrepit as he is, he does not even know the provenance of his own almsbowl."
Chan Master Lingyun Zhiqin of Fuzhou (a successor of Changqing An of the Fourth Generation of the South) attained awakening upon seeing peach blossoms.
He then composed a verse, saying: "For thirty years I have sought the swordsman; Time and again the leaves fall and the branches sprout anew.

Since the moment I first beheld the peach blossoms, To this very day, I have had no further doubts. He presented this to Guishan An, who said: "You have realized it through conditions. It will remain forever..."

There was no loss [of his realization]. He then presented this to Xuansha, who said, "How precise! How very precise! I dare guarantee, however, that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate.
Later, when Xuansha asked Dizang Chen, "I have spoken thus; how do you understand it? Chen replied, "Not..."
This was Gui Chen, who immediately went out and killed everyone under heaven.
Cuiyan Zhi said: "Suppose there were a person today who asked, 'What was Xuansha's meaning?
Tell me, has this person yet reached the ultimate?"
Huanglong Xinzheng said: "Everyone, tell me: when Lingyun first saw it, was it peach blossoms or not?
Wuzu Yan said: "What do you mean by 'correct'? Go and practice for another thirty years."
Zhaojue Qin said: "A crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt does not fire its trigger for a mere field mouse.
Since Lingyun has already shifted the celestial pivot, Xuansha has overturned the terrestrial axis. But tell me, where is the point where they have not yet reached ultimate penetration?"
Jingshan Daowu said: "When one family has business, a hundred families are busy.
Zhongfeng Ben said: "Lingyun, under the white sun and blue sky, was possessed by a demon beneath the peach tree."
Although Xuansha may have removed the heterodox, assisted the orthodox, stirred up the turbid, and elevated the clear, he was unaware that he was merely pasting a hexagram upon the Gate of Ghosts.
Tianning Qi said:
"If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate worries. Even if it were refined gold tempered a hundred times," [it would still not suffice].
To avoid entering the furnace for further smelting.
Dongta Ming said: "A single film over the eye causes empty flowers to fall in confusion;
had it not been for Xuansha’s skillful use of the golden probe, one would have nearly become a blind man."
A new cloud rises in the sky. Not only did Lingyun fail to penetrate it; I dare say Xuansha had not penetrated it either.
How do we know this? "The cloud atop the ridge is too idle; the water flowing down the ravine is too busy."
Yuan'an Yu said: "If it were not for Xuansha, Lingyun would have been misled by peach blossoms for his entire life.
Old Master Guishan was merely like a parent who, out of affection for their child, fails to notice their ugliness. Someone asked: "In what way was Lingyun not yet thorough?
He replied: "It is perfectly fine to harbor doubt."
Lingyin Li said: "Xuansha’s speaking in such a manner is very much like reaching for pearls from the jaws of a black dragon or snatching a sparrow from the talons of a hungry eagle.
Although his heart is sincere and his intentions are transparent, how can he avoid wounding his own edge and compromising his skill?
Today I wish to question him: if it is indeed 'utterly correct, most utterly correct,' why does he then say, 'I dare guarantee that the old man...'"
The elder brother has not yet reached the end. Is there anyone who knows his ultimate destination? After a long silence, he said:
"Were it not for the 'thorny plum' and 'Vajra' koan, it would be difficult to see the mind of the silver mountain and iron wall."
Huangbo Qi said: "Lingyun has added eyes to his eyes; Old Bei has planted eyebrows upon his eyebrows.
Look closely: what kind of face does this make?
Xiqia Cheng said: "If you can penetrate the words of the two elders Xuansha and Dizang, you will see Lingyun."
It is not difficult for the clouds; yet if you are unable [to see them], Shouchang will reveal it to you:
"For thirty years I have sought the sword-wielder, yet those with eyes are as if deaf. How many times have fallen leaves sprouted branches again? Why do your eyes deceive you?
Since the first sight of the peach blossoms, one has been lost; until now, there has been no further doubt—only this single [realization].
[The Master] said, "Half. Dongming Jian remarked, "At that time, Lingyun’s eyes were pierced by peach blossoms;
even until now, he remains blind. He then suddenly held up his whisk and said, "Assembly, the peach blossoms are in bloom. Do you see them?"
After a long silence, he said: "The spring colors fill the garden, unable to be confined; a branch of crimson brilliance emerges from over the wall. Yongzheng Yuan remarked:
"Lingyun’s knowing the pivot upon encountering sights is precisely like having grit in one's eyes.

Xuansha’s letting go of the hawk upon seeing the hare results in the growth of branches outside the joints. If you say Lingyun was right, then you do him an injustice; if you say Xuansha was right, then you do him an injustice."
"If you say Xuansha was right, then you bury Lingyun. But tell me, what is it ultimately like? He then gave a shout and said:
"Do not vainly speak of eyes that transcend the quarters; do not boast of a spring beyond the kalpas."
Lingyun asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to Xuefeng. Lingyun said, "I have a message to send to Xuefeng; would you take it? The monk said, "Please give it to me.
Lingyun took off one of his sandals, tossed it before him, and the monk departed. Upon arriving at Xuefeng, the master asked, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "I have come from Lingyun. Xuefeng asked, "How is the Master doing? The monk said, "He has sent a message for you."
Xuefeng said, "It is there. The monk took off one sandal and tossed it before Xuefeng; Xuefeng then desisted.
Guishan Xiu said, "Since Xuefeng could not discern the essential point of the monk's message, and the monk himself only knew how to follow a mold and imitate a pattern, he merely frustrated Lingyun.
Had he suddenly said at that moment, 'I have a letter for you,' [the outcome would have been different]."
He sent him to another monk, who said, "Please, take your seat. Lingyun simply remained sitting. The monk then wondered how he could communicate his meaning;
it was not fitting for a great man acting on behalf of others to fail in conveying the message, leaving the other unable to utter a single word.
Baiyan Fu said: "This monk corresponded with Lingyun; I sent it back in its original seal, not daring to add a single character.
He was indeed a postal official. Yet, how could he have failed to receive Xuefeng’s letter? It is simply that he did not open it to read it.
One can only wonder what kind of mental disposition Xuefeng possessed."
Lingyun was once asked by Changsheng, "What was it like before the primordial chaos had divided? Lingyun said, "The pillar is pregnant. [Changsheng] asked, "What is it like after the division?
Lingyun said, "Like a single fleck of cloud touching the vast clarity. [Changsheng] asked, "I wonder, does that vast clarity itself receive the touch?
Lingyun did not answer. [Changsheng] said, "If so, then sentient beings do not come forth? Lingyun again did not answer. [Changsheng] said, "Directly..."
"When one attains that which is purely clear and free from a single speck of defilement, how is it? Yun said, "It is still the flow of the eternal and constant.
The monk asked, "What is the flow of the eternal and constant? Yun said, "It is like a mirror that is always bright. The monk asked, "Is there anything further beyond this?
Yun said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is this matter that lies beyond? Yun said, "Break the mirror and then I will see you."
Bazhao Che said, "Meeting thus, one simply rests. He added, "Furthermore, why break the mirror? Baizhao Yuan said, "If you do not break the mirror, how can there be a meeting?
Taiyang Yan said, "It has already been broken right now. Furthermore, how do you meet?
He then said, "The illumination is exhausted and the essence has no dependence; throughout the entire body, it is difficult to discern."
Kaifeng said, "Listen well, all you virtuous Chan practitioners. The entire world of the ten directions is a single mirror. How do you explain the principle of breaking it?

Even if you were to personally witness it with your own eyes and accomplish it with your own hands—such that light and object both vanish, like a hen brooding her eggs and the chick pecking from within at the same moment—you would still deserve to receive the staff of Baoci. Why? Because you are merely playing with shadows."
"Smooth as sesame seeds, like millet.
Huanglong Zhong said, "These two venerable masters have clarified the great matter of our own fundamental share; it can truly be called 'cutting and smoothing, carving and polishing.
It is not without reason, yet when examined closely, it is much like a sweatshirt that fits too tightly against the skin."
This is the ability to liberate the very substance [of the mind], causing it to reach a state where understanding arises in accordance with words, yet one still calculates within the undivided time.
To speak of "breaking through" while explaining principles is like asking when, in the year of the donkey, one will attain enlightenment.

According to Master Muguan’s perspective, what need is there to speak of the division or non-division of primordial chaos (*hundun*), or of breaking the mirror or not breaking the mirror? Even if you were to point directly at a pillar—
One realizes it while dwelling in the womb; this is precisely a single cloud dotting the great clarity. O virtuous ones, do you understand?
Wait until empty space falls to the ground, and then I shall tell you.
Zhaojue Qin said: "One is skilled at questioning; one is skilled at answering. Setting aside for a moment the fact that they are like glue and lacquer meeting or water and milk blending, tell me:
when the mirror is shattered, how do you see one another? After a long silence, he clapped his hands and said:
[Case] Complete.
Tiantong Jue said: "Whether divided or undivided, the jade mechanism moves at night; whether pierced or unpierced, the golden shuttle is cast in secret.
It is indeed a single color of pure clarity, yet one has not yet attained the ten-fold stability of sitting securely. Now tell me, what comes after the mirror is broken?"
"In what direction do you meet him? Do you understand? After the old hare of the clear autumn has swallowed the light, it is the time when the azure dragon sheds its bones in the deep waters.

Chan Master Huiji of Yangshan in Yuanzhou (a successor of Baizhang Huaihai of Mount Shuangfeng) was serving as the *zhisui* (steward) at Mount Guiyang. Once, having returned from his manual labor, he...
Guishan asked, "Where have you come from? Yangshan replied, "From the fields. Guishan asked, "How many people are in the fields?

Yangshan stuck his hoe into the ground and stood with his hands folded behind his back. Guishan said, "Today on South Mountain there are many people cutting thatch. Yangshan pulled out his hoe and departed.
Xuansha Shibei said, "If I had seen him, I would have kicked over the spade.
Jingqing Daowu Fuyu, when asked by a monk, "What was the meaning of Yangshan’s gesture of planting the spade? replied, "A dog carrying an imperial edict;
the feudal lords clear the way for it. "Then what was the meaning of Xuansha kicking it over? the monk asked. Jingqing replied, "There is nothing one can do with a leaking boat."
The water scoop was broken. Regarding the meaning of Nanshan’s “mowing the thatch”: Qing said, "Brother Li Jing has long been experienced in the ranks of battle.
Xuedou Xian said, "All quarters claim that the 'Planting the Hoe' story is extraordinary; this is much like following the heterodox and pursuing evil."
According to Xuedou’s insight, when Yangshan was questioned by Guishan, he was so thoroughly bound by his own constraints that he was ten parts closer to death.
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. (Hundred)
People use their daily lives without realizing it; thus, the Way of the gentleman is rare.
Tian Ningqi said: "Fortunately, there was nothing to do, so Old Man Miaoxi recited a mantra for me, which caused heaven to rotate to the left and earth to rotate to the right."

Boshanlai said: "A father’s kindness and a son’s filiality; a husband’s lead and a wife’s compliance—it is only when one is truly a member of the household that one can properly speak of household matters.

Otherwise, it would be like asking for salt while offering a horse. While there is no lack of instances where these two great elders’ hidden mechanisms were perfectly aligned, as for the one from Nanshan who was cutting grass, I do not grant that his words and realization were in accord.
Tiantong Wu said: "If I were Yangshan, when asked 'How many people are in the field?', I would have simply walked out.
This would not only have cut off the old woman's [Miaoxi's] subsequent machinations, but would also have left her unable to find my head or nose."
Yuan’an Yu said: "When the work is done and they return home, father and son sing in response to one another; it is as if the ravines and valleys were filled, leaving no place to emerge.
Xuedou says that when Yangshan was questioned by Guishan, he was so utterly at a loss that he was 'tied up without a rope,' ten parts dead.
Do you know Yangshan? Walking casually along the path beneath the flowers, he startled the oriole in the treetop."
Zifu Guang said: "The 'birds nesting' and the 'wind coming from the hollows' are all such because they have something upon which they rely.
If it were the boundless ocean of meaning where the subtle mechanism is formless, how could it be possible for there to be anything upon which it relies?
At this point, not only do people of today fail to grasp it by groping about; even if Linji and Deshan were here with their staffs and shouts, they would be of no avail."
It is likewise of no use. But tell me, where does the benefit or harm lie? Have you not heard it said, "On South Mountain there are many who harvest thatch"?
Fengshan Qi said: "To uphold the gate and tradition, one must rely entirely on capable descendants; to provide guidance toward the ultimate, one must..."
This was composed for those who are ready to receive the teaching. An old ox possesses the affection of licking its calf; a minor Śākyamuni knows the grace of being nursed by kneeling.
Though fathers and sons are indeed lovable, it is difficult for a bystander to bear witnessing such scenes.
Yangshan was once asked by a monk, "Does the Dharma-body know how to preach the Dharma? Yangshan said, "I cannot preach it;
there is another person who can. The monk asked, "Where is this person who can preach it? Yangshan pushed out his meditation pillow.
When Guishan heard of this, he remarked, "Ji-zi (Yangshan) employs the matters of the sword's edge."
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Guishan was truly like a parent who loves their child so much that they fail to notice their ugliness.

Yangshan’s act of pushing out the pillow was already a lapse; to further apply a name to it and call it 'the matter on the edge of a sword' misleads those who merely mimic the words, leading them to transmit this empty echo as if it were genuine. Although Miaoxi borrows from the water..."
Offering flowers. For now, there must be no partiality or contradiction in principle. Let there not be anyone here who refuses to acknowledge this;
I wish to question you: when you push out the meditation pillow, does that truly constitute the Dharma-body preaching the Dharma?
Tiantong Hua said: "If this were a matter of the blade of a sword, how could Yangshan have ever known how to use it?
Suppose someone were to ask, 'Does the Dharma-body understand how to preach the Dharma? One would likewise say, 'I cannot say;
there is another person who can. Where is that person who can say it? Simply say: 'Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas.'"
Tianning Qi said: "This monk asked about the Dharmakāya preaching the Dharma; he did not even realize he had missed the point.
When Yangshan pushed out his pillow, how could he have ever seen it as something ordinary? Great Miaoshan took what was mistaken and made it right, fashioning it into a matter on the edge of a sword.
He tied it into a bundle and weighed it on a scale; at eight *liang* and half a *jin*, there was no difference in weight between them."
If, at that very moment upon seeing the monk, he had realized that the Dharma-body preaches the Dharma, he would have immediately strode back to his quarters;
would this not have made him an extraordinary master, sparing the patch-robed monks of the world from further disparagement?
Yangshan Qian said: "The Dharma-body preaching the Dharma has already been circulated at the point of the question.

Pushing out the pillow was merely an act of faith, acceptance, and practice. Although the old man of Mt. Gui may say he has categorized the sections and divided the chapters, as for the main text itself, I dare say he does not know its true destination."
Tianbao Shu said: "Miaoyan’s speaking in this way is like a parent who, out of affection for their child, fails to notice their ugliness.
As for the matter of the blade's edge, Yangshan has never even dreamed of it."
Jingshan Xiu said: "Yangshan pushing out the pillow is the trickery of a beggar;
Yaoshan saying 'My son uses the blade's edge' is precisely the lack of clarity in those who are溺愛 (over-indulgent). Dahui said:
'Although Miaoxi borrows water to offer flowers, the principle is not without its own judgment. Right now, is there anyone who does not agree with this?"
If one were to ask him whether pushing out a pillow can truly be considered the Dharma-body preaching the Dharma, it would still be like a donkey choosing a damp spot to urinate.
Tianjing Xin said: "In the end, Guishan and Yangshan were defeated by this monk."
Yangshan asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Mount Lu. Yangshan said, "Have you ever been to the Five Elders Peak? The monk replied, "I have not.
Yangshan said, "Then you, Reverend, have never traveled the mountains."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "These words were all spoken for the sake of compassion; they are talk that descends into the weeds.
Weishan Xiu said, "People nowadays all say that because of compassion there is talk that descends into the weeds;
they only know how to grasp at the moon, unaware of the depth of the water. Had Yunmen been careful with his lips at that time—let us consider what would have happened then."
If people engage in mere intellectualizing, Huanglong Xin says:
"Yunmen and Yangshan had only the heart to accept the jade; they lacked the intent to divide the city.
Little do they realize that this monk has already understood it all at once. Today, Huanglong treats him as a dead horse.
The physician then took up his whisk and passed it to the monk. As the monk reached out to receive it, he struck him.
Guishan Zhe said, "Yangshan may truly be said to have outshone those before him and surpassed those who followed.
Yunmen, though he grasped the essential principles and forged all the patch-robed monks under heaven, could not help but stir waves where there was no wind. Do you all recognize this monk?
"Ma! He came directly from Mount Lu.
Huanglong Zhen said, "Yangsang has already lost his nose; Yunmen further adds a footnote—what salvation is there?
I am not like this. 'Where have you recently departed from? 'Mount Lu. 'Have you ever been to Wulao Peak?'"
"No, I have never been there. He simply said, "I shall provide this person with offerings of fragrant rice cooked in a separate steamer.
Tiantong Jue said: "Although Yunmen recognized the inner depths of Yangshan, how could he know only one side and not the other?
But tell me, what was Yangshan’s intention? His boundless elegance is too weary to be sold."
[The Master] acted playfully, wishing to spare this fine gentleman from being pointed out [as a fool].
Baoneng Xiu said, "If I were Yangshan, I would simply call for the attendant to bring tea. This monk was exhausted from traveling the mountains;
otherwise, I would have shouted him out, forcing him to seek a different livelihood elsewhere."
Baiyan Fu said: "Yangqiao’s ten-thousand-bushel bright pearls and Yunmen’s thorny brambles covering the ground—both are held within this monk’s bosom.
When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, is there anyone who does not feel a sense of dissatisfaction?"
Yangshan was once asked by Dayue, "How do you understand the wondrous, pure, and luminous mind? Yangshan replied, "Mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars.
Dayue said, "You have only grasped the phenomenon. Yangshan asked, "What did the Master just ask?
Dayue replied, "The wondrous, pure, and luminous mind. Yangshan said, "Can it be called a phenomenon? Dayue said, "So it is, so it is."
Qinglong said this: "When the strings and songs harmonize and the rhythms follow one another, one must yield ground to the fathers and sons of Letan and Guishan.
As for the wondrous, pure, and luminous mind, even if it were the Perfect Ancient Buddha or the Lesser Śākyamuni, they would not have dreamed of it even in sixty kalpas across three lifetimes."
Yangshan dreamed that he went to Maitreya’s Inner Court and occupied the seat of the Second Seat. A venerable elder struck the gavel and said, "Today, the Second Seat shall preach the Dharma.
Yangshan rose and struck the gavel, saying, "The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
Listen closely, listen closely! The assembly all dispersed. Upon waking, he related this to Guishan. Guishan said, "My son has already [attained it]."
As he entered the position of a sage, Shanshan immediately prostrated.
Weishan Xiu said, "To interpret the meaning according to the text is not without merit;
however, at that time in Maitreya’s assembly, there was a master who, upon seeing the Mahāyāna Dharma, said as soon as the sound had not even faded: 'Seal these two flaps of skin! It is not so.
I shall merely stop the drowsy prattle of Yangshan and spare future generations from explaining dreams within dreams.
Langya Jue said: "Tell me, did the assembly of sages at that time approve of Yangshan or not? If they approved, they would have betrayed Yangshan;
if they did not approve, Yangshan would have met with a fall on level ground. Today, this mountain monk [will speak further]...
I pity your eyebrows and shall explain this thoroughly for you all: the Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
If you were to present this to those in various quarters, they would understand it in such a way that you would enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow.
Tiantong Ju said: "The jade maiden moves her loom in the dim night; the silken threads emerge one by one from the shuttle’s eye.
The azure waters and blue sky fall into total failure; the cold clarity of snow and moon are lost in a single hue.
O Zen adepts, when total effort has failed and a single hue still confuses you, how can you realize it so as to attain correspondence? He temporarily hangs up his soiled robe and says:"
"This is the Buddha. Yet, when he again donned his precious robes, who else could it have been?
Dongchan Guanzhi said: "When the Venerable One struck the gavel, the assembly of sages dispersed; this does not prevent people from remaining in doubt.
It will only be after they have been splashed with a second ladle of foul water that they finally awaken. It is late! Take, for instance, Mahāyāna."
The Dharma is free from the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations; the Way has already been realized. Do you people still recognize Yangshan?
Ba’en Xiu said: "If Daomian had understood how to turn the light back upon itself to reflect within, even Wansong would have no place to set his feet."
Is there anyone who is perfectly clear in their dreams and wide awake within their intoxication?
Tiantong Wu said: "How great was Yangshan, yet he thrust his head into a vat of glue!

When the Venerable One struck the gavel, saying, 'Now the Second Seat shall preach the Dharma,' Yangshan’s skull was shattered. At that moment, he should have simply brushed his sleeves and departed."
This directly caused the assembly of the sacred community in that monastery to harbor doubts. Yet he struck the gavel once more; he did not cease even when chasing after a clod of earth.
Qinglong said: "Last night, this mountain monk also had a dream. In the dream, the Dragon King of Lake Anavatapta invited the mountain monk for a meal.
When the meal was finished, he asked: 'What is the name of the father of King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja?'"
This question is extraordinary; I dare not treat it lightly. Thereupon, he let out a thunderous shout. The Dragon King prostrated and withdrew.
Suddenly, upon waking, he saw only fine snow covering the ground. "O Great Assembly, tell me:
was the dream of this mountain monk the same as, or different from, that of Yangshan?"
One day, a foreign monk arrived at Yangshan while traveling through the air. Yangshan asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "From India. Yangshan asked, "When did you leave?
He said, "This morning. Yangshan remarked, "Why so late? He replied, "I was traveling among the mountains and enjoying the waters."

Mount Wu said, "Your Reverence is certainly not lacking in the playful mastery of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi-vikrīḍita*), but as for the Buddha-dharma, you must receive it from me, the old monk, before you may possess it.

The Master replied, "I came specifically to this Eastern Land to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, yet instead I have encountered a 'lesser Śākyamuni. He then produced a Sanskrit manuscript on *tāla* leaves and presented it to the Mountain.
Having paid his respects, he mounted into the air and departed.
Donglin Zong said: "Both the Great and Small Yangshans have been doused over the head with two ladles of foul water by this foreign monk.
At that time, there was a true command right here at Jiyun Peak; why was it not put into practice? O Assembly, for now—"
"What is the true command? "Tsk!
Huanglong Xin said, "How could Master Yangshan have been so easily deceived by this monk? He even produced a *pātra* written in Sanskrit and smeared it with paste once more.
Suppose today there were an extraordinary monk who arrived through the air at the gate of Yunyan; [Yangshan] would call out—
[He] came to wash his feet.
Ledan Zhun said, "It is a pity that Yangshan let this fellow off.

At that time, had it been Baofeng, he would have seized him immediately, ordered the *weina* to strike the bell in the Sangha Hall to assemble the community, and after having him formally reprimanded, driven him out. Moreover, as for the Buddha..."
