The Dharma does not accord with human sentiment. Since you are called an Arhat—one whose outflows are exhausted and whose holy life is established—why do you not return home to sit in peace, instead merely wandering through mountains and playing by the waters?
Daguai Tai said: "Yangshan only knew how to advance forward to chase the deer; he did not know that his own body had fallen into a snare.
The Venerable One [Dongshan] happened to form these words, which possess quite the air of a monk. If you can understand this, I grant you permission to pull the tiger’s whiskers."
Baiyan Fu said: "Let us set aside for a moment the matter of Yangshan being buried alive by a strange monk.

As for whether spiritual powers and the Buddha-dharma are one or two: if you say they are two, how do you account for the fact that worldly speech and the activities of livelihood do not contradict the true mark (*dharmatā*)?
And if you say they are one, it is not that there is no distinction between you, O *ācārya*, and them."
"You must return to the old monk. [Yangshan asked,] "And what then? [The monk] could not provide a decisive answer here; do not say it is better to remain in a state of non-action.
Yangshan pointed to the snow lion and said to the assembly, "Is there anyone who can pass through this form?"
Yunmen Wenyan said, "At that moment, I would have pushed him over.
Xuedou Xian said, "Yunmen only knew how to push him over; he did not know how to help him up.
Langya Huijue said, "I now ask you all: how far apart are 'pushing over' and 'helping up'? Thereupon, he picked it up.
Holding up his staff, he said, "It presses past the eyebrows and the nostrils. He laughed heartily and then threw it down.
Jingci Chang said, "To push him over is wrong; to help him up is also wrong. Is there anyone who can pass through this color? Wrong, wrong!"
Nantang Yu said: "Yunmen pushed it over; Xuedou propped it up. Even if you could pass through this appearance, you would still not be a golden-maned lion."

Baoneng Xiu said: "One knocks it over; one props it up. While this may not be considered impossible within other schools and different lineages, regarding the style of the Dongshan (Caodong) school, you must further understand that there is a moment when one is upright and yet overturned, and a moment when one is overturned and yet upright.
Only after [realizing] this timing will overturning and upright standing be simultaneous, such that neither overturning nor standing is established. Then, you may go out and buy some straw sandals."

"I have been traveling as a mendicant for thirty years," said Gunanmen. "These three old fellows, though they have gained wisdom through their experiences, have not yet stepped upon the pivotal bolt of the higher realm.
What is the pivotal bolt of the higher realm? After the sun has risen, it is a scene of total confusion."
Xuedou Zheng said, "This whole crew has been turned by the Snow Lion.
Bayan Fu said, "The old master Lu was indeed skilled at looking for the holes and driving in the wedges, yet it was all merely returning greetings with his mouth.
As for Bayan, is there anyone who can pass through this color? Simply say 'there is. If he were to look with his eyes..."
As his eyes remained fixed, [Dongshan] struck him across the face with a single palm and then asked, "Is there anyone who can pass through this color?
Yangshan asked Minister Lu, "I have heard that you, Minister, attained awakening while studying the sutras—is this true? He replied, "It is true.
While studying the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, I realized that one enters nirvana without severing afflictions, thereby attaining a place of peace and bliss. Yangshan said:
Zhushizi said, "As for this very thing, how does one enter? He replied, "Even the word 'enter' is unnecessary.
Shan said, "The word 'enter' is not for you, Langzhong. Lü then rose and departed.
Qingliang Qin said, "Tell me, for what kind of person is this single word 'enter' intended? He also said, "Langzhong, do not be distressed.
Xuedou Xian, while at Yangshan, spoke differently when the whisk was raised, saying to Lu, "The whisk has come into my hands."
Furthermore, another account following Yangshan’s words says: "I took you for a mere worldly fellow.
Bayan Fu said: "If I were Yangshan, as soon as the Langzhong uttered the word 'is,' I would have shaken my hand and said:
'You are still far from it. Why? Because I wanted this fellow to establish his own livelihood apart from others, so as to avoid..."
"Planting one's feet within a thicket of entanglements.
When Master Yangshan was asked by Pang Gong, "I have long admired Yangshan; why, upon my arrival, do you instead conceal [the truth]?
Yangshan held up his whisk and said, "Is this revealing or concealing? Pang Gong then struck the pillar and said, "Though there is no person here, even the pillar must bear witness."
Ming-shan threw down his whisk and said, "If you go to other places, feel free to present this to them as you see fit.
Yin-jing Cen remarked, "Master Yangshan, great as he was, was completely caught off guard by Master Pang; he was left with his hands flailing and his feet stumbling."
"But as for the Layman striking the pillar once—how about that? "The whale swallows the ocean water until it is gone, revealing the coral branches.
While Yangshan was sitting, a monk came and paid his respects; Yangshan did not look at him. The monk asked, "Does the Master know how to read characters?"
Mount San said, "According to my capacity. The monk then circled him once clockwise and asked, "What character is this? Mount San drew a cross (十) on the ground.
The monk then circled him once counterclockwise and asked, "What character is this? Mount San changed the cross into a swastika (卍).
The monk drew a circle and, with both hands supporting it like an asura upholding the sun and moon, asked, "What character is this?
Dōsan drew a circle enclosing a *svastika* (卍) and made the gesture of Lūzhide. Dōsan said, "So it is, so it is.
Guard and uphold it well."
Baoneng Xiu said: "Yangshan has already provided his ten-character commentary; he has explained it all away.
Why do you still require so much 'congee-breath' (pedantic elaboration) from here on? Had you waited until the beginning when [the student] asked, 'Do you know how to read and write?
why not have simply said, 'I have always been illiterate'? Look again—how else would he have responded?"
Xiaoyan Bao said: "The Great and Small Yangshans failed to distinguish between mud and water. I, this mountain monk, am not like that.
When a monk makes the gesture of Lou Zhide, I would strike him across the back and say: 'You wild fox spirit! Why do you act like this?'"
"It is not that the Way is difficult to see, nor that the false is difficult to extinguish;
it is simply that the true does not flourish. Yangshan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Youzhou. Yangshan said, "I happen to need news from Youzhou.
What is the price of rice there? The monk replied, "I was passing over his market bridge without cause, and I stepped on it and broke it."
Liang Baoning said, "I grant you thirty blows.
Baoshang Baoyun said, "The great and small Yangshan left their heads and trailed their tails; this monk has simply collapsed."
"Eighty *li* from the city of Youzhou, even with his staff in hand, Baozhang was still unwilling to let him pass.
Puning Ying said, "This monk deserves a good beating. Why? If one does not pay the price, how can one know whether it is genuine or counterfeit?"
When Yangshan arrived at Dongsi Temple, he already possessed the "bright pearl" of Guangnan. After their karmic encounter was concluded, he entered the guest quarters;
thereupon, assuming full ceremonial decorum, he went up once more to pay his respects to the Abbot. As soon as the Abbot saw him, he said, "We have already met.
Yangshan asked, "If we meet in this manner, would that not be appropriate? The Abbot then returned to his quarters and closed the door. Yangshan returned and related this to [his teacher].
Guishan. Guishan said, "Jizi, what kind of mental activity is this? Guishan replied, "If it were not so, how could one recognize him?
Baofu Zhan remarked, "Master Yangshan is much like a mosquito on an iron ox."
Chengtianzong said: "Yangshan recognized Dongsi; while it is possible for him to speak of principles with force, he cannot truly meet him face-to-face.
Why? Even if Wushan were to come in person, he still would not be able to meet Dongsi."
Once, when an official came to Yangshan, Yangshan asked him, "What office do you hold? The official replied, "I am a Circuit Investigating Judge (Tuiguan).
Yangshan held up his whisk and said, "Can you investigate this?"
Nanjian asked, "Dangerous!
Baoyan Fu said, "If that official had been a man of quick temper at that time, when [the monk] asked, 'Can you push this one back?
he should have immediately called for the officers to seize him, bind him, and give him thirty blows. Look at this fellow Yangshan!"
"How shall I deal with this?
As Yangshan was walking along carrying his staff, a monk asked, "What is that in the Master's hand?
Yangshan held it behind his back and said, "Do you see it? The monk was speechless.
Tiantong Wu, acting on behalf of the monk, clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "Today I have recognized the Master.
Yangshan asked Shuangfeng, "How is your realization these days? Shuangfeng said, "According to my realization, there is truly not a single dharma that can be grasped by the mind.
Yangshan said, "Your understanding still remains within the realm of objects. Shuangfeng said, "I am simply like this."
"Brother, what do you say? Shanshan replied, "How can you not know that there is not a single dharma that can be grasped by the mind?
Wuwei Shan Zhe said: "The first arrow was still light; the second arrow is deep. Limitless ordinary people are submerged in the mud."
Dongchan Yue said: "To understand the play, there is no need for a double-edged sword; to prolong one's life, why rely on the nine-fold elixir?
Baoshou Fang said: "The 'Double Peak' is but a single worn-out shirt.
Yangshan exhausted all the strength of his arms, yet in the end he could not even pick it up and hand it back. If I were Yangshan, I would wait until [Baoshou] said, "I have seen it."

In reality, there is not a single dharma that can be grasped by the mind. [If you were truly so,] you would have been well-advised to turn and spit in his face, saying, "I took you for a person," and then return to the abbot’s quarters.
This would have given that fellow from Shuangfeng the opportunity to shed another layer of delusion.

Yangshan once returned to Muzhou to pay his respects. Muzhou asked him, "Since you claim to be a good spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), how do you distinguish between those who come from various quarters—those who know and those who do not know, those with a lineage and those without, and those who study the doctrinal teachings (*yixue*) and those who study the profound mysteries (*xuanye*)?"

"Try to explain it for me," [Zhaozhou] said. Deshan replied, "Huiji has a point of realization. Whenever a monk comes, I simply hold up my whisk and ask him, 'Do the teachers of all quarters speak of this or not?
Furthermore, setting this aside for a moment, what is the intention of the old masters of all quarters?
Guishan sighed and praised him, saying, "This is the very fang-tooth and claw of the ancestral school."
Xuedou said: "Tangshan was creating trouble where there was none, out of pity for his three-year-old son.
Yangshan accepted the empty air and echoed the sound, putting on a foolish display and acting improperly; both were inevitably subject to the ridicule of others.

Had there been a man among the assembly at that time who, upon seeing him raise the whisk, had simply stepped forward, snatched it away, let out a great shout, and departed, Tangshan would have been left speechless."
Even if the father and son of Mount [Shishuang] possessed fangs and claws all over their bodies, they would still have to retreat a thousand miles.
Chan Master Xiangyan Zhixian of Nanyang in Dengzhou (a successor of Shishuang Qingzhu of Mt. You in Nan, Hunan) ascended the hall and said:

"If we discuss this matter, it is like a man climbing a tree, with a branch held in his mouth; his feet do not tread upon the branches and his hands do not grasp them. Suddenly, someone appears beneath the tree."
A questioner asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? If he did not answer him, he would contradict what was asked;
yet if he answered him, he would lose his life. At such a moment, how could one possibly succeed?

At that time, the Venerable Huatou Zhaoshang stepped forward from the assembly and said, "I do not ask about when he was on the tree; please tell me, Master, before he had climbed the tree. Yanguan then rebuked him.
He laughed loudly.
Xuedou Xian said, "It is easy to speak while on the tree; it is difficult, however, to speak once under the tree.
This old monk is going up the tree now—bring me a question!"
Cuiyan Zhi said: "Both the questioner and the respondent cannot avoid losing their lives. How would a monk of today handle this?
Jingshan Gao said: "If you can swallow the *liji pong* thorn and pass through the diamond ring, then look at such talk."
This is also the person from Sizhou seeing the Great Sage.
Daomian Guo said: "Because of Xiangyan’s compassion, he spoke these words of descending into the weeds.
Nevertheless, when examined closely, he cannot avoid turning cleverness into clumsiness."
Gushan Gui said: "Xiangyan was much like Xiao He formulating the penal codes.
Tiantong Jue said: "The Venerable Houtou is a wicked thief; using his 'unrighteous hand,' he strikes where one is not prepared for defense.
Even those who are masters of the true school often fail to manage their own maneuvers. Xuedou possesses a distinct faculty.
One ought to recognize the signs of fortune and misfortune. Reaching this point, one can do no more than conceal the body while revealing the shadow.
Do you understand how Xiangyan acted? "Where are the three thousand swordsmen now? Only Zhuang Zhou is permitted to see the Great Peace."
Tianning Qisong said: "The Elder Xiangyan established skillful means in a circuitous manner, yet Head Monk Houtou failed to discern the beginning and end of it.
Were one to discuss the vigorous promotion of this matter, it would take sixty kalpas across three lifetimes."
Tianbao Shu said: "Before climbing the tree or after climbing the tree, an iron snake lies across the ancient road; meeting face-to-face, he laughs heartily.
Bitter gourds are bitter from root to tip. Nantang Yu said:
"Xiangyan exhausted all his spiritual powers, yet it was not enough to withstand one squeeze of Houtou; immediately, he fell into four [directions]."
Lengtadi. Even if Xuedou possessed the vital spark of life, he could not support him.
Yuan’an Yu said, “Assembly, Xiangyan wields the Kunwu blade; all people throughout the world lose their lives and forfeit their existence.
Holding up his whisk, he said, “Today this mountain monk is going to climb a tree. Bring forth a question! From himself—
Daiyun said: "A metal Kunlun beneath a golden incense burner.
Tongxuan Qi said: "Though the tiger's head recognizes good and evil, it sees only one side. Had I been there at that time..."
He simply performed three prostrations before Xiangyan.
Nanjian asked, "Xiangyan has no village ahead and no shop behind; he did not obtain the Head of the Tiger Seat, and he was nearly left with no way out."
Tianbao Zhen said: "Xiangyan was skilled at deploying battle formations; the Tiger-Head [General] did not move his banner or spear.
Each knew their part. But tell me, what was the meaning of that great, loud laughter? It is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life."
Jingci asked, "Xiangyan’s saying here was intended to cut off the life-root of everyone in the world.
Examining it closely, it is truly like Xiao He establishing the laws. Although Hutou was skilled at discerning the appropriate timing, he still fell down on level ground.
He then laughed heartily and said, "The Buddha-dharma is vast indeed; it is simply that my teeth ache."
Baiyan Fu said: "Xiangyan took the great earth as a single red furnace, its blazing flames reaching to the heavens;
even cast iron and solid steel would have been melted away instantly. How brilliant indeed was the Venerable Houtou at that time!
Yet, alas, his eyebrows still carry the scent of smoke to this day. Nevertheless, Xiangyan’s composition may be called truly skillful. Up to this point.
"Indeed. Yet, I wonder whether your own eyebrows are still intact?
Xiangyan was once asked by Yangshan, "I have heard that you recently attained a realization; try to speak of it. Xiangyan recited his verse on striking the bamboo:
"One strike and all knowledge is forgotten; no further cultivation is required. Moving one's countenance, one reveals the ancient path; yet one does not fall into silence."

"However, as for this faculty (*ji*), it leaves no trace anywhere; its deportment lies beyond sound and form. Those who have realized the Way in all directions all say it is the 'highest of the high' faculty.
Shan said, "This is merely what you have memorized from the past. Let us see if you can speak from a state of authentic awakening.

Yan said, "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty; this year’s poverty is only then true poverty. Last year’s poverty still left enough space to stick a锥 (a small awl) into the ground; this year—"
Nian said, "I am so poor that I do not even have a single awl. Dongsan said, "You may be permitted to understand the Buddha’s Zen, but you have not even dreamed of the Patriarch’s Zen.
Nian said, "I have a device: when I blink my eyes at him, if anyone does not understand, I will call for the novice.
Dongsan then said to Guishan, "My junior brother Xian understands the Patriarch’s Zen."
Baon’en then raised the question, saying, "Tell me, are the Buddha-dharma Chan and the Patriarchal Chan distinct or not?
Changqing Ling replied, "They are settled at once."
Guishan Zhe said: "Xiangyan may truly be said to have not a single tile above him and not a place to plant his staff below.
He is bare and naked, clean and unadorned, with nothing to grasp. Had it not been for Yangshan, he would have almost escaped [the Master's] notice. Why?
For unless one endures the power of snow and frost, how can one know the integrity of the pine and cypress?"
Jingshan Daowu said: "In his later years, Guishan was fond of theatrical performances. He had a set of meat puppets made that were truly lovely.
But what is it about them that makes them so lovely? They look at one another face-to-face while their hands and feet move;
who knows that the speech is someone else's?"
Tianning Qi said: "Elder brother and younger brother, last year and this year—what path have we discussed? What Chan have we expounded?
It is all nothing but brandishing a staff to strike at the moon or digging into the earth to seek the sky. There is no 'wondrous' and no 'mysterious' in Chan;
do not mistake the envelope for the letter."
Xiangyan said, "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty; this year’s poverty is only then true poverty.
Last year’s poverty, one still had enough ground to stick in a锥 (chui—a small awl); this year’s poverty, there is not even a 锥."
Baofeng Wen said: "Last year’s wealth was not yet true wealth; this year’s wealth is only now true wealth.
Last year’s wealth consisted of nothing more than a single robe of coarse black cloth; this year, a hundred-seamed *kāṣāya* has been added.
On the first day of the new year, he shook it out and presented it to the assembly of Chan practitioners—truly, one may say his style of conduct is the authentic lineage of our own house."
Tianning Qi said: "Xiangyan’s poverty is not yet true poverty, for how can he still have a whole body?
Zhenjing’s wealth is not true wealth, for his private property cannot help but be fully exposed. Here at Fengshan, we speak neither of wealth nor poverty;
according to the family’s abundance or scarcity, there is no distinction between the distant and the intimate. He raised his whisk and said: "When gathered in, the rabbit's horn is three feet long."
"Chī! Let go! The weight of tortoise hair is nine *jin*. Boshan respectfully said:

"Xiangyan was poor yet sycophantic; Zhenjing was wealthy yet arrogant. Although Tianning was able to adjust his conduct according to the abundance or scarcity of his household, he could not avoid being burdened by the two characters 'poor' and 'wealthy,' which led him to become crafty and deceitful. Now tell me, what do you say of Boshan?"
"What about this point? [The Master] held up a whisk and said: "A clay ox butts a coral branch until it breaks;
a stone woman sews together fire-washed cloth.
When Xiangyan was inaugurating his Dharma hall, Guishan sent a monk with a letter and a staff to him. Upon receiving them, Xiangyan said: "Cang..."
"O Heaven! O Blue Heaven! The monk then asked, "Master, why do you act thus? Yanyue said, "It is simply because winter regulations are being applied during spring.
Tianjing Xin remarked, "To receive an ox from one person and return a horse to another is indeed the natural course of things;
yet when examined closely, it is still a case of dying without receiving the customary condolences."
Fahen Mi said: "The staff of Mount Gui reaches across a thousand li to a common wind; this monk has brought it right before our faces across a thousand li.
Tell me, where does the error lie? A sweet melon is sweet to the very stem; a bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip."
Tianmu Lü said: "Xiangyan’s doing so is like two rows of tears upon a coral pillow—half are for thinking of you, half are for resenting you.
Dongta Xi said: "Miaoxiang sent the staff as a karmic condition for raising a son; Xiangyan then wept, not because he was dividing [the inheritance]."

Setting aside external matters for a moment: as for the saying, "Spring enacting the ordinances of winter," how is this so? To repay one's debt of gratitude, one must be a person capable of repaying it.
Fengxue Xuanjue said with joy, "This monk was sent by Guishan to deliver a staff. The military follows the seal; Xiangyan received it.
Upon finding the opportunity, he wept and followed the talisman as it was carried away. But tell me, what is the meaning of "spring executing the ordinances of winter"?
*Pah!* Tui’an Zhi said: "Whether great or small, Xiangyan could not hold onto it; he was turned around by the staff.
Had that monk not applied a bit of pressure, Daowei would have been nearly brought to humiliation."
*Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School*, Scroll Twenty-One and Scroll Twenty-Two,
compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, a Dharma Heir of Baiyan at Guhang.
△ Fourth in the Southern Lineage:
Chan Master Hongyin of Mount Jing, Hangzhou (a successor of Nan IV, Master Daoyou of Mount Shishuang). A monk asked: "When the breath has suddenly ceased like ash, what then?
Hongyin said: "It is still the effort of worldly people. The monk asked: "What is it like after that effort? Hongyin said: "The farmer tills his field."
Zhong said, "Ultimately, how is it? Wenyin replied, "The grain is ripe, but it does not yet come forth from the threshing floor.
Tiantong Hua said: "Fragrance sinks in the Phoenix Pavilion; the snow-nest is cold at night. A bright moon fills half the window, and a harmonious atmosphere mingles there.
At such a time as this, tell me: do Guizong and Jingshan have any share of meeting one another or not?"
Let us set aside for a moment the questions of seeing and not seeing. Just as it is with this monk acting in such a manner—does he possess the eye of wisdom?
If you have not yet reached this realization, then clouds hide within the seamless robe, and birds nest upon branches that have not yet sprouted.
Baoning Moshan said: "Beating the drum and playing the lute, we meet as two fellow householders. For nine years no one recognized him;
how many times did he cross the shifting sands?
Chuzhou Dingshan Shenyi Chan Master (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan of Mount Shishuang) once asked this while reflecting on his travels during his time of pilgrimage.
"Without falling into numbers, please, Master, speak. Baizhang held up his rosary and said, "Is this falling or not?
Baizhang replied, "The round beads with three holes—everyone knows these exist. Please, Master, complete the previous statement. Baizhang then struck him. Shouwu shook his sleeves and departed.

Baizhang said, "Thirty years from now, he will go about beating his breast and weeping aloud. Later, after Shouwu had established his own monastery, he addressed the assembly, saying, "The old monk [Baizhang]..."
Ten years ago, I was thoroughly deceived by Dingshan; it was no small matter.

Xuedou Xian said: "Dingshan’s application was indeed effective, yet how precarious it was! Pishu knew it well enough, but he simply lacked the eye for discerning the Dharma. Try to distinguish this for me."
Gounan said: "Among the assembly, they deliberate and say that Bishu was deceived by Dingshan.
Little do they realize that it was actually Dingshan who was led astray by Bishu, pulling at his sinews and shaking his very bones.
Can you all discern this? If you cannot, do not wait for thirty years; even now, you must beat your breasts and weep bitterly. Now tell me, what about Gou?"
Furthermore, what kind of eye does Nan possess?

Zen Master Fadan of Yanqing in Xiangzhou (a successor of Shishuang Qingyuan Wenyi and, by extension, of Baizhang Huaihai and Mazu Daoyi) was once asked by a monk: "If an earthworm is cut into two pieces," [what happens?]
As both ends move, in which end does Buddha-nature reside? Qingzhen spreads out his two hands.
Dongshan Shoujian replies, "In which end does that which you are currently asking about reside?"
Xiaoyan Bao offered a different version, saying: "Simply call out, 'Jie-luo! If the monk responds, he then asks, 'Exactly where does it reside?
Is it at this end or that end?
Huiyun Cheng offered another version, saying: "Upon hearing the celebratory sound, he immediately strikes him, saying, 'It is right here!'"
The Monk Master Jingzhao Mi (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan and the Fourth Generation of Mount Yuanshou) asked a monk, “Where have you recently come from?
The monk replied, “Yaoshan. Mi said, “How has the Old Man of Yaoshan been lately? The monk said, “He is very much like a single piece of solid rock.
Mi said, “Is he so serious? The monk said, “There is no place for you to lift him up. Mi said, “Not only Yaoshan; even I, Hu, am just like that. The monk [remained silent].
The monk stepped forward, looked around, and stood there. Baizhang said, "Look, look! Even a stubborn stone moves. The monk then departed.
Xuedou Xian said, "Baizhang the Barbarian’s skill in yielding and seizing is indeed worth observing; yet, alas, he died without being mourned."
Taisu Zhe said: "Mihu is a fine piece of stubborn rock; how many travelers fail to recognize it?
Yet when a patch-robed monk sees it, he cannot help but take south for north."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Xuedou’s subtle points are as fine as rice flour, and his coldness is like ice and frost;
yet, for all that, he only sees the sharpness of the tip of a needle. According to Jiangshan’s own view, this very rice-stirring ladle merely chases after a rat and breaks an oil jar."
Tiantong Hua said: "Is this monk not one who possesses the eye? Yet he cannot bear to take a single piece of Yueshan’s dull stone and peddle it everywhere.
Had it not been for Mihu’s profound discernment of the subtle nuances, he would have nearly fallen into delusion."
Baoguang said: "This monk’s single question and single response possess both guest and host;
is this not evidence that he has indeed seen Yaoshan? It is a pity that Mihu missed a move.
If it had been Upasaka Bai, I would have struck him across the spine as soon as he turned to leave. Why? Because I want to make this stubborn stone emit light."
Baiyan Fu said: "This monk’s deportment in advancing and retreating is worthy of observation; Master Mi’s reception was conducted with propriety.
Host and guest meeting one another leave nothing to be censured by bystanders. Yet, in the end, they were all inevitably burdened by a single block of dull stone. All you Zen adepts!"
"Is there anyone who can pluck this away for him? Let a master of the fundamental school try to produce such a hand!
Mihu sent a monk to ask Yangshan, "Do people nowadays still rely on awakening? Yangshan replied, "Awakening is not non-existent;
however, it inevitably falls into the secondary. Mihu deeply approved of this.
Touzi said, "Qingyun. Yangshan spoke thus; does he thereby avoid falling into a trap himself?
If he avoids it, there is still one person who is utterly unwilling to accept it. If he cannot avoid it, he likewise falls into the secondary category.
Although Mishan may have approved of him, does he himself still possess a way to emerge? Everyone, try to examine this!
Examine this. If you can examine it through and through, the two will dissolve like ice melting into water. Otherwise, do not act rashly.
Letan Qing said: "As for the formal arrangements of the gate, Mihu deeply approved; as for Yangshan’s entry into the profound discourse on principle, he has not yet awakened to the first head."
Tiantong Hua said: "Mihu raised the essential tongs and hammer; Yangshan displayed the business of the sword’s edge.
These two elders are truly worthy of high praise within the gate of proclaiming the teachings. Yet, in the school of the patch-robed monks, they are both men who have eaten blows."
Fulong Chang said: "It is like a mirror reflecting an image. When the image has not yet arrived, what does the mirror reflect? It is like ice melting into water.
Once the water has returned to its source, what more is there for the ice to melt? Regarding Yangshan’s and Mihu’s speaking in this manner—does it still have a point for benefiting others?
If one takes half a catty and weighs it as eight ounces, one remains mistaken in identifying the scale-pan.
Xing gave a shout.
Mihu then asked a monk, "Since ancient times, have the sages of the past attained the ultimate truth or not? Mihu said, "They have.
The monk asked, "If that is so, how do they attain the ultimate truth? Mihu replied, "At that time, Huo Guang sold a counterfeit silver city to the Xiongnu."

"Who wrote this contract? he asked. [The other] replied, "I have reached the point where I can only keep my mouth shut and remain speechless. Baizhang said, "On level ground, you are making someone act as a guarantor.
Zhaojue Qin remarked, "How could Baizhang not be a great *kalyāṇamitra* (spiritual friend)?"
Jingshan Daowu cited this passage from the *Zhizhi Shu*: "What kind of person composed this?
He said, "If Jingshan had been that monk at the time, he would have uttered a turning word to stop this old fellow in his tracks. But tell me, what word would he have uttered?"
After a long silence, he said, "If one were taught that it is easy to attain, one would simply regard it as something trivial.
Xigyan Bao remarked, "Although both Mishu and Foguo were great spiritual friends (mahā-kalyāṇamitra), they nonetheless could not be said to have reached perfection."
Why? To slaughter a chicken, why use an ox’s knife?

When Chan Master Huici of Jiufeng in Fuzhou (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan of Mount Shishuang), hearing that Master Baizhang of Mount Gui was ascending the hall and saying, "All of you have attained the great capacity, but you have not attained the great function," Huici immediately withdrew from his seat and departed. Baizhang called out to Huici, but Huici did not respond further.
Looking back, Guishan said, "This man is fit to be a vessel for the Dharma.
Baofu Zhan said, "It is like a melody that is vaguely recognizable, yet one loses the beginning and forgets the end.
Gaoshan Jizheng asked, "When Jiufeng withdrew his body and went out, was that a great function or not? Guishan said, "It was."
Shandao said, "This child is fit to be a vessel for the Dharma; whether this is a reward or a punishment for him remains to be seen.
The Monk of Mount Huo at Jinzhou (a successor of Nan Tiansheng Weishan Daoyou) had a monk arrive from under the assembly of Yangshan.
The monk proclaimed himself a "Great Zen Buddha of the Four Cane Strips beneath Jiyun Peak. Huo then called for the *vinaya-dhara* (the rector) and ordered him to strike the bell.
The monk then hurried away.
Xuedou Xian said, "Although this fellow was able to change according to the situation, alas, he has a head but no tail.
Zhaojue Qin said, "This fellow carries the 'Winter Melon Seal' of Yangshan upon his shoulders and parades it before others for show."
Had it not been for Huo Shan, he would have been nearly smeared with mud. Even so, it is a pity that the command was only half-executed.
At that time, he should not have called for the *karmadāna*; it would have been better to seize him and give him four more strokes of the rattan.
Let this fellow ponder this for thirty years!
Zhengguo Xingyun said, "These two fellows have both come with thunderous sound but no raindrops.
Master Yuankang (a successor of Master Shou of Mount Baizhang in Nanji) once went to visit Shilou. As soon as Shilou saw him, he drew up his feet and sat down.
Yuankang said, "How complete your dignified demeanor is! Shilou asked, "What did you just see? Yuankang replied, "Nothing in particular."
Led away by another, Baolou said, "It must be like this before it can be called true seeing. Kang said, "How tragic! How many people have been deceived!
Baolou then rose from his seat. Kang said, "You have seen it; yet, though you move, you do not move.
Baolou said, "Even with all one's strength, one cannot escape being settled [in stillness]. Kang clapped his hands three times.
Nanquan Puyuan said, "No one in the world can judge the right and wrong of these two fellows. If you could judge them, you would be a fellow student of theirs.
The Dharma-preacher Fayu of Sanjiaoshan in Qizhou (a successor of Nanquan and Shishuang Qingzhu) was once seized by a military commander during a period of chaos as he entered the mountains.
Holding his blade, he asked, "What treasures does the Master possess? Zhaojue said, "The treasures of a monk are not suitable for you.
The executioner asked, "What kind of treasure? Zhaojue let out a thunderous shout. The executioner did not understand and struck him with his blade.
Longtang Zhu said: "That ringleader is much like a blind Persian; how could he distinguish genuine treasure?
Sanjiao was not good at keeping it well-hidden, and before meeting another who could do so, he opened his fist. Therefore, both are at fault."

What a display of shamelessness! At that time, when he asked, "What kind of treasure is this? you should have replied: "A broken-legged cauldron, a 'pin-word' hearth, a bottomless alms bowl, and a noseless straw sandal.
If you can make use of these, take them as you please. This would have caused him to realize the flavor of our monastic way:
to cast off the heart of a yakṣa and suddenly manifest the face of a bodhisattva—even then, it would not have been enough.
This can be understood. Bayan Fu said: "One presses his hand upon his sword in the night light; another folds his hands while watching his sister-in-law drown. Both are at fault.

Who among those with their mouths still like yellow chicks and who practice the dharma of women would not say this? Yet they do not realize that when one offers a peach, the other returns a plum—each fulfilling their own role.
As for these two individuals in private, they were truly men of transcendent elegance whose influence has not ceased for a thousand years;
how could those of ordinary caliber ever hope to understand them?
While the Layman Wang Jingchu (a former Attendant at Xiangzhou and successor of Nan Tiansheng Weishan You) was attending to his official duties, Mihu arrived. The Master then—
Xuefeng raised his brush and showed it to him. Baizhang said, "Can you still judge the nature of empty space?

The official dropped the brush and entered the rear hall, never to be seen again. Baizhang harbored doubts; the following day, he sent the drum-mountain offering master to enter and probe his intentions.
Baizhang also followed him inside, hiding behind a screen to eavesdrop. When the master took his seat, Baizhang asked, "Yesterday, I did not yet understand the Venerable Monk Baizhang."
When there are profound words and phrases, one does not see each other. The Official said, "A lion bites a man; a hunting dog chases a clod of earth.
Mi suddenly came out laughing loudly and said, "I understand! The Official said, "Understanding is not non-existent; try to speak of it. Mi said, "Please, Attendant, bring it forth.
The Official then held up a single chopstick. Mi said, "This wild fox spirit! The Official said, "This fellow has seen through it."
Taisuī Zhe said: "Although the Attendant was but a layman, he held the power of life and death within his brush.
Master Mian was a man of knowledge in his own region, yet he could not escape the other's depiction. At that time, when [Mian] threw [the rice],"
He took up his brush and said, "I have always harbored doubts about this fellow.
Yingshan Yun said, "Attendant Wang may truly be said to have eyes of iron and pupils of copper;

he not only caused Mi Hu to harbor doubts, but could also cause all the people under heaven to harbor doubts. Nevertheless, at that time, he let him off too easily. He waited until [the other] said...
This fellow is a wild fox spirit. He withdrew his body and entered [the fire] immediately. Why? It was because he wanted to teach him to harbor a doubt that goes all the way through.
Baoshou then said: "Tell me, at that time when the Attendant raised his brush, what should he have done to be deemed appropriate?
This would have spared him from being scrutinized by the other."
Jingchu and Linji went to the Sangha Hall together. Jingchu then asked, "Do the monks in this hall read sutras?
Linji replied, "They do not read sutras. Jingchu asked, "Do they practice Chan? Linji replied, "They do not practice Chan.
Jingchu said, "If they neither practice Chan nor read sutras, what on earth are you making them do? Linji replied, "I am simply making them all become Buddhas and Patriarchs."
The Patriarch departed. [Nanquan] said, "Though gold dust is precious, falling into the eye it becomes a film. Linji said, "I took you for a common man.
Lingyin Yue said, "One move higher than the last; one step wider than the last. Even before those with clear eyes..."
Regarding the *Lùbù* (Manifesto): "The phoenix does not perch upon the wutong tree.
Jingshan Daokai said: "Linji’s majestic bearing was like that of a king; wielding the Vajra King’s precious sword, he roamed freely throughout the land.
Whenever he encountered an ordinary official, [that official] would crumble like falling tiles or melt away like ice."
Tianning Qisong said: "Where has Linji’s 'whisker-cutting sword' gone? If it were brought forth, what would there be [to fear]?
Attendant Wang came out from the cave himself; he had no rival. Where one can afford to yield to another, one should yield."
Puming remarked, "Everyone says that Master Linji lost one of his eyes upon arriving here;
little do they realize that these two fellows met on a narrow path, where both won and both lost."
Nanjian asked, "When these two great elders met, it was as clear as the bright sun and as vast as the great void.
They were what are called 'authentic masters,' and in their mutual probing and pressing, they fully revealed the local scenery of the original ground.
Were it not for such people, how could one recognize such talk? Is there anyone here among this assembly of monks who can recognize it?"
"Mo! Water does not wash water; gold is not traded for gold. One who casts their body across the universe—who is such a person?
Xiqia Cheng said, "Miaoxi wears the talisman behind his elbow and hangs the mirror on the dais; yet when examined closely, he possesses only a single eye.
What he does not realize is that this official was given a shove by Linji, and to this day he has not been able to rise."
It is attained.
Bairyam-bu said: "Since the question was not good, the answer was likewise not excellent. From within ordinary speech, they have densely arrayed spears and banners;
the two elders' application of mind was indeed thorough. However, one must let the wind blow through the six directions and the clouds roll away across the vast sky."
Furthermore, one must undergo a distinct turning of the path before the eye of a monk is truly seen.
Ancient Tang said: "When the old man Linji was casually pressed by an official, his forehead immediately struck the ground.
Tell me, what kind of eye did that official possess?"
Chan Master Huijiao of Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou (the fourth generation south of Zhaozhou Shen’s lineage) arrived at Chongshou Temple to see Fayan.
Fayan asked, “Where have you recently departed from? Huijiao replied, “Zhaozhou. Fayan said, “I have heard that Zhaozhou has the ‘Pine Tree’ koan; is this true? Huijiao said, “No.
Fayan said, “Everyone who comes and goes says that when a monk asked, ‘What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou said:”
"The cypress tree in the courtyard—how can you say it does not exist, Venerable Sir? Jue said, "The former master truly did not say such a thing.
Do not slander the former master, Master."
Jingshan Daokai said: "If you say these words exist, you have missed Jue Tiezui;
if you say these words do not exist, you have missed Fayen; if you avoid both sides, you have missed Zhaozhou.
Even if you do none of these things and find another way through, you will enter hell as fast as a shooting arrow."
Gushan Gui said, "Jue’s 'iron beak' has not been obtained in vain; it is simply that he has never once dreamed of Zhaozhou.
Tianning Qi said, "The meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West and the 'cypress tree in front of the hall'—this story has already spread throughout the world.
Why then did Jue’s iron beak say, 'The Master had no such words'? Among the assembly, many often..."
They deliberate, saying: "Zhaozhou’s was merely a provisional expedient; it must not be taken as a literal truth. That is why he said 'no.
To speak so recklessly is to slander the ancient Buddhas beyond measure. Miaoxi said: "If you say these words exist, you have missed Jue Tiezui;
if you say these words do not exist, you have missed Fayen; if you say they exist and do not exist both..."
Failing to engage, Zhaozhou once again missed the mark. Today, there are no ripples in the smoke-waves to fish for; there is no need for a new crescent moon to serve as a hook.
Xiaran Bao said: "At that time, Fayen lost one of his eyes. Master Jue speaking thus—[is he not also like that?]
Fuyan Yuan said: "Monastics compete with one another in their confusion over the 'Pine Tree' koan; what they prize is surely not the actual meaning, but the handle for discourse.
Even if you were to understand Zhaozhou’s intent, you must still know there is the 'Iron Beak' of Jue."
At the threshold, he planted his staff on the ground and said, "Those who wish to meet Guangxiao today, try and speak!
As soon as a monk stepped forward, the Hermit struck him. The monk overturned the incense table, whereupon the Hermit beat him straight through and expelled him from the monastery.
Venerable Yanyang of Xinxing in Hongzhou (the fourth generation of the Southern Lineage, successor of Zhaozhou Sheng) visited Zhaozhou and asked, "When one brings nothing at all, what then?
Zhaozhou said, "Put it down. Yanyang said, "Since I am bringing nothing at all, what is there to put down?
Zhaozhou said, "If you cannot put it down, carry it away. At these words, Yanyang attained great enlightenment.
Regarding the "Superior Fruit" [section], under the initial question by Yan Yang, he provides the commentary: "Crying out in grievance while clutching the stolen goods.
Under the subsequent statement, he provides the commentary: "Alas! Alas!"
Fragrant clouds [arise from] the furnace. Zhaozhou’s forging iron at the forge cost little charcoal; Yan Yang invited trouble upon himself, unable to shake it off.
Although he attained awakening, it was merely auspicious grass growing in the courtyard—better that such good things never happened at all.

One day, when the monk Shitai (who was a successor in the fourth generation of the Nan lineage, inheriting from Zhuyou) saw an attendant carrying an alms bowl toward the hall, he asked, "Where are you going?
The attendant replied, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. Shitai said, "How could I not know that you are going to the hall for the meal?

What else would you say besides this? The attendant said, "Aside from this, what else could I say? Shitai said, "I am asking you about your fundamental matter. The attendant said, "As for the fundamental..."
[The Master] divided the matter: "So-and-so has indeed gone to the hall for the midday meal. Tui said, "You are not mistaken in being my attendant.
Tiantong Jue said: "To let him go would be unacceptable. Now, I shall straightaway twist his nose until it hurts and beat his bones until they protrude;
only then will he be spared from following the great crowd of blind donkeys. Therefore it is said: on level ground..."
Countless people have died [in this thicket]. To penetrate the thorn forest is to be a true adept. But tell me, has the monk who just now arrived penetrated it or not?
Much emptiness is not as good as little reality.
Qinghuo said, "Entering this gate, you must have a ground that is stable and secure enough to withstand the hammer and tongs;
though forged a hundred times and struck a thousand times, it must remain unchanging from beginning to end. This is what is meant by 'to recognize true gold, one must look within the fire.
When Shitui accepted him, he was like Lu Gong looking in a mirror. Why did he not give him thirty blows at that time to make him..."
"Even if you encounter a hundred flavors of rare delicacies, you must spit them out before you can attain it.
Huiyun Sheng said: "When Grand Duke Tai hooked a carp, the creature took its life and ascended the line. As for 'his heels touching the ground,' that belongs to his attendant;
as for 'his nostrils reaching the heavens,' wait for another time."
When the Venerable Rirong Yuan (a successor of Nanji Zihu Zong) was visited by the Senior Monk Huo, Rirong clapped his hands three times and said, "A fierce tiger stands at the gateway;
who is the one who can face it? Huo replied, "A fine hawk soars toward the heavens; who can catch it? Rirong said, "Both are difficult to withstand.
Huo said, "Let us stop for now; there is no need to settle this public case. Rirong then brandished his staff and returned to his quarters.
Zhang Huo was speechless. Rujing said, "That fellow is dead!
Zhaojue Renqin said, "Their strength is equal and their power is balanced; it is not without merit that they face each other eye-to-eye and hand-to-hand, distinguishing one from the other."
There was no bargain to be had. It would have been a pity to let him off in the end.

Had he waited until he had brandished his staff back to the abbot’s quarters, it would have been well to clap your hands three times and sweep your sleeves away; thus, not only would both beginning and end be complete, but you would also avoid being subjected to others' critical scrutiny.
Daguang Zhiyun said: "In strength there is yet a hand stronger than the strong; throughout the world there has never been a first-rate person.
Do you know this? Devoid of any skill or artifice, Pāpīyas has lost his way. Here, there is no place for you to find understanding; examine yourself."
Chan Master Liao Ran of Mount Moshan (Nanyue Fourth Generation; successor of Gaoyuan Yu) was once visited by Guankui, who asked, "What is Mount Moshan?
The Mountain replied, "It does not reveal its head. "Who is the master of Mount Moshan? The Mountain replied, "Neither male nor female form.
Guankui then shouted, "Why do you not transform yourself away? The Mountain said, "I am neither a spirit nor a ghost; what would I transform? Guankui... [ceased].
Thereupon, he devoted himself to his studies for three years at Yuantou.
Tiantong Jue said: "Beyond the marks of male and female, transcending the dimensions of existence and non-existence, it penetrates before all myriad functions."
Transcending the three realms, it is ultimate yet pervasive; simple yet appropriate. The pines hold the wind, cold through the night;
the stream carries the rain, swelling in spring. Lingyin said:
"Mount Moshan plays with the false to manifest the true; he always finds this opportunity. Guankui responded to the fundamental.

And at the end: having once eaten their fill, they forget a hundred hungers. Even until the phrase "soaking the hemp" is inverted and stripped away—before the point of a flying arrow, who can bite the tip?
Do you wish to know where Mount Moshan lands? When the Great Garuda wishes to spread its sky-reaching wings, who looks back at the surging clouds across the six directions?

When Master Daowu of Guannan in Xiangzhou (the fourth successor of Nanyue) was visited by Zhaozhou, Daowu donned a leopard-skin loincloth and took up a *jiliao* staff, waiting at the triple gate with one foot raised.
As soon as he saw Zhaozhou, he greeted him with a loud cry and stood there. Zhaozhou said, "Be careful in your attendance. Daowu then gave another shout of greeting and departed.
Fengshan began by saying: "The Great and the Small Guannans have, without cause, handed over their defeat to others.
Nevertheless, do you know that Zhaozhou could not escape his circle? Those who call themselves heroes on the Liangshan marshes—look at them;
they are all nothing but scoundrels."

When National Teacher Juti of Jinhua in Wuzhou (who was a successor of Tianlong of the Southern Heaven) first resided at his hermitage, the nun Shiji came by, wearing a bamboo hat and holding a monk’s staff.
She circumambulated the hermitage three times and said, "If you can speak the Way, I shall remove my hat. She asked this three times, and Juti had no response.
The nun then departed. Juti called out, "The sun is already late; please stay for a moment. The nun replied, "If you can speak the Way, I will stay."
He remained there. As for Zhi, he was also without opposition. Once the nun had departed, Zhi felt remorse and wished to abandon his hermitage to travel everywhere seeking instruction.

That night, a mountain deity told him, "Dhyāna Master, you need not leave this place; a Bodhisattva in human form will soon arrive to preach the Dharma for you. More than ten days later, indeed, a Deva and a Nāga arrived at the hermitage.
Zhi went out to welcome them and paid his respects, recounting the previous events in detail. The Nāga raised one finger to indicate the truth to him. Zhi—
At that moment, he attained great enlightenment. From then on, whenever any student came to inquire about the Dharma, Baizhang would simply raise a single finger.
As he was about to pass away, he said to the assembly, "I obtained the 'finger-pointing Chan' of Tianlong; throughout my entire life, I have never exhausted its use."

Xuansha Shibei said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have broken his finger. Baoci then raised this for examination, asking, "Tell me, what was the meaning behind Xuansha saying such a thing?"
Caoshan Changyun said: "Juzhi’s place of realization was crude; he recognized only a single movement and a single state.
It is all the same whether one claps the hands or strikes the palms—it is simply that Xiyuan was extraordinary.
Baoci then raised a question, saying: "Tell me, had Juzhi truly attained enlightenment? If he had, why did Caoshan say his realization was crude?"
If you do not awaken to this, even Koṭi said that the function of Zen cannot be exhausted by a single finger-pointing.
Now tell me, what was Caoshan’s intention?
Yunju Xi asked: "As for Xuansha speaking in such a manner, does he approve of him or not?"
If you agree with him, why say he "broke off his finger"? If you do not agree with him, where does Guizong’s fault lie?
Jingshan Daokai cited Langya’s verse: "Guizong’s single finger—I tell you: a hawk born this morning swoops down..."
He flies through the heavens. Had he not possessed the strength to lift a cauldron and uproot a mountain, that black steed of a thousand *li* would have been difficult to ride.
Thus it is said that National Teacher Jueyi could not obtain Langya to vent his indignation on his behalf; he was nearly lost to obscurity.
Since Miaoxi has raised this matter in such a manner, I cannot help but provide a commentary following in his wake: One finger of National Teacher Jueyi—eating one’s fill of rice.
Just as he was about to rest, he had a hundred thousand strings of cash wrapped around his waist and rode a crane up to Yangzhou.
Tiantong Muan said: "Langya Miaoxi only knows how to cheer from the sidelines; he does not understand how to seize the banner while on horseback.
Do you all wish to know? Is it not clear where the finger-point falls? Listen further to this mountain elder’s recitation."
A single mantra fills all deficiencies; who does not possess this "Zen of a Single Finger"? The subtle turning of the *Lingshu* lies with the devas and dragons;
when the Great Spirit raises his hand, it requires no more than a moment, splitting apart the myriad layers of Mount Hua.
△ Fourth Generation of Qing:

Chan Master Shishuang Qingzhu of Tanzhou (Heir to Daowu Zhi). Once, while a monk was outside the window, he asked, "Why is it that within the span of a few feet, one cannot behold the Master’s countenance?
Shishuang replied, "The entire world has never been hidden. The monk then raised this question with Xuefeng.
"The intent is that it has never been hidden throughout the entire realm; what does this mean? Feng said, "Where is there that is not Shishuang?
The monk returned and reported this to Shishuang. Shishuang said, "Why is this old fellow in such a state of panic? When Feng heard of this, he said, "I, this old monk, am at fault."
Dongshan Jia said, "He makes the local deity laugh to death.
Xuansha Zhibei said, "The old fellow on the mountainhead missed out on Shishuang.
Langya Huijue said, "Although Xuefeng had the heart to benefit others, he lacked the eye to transcend them. Shishi...
Although Shuangqiao possessed eyes that transcended men, he still did not yet know the single aperture pointing toward the Ultimate.
Taizang said, "If people of today wish to clarify this matter, they must be extremely meticulous.
Consider, for instance, where Shuangqiao’s statement falls. If one is not meticulous, it will not only bring disgrace upon Shuangqiao, but..."
Xuefeng’s legacy was thus passed on.
Jingyin Chengyun said: "Do you all wish to recognize Shishuang Xuefeng? Heaven shares its clarity with the white clouds;
water flows together with the bright moon."
Tiantong Jue said: "How far apart are Xuefeng and Shishuang? Truly, they are a thousand miles, ten thousand miles apart.
If someone were to ask Changlu, 'What is the meaning of [the statement] that the entire world has never been hidden? what would you say?
Where is Shishuang?"
Baoneng Xiu said: "This monk searches further and further, yet grows ever more distant; he asks again and again, yet his doubts only increase.

Xuefeng, not sparing his own life, threw himself across to help him—yet this still falls short of Tiantong by one hundred and eight thousand miles. Do you understand? Cast away the path of approval, and the sense-fields are empty;
liberated from all dependence, one is vividly and preeminently alive."
Qinghua said, "Tell me, does this monk see Shishuang or not? If he sees him, what is his appearance?
If he does not see him, how can it be that he is never hidden throughout the entire world?"
Shishuang Zun said: "Of these two great elders, one has his tongue propped against the Brahma Heaven; the other has flowers spread upon brocade.
Tell me, which one is the one with flowers spread upon brocade? Which one is the one with his tongue propped against the Brahma Heaven?
If you can discern this, it is like a long-term traveler returning to his native village. If you cannot discern it, remain outside the gate for now."
Fengshan began by saying: "Shishuang hid his body yet revealed his shadow; Xuefeng drew legs upon a snake.
Although these two elders traveled together, they did not walk in step. What does Tiantong say? Where is Shishuang? 'The tide is calm and both shores are wide;
the wind is steady and a single sail is hoisted.'"
Baiyan Fu said: "These two fellows answering the question in such a manner are very much like those who judge according to legal codes or interpret texts based on their literal meaning.
Under the gate of the Patriarchs, they would have their lips split from laughing.
At that time, when asked why one does not behold the Master’s countenance despite being within arm's reach, why did he not say, 'You have personally seen Shishuang'?"
Shishuang was once visited by Prime Minister Pei. Shishuang took the ceremonial tablet from Pei’s hand and asked, "In the hand of the Son of Heaven it is called a *gui*;
in the hand of an official it is called a *hu*. Now, in the hands of this old monk, tell me, what do you call it?
Pei had no reply. Shishuang then left the tablet with him.
Xuedou Xian said, "To employ cleverness and end up with clumsiness.
Baoning Yong, acting on behalf of the State Councilor, said, "I only fear that the Master will find no use for it.
Bazu Le said, "To assist Shishuang in doing evil is to support the strong and suppress the weak; to act for Lord Pei is to pull out the root."

Thus, they value the laity while slighting the Sangha; it would be better to expel them all at once, so as to avoid repaying injustice with impartiality—doing which would surely incur the world's hatred.
Qinghua Yan said, "If I were the Chancellor, I would simply say, 'How vulgar! Just wait and see, Shis."
"Can this old man of frost still remain?
Yunxi Ting, acting on behalf of the Chancellor, said: "I do not begrudge giving him a name for his sake; I only fear it will bring trouble upon you, Master."
Shishuang was once asked by Yungai Yuan: "I do not ask about the time when all ten thousand doors are closed; how is it when all ten thousand doors are open?
Shishuang said, "What is the matter within the hall? Yungai was speechless. After six months, he replied, "No one can receive him.
Shishuang said, "To speak is indeed to speak too much; you have only spoken eighty percent. Yungai said, "And yet, Master..."
"How is it? Shuang said, "No one recognizes him.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "The initial journey did not reach the destination; the final stage went too far.
Tiantong Jue said, "In the secure and secret field, one must avoid falling into the realm of achievement; the garment that clings to the flesh must be stripped away."
Setting this aside: in the school of our lineage, discerning the pivot that turns beyond the measure of the intellect requires careful scrutiny before it can be attained.

The difference within the same is still clearly tinged with ambiguity; the sameness within the different is truly difficult to reach its ultimate subtlety. Do you know the point where Shi-shuang and his father shifted their positions?
When the candle illuminates the jade person, the dream is first broken; when the night is cold, the Azure Woman has not yet ascended.
Ji. Tianning Qi said: "If someone were to ask, 'When the ten thousand households are all opened up, what then?
I would tell them, 'Be glad you have arrived. You tell me: is this the same as the ancients, or is it different?"
Lingyan Shuyu said: "These two fellows have, for no reason, split open the 'ghost eyes' in broad daylight and planted thorns there, completely disregarding the laughter of onlookers.
Lingyan does not do so. Suppose someone were to ask, 'What about the affairs within the Hall?
I would simply say: 'Only Kauṇḍinya has a slight advantage.'"
Baiyan Fu said: "To be entirely free of dependence, one must see through to the state where not even a thread of silk is left hanging.
To be dignified and unassailable, one must reach the ultimate limit of the present moment. Here, a deviation of even a hair’s breadth will cause the musical scales to fall out of harmony.
Do you know the place of secure intimacy where Shishuang and his father dwelt? Beyond the secular world, how can there be room for calculation or deliberation?"
A monk asked Shishuang, "Does the True Body appear in the world or not? Shishuang said, "It does not appear.
The monk said, "What then of the True Body? Shishuang said, "The mouth of a glass bottle."
Tiantong Jue said: "Pervading the entire body and exhausting all limits; thoroughly bottomless and without merit. Casting off the hand and arising, one finds utility everywhere.
Do you recognize this old fellow Shishuang? In the hall there is no shadow or trace; throughout the world he has never been hidden."
Baoshou newly said: "What a fine lapis lazuli vase! Although it has a mouth, it lacks a bottom. Can it still be used?
A deviation of a hair's breadth results in a loss of a thousand li."
Once, when a monk was taking his leave, Shishuang asked him, "Will you go by boat or by land? The monk replied, "If I meet a boat, I will take the boat; if I meet land, I will take the land.
Shishuang said, "I say that halfway there it will be somewhat difficult. The monk had no reply.

Yunmen Wenyan spoke on his behalf, saying: "Thirty years from now, this story will spread far and wide. He also said: "The single phrase spoken at the moment of departure shall not be forgotten for eternal kalpas.
When a monk asked Shishuang, "From over three thousand li away, I have heard that you, Master Shishuang, possess a 'not looking back'—is this so? Shishuang replied: [He remained silent].
[The Master] said, "Yes. [The Master] said, "As for these myriad phenomena being clearly manifest, do they regard [you] or not? Xuefeng said, "My Way does not startle the multitude.

[The Master] said, "'Not startling the multitude' means being in harmony with the myriad phenomena; what is it to 'not regard' them? Xuefeng said, "Throughout the entire world, there has never been anything hidden."
Xuedou Xian said: "Who is it that does not look back?
Once, when a monk asked Shishuang, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Shishuang gnashed his teeth to indicate it to him, but the monk did not realize it.
Jiufeng Qian was once asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the former master’s clenched teeth? Qian said, "I would rather cut out my tongue than violate the national taboo.
Yungai Yuan was also once asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the former master’s clenched teeth? Yuan said, "I and..."
The former master had a profound grievance against his enemy.
Jianfu Can said: "Do you all wish to know the application of these two elders? 'A son shall conceal for his father;
the rectitude lies therein.'"

Shishuang addressed the assembly: "Beginners who have not yet encountered the Great Matter must first recognize the head; then the tail will follow of its own accord. Shushan Ren then asked, "What is the head?
Shishuang said, "You must simply know that it exists. [Ren asked again,] "What is the tail? Shishuang said, "Exhausting the present moment.
[Ren asked,] "What is it like when there is a head but no tail? Shishuang said, "Even if you could spit out gold, what would you do with it?"
"Wa. What about when there is a tail but no head? Huishuang said, "There is still something to rely upon. "What about when the head and tail are perfectly matched?
Huishuang said, "Even if he does not form such a conceptual understanding, I still do not grant him my approval."
The *Fuxian pin* (Chapter on Merit and Goodness) says: "Since the beginning and the end correspond to one another, why is it that he is not permitted to remain here either?
How many people have reached this point, only to encounter what is like an iron wall?"
Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School, Volume Twenty-Two.
Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School, Volume Twenty-Three.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Successor of the Patriarch at Baiyan in Ancient Hangzhou.
△ Qing Si: Chan Master Zhongxing of Jianyuan in Tanzhou (a successor of Daowu Zhi of Qing Si). While attending upon Daowu, he went to a lay patron’s home to offer condolences.
Huangbo struck the coffin and asked, "Is he alive or dead? I said, "Alive? I will not say. Dead? I will not say. He asked, "Why do you not say?
I said, "I will not say; I will not say. As we were returning along the road, Huangbo said, "Master, you must speak for me today.
If you do not speak, I shall strike you! I said, "Strike as you please; I will speak."

He did not say anything. Yuan struck him and sent him back to the monastery. Later, he attained realization; however, by the time he encountered my departure from this world, he went to Shishuang and brought up this story to request further instruction.
Shishuang said, "Did you not hear it said: 'I do not say he is born, nor do I say he dies'?"
Yuan attained great enlightenment.
Yunju Yuan said, "Shishuang was adding a point to an arrow; even if he had awakened a thousand Jianyu’s, it would have been of no use.
Had he waited until Jianyu had finished speaking and struck him with a heavy blow, not only would he have become a patriarch of the world, but..."
This was to vindicate Daowu’s grievance. Wuzu Yan said:
"Today Baiyun is filled with indignation and cannot remain equanimous; I must resolve this public case.
First, Daowu did not know how to act as master of himself; second, he was unable to adapt to circumstances and enter the secular world. At that time..."
When he asks, "Is it life? Is it death? simply reply, "I will tell you when we return to the courtyard.
If you can grasp this phrase, a clever fellow will take a single step upon it; even the great Master Daowu would thus escape a beating with his fists.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Daowu laid down his body for the sake of beings, pointing directly to the root-source of birth and death.
Jianyuan went personally to the Treasure Mountain, yet he passed it by right before his face.

Had it not been for his adamantine true nature planted deeply in past lives, how could he have suddenly turned his light back toward the level fields and shallow grasses to see where Daowu exerted his effort to assist him?"
Furthermore, how is it that Daowu exerts his effort to assist others? Try to say it. Jingshan Gao said:
"I will not say 'alive,' nor will I say 'dead. Two layers of legal cases, brought together in a single indictment.
A sharp blade drawn from its scabbard cuts through the essential points. Cast off the foul-smelling robe; discard the grease-stained cap."
Sitting grandly upon the dais, his spirit is vast and sweeping.

Baiyan Fu said: "Master Duan fled from his enemy; he was ten parts away from death and not worth engaging in discussion.

Do you all wish to understand the final word? It is permitted only that the old barbarian knows; it is not permitted that the old barbarian understands.

Failing to distinguish the heterodox from the orthodox and unable to discern the path, when the road is far and the night long, cease holding the torch. Let everyone blow it out and walk in the dark.
Gaofeng Miao said: "The karmic conditions of Buddhas and patriarchs and the public cases of antiquity—their confusions and errors do not go beyond this."
This—some say that because Yantou’s wisdom surpassed his teacher, he thus secretly revealed his intention.
Little do they realize that this commits a transgression as grave as the heavens, bringing calamity for ten thousand kalpas. Tell me, where does the benefit or harm lie?
Clapping his hands and laughing loudly, he said: "Attendant, take this clearly to heart; thirty years from now, there will be someone to bear witness."
Yunmen said: "He secretly conveyed his meaning; the door spirit pasted on the wall bowed its head and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
It would put one to shame beyond measure. Indeed, it was not like ordinary things. A difference of a hair's breadth results in a gap as vast as heaven and earth."
Yuan-an Yu said: "One stands atop the highest peak; one walks upon the deepest ocean floor.
One rows a boat upon the mountains; one gallops a horse before the cliffs. It reaches the point where flowers fly amidst brocade and the moon arrives at the Shang-lin Park.
Nevertheless, though it be so, the grain does not flourish in the glare of the sun; instead, they compete to plant peach and plum trees in spring. It turns out to be a reversal.
It causes those who labor in the fields to become flower-sellers by half.
Gu Nanmen said: "After a word has passed through three transcriptions, 'wu' becomes 'ma.
If you can understand this before the bell tolls and the drum sounds, not only will you pierce the nostrils of Deshan and Mingzhao, but you shall also sit..."
It cuts off the tongues of Yantou and Xuedou; otherwise, when the bowl is dashed to the ground, the dishes shatter into seven pieces.
If you wish to understand the final phrase, proceed with caution.

those who suppress the strong and support the weak bury Yantou. This old monk speaks with sincerity: since the Master’s victory was due to his superior endowment, we must restore the legacy of Deshan and his son.
He gave a shout and said: "A fine hand presents a fine hand from within a fine hand; among those who know, who knows beyond the knowing?"
At Kōngtóng, the clouds of compassion gathered; at both the Great and Small Xuefeng, it was like a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail.

At that time, when [the monk] was about to bow his head and return to the abbot's quarters, why did he not place a hand upon his back and say, "This old fellow, having committed a theft, has a guilty conscience"?

"Do you all wish to recognize the final phrase? After a long silence, he said: "The stars sink into the water, a thousand points of light;
the wild geese pass through the sky, several lines of characters.
Baizhang Le remarked: "The father steals the sheep and the son testifies to it. It is straightforward indeed, yet the whole world does not..."
What can be done? A father conceals for his son, and a son conceals for his father; this is indeed admirable. Yet, what can be done about the fact that the whole world is unwilling [to do so]?
Even if one were to see things with perfect clarity, it would be easy to recognize Yantou, but difficult to recognize Deshan.
"Why? he asked, and immediately returned to his quarters and shut the door.
Baoshou Xin remarked: "Although Deshan created trouble where there was none, when examined closely, it was not beyond his station.

unexpectedly, the lame Persian leaped out from the head, once again performing dangerous feats upon the edge of the sword.

Everyone was secretly wagging their tongues; they could not help but expose their own family's flaws."
However, one does not gain a single bit of wisdom without passing through a single matter. Tell me, has he finally realized the ultimate phrase?
"Where Yu’s strength could not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west."
Xuedou said directly: "Mingzhao only knows how to move forward; he does not know how to retreat.

Feng [Xuefeng] squeezed it out with all his might.

Touzi replied, "Give me some money for tea and salt. Zhaozhou then went ahead to the hermitage first; Touzi returned later, carrying an oil jar in his hand.
Zhaozhou said, "I have long heard of Mount Touzi, but now that I have arrived, I see nothing but an oil seller. Touzi said, "You know only the oil seller."
The Old Man said, "Furthermore, you do not even know Touzi. Zhaozhou asked, "What is Touzi? Touzi held up an oil jar and said, "Oil! Oil!
Zhaozhou asked, "When a person who has died a great death comes back to life, what then? Touzi said, "Night travel is not permitted; at first light, one must arrive.
Zhaozhou said, "I was already waiting for the white; you are now waiting for the black."
Nantang Jing said: "Zhaozhou’s workshop is a furnace for smelting and refining the finest gold;
Touzi’s fundamental tongs and hammer cannot help but be put to use along the way. Do you all wish to see where these two elders land?
Ten years of bitter toil, no one asks; in a single day, fame is known throughout the world."
Boshan Lai said: "To stride across the tracks of the sun and cut off the surging currents of the rushing waters—this is either Zhaozhou or Touzi;
it is neither Zhaozhou nor Touzi. Like a skilled chess player who perceives several moves ahead, one must respond spontaneously and with natural composure to the immediate situation.
Do you wish to know where these two elders land? They pierce through the Iron Ring Mountains."
"Go down; I shall come to the crossroads to meet you.

[Chong] was dissatisfied. Master Linji said, "A renunciant should be like this—without a memorial stone. Thereupon, Chong circled the meditation seat once and departed.

Gounan said: "Let us set aside for a moment this monk’s letting things pass;
but what about one who has eyes but no ears, sitting by the fire in the sixth month—can you let such a person pass at Touzi?"
When a monk asked Touzi, "What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there.
The monk asked again, "How far apart are the ordinary person and the sage? Touzi likewise descended from his meditation seat and stood there.

'How much distance is there between the ordinary and the sage? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. What is the ten?"
"Body Controlled. Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. Tell me, is this the same as what was raised previously, or is it different?

they merely cast it aside as worthless rubble. Xuedou is indeed a man of clear vision who points out the strengths and picks out the flaws, yet he goes too far in criticizing the social norms, causing later generations not to see the perfect gem. Do you all wish to see the perfect gem?
After a long silence, he said, "Come tomorrow and present this to the King of Chu for him to see.
When a monk asked Touzi, "What is the one great matter of causal conditions? Touzi replied, "The Minister Yin has invited me to open the hall for the assembly."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Among the ancient Buddhas of the Tiantong lineage, Touzi was renowned for his extraordinary discernment and his mastery of the plain, practical Way.
Observing how he casually handled matters, one sees that Buddhist teachings and worldly affairs were seamlessly integrated.
Nevertheless, although this was so, it is a pity that his perspective was not particularly expansive. Today, if someone asks Tianning what [the answer] is:"
"This is a matter of great significance. He then said to him: "Holding the golden wheel in hand, you purify the four seas;
may Your Holiness reign for tens of millions of years.
Longxiang Xun remarked: "The old man of Touzi can truly be said to have provided a teaching according to the occasion, without missing a single sharp edge. This is the central point.
Feng could not avoid celebrating the feast; a single hair has from the beginning drawn ten thousand *qun*. To shoulder the burden with one’s whole frame reveals the man of the present moment;
with hands and eyes functioning throughout the body, he picks up and handles it once more. When flowers bloom on a withered tree, the great earth is filled with spring.
Xiuyun of Qingshan said: "The two venerable elders proclaimed the cause and condition of the great matter; fundamentally, there is no superiority or inferiority between them.

I would simply say to him: 'In the morning, watch the clouds drift in layers; in the evening, listen to the water flow with a murmur.'"
Tiantong Muan said: "Foguo’s eyes encompassed the Five Heavens and his chest contained the myriad existences.

he would simply have said to them: "The song of yellow birds outside the green mountains; they monopolize the splendor of the season as its masters."
The former Jin-su said: "Although answering in such a way is ten times more straightforward and honest, it nonetheless startles the crowd and agitates the multitude.
The new Jin-su is not like this. How is it that 'this is the matter of great importance'? Simply say to him: [It is] thus."
"Blowing the jade flute horizontally upon the gull-islands, all the wondrous peaks of the 'Nine Nines' nod their heads.
After Shen Dingzhao, Zhaojue Qin, and Tiantong Min had each spoken these two lines, they concluded by saying:

"These three great elders sat side by side to play the drinking game, each displaying their own family style. It can truly be said that with every step it grows higher, and with every wave it becomes broader. Tian—
Elder Tongxin was not like this. When asked, "What is this one great matter of cause and condition? he would simply say to him:
"The clouds part and the sun appears for all to see; when the water arrives, the channel is formed and flows everywhere."
A monk asked Touzi, "Is there anything extraordinary within the entire Great Canon of the Teachings? Touzi said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is this extraordinary thing?
Touzi said, "The manifestation of the entire Great Canon of the Teachings."
Yunyan’s "New Departure" says: "To expound and enter the entire Great Canon. Zhaojue Qin says:
"When the illness is cured, there is no need for donkey-loaded medicine. Jingshan Gao says:
"As for 'expounding' and 'entering,' these two elders were certainly not lacking; yet, as for a truly extraordinary matter, it is three [times more so]."
"Even after sixty kalpas since birth, one has not yet dreamed of him.

The assembly returned and explained it for you.

Caoshan Ji, when a monk asked him, "What is the meaning of 'I am always most earnest about this'? Caoshan said, "You want the head."

After a long silence, he said: "I shall not refuse to tell you: it is also extremely difficult to maintain continuity."

An unenlightened fellow.
Dongshan and his senior teacher Miji were at a bakery. Miji drew a circle on the ground and said to Dongshan, "Take this away. Dongshan said, "Bring it here."
Baoning Nan said, "Not only can these two people not lift it up; even all the people in the entire world cannot lift it up.

A single palm. Within this single palm there is birth and there is death; there is benefit and there is also harm. Dongshan had a verse that said:

"Three people: one who knows, one who does not know, and one who neither knows nor does not know.
