If it is primordial liberation, why must one further inquire whether it is known or not?
Zibo could say: "To forge and temper one's own mind with fierce and subtle intensity requires a Dongshan;
his coughs, his waving of arms, his laughter, and his reproaches are all nothing other than the samādhi of liberation—this belongs to Shending. Nevertheless, he is like a deity."
Shengding was not cast from the furnace and bellows of Dongshan; how could he have attained such ease?
Dongshan did not strike Shengding, yet he perceived a sign upon the ground.

From your morning beatings and evening hammering, I dare guarantee that your greed, anger, and delusion have not been tamed even for a donkey’s lifetime. If you can discern this here, I grant you my approval.
To speak of "Tathāgata Chan" is still ten thousand miles away from the Chan of the Patriarchs.
Dajue Sheng said: "Speaking in such a manner, it is fortunate that you have not passed through the gate of Dajue.
Had you been under Dajue’s gate, I would have broken your donkey’s back and never let you go. Why? Because you already possess the integrity of the King who yielded his throne."
"What need is there to struggle to wash one's ears for purity? Nevertheless, even so, it must be a person of true caliber.
Dongshan was unwell. A monk asked him, "Reverend, you are indisposed; is there anyone who does not suffer from illness? Dongshan said, "There is."
[The monk] asked, "Does one who is not ill still look upon the Master? Shan said, "This old monk has the lot to look upon him.
[The monk] asked, "I do not know how the Master looks upon him. Shan said, "When this old monk looks, he does not see any illness."
Boshanlai said: "The Gate of Non-duality opens; the sun-face and moon-face are both unlike Dongshan’s habitual ailment.
They cannot be mixed, nor can they be classified as uniform. This is skillfully observing the illness within the illness.
This monk has sinews in his eyes and blood beneath his skin; for him to see Dongshan is not difficult."
Dongshan asked Master Mi, "What are you doing? Mi replied, "I am threading a needle. Dongshan said, "How is it to thread a needle? Mi said, "Every stitch is the same.
Dongshan said, "After twenty years of traveling together, this is the kind of talk you produce.
Mi asked, "And what about you, Elder? Dongshan said, "The great earth is ablaze."
Tiantong Jue said: "The great earth erupts in flames; there is no time for hesitation, not even the space of a hair.
In the Kunlun mountains of the South Sea, the weather is so cold one wears no socks. From patriarch to patriarch, it has been transmitted as a single heap of refuse."

Nanlin Hongyun said: "A single piece of ancient brocade from the Divine Mountain—neither wind could enter it nor rain moisten it—was pressed by Dongshan until it fell apart, piece by piece, so that to this day it cannot be mended."
Dongshan and Yunju were crossing a stream. Dongshan asked, "How deep is the water? Yunju said, "It does not get wet. Dongshan said, "A coarse fellow.
Yunju asked, "What would you say, Master? Dongshan said, "It is not dry."
Wuzu Yan said: "When these two elders speak in such a manner, is there still any distinction of superior or inferior?

Neither is involved. Let the green waters and blue mountains be as they are.
Xiyuan Bao said: "When Master Yan speaks in this way, does it have a connection with Dongshan or not?"
Can you discern this? If you can discern it, you will not only have recognized the Fifth Patriarch, but you will also have personally seen Dongshan.

the Fifth Patriarch was able to discourse on fundamental Chan.
Dongshan was once asked by a monk, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? Dongshan replied, "The head is three feet long; the neck is two inches long.
He then had his attendant take this statement and ask Sanxing Ran. Sanxing pinched the attendant's hand.
Dongshan approved of this.
Wenfeng Yuyun said: "To have so wonderfully attained the living path for turning around that belongs to the Zen monks—to this we must credit Old Man Xinfeng.
Although Sansheng was able to communicate through secret signs, he ultimately lost out by one move.

When you step upon the ground, there will naturally be a moment of clear understanding.
Dongshan gave this instruction: "Only one who knows the person above the Buddha has the capacity for discourse.
A monk asked, "What is the person above the Buddha? Dongshan replied, "Not a Buddha."
Baofu Zhuan said in his parting words, "It is not a Buddha.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "It cannot be named; it cannot be described. That is why it is called 'not.

Tiantong Jue said: "How far apart are these two old masters? They are as similar as the characters '刁' (diāo) and '刀' (dāo), yet as distinct as '魚' (yú) and '魯' (lǔ).
Reaching this point, one must employ a mechanism beyond kalpas and release the arrow before the wind.

Distinguishing the soot within the ink.

The Way has not been transmitted by a thousand sages;
the body of the Dragon Flower is raised. Having finished speaking these words of Yunmen, he suddenly picked up his staff and called to the assembly, saying, "This is a staff.

"Son, there is a certain state that cannot be attained. Nevertheless, if you are not a guest of Longmen, you must take care not to suffer a 'dotted forehead' (a failure).
When Dongshan arrived at Nanquan, it happened to be the anniversary of Mazu’s death, and a vegetarian feast was being prepared.

Nanquan said, "Although this boy was born late, he is quite capable of being refined. Dongsan said, "Preceptor, do not suppress the noble to make them base.
Huiyun Cheng remarked, "Nanquan relied on his status to deceive others; Dongsan saw the host because of the guest.

Dongshan ascended the hall. "There is a person among a thousand or ten thousand people who does not turn his back on anyone and does not face anyone.
Tell me, what kind of countenance does this person possess? Yunju stepped forward and said, "I am going to attend the hall."
Regarding "The resources and blessings are vast; what face do you have to stand beneath? he provided the comment: "Seven hollows, eight protrusions.
Regarding "Go to the meditation hall," he provided the comment: "One obtains but a single peg. He further said: "The Hall of Vacant Whiteness opens; the pearl curtain hangs down."
Every aspect is free from self-interest. Who is it that recognizes this? Even if one were to withdraw and seek swift liberation, it would still be difficult to join companions for a common return.

Zimei said, "Regarding Zhouyun, it is not that Yunju lacked the ability to receive echoes from empty space;
yet, if one wishes to recognize this man’s true face, I fear even the Old Man of Xinfeng would fail to catch a glimpse of him. Why is this? Has it not been said:
'Though dwelling in the midst of the bustling city, he has never seen a guest'?"
While Dongshan was walking in the mountains with his senior teacher, Master Mi, they saw a rabbit leap out from the grass. Mi said, "How spirited!
It is very much like a commoner being invested as a high minister. Shan said, "Old man, you are quite advanced in years to speak such words.
Mi asked, "And what about you? Shan replied, "A family of generations of court officials, reduced for a moment to a state of wandering poverty."
Guangrun Rong said: "Of these two old fellows, one still walks the path of the mind; the other still wears his original robe.
If they were to encounter Guangrun, I would give each of them twenty broom handles. Suppose someone were to ask me, 'Venerable Sir, what about you?
I would then plant my staff on the ground and say: 'Do you understand? Only when one dwells in a great kingdom does one know the value of its treasures.'"
"The waters reaching the Xiao and Xiang rivers are as clear as ever. Now tell me, does this mountain monk still have any leaks?
If you can discern this, the mountain monk will himself eat twenty broom handles. If not, there are another twenty more for each of you to take back to the hall."
Dongshan asked the Dharma Master, "That which cannot be known by wisdom and cannot be recognized by consciousness—what kind of statement is this?
The Master replied, "It is a statement praising the Dharmakāya. Dongshan said, "To call it 'the Dharmakāya' is already itself a praise. The Master was speechless.

A monk asked Master Youxi (who was a successor of Qingyuan Wenyi): "What is it like when the Great Function manifests and no rules or patterns are preserved?
Youxi rose from his seat, circled the meditation platform once, and sat back down. As the monk prepared to offer a word in response, Youxi gave him a kick.
The monk returned to his position and stood there. Youxi said, "When you act thus, I do not act thus; when you do not act thus, I do act thus."
The monk prepared to offer another remark, but Xixi gave him another kick, saying, "Thirty years hence, my Way shall flourish greatly.
Tiantong Hua said, "A skilled archer’s arrows do not miss their mark.
If he were truly such a man, where else would there be a 'Secluded Creek' (Youxi)? Nevertheless, how does the first kick differ from the last?"
Tianbao Shu said: "The gate of Youxi stands like a sheer cliff; his family laws are stern and majestic. Were it not for this monk, how could one see the greatness of his meritorious service?
Gutang said: "This old fellow has exhausted the strength of his wrists, yet he still fails to tread upon this monk."
[The Master] said: "He overturns heaven and earth; he shatters Mount Hua and Mount Yue.
Yet, as for this fellow from Youxi—how unfortunate that he has run into a dull-witted monk! He cannot help but labor in vain. If this monk had [the secret] behind his elbow...

There was a talismanic sign. Waiting for the other to circumambulate the meditation seat once and sit down, he then let out a great "he-he" laugh and said, "This old fellow has been caught on a single cast; I shall ensure that Youxi dies at my hands."

Nantuo said, "When I see the Master, he does not even resemble a Buddha. Yangshan asked, "If he does not resemble a Buddha, what does he resemble? Nantuo said, "If..."

Why? Because when one falls into a silken trap on the main road, even a wise person finds it difficult to forget."

Chan Master Jingtong of Mount Huo in Jinzhou (a successor of Nan Wuyangshan Ji) visited Yangshan. Yangshan sat with his eyes closed.
Jingtong then raised his right foot and said, "Thus it is, thus it is. The twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven were thus;
the six patriarchs of this land were thus; the Master was thus; and Jingtong is also thus. Yangshan descended from his meditation seat and struck him.
"Four willow switches. On this basis, he styled himself "The Great Zen Buddha under Mount Jiyun, Master of the Four Willow Switches.

[The Master] appeared above the cauldron of congee; placing a stirring ladle upon it, he struck it and said, "Mañjuśrī is Mañjuśrī;

Chan Master Xinghua Cunjian of Weifeng (the fifth-generation descendant of Linji Huizhao of the Southern Lineage) served as the head of the administrative quarters at Dajue Temple.

One day, Dajue called out to him, "Head of the quarters, I have heard you say that after traveling throughout the south on pilgrimage, you have not yet encountered a single person with whom your staff could connect regarding the Buddha-dharma. On what basis do you speak in such a manner? Cunjian then let out a shout.

Yunju woke up and struck him. Xuanhua shouted again. Yunju struck him again. The next day, as Xuanhua was passing by the Dharma Hall, Yunju summoned the head of the monastery, saying, "I have a direct doubt regarding those two shouts you made yesterday.
Xuanhua shouted again. Yunju struck him again. Xuanhua shouted once more. Yunju struck him again.
Xuanhua said, "Cunjiang learned a 'guest-host' phrase from my elder brother, Master Sansheng, but it has all been lost to me."
"Brother, you have been defeated! I pray that you will grant me the Dharma-gate of peace and happiness.
Jue said, "You blind fellow, coming here to suffer defeat! Strip off your patched robe and I shall give you a thorough beating!
At these words, Huai realized the principle behind Linji’s receiving blows from Huangbo.
Zhongfeng Ben says: "Beneath two tigers, there is no room for a hoof; between two blades, there is no room for a foot.
At the moment when the staff and shouts of Da-jue and Xing-hua were exchanged, how could there have been any room for thought or intellectual interpretation?
Nevertheless, it is just as Da-jue said: 'Strip off your patched robe and give him a thorough beating. Xing...
Hua attained great enlightenment upon hearing these words. But what exactly did he realize? If you can see it here, I will grant you the status of being half a true descendant of Linji.
Nanjian asked: "When the dragon soars and the tiger bounds, even a single step is still lost; when one releases and one captures, it turns instead into dullness."
Set it aside. The three sages and the Great Awakened One each possess a single eye. Had it not been for the old fellow Xinghua, he would have labored in vain without merit.
Setting aside the matter of stripping off his patched robe and giving him a severe beating, tell me:
what was the principle behind Linji eating the staff at Huangbo? Suddenly seizing his staff, he said: "Peace and stability are originally based on the general..."
The army has arrived. It does not permit the General to see the Great Peace.
Bairyam’s Seal says: Throughout his life, Xinghua has pointed to his chest and ribs, cutting off the tongues of all people under heaven.
Having arrived here, why did he not manifest his majestic power and shout once more?
Instead, he said, "I learned the 'Guest and Host' phrase from Sansheng, but I have been completely defeated by my senior brother.
Yet, although Da Jue’s staff was not broken, why did he not carry out the full force of the command? Thus it is also said: "This blind fellow comes here to hide his defeat and retreat."
"I shall give this lower monk a severe beating! Herein lies a certain degree of ambiguity.
If you have not yet reached a mutual accord with the two elders, Xinghua and Dajue, by receiving a blow from them, then tread carefully if you wish to be a descendant of Linji.
Even if you were to examine these two elders with complete clarity, here at Bairyak, it is not yet so.
"I dare grant you the full measure. Why? Have you not heard it said: 'I have not yet scattered pearls within the purple silk curtains for you'?
Xinghua addressed the assembly: "If you are a veteran general, there is no need for 'how' or 'what'; simply bring forth your single-edged sword."
He entered directly. At that time, the Elder Mindé stepped out from the assembly and shouted. Huìzhào also shouted. Mindé shouted again, and Huìzhào shouted once more.

When Mindé returned to the assembly after bowing, Huìzhào said, "If it had been anyone else just now, thirty blows of the staff would not have been too much for him—not even a single blow could have spared him.
Why? Because Mindé understands how to employ a shout so that it does not function merely as a shout."
Shoushan Nian said: "Look at how Xinghua employs [the shout] in this way;
why does he let him pass? You venerable monks, tell me: in what place does one shout not function as a shout?
As for the first shout and the later shout, tell me: which is the guest and which is the host? Nevertheless, you must be careful."
He then descended from his seat. He further said: "Both have faults;
both are without fault. Langya Jue said: "Tell me, which of those two shouts is not used as a shout?
If Xinghua had not had the latter phrase, he would have left the people of the world in doubt. Even so, those who understand are still rare."
Zhaojue Qin said: "When masters of the Way meet, it must be like this: their mechanism is like a flash of lightning, their eyes like shooting stars;
they examine the beginning and trace the end, supporting the head and joining the tail. This is what is meant by 'feathers and plumage being similar' and 'speech and spirit being in accord.'"
As for the two masters exchanging shouts with one another, how can one distinguish which shout is not used as a shout?
Those who wish to be the true descendants of Linji must clearly grasp this. But tell me, what was the intention of these two elders?
"One must advance further atop the hundred-foot pole; within the purple silk curtain, one scatters genuine pearls."
Jiaochongguang said: "Xinghua and Minde each put forth a single hand, intending to reveal the treasury of the true Dharma-eye of Linji.
Little did they know that the entire lineage of Linji would be swept away like dust. Now tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie?
Let those with the eye of discernment distinguish it."
Yunju Zhuang said: "Of these two venerable masters, one buys a hat to fit the head; the other scratches an itch through a boot.
Although this was a temporary expedient, alas, they merely obstructed one another. Why? To see what is right and not act upon it—what courage is there in that?"
Fu Long said: "The battle clouds come surging from the earth; snow-white blades press against his person. To brandish iron banners and strike iron drums is not yet to be considered a master;
only when one can both kill completely and bring others fully to life does one see a true adept.

Compared to those who were boiled while riding the Nine-Dragon Imperial Sedan, or those who committed suicide upon losing their thousand-li black steed, this man is a hundred thousand times superior. [He drew] his sword and halberd.
All are used as farming implements; the horses and oxen are released to roam upon the southern slopes of Mount Hua. How is this known?
When the King ascends the precious throne, the village elders sing songs of joy.
Tongxuan Qi said: "These two fellows are very much like a pair of unperforated iron hammers. Look at them—you!"
They tossed me about, passing me back and forth while alternately suppressing and elevating me. Although both were indeed nimble-handed, Master Min could not avoid losing a single move;
his face was smeared by him, and to this day he has no place to hide his shame.
Baoneng Xiu said: "Tell me, where lies the point of his shout not functioning as a mere shout?
Even if one is bold and discerning, it is easy to see Minde, but difficult to see Xinghua."
Lingyin said: "Shoushan only recognizes that both have faults or both are faultless;
he does not realize that within this realm, Master Xinghua and his son wield the power of killing and giving life—sometimes letting both pass, sometimes letting neither pass.
You worthy ones, tell me: is it Lingyin who is right, or is it Shoushan? After a long silence, he let out a shout and said: "It must not be so!"
"Touching it! Touching it! Thirty blows!
Xiqia Cheng said, "Xinghua and Minde are making a clamor together; that host and guest are clearly distinct is not in doubt."
"A single shout does not function as a single shout; one must further see Linji before it can be attained. Kōtō Jisen said:
"One person holds the scales in hand, free to gather or release; another carries a shadow-reed with him, performing as the occasion demands.
Although their displays are no different, the roles of host and guest are in order. Yet, alas, they act in mutual opposition..."
"Setting it aside. When examined closely, both lose their advantage. Why? One must not yield when practicing benevolence;
only then is one a true man.
*He shouts.* Baozhang said, "Master Xinghua whittles iron upon the point of a needle and drives thunder within a flash of lightning."

Sending the solitary wild geese away into the autumnal sky; sweeping away the lingering clouds over the remaining waters. When one’s function reaches the point of perfected majesty, there must be no further leakage.
Can the body and mind of the Buddha-dharma still find a place here? If you were to shed tears frequently, even the vast ocean would surely dry up.
Guangyinbiao says: "Observe how Master Xinghua and his son exchange roles as host and guest, transmitting the teaching and receiving its legacy.
That both are capable practitioners who uphold the Dharma with bare hands is certainly true;
yet why did Xinghua further say that Minde understands the single shout not as a mere shout? Do you know where this old fellow was acting for others?"

Master Foji said: "Although Xinghua was accustomed to drawing his bow and setting his arrows upon the tip of a needle, and displaying his prowess in discerning the enemy amidst a flash of lightning, when one examines it closely, it is merely the technique of capturing a surrendered general."
Although his profound virtue has long been tested in the ranks of battle and he disregards danger and death, alas, his nostrils have fallen into the hands of Xinghua.

Truly, he is one who walks hand-in-hand with Linji and Deshan. Had he waited no longer than before Xinghua had opened his mouth, he would have overturned the incense table, dragged him down from the seat, and given him a sound beating—take it for granted that Xinghua [would have been left speechless].
"Birth-reception, birth-reception! Is there anyone present right now who is such a person? New Long’an, your life is in your own hands!
Is there anyone? Is there anyone? He lets out a shout and says: "The Golden-Winged Bird King presides over the universe;
among these, who is the one who emerges with his head above?"
Ziguoxiu said: "Throughout his life, Xinghua’s bearing was like that of a king. Why, then, did he completely let go the moment he arrived here? Do you understand this thoroughly?
From the beginning, those who know each other value true resonance; water flows into water, and gold is traded for gold.
This is not like the ordinary blind and sightless fellows who recklessly use random shouts as their lifelong practice. It is so, yet it is so."
As for Zhijiao’s saying, "The single school of Linji has been swept away to its very foundations," how would you explain this? He shouted.
Many say, "When the sea dries up, its bottom will finally be seen; who knows that as a person grows old, they do not come to know their own mind?"
Xinghua was attending Linji when Luopo came to visit him. Linji asked, "Where have you come from? Luopo replied, "From Luancheng. Linji said, "May I ask you something?
Luopo said, "A newly ordained monk does not know. Linji said, "Even if one were to raze the Great Tang Empire, would there be anyone left who does not know?
He then told him, "Go to the meditation hall. Xinghua followed after him and asked, "Just now..."
A newly arrived monk entered. [The Master] asked, "Is this to strip him of his status or not to strip him? Nanquan said, "I don't care whether you strip him or not.
Huangbo said, "The Master only knows how to pounce on a dead sparrow on the ground;
you do not know how to cover it over with a turning phrase. Nanquan said, "And what about you? Huangbo said, "Please let the Master act as the newly arrived one. Nanquan then said:
The newly ordained monk did not know how to respond. Yunhua said, "This is actually the fault of this old monk. Linji said, "Your words conceal the sharp edge [of the sword].

As Yunhua hesitated, Linji struck him. That evening, Linji spoke again: "Today when I questioned the newly arrived one, it was like striking a dying sparrow on the ground or hitting it right in its nest.
But as soon as you produced a word, I shouted and sent you soaring toward the blue clouds."
Linji struck him from behind. Huizhao said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. Linji then struck him again.
Guangjiao Yuyun said, "If one discusses this matter, it is like sparks struck from flint or a flash of lightning;

whether you grasp it or fail to grasp it, both inevitably result in the loss of body and life. Observe how Linji held the scales of judgment in his hand, bestowing or seizing according to the occasion."
Although Xinghua said he exerted himself to the utmost for the sake of the assembly, it cannot be denied that disaster arose from his own household.

If everyone were like today’s state of affairs, where the lineage of the school has fallen to the ground, what spirit would there be in you lot, who look ahead and glance back? He lets out a shout and says:
"When dragons and elephants trample, who can endure it? The 'Snowy Melody' is rarely heard; those who listen in vain will only hear their own breath."
When Xinghua saw a fellow practitioner-monk arrive, as soon as the monk stepped onto the Dharma Hall, Xinghua shouted. The monk also shouted. Xinghua shouted again; the monk shouted yet again.
Xinghua stepped forward and raised his staff. The monk shouted once more. Xinghua said, "Look at this blind fellow! He still thinks he is the master.
As the monk hesitated, Xinghua struck him down directly from the Dharma Hall. A attendant asked, "Regarding that monk who just now—"
"This deeply offends the Master. Huizhao said, "That fellow just now possessed both the provisional and the real, both illumination and function.
Yet when I crossed my hands before him, he could not proceed. When one encounters such a blind fellow, if I do not strike him, when shall I ever do so?"

Zhaojue Qin said: "Discerning the sword in the royal treasury and shaking the poison-drum of the wilderness—lightning cannot be used to match its swiftness, nor can a thunderclap be compared to its majesty.
It may be called skillfully driving the ox of the plowman and being able to snatch the food from the hungry man.
As for the mutual exchange of host and guest, there is illumination and function, and there is the provisional and the real."
Set this aside for a moment. Where is it that Xinghua held his hand out two inches in front of him?
If you can penetrate this clearly here, you may carry forth the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of Linji. Should you fail to distinguish between the mud and the water, however, [you will not].
"Unable to avoid being a blind donkey following the great crowd.
Tiantong Hua said: "Xinghua’s gates and walls are eight thousand feet high; his ancestral house laws have always been stern.
This monk has secretly penetrated the heavy barriers, yet he wishes to see the spring colors within the cave. It is fine, but it cannot be avoided that both parties lose ground. Only...
As Xinghua said: "I will hold my hand out before him and cross it twice. Furthermore, what then?
"Heaven has not yet been established; hell has already been formed."
Yuwang Guangyun said: "The Patriarchal Seal is held high, shining alone throughout the world. He opens wide the great furnace to smelt both the ordinary and the holy.
Were it not for Xinghua, one could not verify a fellow practitioner; were it not for a fellow practitioner, one could not see Xinghua.
Only when master and guest are exchanged and illumination and function proceed together can this be realized. But tell me, where did Xinghua point his hand toward him?"
If you can understand it right here where these two horizontal lines lie before you, the Linji school will not be reduced to mere dust.
If, however, you have not yet attained this, I, Yuyang, shall break it open for you. [He raises his staff and strikes once. "The golden arrowhead, well-tuned, has seen a hundred battles;
the iron whip is full of strength, yet it grieves that there is no enemy."
Nantang Yu said: "A-he-he! A lion cub turns back to leap; a dragon-horse colt bounds and gallops. Having broken through the ultimate barrier, both host and guest lose their reflection.
Some might say that at that moment one should have let out another shout, or else overturned the meditation seat and departed with one's sleeves brushed.
What common ground for conversation is there for such a view? Mount [Shan]."

The monk would never open his fist unless he encountered someone special. Now that the Great Way Master Brother has arrived from afar, I wish to enable the assembly here and now to see through him as they did with the ancients. Do you understand this thoroughly?
The green mountains do not lock in the soaring momentum; the vast blue sea surely knows its place of origin.
Lingyin Li said: "Xinghua held the true mandate over the realm and displayed the divine talisman from behind his elbow;
he could have had all the people of the entire world receive a blow of the staff at once. Yet, because his command was so severe, it could not avoid wounding the blade and injuring the hand."
Do you wish to know where the monk has met with defeat? If one fails to sever [the problem] when it ought to be severed, one instead invites chaos.
Even if one were to disregard life and death, overturn the meditation seat, and shout to disperse the assembly, such a person is still merely a headless, board-carrying laborer.

Baiyan Fu said: "If this monk were a man who could recognize good and ill fortune and discern the appropriate timing, when Xinghua stepped forward to raise his staff, he should have retreated three paces and said, 'Stop, stop!
If it were anyone else today, they would surely resent the Master. Had the monk’s eyes flickered or wavered, he should have given him a shout and swept him away."
He stepped out from his sleeve. Not only was the bond of mutual practice shared with those of the past revealed, but Linji’s True Dharma Eye Treasury was held within his grasp.
Once, when a monk asked Xinghua, "What is it like when [the opponent] comes from the four directions and eight points? Xinghua said, "Strike the one in the middle. The monk...
He then paid his respects. The transformation-body said, "Yesterday I went to a village feast.
On the way, I encountered a sudden storm of wind and rain, so I took shelter inside an ancient temple and managed to get through it."
Fuyan Rong said: "Although this monk understands how to enter directly with a single blade, he cannot help but encounter Xinghua’s hundred layers and thousand folds.

Thus, it is a matter of strategy rather than mere valor. Though Xinghua may deploy his stratagems from within his tent to secure victory a thousand miles away, he cannot avoid being laughed at by the onlookers.
If you were to ask me, Master, what to do when [the opponent] comes from the four directions and eight points..."
"How is this? [Xuefeng] said, "He is not yet a master. Had he attempted to deliberate, I would have struck him across the spine with my staff.
Xiqia Cheng said, "This monk’s prostration was not out of good intent.
Had it not been for Xinghua having the 'eye' at the crown of his head, he nearly had his skull split open by him."
Ziguoxiu said: "This monk possesses the talent of one who can capture a king and shoot down his horse, yet he fails at the end, like a dragon’s head with a snake’s tail.
Xinghua possesses the skill to break through walls and change the banner, yet he still lacks that final blow.
Had he seen him prostrate at that moment, he would have struck him across the spine. Why? For if one does not enter the tiger's den, how can one obtain the tiger’s cub? Although...
However, as for Xinghua’s final statement being spoken in such a manner—how should one understand it? Panlong Chang said:
"To help others, one must help them to the ultimate; to kill, one must see blood. Yet even Xinghua’s approach was still lacking in stability.
Had he been able to act at that moment, before the drums and banners had even stirred and before his strength had waned, he would have been able to bring [the other] back to life.

He has captured the living and seized it. Not only does he wash the entrails and change the bones of this monk, but he also spares him from following the scent of the savory toward places of sudden wind and torrential rain, where one would have to stumble and retreat.
When Emperor Zhuangzong of the Later Tang returned from his imperial tour of Hebei and arrived at the Uei-fu (Weifu) palace, he issued an edict asking:
"I have recovered a treasure from Central China, yet no one has ever offered a price for it. Xinghua said, "I beg Your Majesty to let me see this treasure.
The Emperor extended the two legs of his *fuhoutou* (official headgear). Xinghua said, "Who would dare to offer a price for the treasure of a sovereign?"
Baoci then raised the point, saying: "Tell me, did Xinghua accept Zhuangzong or not?
If he accepted Zhuangzong, where was Xinghua’s eye? If he did not accept Zhuangzong, where did the fault lie?"
Xuedou Xian said: "That which the Most Honored One has attained can only be viewed from the side. Were it not for Xinghua being a master of the Way, people would often pay a high price for it.
Yunfeng Yue said: "The true does not conceal the false; the crooked does not hide the straight. Let those with eyes discern it!"
Cuiyan Zhi said, "At that time, Xinghua made one move that could be called 'drunk with realization.
How would you judge it today?
Huanglong Xin said, "Xinghua acted according to the occasion; alas, he buried his own brilliance for a day."
"Son of Heaven, at that time, if one had merely directed them toward the Way, the pearls of the oysters and clams would have been collected and left with no use;
thus, he taught them to have a separate livelihood for the future, so as to avoid mutual neglect. Now, if someone were to ask:"
Furthermore, how does one repay this?
Xiyuan Bao said: "A true master-king can indeed act it out and speak it into practice.

Master Xinghua, a teacher of clear eyes, was also well able to distinguish and repay according to the occasion. However, for the time being, I am somewhat obscured; at that moment, it may not necessarily have been so."
This shall illuminate future generations. If I were to promote transformation, I would wait for the Emperor to lift the hem of his *fuhou* headwear and say directly:

"Your Majesty, how can you preach the true method while selling counterfeit medicine? With a mere glance, I would cause him to realize that all views are exhausted and all attachments to treasures forgotten.
Not only would this lead the Sovereign to attain great liberation, but it would also spare the people of the world from merely receiving echoes of empty sounds. Only...
He makes his living at the Gate of Light and Shadow.

Boshan Lai said: "A jade disc of one inch in diameter and a pearl that illuminates a carriage—when looking toward the Central Plains, one cannot hope to catch even a fraction of their light and shadow.
This is because they are obscured by the jeweled crown of Mañjuśrī; it is not that the Vimalakīrti’s chamber has failed to reveal them."
"Come! Xinghua ultimately cannot be paid for his price. Although it is thus, who says that gold is like excrement and soil?
Tiantong Muan said: "Xuedou and Xinghua were not without their oversights; Huanglong Huichang was..."

This would be a fatal blow to the transformation of the wind. If I were this mountain monk, I would wait for him to pull up the hem of his official head-covering and simply say, "The August Heaven has no favorites;

it assists only virtue. This would not only cause Emperor Zhuang to tread upon security while remaining aware of danger, but it would also manifest that within the sleeves of a patch-robed monk lies a golden mallet.
(He draws a stroke with the whisk and says: Tell me, what is this treasure?
He paid the price for its birth. After a long silence, he said, "Pity this three-foot-long dragon’s whisk; it is called nothing more than an ordinary tattered cloth.
Baozhang said, "Zhuangzong was the Son of Heaven for a single reign, yet he carelessly cast the treasures of Central China before others.
Xinghua is a patriarch of the world, yet he could not even dare to encounter the dragon's scales or seize its horns. At that time, he waited for...
He simply extended the feet of his head-wrap and said, "There is no need to bring out the fish-eye pearl.

Even if one were to display it with ten times the skill of Emperor Tongguang, it would still fall short by three thousand li. Why? Because when one casually casts a single line anywhere, one must inevitably stir the dragon of the azure depths.
Baiyan Fu said: "Everyone says that Xinghua had only the breast to stroke a tiger's whiskers in compliance, yet lacked the sharp hand to claw at a dragon's scales in defiance.
Little do they realize that Xinghua’s tongue was like a dragon-sword and a stone chisel;
it possessed great power for both benefit and harm. If anyone can fully comprehend this, please provide a separate verse for Emperor Tongguang."
A turning phrase.
When Xinghua arrived at Yunju, he asked, "If one were to borrow a question as a mere pretext, what would it be like? Yunju had no reply.
Xinghua said, "I suspect you, Master, cannot answer this question; it would be better to bow and withdraw. Later, Yunju went out to reside [elsewhere].
He said: "Twenty years ago, I did not utter a single word to Xinghua; it was for his sake that I posed such a strange question.
Now, reflecting on it, at that time I need not have said, 'What need is there? When Xinghua heard this, he remarked:
'The old man of Yunju spent twenty years saying nothing more than "What need is there? If it were Xinghua, it would not be so. How could it compare to what I have said?'"
"There is no need for 'it must' or 'it need not.

Jingshan Daowei said: 'Why must it be so? Why need it not be so? Continuous and dense, face-to-face at the opportune moment—if anyone can provide the final word, I grant that they have personally seen these two venerable masters."
Tiantong Muan said: "Yunju was acting like a fool; Xinghua was a mere dependent.
Although they thus provoked and stimulated one another, how could it be that they only succeeded in being the 'host within the guest'? They failed to be the 'host within the host.
If it were Tiantong, should a monk ask such a question today, he would simply say, 'Excellent! As soon as the other attempts to deliberate, he would strike him across the back with his staff."

This leaves all other divergent Chan practitioners with no opening through which to speak; it further reveals the master’s hand and eye, in which the three mysteries and the weapons of armor are simultaneously manifest in both illumination and function.
Xinghua addressed the assembly: "I hear that they shout in the front corridor and they also shout in the rear quarters.

My sons, do not shout blindly or shout recklessly. Even if you were to shout Xinghua down from the midst of the sky until he fell flat with not a breath left, wait until I have slowly recovered and then I will tell you it is still not so. Why? Because I—"
"I have never scattered pearls inside a purple silk curtain for you people to pick up. Why this reckless shouting and disorderly clamor?
Tianning Qi said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have simply told him: 'Why bother? Wait for this old fellow.'"
Looking east and west, he then let out a shout. To startle the multitude, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to overcome the adversary, one must be a lion’s cub.
Xinghua said: "If you establish even a single speck of dust, the state will flourish while the village elders frown; if you do not establish even a single speck of dust, the state..."
"When the nation perishes, the village elders rest in peace.
Xuedou Xian cited this, saying: "If you establish even a single speck of dust, the state and its people flourish;
if you do not establish even a single speck of dust, the state and its people perish. He then took up his staff and asked: "Is there any monk who lives and dies together [with me]?"
Zhaojue Qin said: "If at that time there had been a man who could utter a single phrase of mutual guest-and-host, it would have spared this old fellow Xuedou from later on patting his own chest."
Gushan Xian said: "Now tell me, is it 'established' right now? Or is it 'not established' right now?

If you say that sometimes it is established and sometimes it is not established, it is like a malarial fever. If you say that both are illumined and both are concealed, with concealment and illumination occurring simultaneously—"
This is still not yet the ultimate principle of the teaching school. After all, how is it? [The Master] took up his staff and struck it once.
Chan Master Baoshou Zhao of Zhenzhou (the fifth-generation descendant of Linji Huiquan in the Southern Lineage) was asked by a monk while the latter was paying his respects:
"The hundreds of thousands of sages are all contained within this abbot’s quarters. The monk said, "As for what the ancients said: 'The great chiliocosm is like a drop in the ocean...'"
The monk said, "Bubble! I do not understand where this square zhang (room) is placed. Shou said, "A thousand sages are present right now.
The monk asked, "Who can testify to this? Shou then threw down his whisk. The monk moved from west to east and stood there; Shou struck him.
The monk said, "Had you not practiced for a long time, how could you know the ultimate point? Shou said, "Thirty years from now, these words will spread widely."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Baoshou was in the abbot’s quarters spreading his nets and setting his snares.
This monk, holding high his head and clipping his horns at the baited hook, surged against the waves three times, yet three times he was caught in the trap.
Tell me, what did he gain? Do you understand? Under a heavy reward, there must be brave men."
Because a monk asked Baoshou, "What is it like when there is not a single speck of cloud ten thousand miles away? Baoshou said, "Even the clear blue sky must receive a blow of the staff.
The monk asked, "I do not understand; what fault does the clear blue sky have? Baoshou then struck him.
Tianqi said, "Baoshou, great as he was, can truly be called one who has thoroughly understood the person and seen blood when killing;
yet his realization was still incomplete. Xingyun said, "Baoshou was indeed a man of substance; he could speak and he spoke to the point, and he could act and he acted effectively.
It was simply too late. Had I been him, I would have waited for him to ask: 'When there is not a single cloud ten thousand miles away, what then?'"
He then struck him on the head with a blow of his staff, lest he should fall prostrate under the blue sky.
Because of Hu Dingjiao’s inquiry, Baoshou asked, "Are you not Hu Dingjiao? Hu replied, "I dare not say so.
Baoshou asked, "Can you nail the void? Hu said, "Please, Master, break it open for me. Baoshou then struck him. Hu said:
"Preceptor, do not strike me in error," Huo said. Shou replied, "In the future, there will be many eloquent masters who will point this out for you.
Later, Huo went to Zhaozhou and recounted the previous story. Zhaozhou asked, "For what reason were you struck by him?
Huo said, "I do not know where my fault lay. Zhaozhou said, "Even this single seam [of your robe] cannot be dealt with. Huo...
Thereupon, he attained a realization.
Xuedou Xian said: "I would like to strike these three fellows: first, for striking Zhaozhou, who was unfit to blind the eyes of Hu Dingjiao;
second, for striking Baoshou, who could not shut Zhaozhou’s mouth; and third, for striking Hu Dingjiao himself."
"I cannot let Bao-shou pass," he said, suddenly seizing his staff and adding, "There is yet another.
The assembly all withdrew at once, whereupon he struck the meditation seat once.
Taisu Zhe said: "Although this fellow managed to clear himself, it is a pity that Zhaozhou let him off. At that time, had he waited for the question 'Where is it?
and then struck him across the back with his staff, he would not only have inherited the majestic radiance of Baoshou, but would also have served as a model and a mirror for the monastic community."
Jingshan Daowu said: "Even if one were able to nail down that single seam, upon closer inspection, it would still not be the work of a true master.
How pitiable these two old Chan elders, who instead of maintaining their dignity, go so far as to air their family's private failings before laypeople."
Gushan Yong said: "Although Baoshou possessed the tongs and hammer capable of shattering empty space, he could not avoid wounding his hand on the edge of the blade.
That Lord Hu finally attained awakening—whom would have known that his eyes were still clouded with rheum?"
Tianning Qisong said: "Hu Dingjiao originally knew nothing of that single seam.
At that time, had Zhaozhou not provided the thief with a ladder to climb over, even though he had worn through one hundred and twenty pairs of straw sandals, it would still not have been noticed."
Although Ningtiao understood it clearly, he was still three thousand li away from Baoshou.
Zifu Guang said: "A crossbow capable of launching a ten-thousand-jin bolt does not fire its trigger for a field mouse; Baoshou cannot be said to be without fault.
Although Zhaozhou was skilled at turning things around, he was merely shooting sparrows on the ground."
Yunxi Ting said: "Although Baoshou inherited his grandfather’s legacy, he could not help but paint a gourd after the model.
Hu Dingjiao was ultimately a dead man. Had he known how to recognize and repay kindness, he would have had a share in striking Zhaozhou’s fist."
Baoshou came from Xiyuan to inquire about the Way. Xiyuan said, "How was it when you overturned the City of Transformation?
Baoshou replied, "I do not execute a dead man. Xiyuan said, "Execute him! Baoshou struck him immediately. Xiyuan repeatedly cried out, "Execute! Execute! Baoshou struck him again with each word.
After a short while, he said to his attendant monk, "That monk just now met a bare shoulder with a dry stick; why such a desperate rush for death?"
Next, another monk came forward and said, "I, so-and-so, inform the Master: the monk who engaged in that dialogue with you came from the place of Dajue.

The two of them studied together; seeing that their understanding here is exactly like this, I fear that if they are not later made fully aware of your Way, it will be difficult to find anyone to inherit your lineage.
He continued, "You must expel these two men. If you do not expel them, it will be difficult to find someone to succeed you in the future."
Baoshou was about to report this to the monks when he drove him out.
Fengxue said with joy, "Xiyuan has trampled through the provisional city (the *parīttābha* realm), yet his heels have not yet touched the ground.
"If Baoshou had not slain this dead man, blood would have already splattered against the Brahma Heaven. Setting that aside for a moment, what about the one who was driven out?
The monk asked, "What do you mean? "Fully endowed with both strategy and tactics, he possesses great spirit; from the south of Annam to the north of Sai, he has gathered them all together.
Baoshou asked a newly arrived monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Cui Chan. Baoshou said, "Have you brought back Cui Chan’s shout with you?
The monk said, "I have not brought it back. Baoshou said, "If that is so, then it did not come from Cui Chan. The monk then shouted.
Baoshou raised his staff. As the monk hesitated, Baoshou struck him immediately.
Yunju Shun said, "It was perilous that Baoshou questioned him in such a manner; this monk had food already at the edge of his mouth, only to have it snatched away by another."
Baiyan Fu said: "This monk was indeed stubborn and yielding; alas, he had a beginning but no end.

Had he been a true man of character, he should have waited for the staff to be raised, then let out a shout and swept his sleeves to depart. Then Bao-shou would surely have looked upon him with another eye."

When Chan Master Huiruan of Sansheng in Zhenzhou (the fifth-generation descendant of Linji Huiquan in the South) arrived at Deshan’s place, he had just spread out his sitting cloth when Deshan said, “There is no need to spread out your napkin;
here there is no leftover soup or stale rice. Sansheng said, “I am fortunate to have encountered such a place.
Even if there were, where would you put it? Deshan struck him immediately. Sansheng caught the staff and pushed Deshan over onto his meditation seat. Deshan laughed loudly. Sansheng wept and said:
"Blue sky! Blue sky! He then went down to enter the hall.
Langya Huijue said, "If there were no Luan Bu, how could we have seen Han Guang?
Guishan Xingyan said, "Sansheng’s 'brushing away the grass and observing the wind' involves both unfolding and rolling up; Deshan examines the ordinary and tests the extraordinary."
The Sage has both release and gathering. Setting aside for a moment Deshan’s laughing away, what was the meaning of Sansheng’s crying out “Heaven! and then departing?
One who does not crave the taste of fragrant bait may truly be called a dragon in a clear, deep pool.
Yunyan You said: "When Sansheng simply spread out his sitting cloth, it was because 'the mind of a thief is always suspicious. Deshan said: 'There is no need to spread out the napkin;
the tail is already exposed. Sansheng said: 'Even if there were [a way], where would one put it? It is the mouth that is the gateway to calamity."
Shan then struck him. He shattered the past and present. Sheng took up the staff and pushed the mountain onto the meditation couch. "A rat enters a cow's horn.
There is yet another turning word: wait for a man without a tongue to refrain from speaking, and then I shall tell it to you.
Chinghua said: "The red-eyed Fire Vajra—his skillful means are exactly equal to his. A master meets a master; why further wail to the azure heavens?
Who knows of the spring colors within the cave? Outside the gate, the autumnal crimson has been blown away by the wind."
The Three Sages arrived at Yangshan. Yangshan asked, "What is your name? Sanjie said, "Huiji. Yangshan said, "Huiji is my name.
Sanjie said, "My name is Huiran. Yangshan simply laughed loudly.
Zhaojue, having finished reciting Xuedou’s verse, said: "This laugh—throughout ten thousand autumns and ten thousand ages, the pure wind blows with chilling majesty.
Why is it that Xuedou instead says, 'It should only stir a wind of sorrow through the ages'? This too is 'dying without receiving a funeral.'"
Jingshan Hongdao said: "These two fellows who hide their bodies while exposing their shadows do not care at all that bystanders will laugh.
Yufan Yuanwu said: "Yangshan digs a hole in empty space; Sansheng smelts stones to patch the heavens.
Chen Hiyi slept for a thousand years, and even now he does not know [when he woke]. It is truly laughable!"

Fengshan began by saying: "Like sounds respond to like sounds; like vapors seek out like vapors. Appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unfolding, acting with spontaneous mastery according to conditions—this is the very core of the patch-robed monk.
Yet, if one merely stands as steep as ten-thousand-fathom cliffs while facing only clay gods and local deities,"
Furthermore, who can know the transformations of the cloud-dragon, or the lush patterns of the mist-preserved leopard? Nevertheless, tell me:
what was the rhythm of Yangshan’s smile? Having said this, he threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.

The Third Sage ascended the hall and said, "Whenever I encounter a person, I come forth; yet when I come forth, it is not for the sake of others. He then descended from his seat. Xinghua Jiang said, "I am not like this.
Whenever I encounter a person, I do not come forth; yet when I do come forth, I do so for the sake of others."
Baoning Yong said, "These two venerable masters acting in such a manner for the sake of others are still only halfway there.
Today, Baoning saw injustice on the road; picking up his staff, he descended from his seat. The assembly all scattered at once, and he threw down the staff and returned to his quarters.
Baofeng Wen said: "These two ancient sages stole a mere fragment of Linji’s livelihood;
each claimed his own territory and established his own boundaries, their vital energy filling the universe. Were a clear-eyed monk to see this, he could only laugh."
Now tell me, what is it that they laugh at? Do you know where the point lies? If you do, go ahead and act however you please, even if you are utterly disoriented.
If you do not, then for now, chew upon the tangled vines of these two elders.
Zhaojue Qin said: "One person stands atop a solitary peak with a dusty face and a head covered in ash;
another stands at the crossroads, cutting through nails and severing iron. With beginning and end, they die together and live together. Now tell me:
is it the one who 'coming forth does not act for others,' or is it the one who 'coming forth immediately acts for others'? Ten thousand ages, the moon in the empty realm of the azure pool."
"Only after repeated searching and probing can one finally come to know.
Lingyin Yue said: "Those two old fellows extinguished the orthodox Dharma-eye of Linji, yet they proceeded hand-in-hand along the road to Chang'an.
To this very day, they have continued to obstruct one another. But tell me, what does 'proceeding hand-in-hand' mean?"
A single phrase: it pulls open the locks of the golden hall and strikes the bells of the jade tower.
Tiantong Jue said, "Falling! Falling! Today, I am not diminishing the reputation and glory of the ancients; rather, I wish to uphold the integrity of future generations.
If one is a man of true substance, they will carry the seal of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and turn the mechanism of the iron ox. Taking hold—
When the staff pierces through everything at once, only then will you see the handiwork of a true monk.
Jingshan Daowu said, "Old man Zhenjing seems to be deceiving the deceased; I, Upāsaka Daowu, am not like that.
He has cleared open the paths of the Three Essentials and Three Mysteries, sitting astride the first peak of Mount Sumeru. But tell me, where does he reside?
Is it on the side of the noble division? Or is it on the side of the division of flourishing transformation? Let those with eyes discern and take it up.
Yangshan Qin said, "The two elders could be described as a single staff being carried by two people. Today, Tianning has snapped it into two pieces.
Leaning his staff against the left side, he said, "Now listen, each for yourselves. And so it remains level.
Fenbao Enxiu said: "These two fellows are much like those who, possessing great talent and bold speech, rely on their influence to deceive others.
He took up his staff and asked, "Do you see Sanxing and Huihua? Then, leaning the staff back against him, he said, "Even if one possesses the patched robe..."
The monk’s means: for now, stand on this side. Tianning Qi said:
"Why is it that while Sanxing and Huihua were both masters of the clear eye, their livelihoods were fundamentally the same yet their careers diverged so completely?
'Where there is a path to ascend, those of superior stature go further.'"
Jingshan Xiu said: "One person has attained its essence; another has attained its function. Yet neither of them possesses the true skillful means of a master.
Wanshou has already emerged from this; tell me, does he have a way to benefit others, or does he not?
At the summit of Mount Zhurong, dewdrops fall upon the ten-thousand-year-old pines.
Wushan Dao said: "One person stands atop the highest peak; another walks upon the deepest ocean floor.
To wish to uphold the true lineage of Linji is still far from sufficient. Shixi, however, was not like this. How can this be seen?
"Both ends are completely severed; a single sword leans against the cold heavens."
Songyin sighed and said: "These two elders were fellow disciples who traveled together, yet they were enemies from past lives.
One lay upon the moon and slept amidst the clouds atop a solitary peak; the other raised dust and scattered soil at the crossroads of the marketplace.
When examined closely, both are equally deficient; I shall give each of them thirty blows of the staff. But tell me, what about Longfeng acting in this way?"
"This one is rewarded; that one is punished. [The Master] suddenly took up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said:
"In the heavens, all stars bow toward the North; among men, no water flows but toward the East."
Xuedou said: "Of these two fellows, one has a surplus where another lacks; one lacks where another has a surplus.
Examining them closely, I would give each of them thirty blows of the staff. He added: "I, this mountain monk, have rendered such a judgment;
tell me, was it for the sake of people or not? Let those with eyes discern this."
Yuan’an Yu said: "Today this mountain monk has come forth. Is it for the sake of others, or is it not for the sake of others?
If it is for the sake of others, one falls into Xinghua’s trap. If it is not for the sake of others, one falls into Sansheng’s trap.
If it is neither of these, one still falls into this mountain monk’s trap. After all, how is it? He let out a shout.
With one shout, he said: "A tangle of willow threads cannot be gathered up; they are draped with mist upon the jade balustrade. Xiqia Cheng said:
"These two fellows merely beat their two pieces of skin. While it is beautiful, it is not yet skillful. Why?
The numinous tortoise carries the map, yet it brings about the omen of its own destruction."
Baoshou Xin said: "If the Three Sages possessed the ability to sacrifice themselves, how could they have lacked the heart to benefit others?
If Xinghua possessed the heart to benefit others, how could he have lacked the ability to sacrifice himself? Can you truly grasp this?
It is easy to distinguish flour from snow, but difficult to discern soot within ink."
Wulei Quan said: "Fortunately, the Venerable Patriarch broke it off; today, we unworthy descendants cannot help but use phoenix glue to join it back together for him.
To come forth when meeting people, or not to come forth when meeting people—it is two prizes and one wager."
Like an arrow hitting the mark, a golden phoenix carries flowers down from the painted pavilion. From within the pupils of his eyes, he blows the double-reed pipe;
the three stages of the dance must all be hurried together. Boundless pure breezes arise throughout the eight directions.
Zifu’s companion said: "Sansheng is like a tiger with horns upon its head; Xinghua is like an ox or a sheep without horns.
If you can recognize these two elders, then every sip of drink and every morsel of food [is accounted for]. Pshh!"

Baoguang said: "The two venerable masters, Sansheng and Xinghua, took a single weight and cast it back and forth, causing people to try to chew upon it but unable to do so. Tell me, at such a time as this, who was first and who was last?
After a long silence, he said: "A tangle of willow threads cannot be gathered in; they are draped with mist upon the jade balustrade."
Shendǐngzé said: "These two fellows look very much like men holding military passes, each seeking to dominate their own territory.
If they reach the gate of our Patriarchal Ancestor, I shall give them thirty blows of the staff and drive them out. Why? Because the Fourth Patriarch has newly opened his shop;
rewards and punishments must be clear."

After Bodhidhenu finished reciting the words of Zhenjing, he said: "The old man Zhenjing mistakenly applied names and phrases, which have burdened later generations by following established paths and guarding old ruts, delineating boundaries and dividing territories.
Little do they realize that these two great elders drew golden arrows from behind their backs and pulled horned bows with a turn of the body.
While it is not that they lacked the ability to stir up the guest-host dynamic of Linji, as for being truly alive—"
"Consider this: when have you ever dreamed of it? Today, I must also let everyone know where the new Bodhi has fallen.
[He drew a line with his staff and said: "Since leaving the cave, there has been no rival; where one can afford to be generous, one should be generous.
He then cast down the staff and descended from the seat.
Hexu Qian said: "One person has teeth like a forest of swords; another has a mouth like a blood-basin.

Together they take a rope made of tortoise hair, intending to thread it through the nostrils of everyone under heaven. Little do they realize that their own nostrils have already been threaded by everyone under heaven."
The Three Sages asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk gave a shout. The Sage also shouted. The monk shouted again. The Sage shouted again.
The monk said, "If you strike me with a staff, I will go blind," and he shouted. The Sage took up his staff. The monk turned his body and made a gesture as if to receive the blow.
The Sage said, "Running downhill, one does not flee; such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter," and he struck him. The monk said, "You thief! and went out. The Sage then threw [the staff].
[The Master] struck him with the staff. Next, a monk asked, "Just now, how was that monk permitted to enter? The Sage said, "It is because he has seen the former master.
Tianjing Xin said, "To take the head and make it the tail is easy; to look at the tower and strike the tower is difficult. Why? Because..."
The Path of Seeing: "Where the white clouds end, there is the green mountain; the traveler is yet beyond the green mountain. Famin Mi said:
"This monk possesses hands and eyes that transcend the ordinary; the Three Sages exercise their awesome authority beyond the conventional.
Although their methods of granting and revoking are worth observing, they cannot avoid being laughed at by bystanders."
The Hermit Fu-pan (Nan-wu Linji Xuan’s successor) had a monk approach from the foot of the mountain weeping. Fu-pan closed the door.
The monk drew a circle on the door and stood outside. Fu-pan emerged from behind the hermitage and went back down the mountain weeping.
The monk shouted, “If you still act like this, you are right there! Fu-pan then changed hands and beat his breast, saying, “It can be done!”
"What a pity that our former teacher has been so utterly buried! The monk said, "Bitter! Bitter! Baolin said, "The abbot of the hermitage has been deceived.
Bairan Fu remarked, "A monk came weeping up from the foot of the mountain; there was no small amount of fabrication. Baolin then shut the door.
"Why such haste? The monk drew a circle on the gate and stood outside. "I have already waited for the white.
Baofeng came out from behind the hermitage and went up the mountain weeping. "He is still waiting for the black.
The monk shouted, "To still act in this way is to be present right here! Ming was skilled at blaming others but ignorant of blaming himself. Baofeng changed hands and struck him.
Xiong said, "What a pity! Our late Master has been utterly buried. It is like a red-eyed man bumping into a fire-torch.
The monk said, "Bitter, bitter! Truly, truly! Bo asked, "The abbot of the hermitage has been deceived. Heh! For now, believe only half of it. He spoke again.
When these two fellows encounter one another head-on, they are like a dragon finding water or a tiger meeting the mountains;
their majestic and fierce spirit is indeed undeniable. Yet, if they were to arrive here at White Rock, I would give each of them twenty blows of the staff.
Why? Because before the hall of the ancient Buddhas, such things do not exist.
Bingshan Qian said: "Let us set aside for the moment this monk’s demonic arts; the abbot follows the heterodox and pursues evil—he deserves twenty strokes with a broom."
*Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School*,
Volume Twenty-Six and Volume Twenty-Seven.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Dharma Heir of Baiyan at Ancient Hangzhou.
△ Nanyue Wufu Dajue Heshang (Nanyue, successor of Linji Xuan). He visited Linji. When Linji held up his whisk, Dajue unfolded his sitting cloth.
Linji cast down the whisk; Dajue gathered up his sitting cloth and departed for the hall. At that time, the assembly discussed, saying, "This monk..."
"Perhaps you are a relative or acquaintance of the Master; that is why you do not prostrate and yet do not receive a blow.
When Linji heard this, he ordered his attendant to summon Huizhao to him and said, "The assembly says that you came to visit the Elder, yet you neither prostrate nor receive a blow.
Perhaps you are a relative or acquaintance of the Elder? Huizhao then respectfully took his leave and went down.
As Anzhang said: "The wind comes and the trees move; the rain passes and the mountains turn green.

If these two elders were truly masters meeting one another, they could indeed be said to have transcended ordinary sentiment. Nevertheless, when scrutinized, it appears that Dajue still lacks one stroke.
At that time, when the attendant came to call him, he should have struck him with his palm and said: "This one blow should have been taken by the old man of the Hall (the Abbot).
Not only would this have cut off Linji’s throat, but it would also have caused the doubts of the entire assembly to melt away like ice."
Chan Master Shanshui Cui of Dingzhou (the fifth-generation successor of Linji Huiyuan in the South) was invited by Governor Wang Linggong to preach the Dharma at his official residence.
Master Cui ascended the seat, took up his staff, and said, "I will strike you if you come forward; I will strike you if you do not come forward.
A monk stepped forth and said, "What about Chan Master Cui? Master Cui immediately cast down his staff and said, "I have kept you waiting for a long time, Excellency. I pray you take care."
He then descended from his seat.
Wuzu Kei approached another monk and pushed over his meditation bench.
Langya Huijue said, "One who has long experienced the ranks of battle never unfurls his spear or banner."
Yungai Zhiyun said: "To press one's body against a white blade without fearing birth or death—one must be such a monk to achieve this.
Why did Cui Chan let him off at that critical moment? Do you wish to understand? The scaled dragon has already been caught; cease your labor."
"Retire with the silken line gathered;
there is no need to go further. Jianfu Xingyun said: "Cui Chan’s words are indeed beautiful, yet they are not yet perfect. Why? Because they are very much like letting the monk off the hook.
I, this mountain monk, am not like that. I would wait for that monk to emerge from the assembly, and before he had even opened his mouth, I would strike him a severe blow."
“Strike! If there were blood beneath his skin, he would surely have had another career.
Guifeng Guang said: “Cui Chan deployed a long-serpent and crescent-moon grand array, intending to unify the four great continents into a single world.
Had it not been for this monk snatching the banner and seizing the drum, he would inevitably have fallen captive in the enemy’s court. And so it is.
Sitting in the command tent, he planned the Way and brought peace to the eight directions. Water and milk blend together; wind and clouds meet in harmony—how do you express this in a single phrase?
"Had it not been for shooting the stone tiger at Lan-tien, Li General would have nearly been killed."
Nanjian asked: "The monk Yungai said that a practitioner of the Way does not fear life or death when facing a white blade;

it is a pity that Cui Chan let him off at that critical moment. What he did not realize was that this monk had already been struck by Cui Chan’s blow of the staff and, to this day, has been unable to turn himself around.
Do you wish to recognize Cui Chan? He is one who devises strategies within the tent and secures victory a thousand miles away."
Baoshang said: "Cui Chan intended to station troops at ten locations while commanding the hall from within;
he did not know that a salt smuggler had broken through the lines into his cold, deserted camp, nearly capturing Caizhou."
Baiyan Fu said: "This monk, with a single horse and a solitary blade, charges into the midst of a dragon-and-serpent array to slay generals and seize banners;
one cannot help but grant him the status of a hero among heroes. Yet, how could he have anticipated that Cui Chan’s military stratagems would prove even more subtle than those of Sun Zi and Wu Qi?
Nevertheless, neither can withstand the cold eye of the Duke."
Guangjiao Yuyun said: "If you come out, I strike; if you do not come out, I strike. [He continued: "Forged from solid steel, cast from raw iron.

A monk came forward and asked, "What about Cui Chan? [Yuyun replied: "Swords and spears filling the ground. Cui threw down his staff and descended from the seat. "Dug the earth to bury the innocent," they say.
The ancients all remarked that this monk did not spare himself from peril as he pushed forward into the white [of the crowd].
A blade! Little did they know that the monks Da and Xiao Cui Chan had been cornered by this monk; they could do nothing but follow the error with the error.
Is there anyone who can recognize the stench of their sweat?
Chan Master Tantong of Youzhou (a successor of Linji Xuan of the fifth generation in the South) was once asked by the Prefect of Zhenzhou, who had a paternal aunt who was a nun.

Upon her return from traveling the pilgrimage routes, she wished to open a hall to teach others. The Prefect ordered Tantong to examine her. Tantong asked, "I have heard you wish to open a hall to teach others;
is this true? The nun replied, "It is. Tantong said, "A nun possesses a body subject to the five obstacles. How will you go about teaching others? The nun—
He asked, "The eight-year-old dragon girl attained perfect enlightenment in the Land of No Stain in the south—how about that?
Huitang said, "The dragon girl manifested eighteen transformations; try to manifest one yourself. The nun said, "If you aren't a wild fox spirit, what would you transform? Huitang then struck her.
The Abbot of Zhenzhou heard of this and said, "Has the Master broken his staff?
Cuiyan Zhi replied, "Tell me, does the nun have eyes or not? She can only carry a single strand of a broken rope."
"How do you understand this?
Master Guǎnxī Zhìxián of Èzhōu (the fifth-generation successor of Línjì Xuán in the South) went to visit Línjì. Línjì suddenly grabbed him by the chest.
Guǎnxī said, "I understand, I understand. Línjì pushed him away and said, "Let me let you off with one blow."
Tiantong Hua said: "Guangxi’s bearing was like that of a king; yet he was buried alive by Linji in the middle of the crossroads within the city of Zhenzhou.
At that time, had it been Guangxiao, even if his staff had broken, he would not have let him go. Why is this so?"
"A family prospers through filial sons; a state achieves hegemony through strategic ministers.
Lingyin Yue said, "In a forge, even dull iron is still abundant. Nevertheless, were it not for the wild geese arriving last night, how could one perceive the autumn at the sea gate?"
After Guankui took up residence, he ascended the hall and said: "At the place of my grandfather Linji, I received half a ladle; at the place of my grandmother Moshan, I received half a ladle.
Together they made one full ladle which I consumed, and from that time until now, I have been so full that I have never hungered."
Tiantong Jue said: "When Guankui speaks in this manner, tell me: did he obtain this from Linji or from Moshan?
Although it is like an arrow that brings down two eagles at once, how can one avoid being 'run to death' at times and 'sat to death' at others?
How, then, can one attain the perfect state? To grasp and release is entirely up to me; when brought forth,"
Casting it aside, by whom would it be further known?
Guankui ascended the hall and said: "The ten directions have no walls; the four sides likewise have no gates. It is bare and naked; it is stark and clear."
"There is nothing to grasp. He then descended from his seat.
Chongjue Kong said, "The old fellow Guanyin flaunts his elegance on the crossroads, peddling his cleverness."
"I claim to know how to string pearls, carve jade tablets, untangle matted silk, and roll bolts of silk. Yet in brothels and taverns, among the common rabble and the lowly servants;
in tiger dens and demon palaces, amidst the wrath of Nanda—when encountering King Wen, I promoted rites and music;
when meeting Jie and Zhou, I brandished weapons and war. Today, having been spotted by Chongjue, I am utterly humiliated."
Guankui was asked by a monk, "I have long heard of Guankui; having arrived, I see only the hemp-soaking pond.
Guankui said, "You see only the hemp-soaking pond, but you do not yet see Guankui. The monk asked, "What is Guankui? Guankui replied, "As swift as a split arrow."
Xuansha Shibei said, "Even after thirty more years of study, I would still not have understood Zen.
Tiantong Wu said, "Although Guankui was able to pull the nostrils back, what could he do? It merely provoked conceptual views.
Why not wait for him to ask, 'What is Guankui? and strike him across the spine immediately?"
One day, Master Wanshou of Zhenzhou (the fifth-generation successor of Linji of the Southern Lineage) went to visit Baoshou. As Baoshou sat without rising, Wanshou unfolded his sitting mat (*zuoju*).
Baoshou descended from his meditation seat, whereupon Wanshou sat down again. Baoshou then hurried into the abbot’s quarters and shut the door.
Wanshou returned to his own quarters. The following day, Baoshou came to pay his respects once more; Wanshou likewise sat without rising. Baoshou unfolded his sitting mat. Wanshou...
Wanshou also descended from his meditation seat. Baoshou sat back down. Wanshou then returned to his quarters and closed the door.
Baoshou went to the attendants' hall, took some ash, circled the door of Wanshou’s quarters, and then departed. When Wanshou opened the door and saw this, he said, "I do not act like that;
he acts like that."
Qingshan Xiu said: "The two elders—one charging and one colliding—were like two tigers meeting, each baring its claws and fangs;
there was not the slightest flaw in either. They were not ashamed to be fellow practitioners and are truly worthy of being taken as models.
Nevertheless, they could not entirely avoid the laughter of bystanders."
Baiyan Fu said: "When these two elders meet as host and guest, their advances and retreats are worthy of observation.

If those who have caused their teachers to be disgraced and their nations to suffer were to see this, would they not break out in a cold sweat? Nevertheless, both hands emerge level, yet among them one takes the lead.
Do you understand this thoroughly? If I were Wanshou, seeing the ashes surrounding the gate, I would immediately unfold my formal robes and gaze into the void."
He bowed three times.
Master Tongfeng (Nanyue Wulin, successor of Linji Xuan) was asked by a monk, "What if you suddenly encounter a tiger here?
The Master immediately made a tiger's roar. The monk made a gesture of fear. The Master laughed loudly. The monk said, "This old thief! The Master replied, "How so?"
"What can you do about this old monk? The monk laughed loudly in response.
Xuedou Xian said, "It may be so, but these two scoundrels only know how to cover their ears while stealing the bell."
Yuan'an Yu said: "Tongfeng did not use the staff, which is why it is marvelous; this monk did not use the shout, which is why it is marvelous.
Tongfeng laughed loudly; this monk also laughed loudly. They boast of themselves as heroes within the Liangshan marshes, but upon closer inspection, they are all nothing but scoundrels."
Master Yunshan (the fifth-generation descendant of Linji of the Southern Lineage) asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk replied, “From the Western Capital.
Yunshan said, “Have you brought a letter from the host of the Western Capital? The monk said, “I dare not falsely transmit any news. Yunshan said, “A master monk has a natural presence.
The monk said, “Who would eat leftover soup and rancid rice? Yunshan said, “Only you, Reverend, find this unacceptable.”
"Eat! The monk then made a gesture of vomiting. Mount San called to his attendant, saying, "Help that sick monk out. The monk then went out. Zhaojue Qin said:
"Judging from the first encounter, both were masters of the craft; yet upon examining each step of their verification, both have fallen into error."
*Ts'ao*. At that time, had there been someone who could have cut through this tangle of vines, it would have certainly outshone the past and surpassed the future.
Do you understand? Much emptiness is not as good as a little reality.
Ding Shangzuo (Nanwu, successor of Linji Xuan), having returned from a vegetarian feast in the provincial seat, sat upon a bridge. Next, three presiding masters arrived.
One master asked, "What is the meaning of 'the deep reaches of the Zen river must be fathomed to the bottom'?
Ding seized him and prepared to hurl him over the bridge. The other two masters hurried forward and pleaded, "Stop, stop! Do not take offense at disturbing the Senior Monk; please—"
He hoped for compassion. Ding said, "If it were not for these two presiding masters, I would have driven him to his ultimate end.
Nanjian asked, "Master Ding, your life is in the hands of these two masters."

One day, when the lay practitioner Chen Cao, a Minister of the State Department of Muzhou (also known as Chen Si of Muzhou in the fifth Nan), was ascending the tower with his subordinates, he saw several monks approaching from afar.
One official remarked, "Those coming are all traveling monks. The Minister said, "They are not."
He asked, "How do you know it is not he? The Governor said, "Wait until he arrives and we shall verify it. After a short while, the monk arrived before the tower.
The Governor suddenly called out, "Venerable! and the monks all raised their heads. The Governor said to the assembled officials, "I told you so."
Tianping Zhe said: "The Minister Chen may truly be described as one who holds the sun and moon of Confucius in his hands and wears the golden seal of Vairocana at his waist.
Not only are the Confucian scholars struck with awe, but even the monastics are left at a loss. Have you not heard it said: 'When the opportunity arises, it is like a flash of lightning;
only then can one avoid dwelling sick among the reeds'?"
Tiantong Jue said: "Minister Chen Cao was a 'white-handed thief' (a master thief); he could not deceive Changlu by even a single point.
Gushan Yong said: "This monk’s logic is difficult to justify; he is dead and cannot be mourned.
The Minister presses his sword against the gate—who would dare look directly at him?"
Tongxuan Qi said: "The Minister of State may indeed be called one who well discerns auspicious and ominous signs; he changes people's eyesight amidst the clamor.
Although this monk raises his head and calls it marvelous, it is a pity that he remains equally oppressed by injustice."
"New clouds arise in the sky. The various officials have set a trap for the tiger; the Minister possesses the eye that penetrates the pass.
This mountain monk can only keep his eyes level and his nose straight. Examining this from the beginning, Mount Guishan has not only defiled the Minister, but has also buried himself.
Furthermore, what is the "stinking sweat" of a wandering monk? One must speak without avoiding it.
"Cut out their tongues!
[The Master] said. "As for the topknot jewel, it is said that the various officials were deceived face-to-face by the Minister; their feelings may still be excused.
But to involve several Zen practitioners and cause them to suffer injustice for no reason—is that excusable?"
While in his fasting quarters, the Minister held up a steamed bun and asked a monk, "Is there such a thing as this in Jiangxi and Hunan?
The monk replied, "Minister, what did you just eat? The Minister said, "I struck the bell to thank it for its sound."
Yingshan Yun said: "This monk is like a swift falcon soaring toward the heavens; he arrives with great agility.
