Yet, alas, in the end, he falls into his net. As for the saying, 'Strike the bell to thank the echo'—how should one respond here?
Why not say, 'The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated'?"
△ Chan Master Daogyan of Jiufeng (Qingwu Shishuang Zhusi): While Daogyan was serving as the attendant at Shishuang, Shishuang passed away.
The assembly wished to appoint the Head Seat to succeed him on the seat, but Jiufeng addressed the assembly, saying: "One must first understand the meaning of the former master before one may do so."
The Head Seat said, "What was the meaning of our late teacher? Feng then asked, "Our late teacher said: 'Rest! Cease! Be cold and still!
A single thought for ten thousand years! Cold ashes and withered wood! An incense burner in an ancient temple!
A single strand of white silk! I do not ask about the others; as for 'a single strand of white silk,' how do you understand it, Head Seat?"
Zuò said, "This fellow understands only the matter of the 'single color' (the realm of form). Fēng said, "I see now that you have not yet grasped the intent of our former teacher.
Zuò said, "Do you not agree with me? Just bring some incense. When the smoke of the incense is severed, if you cannot go on, then you have truly understood."
He did not grasp the meaning of his former teacher. He then burned incense; as soon as the smoke rose, the master’s body fell from the seat.
Shifeng patted him on the back and said, "To die while sitting or standing is certainly possible, but you have not even dreamed of the meaning of your former teacher."
Yunju Shun said, "The attendant has all his life possessed only one eye.
Kaifeng Ning asked, "Tell me, does the Head Seat understand the late Master’s meaning, or does he not?"
If you say they have attained realization, although it is not that the attendant Qian did not sit and pass away or stand and depart, you have not even dreamed of the former master’s intent.
If you say they have not attained realization, what can be done about the Head Seat Liangzai who so readily cast off his hands and departed?
Tell me, where lies the point of benefit or harm? Do you understand? When the road is long and the night is dark, do not carry a torch. Great!
"His house is blown out and he walks in the dark.

Nanhua Ying said: "To penetrate the barrier of birth and death, to transcend all things, to wield the sword of killing and giving life, and to stand alone within the realm—if one’s eye of wisdom is not clear and penetrating, one cannot avoid leaning on a fence and groping along a wall. Do you understand? The spring orchid and..."
The autumn chrysanthemums each flourish in their own season.

The *Jianfuxing* (Verses on Offering Merit) says: "In general, regarding the seat of one's fundamental practice, one desires the arms and elbows to be heavy; without such weight, one cannot balance the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
One desires the claws and fangs to be sharp; without such sharpness, there is no way to open and expand for humans and devas. Observe him!
When Shishuang passed away, the head seat and the attendant each put forth a hand to support his school’s fundamental tenets;
this was truly brilliant, surpassing all before and after, and rarely heard of in antiquity or today.
If you wish to discern the source of this matter, each of you must please break your bows and arrows and overturn the shooting target, and then come meet with this old monk.
Jingshan Hongdao said: "Two iron hammers without holes; among them, one is the heaviest. Tianning Weiqing said:
"The Head Seat passed away while sitting; the attendant speaks of yellow and black paths. My late teacher’s intent lies at the tip of the hook;
you must believe that within the curve there is the straight. Had this been under Linji’s gate, thirty blows would have been administered."
"Who eats? As soon as one speaks of right and wrong, one becomes a person of right and wrong.
Baoen Xiu said: "The Head Seat carries a shoulder-board and gets only one end of it.

At that time, had he seen the path and said, "If so, then I have not yet realized the meaning of the former master," he would have simply needed to say, "I am not your equal. This would have taught Jiupeng that there is no ground for him.
To have space for one's own body. One does not see the Way as being insufficient when striving, nor as having a surplus when yielding.
Yunmen Cheng said: "The various quarters all claim that the Head Seat has not yet realized the former master’s meaning;

yet if one examines this from the perspective of Jingshan, it is precisely Jiufeng who has not yet realized it. Why? Because he placed him in the Hall of Withered Trees to perform the work of the dead."
Is this not the meaning of Shishuang? "Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded. Is this not the Dongshan school?
Seeing that the Head Seat responded thus, [Zhaozhou] said, "You do not understand the former master’s meaning; you have missed it.
Because the Head Seat did not understand, Zhaozhou then carried out his full command. At such a moment, was it still "one color"?
"It is not merely a single color. When Jiufeng reached this point, his entire body was eyes yet could not discern it;

his whole body was mouths yet could not explain it. He could only forcibly assume the role of master and say: "As for 'passing away while sitting' or 'dying while standing,' these are certainly not nonexistent;

however, as for the intention of our former teacher, one has not even dreamed of it. Although he gained the advantage at that time, what can be done about the fact that later on there is a direct path?
The Elder Shancheng’s cold eye is difficult to deceive. He wishes to clear the injustice for the Head Seat.
O assembly, this guest and host together have completed a single, vast affair of the Buddha.
For you all to vainly seek right and wrong or gain and loss within his tongue is already far removed from the truth. This is how I, this mountain monk, pass judgment.
"Does the great assembly still find this sweet? After a long silence, he said: "Do not take your idle learning and understanding to bury the mind of the Patriarch.
Boshan Lai said: "One who builds well does not pull down; one who discerns well appears as if mute. The Head Seat trims away his floridity to fill out his substance;
he purifies his conduct and models himself after the standard. How could the affairs of the abbot be otherwise?"—Jiufeng.
"Too forceful and rigid; he does not accord with human sentiment. Has he even grasped the meaning of Shishuang? Altogether, he deserves thirty strokes of the broom.
Fuyan Rong said, "The Head Seat has cut off the ten directions and cannot take a single secret step. If it were I..."
When the monk saw the Way, how did he understand it? It is well said: "The precious sword that shaves hair blows cold upon people.
Had he hesitated for a moment, [the Master] would have given him a shout, saying, "Do not disgrace your former teacher! This would surely have left Jiufeng speechless.
Furthermore, they have merely won the position of abbot for a generation.
Qinghua Yun said, "These two fellows are like those from Wu and Yue rowing a boat, each using one side [of the oars].
I suspect that the ancient ancestor Shishuang would certainly not have nodded his head in approval."
Liran Guang said: "If I were the head seat, when he asks, 'What does this refer to?
I would simply say, 'The former master did not say such a thing; do not slander the former master.'"
Yunxi Ting said: "The Head Seat knows only the first and not the second; Jiufeng knows only the second and not the first.
Yet, as for the meaning of our late teacher, you have not even dreamed of it."
Longquan said, "One person is skilled at observing the transformations of the wind; the other is excessively harsh in his pressing and driving.

It is a pity that the entire lineage of Shishuang will be swept away and extinguished. If only there were someone who could cause flames to erupt from a frozen river and flowers to bloom on withered wood."
Waiting for him to say, "Explain what matter this refers to," he struck him with his staff upon the very sound of those words.
This not only glorified the ancestral Way, but also caused Jiufeng to retreat three thousand paces.
Baiyan Fu said: "Shishuang cast down a bottomless boat; the Head Seat took the helm and the Attendant held the rudder.
They sailed directly into the midst of vast, surging waves, riding the wind and carrying the moon—their inspiration was indeed at its height.
Yet, one does not know how many people can sit steadily within the hull."
A monk asked Jiufeng, "In the Western Heavens at the end of summer, those who have attained the Way are as numerous as a forest.

Is there anyone here who has attained the Way at the end of summer? Jiufeng said, "There is. The monk asked, "Who is it? Jiufeng replied, "One whose head bears the midnight moon and whose feet tread upon the golden earth."
Jingshan Xiu said: "Suppose someone were to ask Jingshan today, 'Is there anyone here who has attained the Way at the end of this summer?
You should simply answer, 'No. They might ask, 'Why do you say no? You would point out: 'Each and every one’s eyebrows hang across their eyes;
everyone’s nostrils are large and their heads hang low. Now tell me: which is Jingshan—the one from Jiufeng or the one here?"
A monk asked Jiufeng, "What is the head? Jiufeng said, "Opening one's eyes, one does not perceive the dawn.
"What is the tail? He said, "Not sitting upon the ten-thousand-year throne. "What is it like when there is a head but no tail? He said, "In the end, it is not noble.
"What is it like when there is a tail but no head? He said, "Though full, one lacks strength. "What is it like when the head and tail are perfectly matched? He said: [The text here ends.]
"The children and grandchildren have their strength, yet they do not know what is within the room.
Boshan Lai said: "Pointing out the living path amidst the marketplace; the tongue does not stick to the meat.
Unfolding the 'total raising' (quandi) in the realm above; the skull does not touch the heavens. Jiufeng’s mouth and teeth are like a shuttle in a loom; he naturally possesses skill."

"A wife's work is needlework. What is precious is that her children and grandchildren are capable and diligent, so that nothing is known within the inner chambers. But tell me, what is it that is not known?
Lingyin Li said: "Dongshan’s clarity and subtlety accord with the orthodox and the deviant; the four ministers all serve one sovereign. Nine.
Feng says that within the lineage, nobility and meanness are distinguished; the five sons return their whole bodies to the father.
Yet they do not realize that beyond the limit of Weiyin, five horses do not neigh, and at the gateway of this present world, a single ox does not drink. But tell me:

when clouds arise over the azure peaks and wind rises from the green reeds, when the withered tree roars like a dragon and the skull laughs with joy—how is this? Then he planted his staff on the ground.
Zhaozhou said: "The moon in the empty realm of the azure pool has existed for ten thousand ages; only after repeatedly searching and stirring it will you finally come to know it.
Chan Master Jingxin of Yongquan in Taizhou (a successor of Qingyuan Wenyi and Shishuang Chuyuan) encountered two Zen guests, Qiang and De, on the road.
Seeing a man from Spring Valley riding an ox, [Zhaozhou] did not recognize him and said, "The hooves and horns are quite distinct; what can be done about the rider who does not reflect?
Spring Valley spurred the ox away. Upon returning, he saw two Chan practitioners brewing tea under a tree; he dismounted the ox and sat with them.
He then asked, "Where have you recently come from? Qiang replied, "From over there. Juequan asked, "What is the matter of 'over there'? Qiang lifted his tea cup.
Juequan said, "This is still the matter of 'this side. What is the matter of 'over there'? Qiang was speechless.
Quán said, "Do not say that those on horseback do not possess discernment.
Bǎo Níng Yǒng, acting on Quán’s behalf, pointed to an attendant and said, "When you return to the mountains, report this clearly to him."
Baoshou Fang said: "The Great and Small Yongquan [monks] were much like those who lose their advantage at the southern end and then come back to establish their foundation at the northern end.
At that time, had they waited for [the master] to say, 'The horns are very distinct,' what could they have done? Alas, the rider does not recognize [his own horse].
Why not dismount, step forward, seize the ox by the head, and say: 'Speak quickly! Speak quickly! If he hesitates for a moment, you should immediately strike him across the face with a blow."
Zhang Quehao said, "Do not say that those who ride in a palanquin lack discernment.
When Yongquan went to visit Xuefeng, he escorted him to the carriage door; once Xuefeng had entered the palanquin, Yongquan asked, "This one is carried by four people;
how many carry that one? Xuefeng then sprang up and said, "What are you saying? Yongquan asked again, and Xuefeng replied: [The text provided ends here.]
Xingtao did not understand. Quan said, "If you know, then you know; it is simply that you cannot speak of it.
Yunju Zhuang said, "There is host and guest; there is total gathering and total releasing. You must directly recognize Yongquan.
Xuefeng added, "Even if you are not yet like this, you must by all means avoid driving a stake into empty space."
Chan Master Fu-chuan Hongjian (Fuzhou; fifth generation descendant of Qingyuan and Shishuang): A monk asked, "The place where hook and awl do not reach—please, Master, go there.
Fu-chuan remained silent for a long while. The monk said, "A mechanism as swift as a flash of lightning is in vain for one who stands in thought.
Fu-chuan said, "Try to utter a phrase that transcends the ordinary. The monk stepped forward three paces and then withdrew. Fu-chuan said, "This is a phrase that transcends the ordinary. Immediately—
"How is it with this matter now? The monk brushed his sleeves and went out. Chuan said, "This monk is a man of Tianjin Bridge.

Zhaojue Qin said, "This monk is pure gold and uncut jade; Chuan opened wide the great furnace, and after a hundred smeltings and a thousand refinements, he forged him into a single Vajra-king sword. Do you understand? He is also a man of Tianjin Bridge."
Han: Look directly at the southernmost star of the Big Dipper.
Regarding the story of Fushan: A monk asked, "What is a lion cub? Fushan said, "A fine roar. The monk clapped his hands and said, "A fine hand! A fine hand!
Fushan said, "Under the clear blue sky and bright sun, you have been bewitched by a ghost. The monk made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat.
Chuanbian struck him. The monk said, "The donkey’s business is not yet over when the horse’s business arrives. Chuanbian said, "Truly, you are a master.
The monk shook his sleeves and departed. Chuanbian said, "To use a bowl to hold water and compare it to the great ocean."
Yingshan Yun said: "Had it not been for the efficacious talisman on the back of Fushan’s arm, he would have nearly been robbed by this monk.
Chan Master Yuan'an of Luopu in Lizhou (a successor of the fifth-generation master Jiashan) built a hermitage at Jiashan, yet he did not visit him for years.
Jiashan then composed a letter and sent a monk to inquire after him. Upon receiving it, Luopu sat down immediately; extending his hand, he asked, "Is there anything more?"
The monk had no reply. Baofu struck him and said, "Go back and report this to the Abbot.
When the monk returned and reported it to Mount Yunyan, Yunyan said, "If that monk opens the letter, he will surely come within three days; if he does not open the letter, this man cannot be saved."
Three days later, Baofu arrived. Seeing Jia Shan, he did not prostrate but stood facing him with his hands joined at the chest.
Jia Shan said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix's lair is not of its kind; get out! Baofu replied, "I have come from afar to seek the Master's teaching; please grant me an audience."
Mount Shishuang said, "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*; here there is no old monk. Pufu then shouted.
Shishuang said, "Stop, stop! Do not be so hasty and reckless. The clouds and moon are the same; the streams and mountains are each different.

It may well be that you, *śrāmaṇera*, can cut off the tongues of all people under heaven, but how will you make a tongueless person speak? Pufu paused in thought. Shishuang then struck him. Because of this, Pufu...
Now, humbly receiving [these words], Xinghua Changjiang said, "If you only know how to become a Buddha, do not worry about sentient beings.
Xuedou Chongxian said, "This fellow is pitiable and tragic; he has rendered Linji useless. Since he [regards] clouds and moon..."
"It is the same. My mountain streams and peaks are each distinct. Why do you say that a tongueless person cannot understand speech?
With these words, he struck his own mouth with his sitting mat. Had Jia Shan been a man who knew the way, he certainly would have prepared for this under the bright window.
The Fifth Patriarch Jie cited the words of Luopu, saying: "Let us further discuss the principle," and then he went out.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Although Xuedou is like drawing a bow after the thief has fled, he nonetheless clears the wrong done to Linji.
However, if one examines this closely, only half of the command has been carried out; had he truly taken up the Eye of the True Dharma..."
He waited for him to say, "How can one teach a tongueless person to speak? and immediately overturned the meditation seat, shouting to disperse the assembly.
What more is there to wait for? To arrange matters beneath a bright window—scratch it up and go!

Even if one’s mechanism is like a flash of lightning, one’s eyes like shooting stars, and one’s eloquence flows like a cascading river, one will still find no place to set foot or hand. But tell me: what do you say?
"Wherein lies the error? He then said, "Perilous!

Dongshan Fu remarked, "At that time, although Lu Pu had no words with which to respond and no principles with which to defend himself, his lack of knowledge was like that of Goujian, who ultimately succeeded by sleeping on thorns and tasting gall."
Luo Pu ascended the hall and said, "Today Sun Bin is closing his shop. Let any diviner come forward!
At that time, a monk stepped out and said, "I request a divination from the Master. Luo Pu said, "Your father is dead. The monk was left speechless.
Fayan Yi clapped his hands three times in succession.

Jingshan Daokai said, "This monk has lost his fortune; he has killed his own father. Furthermore, that other person clapping his hands—truly one knows that calamity does not travel alone, nor does blessing arrive in pairs.
Yet Luopu was skilled at divining, and Fayan was skilled at judging; they were like father and son.
Reflect carefully. The auspicious and inauspicious signs of the hexagrams are both revealed simultaneously by the two elders.
Since you have drawn the hexagram *Fuengding* (Fire over Wind), why do you judge it to be *Dihuo Mingyi* (Earth over Fire)? Yunmen would not say so; he suddenly took up his staff and said:
"Under Sun Bin, the father died. He knocks three times and says: "Do you understand? It belongs internally to the Palace of艮 (Gen).
Seeking again for the external image," he knocks another three times and says: "The thousand spirits and ten thousand souls, the myriad saints and a thousand spirits—do not follow human sentiment.
He knocks once more and says: "Good and ill are determined by the hexagram."
Tianning Qisong said: "Luopu says, 'Your father is dead,' and he has blocked his tongue. Miaoxi has grown teeth upon teeth and horns upon horns;
he prattles recklessly of good and ill fortune and forcibly asserts right and wrong, having at once thrown the sixty-four hexagrams into total disorder."
Tiantong Muan said: "The Elder Dahui was mistaken in his naming. One must know that this monk precisely brought blessing out of calamity;
it is only a pity that he did not understand, taking celebration for an omen of good fortune.
Among the dragons and elephants under the gate of the Benevolent One, there must certainly be someone with exceptional merit who can provide a turning word for this monk."
Jin-su Yuan said: "Luopo opened a great divination shop where he was skilled at determining good and bad fortune.
It is a pity that the monk did not return the divination fee, thereby causing bystanders to clap their hands in derision. Here today, it is not so. Sun Bin has packed up his shop and left;
if there is a diviner who comes forward, suddenly a filial son might emerge and say, 'I ask the Master for a divination. Only—"
He said to him, "Your father is alive. O assembly, his father has already died; why then did he say he was alive?
Have you not heard that for seventy-one years his fame resounded throughout the district, and the reputation of this virtuous man remains as enduring as the high mountains and long rivers?
Luo Pu went to consult with Muping regarding the question: "Before a single bubble has arisen, how does one discern the course of the water?
Pu said: "Shift the boat to learn the water's course; raise the oar to distinguish the waves. Muping did not find this satisfactory and went to consult with Panlong. He asked:
"Before a single bubble has arisen, how does one discern the course of the water? Long said: "Shift the boat and you do not need to distinguish the water; raise [the oar]..."
Zhao was immediately lost in the current. Ping entered through awakening from this.
Yunfeng Yue said, "If Muping had understood beneath Luopo’s words, he would still have been somewhat superior;
it is a pity that he was drowned in the stagnant water of Panlong. Later, someone asked, "What is Muping? He replied: [He remained silent.]

He said, "No need for the axe or hatchet. Indeed, it is right here. All you Zen adepts, whenever one speaks words that transcend the mundane, one must distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, and discern the true from the false; only then can one possess even a fraction of the eye's sinews.
Nevertheless, even so, this is like drawing a bow after the thief has already fled.
Gao Feng said, "Had it not been for Master Yue, he would have been deceived by him. Even so, tell me:
where does the confusion of Panlong lie? Moving the boat, one does not change the water; yet lifting the oars, one loses the source."

Tiantong Muan said: "This karmic occasion is much like the story of the Old Monkey Lord distributing chestnuts (*mǔ*). He announced, 'In the morning three, in the evening four,' and all the monkeys were angry.

He then said, 'Then let it be four in the morning and three in the evening,' and all the monkeys were pleased. While the name and the substance did not diminish at all, their joy and anger were nonetheless aroused;
this is certainly established. How much more so when the true teaching is not erroneous, yet the distinction between delusion and enlightenment is so profound!"
"Furthermore, you worthy ones: have you ever been able to discern this clearly? Come forward and communicate some news.
Otherwise, it will be like shooting at a tiger without hitting it—merely exhausting one's arrows in vain. After a long silence, he said, "Study! (or "Enter!").
Baoneng Xiu said: "When these two great elders answered in such a manner, tell me, was there any distinction between them or not?
If you say there was no distinction, why could one cause people to attain enlightenment while the other could not?

If you say there was a distinction, where does that distinction lie? *Poke!* "Once you have reached the shore, cease contending over the raft; once you have returned home, stop searching for the house."
He asked Chenggong about this.

Gounan said, "Though answering in such a manner may coincide with the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching, if it were before even a single bubble had arisen, I would dare say you have not yet reached it.
If someone were to ask me today, 'Before a single bubble has arisen...'"
How was the course of the water discerned before this? To him he said: "The clear lake is as level as a mirror; it does not obstruct coming and going.
When a monk asked Luopu, "What is it like when a student intends to return home? Luopu said: "The house is ruined and the people are gone, my son."
"To where do you return? He replied, "If that is so, then I shall not return. Pufu said, "The remaining snow before the courtyard melts under the sun;
who will sweep away the red dust within the room? Thereupon, he spoke a verse: "Resolute in my intent, I return to my home, Boarding a boat to drift upon the Five Lakes.
Raising the oar, the stars and moon vanish; Pausing the sweeps, the sun stands solitary. Unmooring, I leave the shore of the heterodox; Setting sail, I emerge from the orthodox."
The Path: Having arrived home, one’s worldly possessions are utterly exhausted; thus, one avoids being a fool within the house.
Tianqi Rui said: "This monk has been solitary and exposed for kalpas, which is why he remains mindful of it moment by moment.

Although Luopo’s [fortress] has melted away like ice and collapsed like tiles, there is still fear that a jade tower might be rebuilt—escaping the cage on the outside while maintaining the business within."
I cannot help but offer one more word. Why? "Where the wild geese fly not, people are dragged by profit and fame.

Once, when a servant said, "Master Zhao composed the Four Treatises; they are truly extraordinary," Luopu replied, "Master Zhao was indeed extraordinary, yet he did not see the Patriarch. The servant had no response.
Qingliang Qin said, "Where did the Master see the Patriarch?
Yunju Xi said, "Where is it that Master Zhao did not see the Patriarch?
Is it because there are so many words? He further asked, "How many words did Master Zhao have?"
Luopu asked Haxi, "Since we parted at Lixi, how many years have passed? Xixi replied, "Master, you still remember events from years past.
Luopu said, "I have heard it said that practitioners of the Way generally forget the passage of time and seasons. Xixi said, [and continued: "..."
"The Abbot’s administrative duties are many; let us wait until we have examined the matter closely," [said Xuefeng]. Baofu said, "If you hit me, you will hit one who understands Chan.
Xuedou said, "I am worthy of it. Baofu said, "The practitioner’s mountain-dwelling affairs are many."
Qinglong said this: "The two elders may indeed be said to have host and guest, and to have gathering and releasing.

But when examined closely, they are both merely airing their own family's disgrace. Today, Bian Shan takes a rope made of tortoise hair, ties it into a single knot, hurls it outside the mountain gate into the Jewel-Bead Pond, and drowns it there. Is there anyone who can save it?
"If there is none, trouble Elder Dongchan to explain it for him.
Luopu asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Jingnan. Luopu said, "There is a person who goes like this;
do you encounter him? The monk said, "I do not encounter him. Luopu said, "Why do you not encounter him? The monk said, "If I were to encounter him, my head would shatter into pieces. Luopu—
He said, "The *ācārya*’s three inches are extremely subtle.
When Yunmen Wenyan saw this monk in Jiangxi, he asked him, "Is there such a saying? The monk replied, "Yes."
Gatekeeper Yunmen said, "Lu Pu retreated three thousand li.
Baoyan Fu said, "This monk’s response was grounded in principle; it would not have been improper to grant him the status of a traveling monk.
Why, then, was he buried alive while still in the hands of Yunmen? If there is anyone who can [respond] to Yunmen...
When [the Master] said, "As for those of the future generations," the monk held up one hand. The mountain monk would then give you a "pumpkin seal.
When Luopu was nearing his end, he addressed the assembly, saying: "I now have a matter to ask you all. If you say this is it—"
To place one’s head upon another’s head. If you say it is not so, then you must cut off your own head to seek life.
The Head Seat said, “The green mountains do not lift their feet; beneath the sun, one does not pick up a lamp. Yunpu asked, “What kind of time is this for making such talk?
At that moment, the Senior Seat Yancong replied, “Aside from these two paths, I ask the Master not to question me further. Yunpu said, “Not yet.”
Pufu said, "Speak further. Yancong said, "My way does not reach its ultimate end. Pufu said, "I do not care whether it reaches its end or not. Yancong said, "Yancong has no attendant;
I am responding directly to the Master. Pufu stopped speaking. In the evening, he summoned Yancong and said, "Dharma brother, your response today was truly inspired.
You have grasped the meaning of the former master. The former master said, 'Right before one's eyes...'"

"The Dharma cannot be sought within the present; it is not a phenomenon of the present. It is not something reached by the ears or eyes. Now tell me, which phrase is the guest? Which phrase is the host?
If you can discern this, I shall entrust you with the patriarch’s bowl. Dayuan Cong said, "I do not understand. Fupu said, "You ought to understand.
Dayuan Cong said, "In truth, I do not understand. Fupu shouted at him and drove him out, saying, "Suffering! Suffering!"
After Luopu had addressed the assembly, on the following day a monk brought up the previous conversation and questioned him again. Luopu said:
"The boat of compassion does not need rowing upon the clear waves; at the Sword Gorge, it is a vain labor to release wooden swans."
Baoci then pressed him, saying: "Tell me, is it that you truly do not understand from above, or is it that you are afraid of seeing the alms-bowl bag sticking to you?
Boshanlai said: "At the time of his passing, he entrusted the seal of transmission to his descendants; such wondrous thought is heaven-made."

Their dispositions are inherently distinct. The Head Seat, Master Yan, possesses a great path for his own emergence; yet, as he delights in the aged, it is difficult to establish a standard through words and phrases.
If one seeks him by following outward traces, one cannot avoid being like someone who studies a map to search for a horse.
*Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School*,
Scroll Twenty-Seven and Scroll Twenty-Eight.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Successor of the Patriarchs at Baiyan in Ancient Hangzhou.
△ Qingwu Luojing Shaoshan Huanyu Chan Master (successor to Jia Shan Hui). Bai Tou went to visit him. Shaoshan said, "Are you not that talkative old man Bai Tou?
Bai Tou replied, "I dare not. Shaoshan asked, "How many mouths do you have? Bai Tou said, "My whole body is [mouths]. Shaoshan—
[The monk] asked, "Where do you usually defecate? He replied, "I defecate in the mouth of Mount Shao. The Mountain Master said, "If there is the mouth of Mount Shao, that is fine;
but if there is no mouth of Mount Shao, where do you defecate? Because [the monk] was speechless, the Mountain Master struck him.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "This talk has fallen into the hands of that master; I grant you thirty blows. He said again, "I took you for a cub of the lion.
And he said further, "Today, Shaoshan has been reduced to ruins and melted ice."
Xuedou Xian said, "I have always harbored doubts about Shao Shan.
Yufan Yu said, "Treading on grass and wounding a snake; stirring up fire and burning one's own body—such people are found everywhere."
Because Chan involves many words, one can only end up stifling them by keeping silent. At Shaoshan, there are no words, so one can only end up "defecating" them away.
Qinghua Yan said: "A white-haired old man has his whole body covered in mouths; he cannot bear Shaoshan’s single act of defecation."
Huìyún said: "Everyone says that because one has many mouths due to aging, one is suddenly seized by the throat so that no breath can escape;

though the entire body is full of this, where has it gone? Even if one could recognize some opportune timing or know how to advance and retreat within the space of an eyelash, Shàoshān deserves thirty blows himself."
Baiyan Fu said: "This talkative monk has his reputation for nothing more than empty words. At that time, when he was questioned, how many mouths did he have?
Why did he not step forward and strike him across the face?"
Shao Shan was asked by a monk, "In a place where right and wrong do not reach, is there still a phrase? Shan said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is that phrase?
Shan replied, "A single mass of white clouds does not reveal its ugliness."
Tiantong Jue said: "The entire body shifts and interchanges without touching the dignified; withdrawing from the position, one extracts the essential by way of indirect maneuvering.
Do you see how Shaoshan acted for others? With all his might, he pushed his father toward the inner depths."
Dongshan Fu said: "Shaoshan may truly be said to have struck down the moon of the Chu heavens and plucked away the stars of the Han lands.
To casually utter a single phrase while concealing the tip of the sword so it is not revealed—when examined closely, this has still not been utterly eradicated.
Today, if someone asks Xiansheng, "In a place where right and wrong do not reach, is there still a phrase? he would say directly: "No. If the other...
Why is it that the Way is non-existent? It is simply said: "The autumn waters and the vast sky are one color; the setting clouds and the solitary wild goose fly together.
A monk arrived at Shao Shan to seek instruction; as he rose from his prostrations, Shao Shan said, "A great material for a door, yet you hide your skill.
The monk stood to one side, and Shao Shan said, "You have lost the quality of a ridgepole."
Chengshan Qia said: "The first arrow is still tolerable; the second arrow pierces the person deeply.
When Zun Bunan visited Shaoshan, he happened to find the Master at the foot of the mountain. Zun asked, "Shaoshan Mountain Road—where does it lead?
Shaoshan pointed with his finger and said, "O! It goes toward that dark, verdant spot. Zun stepped forward and seized him.
[Daowu] said, "I have long admired Mount Shao; is it not so? Mount Shao said, "It is indeed so. What business do you have, O *jueli*?
Dazun said, "I intend to pose a question; will you answer me, Master? Mount Shao said, "I see you are no one made of 'golden teeth' (*jin ya*);
how could you know how to draw the bow to shoot Wei Chi? Dazun said, "The phoenix flies straight into the misty heights; he only fears the wild woods."
Zhaozhou asked, "When the drum is spread out before the hall, you may strike it as you wish; try to display your family style like an old monk.
Dongshan said, "A single phrase transcends the thousand sages; the pine and the vine do not equal the full moon.

Zhaozhou said, "Even if you go directly beyond the time of Wei-yin, you are still half a month's journey behind Shao-shan. Dongshan asked, "Where does the fault lie? Zhaozhou said, "This fellow! Dongshan said, "It is you!"
The words of this [master] were known by the people of the time. Cizun said, "If that is so, then true jade is distinct from within the mud; it does not stir up the dust of myriad affairs.
Guishan said, "Under the workshop of Lu Ban, one merely exerts cleverness and ingenuity. Cizun said, "The student acts thus; I do not yet know what your intention, Master, is.
Guishan said, "The Jade Maiden casts her shuttle at night, weaving brocade in the western house. Cizun said, "Is this not it?"
"Is this the style of your house, Master? Sansheng said, "A farmer fashions a jade water clock; it is not the work of a master craftsman.
Dongzhi said, "That is still merely literary expression. What is the true style of your house, Master? Sansheng said, "I cast my body across the universe."
"Who is the one who emerges? Zun remained silent. Deshan then returned with him to the abbot’s quarters. Once the formal greetings were concluded, Deshan suddenly called him forward and said:
"The *dārala* possesses the spirit that pierces the heavens; this old monk possesses the scheme to enter the earth.
The *dārala* swallows the vast ocean across; this old monk carries Mount Sumeru on his back. The *dārala* comes forward brandishing a sword; this old monk thrusts a spear."
[They] waited for one another. [Zhao] Xiangshang said, "The road that goes upward—quickly tell me, quickly tell me! Zongzun said, "A bright mirror stands upon its stand;
I ask the Master to reflect once. Mountan said, "I do not reflect. Zongzun asked, "Why do you not reflect? The Mountain said, "The water is shallow and there are no fish;
it is a vain labor to cast down the hook. Zongzun was speechless. The Mountain then struck him.
Huanglong Xin said, "It would be well to strike such fellows as these! Even if one were to kill hundreds of thousands of them, what fault would there be?
Had they been in Huanglong’s hands at that time, even if his staff had broken, he would not have let them go."
He Shanxun said: "Spreading a net across the heavens to catch the phoenix and snare the dragon; the host carves jade and etches ice, while the guest clusters flowers and weaves brocade.
At the critical moment, there is no yielding; face-to-face, they vie for precedence. With interlocking corners and spiral patterns, they mutually preserve and mutually seize.
Everywhere it is said that a master hand displays its skill within another master hand—is this truly so, or not? If..."

Regarding the perspective of the Wisdom Sun: if Zun Puna can be careful at the beginning and guard against the end, and wait for Shao Shan to point out the path, he will take swift strides and ascend to the inner sanctum.
Rest assured that he will find his place beneath the bright window; not only will he cut off all entanglements, but he will also avoid being caught on their hooks and lines.
Why is this? At the point where a single move has not yet been reached, the entire board is empty and ready for use.
Regarding "Mind," Zhaojue Qin said: "Zun the Padded Robe was like a tiger wearing horns; his majestic wind was chilling.
Yet how could Shaoshan fail to seize the tiger’s head and gather its tail? Thus, he ascended higher step by step, with every sound resonating in harmony. Do you understand?"
As for the resting place of these two elders: a master hand crossing a master hand within the hand;
a red heart piercing a red heart within the heart. Tiantong Hua said: "Master Sishin made a great fuss over nothing.
Little did he know that since Shaoshan suffered the lethal blow of Puna, no one to this day has been able to scrutinize it thoroughly. But tell me, what is this 'strange' matter?"
"Where does the error lie?
Longtang Zhu said, "Bunna, why use such elaborate words? In that dark, deep green expanse," he then prostrated and said, "Today I have personally seen a master.
Even if Shaoshan had a plan to enter the earth, it would still be necessary..."
Treat him as one who "pushes through the grass to catch the wind.
Chengshan Xia said, "Observe these two venerable elders: spear meets sword, and victory or defeat is difficult to distinguish.
This is truly 'when there is spirit, add more spirit; where there is no elegance, there is still elegance. Only it is a pity that..."
The Patriarch’s final stroke—does anyone here have the hand to provide for him?
Zen Master Lingchao of Shanglan in Hongzhou (a successor of Jianyan of Qingyuan) was asked by a monk: "After Sudhana saw Mañjuśrī, why did he nevertheless travel to the South?
Lan said: "Learning relies on entering the chamber; knowing enables one to traverse all quarters. [The monk] asked: "Why did Maitreya..."
Shanglan sent [his disciple] Jian to see Mañjuśrī. Shanglan said, "The Way is vast and boundless; it is inexhaustible when meeting people.
Tianning Qi said, "The most extraordinary among the extraordinary, the most profound among the profound.
To reach the very source of the Dharma, one must be like Shanglan; yet even so, under the gate of the Patriarchs, he has not yet arrived."
Chan Master Weizhu of Niutou in Fuzhou (a dharma successor of Qingyuan Wenzhun and Touzi Datong). A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
Niutou said, "Coarse rice from mountain fields; wild vegetables with plain yellow pickles. The monk asked, "What if a guest of the highest caliber should arrive?
Niutou said, "If you eat, let you eat; if you do not eat, go as you please."
Yingshan Yun said: "Cast from raw iron, his heart and liver ring out with a sharp *ding-dang*.
Chan Master Yantou Quanhuo of Ezhou (a successor of Qingyuan Wude and Deshan Xuanjian) visited Deshan. As soon as he stepped across the threshold, he asked, "Is this ordinary or is it sacred?
Deshan immediately shouted. Yantou bowed. When Dongshan heard a monk recounting this, he said, "If it were not..."
"Master Huo was indeed difficult to handle," [Wuzu] said. Yanguan remarked, "That old fellow from Dongshan does not recognize good from bad; he has wrongly applied these words.
At that time, I would have used one hand to lift him up and the other to press him down."
Xuedou Xian said: "In that case, although the 'grass bows and the wind blows' beneath Deshan’s gate, he still could not shut the mouths of those throughout the world.
At that moment, as soon as [Dongshan] prostrated, Deshan struck him across the spine; this not only decisively cut off Dongshan,"
He has even seized the old fellow *Huo*. Do you understand? General Li has a fine reputation; though he did not attain the rank of Marquis, his life was nonetheless one of leisure.
Langye Jue said: "When Yantou is not questioned by anyone, he is indeed extraordinary; yet as soon as he is confronted by Dongshan’s [punch to the] head..."
With the final stroke of the chisel, it was instantly melted away like ice and crumbled like a fortress.
Nanhua Ying said: "Yantou’s single period of revealing himself was not in vain; that no one praised him was already a slight advantage.
As soon as he was brought to light by Dongshan, he truly caused a stir among the masses. Do you understand? There is none."
Stagnation naturally follows the flow of circumstances; where there is sound, it is mostly due to the arrival of disharmony.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Deshan acted according to his command, yet he obtained only half. Dongshan’s vision reached everywhere, sharing the same wind across a thousand miles.
Yantou was both able to seize the tiger’s head and grasp its tail; he was truly like..."
The author-warrior stands on the battlefield with all seven matters complete; how extraordinary! I dare ask:
where is the place where one hand raises while the other presses down? It is said: "When the dawn has barely broken, there are still travelers on the road."
Jingshan Daowu said: "The fierce tiger does not recognize the pitfall, yet it dies within the pitfall; the dragon does not fear the sword, yet it perishes beneath the sword.

Although Yantou had a way to break through from within the tiger's pitfall and possessed the opportunity to turn back upon the edge of the sword, if one examines this carefully, he still lacked full awakening. Thus it is said.
"Now, is there anyone who can act as a host for Yantou? Come forth and meet Miaoxi!
After a long silence, he let out a shout, clapped his hands once, and said: "In the end, everyone has merely been detained in prison and grown wise."
Jiaochong said, "Do you know where the three great elders have landed? Deshan has cast his entire body down; Dongshan drags through water and mud.
Had it not been for Yantou’s all-penetrating eye and his mechanism beyond the ordinary, how could their high merit and laborious service have been revealed?
But tell me, what is this state of raising with one hand while pressing down with the other? It is the sword that kills."
The "Sword that Brings the Living to Life. Tianning Qi said: "Deshan possessed the hands and feet of one who bites dogs and pigs; Yantou was refined pure gold.
When they met head-on, there was no room for evasion; he traded eight *liang* for his opponent's five *jin*. (Dongshan...)"
"Though he is a master, he can only look on from the sidelines. Why does Miaoxi expend so much effort?
[The Master] picks up his staff, draws a line, and says: 'One.'"
Nantang Yu said, "When the family prospers, filial sons are born; when a state is hegemonic, it possesses strategic ministers.
Xuedou said, "If that were so, then although the 'grass bends and the wind blows' beneath Deshan’s gate, he still could not shut the mouths of the people of the world.
At that time, as soon as [the monk] prostrated, [Deshan] struck him across the spine. This not only completely cut off Deshan [from further discourse], but also firmly seized Huo.
Lao said, "The principle you have articulated is excellent. I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.

Baoen Xiu remarked, "While all quarters claim that Yantou’s 'one lift and one press' was a misstep by Dongshan, they fail to realize that Dongshan’s 'one lift and one press' was even more so. Nevertheless, Yantou’s lifting and pressing..."
"Mountain. This brings forth Dongshan’s "lifting and pressing down. Wansong has exposed it all. Suppose someone were to come forward and prostrate;
why would Wansong let them go instead of striking them? It is because they have no blood beneath their skin.
Yunju Zhuang said: "Deshan was not without the karmic conditions for raising a son; Dongshan was indeed celebrating the feast.
What is it that Yantou does with one hand lifting and one hand pressing down? It is not the hand that shoots the eagle;
it is merely to speak of General Li."
Boshan Lai said: "The question does not reside within the mind; the answer precedes the trigger.
This is what I call entering the gate of Deshan and breaking through the phrase of Yantou; it is vividly a case of two colors and one match.
Although Dongshan’s was a good cause that invited an evil result, who could have known that the son of Yantou was concealing his father’s true nature right within it?
"Drumming it forward for future generations—only by binding these three together as one bundle can it be achieved.
Gu Nanmen said: "Although Xuedou speaks thus, though it is like boring a hole to insert a wedge, he does not realize that Yantou’s lineage has been of noble descent through successive generations.
Had it not been Deshan—who was like gold being matched with gold—it would have been most difficult to respond. Dong... [text fragment]
Shanxiang stood behind him with his hands clasped and said, "If it were not for Master Huo, this would have been difficult to bear.

To falsely accuse another and impose punishment upon them—when examined closely, although these four elders each rely on their own strengths, they all lack the staff within the gate of the patch-robed monks.
Why is this? The green mountains only know how to polish antiquity and the present; the flowing water..."
I have once washed away right and wrong. Suddenly, a man comes forward and says, "Gunan, you too are increasing your ignorance through involvement in idle affairs.
He joins his palms and says, "This mountain monk commits a transgression."
Yuan'an Yu said: "Deshan is the mountain from Jing where jade is hidden; Yantou is the skilled craftsman who cuts the jade.
While they are both exquisite from beginning to end, it was simply inappropriate for him to hold up a single broken thread to measure the extent of the body of the Bodhisattva Wubianshen.
He could not help but be ridiculed by bystanders. But tell me, what was he laughed at?"
"What is it? [The Master] laughed at him, saying, "This is like a noble young gentleman who beats out the *nā* demons while wandering from door to door begging.
Lingyan Chu said: "Yantou only knew how to ride the long wind and break through ten thousand li of waves, yet he did not consider that the Yellow River has no bottom;
Deshan only understood how to drive away Mount Tai and Hua and block the four oceans, yet he did not realize that Black Mountain has roots."
Father and son, father and son, exhaust their strength and energy, yet to this day they have no way to emerge—how laughable!

Furthermore, there are those who, by playing tricks, end up making things worse, inviting ghosts into their own walls, which causes this fellow to stare with wide eyes from within his coffin, intimidating Zhang and scaring Li.
Countless masters of knowledge have appeared in the world since antiquity; each one of them has been like tracing the roots of a plant upon water—empty.
The central painting depicts shadows; though one may endure much hardship and suffering, in the end there is no connection.

Suppose a monk arrives at Lingyan and, upon entering the gate, asks, "Is this ordinary or is it sacred? [Lingyan] simply lets out a cold, mocking laugh, leaving that fellow with sweat pouring down his back.
Xidun Chaoju finished quoting the words of Dahui and asked: "What is the point where there is still a lack of awakening?
It causes all people under heaven to guess east and west at Yantou’s beak, with no day of emergence in sight. Try examining this again;
if you cannot examine it out, I shall prostrate nine times before him. For those who can examine it out, there shall be ninety blows of the staff."
"Even the staff will not be spared.
Yanjiao Le said: "Deqiao deployed a great battle array of dragons and snakes; Dongshan set up a trap for tigers.
Although Yantou had long experienced the fray and was not caught in their snares, he nevertheless covered his ears while stealing the bell. If one were to let him go..."
If one errs, neither side is harmed. But examine it closely: all three are thieves.
Among them, there is one who is the true thief and one who is a mere grass-thief. Now tell me, which one is the true thief and which one is the grass-thief?
Baiyan Fu said: "Deshan occupied the seat of authority in the hall, yet at the end he still lacked one move.
Yantou concealed his sharp edge within the mud; his footing was ultimately unstable, and he must both receive punishment.
As for the old fellow Dongshan, let us set him aside for now—why? Because he has been left for later generations to examine."
Yantou was about to take his leave of Deshan. Deshan asked, "Where will you go? Yantou replied, "I am taking my leave of the Master for a while to go down the mountain.
Deshan asked, "What will you do after this? Yantou said, "I shall not forget the Master. Deshan asked, "On what basis do you say such a thing?
Yantou replied, "Have you not heard that when one's wisdom is equal to the teacher's, it diminishes the teacher's merit by half; if one's wisdom exceeds the teacher's, one transcends him?"
"Only then is it fit for transmission. Deshan said, "So it is, so it is. Guard and uphold this well yourself.
Tiantong Jue remarked, "Deshan usually does not permit even Buddhas or Patriarchs to stand beneath his staff;
yet when this particular moment arrived, he became so doting. Nevertheless, while this was the occasion of raising a child, how could it avoid being scrutinized by later generations?"
[The Master] rebuked him, saying, "I wait for one whose wisdom exceeds that of their teacher before it is fit to be transmitted. He then pulled out his staff and struck him across the back.
Later, when a monk asked Yantou, "What is it like when the three realms arise in competition? Yantou said, "Sit down!
The monk asked, "I do not understand the meaning of your words, Master. Yantou said, "If you could move Mount Lu here, then I would speak to you."
Jingshan Daowu said: "The ancient Buddha Yantou extended his hand from atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff and cast his body into the boiling cauldrons and burning coals;
this was for the sake of his great compassion, and thus he spoke words that descend into the weeds.
Today, if someone were to ask Yunmen, 'What is it like when the three realms arise in competition? I would simply say to him: 'A favorable opportunity is difficult to encounter. I wonder—"
"What is the Master’s intention? [The Master replied: "If you could move Mount Yunmen here, then I would speak to you.
Tianning Qi said: "The three realms arise in competition. Yantou said, 'Sit upon them. When one sees the strange as not strange, the strangeness collapses of its own accord.
Miaoxi said, 'A swift opportunity is hard to encounter; when rowing a boat downstream, apply even more oars and poles. Tian... [text ends]
"Where, then, does the Way reside? Chang’an is very noisy, but my country is at peace. I do not know what you mean, Master.
Wait until I have gone up the mountain to chop wood, and then I shall tell you. These three sections are distinct; they are subsumed under the preceding category.

Dazhu said: "Yantou, the ancient Buddha, answered with a single turning word that was like Mount Tai and Mount Hua suddenly casting down a thousand peaks, or like the vast ocean cutting off all currents.
This was because his Dharma-eye was so brilliant he possessed the hand that can strip away the cataracts [of ignorance].
If someone were to ask Dazhu today, 'What is it like when the three realms arise in competition?'—take care! [He did not speak further. Unfinished.
"Examine the Master’s intention: if you could move Mount Shaowei here, then I would speak to you.
Mei Shan P’ai said, "Although Yan Tou possesses the 'sword that kills,' he lacks the 'sword that gives life.'"
Yantou asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Western Capital. Yantou said, "After Huang Chao passed through, did you manage to recover his sword?
The monk replied, "I recovered it. Yantou leaned forward, thrusting out his neck, and said, "Cut! The monk said, "Your head will fall off! Yantou laughed heartily. Later, the monk went to Xuefeng.
Xuefeng asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Yantou. Xuefeng said, "Yantou has..."
"What words? The monk recounted the previous conversation. Xuefeng then struck him thirty blows and drove him out.
Guizong Zhe said: "This monk had once recovered a sword after Huang Chao passed by, yet he went to deploy it at Yantou's place.
When he reached Xuefeng, however, not even a trace of its sharp edge was revealed. Why? Because Yantou laughed heartily."
With a single shout, heaven and earth suddenly grew dark and the four quarters fell silent. Had it not been for Xuefeng, the world would have nearly sunk into oblivion.
Is this not what is called "the sword that kills and the sword that gives life"?
Chengtianzong said: "What a pity for such a fellow! He has only learned the way of victory and defeat, yet he does not realize that victory and defeat are the causes of birth and extinction.
Had I seen him at that time, I would have simply told him, 'A true master, a true master!
and let him carry his wooden board for the rest of his life."
Baoguang said: "Since this monk has already seized the sword, why is the authority over life and death entirely in the hands of another?
At that moment, while he was stretching his neck forward, why did you not say, 'The grass-robbers are utterly defeated'?
Had he hesitated, you could have laughed heartily and departed; not only would you have choked off Yantou’s throat, but even..."
Xuefeng also merely met him with an equal display. Is there anyone like this today? After a long silence, he said:
"I almost let the prisoner go free and allowed my own wisdom to grow.
Bayan Fu said: "What a pity that this monk possesses a sword but does not know how to use it; every movement brings him into contact with the blade and wounds his hand."
At that time, he was merely waiting for him to stretch out his neck. Why not say, "Those who surrender are not executed"?
When Yantou reached this point, not only did he have no skill left to employ; even the old man Xianggu would have had to stand by and cheer.
Yantou once asked Shishuang while they were idly strolling at Luoshan: "What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Shishuang replied: "You must become cold ashes and withered wood;
you must go where a single thought lasts ten thousand years; you must go where the casket and its lid correspond; you must go where there is pure clarity, utterly free of a single speck."

Mount Shanjian did not reach accord [with his teacher]. He then went to Yantou and asked, "What is it like when arising and ceasing do not cease? Yantou let out a shout and said, "Who is it that arises and ceases?
At this, Shanjian had an awakening.
Baoneng Xiuyun said, "If it were Wansong, he would have finished drinking and left it at that.
Jingshan Xiuyun said, "To kill a man, one must use a sword for killing.
Zifufu said, "The great ocean does not harbor a corpse; the point of a needle does not harbor a mosquito. These two great elders—
A thousand ages of upholding [the Dharma]. Two by two, they illuminate one another. Nowadays, people fall over on the words and phrases;
who has the living eye, and who lacks the living eye? That is why they do not accord with it, and that is why they cut it short.
Not only do they fail to recognize these two great elders, but they do not even recognize Luoshan.
Baiyan Fu said: "One must surely undergo a great death; only then will one behold the spring light upon withered wood. Take up the study of Shishuang;
