Jianfu Can said, "The old man Xuefeng has already wasted salt and spoiled sauce.
These days, when monks enter the gate, ascend the hall, and meet the master, they pointlessly clasp their hands over their chests and further seek instructions."
This is a point of entry. Chewing bitter ginseng root with the roots still intact is not yet truly bitter.
Wushi said: "Xuefeng spread a net across the heavens to strike at the phoenix and ensnare the dragon;
Baofu and Ehu have, for no reason, crashed into its midst and remain unable to emerge to this day. Is there anyone now who can penetrate it?
"Is this the all-pervading net? He planted his staff and said, "Sparse, yet nothing slips through.
Yuyan Meng said, "I ask the Master to go down to the Nirvana Hall."
Gushan Puyun said: "O assembly! When Ehu returned to his quarters and Baofu entered the Sangha Hall, where is the place of their meeting?
After a long silence, he said: 'Two lacquer buckets rub against each other; their cold light pierces through ten thousand layers of mountains.'"
Dajue Sheng said, "The great and small Xuefengs have spent years [in the world] without virtue; how many people have they humiliated and suppressed!
Dajue is not like this: at Wangzhou Pavilion, there is no need to meet; at Wushidian, there is no need to meet."
"Even before the Sangha hall, there is no need to meet one another. Why? The vast universe contains countless people;
which man among them is not a true hero? He let out a shout and descended from his seat.

Xuefeng was once asked by a monk, "It is said that those who hear the voice [śrāvakas] see their nature like seeing the moon at night, while those who are bodhisattvas see their nature like seeing the sun by day.
I wonder, Master, how do you see your nature? Xuefeng struck him three times with his staff. The monk then went on to ask Yantou about it.
He struck his head three times with his palm.
Xuedou Xian said: "To prescribe medicine according to the illness, I have given him three blows. But if one were to act strictly according to the rule, how many blows should he receive?"
Tiantong Jue, having finished citing Xuedou’s words, said: "Xuedou, for a time, sought to catch the wind of his own cleverness.
Often, later generations have taken this as a formal rule to be followed; they fail to realize that Xuefeng and Yantou were men who possessed no fixed attachments or compulsions."
Nantang Yu said: "The three before and the three after—administering medicine according to the illness and acting in accordance with the command. There is a separate point here.
He looked at his attendant and said, "Tell me, which one is that point? As the attendant hesitated, he struck him out.
Yuan-an Meng said: "Xuefeng struck; Yantou struck. If one speaks of seeing one's nature, it is as if separated by a fine gauze. Bao-shou Xin said:
"This monk is much like one who wields an axe at the gate of a master carpenter; how can one blame the two elders for their fierce and pungent tongs and hammers?
Yet, when examined closely, they both amount to nothing more than a single fragment. But tell me, where is that fragment?
At his very first thrust, try to speak!
Baeryam Pu said: "This monk has a vanguard, yet lacks a rearguard;
he brings disgrace upon Xuefeng and Yantou, who can do no more than serve as a mere 'story of equal heads. Is there anyone here who can take his place? The monk stepped forward.
"A single word—'Ma. I, this mountain monk, shall settle the case for you.
Xuefeng ascended the seat and called to the assembly, saying, "Look, look at the east! He said again, "Look, look at the west!
"If you wish to understand," he added, picking up his staff and throwing it down, "understand it right here!"
Lingyan Zuoyun said: "The ancient Buddha Xuefeng cut open his own belly to reveal his heart; he has bestowed the ancestral heritage from the past upon you all with complete sincerity.
If there is anyone among you who is a capable heir, you should take it up and carry it on your own shoulders.
If there is none, this mountain monk will not hesitate to clear it up for you once more. To the east, the jade tree supports..."
"O Celestial One! To the west, green shade covers the earth. He casts down his staff; the four stillnesses are clearly distinct.

To realize it within this very place is entirely a single accord. If a person here is bold and clear, they should properly bind their belly with three strips of bamboo and take up a worn-out axe to plow and sow wherever they go. Do you understand? The Iron Ox."
The spring light fills the place where the lion roars; when the wooden horse neighs, the night river is level. I know not where the staff has gone;
a pair of autumn geese alight upon the sandy islet.
When Xuefeng was serving as the head cook at Dongshan, he was washing rice. Dongshan asked, "Are you washing away the sand to keep the rice, or washing away the rice to keep the sand?
Xuefeng replied, "I wash away the sand and rice all at once. Dongshan asked, "Then what will the assembly eat?
Xuefeng then overturned the basin. Dongshan said, "By your karmic conditions, you should have been at Deshan."
Langye Jue said, "Xuefeng acting in this way is much like casting away a sweet peach tree to climb the mountain and pick sour pears.
Touzi Qian said, "Dongshan speaking in this manner—what kind of principle is that? Although heaven and earth are of one color,"
Alas, how can one overcome such lofty mountains and vast waters? Thus the Wild Man said: "If one's effort does not reach its limit, there will be no squareness or roundness;
if languages do not meet, they are not kin. To remove the sand while rinsing rice, and to remove the rice while rinsing sand—this is the speech uttered on behalf of the Peak:
"The shadowless ever-living cassia frequently bears fruit after withstanding the frost. What do you all eat? The Golden Phoenix.
Gathering fragrances, they never finish carrying them; the jade chicks eat the flower buds, and the leaves grow ever new.
Tiantong Jue said: "Xuefeng climbs higher with every step, unaware that the heel of his straw sandals has snapped.

If one can truly navigate the interplay of the primary and secondary (zhengbian) through simultaneous striking and singing, then naturally speech and spirit will harmonize and father and son will meet. But tell me: [what is it like?]
Dongshan refused Xuefeng; where did his intention lie? "When ten thousand miles are cloudless, the heavens have a fault;
when the green pool is like a mirror, the moon finds it hard to come.
Baolin Xiu said: "In my place, it is not so. To sift the sand to get the rice, and to sift the rice to remove the sand."
Turning toward the Way, one washes away all dust and sand until not a single grain remains. What does the assembly eat? For the congee, they scoop with a wooden ladle;
for the rice, they fish it out with a strainer.
Xuedou Zong said: "Straight timber does not harbor phoenixes; the golden needle has already embroidered the mandarin ducks.
Were it not for the Old Man of Xinfeng, one would see the ice melt and the walls crumble."
Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School, Volume Twenty-Eight;
Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School, Volume Twenty-Nine.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Successor of the Patriarchs at Baiyan in Ancient Hangzhou.
△ On the occasion of ascending the hall at Wuxue Peak, Qing said: "The entire earth, when gathered up, is as small as a grain of millet. I cast it before you.
You lacquer buckets do not understand; beat the drum for a communal viewing!"
Changqing Ling asked Yunmen, "When Xuefeng spoke in that way, was there anything therein that could not be brought forth?
Yunmen said, "There was. Changqing asked, "How so? Yunmen said, "One must not take it all as the interpretation of a wild fox spirit," and added, "The mess is no small matter."
Yunfeng Yue said, "The superior is already insufficient; I shall further entangle you with complications. Suddenly seizing his staff, he said, "Do you see Xuefeng?
*Duh!* Lately the royal decree has become somewhat strict; no more shoving aside others to seize the market."
Taisuī Zhe said, "I shall add more mud upon the earth for you all. Raising his staff, he said, "Look!
Look! The old man Xuefeng has just relieved himself right before your eyes. Tsk! Why do you not even perceive the stench of the excrement?"
Zhihai Yi said: "I am ashamed of Old Xuefeng; both are merely playing with the spirit. Among them, he plays it well.
Nevertheless, even so, better things than this would have been."
Zhaojue Qin said: "To sever the celestial cords and establish the terrestrial chronicles is not enough to be called extraordinary;
to cleave Mount Taihua and divert the Yellow River is likewise no mark of a nimble hand.

If you can see through this point, you may then cast forth the bright pearl from the lair of the black dragon and spray the fragrant air of the sandalwood forest—would that not be a joy? Today, this mountain monk does not avoid the mud."
He lets out a stream of water. Then, picking up his staff, he says, “Do you see Xuefeng? He strikes it once and says, “Zha!
Lingyin Yue said, “The Iron Ox of Shanfu trembles with fear; the Great Elephant of Jiazhou breaks into a sweat all over.”
[The Master] said, "Flow! Now tell me, how thick is the skin on the face of Old Man Xianggu?
Wushi said, "Great or small, Xuefeng throws out three and lets go of two; when will there ever be an end to this? Xingguo, however, was not like this:
he would take the entire great earth and place it upon everyone’s eyebrows and eyelashes, and then sleep—sleeping together with them.
When rising, they rise together; when walking, they walk together; when sitting, they sit together. Do you see this with intimacy? Striking the whisk, he said:
"The earthworm sucks dry the four great oceans; a lotus fiber moves the five Sumeru mountains."
Xuefeng was once asked by Sansheng, "What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? Xuefeng replied, "Wait until you have emerged from the net, and I will tell you.
Sansheng said, "A teacher of fifteen hundred people and yet you do not even recognize the point of the question!
Xuefeng said, "The old monk’s administrative duties are too numerous."
Baoning Zhan said, "They were not enough in their striving; they were too generous in their yielding.
Xuedou Xian said, "It is a pity he let them off; he should have given him thirty blows. Not even a single blow should have been spared."
Truly, such masters are rarely encountered.
Chengtian Zong said: "To spread the all-encompassing net, one must be Xuefeng; to penetrate deeply into the tiger’s den, one must be Sansheng.
Some fellows say that Xuefeng was inside the net and Sansheng was outside the net. Alas, alas! How tragic!
This deeply honors the ancients. Were it not for these two masters, one could not traverse the world with such ease.
Guizong Zhe said: "Sansheng may be called the Ten-Thousand-Fathom Dragon Gate; he is accustomed to being a guest.
Xuefeng is much like the gate of Mengchang opening wide; how could he fear guests of high standing?"
Baofeng Wen said: "How magnificent! How magnificent! How joyful! How joyful! It is just like a hawk; do not startle it. Baoning, however, was not like this. He asked:
"What does a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? Wait until you have emerged from the net, and then I will tell you.
You do not even recognize the teaching topic (huatou) of the Great Master of fifteen hundred disciples."
He then seized his staff and struck out through the three gates, saying again, "This too is a state of great joy!
It is just like a tiger; do not provoke it! "Zen practitioners, tell me: is Baoning’s state of joy superior to that of Sansheng?
Is there anyone here who possesses such joy? Come forth and let us settle this. After a long silence, he said, "I take him by the hand and pull, but he will not enter."
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "One person is as coarse as a mountain; another is as fine as rice flour.
Although their coarseness and fineness differ, when weighed on a scale, their weight is exactly equal. Today, Jingshan gives you a true report:
all of you must take care not to probe the tortoise or strike the tiles."
The *Tianbao Shu* says: "The Three Sages are much like a venomous dragon churning the sea, with white waves surging to the heavens.
Had it not been for Xuefeng’s habitual entry into the great surges, how could the pearl of the black dragon have been held in his grasp? He strikes the whisk once.
Baoneng Xiu said: "The Three Sages set up this question; they might as well have pulled out a sticky bowl from within a thicket of brambles.
Yet, how could they have known that the old man Xuefeng was already thirty paces away?
No matter how much you struggle to disentangle yourself or take another path, you can never escape the net of Xuefeng’s Dharma."
Haizhou Ciyun said: "If I were Xuefeng, seeing Sansheng say 'A golden fish that has passed through the net,' what would I take as food?
I would strike him across the face with my palm and say: 'I take this as my food.'"
Xiaoyan Bao said: "The old fellow Xuefeng left his head behind while trailing his tail. He did not even recognize the critical phrase (huatou) of a spiritual teacher for fifteen hundred people.
However, if one simply says, 'If it were like this, then I would not have been in vain as a descendant of Linji,' [that would suffice]."
Waiting for his eyes to steady and move, [the Master] struck him across the spine.
Boshan Lai said: "The blows could not open him; the screens could not fold him down.
Each possessed the art of invisibility, much like burying troops while seeking battle. Nevertheless, with such a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net, after all, by what means..."
[He] asked about Master Ding of Gaoyou.
Gounan said, "The old fellow Xuefeng was accustomed to taking advantage of the situation. Xuedou deserved thirty blows, but he simply struck too late.
Someone asked Gounan, "What does a golden fish that has passed through the net eat? [Gounan] replied with a shout.
He then struck him, saying, "One blow shall strike you dead! Even if you were a master of the Way, where else could you possibly peck and snatch?
Yuyan Meng said: "Sansheng was the son of a military family; his application of the Dharma certainly possessed a family tradition.
Xuefeng was a descendant of Bo Shang (Mencius); he was skilled at judging men. One was a sea-eagle accustomed to striking down swans; the other..."
This one is like the Great Golden-Winged Garuda, who cleaves the sea to seize and swallow the dragon directly. Nevertheless, it is easy to be Xuefeng;

it is difficult to be Sansheng. He must pass through the forest of swords and spears without a single hair being harmed, and come from amidst a cluster of a hundred flowers without being stained by a single petal—only then is he a true master.
Qixia Chengyun said: "Although Xuefeng’s methods of granting and revoking are worth observing, he nonetheless lacks the marks of a great man.
If someone were to ask me of Sheshan, 'What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? I would simply say, 'A dead cat's head.
If he were to further remark, 'You do not even recognize the teaching topic of the one thousand five hundred virtuous friends,' I would tell him, 'Do not take offense.'"
With humble reverence, may you still partake. Now tell me, how far apart are you from the ancients?
Baozhang said, "Appearing and disappearing atop the grass-heads costs no luster. Xuefeng was indeed a master;
with eyes fixed and head held high, he displayed his fins and stirred his scales. Was not Sansheng also a skilled hand? But this mountain monk is not so.
"What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? [The Master] struck him with his staff as he spoke. "If you move or stir further, I shall strike you out with my staff.
Even if the spirit and momentum of Three Sages were to soar to the heavens, they would still only have their share of baring their gills.
Furong Daokai said: "The three sages' modes of conduct were extraordinary. Xuefeng was habitually adept at seizing the opportune moment;
one push and one press, his functional activity was always in play. One release and one gathering, the point of the arrow struck the mark.
Like a dragon leaping from the vast ocean or a crane dancing in the crimson sky, though each displayed their own strategy, when scrutinized, it was merely planting thorns on level ground."
In the forest, even to this day, it has not yet been completely cleared away. Is there anyone present now who can take up the task of clearing it?
Sanxing and Xuefeng are beneath your very feet. If you do not have them, do not say you are a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net;
you will not even qualify as a loach in the mud.
The *Dānapāramitā Sūtra* says: "Because one rows with the arms, the wind is right and the sails are unfurled. This is the very path traveled by patch-robed monks;
how could it be like an old Mahākaṣṭha, hunched up by the bells and chimes in an ancient temple, standing ten thousand fathoms tall against clay gods and earthen Buddhas?
Fifteen hundred mangy dogs gnaw at a withered stump; here and there, a few sharp-eyed hawks circle.
A cunning hare, yet a leopard carries such majesty that its dark form may be relied upon; a dragon gains the clouds so its transformations may become divine.

When a true spiritual friend encounters such a person, they do not realize it is a case of "voices responding and spirits seeking one another," but instead spend their whole day facing long rows of beds, striking staffs and shouting at yellow-mouthed śrāmaṇeras, mistaking the cry of a crane for the song of a warbler. This too is the fate of the aspiring practitioner.
How great is this pain! Nevertheless, even so, this mountain monk still has thirty staffs with which to strike San-sheng.
Why? When we are hungry, we shall seek food from Xie Renzu; there is no need for the rice of Tao Hunu.
Once, as a monk was prostrating, Xuefeng struck him five times with his staff. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie?
Xuefeng struck him another five times and shouted, "Begone!"
Xuedou Xian said: "I have never engaged in such verbal entanglements with others. The first five blows were like the sun shining upon the world;
the latter five blows were like clouds rising to bring rain. If you could grasp this, I would also give you five blows."

Taisu Xiu said: "This monk has struck his forehead against the ground; his transgressions fill the heavens. Xuefeng was lenient in forgiving him, yet he still does not recognize the nature of his offense.
A second offense will not be tolerated. To further say, 'The sun shines upon heaven, clouds rise and bring rain,' is to confuse later generations.
Why? Having once suffered the bitterness of snow and frost, one is startled even by the falling of willow blossoms."
Dongchan Guanzhen said: "The nature is empty from the beginning; its nature is straightforward. It is not like Xuedou, who deceives people.
When Xuefeng struck the monk with five blows before he bowed, the monk who was struck with five blows afterward had committed no fault.
Everyone, tell me: is it right or wrong? If you say it is right, what need is there for your eyes?"
Baoning Moshan said: "The former is the sword that kills; the latter is the blade that gives life. Alas, these monks do not realize it.
If they were to realize it, they would have a share in Xuefeng’s eating of the punch."
The Epitaph for Xuefeng’s Stupa says: "The brothers stand across the cross; Their hearts are one in a single rite. The local lord is called Songshan; The egg-shaped stupa is named Nandī.
There is also the Hújiā melody— You all must know this thoroughly! I sing the bellowing of the earthen ox."

"You have joined with a wooden horse to neigh; simply wait for the fifth or sixth month. When the ice-flakes fill the long streets and the fire is extinguished for lack of fuel, this secret chamber will rot like mud."
Cuiyan Zhi said: "The imperial decree is issued within the realm; the general’s command extends beyond the frontier. Before reaching the village, Xuefeng has not yet arrived;
after passing the inn, he has not yet encountered it. If it were Cuiyan, I would simply mix mud with water and let it be so.
Thirty years from now, do not be negligent!"

A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? Xuefeng said, "Staring with wide-open eyes, one cannot see the bottom. The monk asked, "And what of those who drink from it?
Xuefeng said, "It does not enter through the mouth. The monk related this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "It cannot enter through the nostrils either.

The monk then asked Zhaozhou, "What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? Zhaozhou said, "Bitter. "And what of those who drink from it? [Zhaozhou said,] "It enters through the pores of the skin."
"What? Zhaozhou replied, "Dead. Upon hearing this, Xuefeng said, "Zhaozhou is an ancient Buddha," and he then prostrated from afar. From that time on, he no longer answered questions.
Xuedou Xian said, "Everyone in the assembly says that Xuefeng did not answer the monk’s question about the head;

therefore, Zhaozhou refused to acknowledge him. To interpret the matter in such a way is a profound insult to the ancients. Xuedou does not think so; he would rather 'sever nails and cut through bolts.'"
Iron-Face Benfen was a master of the school; it is difficult for anyone to surpass him in bringing the low to level with the high.
Jianfu Hui said, "O worthy ones, how do you understand the principle of 'not answering'?
While it is not that there is no praise for Zhaozhou, do you know where a single flaw has appeared in Zhaozhou’s jade? If anyone examines this closely..."
It is achieved. As for the story of Xiangru not deceiving the Lord of Qin, Tiantong Jue said:
"To uphold and establish the School of the Patriarchs, one must rely on a master craftsman.
Xuefeng possessed the mind and body of a teacher of fifteen hundred people; Zhaozhou employed the skillful means of one hundred and fifty years. How extraordinary!"
How strange! Nowadays, within the assembly, people settle matters based merely on words and engage in chaotic praise and blame, which deeply wrongs the ancients.

Thus, while there are naturally those who understand when clapping hands and singing songs together at a banquet, those who can engrave these truths into their bones and hearts and encounter clear discernment are rare indeed.
Jingshan Daokai said: "Xuefeng’s refusal to engage in dialogue has left the people of the world in a state of doubt.
Zhaozhou said, 'Suffering: a flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech. If it were Miaoxi, however, it would not be so. As for the ancient stream and cold spring—how about them?"
Reaching the river, he supports the oars and sweeps the rudders; emerging from the peaks, he brings salvation to the people’s fields. As for those who drink—how so? It cools the inner organs.
These words contain two points of defeat (*paryāya-nigraha*); if one can discern them, I grant you the eye of study.
Fushan said, "If Zhaozhou had not encountered that monk, how could he have met Xuefeng?
If Xuefeng had not received Zhaozhou, how could he have brought this story to its full completion? Great Master Xuedou has driven his head into a glue pot!"
Yuwang said by way of expediency: "One person follows the waves; one person cuts off the flow of all streams.
Examining this closely, both are lacking in understanding. If someone were to ask Yuwang today, "What is it like when the cold spring flows in the ancient ravine?
you must personally see Xuefeng. As for "How is it for those who drink from it?", go ask Zhaozhou.
Ruiguan Yun said: "This monk missed it face-to-face, causing Xuefeng and Zhaozhou to roll into the weeds.
Xuedou and Fushan may indeed be called those who speak deeply of principle and support one another, yet they can only be indirect;
they cannot be direct. Today, if someone asks: 'What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? [The answer is: Ants."
"The Son holds up the pillar of heaven. As for "How is it for one who drinks?"—it is like a lotus fiber hanging Mount Sumeru. Tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different?
Nantang Yu said: "Xuefeng’s attempt to answer in that way did not realize he was scratching at Zhaozhou’s itch. Zhao...
Zhuzhen could not restrain himself; he unwittingly struck at Xuefeng’s most sensitive spot. Where it hurts, there is an itch; where it itches, there is pain.
All at once, this has been transferred onto Xuedou’s own person. But tell me, has this monk ever even dreamed of it?
Wushan Dao said, "Xuefeng has the sword that gives life, but lacks the blade that kills;
Zhaozhou has the blade that kills, but lacks the sword that gives life. This monk is thus brought to ruin: he cannot live, yet he cannot die."
Shixi was not like this. When someone suddenly asked, "What is it like when the ancient ravine contains cold spring water? he simply replied, "Ten thousand miles of azure clouds have gathered;
a single orb of bright moon shines clear. When asked, "How is it for those who drink from it? he said, "The whale swallows the ocean waters until they are exhausted, revealing the coral branches."
Gunan said: "Xuefeng did not answer the question—how admirable! He did not rely on his own excellence.
Zhaozhou said, 'It is bitterly cold,' which is entirely beautiful yet not entirely perfect. Gunan was not like this. When asked, 'What is it like when the cold spring flows in the ancient ravine?
he replied, 'Where did you, Reverend, receive such news? As the other was about to ask further, he struck him with a staff."
He went out. It was not merely that this monk did not turn his heels toward the cold spring by the ancient ravine;
rather, he was made to go forth with a distinct, penetrating, and vital livelihood.
Tongxuanchi said: "This monk bears a cangue and shackles, his crimes filling the heavens; he can do nothing but bow his head in supplication."
"Save him! Although these two elders have beaten the shackles and struck the chains to clear his sins and release him from punishment, I fear that human sentiment and reason cannot tolerate this.
Is there anyone who recognizes that Xuefeng did not answer? It is truly laughable and pitiable."
Tiantong Muan said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. If someone asks, 'What is it like when the ancient stream contains cold spring water?
I say, 'It soaks and rots the nostrils. If they ask, 'What of those who drink from it? I say, 'It pierces through the skull.

Even if there were someone who could perceive its breath and asked, 'Is this the same as the water at Longchi, or is it different? I would tell them: 'How could a mountain brook ever retain [the essence]?"
"Abiding. In the end, it returns to the great ocean to form waves and billows.
[He] claps his hands once. Baoshou Xin said: "Xuefeng possesses the eye of the crown of the head, piercing through the puddle;

Zhaozhou wields the hand that reaches the heavens, guiding all back to the rivers and seas, causing the monks of the world to cast away all floating bubbles and fully awaken to the true source. This is not..."
The great masters of the Dharma-gate cannot be known through ordinary means. As for Xuefeng’s refusal to answer questions from this point on—how should one understand it?
"Do not bring right and wrong to judge me; the worldly life and its artificial interpretations are irrelevant."
Baoguang said: "Beating the felt clappers and blowing the holeless flute—Xuefeng and Zhaozhou were indeed extraordinary.
But this mountain monk is not so. As for 'The cold spring at the ancient stream'—how about it? It would be well to return to the rivers and seas;
there one may long carry the boat that ferries across the world. And as for 'the drinker'—how about him? A pure breeze arises in both armpits, and a refreshing clarity permeates."
Heaven and Earth, for now. As for the Way, is it the same as that of the ancients or different?
Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying, "The entire earth is this gate of liberation; one can take it by the hand and pull, yet they will not enter.
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "Master, you cannot blame me. Another monk said, "What is the use of entering? Xuefeng then struck him.
Xuedou Xian said: "Among these three, one person receives the salvation. Suddenly, if none of them can be clearly distinguished, how many are there on level ground?
Longchi Chuan said: "It is as if both monks were equally enlightened; yet why is it that, upon reaching this point, one receives a blow with a staff?"
There is one who does not receive the staff. Tell me, where does the error lie?
Shushan Shun said: "Since the entire world of the ten directions is entirely this gate of liberation, tell me, where is the main hall?"
Xuefeng ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to understand this matter, it is like a bright mirror set upon its stand: when a Hu comes, a Hu appears; when a Han comes, a Han appears.
Xuansha stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "What if a bright mirror were to come? Xuefeng replied, "Both Hu and Han are hidden."
Sha said, "The old monk’s heels have not yet even touched the ground.
Xuansha Bei replied separately, "I am not like that. If someone were to ask, 'What if you suddenly encounter a bright mirror? how would you respond?
He said, "I would tell them: 'It is shattered into a hundred fragments!'"
Mingzhao Qian said: "At such a time, do not say that both the barbarian and the Han are hidden; how else would you express it?
Xuansha said, "It is shattered. Mingzhao said, "It is lost."
Langya Jue said: "To verify a person at the point of ultimate certainty, one knows them the moment they open their mouths.
Longchi Chuan said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. If a bright mirror were suddenly to come before you, what would you do?
Simply say: 'Pick it up! Pick it up! Why? Because if it is not picked up, how can there be any resolution?"
Xuefeng ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said, "This one is for those of middling and inferior capacities.
A monk then asked, "What if a person of superior capacity were to arrive? Xuefeng also raised his whisk. The monk said, "This one is for those of middling and inferior capacities.

Caoshan addressed the assembly: "Everywhere else they merely employ restrictive measures; why not give them a turning word to make them [understand]?"

As he was about to leave, Yunmen asked, "Why does one not know what exists within the realm of the profound mystery? Shan said, "Precisely because it is so profound and mysterious, one does not know what exists.
Yunmen asked, "How should one approach such a person? Shan said, "Do not approach them within the realm of the profound mystery.
Yunmen asked, "If one does not approach them within the realm of the profound mystery, how then? Shan said, "Only then will you understand how to approach. Yunmen.
"Responding with 'Yes, yes.
Linji Yixuan said this. Juefan Huihong remarked, "The oil is turbid, yet it further moistens the lamp wick.
Dayuan Yingqi said, "Three thousand li south of the Snowy Mountains."
Baiyan Fu said: "It is precisely because it is so dense and hidden that one does not know it exists—wrong!
If you do not approach it from within this density, only then can you truly approach it—wrong! Big and small Caoshan—this mountain monk has already caught you all out.
Now tell me, what is this person? As for how the two elders Miaoxi and Chushih spoke in such a manner..."
Whether there is engagement or non-engagement, one must never unilaterally overlook these matters or fail to correctly understand the ancients;
otherwise, when the Old Man Yama interrogates you at a later time, do not say that you did not warn him.
A monk asked Caoshan, "What is the master of the Dharma-body? Caoshan said, "It is said that there is no one in Qin.
The monk asked, "Is this not it? Caoshan said, "Behead him!"
Baizhang Leshan said: "To rely on the gate and seek the master by questioning the servant—take for instance when Caoshan uttered the word 'sever.
Now tell me, what was his intention? He gave a shout and said: "I thought there was no one here; do not say I did not warn you."

Baiyan Fu said: "One must reach the ultimate peak and the highest summit; even if one has reached them, if one does not take another step forward, one remains nothing more than a corpse sitting on the ground.
Caoshan has here shaken out this monk’s innermost guts and exhausted every last bit of his secret.
Nevertheless, if you immediately understand this as 'not guarding the precious treasure,' you must cut it into three pieces.
Why? Because here there is no place for you to set foot.
Once, when a monk asked Caoshan, "What is it like when the funeral robe is no longer worn? Caoshan said, "Today, at Caoshan, the period of mourning has ended."
Yangshan asked, "After Xiaoman [孝滿] passed away, what was it like? Deshan replied, "Caoshan is fond of wine.
Baolin Xiu said, "Caoshan is sometimes drunk; yet in his drunkenness he is wide awake. Sometimes he is sober, yet he does not distinguish between day and night.
This is because his 'yellow millet dream' has been severed and his attachment to the domestic life has been forgotten. This is why Xin-feng said, 'When one looks at things before one's eyes...'"

The wild forest: this speaks of a life spent in leisure and expansiveness over many years. Thus, after one's filial duties are fulfilled, what ultimately remains? In the four seasons, spring is the height of prosperity;
in all things, wine is the essence of elegance.
Baiyan Fu said: "The teachers and monks of these days carry about a child who does not cry, intending to act like a madman in the middle of a crossroads.
Yet, the venerable masters in the hall have not even received the courtesy of a cup of water;
to hope that they will don the funeral shroud is already like seeking the night sky by looking at an egg. Furthermore, as for what is called...
If filial piety is fulfilled even here, how much more so after what is called the "fulfillment of filial piety"? Truly, this matter is not a matter of three illnesses or two lights;
it must be penetrated through to the very end, and further penetrated, until there is not even a single breath of the state of having already penetrated through to the end.
Only then may one meet Cao Shan. Here in my place, I absolutely do not permit this. Why is that?
It is not that my school lacks those willing to speak; one who rides the dragon is truly no ordinary person.
Caoshan asked a monk, "What have you come to do? The monk replied, "I have come to sweep the floor. Caoshan said, "Do you sweep before the Buddha or after the Buddha?"
The monk said, "I swept both front and back at the same time. Yaoshan said, "Bring me your sandals, then pass them over to Caoshan.
Wuzu Jie spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "Master, what kind of mental activity is this?"
Tianxi said, "The world is full of such talk. Cao Shan has always only known how to act as the host. If it were I, I would not do so.
When he says, 'Sweeping before and after at once,' I would instead call the attendant and say, 'This monk has worked hard sweeping the floor;
let him have a cup of tea.'"
One day, when Caoshan heard the sound of the bell, he said, "A-ya! A-ya! A monk asked, "What are you doing, Master?"
Mount [Shan] said, "It strikes at my heart. The monk had no reply.
Wuzu Jie spoke on behalf of the monk, saying, "The heart of a thief is empty.
Jingshan Xiu said, "The thief does not need to strike; he confesses himself."
Baoshou Fang said, "What limit is there for these fellows who dally with their own spirits? It would be well to banish them to another land.
Qinghua Yan said, "A person of immeasurable capacity yet goes about stirring up the sons and daughters of others amidst sounds and forms."
Fengshan Yan said: "The old man Caoshan intended to test a master of the Way, but he did not realize that he was instead exposed by this monk.
When a monk asked Caoshan, "What is a lion? Caoshan replied, "No other beasts can approach it. The monk asked, "How about..."

"This is a lion cub. The Mountain said, "It is capable of swallowing its own parents. [The Master] asked, "Since it is a creature that no other beasts can approach, why was it instead swallowed by its child?
The Mountain replied, "Have you not heard it said: 'If the son lets out a roar, both grandfather and father are utterly consumed'?"

[The monk] asked, "When the 'successor' is exhausted, what then? Shan said, "The whole body returns to the father. [The monk] asked, "I do not yet understand: when the 'ancestor' is exhausted, where does the father return?
Shan said, "The place also becomes exhausted. [The monk] asked, "Why did you previously say that the whole body returns to the father?
Shan said, "It is like a prince who is able to accomplish the affairs of an entire kingdom."
Baoshou said: "Do you all wish to recognize the meaning of 'the whole body returning to the father'? Great functions manifest simultaneously, forgetting both contact and avoidance;
when the occasion arises, who else could determine killing or giving life?"
Shouchang Cunzheng said: "Since both the 'subject' and the 'object' have been exhausted, from where can the descendants underfoot go to meet their ancestors?
Caoshan asked Upādhyāya Qiang: "The Buddha’s true Dharma-body is like empty space; it manifests forms in response to things, just like water."
Zhongyue asked, "How do you explain the principle of the 'response'? Deshan said, "It is like a donkey looking down a well.
Zhongyue said, "Your explanation is quite thorough, yet it only accounts for eighty percent. Deshan asked, "What about you, Master? Zhongyue said, "It is like a well looking down at a donkey."
Boshanlai said: "The brilliance of a noble hero, the demeanor of a poet—pervading and harmonizing the refined essence, there is nothing further to be hidden.
Caoshan’s guidance transcends the ordinary; it is like performing a somersault down from a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, such that one cannot grasp or look up at it.
It is not merely the Three Mysteries and Five Ranks; it is such that the skulls of Buddhas and patriarchs are all pierced through. Ei!"
Baiyan Fu said: "If it is like a donkey looking down a well, you may explain the principle of the response as you wish;
I will allow you to guess east and west. But when it comes to saying 'like a well looking at a donkey,' how do you understand that?
Here, not even a single eye can be applied; you have not yet become even a servant of Caoshan."
Cao Shan was once asked by Jingqing: "When the principle of pure emptiness ultimately has no body, what then?
Shan said: "The principle is indeed so; but as for the phenomenon, how is it? Jingqing said: "It is just like the principle and just like the phenomenon. Shan said:
"You may deceive Cao Shan alone, but what about the eyes of all the Buddhas? Jingqing said: "If there were no eyes of the Buddhas, how could they discern that which is not thus?"
Mount Cao said, "The official path does not admit a needle; private ways allow for carriages and horses.
Wei Shan Zhe remarked, "Although Mount Cao is well able to cut, grind, polish, and shape, alas, the jade of Jing Qing is inherently without flaw.
Do you understand? Without passing through the hands of a skilled artisan, it will ultimately remain a discarded vessel."
Dongshan Fu said: "The two venerable masters sang and clapped in succession; their fists and kicks were in perfect accord. But tell me, where did they plant their feet?

I, this mountain monk, shall speak for you: Caoshan suddenly thrust out his eyes from within the soot and ink, only to have them all at once plugged by Jingqing with a wedge of empty space. What could be done about it? Caoshan was like this."
Buddhist Monk Fotudeng had a cavity beneath his ribs. From far and near, the multitude of people and things crowded together; their various distinct forms were all clearly visible to him.

Qi Xie Cheng said: "When the signs of creation have not yet been distinguished, the subtle principle cannot be perceived; once the wheel of mechanism begins to turn, the phenomena of things become fully manifest."
Zhang [Zhaoqing] exhausted the mysteries before the path of the birds and discerned the mark beyond the sheep’s-gut pass; Qingjing was indeed already preeminent in his insight.
"The official may not admit a needle, yet private carriages and horses pass through"—these words of Caoshan are no ordinary speech.
To have no body yet possess activity is to transcend the crossroads; to have no activity and no body is to fall into the beginning and the end.
Yanjiao Le said: "When the strings vibrate, one distinguishes the melody; when the leaves fall, one knows autumn. Releasing and gathering, clarity meets darkness;
the orthodox and the deviant are not lost, wondrously harmonizing in impartiality. Not transgressing the head-on encounter, there is a path for turning the body. Why is this so?
It is not that he does not see the Way; it is simply that he is able to avoid touching upon the taboos of the present day.
This is superior to the talent of those former dynasties who had their tongues cut out. A monk asked Caoshan about Xiangyan: "What is the Way? Xiangyan said, "A dragon’s cry within a withered tree.
The monk asked, "What is one on the Way? Xiangyan said, "The eyes within a skull. The monk did not understand and went to ask Shishuang. "What is it? [the monk asked].
"This is a dragon’s roar within a withered tree. Făng said, "It still retains a trace of joy. He asked, "What is the eye within a skull?
Făng said, "It still retains a trace of consciousness. Not yet understanding, he questioned Caoshan: "What is the dragon’s roar within a withered tree?
Caoshan said, "The life-blood is not severed. "What is the eye within a skull? Caoshan said, "It has not dried up."
“I wonder, is there anyone who has heard it? Shan said, “Throughout the entire world, there is not a single person who has not heard it.
[The monk] asked, “I do not understand what verses are these: ‘the dragon’s cry within the withered tree’? Shan said, “If you do not know what verses they are, those who hear them will all perish.
He then presented this verse: “The dragon’s cry in the withered tree is the true seeing of the Way; The skull has no consciousness, yet its eyes first open.”
Mingxi said: "When consciousness is exhausted, the news is exhausted. How can a person discern the clarity within the turbidity?
Xuan Sha Bei distinguished this from Xiangyan’s initial words, saying: "A dragon roars in a withered tree."
Zhaojue Qin said: "When mindfulness does not differ from the mind and there is no deviation, one is perfectly interfused with the five ranks of ruler and subject;
one leaps out of the three poisons of non-action and can then cause flowers to bloom upon withered trees and blow the pitch-pipe within cold cliffs.
Look at those three old masters: one penetrated the leakage of words, one penetrated the leakage of sentiment, and one penetrated..."
Observe where the leakage occurs. If you can investigate and examine this thoroughly, you may then stride alone through the profound barrier. Do you understand?
Do not cling to the green grasses on a cold cliff; if you sit amidst white clouds, your function will not be subtle.
Jingshan Daowu, having finished citing Yuanwu’s words, said: "Can you all discern this?
If you cannot discern it, Miaoxi will not begrudge his eyebrows and shall explain it through for you. Xiangyan penetrated the leakage of words, yet he was bound to death by language.
Shishuang penetrated the leakage of sentiment, yet he was driven to death by conceptual consciousness. Caoshan penetrated the [leakage of] views..."
"Leakage. He is killed by the delusions of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. This has been stated clearly; let those with eyes discern it.
After Tianning Qi finished citing the words of Miaoxi, he said:
"The old man Miaoxi sits with his whole body within the three kinds of leakage, yet he is not constrained by those three leakages. Nevertheless, if you wish to see the directness of the ancients—"
"This is far away. Why is that? It is because there is no reason to corrupt the men and women of others' families.
Tiantong Juo said: "The king dwells within the gate; the ministers do not go out the gate. Ba'en Xiu said:
"Tiantong is able to express immeasurable Dharma-gates as a single phrase; sometimes he expresses a single-character Dharma-gate with ink as vast as the ocean."
Not yet exhausted. Do you still recognize the place where the Celestial Child (Tiantong) settled his family and found peace and joy? A solitary crane often keeps company with the water;
auspicious clouds never leave the mountain when they have nothing to do.
A monk asked Caoshan, "I bring this raw jade to the Master; I pray you, Master, polish it. Caoshan said, "I do not polish it.
The monk asked, "Why do you not polish it? Caoshan said, "You must know that Caoshan is a master craftsman."
Yunju Zhuang said: "Now tell me, does this monk understand Caoshan’s words or not? I, this mountain monk, say:
even if he were to understand them, it would still be groundless."
Baiyan Fu said: "To treat the Great and Small Cao Shan as mere peddlers of old trinkets is to waste a great deal of chisel and hammer;
they were not yet masters of their craft. Today, if someone asks Juewang, 'I bring this uncut gem to you, Master;
I pray you polish it,' he would immediately strike him on the head with a staff. Even if it were a fine jade from Mount Jing, he would make him break it into a hundred pieces."
Miscellaneous fragments. Why? It is to cause them to cast off their foul-smelling cloth robes and discard their grease-stained hats.
When a monk asked Caoshan, "What is it like when the bright moon is in the sky? Caoshan said, "You are still a man standing on the steps. [The monk] said:
He requested the Master to lead him up the stairs. The Master said, "We shall meet after the moon has set.
Tiantong Wu ascended the hall, and having finished his discourse, he said, "Tell me, since it is after the moon has set, how will you see one another?
At that moment, Wanfeng Zang stepped out of the Dharma hall, and Wu immediately descended from his seat.
Jianfu was like a cloud; Old Man Caoshan diagnosed the ailment and prescribed the medicine; and Wufeng of Tiantong followed the prescription to compound the medicine.
All of them were indeed indisputably master-level practitioners of the Peach-Blossom Grove (the medical profession).
Yet, upon close inspection, they all nonetheless retained a trace of the physician’s habitual mannerisms.
Cao Shan was about to take his leave of Dongshan. Dongshan asked, "Where are you going? Cao Shan replied, "I am going to the place where there is no change.
Dongshan said, "In a place of no change, how can there be going? Cao Shan replied, "Even going is not a change."
Baonenglun said: "Do you know the place that does not change? As soon as you form a thought or stir a mental intention, it has already changed.
But what about when Caoshan says, 'Even going forth, there is no changing'? If you wish to understand thoroughly:
When all is exhausted and there is no merit, he falls into his own station; standing solitary and peerless, he does not share a table with you."
Hongyun said: "This plot of land has been occupied by Caoshan.
Nevertheless, the deed remains in Dongshan’s hands."
Chan Master Daoying of Yunju in Hongzhou (a successor of Dongshan Liangjie of the Qingyuan lineage) was once asked by Official Liu Yu, who had come up the mountain to give thanks for rain:
"From where does the rain come? Daoying replied, "It comes from where you, Official, have asked. The official then performed three prostrations and withdrew with joy.
After he had walked several paces, Daoying called out to Official Liu. The official turned his head; Daoying said, "From where did your question come? The official [realized].
He remained silent. He returned home and passed away three days later. Jìngshān Gǎo said:
"Dūngōng’s silence and his death three days after returning home truly scratch the itchy spot of Hóngjué;
he simply did not know the path for turning back. At that time, had he been asked, "From where have you come? he should have simply—
Having performed the three prostrations as before, he withdrew with joy. Furthermore, it is said that Hongjue harbored doubts for thirty years. Tiantong Muan remarked:
"When Yunju asked about 'killing,' the Elder's eyebrows fell off by more than half; having encountered this question, the Elder was liberated.
His speech never borrowed another's tongue. Now, if there is one who asks Tiantong about 'rain following,'" [he would answer].
“Where have you come from? He simply replied, “Shut your mouth. But how, then, can one cause it to rain down?
Simply prepare a heart of resolve, and you will certainly not be deceived.
Yunju ordered his attendant to send a pair of trousers to a practitioner living in a hermitage. The practitioner said, “I have had them since birth.”
Jiū refused to accept the trousers. He sent his attendant back to ask, "What did you wear before you were born? The Chan master was speechless.

Later, when the master passed away, his remains were cremated and produced śarīra. Jiū held them up and said, "Even if one could burn eight bushels and four pecks of relics, it would not be as good as having delivered a single turning word at the beginning."
The Chan master Bodhidai said, "Thank you, Master," three times.
Huiyun Sheng asked, "Tell me, what words could have been spoken at that time to avoid such censure?
Had I been the abbot, when he asked, 'What was there before your mother was born? I would have replied, 'Thank you very much, Master.'"
Chonghui. Tianmu’s Vinaya Record says: "The old fellow of Yunju’s command was truly formidable. The practitioner was speechless; those who know the Dharma are struck with awe.
An attendant monk from the side remarked, "If you had asked at that time, 'What did the Master wear before his mother gave birth?'"
"How so? [The monk] asked. "I do not yet understand; how would you proceed? He then replied, "Who is it that creates?
Although nowadays the teachers and monks among us are not incapable of delivering a thousand words or ten thousand phrases, if one seeks even half a grain of *śarīra*, how could it ever be obtained?
Baiyan Fu said: "The old fellow of Yunju missed the mark, O practitioner; at that time, it would have been no obstacle for you to remain silent as a true master.
It is simply a pity that there was no one to bear witness."
Yunju asked Shangshu Yin Cheng: "The Tathāgata had secret words, which Kāśyapa did not conceal.
What is the principle behind this? Yunju called out, "Shangshu! Shangshu responded, "Yes. Yunju said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. Yunju said, "If you do not understand..."
The Tathāgata has esoteric words. If one understands them, Kāśyapa does not conceal them. Qingliang Qinzheng said:
"Tell me, is that which is called 'esoteric' the esoteric word? Is that which responds to it the esoteric word?
If both the calling and the responding are simply gone, then it is not esoteric. But what, then, is the esoteric word?"
Donglin Zong said: "How strange! For twenty years, Hongjue’s tracks were lost like a wild goat hanging from its horns;
yet, upon being questioned by the Minister, he was immediately reduced to 'carrying water and dragging mud,' inevitably becoming an object of ridicule.
Faldeng acting this way is like lighting a lamp at midday or splashing ink at midnight."
Dongchan Guan said: "When meeting people, speak only three parts of the truth; do not yet cast forth your whole heart. Bairyam Pu said:
"If the Sūtra is not clear, one must explain it with a Commentary (*shu*). If the Commentary is not clear, one must explain it with a Sub-commentary (*chao*).
The old fellow Hongjue has already provided his Commentary and his Sub-commentary. But tell me, does the Minister understand? Even if he were to understand—"
"It is attained, yet it is not yet one's own family treasure.
Yunju went to visit Dongshan. Dongshan asked, "What is your name? Yunju replied, "Daoying. Dongshan said, "Why do you not speak from the perspective above?
Yunju said, "From the perspective above, I am no longer named Daoying. Dongshan deeply approved of this.
Tianmu Lü said: "When those two great elders met in their ordinary daily interactions, they exchanged questions and answers with all their might, seeking to illuminate the path of the noble one.
Little did they know that they were merely acting as intermediaries for him.
As for the matter of the ultimate transcendence, from here to the capital is still a journey of half a month."
Baiyan Fu said: "The curtains hang in the incense chamber, yet Yao’s brows are not revealed. To have attained the profound essence of this is to leave it to the old man Yunju;
thus they became father and son within the Dongshan lineage. However, he only succeeded in expounding upon matters pertaining to subordinates.
"If this is the path of the noble and honored, I dare say it is lacking something. The attendant then asked, "What is the path of the noble and honored?
The mountain monk held out his tongue to show him and said, "If you want my tongue, cut it off and take it!"
A monk asked Yunju, "What is the teacher of all Buddhas? Yunju shouted, "You field-hand! The monk bowed.
Yunju said, "How do you understand this? The monk replied, "This old monk. Yunju said, "So you do not understand after all."
The monk performed a dance and departed. Jujian said, "He was a beggar crawling along the platform.
Zhaojue Renyun said, "To recognize the opportune moment and distinguish between good and ill fortune requires an eye capable of reciprocal maneuvering;
such a person is hard to find even among a thousand or ten hundred. Why, then, did he become a beggar crawling along the platform?"
This too is "cherishing one's child without realizing their ugliness.
He Shanxun said: "To turn the hand over is to become clouds; to cover the hand is to become rain. Host and guest exchange places; they perform a dance at the moment of action.
It is laughable that a beggar on the platform begging for alms is also looking south to see the Big Dipper."
Bai Zhang Le said: "What end will there ever be for this fellow from the fields? Why not wait until the moment he prostrates and kick him down?
Would that not be a definitive severing? Nevertheless, one must not act with careless haste."
Yunju was asked by Dongshan, "Where have you come from? Yunju replied, "I have come from treading the mountains.
Dongshan asked, "Which mountain would be suitable for you to dwell on? Yunju said, "Which mountain would not be suitable for me to dwell on?
Dongshan remarked, "In that case, the entire country is occupied by you, Master. Yunju said, "Not so. Dongshan asked, "Do you perhaps lack a way of entry? Yunju replied:
"There is no path. Mount said, "How then can you meet with this old monk? Ju said, "If there were a path, I would be separated from the Master by a lifetime.
Mount said, "This child will, hereafter, be beyond the grasp of thousands and tens of thousands."
Qingshan Xiu said: "When masters meet, it is like a pearl rolling on a tray; as the tray rolls, the pearl moves—unimpeded in every direction.
How can this be compared to those who beat ice to seek fire or climb a tree to catch fish? Today, if someone comes treading upon the mountain, I shall ask you:
do you come by way of a path, or do you come without a path? If you say you come by way of a path, it is not so."
Yunju says they do not harmonize because there is no path by which to come; Dongshan says they do not harmonize because there is a path.
Qing Shan says both are equally blocked. But how can one harmonize with the meaning of the ancients? Try to say it.
Yunju ascended the hall for the formal discourse: "It is like a person who spends three strings of cash to buy a hunting dog; it only knows how to track down those that leave footprints.
But when it encounters a wild goat hanging from a tree branch—let alone footprints, there is not even a trace of its breath.
A monk then asked, "What is it like when the wild goat hangs from the branch? Yunju said, "Six times six is thirty-six. The monk asked, "And after it has hung from the branch? Yunju said, [silence].

He said, "Six times six is thirty-six. The monk bowed. Yunju asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. Yunju said, "Have you not heard it said that there are no tracks or traces?
When Zhaozhou Congshen heard this monk recount these words, he remarked, "Brother Yunju is still alive. The monk then questioned him.
“How is it when the pronged antelope hangs its horns? Zhaozhou said, “Nine times nine is eighty-one. “How is it after the horns have hung?
Zhaozhou said, “Nine times nine is eighty-one. “It is so difficult to understand! Zhaozhou said, “What is there that is difficult to understand?
“Please, Master, give me an instruction. Zhaozhou said, “Silla, Silla.”
Dongshan Ying said: "One person stands atop a high, towering mountain peak; though he wishes to descend, he cannot.
Another person walks at the bottom of a deep sea; though he wishes to emerge, he cannot. I shall give each of them thirty blows of the staff. Why?
Because they are like a pair of iron hammers without holes."
A monk asked Yunju, "From what do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise? Yunju said, "They arise from deluded thoughts.
The monk said, "Can you give me one ingot of gold from those thoughts? Yunju then stopped speaking. The monk did not accept this.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "This is already a tangle; it cannot be settled. Wait until he says, 'Can one produce a piece of gold?
and then strike him with the staff."
Xiaoyan Bao said: "Although Yunmen was able to bring matters to a resolution, he still lacked directness.
If I were in Yunju's place, when he asked, 'From where do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise? I would strike him across the mouth and say, 'What deluded thought is this?'"
Why is this? Although one may skillfully cut off its flow and break its tendrils, it is not equal to uprooting the root and blocking the source.
Baiyan Fu said: "As Yunju answered the question in this way, how many people throughout past and present have not been surpassed by him?"
In the flow of this discourse, one eye has been lost. Little do they realize that he has brought forth the *indranīla* mani-jewel face-to-face, never withholding it for a moment.
Yet, alas, this monk has eyes like those of a blind man; facing him directly, he does not recognize it.
Yunju had no choice but to return with shame. Nevertheless, if it were Bairyam, when [the Master] said, "Give it to me," he would have...
"Can you imagine a single ingot of gold? Having said this, he laughed heartily and returned to his quarters.
Chan Master Kuangren of Shushan in Fuzhou (a successor of Dongshan Liangjie of the Qingyuan lineage) addressed the assembly:
"Before the Xiantong era, I understood the affairs of the Dharma-body; after the Xiantong era, I understood the matters above the Dharma-body. Yunmen stepped forward and asked:
"What is the matter of the Dharma-body? Shanshan said, "A withered stump. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter beyond the Dharma-body? Shanshan said, "Not a withered stump.
[The monk] asked, "Do you permit this student to speak of principle? Shanshan said, "I do.

[The monk] said, "Is it not the case that the withered stump clarifies the matter of the Dharma-body? Shanshan said, "It is. [The monk] said, "Is it not the case that 'not a withered stump' clarifies..."
Regarding the matter of that which transcends the Dharma-body, Yaoshan said, "It is. [Dongshan] asked, "I wonder, does the Dharma-body encompass all things or not?
Yaoshan replied, "The Dharma-body is all-pervasive; how could it not encompass them? Dongshan pointed to a water pitcher and said, "As for this water pitcher, does it encompass the Dharma-body?
Yaoshan said, "Master, do not seek the Dharma-body within the water pitcher. Dongshan then prostrated himself.
Jingshan Daowei asked: "Tell me, was Yunmen’s prostration a good deed or not? Bairyak Pu said:
