Huanglong Nan said: "Qianfeng’s single-period pointing of the way was a concession to beginners;
Yunmen then mastered its transformations, thereby ensuring that later generations would not grow weary."
Daguang Xiu said: "From ancient times to the present, everyone says that Qianfeng established the ancestral hall for the summer retreat and opened a path for future generations.
Little do they realize that when this monk posed his single question, the old fellow Qianfeng was left with his hands flailing and his feet stumbling.
Zen adepts, tell me: where does the crux lie? After a long silence, he said: 'It is not in the water.'"
It is not in the mountains; it lies only within the shifting movements of the human mind.
Donglin Zong said: "The ancient masters spoke of Qianfeng shaking his head and Yunmen wagging his tail. This monk is merely a fellow who bumps into a pillar;
he does not even realize he has missed the mark beneath his own feet, and thus claims that the neighbor lit the lamp."
The neighbor sits in the dark; the dragon carries the ocean treasure, yet the swimming fish pay it no heed.
Today, this mountain monk cannot simply go along with the waves or follow the current, nor can he strike fear into people at a moment of peril.

Little do they realize that both the great Qianfeng and Yunmen were thoroughly scrutinized and exposed by this monk. But tell me, where exactly was he exposed? After a long silence, he said: "It has been raining for a long time."
Water. It does not reach the sun-dried [tiles].
Bao Feng’s inscription says: "Did Qianfeng see this even in his dreams? If it were Zhenjing, he would have said otherwise:
"The Buddhas of the ten directions all enter the gate of Nirvana by a single path. I wonder where the head of that path lies?
He struck him across the spine with his staff and then asked, "Where is the head of the road? As soon as the monk was about to open his mouth, he gave a hot shout and drove him out.
Furthermore, there was an old, crippled bhikṣu who could not distinguish between the black and the white, nor discern the heterodox from the orthodox.
He held up his fan and said: "The fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking the nostrils of Śakra.
A carp from the Eastern Sea receives a blow of the staff, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin.
For a fellow such as this—one who muddies the waters and mixes the clay—what fault is there if ten or five are buried in a heap of refuse? A-he-he! Joy!"
There is no pleasure; there is neither sufficiency nor insufficiency. Now, fortunately, we face green waters and blue mountains. All such affairs have come to rest for the time being.
Let body and mind be as they are, free from constraint. Everyone, do not nod off to sleep!
Huanglong Qing said: "If you try to understand it through Qianfeng’s statement, that is precisely a 'dead word'—it will sit and kill you, O Master.
If you try to take responsibility based on Yunmen’s words, your karmic consciousness will be vast and boundless, drifting with the waves.
Since both are disallowed, where exactly do you understand it? Do you all know where it lands? From of old, the masters..."
Even the worthy ones do not recognize it; how could ordinary people in their haste and confusion understand it? Nanhua Bing said:
"Qianfeng exhausted his compassion to seize the opportune moment and draw forth the student's potential; Yunmen skillfully opened up expedient means to trigger realization face-to-face.
It truly causes flowers to bloom on withered wood and flames to leap from cold ashes. But tell me, what about Donghai?
"A carp struck with a single blow, the rain pours down like an overturned basin. What side of the matter does this clarify? "Blowing on the fire because of the wind;

not much effort is required. Jingshan Yan said: "The song is sung ever higher, and the response is ever more majestic. Let us grant these two elders their due. As for the 'Ten Directions'... [text breaks off]
"Kāśyapa’s single path to the gate of nirvāṇa—none have yet trodden upon it.
Yuyan Yuan said: "Shaoyang’s response to the occasion was too extravagant; Qianfeng’s answer to the question was too parsimonious.
Being extravagant, it cannot accommodate the ignorant; being parsimonious, it cannot encompass the multitude. Here in my Yunmen school, [the nine...]"
The thoroughfare is a road that branches in eight directions; its path is broad and level as a whetstone.
You may ride donkey or horse, racing south or north as you please, yet at this critical junction on the main road, the mountain monk suddenly extends his hand and says:
"Produce your official pass!"
Gushan Puyun said: "At Qianfeng, the Way is as smooth as a whetstone; at Yunmen, the ten characters run vertically and horizontally.
If you can return by taking a confident step, only then will you know that the Way is always present within it, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down.
If this is not yet so, I, this mountain monk, shall speak further for you: 'The Buddhas of the ten directions share a single path—the gate to Nirvana. This is the head of the road."
"At what place? Holding up his staff, he said, "Going downhill, one does not run; such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter. He then struck the ground once and descended from the seat.
Guangyin Biao remarked, "If it can strengthen the state, do not follow its old ways; if it can benefit the people, do not..."
Following their ritual propriety, these two old fellows, though they were men of the highest caliber, could not avoid exhausting their cleverness until they were forced to resort to clumsiness.
If it had been Wumuan, when asked, "The Buddhas of the ten directions have taught the single path to nirvana; I wonder where the beginning of that path lies?
he would have immediately kicked them over with a shout, causing them to reach a state of total resolution right on the spot. In this way, perhaps—
It was nearly like the story of weeping at the fork of the road over lost sheep.

Yanjiao Le said: "Qianfeng shook his head; Yunmen wagged his tail. While these two elders possessed no lack of supernatural powers and wondrous functions, they could not avoid being seen through by this monk."
Baiyan Fu said: "To transform the true *kaishu* (regular script) of the Two Wangs into the cursive calligraphy of Zhang Xu—Yunmen excelled at attaining its subtlety.

Unless one has long refined the methods of transmitting and bestowing the 'arrays' and 'supplementing the halberds,' it is absolutely impossible to find the points where he transformed and restructured [the characters].
Nevertheless, his path to the gate of nirvāṇa remains ultimately difficult to point out. Thus it is now.
When the monk asked in this manner, what else could those masters on the curved wooden seats of all quarters have done to respond appropriately?
They could not simply have copied the model like drawing a gourd from a gourd.
Qianfeng was once asked by Yunmen to answer a question for him. Qianfeng said, "Have you even reached the old monk yet?
Yunmen said, "If that is so, then Wenyan is late. Qianfeng said, "How so? How so? Yunmen said, "I thought it was Hou Bai;
there is also Hou Hei."

Baoneng Xiu said: "Yunmen’s clear sky flashing lightning, Qianfeng’s thunder crashing on dry land—when it comes to releasing both simultaneously and gathering both back in, even a masterful monk finds it difficult to grasp."
Boshan Lai said: "An extraordinary question, an extraordinary answer. Faster than a clap of thunder to cover one's ears, swifter than a fine steed to catch the wind.
With their winding and circular maneuvers, each employs the skill of probing the profound and seeking out the hidden.
Yet, when examined closely, they deserve a severe blow. Why? Because they create trouble where there is none. To let them pass..."
"No. Ou-feng Cheng said, "Two lacquer buckets have lost their nostrils.
Chan Master Xian-qi of Tiantong in Mingzhou (a successor of Dongshan Jia of Qingyuan) asked Venerable Jian: "When a student stands tall and firm,"
[The Master] said, "Come. Ask the Master clearly. Xuefeng said, "In my place here, one simply defecates once; what is there that is so distinct and clear?
[The Master] said, "If you answer as the Master does, you had better buy some straw sandals and go on pilgrimage. Xuefeng came forward and said, "Come closer."
The monk stepped forward and asked, "As for this old monk’s response just now, where does the fault lie? Xuanjian had no reply;
the monk then struck him. Tiantong Huo said:
"Master Qian was indeed a master of the fundamental hammer, yet he has blocked the mouth of the new Tiantong."
"Those who have not yet attained it remain outside. Although these monks have entered deeply into the inner precincts, they have not yet fully acquired the eye that penetrates the barrier.
Chan Master Qingshan Wensui (of Qingzhou; successor to Dongshan Liangjie) was asked by Layman Liang: "What is it like when 'a single arrowhead pierces the three barriers'?
Qingshan said, "Release the master within the barrier and let him look. Layman Liang said, "In that case, one knows that having committed an error, one must surely reform it."
Mount Shàn said, "When do you intend to wait for? Láng said, "A fine arrow shot, yet it lands nowhere," and he immediately went out. Mount Shàn called out, "Come here, Dharma teacher!

Láng turned his head back. From beneath his meditation seat, Mount Shàn seized him and said, "Setting aside for a moment the idea that 'one shaft pierces three barriers,' let me see you shoot an arrow at Qinshan.
As Láng hesitated, Mount Shàn struck him seven blows and said, "For now, listen to this chaos."
Tonghan hesitated for thirty years.
Chaya of Tong’an said, “Although Master Liang understands how to release the arrow, he has yet to hit the mark.
A monk then asked, “I wonder, how can one hit the mark? Tong’an replied, “Who is the ruler of Guanzhong? When Qingshan heard this, he said:
If Master Liang understood it in this way, he too would have avoided the "mouth of Qian. Nevertheless, although it is thus, Tong’an did not have good intentions;
you must examine this closely before you can understand it.
Tiantong Jue said: "When it comes like mountains piled up and peaks heaped high, and goes away like a wall crumbling and ice melting, then people of this age know it exists.
Let me let out the Lord of Guanzhong for you all to see—how should one act? Some say that at that moment one should simply shout;
others say one should simply strike with the palm. While such a blind application may suffice for a single occasion, it is nonetheless not yet the Lord of Guanzhong."
The Master is present. Can you still grasp his essence? Not sitting upright in the hall, how can one respond to the dual mechanisms of the pivot?
Qinshan, Yantou, and Xuefeng went together to Deshan. Qinshan stepped forward and asked, "Even the Heavenly Emperor speaks thus."
Longtan spoke thus. "I do not know how you, Master, would speak. Deshan said, "Try to cite what the Emperor of Heaven (Tianhuang) and Longtan said, and I shall see.
When Xiqin hesitated, Deshan struck him. After being struck, Xiqin returned to the Yan-shou Hall and said, "It is indeed so;
however, he struck me far too hard. Yantou said, "If you act like this, you will not be able to say [anything meaningful] hereafter."
When Deshan saw him coming, Fayen said, "It is so, it is so; yet he strikes me wrongly.
Xuedou Xian said, "All you Zen practitioners, Qinshan’s setting up of this question is truly extraordinary. But alas—"
"A dragon’s head and a snake’s tail. Try raising your voice and see if you can reach the very bottom of the Way of Emperor Tianhuang and Longtan.
[The Master] struck with his sitting mat. "For a great man to stroke a tiger's whiskers is also his proper duty.
Since he was unable to do so, Deshan’s command was carried out only halfway. Had the command been fully executed, Xuefeng and Yantou would both have been men in the Nirvana Hall.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Qinshan looked only to the front and not to the rear.
Now, how would you provide relief for Qinshan?
Wuzu Jie said, "Deshan only knew how to beat Qinshan to death; he did not know how to beat Qinshan to life."
Zhao of Mount Gui said: "Under Deshan’s gate, the grass bows and the wind blows. But Daopi was not like this; when someone asked, 'I do not yet understand—how does the Master speak?
he would strike them across the spine. Now, tell me: was it Deshan or was it Daopi? Do you understand?
Holding Mohe Panthu crosswise, he maintains the full authority of the True Command; in a world at peace, he slays the dull and the stubborn."
Gunanmen said: "Xuedou supports the strong and does not support the weak.

One does not know that when the old fellow Deshan was pressed by Qingshan, he was driven straight to pass the responsibility on to another. 'If you hesitate, I strike!'—he has already treated a dead horse with medicine.
Had he acted according to the command, why wait for the words 'Tianhuang' or 'Longtan'? As soon as one steps forward, there would have been a great blow."
Taking advantage of the opportunity, he brings forth dragons and snakes, unleashes tigers and rhinoceroses—what fault could there possibly be in this?
Dongshan Yu said: "How great is Deshan’s mastery over killing and enlivening! Although Qinshan possessed a strategy to meet the blade, alas, he failed to follow through;
his head was that of a dragon, yet his tail was that of a snake. Yantou and Xuefeng sat by and watched the outcome; their failure to act was unforgivable."
If one were to act according to every [precedent], one would have to strike him out with a great staff all at once.
Bairyaku Fu said: "Try to cite the ultimate meaning of the Way of Emperor T'ien-huang and Lung-t'an. [The Master] shouted. "This old fellow:
meeting him in person is not as good as hearing his reputation. He shook his sleeves and departed. At that time, Ch'in Shan attained a turning of his hands and feet beneath the master.
Not only did this leave Deshan with nothing to bestow, but it also increased his fellow practitioners' spirit tenfold.
Later, when a monk asked Qinshan, "What is the house style of your teacher? Shan replied, "Brocade and silver incense pouches;
the wind blows their fragrance all along the road. When Yantou heard of this, he sent a monk to deliver a message, saying, "Tell Sister Eighteen: 'Be careful!'"
He served Master Panlang.
Tiantong Muan said: "The old man Suí was not ignorant of the Dongshan school; Master Huó did not violate the legacy of Deshan.
Yet, when examined closely, one of them still wears the clothes of his original nature, while the other still walks the path of the mind."
"You have not yet escaped Cao Shan’s four prohibitions. If you were a monk of this mountain, how would you express it?

"Like jade that is too precious to be worn; like reed pipes whose speech carries a note of sorrow. He then looked around at those present and asked, "Is there anyone here now who can transmit these words?
The assembly remained silent. He then said: "The blood-stained cuckoo calls as spring passes by; for your sake, I cannot [endure it]."
What a pity to damage those beautiful brows!
Lingyan Shuyu said: "Qinshan merely sought to flaunt his charm, regardless of the fact that it causes one's soul to wither and dreams to shatter.
Although Yantou, though he may uphold the laws of the land, how can he avoid a heavy sentence for such a crime? If someone asks this mountain monk, "How [should one respond]?"
This is the family style of our Preceptor. He said, "I know well that you will not arrive," and then ascended once more to the top of the small tower.
Looking left and right, he asked, "Tell me, what is the intent behind this announcement by this mountain monk? After a long silence, he struck his bamboo staff once and said:
"Calling for 'Xiaoyu' repeatedly is originally a matter of no concern; it is simply to have the husband recognize the sound."
Qinshan was visited by the attendant of Deshan. As soon as the attendant prostrated, Qinshan seized him and said, "Do you consent to being treated this way by Qinshan?
The attendant replied, "I regret that I have stayed so long at Deshan; today I have no words with which to respond."
Mount Shishuang let go of his hand and said, "Leave it to you to respond. Deshan pushed open Deshan’s chest and said, "Let me have my say for a moment.
Mount Shishuang said, "That might work under Deshan’s gate, but here not even a single point is of any use.

Deshan said, "For a long time I have known that Mount Shishuang has no sense of human courtesy. Mount Shishuang said, "This will bring shame upon Deshan’s reputation. Deshan said, "Go to the meditation hall."
Jingshan Ce said: "To kill a person without questioning them, and to question a person without killing them—puffing out one's chest and breathing heavily, both are but 'Almsman Bais' (Meng Ba).
Even if you possess a beginning and an end, it is still merely scooping water to splash at one another. Do you wish to recognize Qingshan and this monk?
Li Shunwang’s small sandals were first worn by him when he was thirteen; Li Shiqi’s bag was made from a broken sock."
Once when Qinshan, Xuefeng, and Yantou were traveling together, they arrived at an inn and sat down to drink tea.

Qinshan said, "Those who do not know how to turn their bodies and pass through the air shall not be allowed to drink this tea. Yantou said, "If that is the case, I certainly shall not be allowed to drink the tea."
Feng said, "I am the same as this person. Qin said, "These two fellows do not even recognize the *huatou*.
Tou asked, "Where has it gone? Qin said, "An old crow in a cloth bag; though alive, it is as if dead. Tou stepped back and said, "Look, look!"
Yunquan said, "Let us set aside Master Huo for a moment; what about Master Cunen? Feng drew a circle with his hand.
Yunquan said, "I cannot help but ask. Fong laughed heartily and said, "Too far! Yunquan remarked, "Many have mouths but do not get to drink tea."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Although Qinshan knew how to shift his body and breathe out, he still did not yet have the portion for drinking tea.
Why? The story remains. Ehu Xing said:
"Qinshan was much like the Immortal of Forbearance; though his limbs were severed one by one, his countenance did not change."
The guest said, "If that other son had been present at the time, he would have smashed the tea set right where you first asked the question;
there would have been no need for all this triviality.
When Qinshan was visited by a monk, he raised his fist and then opened his palm, saying, "When opened, it becomes a palm; the five fingers are distinct."
[Changqing] said, "No. He then clenched his fist and said, "Right now it is a fist; there is certainly no high or low. Tell me, does Mount Qin still allow for discussion?
A monk stepped forward and raised his fist. Changqing said, "In doing so, you are merely a man who knows nothing of opening or closing."
Xuedou Xian said, "I do not think so. He then raised his fist and said, "When clenched, it is a fist; there is high and low.

He then opened his hand and said, "When opened, it becomes a palm; there is no factionalism and no partiality. He continued, "Tell me, is it better to act for others by opening [the hand], or is it better to act for others by holding it fast?
Opening it is like building a carriage; clenching it is like fitting the wheels together. If you say one should 'build a carriage within the closed door'..."
"The wheels of the carts meet their tracks as they exit the gate. I also know that you are making your living inside a ghost cave.
Zhaojue Qin said: "The palm is also a hand; the grip is also a hand. What are you deliberating over? He then raised one foot and said:
"Extending it is also a foot; withdrawing it is also a foot. No high, no low—it allows for no deliberation."
Now tell me: are Nanquan and Qinshan the same or different?
Nantang Yu said: "Unfolding it is not the palm; grasping it is not the fist. Both ends are completely cut off."
A single sword leans against the sky, cold. Tell me, is there still a way to benefit others? *Shout!* The western wind blows over the Wei River;
fallen leaves fill Chang’an.
Gounan said: "To err by a hair's breadth is to lose by a thousand li. It is a pity that this man who lacks the ability to open and close was thoroughly deceived by Qingshan.
At that time, as soon as he heard the question raised, why did he not say, "Preceptor, do not speak in your sleep"?
He should have forced Qingshan to throw down his weapons and retreat. Xuedou speaking thus is merely following the heterodox and pursuing the misguided.
Wu Baiyan’s *Fuyun* says: "Qinshan was a man accustomed to using his influence to deceive others;
he was much like someone who merely sets fires to burn down the mountains himself, yet refuses to allow others to light lamps or eat their meals."

Volume Thirty-one and Volume Thirty-two. Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu,

△ Sixth in the Southern Lineage: Chan Master Baoying Huiyong of Nan’uan, Ruozhou (Successor of Xinghua Jiang). Ascending the hall, he said: “Upon this lump of red flesh, one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. A monk asked, “Is it not you, Master, who said that upon this lump of red flesh, one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high? The Master replied, “Yes. The monk said, “Then why do you still speak of the Way? The Master said, “I am speaking of the Way. The monk said, “If you speak of the Way, why do you say there is no Way? The Master said, “Because there is no Way, I speak of the Way. The monk said, “If there is no Way, how can you speak of it? The Master said, “If there were a Way, I would not speak of it. The monk said, “Since there is no Way, why do you speak of it? The Master said, “Because there is no Way, I speak of it. The monk said, “If there is no Way, what is the meaning of ‘one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high’? The Master said, “It is because there is no Way that one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. The monk said, “If there is no Way, what is the meaning of ‘upon this lump of red flesh’? The Master said, “It is because there is no Way that [the meaning] lies upon this lump of red flesh. The monk said, “If there is no Way, what is the meaning of ‘you’? The monk said, "Yes. The Master then overturned the meditation seat. The Abbot said, "This blind donkey is acting recklessly. As the monk hesitated, the Abbot struck him.
Jingshan Hongzhao said: "I now guarantee for you that this matter will never be in vain."
Tiantong Hua said: "This too is 'hooking a thief to ruin a house. Were it not for this monk daring to pull at the tiger's whiskers, how could one see the greatness of his merit in battle?
Nevertheless, I, the mountain monk, shall provide another path: upon this ball of red flesh, one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
If a monk comes forth, strike him across the back with the staff immediately. Why? Because it is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life."
A Sword. One with eyes looks at it.
Gushan Yong said: "Within the flash of lightning, the monastic and the lay are distinguished; without violating even a hair's breadth, he causes the entire clan to be extinguished."
Tianning Qisong said: "This monk dares to scratch his itch atop the head of a venomous snake and to strip away the scales beneath the chin of a blue dragon.
Who would not admire his great audacity? It is only that at the end he lacked one move. From the moment he emerged from the cave, there was no rival hand;
where he could have spared others, he chose to spare them."
Yunju Zhuang said, "Under a heavy reward, there will surely be brave men.
Qingshan Xiu said, "This monk was on the verge of completing a nine-cubit mountain, yet he lacked the final basket of earth to finish it."
Baoshou was about to offer a comment when [the Master] spoke on his behalf, saying: "I knew well enough that the Abbot would leave the dragon’s head and end with a snake’s tail.
Huangbo Qi said: "Nanyuan’s gate was solitary and steep; this monk’s stride was also extraordinary.

It was simply that he did not match the dragon’s head and snake’s tail, resulting in being punished and humiliated—a frustration that would kill a man. He should have waited until the other said, 'Blind fellow, you are acting recklessly...'"
He acted. He struck him across the face with his palm, teaching him to stand like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. To topple him all at once—was this not magnificent? Ziguixiu said:
"Although Nan'uan's display of letting go and seizing can be admired, he only knows how to exhaust the law and does not care whether there are no people left.
This monk was also 'a dragon's head and a snake's tail. If there had been a monk here who would have overturned the meditation seat," [he would have been truly great].
"Simply entrust it to the arrangement beneath the bright window.
Because of this, a monk asked Nan-yuan, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? Nan-yuan said, "The Minister Wang and the Palace Secretary Li.
The monk asked, "What is the intent of this? Nan-yuan said, "The ox-head goes south; the horse-head goes north."
Jingshan Daowei said: "The former answer hit the mark; the latter answer did not.
Mingyin Huai asked: "When Miaoxi spoke thus, tell me: did it accord with Nanquan’s meaning, or did it not accord with Nanquan’s meaning?"
A monk asked Nan-yuan, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? Nan-yuan said, "Neither ascending to heaven nor entering hell.
The monk asked, "And what about you, Master? Nan-yuan said, "Do you know where Old Baoying has fallen?
As the monk hesitated, Nan-yuan struck him across the mouth with his whisk and said, "Do you know who it is that eats this whisk?"
He said, "I do not understand. The Abbot said, "The order is for you to carry it out," and struck him again with the whisk.
Xuedou Xian said, "Since the order was carried out by himself, yet the whisk does not know its place of origin;
Xuedou says 'blind,' which is like adding frost to snow."
Huanglong Xin said: "In that case, while a flaw in a white jade disk may still be polished away, a malady in the vital organs (gao-huang) is most difficult to cure.
Since this monk’s command is already in your hands, why are you unable to carry it out? Where does the fault lie?"
Jingshan Daokai said: "To weigh and balance Linji’s Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, one must look to Nan-yuan.
Xuedou asked why [the whisk] does not know its place of origin; Miaoxi said "Blind!"—this was intended so that both might see each other.
Dongchan Guan said: "The Master ordered the monk to perform the act himself; why then did he do it himself?
One who is muddled might say, 'The whisk was in Nan-yuan’s hand. If that were so, not only would he be suppressing his own majestic light, but he would also fail to recognize Nan-yuan.
Xingkong says: although Nan-yuan ordered the monk to do it himself, he nevertheless struck him."
"Not attached.
Tianning Qi said: "Although Xuedou was a master of clear vision, he still did not know where Old Baoying had landed.
Since he did not know where Old Baoying had landed, for what reason did he instead say that 'the whisk does not know'?"
Regarding the place from which [the patriarchs] came: they possessed but a single eye. Miaoxi said, "Blind. This was like a neighbor mourning when a member of one household has died;
it is as if adding flowers upon brocade.
Kaixian Jin said, "A bystander clapping in approval. There is no lack of this "adding flowers upon brocade," yet Xuedou’s subtlety is unsurpassed.
If Xì were such a treasure, he would not have even dreamed of the place where he fell. Kaixian said, "Blind!
Yet, for now, let us set aside this separate path. Do you all know where Kaixian fell? He then descended from his seat.

Shuiguang said: "To part the hooves within the mouth of a fierce tiger, to snatch a sparrow from under the claws of a hungry eagle, and to strike bone for marrow with the agonizing application of needles and awls—such strategic maneuvers can only be performed by the true bone-and-flesh descendants of Linji."

Yunxi Ting said: "Setting aside for a moment whether Nan-yuan’s killing of the fellow was not a skillful move, as for Miaoxi reporting it in this manner—after all, to what level of mystery does this belong?"
Xuantai said: "Although Nan-yuan was skilled at seizing the drum and pulling down the banner, in the end he could not save himself.
Nan-yuan asked Feng-xue, 'How do you interpret a single blow in the South? Feng-xue replied, 'I interpret it as something extraordinary.
Nan-yuan then asked, 'And how do you interpret a single blow here in this place? Nan-yuan picked up his staff and said:"
"Under the staff, there is the patience of non-arising; facing the situation, one sees no teacher.
At these words, Fengxue attained great enlightenment. Jingshan Daokai said: "At that time, Fengxue should have fully spread his sitting mat and prostrated three times to him.
Otherwise, he should have overturned the meditation seat. He then turned to his attendant and said: "Tell me, did Fengxue prostrate at that time?"

Faying said, "This overturning of the meditation seat is it. Zhaozhou said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. Xuedou Gao said, "Look at this blind fellow making a mess of things," and he struck him.
Qingshan Xiu said, "Xuefeng’s awakening was not without merit, but alas, he fell into the second place. As for me, the mountain monk..."
If one were to act as the Abbot of the Southern Courtyard and wait for someone to ask, "How do you adjudicate this single blow?
one would strike them across the spine immediately, ensuring they become thoroughly proficient and unimpeded in all directions.
Baiyan Fu said: "In the past, while engaged in a formal discussion with Master Sheng of Tianjie, I raised this point.
Tianjie said, 'If I were Nan'uan, when asked how I would handle the matter of "a single blow here," I would simply strike him right across the face.
Fu remarked, 'Master, you are indeed capable of reaching the ultimate point. Tianjie then countered by questioning me in turn."
"What about you, Elder? Fu then rose from his seat and said, "Not considering that the Master is advanced in years;
even though my fist was sore and my hand aching, I would not let go. He then departed.
Nanyuan ascended the hall. "People everywhere possess the eye of 'simultaneous pecking and hatching,' but they do not possess the function of 'simultaneous pecking and hatching.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the function of simultaneous pecking and hatching? Nanyuan said, "A master does not peck or hatch."
"The simultaneous act of pecking and hatching has been missed. The monk said, "This is still not where I was asking. The abbot asked, "Where were you asking?
The monk said, "Missed. The abbot then struck him. The monk did not accept this.
Cuiyan Zhen said: "To deploy strategy within the tent is to secure victory a thousand *li* away.
Although Nanyuan may have fully deployed his tactics against the enemy, alas, the terrain is vast and the men are few."
Taisu Zhe said: "Nanyuan held high the ancestral seal, seizing and relinquishing according to the occasion. This monk was well able to meet the challenge and resist the enemy;
yet, alas, his strength was exhausted and his stratagems were spent. Is there now any monk of true substance? Come forth and meet with Daimu.
It is not for the sake of stirring up a clamor, but rather because we desire that the spirit of the school not fall into decline. Is there such a one?
"How is it? If it is not so, then today at Dayu, it is as if one has sought battle but achieved no merit.
Yunju Wu said: "What is the eye of simultaneous pecking and hatching? If the eye attains clarity, its function is naturally complete.
He also said: "The master does not peck and hatch; pecking and hatching simultaneously is missing the mark. Why does he not peck and hatch?"
Therefore it is said: "If the son roars, the mother perishes. Can you all yet understand this? He then spoke in verse: "If the son roars, the mother perishes;
It returns entirely to the son, pervading the ten directions. When the great function manifests, the principle is spontaneous;
Why need one give rise to thoughts or create artificial forms? If you still do not understand, Yunju’s staff—"
The staff.
Later, while at Yunmen’s assembly, this monk heard two monks raise this same story. One monk asked, "At that time, why did Nan-yuan's staff break?
Suddenly, the monk attained awakening. He then hurried back to pay his respects, but Nan-yuan had already passed away. He then went to visit...
Fengxue asked, "Are you the monk who at that time asked the former master about the saying, 'The chick and the hen peck at the same moment'?
He replied, "I am. Fengxue said, "How did you understand it then? He replied, "At that time, I was as if walking within the light of a lamp. Fengxue said, "You have understood."
Langya Huijue said: "This monk only knows how to hoist the white flag of surrender; he does not know how to seize the sword and halberd.
Cuiyan Zhen quoted the words of Fengxue, saying: "At that time, I would have waited for this monk to attempt a response, and then struck him across the mouth with my sitting mat."
Taisuī Zhe said, "Fengxue, for all his greatness, has instead splashed people with foul water. Daomai was not like this;
at that time, it was as if I were walking within the light of a lamp, and I could have simply said, 'The late master's flesh is still warm.
You, with such a view, would have been struck down from the Dharma Hall with my staff, so as to avoid being left alone."
Regarding Nan’uan, Dongchan Guan said: "To uphold the teaching style of Nan’uan, one must still look to Fengxue.
Though people everywhere often say that he was a monk who could 'accept' [the challenge], they fail to realize that this monk was actually pushed by him into a ten-thousand-fathom pit."
Nanjian asked: "When the whole mechanism overcomes the enemy, it is like grass bowing before the wind. To uphold the supreme纲宗 (guiding principles) requires an old man like Nan-yuan.
This monk later attained enlightenment, but he only knew how to surrender; he did not understand how to pull down the flag and slay the generals.
At that time, Fengxue should have waited for him to say 'Yes,' and then struck him out with a continuous series of blows."
The monks might perhaps establish their own livelihood separately, so as to avoid having later generations groping for it amidst the shadows of the lamp.

[The Master] suddenly brandishes his staff and says: "If there is anyone today who can act as the host for this monk, come forth and meet the staff of this mountain monk! If there is none, then today I have lost out."

Zifu Guang said: "I read the biography of Zhao Kuo and lamented that he was merely able to recite his father’s books without knowing how to observe the mechanisms of the situation or adapt to changing circumstances.
Consequently, he lost his army, suffered a loss of prestige, and died at the hands of the enemy. This was not the case with those such as Lian Po;
they observed the mechanisms of the situation and adapted to changes, being thoroughly proficient in every step. It is through this that one comes to know a true master."
"If the pecking and the hatching do not coincide, they are both lost at once; the meaning of this is profound.
Baiyan Fu said: "The various elders of past and present have each displayed their own insights and hands, and it is not that they failed to uphold the style of their own school;
yet, as for the resolution of Nanquan, how is it any different from scratching an itch through a boot? Shoushan said: "If you..."
"When I am sitting, you must stand; when I am standing, you must sit. Here, one has never even found a head or a nose;
how could one hope for the walls of Nan-yuan? It is more than a thousand li away.
A monk asked Nan’yan, “The sun and moon alternate in their passing; cold and heat shift in succession. What is that which does not involve cold or heat?
Nan’yan said, “A purple silk head-wrap and an embroidered waist-skirt. The monk said, “I have now understood the higher mechanism.
How would those of middling or inferior capacity comprehend this? Nan’yan said, “Hide yourself inside a charcoal storehouse.”
Huguo Long said: "The question already possesses the fundamental principle, and the answer likewise startles the multitude.
Nevertheless, Nan-yuan only knew how to observe the faculties of others to meet their needs and apply medicine according to the illness; Huguo further provides another path. If someone were to ask:
'As the days and months pass by and the cold and heat alternate, what is that which does not involve the cold and heat? one should say to him: 'Before...'"
Deep in the village amidst the snow, last night a single branch blossomed. The upward-moving pivot has now been revealed;
how shall those of middling or inferior capacity understand it? It is said: "Buy a hat to match the head."
Baoshou Xin said: "Although Nan-yuan and Huqiu each displayed their own strategic maneuvers, in the end they were not two different things.
Suppose someone asks me, the New Abbot: 'The sun and moon alternate in their passing, and cold and heat shift in succession;

what is that which does not involve cold or heat? I would say to him: 'What an excellent question! The upward-reaching mechanism is now clear to those of superior capacity, but for those of middling or inferior capacity—"
How would you explain this? He then gave him a slap right on the head. Tell me, how far apart is he from the ancients?
Try to examine them together and see. If you can harmonize them, you will be able to widely extol the transformation of the Dharma and assist in upholding the true wind.
"If that were not yet so," [the Master] said, "the new abbot has more to say. He then struck his whisk and descended from the seat.
Once, when a monk came to visit Nan-yuan, as soon as he entered the abbot’s quarters, Nan-yuan pointed at him with his finger and said, "Defeated!
He then picked up his staff and handed it to the monk; as the monk was about to take it, Nan-yuan struck him.
Yunfeng Yue said: "This monk has light upon his head, yet he does not know that beneath his feet he is as black as lacquer. But how about this?
Even if you were to move with the ten directions at once, it would still be right to give him three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening."
The *Tianbao Shu* says: "At that time, as soon as this monk saw Nan-yuan about to take up his staff, he should have let out a thunderous shout and swept out of the hall with his sleeves.
Even if Nan-yuan had possessed the full power to kill or give life, it would still have been like drawing a bow after the thief has already fled."
A monk asked Nan-yuan, "What is it like when an ancient hall is restored? Nan-yuan said, "The roof tiles of the Hall of Brightness reach down to the eaves.
The monk said, "In that case, the adornments are complete. Nan-yuan said, "When the grass is cut, the snake's head falls off."

Zhaoqing Ting said: "The poor man thinks of the treasure place, yet points his finger toward the conjured city. If he were suddenly to wander off and lose both home and livelihood, what would happen in the end?
One must know that the person who weeps over the jade has, quite unexpectedly, brought about total ruin."
Chan Master Kebin of Shanfang Yuan on Mount Daxing (the sixth successor of Xinghua Jue in the South):
One day, Xinghua said, "Venerable Vinaya Master, before long you will become a leading teacher. Kebin replied, "I will not enter your community.

Xinghua asked, "Do you refuse to enter because you understand, or because you do not understand? Kebin said, "It is neither like this nor that. Xinghua then struck him and said, "Kebin, the Vinaya Master..."
In that dharma-battle he was defeated. As punishment, he was fined five strings of cash and required to provide a single meal of steamed rice.

On the following day at the time for the midday meal, Huaihai struck the wooden gavel himself and said, "The Rector Kebin has been defeated in the dharma-battle; he shall not eat this meal," and immediately drove him out of the monastery.
Xuedou Xian said: "Kebìn wanted to inherit the lineage of Xinghua. Let us set aside for a moment the matter of the fine and his expulsion from the monastery;
he must first receive that one blow of the staff before it is complete. Now I ask you all: since the blow has already been taken, how can it be recovered?
Xuedou wishes to settle this injustice; tonight I shall vindicate Kebìn. [He then held up] his staff.
The staff struck them all at once, dispersing them.

Huanglong Nan said: "Kebin lost his money and suffered punishment; though he had reason, it could not be vindicated. Xinghua used the rigid to decide the flexible, yet this is not enough to be admired.
One must also submit a formal document to take full responsibility."
Taisu Zhe said: "Although Xinghua’s command was carried out, it was much like using one's power to intimidate others.
Although Kebin lost the tactical advantage for a time, how could his fame and glory not remain undiminished through the ages? But tell me, where does the point of victory or defeat lie?
If one has not endured many battles on the field, the deafening war drums will surely sweep away the red dust."
Baizhang Yuan said: "From ancient times until now, the monastic communities have all claimed that only one who knows gratitude can understand how to repay it.
To speak in such a manner is to truly bury the ancients. But tell me, how do you all perceive this Kebin the Rector?
Do you wish to understand? Although he burned incense for Xinghua, for his part—"
"Perfuming the heavens and scorching the earth.
Yunju Shun said, "In a great forge, refined gold should remain unchanged in color. Yet, how could it be otherwise when Xinghua’s commands were so strict?
Even for Kebin the *weina*, this would have been difficult to bear. As for those who nowadays are merely drifting along—
Futile! How much time has been spent merely turning over one's skin?
Jingshan Daokai said, "Yunju twists the crooked to make it straight. Miaoxi said, "If you wish to be a descendant of Linji..."
"You must truly turn over your skin before you can succeed.
Tiantong Hua said, "The great Xuedou and the rector Kebin have cleared their grievances, yet there is still no 'killing blow' (the final decisive word)."
Zhongfeng Ben said: "There are commands that are not carried out and matters that remain unresolved; this is a public malady of the world.
Yet Xinghua both carried out [the command] and resolved [the matter]; he could not avoid being laughed at by onlookers."
Nantang Yu said: "When Master Xinghua Quan went out to battle, Kebin held his walls firm and did not fight.
When his strength was exhausted and his skills spent, he could not avoid being forced to surrender his ox and璧 (jade).
Xuedou wished to settle this injustice and directly vindicated Kebin’s grievance. Do you understand? Though he won one victory, he lost both his feet.
Tianning Qisong said: "Kebin was defeated in the battle of Dharma; Xinghua acted according to the command.
He upheld the style of the Linji school and revealed the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye. From the tip of the staff comes the filial son; in the Buddha-dharma, there is no partiality."
"At that time, I thought it was merely a matter of the length of the reeds; only after burning them did I realize the ground was uneven.
Tongxuan Qi said, "Xinghua’s way of dealing with people can truly be called entering deep into a tiger’s den, yet he simply failed to get the tiger cub.
Although Kebin gnashed his teeth and took the blows, it was very much like returning to one's hometown in a dream. If one were truly clever..."
As for this patch-robed monk, he would surely have managed to break Xinghua’s staff.
Qixia Cheng said: "Xinghua’s striking of the gavel was born of a grandmotherly heart; Kebin’s expulsion from the monastery stemmed from deep maternal affection.
The predecessors of old thus stimulated and exalted one another; how could they have even dreamed of [the notion that] father and son cannot be cut down by an axe?"
The Opening: "What is called 'three-tiered waves high, the fish transforms into a dragon; the deluded man still uses a scoop to bail out the water from a night pond'?
Lingyan Chu said, "Although Xinghua’s [action] was such that there was not even space for a hair between them, he went far too far in relying on his power to deceive others.
Kebin was indeed able to maintain consistency from beginning to end, yet he could not avoid perpetuating his father's faults. Old Man Shun was sufficient, yet he twisted it."
To make the crooked straight: for the time being, the cart shall not be pushed sideways. Because of his compassion, Miaoxi (Wumen) has spoken these words that descend into the weeds.
Furthermore, Xinxing’s transformation of beings does not reside here at all. Have you not heard that it was Yao who governed the world by simply hanging his robes?
The use of sound and color to transform the people is but a secondary matter. How could the gentleman not be sincere?
Truly so. Master Nengren (Jiandun) said: "When Xinghua’s command was being carried out, the rector felt some resentment. Xuedou, acting as rector, cleared his grievance.
But would Xinghua have been willing [to accept this]? If it were not for Yang Deyi, how could one recognize Ma Xiangru?
Baokong Fayun said: "Everyone says that when one fails in the 'Subduing the Disciple' (Kebin) dharma-battle, one is fined and expelled from the monastery.
Yet they do not realize that Xinghua has been pinned down by him; to this day, he cannot rise. Now tell me, where does the point of advantage and disadvantage lie?"
Those with the eye of wisdom discern this.
Longhua Ti said, "A great man’s majestic virtue cannot be bent; this was seen in Kebin.
Nevertheless, had it not been for Xinghua, how could the merit of his distinguished service have been revealed?
Guangjiao Yuyun said: "Everyone says that the gate and walls of Xinghua were eight thousand feet high;

yet how could one see the greatness of his meritorious service on the battlefield of sweat and blood if it were not for Kebin’s bare-shouldered carrying of the burden? Little do they realize that at the Dragon Gate there are no guests who stay overnight—thunderbolts send the soaring ones up. He struck his staff once.
Fayun said: "Since Kebin was a disciple who had entered the inner chamber of Xinghua, he would rather dwell outside the gate;

when will it be that he is neither struck nor punished? Although this is so, three cups of wine adorn the face of a young gentleman, and a single branch of flowers is tucked into the hair of a beautiful woman."
Baiyan Fu said: "The guest remains the guest from beginning to end; the host remains the host from beginning to end.
To support the true lineage of Linji, we must acknowledge Xinghua and his son. As for those who say, 'You will soon become a leading teacher'—you thief!"
"You understand, yet you do not enter; you do not understand, yet you do not enter. Thief! Thief! At that moment, those two words "thief" were truly effective;
had they not been used, one would have seen a chaotic scene. Little did you know that the treading of dragons and elephants is not something a donkey can endure.
Baizhang Yun said: "Naked, one thrusts against the white blade; drawing the sword, one stirs the Dragon Gate. One must indeed be an heroic man to do this.
Since Xinghua shifted the stars and changed the constellations, Kebin simply took the wrong for the right.

But tell me, what was the intent behind these two elders acting thus? Only after the snow has fallen does one know the steadfastness of the pine and cypress; only when affairs are difficult is their true character revealed.
Regarding the "Mind of the Great Man":
Attendant Kuok (Nanlu Xinghua Jiang’s successor) asked Deshan, “Where have all the sages of antiquity gone? Deshan said, “What? What?
Kuok said, “When the Emperor summons the flying dragon horse, the lame tortoise sticks its head out. Deshan then ceased speaking.
The next day, as they were coming out from their mountain bath, Xuankuo passed some tea to Xuefeng. Xuefeng patted Xuankuo’s back once and said, “What about yesterday’s koan?
Xuankuo replied, “This old fellow only just now has had a glimpse of reality. Xuefeng then let it rest.
Xuedou Xian said, "However, even refined gold must undergo a hundred smeltings to require the hammer of one's own true nature.
Since Deshan used himself as a standard for others, this monk likewise suffered a defeat. [Xuedou] drew a line with his staff and said, 'Setting aside the case just presented for a moment:
where have all the sages of antiquity gone? As the assembly hesitated, he drove them all away at once."

Huanglong Nan said: "Deshan maintained deafness and feigned dumbness; although he secretly gained the advantage, Master Kuok covered his ears while stealing the bell—how could he avoid the laughter of onlookers?"
Baoneng Xiu said: "This is not merely a matter of stealing a bell. It is like plucking a pearl from beneath the chin of a black dragon at the bottom of a ninefold abyss while the dragon is asleep;
were it to wake, one would surely be reduced to minced powder."
Taisu Zhè said: "If one does not ascend the Dragon Gate, how can one know the depth of the vast ocean?
Even if the waves surge a thousand fathoms high, what can be done if the Dragon King pays them no heed?"
Yunju Yuan said: "In general, for there to be one guest and one host, they must be cognizant of each other; only when they share the same death and the same life can they withstand the enemy.
Attendant Kuang stood alone upon a precipitous cliff, turning his body around to pull at the tiger’s whiskers."
Vajra Zhou sat peacefully in the heart of the great ocean waves. With his back turned, he grasped the horn of a qilin with his hands crossed behind him.
He drew up battle lines before Mount Dandaka and sought to contend for supremacy within the kingdom of Campā. Clearly there were losses and victories;
tell me, who won and who lost? I ask you all to judge this.
Baoneng Xiu said: "If one were asked, 'Where have all the sages of antiquity gone? Baosong would immediately give them a slap across the jaw and say, 'They are right here!
This would cause even a soaring dragon and a lame tortoise to shrink their necks and clench their hooves, leaving attendant Deshan with his鋒 (edge) lost and his tongue tied.
Nevertheless, do you still recognize this old fellow Deshan? When he was young..."
He resolved the dragon-and-serpent formation; the old man once again listens to the song of a child.
Nantang was about to say: "Deshan is certainly a master smith, possessing the essential tongs and hammers;
yet how can he help it that Attendant Kuò is gold already refined? Let him judge others by his own standard—after all, there is no room for grievance."
"Receiving. Lingyan’s critique was thus. Is there anyone who can act as a patron for Xuedou?
Boshan Lai said: "Deshan’s single staff was usually dripping with blood;
why then is it not used here? Do you understand? He draws the transverse bone from the dark, and sits upon the tongue in the light."
Gounan said: "To thrust one's body across the mouth of a fierce tiger; to rub an itch on the head of a venomous snake.
One out, one in; one push, one shove—truly a fine hand at it. Xuedou presents this case thus:
setting aside all the sages of antiquity for a moment, where have this crew gone? "Pitiful are the countless tide-surfers; in the end..."
He fell back into the tide and died.
Zifu Guang said: "One who sticks their head out too far falls into pits and ditches without realizing it;

one who overreaches in deploying a stratagem to lure the enemy rushes southward only to suffer defeat without protest. A marvelous strategy and divine calculation such as this has been peerless since antiquity. Wait until—"
The eye opened and the sword was gone long ago.
Baryak Pu said: "Master Kwang’s single period of brilliance left nothing for bystanders to criticize; yet the karmic connection of Deishan raising a child cost him a great deal of milk and blood.
As for the place where all the sages go—*tok!* The sword was gone long ago, and you only now begin to carve it."
Regarding the boat:
Lianfu Ce said, "Old Kuò’s wheel and whip penetrate deeply; yet, alas, his striking is ineffective.
Dēngshān withdrew his troops twice, only knowing how to yield to the enemy in the dark. If one lets it pass, both are masters of the craft; if one examines it closely, however—"

Overall, one essential point is missing. Nevertheless, even so, it is not as if he has not long served in the ranks of the battlefield; his great drum resounds to the heavens, putting the red dust to flight.
Shoukuo, while traveling on pilgrimage, arrived at Huayan in Xiangzhou. There, Master Yan ascended the hall and said: "O Great Assembly! If today..."
The descendants of Linji, Deshan, Gaoteng, Dayu, Niaoke, and Chuanzi—do not bother with "how" or "what.
Simply request to enter directly with a single blade, and Huayan shall provide you with verification. Kuo stepped forward, bowed, and as he rose, he let out a shout.
Huayan also shouted. Kuo shouted again; Huayan shouted once more. Kuo bowed and said, "O Great Assembly, behold this old fellow’s performance!"

[Changsha] fell into defeat. He then gave another shout, clapped his hands, and returned to the assembly. Yanguan then descended from the seat and returned to his quarters. At that time, Fengxue was serving as the *karmadāna* (Rector).
When he went up to offer his greetings, Yanguan said, "Rector, you have come. It is truly intolerable that Shoukuo just now twisted and squeezed me so much.
I am waiting for the assembly to gather so I can give him a beating and drive him out. Fengxue said, "It would be too late to drive him out [now]."
"I understand. It was the Master’s own words that were excessive. He is a descendant of Linji; it is his fundamental nature to be thus.
Please, Master Yan, let your anger subside. Later, Xue went down to report this to Guo. Guo said, "For what reason did you try to persuade that fellow?
Before I had even asked him, he already wanted to eat my staff. Now that he has caused my words to be put into practice, if I do not beat him now, I am effectively nullifying those words of mine."
Xue said, "Even so, it has already spread throughout the world.

Tiantong Wu, distinguishing himself from Huayan, said with a tone that quelled the anger: "If I, this old monk, were Huayan, I would have struck him out with a continuous succession of blows, such that Fengxue would not have dared to transmit his words or deliver his phrases."
Fuyan Rong said: "The *Avataṃsaka* has a dragon’s head but a snake’s tail; it could not cause Master Kuok to submit through realization.
Had I been the mountain monk, when I saw him say, 'The great assembly is watching this old fellow,' before my voice had even died away, I would have struck him out with a staff.
Not only would there have been two masters of the way, but it would have further shown that the *Avataṃsaka*’s command was not being carried out in vain."
Nanjian asked: "Beneath two tigers, even a beast cannot fit its hoof; between two blades, a man cannot fit his foot.
The *Avataṃsaka* Sūtra’s single-period arrangement may indeed be called a majestic and rigorous command.

Yet I do not know that Shoukuo was a man who had already broken free from the cage—one who charges crosswise and straight ahead, deploying and retracting at will, until finally this old fellow was forced to lay down his burden."
Jià reversed his halberd; dragon’s head, snake’s tail. Even after a thousand years, how can one avoid being scrutinized by others?
I dare ask you all: where exactly was Huáyán’s point of failure? Suddenly, he took up his staff and said:
"To support and uphold [the Way] requires a hand of heroic spirit; to manifest it requires a person of transcendent capacity."
Zifu Guang said: "Fierce as thunder and lightning, yet resolving like wind and rain—this is the playful sport of the patch-robed monks (sōng).
Yet why did Huayan wish to strike the bell to challenge Master Kuang? Was it to launch an attack from behind the lines, or was there some other underlying principle?
Let those with the eye of discernment try to explain."
Jingci Yan said: "The Avataṃsaka Sūtra did not fail to open its shop from the very beginning. Alas, it was a case of a dragon's head and a snake's tail;
thus, the Great Sword was handed over in reverse, allowing Han to completely defeat Chu, resulting in a lingering regret for a thousand years.
Nowadays, those who merely parrot the words claim that the Avataṃsaka does not know how to act as the host to the end. If it were today..."
This person did not wait for Shoukuo to bow and rise before striking him with a severe blow.
Not only could he thus avoid the fate of "feeding a tiger and having his body harmed," but he would surely come to stand alone as the sole sovereign within the realm.

Such stubbornness arises because his prior training was not profound and he has not encountered the right person since; therefore, every word he utters and every breath he exhales is entirely devoid of shame. Thus it is obtained.
"One will not be ridiculed by those who possess true discernment.
Baoyan Fu said: "The various quarters each display their own hands and eyes; it is not that they lack excellence in having sturdy shields and sharp spears.
However, if one wishes to meet with the two elders of Huayan, Shou and Kuok, I dare not grant permission. Baoyan did not hesitate to commit this offense.
Caution! I dare speak these straightforward words: Fengxue fell into a trap while still in the hands of those two elders;
this goes without saying. Yet, who would have known that the spiritual powers of Huayan Shoukuo were no ordinary matter?
Do you understand this thoroughly? Aside from Mr. Chen of Mount Hua, who among people does not walk about burdened with right and wrong?
Chan Master Ximing Siming of West Yuan in汝州 (a successor of Nanliu Baoshou Zhao) was invited by his fellow practitioner, Master Yong, to reside at South Yuan.
He went to visit him; as soon as they had exchanged greetings, [Siming] said, "I have come from Xuzhou, and I have no gift to present."
Xiyuan presented a razor from Jiangxi to the Abbot, saying, "I have obtained this. Nan'uan asked, "You have come from Xuzhou;
why have you instead brought a razor from Jiangxi? Xiyuan then pinched Nan'uan’s hand.

"Lalala alalala. Guishan Zhe said, "Although Xiyuan managed to acquire the razor of Jiangxi, he had nowhere to display it;

"Look! As if there were nothing. [The Master asked: "What do you usually use?
Xiyuan was once asked by a monk: "When a student has a question to pose to the Master, what then?
Xiyuan said: "Even if it were presented, I would cut it into three pieces. The monk bowed, and Xiyuan then ceased speaking. A monk in the assembly remarked: "The Hall..."

The monk who had been questioning him then dragged the other monk up to the abbot’s quarters and reported, "This monk refuses to accept the Master's words. The Abbot asked, "Is it that you, Senior Monk, refuse to accept me?"
The monk said, "I have never been conscious of such a matter, nor have I ever spoken of it. The Abbot then shouted at him once and sent him down.

When the monk reached the Dharma Hall, he spoke again, saying, "What do you mean by 'too much'? It is not yet finished right here! The monk who had asked the question then dragged that monk to the Abbot’s quarters.
The Abbot said, "Is it true, Senior Monk, that you do not accept me? The monk replied, "Do not believe this fellow; today—"
Three times he saw that [the master] manifest his wind, and then he pursued him all at once.
Yunyan said, "Xingshan had eyes on the tip of his staff; this monk acted according to the occasion.
But if one examines it closely, he was entirely made to go up and down by that fellow carrying a single board."
