Langya Jue said, "If it were not for Sansheng, how could we reach this day? Although this is so, many misunderstand it.
Taisu Xiu said: "Baoshou acted as the general; why then did Sansheng act as the central command?

It is a pity that the people of the entire city of Zhenzhou have, to this day, failed to distinguish east from west. However, where there is public censure, there must be some place where the 'flute was stolen' [i.e., a point of error].
Had he driven out Sansheng at that time, he surely would have saved the people of the entire city of Zhenzhou."
"Eye. Le Tan Zhun said: "When Sansheng praised Baoshou’s appearance in the world, it was indeed excellent;
yet, he only managed to grasp one fragment."
Zhao of Mount Gui said: "Baoshou is much like an Emperor issuing his decrees within the realm;
Sansheng is like a General beyond the borders executing his orders. Is there anyone who does not spare their own life? Come forth and meet this old monk!
Today this old monk intends to settle matters of injustice. After a long silence, he said: "Transversely grasping the Mohe sword, [he is] fully..."
The Correct Command: "In the Great Peace of the Realm, the dull and stubborn are severed.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Baoshou’s total exertion in taking up the burden is indeed extraordinary; however, he only sees one side.
Had he then skillfully revealed the Treasury of the True Dharma-Eye of Linji, when Sanxing said, 'If it were so...'"
To act as a person is not merely for the blind; the monk’s own eyes are blind, and he has blinded the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
I shall immediately provide him with his rightful fodder. Why? Because once one has made the first move, one does not stop until the second is completed.
Tiantong Hua said: "Everyone says that Baoshou and Sansheng were masterful smelters and essential tongs and hammers; what connection does this have?
Little do they realize that these two great elders, having been pressed once by this monk, remain until this very day unable to rise.
Is there anyone today who can clear their names? Come forth and [compete with] Mingguo!"
They met face to face. [Zhaozhou] suddenly picked up his staff, threw it down, and said, "It is easy to distinguish dragons from snakes;
it is difficult to deceive a patch-robed monk. Tiantong Jie said, "While these two venerable masters are indeed excellent, if one wishes to uphold the true lineage of Linji, [one must go further]."
"Each person must receive a blow of the staff before they can attain it. Now tell me, where is the deficiency? Those with the eye of discernment should try to determine this for themselves.
Dongchan Guan said: "Everyone says that Sansheng had the 'work' of crossing the rushing current and passing through the blade, yet he did so upon level ground."
Surging waves and billows. Baoshou employed the mechanism of a "flaming fire passing through the wind" to thunder a clap of lightning within empty space.
These two elders each extended a hand to uphold the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of Linji.
To speak in such a manner while wishing to be a descendant of Linji—wait, slow down! Xingkong said: "How can a mosquito support a great pillar? The lotus...
How could a single thread bind Mount Sumeru? If this were truly the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of Linji, it would surely have been extinguished with the two elders.
Lingyin Yue said: "The two venerable seniors, in their casual jostling and pressing one another, directly revealed the essence of Linji."
The "Essence of Mind" (Cittasāra) merely fails to realize that life and destiny are entirely in the hands of this monk. Is there anyone who can discern this?
Longxiang Yin said: "Chopping nails and cutting iron to manifest the true mechanism beyond the norm; gathering and releasing to reveal [the ultimate]."
Revealing the true eye of the present moment, it directly causes dragons to roar as mist rises and tigers to howl as the wind stirs;
a single ray of divine light penetrates both past and present. Even such a proclamation still involves the journey along the path.
But tell me, what is the saying for arriving home and sitting securely? "The three-fold robe beyond the green peaks; a censer of agarwood amidst the white clouds."
Yangshan Qian said: "One gathering and one releasing; there is host and guest. This is merely ordinary fare, yet among them, Baoshou and Sansheng are still one step ahead.
How can this be seen? If one lacks the strength to lift the cauldron and pull the mountain, the black steed will not easily be ridden for a thousand li."
Nantang Yu said: "Hand and eye pervade the entire body; fist and kick correspond with one another.
Baoshou and Sansheng were indeed masters, yet if you wish to reveal the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of Linji, they have not yet reached it. Xuedou said:
"If this monk had been a true man, he would have overturned the meditation seat. He was not an archer capable of shooting down a falcon; he merely spoke of Li [Longji]."
General Wushidao said:
"Baoshou employed the tactics of the powerful armies of Qin and Chu; the Three Sages devised the stratagems of Sun Wu and Wu Qi for annexation.
Each possessed the bearing of a sovereign, desiring to unify the borders so that the myriad people might enjoy peace and prosperity."
"It has not yet been attained. Why? 'The Great Peace was originally brought about by the General; it is not permitted for the General to witness the Great Peace.
Jingshan Xiu said: "Baoshou and Sansheng revealed the True Dharma-Eye Treasury of Linji; it is truly a matter of decisive severance."
It is like nailing down iron; alas, those who can truly take it up are few. Since Xuedou holds the authority in his hands, he ought to have vindicated this monk.
What does it matter what happened "at that time"? Do you understand? If one lacks the strength to lift the cauldron and pull the mountain, the black steed of a thousand *li* is not easy to ride.

Dongshan Fu said: "Although these two great elders were such that not even a drop of water leaked through, they could not avoid leading people to wander into the fray of right and wrong, victory and defeat.
Today, when I open the hall, if someone pushes a monk forward, I shall neither use the staff nor the shout; I will simply say to him, 'I am not as good as you. If he..."
To act as a teacher in such a manner not only blinds the eyes of the monks, but it goes so far as to blind the eyes of the entire city of Yue.
Nevertheless, one may still say to him, "Blind! But tell me, how does this differ from the ancients?
Those who have not yet passed through the barrier, look closely!
Dongming Ji raised up the words of Tiantong Jie and concluded by saying: "If we discuss upholding the true lineage of Linji, it is not merely that these two elders received blows;
even if every person throughout the entire world were to receive blows, one would still only have upheld half of it.
Why? Have you not heard it said: 'To devote oneself to heterodox paths is harmful'?"
Nanjian asked: "These two elders were the direct bone-and-son descendants of Linji; thus they were able to reveal the very marrow of Linji before the assembly of devas and humans.
It is a pity that at that time there was no one to take up their mantle, which caused these two great elders to be unable to turn themselves around and breathe freely."
Kaixian Jin said: "To cultivate openly while crossing over in secret is not without the Three Sages; to decide victory and deploy strategy is still due to Baoshou.
It may be so, but as for the Way of the Three Sages—to act for others in such a manner does nothing but blind the eyes of monks."
"The eyes of the entire city of Zhinzhou have been blinded! I do not know how you all understand this.
As soon as the Sleeping Dragon stirs, the Vermilion Phoenix soars."
Qixia Chengyun said: "Wind-sweeping and lightning-rolling; the seas shake and the mountains tremble. These two elders have indeed produced works that startle the multitude.
Yet, when one examines their actual substance, they cannot avoid being nothing more than a hollow performance.
This not only brings laughter to the bystanders, but has also been seen through coldly by this monk."
Daofeng Qingyun said: "Baoshou upheld the ancestral command; it did not merely blind the people of the entire city of Zhinzhou, but rendered the ten directions dark and the sun and moon lightless.

Had it not been for Sansheng holding aloft the ancient mirror, everyone would have been left groping along walls and leaning against fences. Today, as no one has come forth to push Daofeng forward," [he continued].
When a monk approaches, this mountain monk likewise does not strike him with his staff; yet, he intends to blind the eyes of all people in the world.
Tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie? Holding up his staff, he says: "A single mass of white clouds spans the mouth of the valley;
how many returning birds are utterly lost in their nests?"

Dongta Xi said: "I want to overturn Xuedou’s case. Even if that monk, as soon as he was pushed out, had overturned the meditation seat, it would still have been merely staring eyes from within a coffin;
what use would there have been? If that monk had truly been a man of substance, as soon as he was pushed out, he would have simply said 'Take care' and departed.
Not only would the entire assembly have had the opportunity to witness his brilliance, but it would also have made both [Xuefeng and Xuedou]..."
Old Yiji suspected he had been killed.
Bairyam Pu said: "These two great elders exerted all their strength to manifest the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of Linji;
yet, in the end, they could not avoid being coldly laughed at from behind the back by that monk."
Baoshou was formerly the master of offerings at Baoshou Pond. The Master of the Pond asked him, "Before your parents were born, bring me back your original face.
Baoshou stood there until late at night, but his response did not accord with the truth. The next day, he took his leave. The Master said, "Where are you going?
Baoshou replied, "Yesterday I received the Master’s question, but I could not accord with it; I am going south to seek instruction from other teachers."
When the good friend was about to depart, Zhao said, "In the south, summer retreat is observed but winter is not; here in my region, winter retreat is observed but summer is not.
You should spend the summer as a street monk. If it is the Buddha-dharma, then even amidst the vast dust and clamor of the marketplace, the True Dharma is constantly being preached.
Shou did not dare to disobey. One day, he saw two people quarreling on the street and struck one with a single punch.
Yunmen said, "You have attained such facelessness. At these words, Shou attained great enlightenment.
Zhaojue Qin said, "Striking it, bumping into it—right at the head, the local scenery of the original ground is revealed; responding to sound, responding to form."
"Directly beneath, there is not even a hair’s breadth of leakage. Do you still recognize how he could speak with such facelessness?
"The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the whole body is revealed.
Qingshan Xiu said: "To have such facelessness—alas! One has run right into it amidst the brocade and embroidery. White Cloud.
Buried alive within a mound of earth, one clearly perceives the local scenery; one’s true face remains ever-present.
*Ai!* Zen Master Rizhao of Jizhou Zifu (Nanliu Xita Mu-si). A monk asked: "What was the intent behind the ancients' raising of the mallet and brandishing of the whisk?
Rizhao said: "The ancients acted thus. The monk asked: "And what about raising the mallet and brandishing the whisk? Rizhao—
He then shouted and drove him out.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "What kind of eyes did that ancient have? A monk asked, "If the Master acts like this, when will you ever understand?
Yunmen then called to the monk, "Come here, come here. As the monk approached, Yunmen struck him in the mouth with his whisk.
"Strike! [The Master] said. "The topknot jewel is a cloud. Here, it is not so. When the ancients raised their mallets or held up their fly-whisks, what was their intent?
It is said: 'Frequent calls for Little Jade are originally for no reason; one only wishes for the lover to recognize the sound. If this monk..."
This is a man who knows a cow by seeing its horns; here he must surely be able to reveal a glimpse of his insight, sparing Zifu the waste of so much salt and sauce.
When Minister Chen Cao arrived, Zifu drew a circle. Cao said, "I have come as a disciple."
He was already lacking in presence; how much more so when he acted in such a manner! Xuanshu Fu added a single dot within a circle.
Baoshou Cao said, "I took you for the shipowner from the Southern Barbarians. Xuanshu Fu then returned to his quarters and closed the door.
Xuedou Xian said, "Chen Cao possesses only one eye.
Guishan Zhe said, "Although Zifu is a furnace of the fundamental school, how could he withstand Chen Cao’s refined gold?
Do you all wish to recognize Zifu? He casually casts a single hook, startling the dragon of the azure depths.
Lingyan Zhu said: "Xuedou’s critique in this manner means that his elbow and arm will never bend outward.
Yet he fails to realize that the Minister cleared away the white clouds to seek a kindred spirit, while Zifu opened up the green peaks to respond skillfully to the incoming stimulus.
Although both were indeed masters of their craft, they could not avoid merely copying patterns."
When a monk asked Zifu, "What is 'a single mote of dust entering into meditative absorption'? Zifu made the gesture of entering samādhi.
The monk asked, "What is 'the arising of all motes of dust from samādhi'? Zifu replied, "Whom are you asking?"
Lingxi Yu said: "Lingxi does not think so. What is 'one mote of dust entering right concentration'?
He raised his fist and said, "This is a fist. "What is 'all motes of dust arising from samādhi'? He then struck him across the mouth with it.
Longtang said: "The old fellow Zifu merely follows others in rising and falling. Here it is not so.
What is 'a single mote of dust entering right concentration'? To whom do you ask this? What is 'the samādhi of all motes of dust'?"
He then assumed the posture of entering meditative absorption.
Chan Master Huiqing of Bajiao in Yingzhou (a successor of Nantou Xiyun of the Sixth Patriarch’s lineage) ascended the hall, held up his staff, and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff, I take it away from you."
[Zhangzi] leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
Guishan Zhe said, "Daming does not do it this way. When you have a staff, I take your staff away;
when you have no staff, I give you a staff. Since Daming is thus, [what of] all others?
Does anyone still have use for it? If someone has use for it, it is the vanguard of Deshan and the final command of Linji.
If you do not have use for it, then return it to its original owner.
Touzi Qingyun said: "If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate anxieties.
Tiantong Juexian said: "If you have it, everything has it; if you lack it, everything lacks it—existence and non-existence are simply as they are.
When one is thus engaged in giving and taking away, what does this have to do with the banana tree? At such a time, how is it that you support yourself?
Zhangzi’s *Baofeng wen* says: "O Great Assembly! When buying and selling with cash, do not allow yourself to be deceived by others. Do you understand?
Whether there is profit or no profit, one does not leave the marketplace."
Tiantong Jie said: "The old fellow Bajiao took communal property and placed it in his private ledger, squandering it beyond measure.
This caused his descendants in later generations to add further knots upon the joints of the staff, thereby insulting the ancestral wind.
At Mount Jing, everything is utterly bare; if there is something, he does not give it away; if there is nothing, he does not take it away. Why is this?"
Thus it is. He took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "One day when power is in one's hand, watch for the time the command is executed.
Tianbao Shu said: "If you have a staff, I give you a staff—wrong.
If you have no staff, I take away your staff—wrong. After a long silence, he said: "Wrong, wrong."
Wushi Dao said: "Where there is already something, adding more to it is like adding embroidery to brocade;
where there is nothing to take away, how, after all, can one speak of it? O virtuous ones, can you discern this? After a long silence, he said:
'Next year there will be new branches again; the spring wind’s vexation shall never cease.'"
Yuan'an Yu said: "This old fellow has a surplus in his broad places and a deficiency in his narrow places.
It is not so at Xiansheng: when you have a staff, you cannot lift it with both hands; when you have no staff, you cannot even set down your body."
Jin-su Yuan said: "Holding [the student] face-to-face and granting or revoking according to the occasion—these two venerable elders certainly did not fail to let the army follow the seal;
yet they established their own schools in vain labor without merit. They did not recognize that the staff of the person here is present.
But what is this staff of the person here? If you can speak it, not only will you sit..."
He cut off the tongues of the ancients and also gave vent for the monks of the world.
Jinxian Can said, "That fellow Bajiao is much like a small child from a village of three households;
he digs up balls of stinking mud, rolling them into spheres or flattening them, shrinking them or stretching them, spinning them round and round with lively agility. Although..."
This means that while taking up and putting down is free, it still does not avoid the labor of the palm and the expense of the fingers.
Bian Shan was not like this: if you have a staff, he takes your staff away; if you have no staff, he gives you a staff.
Tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different? If you can discern this, I grant that you possess the single eye.
Shendǐngzé said: "To buy a pair of straw sandals for a single piece of silver is nothing extraordinary.
It is simply that no one is permitted to wear them. Why? Because such is the nature of the Dharma. He gave a shout.
Shendǐng Fú said: "Bājião speaks thus: 'Humanity and righteousness are mostly severed where there is poverty;
worldly sentiment tends toward those with wealth. Tiantóng does not think so. Whether you have it or you do not, I will give it to you;
I only require that you recognize the origin of this staff. If you can recognize it..."
As for this place: if there is something, it is like adding flowers to brocade; if there is nothing, it is like sending charcoal into the snow.
In ordinary application, it is like a dragon finding water or a tiger relying on a mountain.

If you do not recognize its source, then throughout the twenty-four hours of the day, when you wish to move horizontally you cannot, and when you wish to move vertically you cannot; you will inevitably be obstructed by it. Suppose there were a man who said:
"I have it and I do not want it; I lack it and I do not want it. How about you, Master?
I too wish to ask about the origin of what you possess. You have it and you do not want it; from where does yours come?
If you recognize that which is your own, it is the same as this mountain monk’s; yet, for now, it cannot be pushed away. If you lack it and do not want it, then I, for my part—"
I ask you: when you habitually part the weeds to gaze at the wind, or pierce through clouds and cross waters, whose power do you entirely rely upon?
Thus, you are wide open, unobstructed, vast, and expansive. Lately, you have been as numerous as rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds.
Great assembly, do you know where this comes from? It is inconceivable. If you do not know where it comes from, it has no fundamental basis. After all, from where does this staff come?
After a long silence, he said: "Do not seek beneath the forest; do not look for it by the stream.

Bāzǎo addressed the assembly: "It is like a person walking along who suddenly encounters a ten-thousand-fathom deep pit ahead, while a wild fire presses from behind, with thorny thickets on both sides. If you move forward, you will fall into the pit; if you retreat..."
Afterwards, wild fires will burn your body; if you try to turn over, you will be obstructed by thorny thickets.
At such a time, how can you avoid this? If you can avoid it, you must possess a way to emerge from the situation. If you cannot avoid it, you are a man who has fallen and died.
Guangyin Biao said: "The old fellow Bajiao has been caught red-handed right here for you.
Do you people still have blood under your skin? Furthermore, what kind of phrase could you possibly utter now to meet with Bajiao?
Do you know? If it were Ling Xingpo, she would surely cry out to the blue heavens."
Bajiao was asked by a monk, "When a thief comes, one must strike; when a guest comes, one must welcome. But what if both guest and thief arrive at once?
Bajiao said, "In the house there is a pair of worn-out straw sandals. The monk asked, "As for those worn-out straw sandals, are they still fit for use?
Bajiao replied, "If you take them away, it will be ominous in front and inauspicious behind."
Zifu Guang said: "With a double-pronged grasp, one holds fast; with a single stroke of the sword, all is opened wide.
If you are but a petty peddler, you will see your defenses melt away like ice and crumble like tiles. Even so, I do not act in this way.
When suddenly encountering both guests and bandits arriving together, what then? Simply say to them: 'You are a master.'"
Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School, Volume Thirty-Two and Volume Thirty-Three.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Dharma Heir of Baiyan at Ancient Hangzhou.

△ Chan Master Changcha of Tong’an in Hongzhou (the sixth generation descendant of Jiufeng Qian): A newly arrived monk circumambulated the meditation seat three times, struck his staff once, and said, “At the place where neither ordinary beings nor sages reach, I ask the Master to speak.
An [Changcha] snapped his fingers three times. The monk said, “It is the same.”
An was so startled that he forgot what had come before him and what lay behind. An asked, "Where did you set out from, O *śramaṇa*? The monk said, "Goodbye," and departed.
An remarked, "A patch-robed wanderer of the Five Lakes, a single-staffed Chan practitioner—had you not yet reached Tong’an, you would have been left with doubts."
The monk turned his head and said, "What one sees nearby is not as good as what one hears from afar. An said, "In greed for a single cup of wine, he lost the fish in the entire boat.
Zhaojue Qin said, "The entire army's ranks, with both cavalry and infantry intermingled—when two armies clash, it is truly extraordinary."
"Extraordinary! Alas, both have suffered a loss. Let those with the true eye try to discern it. He Shanxun said:
"Exerting great function, manifesting great potential; light comes and meets darkness; the level and the precipitous are one.

Since he has already taken up the staff of killing and enlivening, I am but a weight wrapped in cotton. Even if the eyes of all quarters were to look upon it, they would find it difficult to cut through.
"It is this; it is not that. Ultimately, how is it? It is laughable—this single unperforated flute, with host and guest inverted, blows at both ends.
Dongshan Ying said: "This monk is as excellent as Zhang Yide charging straight through on the Bridge at Baling."
The display of his martial prowess was truly awe-inspiring. Yet, as soon as Tong'an softly recited a single mantra, he could no longer hold on.
Thus, he suffered this reprimand: "For the sake of a single cup of wine, you have lost the fish from your entire boat."

When Xuansha arrived at Putian County, he was welcomed with a grand display of various performances.
The following day, he asked the Elder Xiaotang, "Where did all that clamor go yesterday? Xiaotang lifted the corner of his *kāṣāya*. Xuansha said, "I suspect you have missed the point."
Fayan Yi said, "Yesterday there was so much clamor.
Qingliang Yin said, "Today it is even more laughable.
Guishan Zhe said, "Daguishan would not do it this way. If someone were to ask such a question, he would simply snap his fingers once."
[The Master] said: "Suppose a monk were to come forward and say, 'I have already discerned this; there is no further connection. If you were to approve him, why?
A man of great character plucking a tiger’s whiskers is his very duty. But tell me, where does the point of danger lie?"
Huanglong Xin said: "How extraordinary! All you practitioners of Zen, it must be an elder like Xiaotang who can truly uphold the Dharma-vehicle.
Why did Xuansha say, 'It is like trying to catch a reflection in water—there is no connection'?
I do not think so. Where have all the clamor and bustle of yesterday gone? Heaven shares its clarity with the white clouds at dawn; water merges with the bright moon."

Liu Zhaojue raised the words of Guishan and, having finished, said: "Although these two elders were indeed uplifting the fundamental tenets of the school, they were essentially preoccupied with gazing at the moon in the sky.
Suppose someone were to ask me today: 'Yesterday there was such a great commotion—'"
"Where are you going?"—if you simply say this to him, it is starting all over again from the beginning. If he says, "I have already discerned it;
there is no connection," strike him across the spine with your staff immediately. Why? "The waves at Caoqi are just like this;
countless ordinary people are submerged."
Nanhuabing said: "When Xuansha spoke in this way, was there still gain and loss, or right and wrong?
If you say there was, then people have not yet attained the eye. If you say there was not, why did he say, 'Even if you were to guess, it would have no connection'?"
Do you understand? Right and wrong have already departed;
seek realization within right and wrong. Boshan Lai said: "A person probes with words; one probes water with a staff. Discern true gold amidst a blazing fire;
recognize the Son of Heaven in the midst of a bustling market. Identify this old monk beneath his monastic robe. Xuan Sha’s Xiao Tang was such a person.
"Even if one covers it over, bitter in the mouth yet sweet in the heart—there is more to it than that.
Qingshan Xiu said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. If someone were to ask, 'Where have all those clamors of yesterday gone?
I would simply say, 'Today’s departure is even superior to yesterday's. If he were to say..."
"It is beyond reach. I also know you are a blind man.
Kaisu Jin said, "Had it not been for Xuansha, you would have been thoroughly deceived by Xiaotang. Huanglong said, "The heavens share their brightness with white clouds;
the waters flow with the bright moon. This too is something that can be used to cast him aside. It is beyond reach.
Sheshan asked, "For what reason? It is simply because one does not see the Way that one speaks too much; all afflictions arise from forcing oneself to emerge.
Once Xuansha and Tianlong entered the mountains and saw a tiger. Long said, "Monk, it is a tiger. Sha said, "It is your tiger."
After returning to the monastery, Long asked, "Just now, when you saw the tiger, you said it was you. I wonder what your intention was?
The Śramaṇa said, "In this Sahā world, there are four kinds of most weighty matters. If a person can penetrate them, they will be able to transcend the realm of the five aggregates."
Xuedou Xian said, "If you wish to act as a teacher for gods and men, right before your eyes is a tiger.
Jingshan Gao, speaking on behalf of Tianlong, offered this remark: "I know that the Master’s concern for others is earnest indeed."
Tianning Qisong said, "In the end, what is it? Following the convention, he replied, "A tiger; a shrimp cannot leap out of its bucket.
Baoshou Fang said, "Xuansha and Tianlong humiliated one another; each has lost their very life.
Is there anyone who can lend a hand for these two elders?"
Nanjian asked: "Tianlong threw a brick; Xuansha drew out a jade. Turning the hand over and turning it back, straight and curved—how many people's lives have been deceived by this?
Do not harbor delusions or falsely create things by rubbing your eyes.
Today, this mountain monk shall act according to the mandate. He struck his staff and let out a shout.

Regarding "How does the Venerable One intend for the cloud of wisdom to flourish?"—the subsequent phrase "the sand immediately makes the sound of a tiger" [indicates that] regarding "I allow you to emerge from the realm of darkness," the subsequent phrase "the dragon says: 'If it is broken by light, it is not fit'" [indicates that].
When Xuansha saw Gushan approaching, he drew a circle and showed it to him. Gushan said, "No one can get out of this.
Xuansha said, "I knew you would be making your living in the wombs of donkeys and horses. Gushan asked, "And what about you, Master?
Xuansha said, "No one can get out of this. Gushan said, "But when the Master speaks thus..."
[The Master] said, "He has attained it. [The monk] asked, "If so-and-so speaks in this way, why does he not attain it? Sandō said, "I have attained it; you have not attained it.
Xuedou Xian said, "He only knows how to greedily gaze at the white waves, yet he fails to realize that he has lost the oar in his hand."
Yunfeng Yue said: "Whether you can speak it or cannot speak it, all are within Xuan Sha’s circle.
Now, how will you get out of that Xuan Sha circle?"
Zhaojue Qin said: "The 'blazingly clear' is a single path known only by those who have truly realized it.
It reaches so far as to span heaven and earth and endure through ten thousand ages without shifting; it exhausts the kalpa-stone and empties the mustard-seed city without end.
Even one who has penetrated this barrier must still apply their eyes [with discernment] before they may attain it. It is all the same at such a time—why then do you say, 'I...'"
Whether you attain it or not, you must by all means avoid making your livelihood within the wombs of donkeys and horses.
Jingyin Cheng said: "In the monastic groves, there are often those who understand this by taking it to be the realm of Xuan Sha before he reached the stage of Gu Shan.
Do you people wish to recognize Xuan Sha and Gu Shan? Have you not heard it said: 'None can escape this'?"
Nanhua Bing said: "To twist the nostrils and exchange the eyes—if one did not possess such a means, how could one uphold the School of the Patriarchs?
Nevertheless, it is truly laughable; one must laugh for thirty years. But tell me, what is there to laugh at?
I know full well that you are making your living inside the womb of a donkey or a horse."
Dongchan Guan said: "At that time, had I been Drum Mountain, I would have waited for the man of the Way to come forth with this [realization].
Had he not succeeded, I would have told him: 'Master, you actually have another excellence;
it is not that you seek to complete your prior merit, but rather you wish to meet Xuansha within the wombs of donkeys and horses.'"
Tiantong Jue said: "Xuansha was much like one who relies on power to deceive others and uses strength to oppress the weak.
This is because he was able to shift his perspective and bring forth his realization; both were the same. Why then did he say, 'I have attained it, but you have not'?
What is true cannot be concealed; what is false does not flourish."
Baoneng Xiu said: "The celestial palaces and pure lands—everyone loves to go there, yet Gushan does not love them.
The wombs of donkeys and horses—everyone fears falling into them, yet Xuansha does not fear them. Therefore, he lowers his voice and carries his own spirit;
he looks down with disdain and strides across, possessing the power of the lion king that cannot be deceived. Do you still believe in the guarantee of Tiantong? Amidst the dust..."
He acts as the host. Guests come from beyond the borders of transformation.
Gu Nanmen said: "You speak of this; I also speak of this. But what, after all, is this?
If you can discern it, even making a living in the womb of a donkey or the belly of a horse will not be difficult. Its...
Some lose their oars; not only do they fail to observe that the white waves are merely a manifestation of greed, but they are certain to find their karmic consciousness drifting aimlessly.
Master Fuchuan said: "In the monastic communities, it is often said that Gushan’s spiritual insight was not yet perfected and that he fell into Xuansha’s trap.
Little do they realize that Gushan has, in fact, pierced Xuansha’s nostrils, which remain so even to this day."
That will not do. If there were someone who could act as the host for Xuansha, I would question him: "Since you both spoke in this same way, why was it that I attained it while you did not?"
Benjue says: "Xuansha’s heart, liver, and five viscera were squeezed out by Gushan with a single squeeze; to this day they have not been put back together.
Why is this? Have you not heard it said: 'If you do not enter the startling waves, how can you see the one who plays with the tide?'"
Baiyan Fu said: "Everyone says that this one cannot be attained. When people speak in such a manner, why is it that some attain it while others do not?
If you can fix a single eye here, I will grant that you have personally seen Xuansha."

Xuansha instructed a monk to deliver a letter to Xuefeng. When Xuefeng opened the seal, he found three sheets of blank white paper. He then asked the monk, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
Xuefeng said, "Did you not hear it said that 'the gentleman shares the same wind from a thousand miles away'? The monk returned and reported this to Xuansha.
Xuansha said, "That old fellow on the mountain missed it, yet he does not even know it. The monk asked, "How about the Master? Xuansha said, "Meng! (A name for a simpleton).
"Spring is still cold. He did not understand the meaning.
Wuzu Kei came forth with these words: "I thought his beard was red. Xuanjue Qian said:
"Xuefeng’s three sheets of white paper—how can it be that the patterns and colors have already been revealed? Xuefeng’s thousand...
"The same wind blows throughout the villages. Why do you not realize you have missed the mark? Have you not heard the saying: 'When raising a child, do not let him grow too large;
once he is grown, he will love to scold his father'?
Yunmen Cheng said, "Xuefeng, 'In early spring it is still cold. Xuefeng, 'A thousand miles share the same wind. These are all [instances of] opening [the way]."
Postscript to the Letter: Before the letter was even opened, how would you speak of it?
Taixu said word for word: "Before Xuefeng sealed the blank paper, it had already melted away like ice and crumbled like a fortress.
Xuefeng’s saying, "A thousand miles of the same wind," can truly be called adding frost to snow. When examined closely, these two [masters]— [The text ends here.]
Both were mistaken.
Xuansha asked Jingqing, "The scriptures say that not seeing a single dharma is a great calamity. Now tell me, what dharma do you not see?
Jingqing pointed to a pillar and said, "Is it this dharma that you do not see? Xuansha said, "In Zhejiang..."
"Clear water and white rice—eat from them, yet you have not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma.
Xuedou Xian said, "How great Master Jingqing was deceived by Xuansha! Had I been there at the time, I would have simply said to him:
'The prophecy at Vulture Peak has not yet reached this point.'"
Taisu Zhe said: "If it were not for Jingqing, I would have almost lost both the beginning and the end. Why?
Because had I not met someone else, I would never have opened my fist."
Tiantong Jue said: "When Jingqing answered in such a manner at that time, and Xuansha spoke in such a way at the end—did they accord with each other or not?
Nevertheless, Jingqing had long since ceased dreaming of the Buddha-dharma; he must have been a fellow student of Xuansha to begin with."
Tiantong Hua said: "Jingqing let his stubbornness run wild; even the Buddha could do nothing with him.
Had it not been for Xuansha seeing through him, he would have nearly been swallowed up by a pillar."
Tiantong Jie said: "When these two venerable masters met face-to-face, it was much like children playing;
where were their Buddha-dharma and their very selves? Having finished citing the words of Ying’an Hua, he let out a shout and said:
'If one were to cause tears to fall frequently, even the Eastern Sea would have to dry up.'"
Yuan'an Yu said: "Xuansha was fortunate to encounter Jingqing. If he had been a man of true reverse-stride, how could Jingqing have tolerated him?
I often observe that those who seek to deceive their enemy perish."
Baoshou newly said: "The wooden man raises his hand; the stone woman nods her head. If we discuss the two words 'Buddha-dharma,' it remains as before—facing south while looking at the Big Dipper.
After a long silence, he said: "Do you understand? In North China they use hoes; in South China they use oxen."
Baiyan Fu said: "Boya and Ziqi were no ordinary acquaintances. To whom did these two elders refer?
Nevertheless, at that time, Jingqing was almost like one who had no tongue in his mouth; I wonder if Xuansha could have truly trusted him.
Xuansha addressed the assembly: "If we discuss this matter, it is like a plot of land whose boundaries on all four sides have been demarcated and sold to others by contract;
there remains only the tree at its center, which still belongs to me, the old monk."

Fochuan Yizheng said: "Virtuous practitioners of Chan, since you have already reached a mutual agreement and finalized the sale of the boundaries of the four directions, why does the tree at the center still belong to Xuansha?"
Xuefeng once said to Xuansha, "The world is one chi wide; the ancient mirror is one chi wide. The world is ten zhang wide;
the ancient mirror is ten zhang wide. Xuansha pointed to the brazier and asked, "How wide is this brazier? Xuefeng replied, "It is as wide as the ancient mirror.
Xuansha said, "This old fellow has not yet even touched the ground with his heels."
Jingqing Huifu asked a monk, "Is it that the ancient mirror causes the brazier to be so wide, or is it that the brazier causes the ancient mirror to be so wide?
Xiyuan Ming said, "Even asking such a question is not yet permissible."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "Rancid rice and a clay tea stove.
Zhaojue Zhenqin said, "A ready-made case. An ancient mirror was never originally a fire stove; break open the cage, and the fire stove is itself the ancient mirror.
Were it not for father and son meeting in harmony, how could one see these pieces of naked heart? It is just like this:
Xuan Sha said, "This old fellow’s heels have not yet touched the ground. How will you all ultimately understand this?
Tian Bao Shu took up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said: "The world, the ancient mirror, and the brazier—all shattered into a hundred pieces!"
"You have understood. But as for the old man Xuansha, his heels are not yet touching the ground. What do you think?
"A talent like Guoqing’s is noble; a child from a wealthy family is arrogant."
Tianqi said: "Tell me, whose world is this world? Whose ancient mirror is this ancient mirror?
One must not chase after objects and split them into two pieces. He held up his staff and said: "This is the world; this is the ancient mirror.
If you can directly accept this, you will cut off Xuefeng and Xuansha at once. Great men, take care not to dwell vainly in a ghost cave."
Wasting years and months.
Jizhu said: "Once a word has been spoken, even four horses cannot overtake it. He then gave a shout.
Bairyam Pu said: "The Old Man of Elephant Bone was so pressed by Xuansha that he was made to urinate on the spot."
Nevertheless, although Xuan Sha had spoken thus, Xuefeng did not utter a single word here. Do not say there was no matter of urgency or significance.
Because Xuan Sha was renowned for his mastery of the Tripiṭaka and his skill in distinguishing sounds, King Liu invited him to test this; Xuan Sha then took—
He struck an iron brazier with a copper fire-tongs and asked Śubhākarasimha, "What sound is this? Simha replied, "The sound of copper and iron.
Baizhang said, "Great King, do not allow yourself to be deceived by foreigners."
Xuedou Xian commented on Xuansha’s words, saying: "The Great King should increase his faith and reverence.
He also commented on the Tripitaka Master’s words, saying: "Do not deceive a foreigner."
Qingliang Qinda said to the Tripiṭaka Master, “In fact, it is the Master who is deceiving Your Majesty.
Jingyin Cheng said, “Since it is not the sound of copper or iron, what kind of sound did Xuansha call it?

Thus, the Tripiṭaka Master only knew how to cross the water, yet remained unaware that his clothes were getting wet; Xuansha was particularly adept at framing others, but what could he do about the State?
There is a precedent. Now tell me: how does the Tripitaka Master deceive the Great King compare to Xuansha deceiving the Great King?
Tiantong Jue said: "When principle accords, it is spiritual; the poor man obtains the treasure within his garment. When sentiment is sealed, it is a thing."
The wrestler lost the pearl from atop his forehead; the Tripitaka Master only knows how to look forward and cannot look back—do you understand?
To falsely accuse another of a crime and then impose that very punishment upon them.
Gao Feng said, "The great and small Xuan-shas have not forgotten what they were capable of or failed at. At that time, it was fortunate to encounter this Great King Liu;
had he run into a monk of true caliber, you can be certain there would have been a total exposure."
Lianfu Ce said: "Xuansha deceived the Hu and mocked the Han; he betrayed the grace of the state.

The Tripitaka Master merely understood the sound [of the teachings] but was not permitted to behold the splendor of the Imperial Capital. At that time, the Great King would not tolerate being hoodwinked by others;
Xuansha and the Tripitaka Master both deserve to be driven out beyond the city gates."
Once, Attendant Guang provoked Xuansha by saying, "If you, Uncle, can learn Chan, I shall build an iron boat and sail out to sea.
After Xuansha had taken up residence [at his monastery], he sent a letter to ask Guang, "Have you built the iron boat yet?"
Fayan Yi, acting for Guang the attendant, said: "The Master will certainly not do so.
Qingliang Qin, acting for Guang the attendant, said: "Please, Master, board the boat."
Zhiti Ai said: "Xuansha was also like a poor man thinking of an old debt.
Huelin, on behalf of Attendant Guang, said: "Yesterday I passed through Silla."
Yunju Yuan said: "I have never even attained Zen; what use is there in pondering old matters?
Suddenly, he was moved by that iron boat—what could Xuansha possibly do?"
Yunju Zhuang said: "Those who offer critiques from various quarters are not few; yet they can only support the strong and cannot support the weak.
Today, this mountain monk has long investigated the matter and finds it does not deviate from the original facts. I dare say that Xuansha was led astray by Attendant Guang;
even a direct analysis would not suffice. After all, how is it? The law has no fixed statutes; let it follow its course."
The people made a private agreement.
Once, a monk asked Xuansha, "I have heard the Master say that the entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl;
how may a student understand this? Xuansha said, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl—what need is there to understand it?"
"What is it? The monk then stopped. The next day, Shishuang asked the monk, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl.
How do you understand this? The monk replied, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl; what need is there to understand it?
Shishuang said, "I know you are making your living inside a ghost cave."
Baoci then raised the point, saying: "In one way, you speak thus; why does it instead turn into a ghost cave?
Xuedou Xian commented on Xuansha’s words, saying: "It would be acceptable in other quarters, but here it will not do."
Dajue Sheng said: "This man from Fujian has, throughout his life, possessed a spine as straight as iron.
Yet here, he has collapsed body and soul. As for this pearl, not only does this monk not recognize it; I dare say that even Xuansha did not recognize it."
Why is this? "The people may be made to follow, but they cannot be made to understand.
When Xuansha addressed the assembly, he said, "The World-Honored One spoke of the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye being entrusted to Mahākāśyapa;
this is like talking about the moon. Caoxi held up his whisk; this is still like pointing at the moon. At that time, Gushan stepped forward and said, "What about the moon? Xuansha [laughed].
It is said that this master [Xuansha] sought the moon from me; Mount San did not consent, yet returned to the assembly and said, "He says I am seeking the moon from him.
Xuedou Xian said: "Xuansha and Gushan were like two generals arraying a million-man battle formation, yet they merely threw pebbles and rubble."
They strike one another. There are patch-robed monks who can discern this; you should know that the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye has been entrusted to those who possess it.
Huguang Yuan said: "Xuansha and Gushan each speak according to their own principles, yet they still do not recognize the moon.
Do you all wish to recognize the moon? Fortunately, there is no place where it does not shine impartially, yet people stubbornly insist on remaining ignorant.
Gounan said: "Xuansha lured people into breaking the law; Gushan bought a hat to fit their heads.
Had it not been for Xuedou’s clear discernment of the subtle nuances, many would have understood this in terms of 'accepting' or 'refusing.
Is there any monk here today who remains unconvinced? I must ask you: what do you call the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye?"
While Xuansha was attending Xuefeng, they were walking along when Xuefeng pointed to the ground and said, "This plot of land is well-suited for building a seamless stupa.

Xuansha asked, "How high shall it be? Xuefeng looked up and down. Xuansha said, "The merit and reward of humans and devas is not lacking, but you have not yet seen the prediction granted at Vulture Peak. Xuefeng asked, "What do you say to this? Xuansha replied:
Seven feet eight inches. Langya Jue said:
"In the state of Qing, the man of talent is noble; in a wealthy household, the child is arrogant.
Baoshou Fang said: "Xuefeng acted like a fool; Xuansha displayed his brilliance. The Master’s superior endowment and strength are peerless throughout the ages.
"Meeting [him] is possible right here in this bustling courtyard; however, if it were a seamless stupa, one would have to proceed slowly.
Because Xuefeng had passed away, the assembly requested Xuansha to serve as the presiding mourner.

On the third morning, while the assembly was gathered for the tea ceremony, Xuansha picked up a single tea bowl before the spirit altar and asked, "The Great Assembly, when our late teacher was alive, he followed you..."
"Speak! Now, how would you speak? If you can speak it, the former master is not at fault;
if you cannot speak it, the fault lies with the former master. He asked this three times, but the assembly remained silent.
Sha then smashed his bowl to pieces and returned to the hall.
Zhongta asked, "Xuansha, how do you understand this? Zhongta said, "What fault did my former teacher have?
Xuansha then turned his back to the wall. Zhongta then went out. Xuansha called to Zhongta again; Zhongta looked back. Xuansha said, "How do you understand this?
Zhongta then turned his back to the wall. Xuansha ceased questioning him.

Xiaoyan Bao said: "At that time, there was a monk who, as soon as he saw him raise the matter in such a way, would have overturned the tea table, thereby sparing the ancestors from leaving their karmic debts unresolved to be inherited by their descendants."
While Xuan Sha was sitting, he saw a single white spot on the ground before him. Pointing at it, he asked his attendant, "Do you see it? The attendant replied, "I see it.
He asked this three times, and received the same answer each time. Xuan Sha said, "You see it, and I see it too. Why then do you say you do not understand?"
Gao Feng said, "Miaoyun, when the assembly sees it, they see it; when they realize it, they realize it—there is no further doubt.
But tell me, what exactly is this single point of white? Baiyan Fu replied, "I do not know, I do not know."
Xuan Sha once remarked to Wei, the Military Commissioner: "The Venerable Cao Shan is truly extraordinary.
Xuan Sha then asked, "How many *li* is it from Fuzhou to Cao Shan? Wei turned to a monk standing nearby and asked, "Have you ever been to Cao Shan?
The monk replied, "I have. Wei then asked, "How many *li* is it from Fuzhou to Cao Shan? The monk said, "One hundred and twenty *li*. Wei said, "If that is so, then the Master..."
The Master did not take his seat at Cao Shan’s level. Wei rose and prostrated. The Master said, "The Inspector must indeed pay respects to this monk;
this monk, in turn, possesses a sense of shame."
Yunju Xi said: "Where is it that this monk possesses a sense of shame? If you can discern this, I will grant you the eye of a true traveler.
Chengtian Zong said: "This monk is pitiable and tragic; even if Xuansha possessed the adamantine eye, [he would not have been able to see it]."
Wei the Military Commissioner has already been missed.
While Xuansha was sitting in conversation with Dizang in the abbot’s quarters, it grew late at night. Xuansha said, “The attendant has closed the door and barred the bolts;
how will you get out? Dizang replied, “What do you call a ‘door’?”
Xuedou Xian, when taking his leave of Dizang, said, "At that time, I bid you farewell with deep respect" and then departed.
Qingliang Qin, when taking his leave, said, "Preceptor, do you wish to stop here?
Xuansha, because of Wei the Military Commissioner, said: "The speech of the people of Jambudvīpa is already somewhat difficult to discern; how much more so the Sanskrit of the Five Indias!"
[The Master] spoke: "Is there anyone here who can discern this? Xuefeng asked, "If one recognizes this very thing, then one has discerned it.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "Why does Xuansha use such elaborate words? He then asked, "What did you just say?"
Once, when the elder Nanji had been at Xuefeng for several days, he went next to Xuansha. Xuansha said, "Regarding this matter, I alone am able to know it.
How do you understand it, Elder? Nanji replied, "One must know that there is one who does not seek to know."
Xuan Sha said, "Old man at the head of the mountain, why do you trouble yourself so?
Xuedou Xian commented on this dialogue, saying, "How many under Xuefeng’s gate are like this?
Xuan Sha said to Xuefeng, "I am now going to employ the Great Function. What about you, Master? Xuefeng—
He threw three wooden balls out at once. Sashaku took up a stance as if to strike them with his board.
Xuefeng said, "Only when you were at Mount Ling could you act like this. Sashaku said, "This too is my own business."

Yingshan Yun said: "The father acts and the son follows; truly he has maintained the family legacy. Yet, when examined closely, he cannot avoid being a subject for people's gossip. Huiyun Sheng said: "Look at this father and son;
they are remarkably similar. Their movements follow one another like dancers, and their tones harmonize like the musical notes gong and shang."
Regarding this: if we discuss its great function, it sets aside the Elephant Bone Cliff and allows that there is a point for understanding.
Once, when Jingqing asked Xuansha, "I am a student who has newly entered the monastic community; I beg the Master to point out a way of entry," Xuansha said, "Do you hear the sound of the Yan River?
Jingqing replied, "I hear it. Xuansha said, "Enter from here. Jingqing attained realization.
Wuzu Yan said: "If you have truly attained entry, you may go freely in all four directions and eight facets.
If it is not yet so, you must by no means depart from this very place."
Jingshan Daowu said, "If you wish to truly gain entry, you must depart from this very place.
Tiantong Jue said, "These three great elders were all merely contending at a crossroads, rubbing one wooden bucket against another;
what joy is there in that? I, this mountain monk, am not like them—I do not even like to hear the word 'entry'."
Tianning Qisong said: "What place is this? To speak of 'leaving' or 'not leaving,' to whom would you even ask?
I recall those days by East Creek, when flowers bloomed and leaves fell; for many moments I intended to cast gold to forge a Zichqi."
Ji Cui said, "Run-yun! It is not so here. We pay no heed to whether you have departed or not.
But tell me, what place is this? The assembly had no reply. The attendant said, "Please have some tea. Run-yun struck him, saying, "Who taught you to be so talkative?"
The ancient forest is like clouds; having found an entrance, one may grant this to Jingqing. To advance one step further, one must return to Miaoxi.
Yet, even so, one has not yet reached the inner sanctum.
*Anthology of the Ancestral Hall’s Excerpts from Ancient Cases*,
Scroll Thirty-Three and Scroll Thirty-Four.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Successor of the Lineage at Baiyan in Ancient Hangzhou.
△ Sixth Patriarchal Lineage:
Chan Master Hui-ling of Changqing in Fuzhou (Dharma heir of Xuefeng Yicun). Once, a monk asked: "When many hands sift through gold, who is it that obtains it?
Changqing said, "Those with skill obtain it. The monk asked, "Does this student obtain it as well? Changqing said, "Too far."
When Xuedou Xian was acting as the respondent for the monk, he immediately shouted. He then said: "Those with skill receive it with one hand;
those without skill receive it with both hands. Does the student receive it or not? Cang.

Sentient beings do not recognize the ancient Buddha; the ancient Buddha does not recognize sentient beings. Now tell me, what about Nanshan?
"Clouds arise on the northern mountains and it rains below—what is the significance of this? [The Master] picks up his staff and says, "The subsequent text is long.
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still transgression? Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru."
Yuantong Shanyun said: "Regarding this koan, some say that as soon as one intends to ask, it is already as vast as Mount Sumeru;
others say it is like Mount Sumeru, unmoved by the eight winds, eternally peaceful throughout the ages;
still others say it is difficult for people to penetrate, like Mount Sumeru. To deliberate in such ways is, however, not even to have dreamed of Yunmen. [He] removed [the obstruction].
When the bottom of this bucket slips and the red silk thread snaps, one finally knows that it is not like this at all. Have you not heard it said:
"The three phrases clarify the one phrase; the one phrase clarifies the three phrases. One and three do not intersect; this is clearly the path above."
Tiantong Jie said, "Even the great and small Yunmen did not recognize this koan.
Jingshan Xiu said, "This monk has worn this skin-tight undershirt for immeasurable kalpas;
had he not encountered the master Yunmen, it would have been difficult to take it off."
A monk once asked Yunmen, "How many years of lifespan does the Master have? Yunmen said, "Seven times nine is sixty-eight.
The monk said, "I do not understand. Yunmen said, "Since you do not understand, I shall reduce your lifespan by five years."
Furizhi said: "The Great Master Yunmen’s presentation of the school during his lifetime was indeed magnificent;
yet, it cannot be said that he did not indulge others to the point of causing them to lose their virtue. Here in my own monastery, it is otherwise. If someone asks, 'How old is the Master?
simply reply, 'The same age as this staff. If they further ask, 'How old is the staff? [simply reply, 'The same age as the Master']."
He then struck him once across the back with his staff, ensuring that he would find fulfillment for the rest of his life. Nevertheless, this too was said by Hanshan.
Yunmen, ascending the hall, said: "Awaken to the Way through sound; clarify the mind through form. He then raised his hand and said, "Avalokiteśvara."
A Bodhisattva bought some Hu-ping (Persian pies) with money; as he let go of his hand, he said, "I see now it was only steamed buns.
After Baizhang End raised this story, he opened both hands and said, "Is there any? Is there any? Then he shook his hand and said, "There is none. There is none. He then said:
"Having once been in the great ocean, other waters are difficult to call water; were it not for Mount Wu, all else would be but mist."
Fayun Xiu took up his staff, struck it once, and said, "This is sound and form; which one is the mind?
After a long silence, he said, "In this world there are countless masters of brush and ink, yet none can paint it here at all."
Huanglong Qing said, "Yunmen can truly be called 'eating to the point of heartache. Everyone must take care not to seek the flavor within a sesame cake.
Wuzu Yan said, "I am not like that," and then, making a gesture of beating a *janggo* drum with his hands, he said, "Eight on the stand."
Lazha. Nantang Jingyun said:
"The old monk does not think so. When Lord Zhang drinks, Lord Li is drunk; when Lord Li drinks, Lord Zhang is drunk.
Lord Zhang and Lord Li are both intoxicated to the point of oblivion; their snoring is like thunder as they sleep within a jar."
Jingshan Daowu held up his staff and said, "This is form. He struck the ground once and said, "This is sound.
All of you see this and hear this; which one is the luminous mind? Which one is the Way of awakening?
He let out a shout and said, "To covet another's single grain of rice, one loses six months' worth of provisions. He then struck the ground with the staff once more.
Yuantong Shanyun said: "The old man of Shaoyang may indeed be said to have a chant that grows ever loftier while those who join in the harmony grow ever fewer.
Now, however, he enters the Fangwang Samādhi upon the tip of Tingshou’s whisk—entering meditative concentration in the East and arising in the West."
Even to the point of entering meditative absorption in a male body and arising in a female body—do you understand? The wild colors are no longer interrupted by mountains;
the light of heaven flows directly through to the water.
Tianning Qi said: "All of you have not failed to hear sounds; why, then, do you not awaken to the Way?
You have not failed to see forms; why, then, do you not clarify the mind? Yunmen speaks thus to expose the truth; Miaoxi judges it thus:
"One tune, two tunes—no one understands them; after the rain has passed, the autumn waters in the night pond are deep."

Yangshan Qin said, "This lame-legged master pities the infant; whenever he moves, he empties his belly and pours out his guts, yet it is nothing more than a frantic fabrication, leaving behind some sticky, tooth-chattering dregs. I, the monk Qin, am not like this:
I awaken to the Way upon hearing sound and clarify the Mind upon seeing form. He planted his staff and said, "Every household has Avalokiteśvara."
Fulong Chang said: "The great and small Yunmen were merely appearing and disappearing within the realm of sound and form.
Here, it is not so. He then took up his staff, struck it once, and let out a shout.
Yunju Zhuang said, "I am not like Yunmen, who mistook a servant for his master and pointed to a deer as a horse.
He suddenly seized his staff and said, "Look! Look! This staff pierces through the skulls of you all," and then he struck it once.
Boshan Lai said: "If one awakens to the Way by hearing sounds, the void does not ring when struck. How then is it so?
If one clarifies the mind by seeing forms, the pure breeze has no physical substance. How then is it so?
Though there is no lack of speaking in barbarian tongues or Chinese, where can this fellow Yunmen search for the Bodhisattva Guanyin who has entered the Samādhi of the Universal Door?"
Xuedou said this and that. Shaoyang speaking in such a manner is much like chewing food and feeding it to an infant.
I, this mountain monk, am not so: "Hearing sounds does not awaken one to the Way; seeing forms does not clarify the mind.
Realize samādhi! Namo Avalokiteśvara!"

Yunmen asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from paying respects at the pagoda. Yunmen asked, "Are you mocking me? The monk said, "I truly have come from paying respects at the pagoda.
Yunmen said, "In that case, you do not even observe the five precepts."
Baofu Zhan said, "The wise do not reproach the foolish.
Fenyang Shao said, "Each side leaves the other hanging.
Once, a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? Yunmen replied, "A sesame cake."
Jingshan Hongzhi said, "Yunmen was truly just a fine piece of fried cake; yet, fundamentally, he lacked the principle that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs.
Songyin Ruan said, "Miaoxi raises with one hand and presses down with the other; he cannot avoid turning a single matter into two separate parts. Since—
"This is a fine piece of Hu-bing (barley cake). Furthermore, it is said there is no principle for surpassing Buddhas or transcending Patriarchs.
All you practitioners of Chan: tell me, does Miaoxi have any way of acting for the sake of others? Examine this!"
Tianning Qi said: "Zhu. Tianning Jie said:
"Yunmen bestowed his compassion spontaneously without expending any mental effort; Tianning, however, does not act in this way.
If someone were to ask, 'What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? he would reply, 'In the early morning, eat white rice.'"
Congee. After midday, one no longer feels hunger.
An Guocong said: "Miaoxi knows only the first [principle] but not the second.

He did not realize that Linji’s profound essentials consist of host and guest, and Dongshan’s [teachings] consist of ruler and minister, the biased and the correct; indeed, there are hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable subtleties.
The meaning does not, in total, go beyond this "Hu-bing" (Persian cake). Do you all understand it thoroughly?
If not, then for now, chew upon this Hu-bing.
Yunmen gave this teaching: "Everyone possesses radiance; yet when one looks for it, it is dark and dim.
What is this radiance of yours? He provided his own substitute answer: "The kitchen, the storehouse, and the mountain gate. He further said: "Better that good things never existed at all."

Yuan'an Yu said: "Yunmen’s two substitute responses—one 'picking out stars in the water,' the other 'spreading a net on the mountain peak'—are like beating a drum in the land of Great Tang while ringing a bell in the land of Silla; they have no connection whatsoever."
"Please return to the hall for tea.
Lingyan Chuzhuo struck his staff and said: "The kitchen, the storehouse, and the mountain gate are all opened wide with a single blow.
Whether the ladle is large or the bowl small, it is up to everyone to examine; after all, where does the radiance reside? Have you not heard it said?"
"To open the mouth is an error; to conceive it with the mind is to deviate.
Yunmen, when asked by a monk, "What is the Way? said, "The single word that penetrates through.
Jingshan Daoyuan remarked, "'The single word that penetrates through' does not quite hit the mark. One must quickly turn one's head; there is Zhang San and Li Si."

4. Tianning Qiyun said, "How would Tianning have responded? He took up his staff, struck the meditation seat, and said, "It would have been better to stop while the prisoner was still in custody, rather than letting his cleverness grow."
Yunmen said, "Bring forth a single phrase from the tips of the hundred grasses. The assembly was speechless. [Yunmen] spoke on their behalf, saying, "All together. Zhaojue Qin said, "A pin!
He added, "It is such that the myriad functions are stilled and the thousand eyes are suddenly opened.
It is as fine as a hair and as vast as Mount Sumeru; it is as soft as iron and as hard as mud. Even so, this only accounts for one side."
"Half. Or if someone asks the mountain monk, he simply answers, "Withdraw. But tell me, where does it land?
Jingshan Gao said, "Pǔ. He added, "Both are *zhā-pǔ*. The sun is at its zenith. General Li shot the stone tiger."
Although they aimed their thousand-jin crossbows toward that direction, Tianning Qi said, "Yunmen is mostly empty and lacks substance.
Yuanwu Zha remarked, "There is no connection at all. Miaoxi Pu stated, "You must directly realize it.
These three fellows each established their own livelihood; shaking their heads and wagging their tails, they arrived.
Meeting another in this place: deep mountains hide fierce tigers; shallow grass reveals swarms of snakes.
Lingyan said, "Old man Yuanwu does not know good from bad; he has wrongly applied these words.
Yunmen’s response at that time caused no small amount of confusion among people. How much more so when one adds mud upon earth! If today...
Someone asked Guoqing, "Bring forth a single phrase from atop the heads of the hundred grasses. Guoqing seized his staff and struck him across the spine.
Why? To prevent him from hiding and dodging atop the heads of the hundred grasses.
Fochuan Zongyun said: "A single tangle of willow threads cannot be gathered; it is draped with mist upon the jade balustrade.
Yunmen, when asked by a monk, "How can one ensure that the twelve periods of the day do not pass in vain?
Yunmen said, "Where would you place this question? The monk said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master to provide an example. Yunmen said, "An example cannot be provided."
[The Master] looked back. It was immediately contradictory. [If one] attempts to deliberate upon it, in what kalpa will one awaken?
Jia Shan Yu said: "Yunmen acting as a teacher in this way is precisely hitting the mark at the beginning but missing it at the end.
If I were he, I would wait until he said, 'Students do not understand; I beg the Master to provide an example,' and then strike him right across the head."
A single blow. He said to him, "When meeting people, do not fail to cite [the truth] correctly.
Yunmen asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying? The monk replied, "The *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*. Yunmen said, "Your meaning has fallen.
The monk asked, "In what way has my meaning fallen? Yunmen said, "Take it upon yourself and get out!"
Zhongfeng Ben said: "Frost upon snow; shackles upon cangues. Face-to-face, there is no partiality; stars and constellations are shifted.
Do you wish to see where this monk’s talk fell? Wait until thirty years hence."

Yunmen addressed the assembly: "There are two kinds of illnesses when light does not penetrate through. First, there is the lack of clarity in all places, as if there were an object before one's face.
Second, even if one has penetrated such that all phenomena are empty, there is still a lingering sense, as if something were present;
this too is light not penetrating through. Furthermore, there are two kinds of illnesses regarding the Dharma-body. Reaching the Dharma-body yet remaining attached to it as a 'dharma' is one."
[The previous thought] has been forgotten, yet the trace of one's own view still remains. To sit within the vicinity of the *dharmakāya* is one thing;

even if you manage to penetrate through to the *dharmakāya*, it is not permissible to let it pass unexamined. If you scrutinize it closely, what kind of "vital breath" could there be? It is also a sickness.
Boshan Lai said: "To reach the ultimate of refinement and to investigate the minutest flaws requires an eye of wisdom to discern them.
As for those whose minds know and whose bodies merge, they sever the root of the disease of the flowing stream; those who reach the source and forget emotion mirror the phenomena of the non-self.
Aside from such as these—who have manifested themselves beyond the limit of Avidyā (Wei-yin) or who sleep soundly at the crossroads of the marketplace—none can do so."
Only then may one proceed with diagnosis. Otherwise, do not mistake a daily malarial fever for *śītalā* (typhoid/scholar’s fever).
Yuyan Meng said: "The World-Honored One’s samādhi was unknown to Kāśyapa; Kāśyapa’s samādhi was unknown to Ānanda;
Ānanda’s samādhi was unknown to Śāṇakavāsin; and the samādhi of the Buddhas and patriarchs is unknown to sentient beings."
Sentient beings do not know the samādhi of mountains, rivers, and the great earth; lanterns do not know the samādhi of the incense pillar.
Break through the nest of emotional consciousness and overturn the ghost-cave of the past.
When the cypress tree blooms and empty space shatters into dust—tell me, is this samādhi or is it illness? If you can discern this, you may well study Yunmen Chan. If...
If you cannot examine this thoroughly, you will inevitably see ghosts before your own skull.
Once, a monk asked Yunmen, "One may repent before the Buddha for killing one's father or mother; but where does one go to repent for killing the Buddha or the Patriarchs? Yunmen said, "Exposed."
Master Yuyuan said, "Yunmen possessed the skillful means of one who would not blink an eye when killing a man;
yet, when pressed lightly by this monk, he was left with no words to respond and no principle to assert."
Once, while Yunmen was lecturing, a monk came to visit him. After some time had passed, the monk said, "Before I reached Yunmen, it was just like the newly risen moon;
but once I arrived, it became all crooked and bent. Yunmen, knowing his intent, asked, "Is that what you say?
The monk replied, "Yes. Yunmen said, "Very good. Let me ask you: what is the newly risen moon? The monk then raised his hand to his forehead and made a gesture of salutation.
Wangyue Shi said, "If you continue like this, you will lose your eyesight in the future.
After ten days had passed, the monk returned. Shi asked again, "Have you understood yet? The monk replied, "I have not understood. Shi said, "Ask me a question.
The monk then asked, "What is the newly risen moon? Shi replied, "It is curved and crooked. The monk was at a loss. Later, the monk indeed lost his eyesight.
Langya Huijue said: "Tell me, is the Buddha-dharma efficacious or not? Suppose someone were to ask Langya today, 'What is the newly risen moon?
I would tell them: 'The sound of the wooden board being struck before the sutra hall.'"
Baizhang End said, "This monk has lost his eyes; Yunmen, moreover, cannot see his nostrils.
Although it is so, his home is in the western part of Xiangzhou.

Huanglong Xin said: "His words startle those who hear them; they leave no room for the movement of conceptual mechanisms. If one were to say that this monk has lost both his eyes and enters hell like a shot arrow, [it would be so]."
Dongchan Guan said: "Although this monk has lost both his eyes, his light shoots up to the nine heavens.
Although Yunmen’s two eyes remain, he is bright in front but dark behind.
When Yunmen ascended the hall, he said: "On level ground there are countless dead people; only when one passes through the thorn-brake forest is one a true master."
At that time, a monk stepped forward from the assembly and said, "In that case, the first seat in the hall must have some merit.
Yunmen said, "Suru suru.
Weishan Zhe remarked, "Had it not been for Yunmen being questioned by this monk, he would have nearly mistaken south for north."
Huanglong Nan held up his whisk and said, "O assembly, if you call this a whisk, you are a dead man on level ground;
if you do not call it a whisk, you have not yet penetrated the thicket of brambles."
Wuzu Yan said: "Tàipíng is not like this. On level ground, everyone is a man of stature;
only when one can sit within a thicket of brambles is one a true master. Why? Because it is a test."
Letan Qing said: "This very whisk is a thicket of brambles. How will you all pass through it?
Even if you were to pass through it, it would still be like a monkey tying itself to a pillar."
Yunju Zhuang said: "Yunju is not like this. On level ground, there are countless people who are already alive;
to enter the thorny forest is to be a true adept. If someone comes forth to speak of long and short, I pick up my staff and strike them immediately.
Why? Water wets what is moist, and fire seeks out what is dry. Misfortune and blessing have no gate; they are summoned only by oneself."
Xiaoyan Bao said: "When Yunmen was pressed by that monk, he immediately jumped ahead and sat down in the thicket of thorns himself.

I would not do so; rather, I would wait for him to say, 'In that case, the first seat in the hall has a point,' and then strike him right on the head, saying: 'Why have you again plunged into this further layer?'"
