Volume Thirty-Five and Volume Thirty-Six.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, a Dharma Heir of Baiyan in Ancient Hangzhou.
△ Sixth Yunmen said:
"To speak horizontally or vertically as one pleases is not yet to be a scion of the School Gate. As for being a scion of the School Gate—what is that?
It is like the clanging of a hot bowl. The Three Vehicles and Twelve Divisions of the Teaching are but dreams; Bodhidharma came from the West [to preach]..."
Dream. If an elderly master were to open the hall and preach the Dharma for others, what fault would there be in taking a sharp blade and killing hundreds of thousands of millions of people?
Tiantong Mian said: "His eyes overshadow all quarters; his spirit overpowers an entire age. One must grant this to the old man Yunmen. He then examined [the case].

"Look at this! That lame monk can speak, but he cannot practice. Had I been there at that time, I would have stepped right out before the assembly, gripped my wrist in frustration, and stood facing him, saying: 'Monk, why do you not cast off the three-hundred-pound iron cangue upon your neck?
Waiting for him to react, I would have immediately overturned his meditation seat."
Baiyan Fu said: "The old fellow of Shaoyang speaks from his heart and mind with his mouth; he seems quite oblivious to those around him.
Little does he realize that he has fallen into a trap of words. Is there anyone who can surpass him?"
Once, a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the Buddha? Yunmen replied, "A dried piece of excrement.
Lian'an asked, "This phrase that startles the multitude is truly startling; this extraordinary matter is indeed extraordinary.
Master Yunmen may be called peerless in his stern severity. You all must take care not to gnaw upon it here."
[The monk] chewed [on the words]. Yunmen said, "Since you know where he comes from, in which eon has there been no patriarch? He spoke on his own behalf, saying, "I am not in a good position today."
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Yunmen was like 'the guilty conscience of a thief. Jingshan is not so.
Since one already knows the source, in what kalpa have there been no patriarchs? It is not that he intends to strike the grass; he simply wishes to startle the snake."

Yunmen ascended the hall while the assembly was gathered. Pointing his staff toward the space before him, he said: "The great earth, heaven and earth, and all the buddhas as numerous as motes of dust are all contained within this.
Who can dispute the Dharma or seek victory and defeat? Is there anyone here who can offer a word of admonition?
If no one can offer an admonition, wait until I, this old fellow, do so for you. A monk said, "We request the Master to admonish us. Yunmen said, "This wild fellow!"
A fox spirit.
Yuan'an Yu said: "This old fellow uses his power to bully others. Bring me a mirror;
let us ask this old fellow to try and look into it and see how thick his face-skin is."
Yunmen asked the rector Shun of Lingzhong, "What was the meaning when the ancients held up a whisk and then lowered it?
Shun replied, "One sees before the whisk; one sees after the whisk. Yunmen said, "So it is, so it is.

Later, Yunmen raised the same question for a monk, asking, "Tell me, did you approve him at the beginning or not? The monk had no reply. Yunmen said, "It is understandable that he has lost his manners."
Yuan-an Yu spoke on behalf of the monk, saying: "The Master must also guard his verbal karma.
Yunmen addressed the assembly: "I shall not ask about the period before the fifteenth day;
bring me a single phrase for the period after the fifteenth day. He then said himself: "Every day is a good day."
Tiantong Jue said: "Those whose birth sign is the Tiger have their natal year; those whose birth sign is the Monkey are in conflict with it.
When Yunmen arrived at the storehouse, he asked a monk, 'What are you doing? The monk replied, 'Preparing an offering. Yunmen asked, 'Where are you from?'"
[The monk] said, "A person from such-and-such a place. Yunmen then called for the kitchen steward and had that elder set out the offerings.
Guishan Zhe said, "Yunmen’s temporary act of compassion ended up being too much trouble; he should have simply turned back then and there."
[He said: "To avoid being caught on people's lips and teeth. After a long silence, he said: "If one does not ascend the tower to look out, how can one know the vastness of the blue sea?
Yunmen said: "The Buddha-dharma is indeed abundant; it is simply that the tongue is too short. Then he added of himself: "It is long."
Tiantong Jue said: "Although Master Yunmen raises himself up and topples himself down, his chariot does not veer from the straight path and his principle is never crookedly severed.
Jingshan Guangzhao said: "I told you not to travel the road beneath the mountain; indeed, one hears the heart-rending cry of the monkey."
Tianning Qisong said: "Yunmen originally did not know that there was such a thing as Buddha-dharma; each of his tongues covered the worlds of the ten directions.
To deliberately speak of non-existence, existence, shortness, or length—[if I were there], I would have struck him right across the mouth with my palm."
Now tell me, where does Tianning’s intention lie? "Losing money in the river, one searches for it in the river.
Baoshou Xin said: "The two words 'Buddha-dharma' are held in Yunmen's hands as a singular piece of rare merchandise."
Little do they realize that in the school of the New Elder, not even a single bit is of any use. Why is this?
It is too short to serve as a staff for knocking on the great gate, yet too long to serve as a fire-tongs.
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the pure dharmakāya? Yunmen said, "A flower garden.
The monk asked, "What is it like when one goes forth in this very way? Yunmen said, "A golden-maned lion."
Xuedou Zhenzhu said, "Too reckless.
Zhaojue Chengqin said, "Do you know where this monk asked his question and where Yunmen gave his answer? If you can know this..."
Two mouths have but one tongue. If you do not know this, you cannot avoid being coarse and superficial.
Tiantong Jue said: "When a thief comes, you must strike; when a guest comes, you must wait. Both Yunmen and Xuedou were masters of their craft.
Is there anyone here who can go directly like this? Be careful not to bump your head or knock your forehead against something.
Yunmen addressed the assembly: "The staff has transformed into a dragon and swallowed up heaven and earth; from where could the mountains, rivers, and the great earth have come?
Tongxuan Qi said: "Yunmen’s temporary expedient is indeed fresh; yet, when one examines it closely..."
This is like clutching one's stolen goods while crying out in distress.
Lingyin Li said: "Yunmen speaking thus is much like hiding away the moon over the heavens of Chu, yet leaving behind a star in the land of Han.
I, this mountain monk, am not so. (He plants his staff. "The staff has already secured heaven and earth!"

[He said: "To whom, then, are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth entrusted? He then struck the ground with his staff and said: "When one person has cause for celebration, ten thousand people depend upon it.
Once, when a monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? Yunmen replied, "The body is exposed in the golden wind."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Yunmen’s skillful means can truly be called 'identical with phenomena and identical with principle,' 'identical with the hidden and identical with the manifest.
The three phrases may be distinguished, yet one arrowhead pierces the vast sky. Nevertheless, this is still merely sticking to the skin and clinging to the bone.
If someone were to ask Jangshan, 'What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? I would answer him, 'Supporting the heavens and buttressing the earth. Now tell me,"
These three phrases constitute a single arrowhead. To test jade, it must pass through fire; to seek pearls, one does not leave the mud. Tianning Qi said:
"If this monk had said, 'I thank the Master for answering,' Yunmen would have ensured he had no way to vindicate himself.
I, however, am not like that. When the trees wither and the leaves fall, what then? He raises his staff.
The staff. As soon as he paused to reflect, Yunmen struck him down from the Dharma Hall to avoid being scrutinized by those from all quarters.

Zhaojue Yuan said: "Yunmen possessed extraordinary faculties; striking the joints and knocking at the gate, within the flash of lightning, he untied adhesions and removed bonds for others, pulling out wedges and extracting nails. He was indeed a skilled hand. Yet, when examined closely, [his actions] were great..."
This is like handing a ladder to a thief. Here, it is not so. If someone were to ask, "What is it like when the tree withers and the leaves fall?
I would reply: "The setting clouds and the solitary wild goose fly together; the autumn waters and the vast sky are one color."
Yunju Zhuang said: "This monk poses a question that is indeed intimate and direct.
As for Yunmen answering in such a manner, does he have any way of benefiting others? Jingshan, however, is not like this. If someone were to suddenly ask such a question..."
"Just point directly. "If it were not for the wild geese arriving at night, how could one see the autumn at the sea gate? He brandished his staff, drew a line, and descended from the seat.
Tianbao Shu said, "When you receive an ox from one person, you return a horse to another," and gave a shout.
Yuanwu Keqin said: "Old Śākyamuni, having nothing to do, reaches into the water to fish for the moon;
Patriarch Bodhidharma has hands that can only grasp at empty space. Having endured the painful staff of Huangbo, he returns again to be broken-legged by Muzhou.
Three balls roll forth all at once; with whips on all sides, it is well to call one a Chan Buddha. He held up his whisk and said:
"Master Yunmen has arrived! If you seek him within the 'golden wind revealing its essence,' you are ten thousand *li* away from Yuzhou.
Baiyan Fu said, "As for following along with words and meanings, we must acknowledge Shaoyang’s response.
But as for Baiyan, it is otherwise. When the trees wither and the leaves fall, what then? He simply said to him: "Entrust it to the head of the brazier."
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the samādhi of every dust mote? Yunmen said, "Rice in the bowl; water in the bucket.
Xuedou Xian remarked, "Even a teacher with many mouths would find it difficult to bring his beak down upon this."
Baoneng Xiu said: "When this monk asked his question, he was simply demanding that [the master] produce [the answer] directly before his face.
Yunmen spoke thus; tell me, did he produce it or not?"

Zifu Guang said: "Not only within the alms bowl or the wash-tub, but even when one has attained total pervasiveness throughout the entire body, there are still those seen to suffer from hunger and thirst. Tell me, where does the fault lie?"
A monk asked Yunmen, "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in the water? Yunmen said, "In the clear waves, there is no path through.
The monk asked, "From where did you, Master, obtain this? Yunmen said, "If you ask again, from where would it come? The monk asked, "At such a time as this, what is it?
Yunmen said, "Layer upon layer of mountain passes and roads."
Zhaojue Qin said: "This monk launched a single boat onto the Dharma-sea of Yunmen and stirred up a gale of wind;
it was no easy matter to withstand him as he steered his rudder and unfurled his sails.
Yet, in the end, it is a pity he lost by one move. Tell me, where did he lose? Try to discern it."
Xiuyun of Qingshan said: "This monk has repeatedly dredged the eternal azure depths;
yet, alas, Yunmen possesses the power to overturn heaven and earth.
Chuyun of Lingyan said: "This monk was on the verge of completing a nine-tiered mountain, only to fall short by a single basketful of earth. At that time...
At that time, he simply pointed toward the Way, saying: "Who will repay the cost of the straw sandals on the Master's feet?
He waited until the other’s eyes flickered with movement, and then let out a shout, thereby sparing many people from groping for the truth within shadows and glimmers.
Yunmen ascended the hall and said: "The eyelashes span across the ten directions; the eyebrows reach upward through heaven and earth and downward through the Yellow Springs.
Mount Sumeru blocks your throat. Is there anyone who understands this? If there is someone who understands, I will drag him off to the kingdom of Campā to wrestle for the forehead with King Silla."
Yuan’an Yu said: "I am boarding a boat for Nanjing to go to Fujian. A person from Beijing has arrived;
why can I not receive news from Jiangxi? Try to say something."
Yunmen ascended the hall and, picking up his whisk, said: "If you find an entrance here, you will be a source of wonder.
In the land of Japan, they speak of Chan. A person from the Thirty-three Heavens comes forth and calls out: 'Teshar carries the cangue and passes the indictment!'"
Yuan'an Yu said: "At that time, the Son of Heaven rained down *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, *mañjūṣaka* flowers, and *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers.
A sandalwood-scented breeze delighted the hearts of the multitude; the 'Lacquered Barrel' was displeased and requested to be moved aside."
Yunmen addressed the assembly: "To speak to you of bodhi, nirvana, suchness, and liberation is to burn *fengxiang* incense as an offering to you.
To speak to you of Buddhas and patriarchs is to burn *huangshu* incense as an offering to you.

To speak to you of discourse that transcends Buddhas and surpasses patriarchs is to burn *bingxiang* incense as an offering to you. Take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Thus he spoke.
Jingshan also said: "Yunmen’s bearing was like that of a king, yet he held such a view as this master of the Dharma.
Here in my place, I speak of bodhi, nirvana, true thusness, and liberation—this is using black beans to trade for your eyes."
To speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs is to trade wooden *nāgapuṣpa* seeds for your eyes;
to speak of talk that transcends Buddhas and surpasses Patriarchs is to trade fish eyes for your eyes. Go forth and take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
Jiaoshan Chengyun said: "I am not like that either. To speak of bodhi, nirvana, true thusness, and liberation is to entangle you with old vines and strangle you to death.
To speak of Buddhas and patriarchs is to smoke you to death with dry dung.
To speak of discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs is to choke you to death with a chestnut thorn. Take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha."
[The following] is below.
Once, Yunmen was asked by a monk, "What is the True Dharma Eye? Yunmen said, "Universal.
Later, Fengxue Zhaoyan was asked by a monk, "What is the True Dharma Eye? He replied, "Blind."
Tiantong Jie said: "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? A broken sand pot. Damei Zhi said:
"These three great elders each played their own notes, composing melodies of their own accord. Tell me, is there still any distinction between near and far?
*The song of springtime snow has no one to join; once it meets a true connoisseur, it is played for them.*
Yunmen addressed the assembly: "Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a single treasure secretly hidden within the mountain of form.
Take the lantern and place it inside the Buddha hall; bring the mountain gate and mount it upon the lantern."
Lingyin Li said: "Yunmen’s announcement like this may be called 'drawing out from within the concealed point,' but at Furi, it is not so.
Within the four modes of deportment, amidst the ten thousand phenomena, there is a treasure hidden right before one's face.
He struck the meditation staff once and asked, "Do you understand? After looking around for a long while, he struck the staff once more.
The Cloud said: "The sea deity knows its nobility but not its price; it remains in the human world to illuminate the night.
Yun'an Yue said: "Yunmen’s ground is stable and secure; his supernatural powers and wondrous functions are indeed present.
Yet, if one compares this to 'loosening the glue and removing the bonds,' he still lacks one more step."
While traveling, Yunmen arrived at the residence of Chancellor Chen Cao. Cao asked, "I shall not question you regarding the Confucian classics;
you have your own masters for the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings. What, then, is the matter of a monk’s pilgrimage?
Yunmen replied, "Chancellor, how many people have you questioned on this before? Cao said, "I am questioning you, Venerable Sir, right now. Yunmen said, "For now, let that be set aside."
"What is the meaning of the teachings? Baofu Congzhan said, "Yellow scrolls and red volumes. Yunmen said, "These are merely words and language. What is the meaning of the teachings?
Congzhan said, "The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail; the mind wishes to contemplate, yet thoughts vanish.
Yunmen said, "'The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail'—this is in response to the existence of speech. 'The mind wishes to contemplate, yet thoughts vanish'—this is in response to delusion."
[Zhimen] asked, "What is the meaning of the teaching? Cao was speechless. Zhimen said, "I have heard that you, Minister, study the *Lotus Sūtra*;
is this true? Cao replied, "It is. Zhimen said, "The sūtra states: 'All worldly speech, livelihoods, and occupations...'"

All of these are not in contradiction with the true mark (*dharmatā*). Now tell me, how many people currently in the Heaven of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception (*naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana*) are falling from their positions?
Cao was again speechless. The Gatekeeper said, "Minister, you must not be so hasty. Monks abandon the thousand sutras and five treatises;
even after ten or twenty years, they still cannot manage it. How can you, Minister, be so surprised?"
Baoning Mu said: "Yunmen taught that within a single phrase there are three phrases. Now tell me: do all these previous complications lie within the three phrases or outside the three phrases?
The practitioners of all quarters have discussed this, saying that Yunmen possesses a mechanism as swift as a flash of lightning.
Although Minister Chen Cao had the sun and moon slung across his shoulders and Mount Sumeru borne upon his back,"
To come forward with a greeting is inevitably like binding oneself with a straw rope. To engage in such a discourse is to be far, far removed from the ancients.
After all, how is it? General Li has a fine reputation; even if he does not receive a fief, his life is still one of leisure.
National Teacher Shenyen of Gushan in Fuzhou (a successor of Qingliu Xuefeng Cun) addressed the assembly: "Under the gate of Gushan, one must not even cough.
At that time, a monk coughed once. The Master said, "What are you doing? The monk replied, "I have a cold. The Master said, "A cold is fine."
Langya Jue said, "The National Teacher’s thunder was quite loud, yet there were no raindrops at all.
Yungai Ben said, "Although Gusuan’s [method] is like a probing pole or a shadow-grass, he cannot help but take the crooked for the straight. Daolin said, "It is not so.
How can one avoid catching a cold? There is no other medicine within the mountains; outside the gate there are green pines."
Chengshan Huiquan said: "Gushan held fast to his borders and did not allow even half a person to pass through;
why then did he let this monk go? Have you not heard it said: 'A lion does not eat the remains left by a vulture; a swift falcon does not strike a rabbit already lying down'?"
Guangjiao Yu said: "Gushan cast his hook across the four seas, yet this monk dragged his hem at Longmen.
Although he did not employ fists or kicks, he nonetheless had a documented lineage. Everywhere it was said that Gushan was a dragon’s head with a snake’s tail."
Little did they know that this monk had already been pushed by Gushan into the deep pit of Baizhang, from which he has remained unable to emerge to this day.
Gushan addressed the assembly, saying, "If you wish to know this matter, it is like a single-edged sword. A monk then asked, "The student is a corpse."
"What is the sword? The Master said, "Drag out that corpse. The monk responded with an assent, then immediately returned beneath his robes and bowl, packed up, and departed.
That evening, the Master asked the Head Seat, "Is the monk who engaged in that dialogue still here? The Head Seat replied, "He left right then and there.
The Master said, "Well done; give him thirty blows of the staff."
Dongshan Qi said: "If this monk was unwilling, what fault did Gushan commit? If he was willing, why did he depart so abruptly?
He further said: "Gushan’s staff both rewards and punishes him. Let those with eyes try to deliberate upon this."
Xuedou Xian said: "The elders of all quarters all say that Gushan has lost one eye.
Little do they realize that beneath a heavy reward there must be brave men. Even so, if one were to examine this closely, it would inevitably result in everyone being buried at once."
Dongchan Guanzhi said: "This monk brings out a corpse and makes it appear as if it were alive.
Gushan has indeed a fine sword, yet it still lacks polishing."
Baoshou said, "Everyone says that Gushan’s staff is excellent; it is a pity, however, that he used it too late.
When the student asked, 'How is it with the sword? [Gushan] struck him across the spine twenty times and drove him out.

Although there are those in all quarters who possess tongues like swords and lips like blades, who would dare to critique him? To pass such a judgment is to have not even dreamed of Gushan. You people—"
Try examining this for yourself.

Gu Nanmen said: "This monk concealed his blade while wielding his sword, yet he was struck down by Gushan’s twenty blows until his corpse lay sprawled ten thousand *li* away. Even so, bystanders merely laugh."
A verse from Gushan says: "Directly beneath, it is still difficult to realize; Seeking through words only makes it more remote.
If one speaks of Buddhas and Patriarchs, They stand apart by the ends of the earth. He raised this to question a monk, saying, "How do you understand this?
The monk was speechless. The monk then said to his attendant, "I do not understand; please provide a substitute phrase for me. The attendant said, "The Master has..."
"How can you say that? You are still as far away as the ends of the earth. When Shanshan heard this, he called his attendant and asked, "Did you provide that monk with a substitute response for him?
The attendant replied, "Yes. Shanshan then struck him and expelled him from the monastery.
Kaixian Jin said: "Gushan and his attendant were not discreet in their actions; they were both completely exposed by this monk in one stroke. Setting that aside for a moment, consider this:
Kaixian also said, 'Directly beneath it is still difficult to comprehend; following words only leads further astray.
If we speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs, they are separated by a vast distance across the heavens. How, then, do you all understand this?"
Huìyuè’s Bǎiyánfú said: "That monk was speechless; it does no harm to understand directly right here. Gǔshān and his attendant, however, remain far away on the edge of the world.
It is not said that even understanding directly is difficult, yet seeking through words makes it all the more remote."
When Gushan first visited Xuefeng, as soon as he entered the gate, Xuefeng grabbed him and asked, "What is this? Gushan attained sudden enlightenment;
he raised his head and shook himself with a dance. Xuefeng said, "Are you applying intellectual reasoning? Gushan replied, "What reasoning could there be?"
Fengwei nodded in agreement.
Jingshan Xiu said: "As soon as the Sleeping Dragon exerts himself, the Vermilion Phoenix soars aloft.
Chan Master Ling of Cuiyan in Mingzhou (a successor of Xuefeng Cun of Qingliu) ascended the hall and said: "For one summer, I have been conversing with my brothers to the east..."
A Westerner says: "Look, are Cuiyan’s eyebrows there? Changqing says, "They have grown. Yunmen says, "A barrier.
Baofu says, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive."
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Exerting one's utmost for the sake of the assembly brings disaster from within one's own gate.
Yunju Yuan said, "Cuiyan knew it was wrong yet committed it intentionally; though he passed through the amnesty, he was not pardoned.
Yunmen will now apply the law and carry out the execution, judging the crime according to the facts. Do you recognize Changqing and Baofu? A man from Puzhou delivers a thief."
Zhaojue Qin said: "The secret of calculation is the foundation for those who reckon. Cuiyan sat still, leaving all people under heaven with their tongues tied, unable to utter a word.
Changqing said, "He is born! Through experience, wisdom grows. Baofu said, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive. This is the discernment of the refined by the refined.
Yunmen said, "The barrier. To settle the case based on the facts. Although the patriarchal masters vied with one another...
[The Master] replied: "Have you yet managed to seize the heels of Cuiyan? Do not follow in his footsteps; try to speak on this. Xuedou Zong said:
"The entire great earth is but a single eye of Cuiyan. What more need be said of whether the eyebrows are there or not?
It has reached the point where the venerable masters of all quarters have exhausted every artifice, yet they cannot escape his trap."
"What about Senior Monk Zong? [The Master] drew a circle with his whisk and said: "Entrusted to the unburdened guest of the sea and mountains;
when fishing for the giant tortoise, he casts down one perfect circle."
Daguai Tai said: "Baofu said, 'The mind of a thief is always apprehensive; only those on the same path know.
Changqing said, 'He has already been born,' which is to produce interpretations following the words. Yunmen said, 'A barrier,' which blocks the throat.
If someone were to ask Daguai, 'What then? [he] would take up his staff, strike it once, and say, 'All are threaded through as one.'"
Baoneng Xiu said: "Xuedou says that when a thief is skillful, even ghosts and spirits do not know him.

Since he has been seen through by both Baofu and Tiantong, Cuoyan is clearly no good hand. What he fails to realize is that such great masters as Yunmen and Changqing have all had their feet and nostrils pierced at once by a single strand of Cuoyan’s eyebrows."
Jingshan Xiu said, "Cuiyan was also selling flour along with the bran. He further said, "A troop of unperforated iron hammers.
Songyin Ruan said, "Baofu said, 'The heart of a thief is always apprehensive; good deeds do not leave the door. Changqing... [text fragmentary]
The Way arises from this. Evil news travels a thousand miles. Yunmen’s "Gate of the Way" is a mistake;
this whole crew of fellows only knows how to protect their eyebrows, yet they do not realize they have lost their nostrils.
Today, Longfeng intends to settle the case with them based on the facts. Does the assembly understand? The summer heat departs entirely with the clouds and rain; the clear breeze penetrates—
Entering the courtyard, he let out a shout.
Puming responded, "Truly a thief! Truly a thief!
Baoshang said, "Cuiyan only knows that it is easy to open one's mouth; he did not realize his tongue was so long. Changqing was stirred.
Entering the head of the realm of craving: Yunmen hangs a medicine bag upon his funeral bier; Baofu embraces his stolen goods and cries out for injustice.
Today, Baozhang has closed the case based on the evidence. Yet, I wish to reveal a further message so that all may know it together.
He then raised his whisk and said: "If you do not take it when you see it, you will regret it a thousand miles away."
Tianmu Lü said: "Cuiyan thought he was wiping away spittle, but who knew that the mess would become even greater?
Baofu, Changqing, and Yunmen—unfit for this—they added further filth upon the existing mess.
Nevertheless, when these brothers act in such a manner, tell me: do they still rely on their own calculations?"
Cuiyan was invited by the Dharma Seat Master to a lecture hall feast. Cuiyan said, "I, this mountain monk, have a question. If you can answer it, you shall have the meal.
He then picked up a sesame cake and asked, "Does this possess the Dharma-body? The Seat Master replied, "It does.
Cuiyan brought the sesame cake to his mouth and said, "In that case, you have eaten the Dharma-body. The Seat Master was speechless.
Yunmen Wenyan spoke on behalf of the presiding master (zuozhu), specifically thanking the Master for descending to honor the empty assembly.
Mingyin Hui spoke on behalf of the presiding master, saying: "I did not expect that even a master of our school would hold such a view."
Chan Master Jiaoran of Changsheng in Fuzhou (the sixth generation descendant of Xuefeng Yicun) was once asked by a monk, "What is the first phrase?
Xuefeng remained silent for a long while. The monk reported this to Jiaoran, who said, "This is the second phrase.
Xuefeng then instructed the monk to ask again, "What is the first phrase? Jiaoran replied, "Heaven! Heaven! (Cangtian, Cangtian).
Baiyan Fu said: "Xuefeng Changsheng exhausted his divine insights and wondrous strategies, yet he could only maintain the second phrase.
Even if Gautama closed his room and Vimalakīrti remained silent, they too could only maintain the second phrase.
But what is the first phrase? Return to the hall and drink tea."
Changsheng was asked by a monk: "An ancient said, 'Ignorance is itself Buddha-nature; there is no need to eliminate afflictions. What is meant by 'ignorance is itself Buddha-nature'?
Changsheng became enraged, changed his expression, and raising his fist, scolded him, saying, "Today I am going to beat this monk away!
[The monk asked: "What is meant by 'there is no need to eliminate afflictions'? Changsheng grabbed the man's head with his hand and said, "This..."
The Master [Zhaozhou] was able to provoke such karmic activity in people.
Jianfu said, "Changsheng’s response to the question was much like following another's footsteps.
Chan Master Hongtao of Anguo in Fuzhou (a dharma heir of Xuefeng Yicun) cited the inscription on the National Teacher’s stele, saying: "Obtained from..."
The mind is like an *eranda* tree that has become a sandalwood tree; it loses its essence. Ambrosia becomes a garden of thorns.
He said to the monk, "A single word must encompass both the meanings of gain and loss. How would you say it? The monk held up his fist and said, "One cannot call this a 'fist.
Daoyao did not approve, so he also held up his fist and said differently, "It is precisely because one calls this thing a 'fist' [that it is so]."
Regarding this, Xuedou Xian said: "A fellow who binds himself with no rope; he does not even recognize his own fist.
Daopi Xiu said: "Xuedou An and Guo all claim to be solitary and lofty beyond the mundane world, yet when it comes to facing the edge of the blade..."
The Enemy. Furthermore, he follows the ranks and marches along with them.
Tiantong Hua said: "If you can see through Xuedou, then you will see that Anguo has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake."
If one's insight is not penetrating, one will see the *eranda* tree as a sandalwood tree and nectar as a garden of thorns.
Dongchan Guanzhuo said: "This monk could not silence the mouth of An-guo;
An-guo could not stop the criticism of Xuedou; and Xuedou could not avoid the censure of Dayue. Pity this band of fellows! Not so.
How can one deal with a single fist? He waited for [the Master] to say, "I want a phrase that encompasses both the meanings of gain and loss," whereupon [the Master] simply said, "Stop.
Why is it so? A single drop of lion’s milk scatters ten bushels of donkey’s milk.
Nantang Yu said: "I am not like An-guo, who could only speak of the gain and loss of a treatise with a single word and two meanings.
He took up his staff and said: "This staff of mine can kill and can give life; within giving life there is killing, and within killing there is giving life.

Sometimes killing and giving life occur simultaneously; sometimes killing and giving life do not occur simultaneously. If you can employ it skillfully, [it applies to] both the mundane and the supramundane."
There is no dharma that is not fully prepared; thus, one can observe the mastery of taking and letting go, with unimpeded flexibility and contraction.
If you cannot employ it, you are nothing but a fellow who binds himself without a rope.
Xiyuan Bao said: "Big or small, An Guo’s heels have not yet touched the ground."
Gounan said: "An-guo is one who falls down by his own doing. To call it a 'fist'—is this losing?
It cannot be called a 'fist'—is this gaining? Precisely because you call it a 'fist,' if you run about on the path of gain and loss, what end will there ever be?
Although Xuedou shifts the strings to produce a different melody, he nonetheless [remains within the same realm]."
"Having emerged from this old circle, how is it ultimately? He spreads his hands and says, "One must quickly turn one's eyes to look at the immortal.
Fourth Patriarch Lang said, "Where is the place where An-guo has a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail? If you can examine and discern this, [you will understand]."
The *eranda* plant acting as a sandalwood tree—when examined, it is not so. Nectar being a garden of thorns.

The Venerable Fu of Taiyuan (a successor of Xuefeng Cun of Qingliu) went up to Xuefeng. Upon hearing this, Xuefeng gathered the assembly; they proceeded to the Dharma Hall, where Xuefeng looked around.
Xuefeng then went down to oversee the administrative affairs. The next day, [Fu] went up again to pay his respects and said, "I, this humble one, yesterday..."
Ri touched upon an offense against the Abbot. Feng said, "Knowing it is such a matter, one simply leaves it at that.
Xuedou Xian said, "A master of the school with fifteen hundred disciples was caught by Old Fu’s single glance and immediately raised his white flag of surrender.
It is indeed so when he says tomorrow, 'Knowing it is such a matter, one simply leaves it at that.'"
When a monk asked Yunmen Wenyan, "What is the point of offending him? Yunmen struck him. Xuedou said, "Even if he were to strike hundreds of thousands of people, what use would that be?
One must wait until all the people of the great earth have been struck with the staff before one can truly uphold Xuefeng.
But tell me, what kind of eye did Taiyuan Fu possess?"
Yunju Shun said, "The great and small Xuefeng were both deluded by Elder Fu for a time.
He further said, "This very Elder Fu is also one who carries his own shackles while passing through the legal proceedings."
Xuedou Zong said: "They know only one, but do not know two; they fail to realize that Xuefeng was planning his strategy within his tent to secure victory a thousand miles away.
Although the Venerable Fu presented his lifelong insights, he remained entirely within Xuefeng’s circle."
Nantang Yu said: "Eye meets eye; mind knows mind. A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the point of offense?
Yunmen struck him. "The eyes upon the staff are as clear as the sun," [said] Xuedou.
"Even if you strike a thousand or ten thousand people, what use is that? If you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire."
Famin Mize said: "When Master Fu went up to the Dharma Hall and looked around, he then went down to oversee the administrative affairs.
Where was it that he offended him? Xuefeng said, 'Once you know this kind of matter, you can stop. But tell me, what matter did he know?"
Baiyan Fu said: "Xuedou says that the master patriarchs of fifteen hundred people were defeated by Old Fu with a single glance and immediately raised the white flag of surrender.
But did he know that the old fellow Xuefeng was able to sit and observe the victory or defeat without moving a weapon?"

Daowu Yuan went from Mount Gu to attend to the invitation of the Prince of Min. As he was being escorted out by the gatekeepers of Xuefeng, Xuefeng said upon his return to the Dharma Hall, "A single holy arrow has been shot into the innermost city.
Daowu said, "He is not yet there. Xuefeng said, "He is a man who has reached the very bottom.
Daowu said, "If you do not believe me, wait until I go and examine him for myself. He then pursued him to the middle of the road and asked:
"Brother, where have you been going? Shanshan said, "I have gone into the nine-layered city. Yuan asked, "What if you suddenly encounter an encirclement by a threefold army?
He replied, "He has his own path leading to the heavens. Yuan said, "In that case, you have left the palace and lost the hall.
He replied, "Where would he not be entitled to his dignity? Fufu shook his sleeves and turned back. Feng asked Yuan, "How was it? Yuan...
Yuan said, "What a fine holy arrow! It has snapped in mid-course. He then recounted the previous conversation.
Feng said, "He still has something to say. Yuan remarked, "That old fellow still has some local sentiment. Feng then withdrew.
Taisu Zhe said: "There has been no small amount of deliberation on this story among the assembly. Some say that as soon as he asks, 'Where are you going?
one should strike him right here; not striking is where the sage’s arrow breaks. Others say, 'What if one suddenly encounters being surrounded by a threefold army?
One should strike; not striking is where the sage’s arrow breaks. To theorize in such a manner is not only...
To deceive others is also to deceive oneself. Do you understand? Xiangru once seized the "City-of-Ten-Thousand-Leagues" jade; the Lord of Qin remained at ease, bringing about peace and prosperity.
Baofeng Wen said: "Xuefeng was a spiritual friend of fifteen hundred people, receiving the offerings of kings and lords."
"The causes and conditions for karmic retribution are not non-existent. If this were the Buddha-dharma, it would not yet have reached the point [of realization].
Dongshan, however, was not like that. When [Fushan] said, 'A fine holy arrow,' [Dongshan] broke it in mid-flight. He then asked him, 'What did you say?
As Fushan was about to speak, Dongshan struck him with a heavy blow and drove him out. This was done so that Master Fu would, from then on, become a monk of true substance."
Second, he sharpens the edge of the noble arrow for his disciples. Third, he serves as a true patriarch of the Chan gate to act as eyes for future generations.
All you virtuous Chan practitioners: is this so or not? Let those with eyes discern it.
Baoning Yong said in a separate dialogue with Gushan: "Upāda Fu, I also know you are a wicked man. Jingshan Hongzhi asked:
"In the midst of the assembly, where was it that the holy arrow broke? [The monk] replied: "Gushan was not right to answer his question;
this is where the holy arrow broke. Gushan was not right to speak of principle; this is where the holy arrow broke."
To critique it in this way at the point where the arrow broke is not only to fail to recognize Gushan; it is also to fail to recognize Old Fu.
Little do you realize that Upāli Fu was precisely a rogue who suffered a total defeat before Gushan and returned home in shame.
To come now to Xuefeng to uproot him from his foundation is much like peddling goods within one's own house.
Yangzhou. Had it not been for Xuefeng’s marks of a great man, where would that thief have had room to hide?
It was a pity he let him go at that time; it became an unresolved case.
Is there anyone here now who can avenge the ancients? Come forward and I shall ask you: where did the holy arrow break?
Tianning Qisong said: "The holy arrow of Gushan has shot its way into the nine-layered city, full of martial spirit.
Yet Fuzhao Zuoshang said, "The arrow is broken. This is to falsely impute a crime upon another and then charge them with it.
Miaoxi says that Fuzhao Zuoshang was a mere bandit who returned from the presence of Gushan having suffered a defeat; he went back riding the very horse of his enemy to kill him.

"Thief! Heaven above! Heaven above! Generally speaking, nothing arises in isolation. At that time, Xuefeng was merely flaunting that one 'sage arrow,' which led to the thief coming to plunder his house.
Had he bitten down with clenched teeth, who would have dared to stir up waves where there is no wind?
Even if the entire world—its rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds—were transformed into monks, they would still not be able to..."
Even Guishan had no opening to speak; Tianning was not disparaging the ancients. What is this "sage’s arrowhead"?
It is like tossing a stalk of latrine grass onto a rubbish heap. If you further ask where it breaks, do not let yourself boil in cauldron soup.
Yunmen Cheng said: "One person revives from within death; a fine hand, indeed a fine hand! Another withdraws from the road;
where he gains the advantage, he loses it. Xuefeng said: "A fine holy arrow shot into the nine-layered city.
This is already like casting a hook and throwing a line. Fuzhao Shouzhuo said: "Wait for me..."
Only after thorough investigation can one succeed; the blind turtle and the lame tortoise have already met with defeat.

Fufu pursued [his teacher] halfway home and reported the matter to Xuefeng, which was much like "seizing the hair-tuft and heading to the yamen. Xuefeng said, "He still has something to say; you must know that this is not a good heart.
Fufu said, "This old frozen fellow still has some local sentiment. [He] greedily looked ahead and did not realize—

The Way. A night’s separation by cold and warmth; a guest’s beard, spurred on for two years. Tell me, how far apart is this from the ancients?
Zen Master Guangde Zhou of Xiangzhou (the successor of Qingjiu Guangde Yan) was asked by a monk: "Ajita, without severing afflictions..."

[He] was practicing dhyāna-concentration. The Buddha prophesied that this person would undoubtedly attain Buddhahood. How is this principle to be understood? Zhou said, "The salt is exhausted and the charcoal is gone.
[The other] asked, "What is it like when the salt is exhausted and the charcoal is gone? Zhou said, "Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful."
"To speak of giving rise to sorrow is to kill oneself with sorrow.
Jingshan Daokai said, "The ancients did so; it is called 'washing one's feet and then stepping onto the boat.
Yuan'an Meng said, "Were it not for coming to the ferry crossing to inquire about the way, how could one have roamed through the springtime of Wuling?"
Chan Master Chengyuan of Xianglin in Qingcheng, Yizhou (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan of Qingzhou). A monk asked, "What is the single lamp inside the room?
Chengyuan said, "Three people testify that a tortoise is a turtle."
Suīyán Yùn said: "The three men have taken a tortoise and turned it into a turtle; each has a tongue in its mouth.
When the occasion arises, they fail to discern the wind coming from; even when drinking water, one must guard against choking. Old Xiānglín was able to twist and pull;
the true lamp illuminating the world was blown out entirely. He let out a shout.
Xianglin was asked by a monk, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? Xianglin said, "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains. Xuedou Xian commented:
"In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains—ten thousand kinds, a thousand variations. The crane perches on the pine, cold;
the man treading through snow, freezing. Bodhidharma did not understand it; truly a great difficulty, a great difficulty!"
Zhaojue Qin said: "To bring up one is to clarify all three; the apertures of the patch-robed monks are of a single track despite their thousand differences.
This is the essential tongs and hammer. Even so, Daolin does not think so. If someone were to ask, 'What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
I would simply answer him: 'Cotton wrapping a stone; iron encasing a lump of mud.'"
Tiantong Hua said: "When Xianglin spoke thus—'A rat enters an ox's horn'—if someone were suddenly to ask Guizong, 'What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
he would simply reply to him: 'Next year there will be new branches again;
the spring breeze that disturbs us shall never cease.'"
Tiantong Muan said: "The ancient ancestor Ying’an speaking in this way still cannot avoid the fault of grasping at the front while losing the rear.
If it were I, and someone asked, 'What is the matter beneath the patched robe? I would simply say to him:
'A single breath speaks not, yet it contains all forms; where do the myriad spirits go to thank its impartiality?'"
Gounan said: "Xianglin practices spring ordinances in winter; Xuedou tears down the east to patch up the west.
If you wish to understand the matter beneath the patched robe, each of you must seek it for yourselves."
Lingyan Chu said: "To answer in such a manner, though it may be timely and appropriate to the occasion, cannot avoid shifting from the east to patch the west.
If it were Dongshan, it would not be so. [Question: 'What is the matter beneath the monastic robe? [Dongshan] replied: 'Movement gives rise to wind. Now tell me:
which is it, that of Xianglin or that of Dongshan? If you can discern this, then [you have realized] Dongshan."
"Your life and nature are in the hands of others; you cannot find them through inspection. Your life and nature are in the hands of Dongshan.
He threw down his staff and said, "Those who carry their lives, come to the hook!"
New clouds form in the sky. Where Xuedou drags through mud and carries water, Zhaojue cuts iron and chops nails.
Where Zhaojue cuts iron and chops nails, he drags through mud and carries water. Do you all know how Xianglin acts for others?
A dog runs off with a dry bone in its mouth.
Baoguang said: "The lead call was lofty and the response was likewise steep; this indeed belongs to those two elders.
As for the matter within the patched robe, one has not yet even dreamed of it."
Ou-feng Chengyun said: "This lot of fellows have wrongly added annotations beneath the matter of the patched robe;
each deserves thirty blows of the staff.
Xue-zhai said: "The two venerable masters dangle their hands before the emerald steps and pass through the lapis lazuli hall."
[This is] practice. If this is the matter beneath the patched robe, it is ten thousand miles of white clouds.
Chan Master Baiyun Zixiang of Shaoyang (the seventh generation successor of Yunmen Wenyan) asked a monk: "Without destroying conventional designations, you speak of the true mark (*dharmatā*).
How do you understand this? The monk pointed to a chair and said, "This is a chair. Xiang pushed the chair away with his hand.
Yi said, "Bring me my shoe bag. The monk had no reply. Xiang said, "This fellow is a hollow-headed charlatan.
When Yunmen Wenyan heard this, he remarked, "One must be like him to achieve it."
Jingshan Daowu said: "Yunmen supports the strong and does not support the weak; yet how can one help it that a parent, out of affection for their child, fails to notice their ugliness?
If that monk had been a true man at that time, when Yunmen said, 'Bring me your shoe bag,' he would have overturned the meditation seat.
Even if Baiyun’s teeth were like sword-trees and his mouth like a blood-basin, he still could not have distinguished between them."
Tianning Qi held up his staff and said: "This is the provisional name; that is the true reality. This is the true reality;
that is the provisional name. One is not so; two do not hold. When the road is long and the night is deep, do not carry a torch;
let us all blow it out and walk in the dark."

Zhaoqing Ting said: "The public way is impartial; the sentiments of the people find their proper place. Since you are well-versed in the principles of wind and constitution, how could you permit a substitute?
Although it is easy to discern the oncoming blow, alas, it is difficult to decide whether to advance or retreat. After a long silence, he said: "I let this one move pass."
Nanjian asked: "Yunmen’s 'loving his son so much that he fails to notice his ugliness'—I do not know why Baoyun lost one of his eyes at that time.
Why? He had only the sword that kills, but lacked the sword that gives life."
Chan Master Yuanmi Yuanming of Dingshou (the seventh generation descendant of Yunmen Wenyan) ascended the hall and said:
"When all is exhausted and gone, even the Buddhas of the three periods of time have their mouths hanging on the wall. Yet there is still one person who laughs loudly, 'Ha-ha!
If you can recognize this person, your studies as a seeker are finished."
Touzi Qingyun said: "The moon over the楚天 (Chutian) has been hidden away; yet the stars of the 汉地 (Handi) still remain.
Ba’en Xiu took up Touzi’s words and concluded: "The cart has already gone; what use is there for the oil vat?"
Boshan Lai said: "To stand alone in peril is not yet enough; one must further apply intimacy. To have no self beyond the Dharma still lacks the lion’s roar.
The nostrils and the eyebrows have never known each other; once they do know each other, the tongue is originally within the mouth."
Baiyan Fu said: "This mountain monk intends to take leave of Xianxiu to travel far to Chang'an.
I bid a long farewell to the mists, clouds, birds, and trees; I clasp arms with carriages, horses, robes, and official caps.
If you can perceive even a single glimpse here, what difficulty would there be in meeting those of other mountains?"
Deshan ascended the hall. Whenever Master Juzhi was questioned, he would simply raise a single finger.
When it is cold, it is cold throughout heaven and earth; when it is hot, it is hot throughout heaven and earth.
Xuedou Xian said, "Where did you see Old Jizhi? Do not mistake the fixed mark on the scale. He further said, "The myriad phenomena of the forest and mountains are utterly solitary and perilous;
the great earth, rivers, and mountains pierce through to the heavens in their sheer danger.
Where can one find the 'one-finger Zen'? Miaoxi remarked, "One might say this is like a person of high station who easily forgets."
The Ancient South Gate says: "Whether there is profit or no profit, one does not leave the marketplace.

Regarding this, Zen Master Xinkai Haojian of Baling in Yuezhou (the seventh generation descendant of Yunmen Wenyan): A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
Baling said, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it goes down into the water."
Wuzu Yan said, "Great Ba Ling only managed to say half of it. Baiyun, however, was not like this: "Scoop up the water and the moon is in your hand;
play with the flowers and their fragrance fills your robes. Furthermore, when a monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
he replied, "When a man is poor, his ambitions are short; when a horse is thin, its hair is long."
Foji said, "Master Yan’s writing is all wrinkled and crinkled; he too only managed to say half of it. Long’an, however, was not like this.
Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? A horse is saddled; a donkey pulls a millstone.
Baling addressed the assembly: "The Patriarch said, 'It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. Since it is neither the banner nor the wind, where does it reside?
If there is anyone who can act as the Patriarch's advocate, let them come forth and meet with Baling."
Xuedou Xian said: "Xuedou says, 'The wind moves, the banner moves. Since these are both wind and banner, where can they be placed?
If there is anyone who can act as a patron for Ba Ling, let them also come forth and meet with Xuedou."
Gunan said: "Baling was much like seeing the horns and knowing it is an ox; Xuedou, too, was merely blowing fire with the wind.
Though he was certainly able to exert his full strength in upholding [the teaching], he nonetheless did not know how to act as the master for the Patriarch.
Gunan, too, was merely blowing fire with the wind. 'It is not the wind moving, nor is it the banner moving. O assembly, Master Caoxi—"
He comes! Keep your eyes open!
Chan Master Shuangquan Shi Kuanming of Suizhou (the seventh generation descendant of Yunmen Wenyan) returned from his mountain tour. The Head Seat led the assembly to the gate to receive him.
The Head Seat said, "It was no easy matter for the Master to traverse these perilous mountains. Kuanming raised his staff and said, "I have attained it entirely."
"This is that very power. Nanquan then snatched away the staff; Huikuan relaxed his body and fell down. The assembly all stepped forward to help him up.
Once Huikuan had risen, he used the staff to drive everyone away at once. Turning back, he said to his attendant, "I told you: it is entirely this very power that prevails."
Huanglong Nan said: "Although Mingjiao knows how to rise and how to fall, he did not realize that his cleverness resulted in clumsiness.
Zifu Lu said: "One fall and one rise have their own established protocols; yet at that time, the entire assembly failed to help him up.
Not only was this a way to spare him a blow from the staff, but let us see how this old man will get up. Furthermore—
"Cloud," "Perilous. Baiyan Fu said:
"The Head Seat saw the righteousness and acted with courage, yet he still lacked the final stroke; his attendant, Zhichong, exerted force to protect him, thereby needlessly provoking resentment.
As for a man of clear instruction, though it is said that his hands and eyes are everywhere, capable of bestowing or withholding..."
[He was] at ease. However, he could not avoid having his lips and skin split from laughter by his attendant.
Chan Master Shouchu of Dongshan in Xiangzhou (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan) visited Yunmen. Yunmen asked, "Where have you recently come from?"
Shan said, "Chadu. Mendun asked, "Where is Xia? Shan said, "Baoci in Hunan. Mendun asked, "When did you leave there?
Shan said, "The twenty-fifth of the eighth month. Mendun said, "I grant you three blows of the staff.
The next day, Shan went up to pay his respects and asked, "Yesterday I received the Master’s three blows of the staff; I do not know where my fault lay. Mendun—
[Shishuang] said, "You rice-bag! You go off to Jiangxi and Hunan acting like this. At these words, Xuefeng attained great enlightenment.
Xuedou Xian said, "Yunmen’s spirit was like that of a king; when pressed, it would melt away like ice or crumble like tiles.
Had he enforced his command at that time, his descendants would not have been cut off even today."
Baizhang Yuan said, "The great Yunmen was so struck by Dongshan’s single question that he was left with sweat pouring from his forehead and glue forming in his mouth.
Tiantong Jie said, "Yunmen was too generous in letting go and too stingy in gathering back; what was the point of his final earnestness?"
"To not give him his own share of grass and fodder. Dongshan’s awakening in this manner was also like "divining with a ladle while listening to empty sounds.
Lingyin Yue said: "The various quarters all claim that father and son meet in resonance, that the pecking and the prodding occur simultaneously; yet they do not realize..."
Yunmen’s true command was not carried out; instead, he rolled about in a patch of weeds, causing Dongshan to lose his nostrils so that, to this day, there is no place to search for them.
Baoning Moshan said: "Yunmen held the probing pole in his hand; Dongshan accepted the crime with the stolen goods in his arms.
Had Yunmen only just opened his mouth at that time, Dongshan should have fully spread his sitting mat and prostrated three times, then returned to the guest quarters.
Observe this fellow—where would he have applied the wedge?"
Fushan [Yuan] said: "When grasping the universe, there is no path for Buddhas or patriarchs to enter;
when opening wide the rivers and seas, fish and dragons find the means to swim. The old man Yunmen was indeed extraordinary.
Xuedou said: "Yunmen’s bearing was like that of a king; once pressed, he would melt away like ice. What did he know of good and evil? At that time, if..."
"Acting according to the command, he blinds the eyes of all people in the world.
Ruoyan Yun said, "Yunmen bestowed three blows of the staff upon Dongshan; how do you all understand this?"
When people gather together, they say: "Dongshan was accustomed to being a guest and rarely met with those who understood him;
Yunmen’s restaurant, though open, did not permit anyone to eat. Therefore, Xuedou suppressed Yunmen and brought Dongshan forth, while Fushan diminished Xuedou and supported Yunmen.
Such perspectives are as far apart as heaven and earth. If you people wish to...
Do you understand? Every year on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, at Chadu, it remains as ever, steeped in autumn chill.
Tianjing said: "The mountains are high and the waters are deep; clouds move and birds fly. This may be acceptable for Yunmen, but it is not acceptable for Tianjing.
Why? Because a house is not wealthy if it has no goods that do not circulate.
Lingyan Zuoyun said: "When Xuedou speaks thus, does he intend to discredit Yunmen, or does he intend to discredit Dongshan?
If you say that 'a single drop of ink forms two dragons,' you miss what is right before your eyes;
yet if you further say that 'the two parts are different and are gathered into the superior category,' you betray the former sages. Today, this mountain monk does not seek..."
Salt added to snow. If you all have it, with the hairs on your body standing on end—do you have it? Do you have it?
After a long silence, he struck the ground with his staff and said: "You rice-bag! Go off like this to Jiangxi and Hunan!"

Yuan-an Yu said: "When Yunmen reached this point, he could not hold it back either; he caused people to ascend further and further, seeing that the single branch of the Old Barbarian has been swept away to its very roots."
Fahen Mi said, "If Dongshan had not been diligent at the very end, he would have fallen into a pit of烂泥 (rotten mud) from which he could never have been pulled out.
He also said, "It was precisely because of his diligence at the very end that he fell into a pit of rotten mud from which he could never be pulled out."
Xuefeng Xian said: "Yunmen let go of Dongshan’s three blows of the staff; this was a lack of filiality on the part of the father. Xuedou acted according to the mandate;
this is righteousness that brings a bountiful year. Do you wish to see Dongshan? Only when one dwells in a great state does one know the value of nobility."
When water reaches Xiao and Xiang, it is equally clear.
Dongshan addressed the assembly: "On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a 'dog-urine day.
On the top of the banner pole, they fry *zhui* seeds; three monkeys toss coins at night."
Daowu Zhen gave a different version, saying: "The old monk does not say it this way. A three-faced wildcat treads upon the moon;
a two-headed white ox grasps smoke in its paws. A crowned green hare stands upon the courtyard cypress; a shell-shedding turtle flies up into the heavens."
Furthermore, tell me: where does the error lie?
Baofu Da said, "It is equally like painting eyes and eyebrows upon empty space; Dongshan and Dowu are only slightly different."
Yunxi Zhen said: "Shang Daren! Pack it up! What is it? How is it? Zhao, Qian, Sun, Li!
When Dongshan ascended the hall, his words did not elaborate upon things, and his speech did not hit the mark. Those who rely on his words perish; those who linger in his phrases are deluded."
Furthermore, it is said: "Within these four lines of verse, you must see clearly and become a liberated monk.

With a roof of rafters and a floor of tiles, through the causal conditions of rice gruel and meals, you will be fit to serve as a spiritual friend to gods and humans. If you do not understand this, you will ultimately remain muddled and confused."
Yuan'an Yu said: "In a dream at night, something inauspicious appeared; I inscribed it upon the wall. When a gentleman read it, it was transformed into a great omen of good fortune.
Dongshan, when asked by the Imperial Censor Taibao, said: "The eye enters into right concentration; from all sensory objects, samādhi arises. This is the meaning.
"How is it? Dongshan asked. "In Taibao’s tea bowl there is Dongshan; in Dongshan’s tea bowl there is Taibao. Taibao was speechless.
He then took these words and asked Guyin about them. Guyin said, "It does not fall into the realm of wordlessness.
He then asked Yanqing. Yanqing said, "What do you call samādhi?"
Huanji said to Ji: "When Sanlao speaks in this way, he is far too verbose.
If someone were to ask Huanji, 'What is the samādhi of entering right reception through the sense-base of the eye and arising from the various sensory objects? I would simply say to him: 'Pass.'"
Yuan'an Yu said: "One kind of Chan for a matron, one for a bride, and one for a daughter—all have been defeated by the Grand Guardian."
A monk once asked Dongshan, “What is the Buddha? Dongshan replied, “Three pounds of flax.
Tianbao Shu said, “It is still tolerable that a rope might grow from flax, but how can one bear for a snake to grow from the rope?
He let out a shout and said, “A single path traveling back and forth through the streets of Chang’an.”
Jin-su Yuan said: "If you can understand it here, it is easy to see Dongshan; it is difficult to see yourself.
Now that you have seen Dongshan, why do you not see yourself? He then held up his fist and said, "Look, look!
How much does this weigh?"
Songyin Li said: "I am not like Dongshan, who pointed east to speak of the west. When asked, 'What is the Buddha?'—to whom were you asking?
If his eyes flickered or he moved, I would have simply told him: 'The ancient Buddhas passed away long ago.'"
Chan Master Wukong Jì of Beichán in Qízhōu (a successor of Yúnmén Wǎn of the Seventh Generation of Qīngyán) asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "Huangzhou.
The Master asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The monk replied, "Zífú. The Master asked, "With what do you sustain that 'fortune'? The monk replied, "A double case.
The Master said, "What can you do when you are in the hands of Beichán? The monk said, "If it is in your hands, then take it back. The Master then—
He struck him. The monk was not satisfied. Chan followed him out. Xuedou Xian said, "Strange!
He truly possesses a talent that surpasses his teacher. Do you know this monk? He only knows how to pursue what is ahead and cannot look back.
Had he been in Xuedou’s hands, even if the staff were broken, I would not have let him go."
Baoning Mocheng said: "Beichan cast his hook; this monk offered his line. One was half a pound, the other eight ounces.
Tell me, where does the superiority or inferiority lie—is it with this monk or with Beichan?"
Nantang Yu said: "Once you have started, do not stop until it is finished. To strike someone, one must have an iron fist.
When Chan Master Fengxian Shen of Jinling (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan) was among the assembly with Master Tongming, he heard a monk ask Fayan, "What is form?
Fayan held up his whisk. Some say he meant "cock's comb flower," while others say he meant "clinging to the flesh."
Sweatshirt. The two men went specifically to seek instruction. They asked, "We have heard that the Master has 'three kinds of colored talk'; is this so? Fayan said, "Yes.
Shen said, "A hawk flies over Silla," and immediately returned to the assembly. Li Houzhu was present in the seat and did not agree.
He said to Fayan, "Tomorrow I shall prepare a tea ceremony and invite the two monks to ask their questions anew. The next day...
Later, the Master prepared a chest of colored silks and a sword, and said to the two men, "Today I invite the Abbot to ask questions anew.
If he answers correctly, he shall be rewarded with the assorted silks; if he answers incorrectly, he shall receive only the sword.
Fayen ascended the seat, and Shen stepped forward to question him: "Today I have received an imperial decree to inquire of you; does the Master grant permission? Fayen replied, "I grant permission."
Deshen said, "A hawk passing over Silla. He took the ceremonial cloth and departed immediately; the assembly dispersed at once. At that time, Fadeng was serving as the *karmadāna* (Vina).
He struck the bell to assemble the monks before the Sangha hall for an examination and inquiry. Fadeng said, "I have heard that the Senior Monk [Deshen] has long been at Yunmen.
What extraordinary causes and conditions does he possess? Let us cite one or two cases to deliberate upon them. Deshen said, "The ancients..."
A person said: "The egrets descend upon the fields—a thousand dots of snow; the orioles ascend the trees—a single branch of blossoms.
The *vinaya-dhara* asked, "How do you deliberate upon this? As Deng hesitated, Shen struck him with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*) and immediately returned to the assembly.
Furiru said: "The Dharma-eye is the mark of a great man; the Dharma-lamp is for a petty fellow. Senior Upasaka Shen is accustomed to finding his advantage therein.
Nevertheless, once you reach the gate of Long’an, you shall not be permitted to move a single thing. Why? Because one who recognizes the Dharma stands in awe."
Yunxi Ting said: "Even if Faideng were to dig a pit ten thousand feet deep and bury him all at once, it would still be like drawing a bow after the thief has already fled.
How much more so when he was captured on the spot—this cannot but result in the loss of troops and the disgrace of the state.
Master Shen, Master Shen, having gained the advantage, you must not go back again."
Fengxian and Master Ming went together to the Huai River. They saw a man pulling a net when a fish leaped out from within it.
Fengxian said, "Brother Ming, how magnificent! It is just like a true monk. Ming said, "Even so, it would have been better had he not run right into the net in the first place.
Fengxian said, "Brother Ming, you have realized the truth! Ming then reached the center [of the river].
At night, Ming finally attained realization.
Jingshan Daokai said, "As for that which the Venerable Ming has realized, tell me: is it within the net or outside the net?"
Yuan'an Yu said: "Once bitten by a snake, for three years one fears rotten grass.
Xidun Chao said: "One must know that the words of the ancients were not spoken in vain. But tell me, where was his lack of awakening?
If you seek it within the words of Minggong, you will have to strike until the staff is broken—if you remain muddled and vague..."
I have spoken to cause some confusion; I have beaten them until the staff was broken, yet I still do not let them rest.
Aside from these two paths, is there anyone who knows where the two masters have fallen? Then, laughing heartily, he said: "They have entered! They have entered!"
Dongta Xi said: "Deep Chan spreads the net of Heaven to test the nostrils of monks.
It is a pity that Master Ming, a man of such vast capacity, was turned back by the flow of words. Although he had no lack of realization at the end, he could not avoid passing through his net."
Chan Master Huanglong Zan of Meizhou (a successor of Yunmen Wenyan of Qingzhou) asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xianglin.
Huanglong asked, "How long have you been there? The monk said, "Six years. Huanglong said, "The World-Honored One stayed at the Snow Mountains for six years and realized unsurpassed bodhi.
What have you accomplished during your six years at Xianglin? The monk was speechless. Huanglong said, "Move!"
A man who eats his meals in the kitchen.
Baoshou Xin said: "According to Huanglong’s judgment, this monk is not worth a single coin. Yet, if one looks closely, he is not without merit.
But tell me, where lies his merit? One sees only the vast expanse of waves, without realizing—"
Dongting is deep.

While Chan Master Daokuang of Quanzhou Zhaqing (a successor of Qingyuan Weixin and Changqing Huiheng) was engaged in communal labor carrying mud, he leaned on his staff midway along the path and asked a monk, "Mud for the upper cave?
Mud for the lower cave? The monk replied, "Mud for the upper cave. Daokuang struck him with a blow of his staff, then asked another monk.
The Master asked, "Is it the upper cave mud? Or the lower cave mud? He replied, "The lower cave mud. The Master struck him with a staff as well.

He then questioned Mingzhao, "Is it the upper cave mud? Or the lower cave mud? Mingzhao set down his mud-bag, stood with his hands clasped, and said, "I pray you, Master, examine this. The Master then desisted.
Jingshan Daokai said: "Although Zhaoqing had indeed set his mind at rest, how could Mingzhao bear it?
Had Yunmen seen him putting down his burden of mud and saying, 'I ask the Master to examine me,' he would have struck him across the spine with a blow—just see how he would have settled the matter!"
Tianning Qi said: "At Guoqing, the talent is noble; in a wealthy household, the children are arrogant.
Yufan Yu said: "Strike the upper cave, strike the lower cave; once you have laid down the burden of clay, simply rest."
This will not lead to a good outcome. Now tell me: is this a reward for him or a punishment? Since you cannot discern it, I shall give you a blow of the staff as well.
Chan Master Guangyun of Baoci in Fuzhou (a dharma successor of Qingyuan Weixin of Changqing) asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Wolong."
Cizhi asked, "How long have you been there? He replied, "I have passed through winter and summer. Cizhi said, "The Dragon Gate has no guests who stay overnight.
Why were you there for so long? He replied, "In a lion’s den, there are no other beasts. Cizhi said, "Try to let out a lion’s roar.
He replied, "If I were to let out a lion’s roar, there would be no more Master. Cizhi said, "I am mindful of your status as a newcomer."
"I grant you thirty blows.
Xuedou Xian said, "How extraordinary! All you practitioners of Chan, if one were to proceed with impartiality, neither side would be harmed;
yet according to the strict rule, both are in peril. Can you still discern this?"
Gunanmen said: "Let us set aside this monk for a moment. If he were to suddenly issue his command, how many blows of the staff would Baozi deserve?
Qinghua Yan said: "The host examines the guest; the guest is able to examine the host. This may be called both being masters of their craft.
Nevertheless, if it were here in my own place, I would simply apply the law to its full extent, regardless of whether there are any subjects left."
The *Renwang jiao* (Teaching for Benevolent Kings) says: "Though one host and one guest may be skilled practitioners, they cannot avoid being mutually stymied.
Nevertheless, at the end, Baoci said, "I grant you thirty blows, you newcomer! Now tell me, was this a reward or a punishment?
At that time, a monk stepped forward, and the Master struck him immediately.
The Layman Wang Yanbin (Qingqi Changqing Leng’s successor), Grand Tutor of Quanzhou, entered the Buddha Hall at Zhaoqing.
Pointing to a bowl, he asked the hall attendant, “What is this bowl? The attendant replied, “It is a Bhaisajyaguru bowl. The layman said, “I have only heard of the Dragon-subduing bowl.
The attendant said, “Wait until there is a dragon, and it will descend. The layman said, “What would you do when a dragon suddenly appears, seizing the clouds and leaping over the waves?”
"How is it? The Abbot said, "He did not even look back.
Yunmen Wenyan said to the Hall Master, "In a future life, when you are reborn in the heavens, do not let me down."
Xuansha Shibei addressed the Hall Master, saying: "Even if you exhaust all your supernatural powers, where could you go?
Baofu Zhan offered a different response, saying: "I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha."
Baizhang was constantly acting as the hall master and made the gesture of overturning a bowl.

Guishan Zhe said, "The hall master only knows how to look ahead and does not know how to look behind. Now that the Great Minister’s divine majesty has been displayed, the hall master’s almsbowl remains overturned.
At that time, if Daopei had seen him say, "Seizing the clouds and crashing through the waves," [he would have understood].
"How is it when [the Buddha] comes? Holding up his alms bowl, he said: "Exhaust all your supernatural powers;
even if the Eight Great Dragon Kings were to arrive, they would have no choice but to cower in awe and submit."
Baiyan Fu said: "If you suddenly encounter [a cloud] grasping the sky and [a wave] leaping over the billows, what then?
Pointing to the sky, he said: "I release you to go as rain into the clouds and mists. Then, pointing to his alms bowl, he said: "Do not forget that you come from within this."
At that time, the Abbot displayed such skillful maneuvers that it was certain the Grand Tutor would have to bow his knee.
When the Grand Tutor arrived at Zhaoqing for the tea service, Senior Monk Lang and Mingzhao were holding the teapot; suddenly, the teapot overturned.
The Duke then asked, "What is beneath the tea stove? Lang replied, "It is the Spirit Who Supports the Stove. The Duke said, "If it is the Spirit Who Supports the Stove, why has it overturned?
Lang replied, "After serving an official for a thousand days, one may lose his position in a single morning. The Duke brushed out his sleeves and departed.
Mingzhao remarked, "Dharma Seat Lang has finished eating the meal at Zhaoqing, yet he goes outside to gather wild roots."
Lang said, "How about you, Senior? Zhao said, "No one would have found an opportunity to take advantage of him.
Xuedou Xian said, "At that time, he should simply have kicked over the tea stove.
Weishan Zhe said, "Grand Councilor Wang was much like Zhuge Liang seizing the jade; his hair stood on end with rage. Mingzhao [said], "..."
This too was an occasion where one could not restrain a smile; it was a rare opportunity for a swift response.

If Daowei had been in the position of Layman Lang at that time, when asked, "Since you are the incense-bearer deity, why did you overturn the brazier? he would have simply laughed heartily. Why? Because...
If you see it and do not seize it, it will be difficult to pursue for a thousand years.
Yingshan Yun said, "Wang Taifu is like the star on the beam of a scale; he distinguishes every ounce and pound, weighing out all the monks of the world.
Yet, when examined closely, he was nevertheless defeated by Mingzhao of Zhaoqing. Furthermore—
"Where was he caught and defeated?
Baoshang said, "The Grand Tutor is much like one who challenges others to battle without success. If I were Master Lang, I would—"
When asked, "What is beneath the tea stove? he immediately let out a thunderous shout, ensuring that the worldly fellow’s mind was pacified and his will subdued.
He further remarked, "Mingzhao is like a neighbor from the east mourning for a deceased person from the west."
The *Zifu lu* (Record of Zifu) provides a different version:

Master Jingzhong Guixin of Yizhou, a successor of Qingfeng Chu (the seventh generation of the Qing lineage), was asked by a monk: "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?
Jing said, "The blossoms fill the pool. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has emerged? Jing said, "The leaves fall and are no longer known."
Autumn. Tiantong Jue said: "Li Ling held the Han flag; Pan Lang rode his donkey backward. Niuan Jing said:
"If Jingzhong answers the question in this way, he cannot avoid provoking intellectual interpretations. As for this mountain monk..."
The inner truth is not so. When the lotus has not yet emerged from the water, what is it? [It is] the Dragon Master and the Fire Sovereign. After it has emerged from the water, what is it?
[It is] the Bird Official and the Human Sovereign.

Chan Master Mingzhao Deqian of Wuzhou (successor of Xiansi of Qingshan) asked Guotai: "The ancients said that although Jushi only recited three lines of incantation, he was thus able to surpass all others in fame.
How would you remove those three lines of incantation for him, so that he might likewise be named as surpassing all others?
Guotai held up one finger. Mingzhao said, "Had it not been for this very day, how could I have known?"
"Those who recognize him are the travelers from Guazhou.
Letan Qing said: "Mingzhao only recognized the traveler from Guazhou; he did not recognize Guo Tai.
Even if one were to recognize him, one has still not seen the old man Jueyi in a dream."
When Mingzhao was unwell, National Teacher Taishen came to inquire after his illness. As soon as he entered, Mingzhao said, "Ai-ai! Ai-ai! Uncle Taishen, save this old monk!
Taishen replied, "What is there for the Master to save? Mingzhao raised his head, looked at him once, and said, "Ei!
Those eyes are dark and piercing; you are still that same old Upāsaka Taishen. Thus it is said.
He turned his body and faced the wall; they never saw each other again.
Jingshan Yin said: "If Mingzhao had not turned his body and faced the wall, what face would he have to show Guotai?"
"If one cannot even cope with a single illness, how much less can one navigate the cycle of birth and death?
Fuyan Yuan said this while loudly calling for his attendant to bring some hot water. He then added, "How bitter!
How unjust!"
While Mingzhao was huddling by the brazier, a monk asked: "There is no dharma before the eyes; the intent lies before the eyes.
It is not a dharma of the present moment, nor is it something reached by the ears or eyes. Which phrase is the guest? Which phrase is the host?

Mingzhao pointed to the fire and said, "Can you extract a single strand of eyebrow-hair from within this for me? The monk replied, "Not only I, but all people throughout the great earth [cannot do so]."
He lost his body and forfeited his life. Mingzhao called out, "For what reason did you yourself take your topknot to the yamen?
Jingshan Daoyuan said, "This monk has a head but no tail; Mingzhao has a tail but no head.
If anyone can utter a phrase where both head and tail are complete, Yunmen will give him a staff."
Tianning Qi said: "He does not understand how to bring forth the eyebrows from within the fire;
he does not know which of the four lines is the guest and which is the host. Miaoxi says that this monk has a head but no tail, while Mingzhao has a tail but no head.
Even if one could speak the sentence where Miaoxi’s head and tail are perfectly complete, Tianning’s staff—"
"You have not yet let him go," said Yungan Meng.
"He has not encountered a village ahead and has not reached an inn behind; fortunately, he still retains this fire-pan."
Lingyan said: "That monk thrust his head out from within a thicket of brambles; Mingzhao reached down with his hand amidst a blaze of flames.
Although their granting and withholding were adapted to the moment, if one examines them closely, neither of them reached a final resolution.
At that time, had Lingyan seen that monk ask such a question, he would have given him a shout right between the eyes, not only to..."
Thus, the Sangha immediately transforms a thorn forest into a place of jewels, and it also adds several degrees of brilliance to the lacquer buckets passed down from above.
When Mingzhao arrived at Zhaoqing, there was the Elder Du who asked Luoshan, "You usually say that everywhere else is all just flour-dust."
"Rice. Only Luoshan serves white rice. The Elder came from Luoshan, so he extended his hand and said, 'I ask for a little white rice.
[Luoshan] struck him twice with his palm. Deyu said, 'I thought it was white rice; it turns out it is only powdered rice.'"
