Zhao said, "This fool cannot be beaten to death with a staff. That evening, when Fadu was discussing this with several Zen practitioners, Zhao approached and said, "I hope you are well.
Fadu replied, "Today, I shall give this very monk two slaps. At that moment, the monk Taoyao said:
"Do not use the lower palm. Regarding this 'inner allowance,' how would you speak? Zhao said, "Regarding this 'inner allowance,' speak, speak!
Daoyao had no reply. Zhao said, "All of you, I shall bind you together as one bundle and hang you upside down beneath the urinal."
"See you tomorrow; take care.
Tiantong Jie said, "I have always told people: 'All day long, one is in the midst of vast, surging waves, yet when scooping up water to splash others, not a single drop wets the body.
This was because Mingzhao had stepped upon that very 'something' himself."
Yet he deploys it from a state of leisurely ease; what a pity that his锋头 (fēngtóu, the "tip of the blade") lacks sharpness, thereby inviting so much entanglement.

If Huazang had seen him say, "I thought this was white rice, but it turns out to be only parched flour," he would have struck him twice across the cheeks with his palm, leaving this fellow in doubt for thirty years.
Mingzhao ascended the hall. As soon as the assembly had gathered, he said, "The wind at the peak is somewhat stiff; this is not where you should establish your body or settle your life.
Return for now to a warm room to deliberate. He then returned to his quarters. The assembly followed him to the quarters, where Mingzhao said:
As soon as they reached the warm room, they were seen to be dozing; [the Master] struck them all at once with his staff and dispersed them.
Jianfu Can said, "The wind on the mountain peak is somewhat harsh; let us return to the warm room to deliberate. There is bait on the hook.
The assembly followed him to the Abbot’s quarters. Huanglian said, "Chewing the root of *hellebore* is not yet bitter; it is only when one reaches the warm room that..."
He then dozed off, so [Mingzhao] struck them all at once with his staff, scattering them. "A pity that gold is treated like dung and soil," he said.
He continued, "Mingzhao’s vanguard has taken action, but the rearguard is missing; it is a pity there was no one in the assembly who could have said at that time:
'The wind here is rather stiff, let us return to a warm room to deliberate. Had they been able to say this, they would have been dismissed all at once."
"Go! The old man who teaches wishes to return to his quarters; you may not yet stay.
Chan Master Huanglong Huiji (Qing, seventh generation; successor of Xuanquan Yanshi) of Ezhou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of Chan?
Jie replied, "Its meaning lies in slander."
Xuedou said: "To say that the Buddhas of the three periods are slanderous; that the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven are slanderous;
that the six generations of patriarchs in the land of Tang are slanderous; that the old monks of the world are slanderous; that the masters of the various mountains are slanderous;
and that this mountain monk is slanderous—among these, is there anyone who is not slanderous? There are sands of Ganges in number who discuss the profound and expound the wondrous."
"How can it compare to the Double Peak [Monastery] slandering its own Master?
Tianning Qi said: "If someone were to ask Nanhu, 'What is the meaning of Chan? I would tell him, 'Its meaning is praise. Now tell me:
is it the slander that is true, or is it the praise? If you see with your eyes, you are blind; if you hear with your ears, you are deaf."
To speak with the mouth would leave one mute; to ponder with the mind would lead to exhaustion. Snow buries stones a thousand fathoms deep at the edge of heaven;
frost breaks several pines at the cave entrance.
Chan Master Liao Zong of Zhishan on Mount Gu at Fuzhou (the seventh generation descendant of Mount Gu Yan): Initially traveling abroad, he arrived at Huang... in Ezhou.
Long asked, "I have long heard of Huanglong; yet upon arriving, I see only a striped red snake.
Huanglong said, "You see only a striped red snake, but you do not recognize Huanglong. Shanshan asked, "What is Huanglong? Huanglong said, "Flowing and surging.
Shanshan asked, "If a garuḍa were to suddenly appear, what then? Huanglong said, "One's life would be difficult to preserve. Shanshan...
[Daowei] said, "If that is so, then he has swallowed you up. Long said, "Thank you for your offering, Dharma brother. Shan then prostrated himself.
Yingshan Yun said, "Today I have run into a swordsman looking to buy; I have sold him one for thirty coins."
Baiyan Fu said: "Huanglong’s manner of acting was on par [with his predecessors], and his bestowing and withholding were appropriate;
he did not fail as the legitimate grandson of Yantou. Yet, in a moment of unawareness, he was swallowed whole by Gushan.
Is there anyone who can discern this?"
Chan Master Dazhong Zhihong Hongji of Dingzhou (Seventh Generation of Qingyuan; succeeded Yuan of Baizhao). A monk asked: "The physical body decays;
what is the indestructible Dharma-body? Long said: "Mountain flowers bloom like brocade; stream water is as deep blue as indigo."
Jingshan Hongzhi said, "If one uses this to clarify the adamantine Dharma-body, then the physical body enters hell.
Yufan Yuanmeng said, "Let me ask: has Dalong ever dreamed of the adamantine Dharma-body?"
Guangjiao [Yuan] brandished his whisk and said: "Do you understand? Yesterday was the thirtieth; this morning is the first.
Do you know whether the unfolding of the ritual accords with the occasion? The rustic elder loves the leisurely smoke among the trees; infinite hammer-blows cannot split it open.
From antiquity to now, they have vainly shot at the halberds of the gate. Whether you intend to grasp it or not, it stands firm like a mountain in the dead of night."
Passing through the sturdy barrier, his loyal words did not shy away from weeping before the wind.
Chan Master Wenqin of Baoci Monastery in Fuzhou (disciple of Baofo Zhuan; lineage Qijingbao): A monk asked, "What is the wondrously enlightened, luminous mind?
Wenqin said, "This year’s winter rice will be excellent; it was produced by the autumn rains."
Yingshan Yun said: "To know the time and recognize the occasion, one must be Baozi; yet as for the wondrously enlightened luminous mind, one has not even dreamed of it.
But ultimately, what is this wondrously enlightened luminous mind? He gave a shout.
Chan Master Guichen of Dizang at Zhangzhou (the seventh-generation descendant of Xuan Sha Bei) asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From Nanzhou. Dizang asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma there? The monk said, "It is full of endless debate and discussion.
Dizang said, "How can that compare to us here, where we till the fields and eat our fill? The monk asked, "What then of the three realms? Dizang said, "What do you call 'the three realms'?"
Taisuī Zhe said: "In purity there is long-lasting happiness; in turbidity there is much anxiety.
Baōn Shòu remarked: "How could it be like this? Here we till the fields to earn our food. He added:
"At that moment, one should have simply said: 'If so, then it is not only the Southern Province.'"
Boshan Lai said: "This monk is tethered to the three realms and brings misfortune upon the Chan practitioners of the South by failing to eliminate his worldly airs.
Is there anyone here now who can truly meet Dizang? You must first cast away your plow, rake, and hoe before you may succeed."
Daciyanyun said: "The Great and Small Kṣitigarbhas both spoke of 'plowing fields to earn one's rice. This is enough to leave people in doubt.
To speak of the beginningless and endless, yet then say, 'What do you call the three realms?'—this is like having the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake."
The *Renwang jiao* says: "The family style of Kṣitigarbha is without shame before the ancient Buddhas; truly, such a person is encountered but once in a thousand years.
Yet, when pressed by this monk with a single blow, he was reduced to a state of total disintegration.
Dizang asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Qinzhou. Dizang said, "What have you brought with you?
The monk replied, "I have brought nothing. Dizang said, "Why do you lie before the assembly? The monk was speechless.
Dizang then asked, "Is it not true that Qinzhou produces parrots? The monk replied, "Parrots are produced in Longxi. Dizang said, "That is not so either."
[The Master said: "Quite a few.
Guishan Zhe said: "This monk came directly from Qinzhou; why does he say he is speaking falsehoods before the assembly?
Do you wish to understand? As a guest, he was not diligent, and he brings disgrace upon his host by dragging through mud and wading through water."
Chan Master Huigqiu of Anguo Temple in Fuzhou (the seventh-generation descendant of Xuefeng Yicun and successor to Xiansha Shibei) ascended the hall and said:

"The circumstances of our daily meals here, which I have used for the sake of you, my brothers, to proclaim the Dharma, are ultimately not permanent. If you wish to attain the essential point, it is rather the mountains, rivers, and the great earth that reveal it to you.
Since that Way is eternal, it can also lead to ultimate realization. For those who enter through the gate of Mañjuśrī, all things—"
Inanimate things—earth, wood, tiles, and rubble—assist you in triggering the mechanism.

If you enter through the Gate of Avalokiteśvara, all sounds and noises—even those of crickets, frogs, and earthworms—will assist you in triggering the mechanism. If you enter through the Gate of Samantabhadra, you arrive without taking a single step.
These three gates are shown to you as skillful means, like using a single broken chopstick to stir the waters of the great ocean. Let it be so.

Those fish and dragons know that water is their life; do you understand? If one lacks the eye of wisdom to examine this with discernment, then no matter how many hundreds of skillful means you employ, they will not lead to the ultimate realization.
Langye Jue said, "Though it be a good cause, it brings about an evil result.
Jianfu Xing said, "If one were to examine this according to my own assessment, even An-guo’s own life and soul would not yet know where they have fallen.
Here, even a single broken chopstick would not suffice. Is there anyone who can snatch food from the jaws of a tiger?"
"Or so it is. If there were none, this mountain monk would not hesitate to apply another cauterization upon a healed scar.
[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Dongchan Guan said: "An-guo has at once fed an infant with his own chewed rice; one does not know that those looking on will feel revulsion."
Chan Master Qieru of Dazhang Mountain in Fuzhou (a dharma successor of Xuefeng Yicun and Qingyuan Xingsi). A monk asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them?
Qieru said, "The edict arrives; it must be executed. The monk said, "In that case, one will be taken away by birth and death. Qieru said, "A-ye, a-ye."
Yingshan Yun said: "This old fellow acts so recklessly that even the Lord of Yama must fold his hands in submission.
Nevertheless, you must still put him to the test before you can truly understand."
*Compendium of Anecdotes from the Chan School*,
Volume Thirty-Eight and Volume Thirty-Nine.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Successor of the Patriarchs at Baiyan in Ancient Hangzhou.
△ Master Shengnian of Mount Shou in Nanyue (a successor of Fengxue Zhaoyan) addressed the assembly. Holding up a bamboo staff, he said: "To call it a 'bamboo staff' is to offend;
not to call it a 'bamboo staff' is to turn one's back. You all—what do you call it? At that time, [Master] Ye...
The County Governor was present in the assembly hall. He stepped forward, seized [the staff], and threw it onto the steps before asking, "What is this?
Shanshan replied, "Blind. At these words, the Governor attained great enlightenment.
Guanghui Lian said: "The donkey-man’s awakening is indeed a most thorough awakening; yet, it still does not exhaust the meaning of the former master.
Tianning Qi said: "If Guanghui speaks thus, does the former master truly have a specific meaning? Take this handful..."
Fire illuminates how thick one's skin is. Not running down the slope—such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter.
If you would uphold the teaching that points upward, you must first return my bamboo whisk, elder brother.
Yunju Zhuang said: "To possess a wind-and-flow elegance throughout one's entire being, one must be Shoushan; to confront and resist the adversary when the occasion arises, one must be Yexian.
To proceed exclusively in this manner would cause the Buddha-dharma of Linji to be swept away and utterly destroyed."
Ou-feng Chengyun said, "In the armory of our King, there is no such blade.
Ming-zhao Bu added, "If I had been there at that time, I would have waited for him to say, 'What do you all call this?
and then simply let out two sighs; I guarantee that this fellow from Shou-shan would have crumbled like ice melting away."
Shoushan was once asked by Fengyang, "What is the meaning of Baizhang rolling up his mat? Shoushan said, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the body is fully revealed.
Fengyang asked, "What is your own meaning, Master? Shoushan said, "Where the Elephant King walks, there is no trace of the fox. At these words, Fengyang attained great enlightenment.
Rising from his prostrations, he said, "The moon in the empty expanse of the ten-thousand-year-old green pool—only after repeated stirring and searching does it finally respond."
Baoning Miao said, "The Great and the Small Shoushan [both] have dragon heads and snake tails. Someone might say, "The true does not conceal the false;
the crooked does not hide the straight. He struck the meditation seat and said, "Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on this long ago, continuing right up until now."
Now, this was not considered "wondrous.
Thereupon, when a monk asked Shoushan, "What is the Buddha? Shan said, "The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it.
The monk asked, "In what phrase is this contained? Shan said, "The Three Mysteries cannot contain it; how could the Four Phrases encompass it? The monk said, "This..."
"What do you think? Shanshan said, "Heaven is long-lasting and earth is enduring; the sun and moon shine together.
Later, Nian of Shoushan was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of 'The new bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it'?
Shanshan said, "A hundred-year-old grandfather has lost his father. The monk asked, "How can a hundred-year-old grandfather have a father? Shanshan said: [The text ends here.]
"You understand. He also said, "This is solitary sitting where there is neither high nor low; from the beginning, not a single dharma has been given to anyone.
Yungan Yu said, "Profound and deep silence; the lacquer chicken's head is large; the general removes the fleas."
Guangxiang said: "To answer a question in such a manner may indeed be swift and effective for responding to circumstances and engaging with others;
yet, when scrutinized, it cannot avoid being laughed at by onlookers."
A monk once asked Shoushan, "What is the Buddha? Shoushan replied, "The bamboo-stem whip beneath the Zhangling Mountains.
Daofeng Qing said, "Shoushan was like one who controls a thousand-li horse and looses a 'piercing the willow' arrow; there is nothing it does not hit.
Yet, alas, he encountered this particular monk, which caused him to labor in vain. Had anyone else asked Daofeng, it would have been as follows:"
"What is this Buddha? He replied, "Where does this question come from? Tell me, is this [question] the same as or different from that of Shoushan?
Chan Master Zhen of Guanghui in Ruizhou (a successor of Nanʼan Fengxue Zhao) was asked by Fengxue: "At the time of the Huichang persecution of Buddhism, where did the Dharma-protecting spirits go?
Zhen said, "They are always in the midst of the marketplace; yet, no one sees them. Fengxue...
[The Master] said, "You have attained thorough penetration.
Jingshan Daokai said, "Tell me, has Fengxue himself also attained thorough penetration? △ Qingba.
Chan Master Yuan Guan of Liangshan in Dingzhou (a successor of Tong’an Zhi of Qingyuan) addressed the assembly: "To those who come from the south, I give thirty blows;
to those who come from the north, I give thirty blows."
Langya Huijue said: "Liangshan has a great piece of pure gold, yet he sells it as if it were common iron. Langya is not like this:
to those who come from the south, I give thirty blows; to those who come from the north, I give thirty blows."
"Following this, he instructs all people under heaven to denounce and strip away [the truth].
Tiantong Muan said: "Although Langya does not sell gold for iron, how can one blame him for not stating the price and demanding that others pay the money?
Guangrun, however, was not like this: to those coming from the south, he gave them thirty blows; to those from the north... [he gave them thirty blows].
"To those who come, I give thirty blows. At the tip of the staff there is an eye as bright as the sun; if you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire.
After Master Foyue Zhi finished citing the words of Langya, he said: "The two elders may be said to have been too over-anxious in their compassion; they only knew..."
Entering the water, entering the mud—disregarding the laughter of onlookers. Long’an was not like this: let those coming from the south come from the south;
let those coming from the north come from the north. "Thirty blows of the staff—do not dare to touch them. Why is this?
Gold has its own price; why must it be mixed with sand before being sold to others?
Baiyan Fu said: "Langya was cutting in line and snatching the market; his awl was indeed that sharp. Guorong intended to go one step further:
"His chisel was indeed that square. If you wish to see Liangshan, you are still three thousand li away.
Liangshan ascended the hall. Zhen, the head gardener, came forward and asked, "When it is said that 'the domestic thief is difficult to guard against,' what does this mean?
Liangshan said, "If you recognize him, he cannot be an enemy. Zhen asked, "After recognizing him, what then? Liangshan said, "Exile him to the realm of non-birth.
Zhen asked, "Is this not where one establishes one's own dwelling and sustenance? Liangshan said, "Dead water does not harbor dragons. Zhen asked, "What is living water?"
Longshan said, "The mountain rises waves but does not create billows. [A monk] asked, "What if one suddenly encounters a time when the torrential pools overflow and the mountains topple?
Longshan descended from his seat, seized him, and said, "Reverend, do not let it get the corner of this old monk's cassock wet."
Huanglong Qing said: "The old man of Liangshan thoroughly understood the pivotal points of the teaching and could truly be called a master.
Yet, alas, he took advantage of the occasion to open the door, leading people through a series of complications right into the hands of the thief.

Huanglong would not do it this way. As soon as he saw the question, 'How is it when the house-thief is difficult to guard against? he would have cut it off with one stroke, ensuring that they could never again harbor a glancing look [at the truth]. Nevertheless..."
It is so. Suppose suddenly a patch-robed monk comes forth and points at this mountain monk, saying, "Thief! Thief!
What then? Let those with eyes discern it.
Tiantong Hua said: "Master Liangshan only knows how to fight the thief; he does not know how to kill the thief.
If someone were to ask me, 'How is it when the household thief is difficult to guard against? I would strike them across the back.
Why? Have you not heard it said: 'Unify them with ritual'?"
Yunmen said, "Yuantou has long kept this essential point in silence; he truly possesses the strategic skill to decide victory a thousand *li* away from within his tent.
Had it not been for the great difficulty of resisting the formidable challenge at Liangshan, although he was ultimately struck by an arrow in the end."
How joyful it is to return home having cast off the armor! Is there anyone who can save us? If you ask Yunmen, "What is it like when suddenly the mountain torrents overflow and the peaks collapse?
simply tell him: "Take care of your tail. Now let us see how the head gardener will settle this matter.
Qixia Chengyun said: "To capture a bandit, one must capture the king. Why did Liangshan let him go instead of capturing him?
It was because he wished to test whether the bandit’s skillful means were truly fit for kingship. Ying’an said: "He only knows how to fight bandits;
he does not know how to kill them. Alas! Killing is no more difficult than fighting; it is simply that he has not yet broken his bow or exhausted his arrows.
If they all willingly surrender, then the rebels can be transformed into peaceful subjects. To regulate them with ritual, one must first lead them with virtue.
Longhua says: "The Old Man of Liangshan was picking up a scorched-tail [pheasant] in the level fields and shallow grass."
"Insects! This is truly a matter of life and death. Had he not been deeply versed in the methods for subduing tigers, he would have nearly met with their venomous fangs.
He then called out in a loud voice, "Great assembly! There is one here as well; guard yourselves well! Do you see him?
Thereupon, he suddenly seized his staff, descended from the seat, and struck everyone down at once, dispersing them.

Fengshan began by saying: "The harmony between the Correct and the Deviant is like the jade thread and golden needle. This monk is like Cook Ding, whose skillful handling of the blade leaves him with ample margin;
he is like Liangshan, who, like a master carver from Ying, wields his axe so that not even a hair’s breadth is damaged.
Ying’an said, "He only knows how to fight the bandit, but does not know how to kill the bandit. Little did he realize that it was Yao who governed the world simply by wearing his robes.
Shun also [said this].
Hequan of the River Marsh said: "Mount Liangshan was originally a coward; he could only recognize thieves and condemn thieves, but he could not employ them.
If it were I, a monk, when asked, 'How is it when one says that a household thief is difficult to guard against? I would simply say: 'Use him.'"
"How so? It is not that in the Way there are no minor tasks by which one cannot become a gentleman.
Baiyan Fu said: "Master Zhen’s pushing and prodding show he has the boldness to pull a tiger’s whiskers;
were it not for the old man of Liangshan’s broad and high walls, it would have been difficult to contain him. Nevertheless, here it is not so.
"So it is. [The Master] waited for [the monk] to ask, "What if one suddenly encounters a time when the torrents of rain overturn the mountains?
He then struck him across the spine and said, "You beast! Let me see where you can run!"
Baoguang Yuan said: "The old man of Liangshan was also one who failed to cut off what should have been cut off, thereby inviting further chaos.
According to Baoguang’s own view, when someone asks, 'How is it when a domestic thief is difficult to guard against? he would immediately strike them with thirty heavy blows and drive them out.
Why? Have you not heard it said: 'He who comes to speak of right and wrong is himself a person of right and wrong'?"
Liangshan asked Taizang Xuan about the "formless site of enlightenment" (*amūrti-mārga-kṣetra*).

Pointing to an image of Avalokiteśvara, Liangshan said, "This was painted by the Layman Wu. Just as Xuan was about to offer a response, Liangshan hurriedly interrupted him, saying, "This one has form.
What is the formless one? At these words, Xuan attained sudden awakening. He then prostrated himself, rose, and followed [the Master].
As he stood there, the Master said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? Xuan replied, "I would not decline to speak, but I fear it would take up paper and brush.
He then sent word to his kinsmen’s boat, saying: "It is very much like thunder and lightning escorting one another; soaring to the heavens and crossing the Milky Way occurs in but a moment. Heh!"
Qinghuazhen said: "The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horn because it gazes at the moon; the elephant receives flowers in its tusks because it is startled by thunder. Qixiacheng said:
"Liangshan may indeed possess the mechanism of rushing through flowing water and crossing blades; he has the hand that captures the living and seizes the alive.
Tāiyáng is like a fragrant elephant crossing a river, cutting through the current as he goes; yet suddenly looking back, he is brought directly to a standstill."
"Fallen blossoms cover the ground, red as brocade; the hundred rivers and four torrents are all fragrant.
Wulongcen said, "To embroider mandarin ducks upon brocade with jade thread and golden needle requires none other than Liangshan.

When the Lord of Spring issues his decree, one beholds the handiwork of spring in a single branch; this belongs to the Master Xuanshi. Although they were both outstanding figures of their time," [the former] was surpassed by the latter.
Before he had even moved his lips, Zen Master Fayan Wenyi of Qingliang in Jinling (d.u.;
successor to Dizang Chen of Mount Qing)—who was the eighth generation—asked the Mountain Master Xiu, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.
How do you understand this? Xiu replied, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth."
Yan said, "Even so, how could it be sufficient? Xiu asked, "How about you, Master? Yan said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth, and heaven and earth are as far apart. Xiu then bowed in prostration.
Dongchan Qizheng said: "The abbot answered in such a manner; why was he not accepted?
Yet when he sought further instruction from Fayan, he still spoke in exactly that same way. Tell me, where does the error lie?
If you can see through this point, I grant that you possess the 'one eye'."
When the Fifth Patriarch Jie was about to transmit the Dharma-eye, he struck Fayen across the back.
Baoning Yong said, "At that time, why did not Master Xiu also say to Fayen:
'Even if you understand it in this way, how can you attain it? Bairyak Pu said, "The great Baoning missed the mark regarding Master Xiu."
To know this and then prostrate is also extremely convoluted.
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Fayan and Master Xiu went back and forth like drawing silk and weaving thread;

they maintained the tradition of Dizang’s school with such continuity and density that it truly makes one's whole body bristle with joy. But as for those under Jingshan’s gate, they must buy it anew."
Only by traveling on straw sandals can one truly attain it. Why? Because a difference of even a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.
From where does this news come? Tianning Qi said:
"Those two old fellows did not understand the 'turning-around' phrase. Furthermore, if someone were to ask Tianning today: "A hair's breadth..."
"A difference of a hair's breadth separates heaven and earth—how do you understand this? He said to him: "Yesterday someone asked this very question;
thirty blows of the staff will send them out of the monastery."
Baoneng Xiu said: "At that time, Wansong saw that Fayan said, 'Even so, how could it be attained?
[Wansong] replied, 'I have long heard that the Master possesses such a vital pivot. Otherwise, he would have simply waved his hand and departed, surely cutting everything off at once."
Boshanlai said: "Fayan drew people into a state beyond doubt; tell me, how many magical arts does he possess?
When a king speaks, his words are like silk threads, yet what issues from them is like a thick rope."
In the *Xuanshu*, Qian Daixiu comments: "The Master originally had another point of excellence.
Fayan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from Sizhou to pay homage to the Great Sage.
Fayan said, "Did the Great Sage take his stupa out this year? The monk replied, "He did. Fayan then turned to a monk standing nearby and asked, "Tell me, did he reach Sizhou or not?"
Regarding Sizhou, Fushan Yuan said: "This monk did indeed arrive at Sizhou, yet he simply did not see the Great Sage.
Daochang Quan said: "This monk did indeed see the Great Sage, yet he simply never recognized Fayen."
Dongchan Guan said: "This monk has arrived; he has reached Sizhou. He has seen him; he has seen the Great Sage. He has recognized him; he has recognized Fayen.
It is simply that he seeks his own head and cannot see it."
Baoneng Xiu said, "This lot of fellows have their illness deep-seated, beyond remedy; they only look at how that monk was not seen.

Who would have known that it was actually they themselves who did not recognize him? If someone were to come forward and say, 'Master, you are merely helping the weak and not the strong,' Baoneng would strike him on the spot as he spoke. Now tell me: did he accept him, or did he reject him?"
Fayan was once asked by a monk, "Who can penetrate the two characters 'sound' and 'form'? Fayan then said to the assembly, "Venerable elders, tell me:
has this monk penetrated them yet? If you understand where this monk’s question lies, penetrating sound and form will not be difficult."

Tiantong Jue said: "Failing to understand from the outset is simply because the 'house-thief' is difficult to guard against. To be clearly enlightened right now, for the time being, take up residence in a grass hut.
Gaofeng Miao said: "Openly repairing the plank road while secretly crossing at Chen-cang Pass."
Yuanwu Keqin said: "On level ground there are countless dead people.
Fayen pointed to a chair and said: "If you recognize this chair, you will have more than enough room all around."
Yunmen Wenyan said, "If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different.
Xuedou Xian said, "A vast marsh conceals mountains; this principle can subdue even a leopard.
Jianfu Hui said, "Recognizing the bench as being made of nanmu wood."
Yuantong Xiu said, "Recognize the bench; its four legs rest firmly on the ground.
Letan Qing, having finished citing the words of Fayen, Yunmen, and Xuedou, said, "These three fellows all rely on external interpretations;
they possess two divergent paths—clarity and obscurity—and have not escaped the realm of seeing and hearing. They are like the moon reflected in water. Huanglong, however, did not...
"Indeed. It fills the space beyond heaven and earth and unfolds before the sun and moon.
Jingshan Daowu Gao said, "If you recognize the bench, it is easy to shave your head and wash your feet. Although this is so, there are many who misunderstand it.
The *Longchi chuan* says: "If you recognize the bench, study for another thirty years; upon returning, cease saying it is still just the bench.
Yunmen Cheng said: "Recognizing the bench—there is still something more to it."
Chinghua Yen said: "If you recognize the bench, do not allow yourself to sit upon it; to sit is a calamity.
Zifu Lu said: "If you recognize the bench, both eyes will be as if blind."
Lingxi Yu said: "Fayan knows how to let go but does not know how to gather in; Yunmen knows how to gather in but does not know how to let go.
Tianyi meets with a fall on level ground—all of these are merely leaning upon grass and clinging to wood. How can they compare to pulling one's staff and watching the clouds arise?"
"Idly listening to two or three notes of the oriole.
Fayan asked the senior monk Jue, "Did you come by boat or on land? Jue replied, "By boat. Fayan asked, "Where is the boat?
Jue said, "The boat is in the river. Jue withdrew. Fayan then asked a monk standing nearby, "What do you say of that monk just now?"
"Those with eyes and those without eyes.
Boshan Lai said: "The void has no colors; the great ocean has waves.
Baoneng Xiu, acting on behalf of a monk from the side, said: "A thief passes by, and they count the soldiers."
Yishan Nu said: "The thread comes and the line goes, without revealing a single sharp edge.

Were it not for a state where one's insight is brilliant and clear and one's application is sovereign and free, how could such a thing be possible? Nevertheless, if you interpret this as being about the Buddha-dharma, you will bring disgrace upon those two elders, making them worth not even half a cent."
Huìyún said: "The Elder Jué treads firmly on all four corners of the ground; therefore, Fǎyǎn withdrew from his own position to yield it to another.
If a monk by my side were truly a man of substance, I would say to him: 'In Tanzhou, paper is expensive; one statement shall suffice to settle the matter.'"
Baiyan Fu said: "To meet him in such a manner may be called 'the Great Broth and Dark Wine'—a total clearing away of all the leftovers from ancient and modern times across the various quarters.
It is indeed extraordinary within the extraordinary; yet, to pointlessly expose one's own foul-smelling urine to a bystander monk is bound to make people feel nauseated."
Xue Yun said: "If one takes Fa-yen’s question and Jue Zhashang’s answer as being about the Buddha-dharma, one will enter hell as fast as a shooting arrow."
While Fa-yen was receiving monks in audience, he pointed his finger at the curtain. Immediately, two monks went to roll it up simultaneously.
Fa-yen said, "One gains, one loses.
Huanglong Qing said, "Fa-yen held the Mo-he sword in his hand; killing or giving life was left to the occasion. When the two monks went to roll up the curtain together—"
The Curtain. Now tell me, who gains and who loses? Do you understand? "Matters of the world should be judged with impartiality;
the human heart is difficult to align with the full moon."
Nanjian asked: "Fayan sticks his head out; the two monks chase after the clod of earth. Even if one’s withdrawal is swift and nimble, one cannot avoid falling flat on one's face on level ground.
Bai Zhang Le said: "Opened wide like the eight characters: brows arched and nose straight. No sinews in the eyes—one remains poor for a lifetime."
"Throughout ten thousand ages, we can only recall it in vain. Fayen said, 'Yi gains one and loses one. Is there anyone who can discern this?
[He] strikes the meditation staff and says: 'This mountain monk’s mouth is too narrow.'"
The Zifu companion said: "In the Hall of the Tiger’s Roar, it is not like that either. Suppose two monks roll up the curtain at the same time;
simply tell them: 'A pair of iron hammers with no holes. Now tell me, would you reward them or punish them?
If you go to other places, do not misquote this."
Caoxi Zhu said, "The old fellow Qingliang possessed great spiritual acuity upon the tip of his finger. Those two monks were ill-equipped to evade it;
they could not help but lose their lives. Had he been a true man, when the curtain was pointed out, he would have immediately overturned the meditation seat."
Fayan was once asked by a monk: "I have heard it said in the teachings that 'from the root of non-abiding, all dharmas are established.
What is this root of non-abiding? Fayan replied: "Form arises before there is substance; names arise before there is naming."
Boshan Lai said: "Before form had arisen and before names had emerged, tell me, from where did the myriad phenomena come?
If you let this point pass, it will not do. He gave a shout.
Fayan ascended the hall. When the three rounds of drums had ceased, the assembly crowded forward; matters of both the Buddha-dharma and human affairs were settled all at once.
Master Huizun said, "When the three rounds of drums have ceased and the assembly has crowded forward, the staff is not here;
I shall give you thirty blows with the handle of a broomstick."
Tiantong Muan said: "Fayan used the hook; Huiwen used the awl. This mountain monk neither hooks you nor pricks you;
let me set you free for a while so that you may look upon it with clarity. He then said: "When the three beats of the drum have ceased, they all come crowding forward."
The subsequent text is extensive; it shall be entrusted for another day.
Fayen asked Yongming Qian, saying: "In the Vinaya it is said that if one hears the sound of hairpins and bracelets from across a wall, it is called breaking the precepts."
Presently, one observes gold and silver mingled together and crimson and purple robes crowded side by side. "Is this breaking the precepts? or "Is this not breaking the precepts?
On the next day, [the Master] said, "What a fine entrance! Yuanian said, "In the future, you will have five hundred disciples who will be held in high esteem by kings and lords."
Tianning Qi said: "Truly, one who can enter this is like adding flowers upon brocade; if one cannot enter it, it is like having grit in one's eyes.
Guangxiang De said: "Fayan wished to pluck a single eyebrow from within a blazing fire, yet he could not do so."
He attained it; yet Yongming was truly skilled at "striking the nest," and thus he is well worthy of praise. However, he only understood how to look ahead and could not look behind.
Zifu Guang said: "When Master Shiyu resided at Yunmen, he would frequently bring up this koan to question people, but [no one]..."
There was one who struck the essential point; when Guang arrived later, he too was questioned about this.
Guang replied, "This is merely the functional activity (*yòngzuò*) of an ancient. Yuyu held it up to show the assembly, who praised it greatly.
The following year, [Yuyu] again raised this story and asked Guang, "Last year you said this was 'functional activity. Tell me, what kind of functional activity is it? Guang said, "Great..."
"It is like riding a bandit’s horse to kill the bandit; once it rains, one simply stops and does not utter another word. "Great assembly, tell me:
do these two phrases of mine have merit or lack merit? Master Yu praised them and then stopped; was this a good intention or not?
If you can see into this, only then will you possess the eye of study."
Regarding the question asked by a monk: "What is a single drop of water from the Cao source? Fayan said, "It is a single drop of water from the Cao source.
Tiantong Jie said: "Master Fayan brandishes his banner on the field of a hundred battles; he cannot avoid being a bystander."
The onlookers laughed. Suddenly, someone asked Lingyin, "What is a single drop of water from the Cao River source?
He replied to him, "It is excrement mixed with urine.
Later, when the monk Huichao asked Fayan, "What is the Buddha? Fayan said, "You are Huichao."
Jin-su Yuan said: "Fayan’s response was such that it could be called 'treating an illness without needing a donkey-load of medicine;
if one can play, what use is a jade-stringed lute? That monk’s realization was indeed admirable, yet when examined closely..."
There is still more to it. Tell me, what is this matter? *Duh!* Xuan Sha’s "bottom" [his ultimate statement]. Guangyin Biao said:
"Melting snow in a red furnace—this belongs to the true artist. This monk was muddled and confused;
he carried around a noseless ancient Buddha and wanted Fayan to give him the final touch of the eyes. Fayan lightly [bestowed it upon him].

He tapped it once; immediately, the light of the heavens shone upon the earth. Yet, when one arrives at the gate of a Zen monk, one must further gouge out one's own eyes before being fit for conversation.
Once, a monk asked Fayan, "Before the hall of the ancient Buddha, who arrives first? Fayan replied, "The one who does not move a step."
Zifu Guang said: "Fayan’s response to the question in this manner leads those whose karmic consciousness is vast and wandering to sit in a place devoid of spirit and certain death.
They imagine that one can achieve realization effortlessly before the Hall of the Ancient Buddha; little do they realize they are merely wasting their brilliance and consuming their years in vain.
Before the Hall of the Ancient Buddha, they will not see a dream for as long as a donkey's lifespan. Nevertheless, it is finished."
When asked, "In the end, who arrives first? he replied to him: "The Ox-Headed Hell-Warden.
Chan Master Hongjin of Qingxi in Xiangzhou (a successor of Qingyuan Weixin and Dizang Cheng) asked Master Xiu:
"If you clearly understand the principle that birth is non-birth, why are you still carried away by birth and death? Xiu said: "A bamboo shoot will inevitably become a bamboo stalk."
"Now, can you still make bamboo strips? Zhenjin replied, "You will realize it for yourself in the future. Xiu said, "My understanding reaches no further than this;
what is your intention, Senior Monk? Zhenjin pointed toward the corridor and said, "That is the Director's quarters;
that is the Head Cook's quarters. Xiu then prostrated himself in thanks.
Baiyan Fu said: "As for Da and Xiao Qingxi, they were the sons of a military family; it was not that they were accustomed to deceiving their subordinates.

It was simply because their wealth could rival that of a state, and they would casually cast away rare treasures here and there as if it were their everyday business—so what is there to be surprised by?
Nevertheless, as for the way Master Xiu performed his prostrations of thanks, tell me: what does this signify?"
To understand it thus, or not to understand it thus—why? It is because there is something else at stake.
Chan Master Longji Shaoshou (Qingba Dizang Chen’s successor) of Fuzhou asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk replied, “From Cuiyan.
Longji asked, “What words or phrases did Cuiyan use to instruct his disciples? The monk said, “He usually says: ‘When you go out the door, you meet Maitreya; when you enter the gate...’”
Upon seeing Śākyamuni, Linji said, "Even if you speak in such a manner, how could it suffice? The monk then asked, "How about you, Master?
Linji replied, "Who do you encounter when you go out the door? What do you see when you enter the gate? At these words, the monk attained realization.
Jianfu Huai said: "I, this mountain monk, am not like that. When one goes out the door, there are the mountains of Wu and the waters of Chu;

when one enters the door, there are the Buddha hall and the corridors. If some monk should emerge and ask, 'What is the meaning of the Master's intent? then I would grant that he possesses a single eye."
Xichan Xu said: "Longji’s head is white and his teeth are yellow, yet he speaks such words. Lan’an, however, is not like this:
'When leaving the gate, the bamboo path has no one to sweep it; when entering the courtyard, the square pond reflects a cold image.'"
Longji ascended the hall and said: "The ordinary person possesses the dharmas of an ordinary person, yet the ordinary person does not know them.
The sage possesses the dharmas of a sage, yet the sage does not understand them. If the sage were to understand, he would be the same as an ordinary person;

if the ordinary person were to know, he would be a sage. These words possess one principle and two meanings. If a person can discern them, there will be no hindrance to finding a point of entry into the Buddha-dharma. If...
"I cannot distinguish it. Do not say you have no doubts; take care.
Huanglong Qing said, "Master Xiu only knows how to spread his nets and set his snares, yet he does not realize he has caught himself within them."
To this day, he has not been able to emerge from his station.
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "It is easy to transform iron into gold and jade; it is difficult to exhort others to abandon their right and wrong.
Tianning Foyin Weiqing said: "Master Xiu finds it difficult to forget what he is familiar with; this is like bamboo shoots sprouting in winter on foreign soil."
Jingci once said: "Even if one has a point of entry, what can it accomplish? An ordinary person remains an ordinary person;
a sage remains a sage. Now tell me, when both the ordinary and the sage are forgotten, how do you speak this one phrase?"
Holding a scroll of scripture, leaning against a pine tree, he stood there. Smiling, he asked the guest, "From where have you come? Yuanwu Keqin said:
"Whether you can discern this or not, you are still a fellow of the weeds. Fuyan Huiyuan said: "Whether you can discern it or not, you are still a fellow of the weeds."
"If you are Longji, you would not dare to criticize this; please take it with you yourself.

Longji offered this verse: "If you wish to know the path of liberation, All phenomena do not reach one another. The eyes and ears are cut off from seeing and hearing, While sounds and forms remain in a vast, tumultuous roar."
Zhaojue Qin said: "Sound does not reach the ear; form does not reach the eye. When sound and form intersect, the myriad dharmas manifest.
Tell me, have you yet trodden upon the path of liberation? If you do not comprehend this meaning, your practice will be nothing but bitter toil."

Longji’s verse says: "When the beginner has not yet entered the Way, one must not allow the mind to be in a state of chaotic clamor. Realize it amidst the tolling of the bell; be overturned amidst the beating of the drum. Tianmu Li said:
"Master Xiu may truly be said to have mastered the five notes and six scales such that their distinct qualities do not interfere with one another. How beautiful!"
How beautiful! Yet, for now, you are buried alive amidst a heap of sounds and dust; even until today, you have been unable to emerge. Why is this?
It is because Xuansha has spoken the ultimate truth.
Longji’s verse says: "Two breakings do not constitute one; the One Dharma remains forever. If a person understands 'one' and 'two'..."
They undergo the cycle of suffering for kalpas.
Zhaojue Qin said: "Master Xiu is like a sky-reaching long sword, its majestic spirit awe-inspiring;

where it is level and smooth, it stands upright like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high; where it stands upright like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, it is level and smooth. Nevertheless, he only says:"
"You have attained half. I, the mountain monk, am not like that: two breakages do not constitute one; even the single dharma does not remain.
