But what is Wushi’s livelihood? He struck his staff and said: 'Swallows chatter and orioles sing in spring.'"
The sun is warm; in these gardens, the hundred flowers are fragrant.
Xuedou ascends the hall: "In the ten directions there are no walls, and on the four sides there are no gates. Where did the ancients look for guests?
If you can utter a line that takes up the hand [of the teaching], I grant you dominion over all under heaven.
Chongxian Qiyun said: "If Xuedou had acted as he did to benefit others in this way, how could he have cut off the tongues of everyone in the world?
Had there been a monk among the assembly at that time who came forward and simply said to him, 'Venerable Sir, you have fallen into error,' [Xuedou would have been truly formidable]."
Not knowing how to wait for his eyes to blink or move, he shook out his sleeves and departed.
Lingfeng Xiangyun said: "I want to ask Xuedou: where would you place this question right now?"
National Teacher Deshao of Mount Tiantai (the successor of Qingzhou Fayen Yi) addressed the assembly: "At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of this world;
outside the mind there is no dharma—before one's eyes are the green mountains. Upon hearing this, Fayen remarked, "This single verse alone is sufficient to revitalize my school."
Jingshan Daowu said: "The reason the Fayan lineage was extinguished is due to this one verse.
Zhaokong Ting said: "Heaven does not cover it; earth does not bear it; there is nowhere to hide the body. The water is green of itself; the mountains are green of themselves.
A single hair obstructs the eye. As for the summit of Tongxuan Peak, which is not of the human world—tell me, what is it?"
"Where is it? A single petal of falling blossom; ten thousand realms return to spring.
Tiantong Wu said: "Xintongxuan does not do so. Today I shall open another path: At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is a different world from the human realm.
It is only because you fail to realize this that you mistakenly identify with the green mountains. He gave a shout and said: "Do you realize it yet?"
"Ma! He then descended from his seat.

Later, a monk asked Tiantai: "Having just left the master’s chamber at Mount Ningfeng and come to sit in this Prajñā practice hall, we ask the Master for a single phrase regarding today’s 'family style' (jiaweng).
Tiantai said, "In what way have you failed me? The monk said, "If that is so, then the thunderous voice resounds."
"Throughout the realm of heaven and earth, there is not a single person who does not receive this grace. Daizhu said, "Fortunately, you have not yet understood; for now, do not poke your head out.
The monk bowed. Daizhu said, "Poking your head out is precisely what will not do."
Huguo Yun said: "The National Teacher’s response was indeed sufficient to reveal the ancestral style of the Buddhas and Patriarchs;
nevertheless, that monk still would not nod his head in approval. If someone were to ask me today, 'Please grant us one phrase regarding the current house style,' I would simply say:
'Tiantai is eighteen thousand feet high; morning and evening, mist and clouds.'"
Seal of the Preface.
Dharma Lamp Taichin, Zen Master of Qingliang in Jinling (a successor in the ninth generation of the Fayan lineage), ascends the hall.

This mountain monk originally intended to dwell in the mountains, concealing his ineptitude and nursing his illness until the end of his days; yet, constrained by the fact that my late teacher has a case of unfinished business, I have come forth to address it.
He brought it to a conclusion. At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "What is the unresolved case of the former master?
Dēng struck him and said, "If the patriarch does not settle it, the calamity falls upon his descendants. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? Dēng said, "The fault lies with me;
the calamity falls upon you."
Cuiyan Zhi said, "To exert one's utmost effort for the sake of the assembly, yet disaster emerges from one's own private door.
Yunfeng Yue said, "This old fellow’s display of bestowing and withholding seems to outshine the past and surpass all that came before;
yet when pressed to the limit, he again proves to be headstrong and tail-weak. Is there anyone here now who can act as the master for Qingliang?"
Zhaojue Qin said: "The Dharma-lamp, though within the realm, wields the power of killing and giving life;

it grasps the sovereign authority beyond the threshold, such that its spirit and resolve startle the multitude and its wind-like standard stands alone. This humble monk’s lowly ambition was originally just like this.
My coming forth today is solely because the Fifth Patriarch has a ready-made public case (*gong'an*) which I shall proclaim before the assembly, without begrudging [my life]."
"Come forth and see if you can offer a greeting regarding the very nature of life and destiny. If not, I shall have no choice but to pick it up and play with it myself.
He gave a shout, struck the whisk, and descended from his seat.
Tiantong Jue said: "If this monk were a true man, he would have come forward and overturned the meditation seat;
not only would he have found a way for himself to emerge, but he would also have spared his ancestors from leaving unfinished business that brings calamity upon their descendants."
Dongchan said: "When a thousand-jin bowstring is drawn, one must think of a fierce battle; when an inch of iron is in hand, one fears only that there may be no foe.
Since this monk did not begrudge coming forth, it would have been well for everyone to set aside their concerns and investigate together.
Instead, you merely smeared him over with such talk. That is why the Qingliang Gong'an remains unresolved to this day."
Yangshan Qin said, "To start a household by leaping over the hearth—Fadeng is indeed a skilled hand.
Yet, alas, he did not understand himself, and his misfortune has reached back to his ancestors. If New Husheng wishes to resolve the public case of his late master, there is someone else present.
Tell me, who is it? He then let out a single sneeze.
Baizhang Xue said: "This mountain monk originally intended to dwell in seclusion among crags and valleys to pass his time nursing his illness.
However, because my late master has a case that remains unresolved, I have come forth today specifically to settle it. If someone were to ask, 'What unresolved case does Yunmen have?
I would simply say to them: 'The stone woman is startled from her frosty night dream; the wooden man..."
A star fell at noon. He was asked again, "Where does it go? He replied: "It is easy to let the clear breeze comb the green bamboos;
it is difficult to make the bright moon stay upon Mount Sumeru."
Gunanmen said: "Fadeng can be called one who guides beings with modesty and brilliance; he bends the inch to straighten the fathom.

I, this mountain monk, am not like that. The entire world has never hidden me. Though I occupy the solitary peak and its summit, I have never been anywhere other than in the depths of the waters and clouds.
And when have I ever lived in seclusion? My Master is currently present, eating and defecating as usual—what public matter is there?"
I cannot fathom this. Since it is thus, why do you cry out again before everyone today?
The ancestral lamp continues its flame with endless brilliance; one simply must catch the scaled fish at the hook.
Longtang Fu said: "When it comes to practicing benevolence, one does not yield; the Lamp of the Dharma is certainly that of a master.

To act with courage upon seeing what is right—this monk, however, has instead acted quite unnecessarily. If you wish to settle the public case of the former Master during this era of peace, it is likewise not so."
After a long silence, he said: "The iron ox has finished grazing on the grass by the fence; its thundering horns cause the spring wind to arise throughout the earth.
One day, a newly arrived monk came to visit Master Hui-ming of Bao-en Temple in Hangzhou (a dharma heir of Qing-jiu Fayen Yi). When the Master asked him, "Where have you recently departed from?
the monk replied, "Chengdu. The Master said, "When you left Chengdu to come to this mountain, did Chengdu decrease?"
"Elder, here there is a surplus of elders; if there is a surplus, then dharmas exist outside the mind. If there is a deficiency, then the dharmas of the mind are incomplete.
If you can explain the principle, then stay; if you do not understand, please leave. The monk had no reply.
Dongshan Ying, acting on behalf of a monk, said: "Even if I were to explain it with perfect logic, it would ultimately not be as good as the Master's.
Chan Master Dongshan Xiaocong of Ruizhou (the true successor of Qingzhou Wenshu Zhen) ascended the hall. He said: "The morning cock announces the dawn; after the gruel, it is already bright.
The lantern-lamp still dozes, while the pillar is wide awake. He added: "If you are wide awake, speak plainly of being wide awake."
"Awake! Clearly, clearly, speak directly. Tomorrow and the day after tomorrow, do not mistake the servant for the master. Take care. Chongxian Qi said: "The assembly, these are excellent words.
If anyone accepts and practices them with faith, I dare guarantee they will receive their prediction of enlightenment in this very life.
Let it be said that thirty years hence, someone will remark: 'Gaoting [Chongxian] mixed mud and water.'"
Baiyan Fu said: "When it is said that the lantern is still drowsy while the pillar is wide awake, he stops there;
this is enough to leave people in doubt. A song of springtime snow is difficult for others to harmonize with. He then added: "To say 'wide awake' is simply to say 'wide awake';
to say 'clearly distinct' is simply to say 'clearly distinct. How can the folk songs of the lowlands ever befit a king?"
Listen. Nevertheless, he cannot say that one recognizes a servant as a lord. Eating and wearing clothes is the servant;
raising the fist and pointing the finger is the servant. But where, after all, is the lord?
Dongshan addressed the assembly: "When the weather is clear, cover the house; when the time comes, harvest the grain. Once the royal tax has been paid, one beats the belly and sings songs.
Jianfu Can said, "Who does not know how to hit a clean ball? Kaixian, however, is not like this: 'When the weather is clear...'"
The clear sky covers the house; seizing the moment, one reaps the grain. Having finished paying the king’s tribute, autumn and winter affairs multiply.
Heh heh heh! When one does not turn their head when called, what can be done?
Zhishan Xuan said: "The family tradition of Dongshan is indeed strict and meticulous; yet, when examined closely, it is a pity that it is too much of a contrived arrangement.
Here at Zhishan, the fields are not plowed and taxes are not paid. A few dilapidated huts are repaired as circumstances allow, and there is no great song to be sung.
Friends, tell me: how does the family tradition of Zhishan compare [to that of Dongshan]?"
How far apart are the lineages of Dongshan?
On New Year’s Eve, Chan Master Zhixian of Beichen in Tanzhou (a successor of Fuyan Ya of Qingzhou) gave a small lecture: "The year is spent and the age is ended;
there is nothing with which to share the year-end feast with you all. This old monk shall roast a white ox from the open field, cook millet rice, and boil—"
[The Master] ate vegetable soup and burned firewood logs. After everyone had eaten, they sang the *murata raku* (village music). "Why?

So as to avoid leaning on others' doors or relying on others' walls, yet being stubbornly called 'Sir' by the people of the age. He then descended from his seat and returned to the Abbot’s quarters (*hōjō*).
Deep into the night, the *vinaya-dhara* (*ninna*) entered the quarters to pay his respects and said, "An official has arrived from the county. The Zen master asked, "To what end?"
Mona said, "The Master says that when he slaughters an ox, he does not take the hide or the horns. Chan then pulled off his head-cloth, threw it to the ground, and Mona picked it up.
Chan descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Thief! Thief! Mona then returned the cloth, saying, "It is cold;
please return this to the Master, Reverend. Chan laughed heartily. As Mona was leaving, Fachang was serving as the attendant. Chan—
Guchu asked Chang, "How would you handle this public case? Chang replied, "Paper is in short supply in Tanzhou;
one statement covers it all. Yangshan Qin said, "He is like skinning a live ox. Beishan is indeed a skilled hand, yet his walls and moats are not secure;
he has been caught red-handed by a salt smuggler. Tianning said, "I am not like that. Tonight..."

There is nothing to look after. The assembly could not help but roast a solitary horned clay ox, cook rice where there was no grain, and sing a song that has no sound, celebrating the New Year with everyone.
Suddenly, a man comes forward and says, "The authorities are seeking the Master's sinews and horns.
He then strikes him with a staff in unison with the sound of his words. Why? Because those who have merit are rewarded.
Baohua Ren said: "Beiquan used official roads for personal favors and put on a hollow display of dignity;
Qinzu withheld the accumulated funds from others and brought you all to ruin together. Lingyou was not like this:
he did not cook the white ox of the open field, so as to avoid having his head bared by the cold winds and freezing earth; nor did he slaughter the one-horned beast."
The clay ox is spared; though the year has reached its end and one might exert oneself by brandishing the staff, even so, how ultimately is the phrase for "celebrating the year" to be resolved?
Thereupon, he dragged his staff and returned directly to the abbot’s quarters.
Baoshou said: "New Yunmen has nothing to offer you all for the year-end feast tonight.
I shall simply boil some wild vegetable soup and cook some millet rice for you brothers to eat. We shall burn logs of firewood and sing a rustic village song.
However, we will not slaughter the white ox of the open field. Why? Because I do not wish to consume the property of the Sangha."

Regarding the phrase "things are private and human feelings are made," Bukkwan’s commentary states: "In this wild mountain, there is no moon at the bottom of a pool to be sliced; there is no cloud atop the ridge to be cut;
there is no mud ox with broken horns to be slaughtered; and there is no white ox in the open field to be boiled."
I only seek fire from within a river of ice, pluck flowers from withered wood, gently play a stringless lute, and vainly blow a holeless flute.
Singing a *Púsàmán*, I shall distribute the New Year’s greetings to you all.
After a long silence, he said: *Lìluó lìlìluóluó lìluóluó lì*.
Chan Master Congyi of Tianting Mountain in Xiangzhou (the ninth generation descendant of Qingxi Jin) stayed at Xiyuan for ten days.
He once said to himself, "Do not speak of 'understanding the Buddha-dharma'; there is not even a single person to be found who can raise a koan. When Xiyuan heard this, he remained silent.
On another day, as [Congyi] was ascending the Dharma hall, Xiyuan called out, "Upādhyāya! Congyi raised his head. Xiyuan said, "Wrong. Congyi took two or three steps forward. Xiyuan—
Yangqi also said, "A mistake. Yangqi stepped forward. The Master said, "Just now there were two mistakes: was it the Senior Monk’s mistake, or was it the old fellow Ximing’s mistake?
Yangqi said, "It was my mistake. The Master said, "Mistake! Mistake! He then said, "Senior Monk, stay here for the summer retreat;
we shall deliberate together on these two mistakes. Yangqi was unwilling and departed immediately. After he had established his own monastery, he would cite this previous conversation every time.
He said, "When I was traveling on foot, I was carried by the winds of karma to Ruizhou. There, the Elder Westyuan examined me and made two consecutive mistakes.
He then kept me for the summer retreat, saying he wished to deliberate with me. I did not say that I was mistaken at such a time."
"When I set out for the south, I already knew I was mistaken.
Shoushan Nian said, "According to Tianping’s understanding, he has not even dreamed of Xiyuan. Why?
Because the story remains."

Zhaojue Qin said: "If people nowadays hear someone say, 'Even before setting foot toward the South, you already knew it was wrong,' they immediately begin to speculate, thinking, 'Before I went on pilgrimage, I certainly did not have all this Buddhist Dharma or Chan Way.
Yet, once they have gone on pilgrimage and been thoroughly deceived by various quarters, they cannot even call the earth what it is."
To call heaven "mountain" and "water" is fortunately no small matter.
If you all proceed in this way with such vulgar interpretations, why not simply buy a piece of cloth for a hat and wear it together? What use would that be?
The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of such logic.
Longxiang Xun, having finished reciting the verse by Xuedou, said: "Regarding this koan, there are many in the monastic community who discuss it, but few who reach a definitive judgment.
Today, Zhongfeng shall judge it for you all: one person is a supervisor who stole from the treasury himself;
another is a seller of stolen goods who released the loot; and the third knows of the theft but does not report it. To each, I grant thirty blows of the staff."
Why is this? If it is done quickly, it is easy to correct;
if it has lasted long, it is difficult to remedy. Yuyan Meng said: "I, this mountain monk, wish to walk hand-in-hand with these two elders.

Xiyuan wishes to become a true bone-and-blood descendant of that house. Observing the winds to know the changes, he does not obscure his source. The seven items follow him at all times—this is the Lion."
Majestic and fierce; possessing both illumination and function, Tianping was truly such a person. Linji’s "claws and fangs" were indeed expected of him.
Who would have known he was a fellow who came to bathe while clutching the bridge pillar?
For those who wish to vindicate Tianping’s grievance, try coming to discuss with me these four errors. Look! Look!
Wuzu Gang said, "Even if one were to use the iron of the nine continents, it would be difficult to forge these two hammers.
Fengshan Qi said, "The old man of Tianping drives in his stake and rows his oars; he wishes to compete for wealth with the Dragon King using fish eyes—this may be called a lack of self-awareness.
If one can freely exchange host and guest and grant or take as they please, not only...
He did not fail the Xiyuan tradition, nor did he carry his "one-sided board" to its ultimate conclusion.
Xidun Chao said: "Many are those who have judged the ancients and the present; they all merely employ their strategic wits like winter maneuvers, each establishing their own camps and fortifications.
Yet they do not recognize that in the military arts of Sun and Wu, there are the positions of host and guest, and the strengths and weaknesses of these forces depend upon oneself."

Listen! I, an old man, now employ the spirit of the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties to sweep away all military formations, seeking only that the sovereign be honored and ministers serve, fathers be stern and sons obedient, so as to manifest the vision of Great Peace. Do you understand?
Do not bring disgrace upon these two great elders by making them blind men!
Baiyan Fu said: "Those two 'mistakes' just now—were they the mistake of the Venerable Elder? Or were they the mistake of Old Man Ximing?
A mistake, a mistake! Had Tianping been able to deliver those two 'mistakes' at that time, one can be certain that Xiuyuan would have ended up looking foolish and desisting."
This avoids the need for much further verbal elaboration hereafter;
otherwise, one would still be subject to scrutiny by others to this day.
*Zongmen Niangu Huiji*, Volume 40; *Zongmen Niangu Huiji*, Volume 41.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Jingfu, Successor of Baiyan Sizhu at Ancient Hangzhou. △ Southern Lineage, Tenth Generation:
Chan Master Chiming Cuiyuan of Shishuang in Tanzhou (Southern Lineage, Tenth Generation; Successor of Fenyang Zhaoyuan). In his quarters, he always kept a sword inserted in the wall.
A basin of water was placed to one side, along with a pair of straw sandals. Whenever a monk came for an audience, he would suddenly say, "Look at the sword!
If the monk hesitated even slightly, he would immediately shout and drive him out.
Tiantong Hua said: "If I had been there at that time and seen him, I would have gone to his left ear and whispered a turning word.
While he was greedily gazing at the heavens, I would have pointed my finger at him; as soon as he hesitated, I would have drawn my sword and struck him down.
Then, suddenly picking up my staff, I would have descended from the seat and driven everyone away at once."
Gao Feng said, "The Great and Small Cimings labored in vain without merit; Xifeng remained unmoving, with neither spear nor banner.
Let the wild ducks be short and the cranes be long—why? Because every year on the ninth day of the ninth month, chrysanthemums fill the earth with fragrance."

Qixia Chengyun said: "Ciming was like Emperor Gaozu singing 'The Great Wind'—if he had been unable to set it aside for even a single day while sleeping or eating, how could he have spent his entire life awaiting the world with weapons?
Why was he so full of fear?"
Daowei Haichun said: "The Elder Ciming’s arrangement of things was very much like constructing a pitfall of snares and traps to ensnare ordinary people.
Here at Daowei, it is not so. When a monk enters the gate, I immediately shout 'Be careful! at the top of my voice.
If his eyes flicker or waver, I strike him out with a succession of blows."
After Ciming and Chief Seat Yong took their leave of Fenyang, they traveled together for twenty years without ever breaking free from one another.
One night, as they sat around a brazier deep into the night, Ciming struck the charcoal with his fire tongs and called out, "Chief Seat Yong!
Chief Seat Yong! Yong gave a shout of "Hah! and said, "Wild fox spirit! Ciming pointed his finger and said, "Surprise! This clumsy fellow has gone off like that again. Yong—
He attained sudden enlightenment upon hearing these words. Gao Feng Miaoshan said: "Ciming has groundlessly cast a pitfall for an ordinary person; he deserves thirty blows of the staff.
Yong the Head Monk was improper in following the wind and shifting his rudder; he too should receive ten blows of the staff in his stead. If there were someone who felt such injustice..."
He stepped forward and said, "Xifeng? He simply replied, "The mind does not betray the person; the face has no shame.
Longchi remarked, "Although Master Yong attained enlightenment, he was nonetheless seen through by the brazier.
Although Ciming possessed the skill to raise the dead and return them to life, he nevertheless did not escape the views of a wild fox. He deserves to be buried in a single pit."
[The question] was buried.
Ciming asked Zhen Dianxiong, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Zhen said, "Cloudless, a peak rises;
with moonlight, it falls into the heart of the waves. Ciming rebuked him, saying, "With hair white and teeth yellow, you still have such a view! Zhen, however—
Wenming asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Ming replied, "Cloudless peaks arise; the moon descends into the heart of the waves.
At these words, Wenming attained great enlightenment.
Zhongfeng Ben said: "To drive away the oxen of the plowman and snatch the food from the hungry man—Master Ciming was not yet a master of his craft.

Although Zhen Dianxiong may have let go over the precipice here and revived after being cut off, if you wish to understand the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma, you must practice for another thirty years before you will attain it."
Cuiyan Zhe said: "Ciming employed the tongs and hammer of the ultimate realm to strike forth the five-colored marrow of the phoenix;
the True Old Man exhaled his breath beneath the words, shattering the bright moon-jewel of the black dragon. Although the teacher and disciple were thus wondrously in harmony,"
The chick pecks and the mother hen pries open the shell at the same moment. Even if you examine this closely, you cannot avoid receiving the staff from Cuiyan’s hand. Why?
Because clouds arise upon the mountain peaks, and the moon descends into the heart of the waves.
Shendǐng Fú said: "Although Címíng understood how to strike a blow from within the nest, how could one blame him for lending the thief a ladder?
Cuìyán’s awakening was indeed not without merit, yet there is a place where he has grievances but no one to cry out to. Why is this so?
Had he known earlier that the lamp is fire, the rice would have been cooked long ago."
Baiyan Fu said: "He is accustomed to knocking at the locks of consciousness and skilled at breaking through the barriers of emotion; he possesses the methods of Liuyang.
Although Master Zhen has attained awakening, Wen Cheng’s realization was merely incidental. As for the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, how could he have even dreamed of it?"
Ciming addressed the assembly: "All sages and worthies are distinguished by means of the unconditioned dharma (*asamskṛta-dharma*).

That mountain in front is the supporting mountain; that one behind is the principal mountain. Which of these is the unconditioned dharma? After a long silence, he said: "The subsequent text is extensive; it shall be entrusted to a future day."
Tiantong Hua said: "Tiantong also wears one eye. All sages and worthies have their distinctions based on the dharma of non-action (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*).
Whether sweeping to the east of Pūrvavideha, to the west of Aparagoyānī, to the south of Jambudvīpa, or to the north of Uttarakuru—going and coming everywhere—it is not as good as being right here."
Tiantong Muan said: "I, this mountain monk, also cast open one eye. All sages and worthies have distinctions based on the dharma of non-action (*anabhisaṃskāra*).
Turning over the body, he kicks down the Jiamen Pass; throughout the great earth, mountains, and rivers, there is not a single inch of soil."
Guangjiao Yuyu said: "If the two great elders, Ciming and Ying'an, had possessed a place for turning over [the body], the Buddha-dharma would not have been reduced to dust by today.
Guangjiao takes a separate path; 'All sages and worthies are distinguished by means of the unconditioned dharma' (Avyākṛta-dharma).
When the cup falls to the ground, the dish shatters into seven pieces. To scold one another is already a concession."
"You take up the words. You spit and say you will spare me; can you still do it? [He strikes the whisk and says:
"If the great ocean were to know contentment, the hundred rivers would flow backward."
In winter, Ciming posted this inscription on the Sangha Hall: [Image of characters] Beneath it, he noted: "If anyone can recognize these, they will not be separate from the four modes of deportment.
When the Head Seat saw this, he remarked, "The Master has canceled today's evening session.
Ciming heard of this and laughed.
Longxiang Yun said: "The assembly all engage in extraordinary deliberations, yet they cannot help but be ridiculed by onlookers.
Longxiang, however, is not like this. 'Ciming was like insects gnawing at wood; the Head Seat happened to form a pattern. From where Kunlun comes, there is not a single drop;
it flows out as the turbid waters of the Yellow River's nine bends.'"
Furong Jue said: "The great and small Ciming pulled out a lacquer basin before even King Bhīṣmagarjita.
The Head Seat followed the heterodox and pursued the evil, immediately fashioning patterns upon his master’s realm of function.
Raising a son who does not equal his father causes a family lineage to decline for a generation. Had I been there at that time, I would have simply said: 'Grass.'"
"Originally, there was no need to bring this up.
Shendeng Yun said: "One person’s talisman behind the elbow is difficult to deceive those who recognize it;
another person’s eye at the crown of the head is correct, yet they have already fallen into the snare. Examining them closely, each has their own errors. Nevertheless, [it is like] Bo Ya and his..."
This is no ordinary acquaintance. Nevertheless, tonight at Tiantong, we cannot let it be in vain.
He raises his staff, draws a circle in the air, and says: "If there is anyone who can leap out of this, I will give them a pair of Yquan cotton trousers this morning."

Dongta Xi said: "Although both the Great and Small Shishuang were excessively compassionate and employed many skillful means, when examined closely, it was still like gouging a sore on healthy flesh."
Ciming asked Chief Seat Xianying, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From Jinkuan. "Where did you spend the summer retreat? "In front of Jinkuan.
"Where did you spend the previous summer retreat? "In front of Jinkuan. "Where did you spend the summer before that?
"In front of Jinkuan. Ciming said, "Why do you not grasp the meaning of my words? Ciming continued, "I am unable to test you; let the servant from the storehouse come forward."
"Examine it! For now, I will serve you a bowl of tea to moisten your mouth.
Yuyan Meng said: "How could Shishuang bear such a one-sided fellow? He can only perform a 'suspended somersault' in mid-air.
Why not give him his rightful fodder and drive him out of the mountain gate, so as to cut off his path for a lifetime?"
He sat facing the Golden Throne.
Zen Master Huijue of Langye in Chuzhou (a successor in the lineage of Nanquan Puyuan and later Fenyang Shanzhao) asked a monk: "I do not ask about brandishing the mallet or raising the whisk."
"What is the matter with blinking and raising the eyebrows? Ya said, "Zhaozhou once met Nanquan. [The monk] said, "I do not yet understand.
Ya said, "This winter there will be much snow and rain; what can a poor family do about it?"
Baoshou said: "Langya’s response to this question may be called the great opening of the treasure storehouse;
yet, alas, he did not meet with one of high discernment, so his achievement was wasted. But were it not for the wild geese arriving last night, how could one see the autumn at the sea gate?"
Layue ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "Panshan said, 'The one path leading upward is slippery.
Nanyuan said, 'Standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high is perilous. Linji said, 'A spark of stone-fire or a flash of lightning is dull. Layue has a phrase that settles heaven and earth."
"Each of you, raise your eyes high! Raise your eyes high! He planted his staff and descended from the seat.
Baeryam Pu said: "These three ancient masters were each splashed with a ladleful of foul water by Langya.
Yet they further claim, 'I have a phrase that settles heaven and earth. Brothers, as for him planting his staff—"
"Descend from your seat. "Is this a phrase that settles heaven and earth, or is it not? After a long silence, he said:
"This ladle of foul water—Langya has poured it over himself."
Langya was once asked by a monk, "The nature is fundamentally pure; how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Langya replied, "The nature is fundamentally pure;
how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? The monk attained realization.
Songyin sighed and said: "Riding the bandit’s horse to pursue the bandit—Dadao and Langya were indeed masters. Yet, they still lacked refinement.
If someone were to ask Longfeng today, 'The nature of reality is fundamentally pure; why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?
he would strike them across the spine with his staff. Tell me, is this the same as or different from Langya? Those with eyes..."
Let the patch-robed monks try to discern this.
Zifu Guang said: "Lanxi Shanhua strikes the prize right from the nest; he does not rely on external strength. Truly, he is a clever son.
Yet, even if it were fundamentally pure and still, one would ultimately never know its ultimate destination."
Chan Master Shouzhi of Dayu in Ruizhou (a successor of Fenyang Shanzhao of the Southern Lineage) addressed the assembly: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it exists;

the black oxen and white cows, however, do know it exists. He then picked up his whisk and said, "The black oxen and white cows are all here, emitting light and shaking the earth. Why is this so? Because there are two distinct parts."
Jingshan Daowu said: "If Dayu had not spoken those final words, he would have surely been deprived of his eyes by that black ox and white cow.
Even so, he still cannot avoid being like a scale-beam dipped in vinegar."
Yuan'an Meng said: "Did Daoyu ever dream of that 'tawny slave' and 'white ox'? Daoyu asked his attendant:
'When you have finished your salutation, you stand to one side—what is the principle behind this? The attendant replied, 'I do not understand.
Daoyu said, 'Stand over here. The attendant then moved over. Daoyu said, 'Pointless, pointless!'"
Tianning Qi said: "Those who complete themselves are few; those who ruin themselves are many. Guangyin Biao said:
"An attendant is indeed difficult to find. How can this be seen? Were it not for the wild geese arriving last night..."
"How can one see the autumn at the gate of the sea?
Daoyu addressed the assembly: "Vertically it exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally it pervades the ten directions. When picked up, even Śakra is startled;
when set down, even the Earth Deity trembles with fear. What do you call it when neither picking up nor setting down? He said himself: "A shrimp."
Lingyan said: "Xiangfu was not like this. Vertically, he exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally, he pervades the ten directions. To pick it up is most simple and easy;
to let it go is to be one with heaven and earth. What is it called when neither picking up nor letting go?
He himself said: "A-che! (A sneeze).
Daiyu was once asked by a monk, "If your entire body is eyes, where is your mouth? Daiyu said, "Three leaps. The monk said, "I do not understand.
Daiyu said, "The seasonal rhyme of the verses has ended; the melody of the song arises toward spring."
Yuanwu Keqin’s *Blue Cliff Record* commentary states: "Even if Dayu truly possessed a torrential eloquence, what could he do? This monk simply lacked eyes.
Dayu addressed the assembly: "We are all gathered here to eat a stalk of leek. If you call it 'a stalk of leek,' you will enter hell as fast as a shooting arrow."
Nengren Jian said: "If you do not call it 'a stalk of leek,' you will enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow. Ultimately, how is it?
If one can simply serve the meal into the bowl of no-mind, someone will naturally come along carrying a broken-legged cauldron."
Lingquan said: "To speak in such a manner is very much like breaking the bones of tofu to remove the vinegar from it. West Mountain, however, does not do so;
everyone shall eat this single stalk of radish together. If you do not call it a single stalk of radish, then what is it?"
"Entering hell is like an arrow flying. Why is this? "Beating a stone man’s head with a staff—this is simply a matter of reality.
Chan Master Quanju of Fahu Monastery in Shuzhou (a successor of Nanquan Puyuan and eventually to Fenyang Shanzhao) arrived at Langya. Langya asked, "Where have you recently departed from?"
Huā said, "The two Zhe regions. [The monk] asked, "By boat or by land? Huā said, "By boat. [The monk] asked, "Where is the boat? Huā said, "At the quay.
[The monk] asked, "How do you express the phrase that does not involve the journey? Huā struck his meditation mat once and said, "Fabricating elders are as numerous as hemp and millet.
He then shook out his sleeves and departed. Lǎ asked an attendant, "What was this?"
"Who is that person? The other replied, "It is Master Ju. Ya said, "Could it be Master Ju, my junior uncle? My late teacher instructed me to seek him out.
He then went down to the guest quarters and asked, "Master, are you not Master Ju, my junior uncle? Please do not take offense for my earlier intrusion. Hua gave a shout.
He then asked, "When did you arrive at Fenyang, Elder? [Ju] replied, "I arrived at such-and-such a time. Hua said:
"I have long heard of your reputation in Zhejiang. It turns out your understanding is merely like this; how could it have spread its fame throughout the world?
Layu then performed a prostration and said, "I, this humble one, am at fault."
Jingshan Gaofeng said: "The guest remains a guest from beginning to end; the host remains a host from beginning to end.
When these two great beings meet suddenly, host and guest are exchanged, directly revealing the heart-essence of Linji.
Were it not for one who has thoroughly realized the ultimate core and possesses the orthodox eye that transcends ordinary sentiment, one could not avoid weighing matters in terms of gain and loss."
Yunmen Xincheng said: "A fist comes and a foot goes—this is the essential tongs and hammer.
If you were to use a broken basket to carry water to extinguish a fire, it would make all bystanders laugh. After thirty years, someone will explain this through."
Dongshan Fu said: "If you, my fellow brothers, can swing a swing upon the tongues of these two venerable masters, only then will you be able to express the Way beyond ordinary circumstances.
Not only will you not be entangled by right and wrong, but you will even perform the Buddha-work through right and wrong themselves. Otherwise, you go to West Qin while I go to East Lu."
Baoshou said, "The hard is as hard as iron; the soft is as soft as cotton.
While it is not that he fails to expound upon the fundamental principles of Linji, when viewed with the correct eye, this too is merely puffing up the air of a meal.
Qinglong said: "The two elders—one guest and one host; one lifting and one restraining—there is no doubt that they reveal the家风 (house style) of Linji.
Yet, alas, it all amounts to nothing more than the Zen of petty folk.
If my Dharma brother were to arrive today, Yunmen, and you asked him whether he came by boat or by land, I suspect he would not say 'I am here.'"
Descending from the riverbank, he simply called for his attendant to fetch water from the Xiye Creek to brew tea on Lufeng Peak.

Once they had finished drinking, they sat with knees pressed together and palms touching, engaging in conversation and polite greetings. Now tell me: was this the circulation of worldly conventions, or was there another Dharma?
After a long silence, he said: "One must know that beyond the distant mist and waves, there is yet another fine matter to deliberate upon."
Yunyan said: "To say that the Elder [Dongshan] 'carries his bamboo staff with him and performs on stage as the occasion arises' is indeed apt.
Nevertheless, were it not for Langye’s singing and clapping in harmony, how could there have been the 'Songs of Spring and Snow'?"
Dongta Xi said: "The words of these two elders carry spears within their speech while concealing their blades within.

Although it is like a game of chess meeting a worthy opponent, even so, it is difficult to deceive those who possess true discernment. As for one man brushing aside his sleeves and another performing a prostration—where does the meaning lie?
Those with the eye of wisdom should surely examine this."
Ziguoxiu said: "Langya possesses the mechanism for trapping tigers; Fahua possesses the maneuver for capturing dragons.
Although both are masters of their craft, Fahua still cannot avoid losing one move by stealth. Let those with clear eyes try to discern this."
Master □□ said: "The dragon and the elephant trample one another; both host and guest are fully present.
From beginning to end, it is clear that both are masters of their craft. Nevertheless, here are thirty blows, which the two shall share equally."

Fahua addressed the assembly: "If Śākyamuni had not appeared in the world and Bodhidharma had not come from the West, the Buddha-dharma would have pervaded the world, yet one’s mouth would remain closed when speaking of the profound mystery.
Jingshan Daoyuan said: "The heart of a thief is naturally apprehensive."
Yuan-an Yu said, "In the *Lotus Sūtra*, the beginning is grand but the end is weak.
Yi-zhi Hai said, "Since it is called 'discussing the profound,' why does he say his mouth does not open?

He then struck the desk with his *nyoi* (ceremonial whisk) and asked, "Do you understand? If you try to hear this with your ears, you will never comprehend it; only when heard through the faculty of sight can it be realized."
This was the beginning.
Chan Master Guquan of Bajiao on Mount Nanyue (a successor of Fenyang Shanzhao of the Southern Lineage) went to Ciming. Ciming asked: "White clouds hang across the valley mouth;
from where does the traveler come? Guquan looked to the left and right and said: "Where was the fire last night that burned out the ancients?"
Fenming said, "Not yet; speak further. Nanquan then made a tiger’s roar. Fenming struck him with his sitting mat, but Nanquan caught it and pushed Fenming onto the meditation seat.
Fenming then made a tiger’s roar in return. Nanquan laughed heartily and said, "I have encountered more than seventy virtuous teachers (śāstrins), but today I have finally met a true master."
Longxiang Yun said: "If one speaks of true adepts, neither of them has yet arrived. Why? One has attained the essence but not its function;
the other has attained the function but not its essence. How can they dare to call themselves descendants of Linji?"

"Virtuous ones, if you can examine this thoroughly, not only will you fulfill the ancient sayings of the past masters, but you will also spare me from being left stranded today without a teacher to transmit the Dharma to me.
He suddenly took up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said: "The eye upon the tip of the staff is as bright as the sun;
if you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire."
Tianning Qisong says: "To apply such terminology is an error. At that time, how could Ciming have tolerated this madman speaking in such a manner?

He would have further struck him with a sitting cloth; see what kind of trickery he would have performed! As soon as his eyes flickered, [Ciming] would have driven him out with a continuous blow of the staff.
Had it been so, the Dharma-lineage of Linji would not have fallen into such desolation."
Yuan'an Yu said: "When these two great elders encounter one another head-on, it is like Ma Fubo deploying his army—whether advancing or retreating, all is wondrous.
It is like Sun Wuzi employing his troops—advancing and retreating with what is appropriate. Like a dragon with wings outspread, like a tiger with horns upon its head;
they are truly unassailable and cannot be approached. Nevertheless, beneath the gate of Linji, this is quite sufficient."
While touring the sights, if they were among those who had manifested the sacred, [Guquan] would strike the left desk and say, "Stand to one side for a moment and watch.
Once, while Guquan and Ciming were walking in the mountains, they encountered a pool of a venomous dragon. Guquan seized Ciming and entered the water together to bathe.

Ciming pulled his arm away and departed. Guquan undressed and leapt in; a thunderclap followed immediately, and a stench-filled wind blew with rain as the trees and forests shook violently. Ciming crouched down.
"Within the grass, Yiquan has died. After a short while, the weather cleared and brightened; Quanshou then raised his head from between the waves and said, "Hmph!
Nanjian asked, "Guquan risked his entire life to test the monks of the world."
Yet he was exposed by the old fellow Ciming. Huangbo Qi said:
"Guquan is a shrimp at the bottom of a well; after many years and months, it has become a spirit and a monster.
How is this any different from a venomous dragon? "Big or small," Ciming pulled his arm and departed. Although he was not deluded by him, [he had still been caught].
It would be better to remain crouching in the grass without showing one's head.
If I were a mountain monk, I would strike him dead with a single blow as soon as he craned his neck, lest he stir up a stinking wind and waves, bewitching the men and women of the household.
Zifu Guang said: "Guquan’s display of bravado would have been nothing more than futile labor had it not been for the corroboration of Ciming.

Chan Master Haotai of Tiansheng Monastery in Anji Prefecture (a successor of Fenyang Shanzhao in the tenth generation of the Linji lineage) arrived at Langya. Langya asked him, "To bury your troops and brandish your weapons is not yet the mark of a master.
If you are a true man, come meet me on horseback with a single spear. Haotai pointed at Langya and said, "The head is already taken—" [The text ends abruptly.]
Meng struck Sanjun; Layi struck Taiyi’s sitting mat. Taiyi also struck Layi’s sitting mat.
Layi caught it and said, "Just now, that one sitting mat was the command of this mountain monk. Where did the Venerable’s sitting mat land?
Taiyi said, "I humbly pray you will continue to enjoy [this offering]. Layi pushed him away and said, "Rising early at the fifth watch, there is yet more night."
The traveler said, "It is like drawing the bow after the bandits have passed. Baoyue said, "Please sit and drink tea.
Bairyam Pu remarked, "When these two elders meet, it may be called meeting a fellow from one's hometown and speaking the dialect of one's hometown.
Nevertheless, while their true character is indeed authentic, if one examines them closely, they cannot avoid being tinged with a touch of formality."
△ Qing Shu, Chan Master Yiqing of Touzi (Qing 10, Successor of Taiyang Xuan). A monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed?
The Master said: "Before the Avīci Eon, a single arrow pierced through two layers of mountains. The monk asked: "What is this?"
Regarding this transmitted matter, Master Zhi said: "It is entirely because the moon over the Huai lands is able to illuminate the spring of Yingyang.

The monk asked, "If that is so, then one has seen the long man upon entering the water. Master Zhi said, "One only knows that gold and jade are different; how can one discern the heart of the King of Chu?
The monk bowed, and Master Zhi struck him with his whisk.
Baoyuan said: "This monk asked in such a manner, and Touzi answered in such a manner. This is discerning the essence within the school and shifting the pivot beyond the measure.
It may be said that the facts are like a box and its lid fitting together, and the principle is like the points of two arrows meeting. Do you understand this yet?
If you are still muddled and superficial, Baoyuan will speak for you. He raised his whisk and said, "Ha! (laughter).

He pierced the golden needle through the broken thread and earnestly entrusted it to his descendants. He then cast down his whisk. Chongxian Qi said: "Opening up new frontiers and clearing away the old, overturning the past and inaugurating a new era—the Elder of Touzi was truly a hero of a generation. But tell me, where does this single arrow fall now? Someone said: [The response follows: "It falls upon the head of the one who dares to speak. Chongxian Qi said: "A thousand people cannot pull it back; ten thousand people cannot push it forward. It is like a great fire burning in the midst of a vast forest—how can you extinguish it? If you can say a word, I will grant you a share of the Dharma. The monk said nothing. Chongxian Qi said: "If you had been able to say a word, you would have been like a dragon leaping from the deep, or a tiger pouncing from the high. But since you could not, you are like a man trying to cross a river on foot, or a bird attempting to fly without wings. You have failed to see the Elder of Touzi’s great function. Do you understand? If you do, I will let you see the Elder of Touzi’s true face. If you do not, you will surely lose your life. He then struck him once with his staff and said: "This is the place where the arrow falls. He attained it. He roamed freely throughout the world.
Because Fenyang Shanzhao had questioned Touzi, [Touzi] said: "The words and phrases of the Patriarchs are like everyday tea and rice.
Apart from these, is there another way to guide others? Fenyang replied: "You say that within the realm, the Son of Heaven—does he still require Yao, Shun, or Yu?"

Tang was not there. Yunrong prepared to offer some words, but the Master struck him across the mouth with his whisk and said, "The moment you first conceived this thought, you already deserved thirty blows.
Yunrong suddenly attained enlightenment; he prostrated and then departed. The Master called out, "Wait a moment, *kalyāṇamitra*! But Yunrong paid no heed.
The Master said, "Have you reached the ground of non-doubt? Yunrong covered his ears and left.
Qixia Chengyun said: "When Fuyong stepped out directly at that time, did it not cause people to harbor doubts?
Yet Touzi gently pulled him back, and he was unwittingly caught in a full exposure. If one can stir up waves and create ripples right here,"
When Jiaoguan Touzi evaded and did not come forward, Chongxian Qi said, "How brilliant!
He is truly like one who breaks through a wall and soars away. These thirty blows have been bestowed upon him with perfect propriety."
Nevertheless, when examined closely, there are still thirty blows remaining.
Chan Master Qingpu of Xingyang in Yingzhou (Qing was a tenth-generation successor of Taiyang Xuan) served as the garden head under Taiyang.
While he was planting melons, Taiyang asked, "When will the sweet melons ripen? Qingpu said, "They have already ripened and rotted right now. Taiyang said, "Pick out the sweet ones."
Yang picked some [fruit] and asked, "Who will eat this? [The monk] said, "One who does not enter the garden. Yang said, "I wonder if even one who does not enter the garden still eats?
He replied, "Do you recognize him? Yang said, "Even though I do not recognize him, I cannot help but give it to him.
Taiyang smiled and departed.
Chongxian Qiyun said: "The melons ripen and the seeds fall away; those who do not enter the garden sit and enjoy the fruit without merit.
For the Sun-father and his son to make such a discernment can be called "that which is sweet is sweet all the way to the core. Alas!
Baiyan Fu’s commentary says: "When will the sweet melon ripen? Why are you scooping up fish and shrimp on level ground?
It has already rotted away. How thick is your skin? Pick out the sweet ones and pluck them; you have plunged deep into the tiger's den—whom will you feed?
You have turned the spearhead back upon yourself. For those who do not enter the garden, the words are split in two.
"Kueh! I do not know whether those who do not enter the garden still eat or not. What a great squeeze!
Do you recognize him? Alas, alas! Although you do not recognize him, you cannot help but grant it to him—what words are these?
He laughed and departed. For now, believe half of it.
A monk asked Xingyang: "When the *Sakṛt* emerges from the sea, heaven and earth tremble; when you present yourself face-to-face, what is the matter?
Xingyang said: "The Golden-Winged Bird King presides over the universe; who among them is one who has emerged? The monk asked:

"What if one suddenly encounters such an emergence? Xingyang said: "It is like a hawk seizing a pigeon; you may not believe it, but you shall know for certain when you are tested before the Imperial Pavilion."
Zhen said, "If that is so, then I shall fold my hands at my chest and retreat three paces.
Yang said, "You turtle under Mount Sumeru, do not wait for me to paint another mark on your forehead."
Baoneng Xiu said: "This monk was like the dragon Lohitaksha when he first competed with Śāriputra over the construction of the Anāthapiṇḍada Garden.
Although the dragon is surely the sovereign among scaly creatures, it could not ultimately avoid becoming food for the Garuḍa."
Huan Ji wrote in a letter: "Master Pifu was unaware that he was dealing with a bandit; he even handed over the Great Axe (the ultimate authority) to him.
This is truly tragic and painful. Chan Master Tianyi Yihuai of Yuezhou (in the Qing edition, a successor of Xuedou Xian) addressed the assembly:

"The hundred limbs all fall apart and scatter, yet one thing remains eternally numinous. When the hundred limbs have scattered and returned to the earth, where does this eternally numinous one abide?"
Nantang Jing said: "A single thing is eternally numinous; where is it situated? The vast sky is wide as clouds disperse across the azure heavens.
Within the lotus palaces and Buddha-fields, flowers are countless—raise your eyebrows for a moment and observe them closely. Tianning Qi said:
"Observing is not non-existent, but what do you call 'a single thing'? He let out a shout.
Nengrenjian said: "When Nantang speaks in this way, he is fit only for the Buddha, not fit for the demons.
As for my own view, I wish for all of you to know it as well; I have also a verse: 'A single thing eternally alive—where can it be placed?'"
Turning around, he tramples through the full orb of the moon; the mountains of knives and trees of swords must be shattered. The molten iron and boiling copper must be drunk dry.
Xiangshan Ji said: "Since the hundred limbs have already disintegrated, what do you call 'one thing'? After a long silence, he said:
Where is this one thing, eternally numinous, securely placed? Within it lies a phrase—allow whom to investigate it? Clouds gathered and mists rolled away, the autumn sky is still;
ten thousand miles of moonlight, a single sphere of jade.
Tianyi showed this to the assembly. An ancient said: "A segment of emptiness atop the mountain of the five aggregates;
entering and exiting through the same gate, yet we do not meet. For immeasurable kalpas we have lived in rented houses, yet in the end we do not recognize our own master.
An old master remarked: "If you do not recognize him, whom did you ask when you first began renting? Such a presentation is far-fetched. Why? It must...
Know that upon the road of the dead lies the place where living people emerge; upon the road of the living, the number of the dead is countless.
Which is the place where living people emerge upon the road of the dead? And which is the road of the dead where the number of the living is countless?
If you can investigate and discern this clearly, you will cast off the cap of dripping grease and strip away the foul-smelling cloth robe.
Jingshan Hongdao said: "The ancient Buddha Tianyi’s [verse] is beautiful indeed, yet it is not yet perfect.
Let the discerning monk try to distinguish it.
Yufan Yuan said: "To differentiate gold from brass and distinguish jade from stone—this is still owed to the ancient Buddha Tianyi; he did not know how to bring it forth."
Even though you have a body, you have not yet escaped making your living inside a ghost cave.

If you can discern this here, it is precisely the right time to don the cap of dripping fat and put on the cloth robe smelling of vulture droppings. Tell me, are you the same as the ancients, or are you different?

The wind is chilling as the willows and poplars change; I see not my old friends coming. At such a time as this, what is it like?
Longing thoughts accompany the falling yellow leaves; White dew dots the gray moss."

On the day of the opening of the hall by Chan Master Xiangjiao Tan of Xuanchou (the eleventh successor in the South, heir to Langya Huijue), the snow-sweeping master (huazhu) Shengzong came forward and asked:
"Before the Buddhas appeared in the world, everyone’s nostrils reached the heavens; why is there not a single trace of news after they appeared?
The Master said: "Before Mount Jizu, the wind is still. Shengzong said: "Not yet—speak further! The Master said: [Silence].
"Great snow fills Chang'an. Zong said, "Who understands this meaning? It makes me remember Nanquan. He shook out his sleeves and returned to the assembly, refusing to prostrate.
Master Jiao said, "The new teaching has lost ground today," and immediately went to his quarters. He ordered an attendant to invite Zong to him.
Jiao said, "Just now I missed a turn of phrase in our exchange. Before the assembly of devas and humans, why did you not [prostrate]?"
As he was about to prostrate, Yaoshan covered him over. Yunmen said, "A great man has gold beneath his knees;

how could he be willing to prostrate before a blind old monk? Yaoshan said, "I have another saying. Yunmen then reasoned through Yaoshan’s previous words until reaching the point where he had said, "Wait until later, and I will tell you more.
Yaoshan said, "I have thirty blows of the staff for you to deliver to Xuedou. Yunmen then prostrated.

Nanjian asked: "If the guest is always the guest from beginning to end, and the host is always the host from beginning to end, then when guest and host suddenly exchange places, one cannot avoid having gain and loss. If you say Xingjiao is the host, how can you account for his being refused by Xuefeng?
If you say Xuefeng is the guest, why did he then strike Xuedou with his staff? Here, distinguish between black and white."
"Clearly! I grant you the eyes that transcend the ordinary. But do you truly understand? Were it not for the wild geese returning at night, how could one perceive the autumn at the sea gate?

Tianjing Xin said, "Although both were masters of their craft, they were nonetheless defeated together. At that time, Zong... (Note: The source text appears to be an excerpt from a *gong'an* (public case) commentary, likely by Tianjing Xin, critiquing a dialogue involving the phrase "autumn at the sea gate.")
When Huazhu performed his prostrations, Xingjiao asked him, "What phrase can you offer to complete the previous statement? Liang said, "Biting at the red edge.
Longtang Zuyun remarked, "Master Huazhu is accustomed to facing great adversaries; though he is a master, what can he do against Tantang?"
With their heads buried in battle and their hair disheveled, they nonetheless devised a strategy for a surprise attack.

Had he been a true man, when the other said, "I have thirty blows to send you to strike Xuedou," he would have replied, "How fortunate that the matter of the Monk’s appearance in the world is now concluded."
Is it not the case that when the head is upright, the tail is also upright?
Guangxiang obtained the sign of verification by saying, "Before the Master of the School, I did not prostrate with my head; later, I prostrated with my head.
Now tell me: is there benefit or harm in this?
Regarding the "Clouds Relying on the Dāna-pāramitā": The auspicious qilin does not tread upon living grass; the great garuḍa is ashamed to roost in a chicken coop.
Although Hanshanzi forgot the path by which he came, one must nonetheless recognize that he possessed the skillful means to act with deliberate contrariness.

Though the phrases concerning Chicken Foot Mountain and Chang’an are like empty flowers or the moon in water, they have shone through antiquity and surged through the present. Yet, even so, I do not pay homage to this lofty wind at Xuedou.
[The Imperial] Gate: I must consider Xingzong to be a giant among men. Yet, as for those thirty blows of the staff—who, after all, received them?
Chan Master Wenyue of Yunfeng on Mount Nanyue (a successor of Dayu Zhi, the eleventh generation of the Southern Lineage) ascended the hall and said: "All of you, in this manner..."
What has come above is much like piercing the brain and thrusting it into a vat of glue; what follows below is likewise stumbling on level ground.
Even if one neither comes nor goes, one shall still receive three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening.
Baoshou said, "Yunfeng was like a mirror placed upon a stand; he could only reflect others but could not reflect himself.
Little did he know that even before one has stepped out of the abbot’s quarters, one has already been 'eaten' (defeated)."
Yunfeng was once asked by a monk, "What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground? Yunfeng said, "It is not obtained from others.
The monk asked, "When it is not obtained from others, what then? Yunfeng said, "Hengyang is not far from here."
Jingshan Daowu said: "Yunmen was not like this. What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground?
It is not obtained from others. When it is not obtained from others, what then? Look beneath your feet."
Longhua Ti said: "Bianshan, moreover, was not like this. What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground?
It is not obtained from others. When it is not obtained from others, what then? When weary, one sleeps; when hungry, one eats."
Jinming Jin said, "The two elders answered the question in such a manner; when have they ever even dreamed of the Dharma-gate of the Mind-ground?
Jinming does not do so. What is the Dharma-gate of the Mind-ground? It is not obtained from others. When it is not obtained from others, what then?
[He would] strike them across the spine with his staff."
Baizhang Jingyun said: "In this matter, it is not so. What is the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground? It is not obtained from others.
When it is not obtained from others, what then? Reaching the river, the land of Wu ends; beyond the bank, the mountains of Yue abound."
△ Qīng 11: Tōkyō Tennei Fuyūdōkai Zenji (Qīng 11; successor of Tōji Qīng). While at Tōji, he served as the head cook (diànzuò).
The Master said, "Managing the kitchen duties is no easy matter. Yunrong replied, "I dare not say so. The Master asked, "Do you cook porridge or steam rice?
Yunrong replied, "The laborers wash the rice and light the fire; the practitioners cook the porridge and steam the rice. The Master asked, "Then what do you do?"
Yong said, "Monk, out of compassion, let him go in peace.
Chongxian Qi said, "He deeply understands and trusts me; he comes and goes without hindrance. Fuyong has attained it.
After thirty years, people will become lax; where will one find such a free-spirited fellow?"
Wenfeng Yuyun said: "Those who hold the tally and devise strategies already have their own ministers; to simply sit upright and act non-action, one must return that to the Sovereign.
In this way, Fuyan responded; it can be said he well captured the essential meaning. However, as for Wenfeng’s position here—
Yet you must still have a separate way of understanding before it will do. Why? "The waves at Caoxi are just like this;
countless ordinary people are submerged."
Furong met with the Layman Yang Jie, the Minister of the Court of Ceremonies. The Layman said, "How many years has it been since we last parted?
Furong replied, "Seven years. The Layman asked, "Have you been studying the Way? Have you been practicing Chan? Furong replied, "I have not been playing that drum and flute.
The Layman said, "If that is so, then you have merely roamed among the mountains and waters, accomplishing nothing at all. Furong said, "It has not been long since we parted; [the Master] is well."
Nenggaodian laughed heartily.
Dongmingji said, "In a place of level ground, there is no hindrance to being solitary and precarious; in a place of solitude and precariousness, there is no hindrance to being level."
Boshan Fenyun said: "Were it not for Master Yang, he could not have perceived the craftsmanship of the lotus;
were it not for the lotus, it could not have withstood Master Yang’s investigation. It is certainly true that gold, when met with fire, reveals its brilliance all the more.
Yet, if one were a master of clear-eyed discernment, both would be difficult to scrutinize. But tell me, where is it that they are so difficult to scrutinize?"
At that point, if a person can discern it, I grant you the eye that transcends all quarters.
One day, while Fuyong was attending Touzi as they were walking through a vegetable garden, Touzi passed his staff to Fuyong. Fuyong took it and followed along.
Touzi said, "It is only right that it should be so. Fuyong replied, "Carrying the Master's shoes and holding his staff for him would not even suffice."
[The Master] said, "There is someone traveling with you. Rong said, "That one person does not accept instruction. [The Master] told him to leave.

When evening came, he asked Rong, "What you said this morning was not yet finished. Rong said, "Please, Master, bring it up. [The Master] said, "Born in the hour of the Rabbit, born in the month of the Dog.
Rong immediately lit a lamp and came forward. [The Master] said, "Your coming up and going down has never been in vain. Rong...
Yang Rong said, "It is only right that he should be by the Master's side. The Master said, "Every household has its servants and maidservants.
Yang Rong said, "The Master is advanced in years; we cannot do without him. The Master said, "To be so devoted? Yang Rong said, "It is my lot to repay your kindness."
Fengxue said with joy: "The bright casts itself into the dark; the jade turns and the pearl returns. Host and guest are in harmony, and there is indeed a profound penetration.
Thus, the exchange of verses at the gate is sufficient to behold the splendor. Yet, if one speaks of the path beyond, it is still not yet there. Why? Have you not seen it said:
'If one does not sit upon the throne of the Empty King over there, how could one be willing to till the fields here below?'"
Riyun. Fuyong was asked by a monk: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does the school follow? Fuyong said: "The golden phoenix perches at night on the shadowless tree;
the mountain peaks have just appeared when the sea clouds hide them."
Tianmu Lü said: "Do you see how the old fellow Fuyong answered so that it penetrates the profound mystery?
Did you not hear it said that Shaoyang once studied under Muzhou?
When a monk asked Fuyong, 'What is the seamless stupa? Fuyong replied, 'White clouds enshroud the mountain peak,' and he never..."
The dew is high and towering.
Fengshan Qiyun said: "To the south of Xiang and north of Tan, the golden scissors have already cut it so it cannot be opened;

amidst white birds and reeds, the jade door pushes it back so it cannot be returned. Although Fuyong’s words were thus, though their needlework and thread were dense and meticulous, they still fall short of the ultimate.
The nose is entirely absent; one must see the seamless stupa, yet this is truly difficult. Why?
On a frosty night when the moon has set and midnight approaches, who can share the cold reflection in the deep pool?
Chan Master Fajian of Mount Jiang in Jinling (Qingxiu 11, Yunju Shunsu). A monk asked, "What was the meaning behind the First Patriarch’s wall-gazing?
Fajian said, "Supporting heaven and propping up earth. The monk asked, "How is it when one proceeds in this very way? Fajian said, "Seven down, eight down.
He asked again, "What was the meaning behind the Second Patriarch standing in the snow with his waist level to it? Fajian said, "Once every three years."
[The Master] asked, "Why did he transmit the Dharma and pass on the robe? Quan said, "Village wine is enough for anyone to buy.
Baiyan Fu said, "There is resonance within Jiangshan’s words; that resonance can be observed.
It is truly fit to be the eyes for devas and humans—a rare encounter in a thousand ages. "If it were in my own place, it would be otherwise: the First Patriarch faced the wall."
What is the meaning? "Sifting for fish and shrimp on level ground. If one goes directly like this, what then? "The waves at Caoxi are just like that;
countless ordinary people sink beneath them. What is the meaning of the Second Patriarch standing in the snow with his waist covered?
"Piercing the brain and entering the glue-pot. Why was the Dharma transmitted and the robe passed on? "If you wish not to invite [retribution]..."
Do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma.
Chan Master Foji Jibei of Hangzhou (successor to Qingliang Yuyang Liaoyuan) was asked by a monk, "What is the Vairocana Seal?
The Master said, "A straw sandal treading through snow. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Every step leaves its trace."
Fengguo Miaoyun said: "Although Master Fomu held high the ancestral seal and did not fail those who came with karmic potential, he did not realize that ancient script is difficult to clarify;
thus, this monk met [the teaching] as if he had not met it at all. If it were Fengguo, it would not be so. Suppose someone were to ask, 'What is the Vairocana Seal?
He would simply say, 'Not a single stroke added to the characters. (The student asked for instruction.)
People do not understand. How could they possibly understand? Tell me, is this the same as Buddha Day, or is it different?
Qinghua Yan said: "Students of the past and present are often blinded by a single pair of straw sandals, failing to see the radiance.
Had they opened a second eye at that moment, they would have been able to see right through the face of Buddha Day."
Gate. Looking back at the Vairocana Seal—what is this but a broken copper coin?
Chan Master Fayan Wuantong Fa-xiu (Succeeding Tianyi Huai; Vol. 40, Day 11) ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk does not know how to speak with artifice;
I simply respond to the occasion. When we call one another to drink a bowl of tea, there is no secret technique of the Patriarchs."
If you practitioners have not yet become intimately acquainted with this, you will find that treading upon a scale-weight is as hard as iron.
Longtang Zhu said, "Baoshou was not like this. This mountain monk is accustomed to skillful speech; every word is timely and appropriate.
There is no need to call for tea or soup—the subtle secret of the patriarchs surpasses them all. If you practitioners can also...
They were well-acquainted with one another. In the great smelting furnace, there is no dull iron.

△ The Twelfth Ancestor of the South, Chan Master Zuxin of Huanglong in Hongzhou (The Twelfth Ancestor of the South, Huanglong, was the successor of Nan). While conversing with Xia Yigong about the *Zhaolun*, [he said:]
When he had reached the state where all things are taken as his own self, and where the sentient and the insentient dwell as one body, there was a dog lying beneath a fragrant table.
Long picked up a ruler and struck the dog; then, striking the fragrant table, he said, "The dog has sentience, so it departs."
"The incense table is insentient and dwells in itself. How can the sentient and the insentient become one body? Gongli was unable to respond.
Long said, "As soon as one engages in discursive thought, it becomes a superfluous dharma. When have you ever realized that all things are oneself?"
Suiyan Yun said: "The old fellow Huanglong was not sparing with his compassion. Xia Gongli entered a mountain of jewels and returned empty-handed.
Do you all wish to understand that the myriad things are oneself, and that the sentient and the insentient are of one body?
Then beat to death the sentient dog and smash the insentient incense table; gather them all up completely!"
"Come! I shall bind you into a single bundle and cast you into the great ocean of the East; there you will naturally be free and at ease.
Nevertheless, you must further know that there is a single aperture at the crown of the head before you can truly attain it. [The Master] raised his staff, struck the incense altar, and said:
Alala! Alala! Climbing the mountain, my feet and knees ache; drinking tea, my tongue is slippery. At the crossroads stands the stone spirit Gandaṅga;
facing the moon and the wind, he blows the *shichaba* flute.
Tiantong Muan said: "To pull out the nails and extract the wedges is not something of which Ruiyan is devoid; yet, alas, he wounds his own edge and offends his hand. How so?
He leaves the 'sentient' dog to guard the night and keeps the 'insentient' incense table for use.
Do you wish to understand how all things are oneself, such that the sentient and the insentient are of one body? For now—"
"Listen, as this staff shall exert its power for you. [He] struck the incense table once.
Longhua Ti said, "Huanglong has gained some small profit; he cannot avoid being laughed at by onlookers.
Shuzhong, though able to settle the case according to the facts, has still not escaped the conceptual trap of Master Zhao. In total, it is not as good as..."
At the time of its establishment, it was indeed somewhat superior.
Master Yun’an Zhenjing Kewen (ninth generation of Huanglong Nan, Southern Lineage) of Baofeng during the Longqing era addressed the assembly:
"Today is the first day of the ninth month; the frosty air is cold tonight. You should know that every path outside the gate leads straight through to Chang’an. *He let out a shout.*
"Ho! Shuigan Un said, "Old Jingning was urinating and defecating upon a clean and pure ground. At that time, where did the entire assembly go?
This mountain monk dares to add his dog's tail to the fox fur, continuing the tradition this morning on the ninth day."
Once a month. The mountain wind blows cold against my face. Beyond a thousand miles, those who understand me; white geese announce my peace and safety.
This is so, yet you have not yet seen a true master. Have you not heard it said: "One who is skilled in speech speaks that which cannot be spoken;
one who is skilled in traces leaves traces that cannot be traced. *He lets out a shout.* As soon as there is right and wrong, confusion arises and the mind is lost.
Baofeng asked Huanglong Nan, "Just now I had an attendant roll up the curtain and questioned him: 'When the curtain is rolled up, what is it like? He replied, 'It illuminates all under heaven.
I asked, 'When the curtain is lowered, what is it like? He replied, 'Not a drop can leak through. I asked, 'What is it like when it is neither rolled up nor lowered?
He was speechless. What would you have done? Baofeng said, "The Master should have taken the attendant's place."
Only after entering the Nirvana Hall did he finally attain it. Longhe said, "People from Guansi truly have no brains. He then looked around at the monks nearby.
Feng, however, pointed at him and said, "Even this monk here has not yet seen it in his dreams. Longhe laughed loudly.
Baiyan Fu said: "When Huanglong Daoqin asked, 'What do you say when there is neither speech nor silence?
if one were a student of the present day, nine out of ten would fall into error at the point where he neither rolls up nor lets go.
Baofeng, however, did not act in this way. Baofeng said: 'Only when the Master takes the place of the attendant and descends to the Nirvana Hall does it finally work.'"
If one were like the teachers of today, they would either resort to coarse verbal abuse or blind blows.
But Huanglong was not like that. Tell me, where does the essential point of this father-and-son relationship lie?
"Face-to-face, seizing the opportunity, swift as thunder and lightning. Yet, even so, he could not avoid the cold eyes of the bystanders.
Baofeng returned from Xiangcheng and visited Huanglong. Huanglong asked, "Where have you come from? Baofeng replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master.
Huanglong said, "It happens that the old monk is not here. Baofeng asked, "Where have you gone?
Huanglong said, "To Tiantai for a communal work session, and to Mount Nanyue to sightsee. Baofeng said, "In that case, this student has attained freedom. Huanglong—
Yangshan asked, "Where did you get those shoes on your feet? Feng said, "I bought them for seven hundred and fifty cash at Mount Lu.
Longtan said, "When have you ever attained mastery? Feng pointed to his shoes and said, "When have they not been mastered? Longtan was struck with awe.
Zifu Guang said: "Huanglong attacks where he is not defended; Baofeng defends where he is not attacked.

War-chariots approach the ramparts; fire-arrows drift through the air. When adversaries meet hand-to-hand, victory or defeat is difficult to decide. A spare boat suddenly calls out, and the response follows the sound.
One boat of the Jingman tribes is seized. Now tell me: on the side of the guest, or on the side of the host?"
At Baofeng, the Master ascended the hall. "In the school of the patch-robed monks, there is nothing that is not a realm of transcendent measure. This is sovereign meditative concentration.
He then let out a shout and said, "Is this not a realm of transcendent measure? He then cleared his throat once and said, "Is this not [sovereign meditative concentration]?"
"In meditative concentration. A-he-he! To offer this profound mind to the lands of dust and atoms—this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.
Yunju Zhuang said, "This reveals the sovereign meditative concentration of a transcendent realm; it truly belongs to the Elder Zhenjing.
Yet, from the perspective of the monastic lineage, there is still a lack of awakening here. Jingshan, however, was not like this; he took up his staff.
Zhuozi said: "Attained within the mind, every matter is unimpeded; manifested through the hands, every dharma is perfectly accomplished.
Leaning on his staff, he said: "He has a path of his own that reaches to the heavens; he does not travel where the Tathāgata has traveled."
Six Verses on the Three Contemplations of the Dharma-realm at Baofeng. The first says: In the non-obstruction of phenomena and phenomena, there is sovereign mastery as one wishes.
Grasping a pig’s head in hand while reciting the pure precepts in the mouth; chasing someone out of a brothel yet not having repaid his wine debt;
at the crossroads, he unties the cloth bag.
“Zhihai Yun, that old fellow Baofeng is truly extraordinary—extraordinarily so! Yet, viewed with cold eyes, he is nothing more than a precept-breaking bhikṣu.
I, however, am not like this. In all matters I am unimpeded; I act as I wish with sovereign ease. I do not concern myself with the number of meals; I am too lazy to even untie my belt when sleeping.
I do not feel anger upon seeing evil, nor do I feel attachment when seeing what is good. This has been my way from the start of my life.”
Do not fabricate strange interpretations, O assembly. Let us consider for a moment: is this the mountain monk’s [view], or is it Bao Feng’s?

Chan Master Hongying of Lengtang in Longqing Prefecture (a successor in the lineage of Huanglong Nan, the twelfth generation of the Southern School) was visited by a monk who, upon rising from his prostrations, pulled down the corner of his *kāṣāya* robe and asked:
"When one has stripped off the clothes and cast aside the armor, what then? Lengtang said: "Fortunately, the smoke of the war drums has ceased."
The bow-tip was hanging on the wall. The monk, however, pulled up his *kāṣāya* and said, "What is it like when one readjusts one's armor?

Dantan said, "Had you not reached the banks of the Wu River, I would have known you were unwilling to rest. The monk then gave a shout. Dantan said, "That startles me! The monk clapped his hands once.

The talent that could have shattered Zhao was originally that of a smuggler of salt.

Thief! and immediately come forth?
