Although Letan was able to deploy a long snake formation, how could he avoid lacking the means to capture the enemy alive? He looked to his left and right and said: [The rest of the passage follows].
Is there anyone here who, disregarding danger and ruin, enters with a single blade directly? If not, look!
This mountain monk shall snatch food from the mouth of a starving tiger. (He brandishes his staff and drives them all away at once.)
Yong, the Abbot of Jicui at Huangbo (the twelfth successor in the Nan lineage of Huanglong), asked the monk Shenqi, "It has been a long time since we last met;
what have you been doing? Shenqi replied, "Recently I saw the Librarian Wei, who has found a place of peace and ease. Yong said, "Try to describe it to me."
Qiji then recounted what he had attained. Yong said, "You are right; Wei is not. Qiji could not fathom this. He returned home and told Wei, who laughed and said, "You are wrong; Yong is not wrong.

"Light and darkness intermingle; the pivot of killing and giving life. This is the realm of the Great Man, the Universal Worthy (Samantabhadra)."
"I know. Born from the same root, yet dying from different roots. The old master in the hermitage is laughing to the point of collapse.
Yangshandeng said, "These three old fellows—there is a needle within the cotton, there is a thorn within the mud.
It is not that rewards and punishments are absent; however, as for the true core of a monk, it is worlds apart. Why? Because it is improper to speak of it."
"This is a false statement," said Bairan Fu. "These three fellows have laid out a brocade pit on level ground.
At first glance, it seems this monk has been clearly and alive-trapped by them. However, when I examine the matter, it turns out they are merely father and son."
The three men were bound with a single strand of rope, which the monk took and cut into strips, threading them all through together.
Chan Master Shouzhen Baoyun Wendeng (Nan 12, successor of Yangqi Hui) ascended the hall and said:

"If you can truly achieve a moment of breaking into a sweat, then even upon a single blade of grass you will manifest jade palaces and crystal halls. If you have not yet truly achieved a moment of breaking into a sweat..."
Sweat breaks out. Though there be towers of jade and palaces of crystal, they are nonetheless covered over by a single blade of grass.
How can one get this sweat out? Naturally, there is a pair of hands from the depths of poverty that have never lightly performed the *San-tai* dance.
Jingshan Hongzhi said: "A jade tower and a crystal palace manifest upon a single blade of grass—this can certainly be believed.
Yet that jade tower and crystal palace are themselves covered by the single blade of grass; do not let him deceive you with his heat.
Jingshan speaks thus for those who have already broken out in a sweat once; as for those who have not yet broken out in a sweat once, you must by all means not move."
Zhuo. Fu Longchang said: "A good spiritual friend is a great cause and condition. To untangle the sticky and remove the bonds is merely commonplace;
to snatch away the food and drive the plow requires a nimble hand. Baiyun draws a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt—how could it be for the sake of a mere field mouse?"
The rat triggers the mechanism; Great Wisdom lowers the hook across the four seas, solely to catch the fierce dragon upon the line.
But tell me, what is to be done here within ignorance? Since there is already a pair of hands that have exhausted all means, it is no trouble at all to perform the Three Terraces Dance.
Tianning Qisong said: "If you set aside even a single blade of grass, where would the jade towers and crystal palaces be?
When the land of Wu ends at the river, on the opposite bank, the mountains of Yue abound."
Xiaoyan Bao said: "Baoyun and Dahui were both skilled at suppressing and elevating; they were certainly not without merit for their time.
Yet, alas, the stench of sweat still lingers, hitting one right in the nose.

If one does not know that a single blade of grass is entirely a palace of jade and crystal, what can be said of "correct" or "incorrect"?
The palace of jade and crystal is precisely this single blade of grass; what more would you have to manifest?
Even if Fengshan were to deploy another stratagem and bring forth his extraordinary talent, when it is all calculated to its conclusion, he would only achieve half. Why? Because—only...
One sees the sharpness of the awl’s point, yet one does not see the squareness of the chisel’s head. Do you still know where the new elder has fallen?
Fortunately, he is a guest from the south bank of Lake Wu; together we shall take his hand and step out through the Cloud Tower.
Zifu Guang said: "Jade towers and crystal palaces have been covered over by a single blade of grass; this has occurred throughout antiquity and the present.
If one were to manifest jade towers and crystal palaces upon a single blade of grass, I fear that the white clouds would merely be repeating empty words.
Why? Have you not seen it said: 'When the branches are too large, they will surely break; when the tail is too large, it cannot be wagged'?"
Furiji said: "At Long’an, it is not like this. There is no need for you all to break a sweat;
simply eat when hungry and sleep when tired."
Baizhang Baoyun ascended the hall and said: "The ancients left behind a word or a half-phrase; when one has not yet penetrated it, it is as if one has run into an iron wall.
Suddenly, one day, if one sees through it, one will finally know that this very self was originally the iron wall.
Now, how do you penetrate it? He added: "Iron wall! Iron wall!"
Shilin then said, "Baiyun has seen through the iron wall and lost one eye.
Fulong let out a roar and said, "What is the use of an iron wall?"

The kalpa-vase is empty. The youth said, "When birth accords with the father, the entire body is without a trace of illumination. [The Master] asked, "If the principle is thus, what of the phenomena?
The youth said, "As each distinct instance returns to its source and differentiates into phenomena, how could the responsive function throughout the ten directions be any hindrance?"
[The Master] said, "If that is so, then every speck of dust manifests the original body. Tong said, "To transcend all forms and surpass all thoughts.

[The Master] asked, "And what about 'in accordance with principle and in accordance with phenomena'? Tong said, "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; take it home in a bottomless basket.
[The Master] said, "Entering the marketplace, one can let out a long啸 (shout/sigh); returning home, one puts on a short shirt. Tong... [continued].
It is said: "The wooden man sings atop the ridge; the stone woman dances by the stream.
Chongxian Qiyun remarked, "This monk has long been a traveler and has not yet returned home; he still yearns for the scenery of his old garden.
The Elder of Tiantong did not begrudge his grandmotherly kindness, exhausting the clouds and mountains in his discourse for him. Yet, if one is unable to step out from within oneself...
What difference is there between this and the sorrows and joys within a dream? Nevertheless, even so, one cannot deceive Gaotingsan.

Bayanfu said: "The question lies where the answer is; the answer lies where the question is. To encounter it in such a manner requires more than merely passing through winding alleys and winding corridors;
it is impossible for anyone who has not come through this path to insert a word of their own. It cannot be known otherwise.
However, if one examines this closely, it is either entirely correct or entirely incorrect. Why?
Because within the armory of our King, there is no such sword.
A monk asked Tiantong, "What is one who has gone forth? Tiantong said, "The white clouds have vanished into the ravines;
the green peaks lean high against the void. The monk asked, "What is one who has returned? Tiantong said, "With a head full of white hair, he leaves the mountain valleys;
at midnight, he pierces the clouds to enter the marketplace. The monk asked, "What is one who neither goes nor comes? Tiantong said:
The stone woman calls back the dream of the three realms; the wooden man sits and cuts off the mechanism of the six gates.
Qinghuayan said: "The Patriarch’s realization was truly such that the pivot of the Way was dense and subtle, and the realm of wisdom was profound and deep.
In his casual dealings with people, his sincere heart was revealed piece by piece, reaching the ultimate depths of mystery. Now, I, his unworthy descendant, also wish to level [the ground]."
Dividing wind and moon, adding mud upon earth. When asked, "What is the person who goes forth?"—opening one's eyes, one does not perceive the dawn.
What is the person who returns?—at midday, striking the third watch. What is the person who neither goes nor comes?—even before the Nameless One (Viyūna), there is no abiding;
how could one respond to the mechanisms of both extremes? Now tell me, how is this compared to Tiantong?
"How far apart are they? Try to examine this closely.
Master Fajian of Zhiyi in Wuzhou (Qing 13; successor of Changlu Xian) ascended the hall and said: "To strike the profound pivot, one must possess integrity and be utterly resolute.
Only a man who can cut through nails and sever iron—a person of stark, unyielding resolve—will succeed. If..."

These are but mediocre fellows, fearful of the blade and evading the arrow; they have a share in this only by looking. [The Master] struck the meditation seat with his whisk and descended from the seat.
Tianning Qi said: "The great and small Zhi exhausted his own mind to break the other's mouth into laughter. Longshou.
The mountain has nothing particularly extraordinary about it: in the morning one washes one’s face with warm water, and at dusk one removes one’s socks to sleep.
The great ocean allows the fish to leap; the vast sky permits the birds to fly.
Yingshan Yun said: "Zhizhe and Tianning—one is as tight as an iron箍 (band), the other is as wide as a leather bag.
While it is certainly true that each saw only one side, what about those currently in all quarters?
How can they begin to produce a distinct path apart from these two elders? After a long silence, he said: "Cutting off both sides, one does not stand in the middle."
"Returning him to one who oversteps the bounds of human emotion.
Qinglong Cao said, "Water is dripping from his own mouth; if he requires others to cut him off, it will likely be difficult.
(From *Zongmen Niangu Huyi*, Volume 43)
*Collection of Anecdotes from the Zen School*, Volume Forty-Four.
Compiled by the monk Jingfu, Dharma Heir of Baiyan at Ancient Hangzhou.
Section Fourteen: Nan.
Chan Master Yuantong Daomin of Jiangzhou (Southern Lineage, fourteenth generation, successor of Letan Qian) once visited while Fan Chong, the Vice President of the Left (style name:

Zhixu), was serving as Governor of Yuzhang. After the tea had been served, [Fan] said, "I am approaching old age; having fallen among those in purple and gold robes, I have drifted somewhat far from this matter.
Daomin called out, "Director of the Imperial Library! [Fan] responded, "Yes? Daomin said, "How could there be any distance?"
The official sprang up and said, "I beg you, Master, to grant me further instruction. Yunmen said, "From here to Hongdu, it is four stages away.

The official stood there reflecting. Yunmen said, "If you see it, you see it immediately; if you deliberate upon it, you have already missed it. At these words, the official suddenly attained realization.
Yingshan Yun said: "The Elder of Yuan Tong has a wondrous medicine within his bag that can raise the dead and restore life in an instant.
Although the Left Vice-Minister has gained insight into this and is not far from realizing it, alas, his native accent is still easily recognized and his homeland remains obscure."
Chan Master Foguo Keqin of Zhaojue Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture (the successor of the fourteenth and fifteenth Southern Patriarchs, Yuan), ascended the hall and said:
"Utterly without dependence, transcending all schools and categories; neither thing nor mind, standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. An arrow is shot at a mulberry tree;
sap flows from a willow tree."
"New clouds in the sky. Even if you were to respond in such a way, it would still only account for half of it. But tell me, which half is that?
Not having truly understood the matter, one calls a bell a jar.
Zhaojue addressed the assembly: "The whole body is eyes, yet they cannot see; the whole body is ears, yet they cannot hear; the whole body is a mouth, yet it cannot speak;
the whole body is a mind, yet it cannot discern. Setting aside for a moment the idea that 'the whole body' is so, suppose there were no eyes—how would one see?
No ears—how would one hear? No mouth—how would one speak? No mind—"
"How do you discern it? If you can find a single thread of the path here, you will then be a fellow student with the ancient Buddhas.
But tell me, whom are you studying?
Jingshan Daowei said: "What a pity that I was not there at that time. Had I been there, I would have lit a torch to illuminate it."

"How thick is the skin on that old fellow's face? [The Master said: "Right now, might there not be someone who cannot bear this from the sidelines coming forward and saying, 'The Master is also a man from Puzhou'? What then? To him, I would say:
'In the Western Heaven they cut off heads and arms; here, you must go out and experience it yourself.'"
Zhaojue addressed the assembly: "An ancient worthy said, 'It has already been eleven days since the summer retreat began;
what about Hanshan? Another said, 'It has already been eleven days since the summer retreat began; what about the water buffalo? I, this mountain monk, am not like that:
it has already been eleven days since the summer retreat began; what about the lanterns and the pillar? If you can recognize the lanterns and the pillar, then..."
If you recognize the water-buffalo, you will recognize Hanshan. Jingshan Xiu said:
"O Assembly, to shatter the golden phoenix-head and extract the five-colored marrow is surely the handiwork of those three great elders.
But for me, the new Lingyan, there are no such matters at all. Why? Before the door of every house..."
Brilliant as the sun and moon! In the Great Peace, there is no need for the majesty of a general.
The Inscription on White Rock says: "I wish to ask Zhaojue: how does Hanshanzi recognize [reality]?
If his eyes flicker or move, he would immediately overturn the meditation seat.
Chan Master Fuyan Qingyuan of Longmen in Shu State (the fifteenth patriarch of the Southern Lineage, successor to Nanquan) was one day unwell.
A monk asked, "When birth and death arrive, what then? Yüan said, "Mount Huankong. The monk asked, "Is it only this, or is there something else?
Yüan said, "Tongcheng County. A monk reported this to Chief Seat Li, who said, "Brother Yüan, I have not seen you for some time."
"Thirty years"—this refers to Han Che. The Record of Jianfu says:
"He paid respects to the Head Seat, who was a fellow student of his late master. It is a pity that he died trapped beneath the words."
Baiyan Fu said: "In the palace of the Sea Dragon King, there are no ordinary things. Foyan’s response was indeed enough to startle the multitude;
yet, alas, because the connoisseur was not the right person, it resulted in a failure to penetrate the meaning. Had I been the Head Seat, I would not have spoken thus.
But how would you have spoken? Brother Yuan, we have not seen each other for thirty years, and yet you still act in such a manner!"
[This is a] view. Have you even seen a dream?
Zen Master Qing Su of Jiuzheng (who was the successor of the fourteenth and fifteenth patriarchs of the South, Yuan) once had the Governor Lü visit to behold the Great Image.
The Governor asked, "Since this is the Great Image, why does it carry such large pillars on its shoulders? Su replied, "There are no day laborers on board the ship."
Shou then performed a prostration.
Zhaojue Qin said, "I feared I had killed everyone under heaven.
Jianfu Xing said, "I thought there was no one [to match me]," and he also said, "Originally, I had surplus strength."
Daguo Bie said: "To carry it on one's entire body.

Regarding the question posed by the head monk Yuánlǐ (who was the successor of the fourteenth and fifteenth patriarchs of the South): A monk asked, "The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* says to 'cultivate all wholesome dharmas.
What are wholesome dharmas? Yúnlǐ suddenly rose and said, "Above is heaven; below is earth; what sits in between—sitting or standing?"
As he was about to strike, [the monk] stepped back. [The Master] called out, "What do you call 'wholesome dharmas'?
The assembly had no reply. He prostrated and struck him. Jianfu Xingyun said: "O Great Assembly! The Way has no crosswise path; when principle is right, one acts immediately.
I dare say that the nose of the Head Seat fell into the hands of this monk. If anyone can examine this through and through, they may roam freely throughout the world."
The Elder Fahu (the fourteenth and fifteenth patriarchs in the South, successor to Yan) arrived at Donglin under the guidance of [Zhao]du.

Seeing that Du had attained the essence of the "even and real" (pingshi), one day he took up a branch of flowers, circumambulated Du’s meditation seat once, and with his back turned, inserted it into the incense burner, saying:
"Preceptor, tell me: what is your meaning? Although Duan offered his responses several times, none were in accord with the truth.
After two months had passed, he finally asked Huichu, "Try explaining it for me. Huichu replied, "I simply take flowers and insert them into the incense burner."
The Master himself wondered what was on his mind.
Nanjian asked the Master, "Tell me, where does your intention lie? The Master said, "This wild fox spirit!
Had I been Donglin at that time, I would have struck him across the back with my staff and driven him out, so as to avoid this mutual wasting of effort."
At this, the Upādhyāya himself began to doubt what was happening and sighed twice, saying:

"From ancient times until now, everyone has said that Master Chueh drives the oxen of the plowmen and snatches the food from the hungry; he can both seize and release, and can both kill and bring to life."
If I, this mountain monk, were to examine the matter, even someone like this would merely be a "dragon-headed and snake-tailed" fellow;
he has not yet attained self-salvation.
Píngtián said: "In a house where there is no *Báizé* talisman, such a monster will surely not appear."
Whenever a monk arrived, Yu Daopo of Jinling (Nan 14, Langlangqi Sisi) would say, "Child, child. If the monk hesitated, she would immediately shut the door.
Fodeng Xun went to test her; when she saw him, she questioned him as before. Fodeng said, "Where is your father?
Daopo turned around and bowed to a pillar. Fodeng then kicked it over and said, "I took you for someone of great distinction, but there is nothing particularly extraordinary about you."
He then went out. The old woman rose up and called out, "Child, child! Come here; I cherish this lamp for you!
But he paid her no heed. Bairyak Fu said: "The numinous tortoise bearing the diagram brought about its own death; the old woman was indeed pitiable.

Although He Shan held the iron tally in his grasp and could effectively sweep away the smoke of the barbarians, he only knew how to strike with brilliance, but did not understand [the underlying principle]."
A covert attack. Those with eyes—how would they distinguish this as a hand reaching out from a mountain?
△ Qing 14: Chan Master Hai of Yuelu, Tanzhou (a successor of Kaixian of Qing 14). Because a monk asked: "When taking three steps forward..."
"What? Jueluo said, "Bumping one's head and knocking one's forehead. "When you step back three paces, what then? Jueluo said, "Falling into a pit or a ditch.
"When you neither advance nor retreat, what then? Jueluo said, "A man dead standing on his feet."
Baiyan Fu said: "Master Hai knows only the severity of frost and the intensity of summer heat; he does not understand the warmth of the sun and the spring breeze.
Here it is not so. What is it like when you take three steps forward? A full cup of golden flowers. What is it like when you take three steps back?
Returning in glory with a purple edict. What is it like when you neither advance nor retreat? The Immortal Elder asks after your welfare."
Reluctantly turning his head, the Son of Heaven called out, but he would not board the boat.
Chan Master Zongjue of Tiantong in Mingzhou (Qing 14, successor of Changlu): A monk asked, "What is the Way?
Tiantong said, "At the crossroads, do not let your head be cut off."
Yingshan Yun said: "The old fellow Tiantong, when at Dangyang, pointed out the broad, eight-lane highway where everyone can tread;
he was certainly called a master for this. Yet, even so, it was not yet the痛快 (pángtài—thoroughly exhilarating/penetrating) realization of a monk.
If someone were to ask me, 'What is the Way?', I would immediately give them a slap across the face and say: 'Who told you to run through the weeds?'"
Go out! Chan Master Wuweijun Jixiang Yuanshi (Qing 14; successor of Tianyi Cong) went to visit Tianyi. One day, he happened to laugh loudly and disturb the assembly, whereupon Tianyi expelled him.
During the middle of the night, while staying in a field, he beheld the stars and moon shining brilliantly and attained realization. He returned and presented his understanding.
When Yunyan saw Baofu’s robe, he asked, "How do you explain the Five Ranks of Lord and臣 (Minister) of Dongshan?
Baofu Xiang replied, "In my place, there is not even a single rank. Yunyan then ordered him to attend the hall and said to his attendant monk, "This fellow actually possesses a point of view."
"How can it be that he does not recognize the fundamental principle? As Xiang entered the room, he had five attendants stand in a formal line beforehand.
Upon Xiang’s arrival, they all called out, "Venerable Shishang. Thereupon, Xiang secretly grasped the profound essence and composed this verse:

"The single rank is just revealed, yet the five ranks are divided; Ruler and minister are in harmony, and purple clouds gather. The night-bright curtain is rolled up, shining without partiality; The golden..."
The Hall, with its layered tiers, manifests supreme dignity;
the robes are well-suited to the occasion. His merit is as vast as the clouds. Yet, because he has not yet penetrated the ultimate barrier of the celestial robe, the Great Dharma remains unclarified.
This was merely the result of his momentary compassionate heart (*poxin*); it is something that even a master hand or a clever mind finds difficult to describe. Were it not for this auspiciousness...
It is not easy to comprehend through spiritual resonance. Yet, was there truly such a thing under the patriarchs?
Or was there truly no such thing? Jixiang said, "Once a single rank is revealed, the five ranks are distinguished. I would like to ask him:
setting aside those five ranks for a moment, from where does this very 'one rank' come?
△ South Fifteen:
Chan Master Dahui Zonggao of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou (South Fifteen: Successor of Zhaojue Qinquan). Following the descent from the seat on the day of opening the hall.
Deputy Minister Feng Gongjie asked, "Master, you often say that one should not act like such a creature; why then have you failed today?
The Master said, "The entire earth is this Venerable Gaofeng. How do you see it? Feng hesitated.
Mount Sanbian held up his palm.
Tiantong Muan said: "Feng Jichuan may indeed be said to have a method for wielding the adze; yet, alas, he has no success in carving the plaster.
If it were this mountain monk, the entire world would be this Venerable Gaoyao—how would you see it? He simply said: [The text ends here.]
"If that is so, then the entire world has been occupied by you, Master. Wait for him to move or act, and then shout immediately;
would this not add luster to your official status? Nevertheless, one must also raise up Dahui.
Suppose someone were to ask me, a mountain monk, on this very day—what would I say to him? 'Clouds parting reveal the moon in every house; spring arrives everywhere.'"
Huā. Bairyánfú said: "When Minister Fēng sought a tall person amidst the vast, surging waves, he was like a vessel of but a peck or a bushel, accustomed to searching for others' shortcomings.
Yet how could he have known that Mìoxǐ is a golden-winged garuḍa soaring to the heavens?"
Not only did he fail to become entangled in its nets and fetters, but he was even able to seize the dragon directly and swallow it.
Nevertheless, upon closer inspection, it still lacks a certain pivotal mechanism. Today, when asked about New Baoshou, [the Master] said:
"The Master always says that one does not act like such a creature; why then are you here? He replied: "Today, Upāli (Fuzhang) Upāsaka’s life is at stake."
"It is in your hands.
When Jing-shan was first serving as the head of the assembly at Yun-ju, Yuan-wu ordered him to hold the whisk for a small lecture (*xiaocan*).

Zhao-jue Yuan stepped forward and asked, "When the sword is suspended from the brow, what then? Jing-shan replied, "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven. From behind his seat, Yuan-wu shouted in approval: "Excellent!"
"Stop, stop! Your question is excellent; your answer is even more extraordinary. Yuan then returned to the assembly, and from this, his fame as "Mount Yuan" (Yuanshan) arose.
Longxiang Yin said: "How marvelous, how marvelous! The vital spirit of these seventeen hundred virtuous teachers (kalyāṇamitra) remains vivid and imposing.
Who would have known that two hundred years later, within the city of Jinling, we would encounter another such master, like the sinews of a lion?"
When a single string of the lute is plucked, all the other strings snap; it is like a drum smeared with poison, where all who hear its strike perish.
You, members of this assembly, should attend upon me and serve me without weariness or fatigue. Each of you shall, according to your own faculties, become a perfected vessel of the Dharma.
Nevertheless, there are clouds and billows reaching to the heavens that can accommodate fish as large as boats; there are [the depths] of ninety thousand li...
Such is the wind of his character. One might indeed bear wings that reach the heavens;
yet Dongmingji says: "Though Old Man Yuanwu had the karmic connection of being a foster son, how can he avoid the laughter of bystanders?"
Daciben said: "It is indeed extraordinary, yet how can one help but feel that a parent’s affection blinds them to their child's flaws?
Observe this father and son in their single bout of dharma-battle; how does it compare to seeing a true master on a hundred-fold battlefield?
If you can discern the truth here, I grant you the power to turn yourself around upon the edge of a sword. If not, you will inevitably suffer a wound."
A blunder. "Tut! Jingshan asked a monk, "The Way does not require cultivation; it only requires that you do not defile it. What is this undefiled Way? The monk said, "I do not dare speak of it.
Jingshan said, "Why do you not dare speak of it? The monk replied, "For fear of defiling it. Jingshan raised his voice.
He shouted, "Attendant, bring the dustpan and broom! The monk was bewildered, and the Master struck him out. Bayan Fu said:
"Let us set aside for a moment the fact that this monk was at the point of completing a nine-cubit mountain, yet lacked the final basket of earth;
but as for Dahui speaking in such a manner—has he truly escaped being in the wrong? If I were in his place..."
The monk waited for the Way; what is this "unstained" Way? He simply took a basin of water, placed it before Miaoxi, and departed.
Jingshan asked the monk, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. How do you understand this? The monk said:
Xuefeng said, "I lead you to your seven generations of ancestors in your own home. The monk then shouted. Xuefeng said, "Just now I led you;
now you shout. Is this not his mind? Is it not the Buddha? Is it not a thing? What is it? The monk hesitated, and Xuefeng struck him out.
Suīyán Yùn said: "The Elder Dàhuì held fast to this one pivotal point;

even if one were to take the vast void as a mouth and Mount Sumeru as a tongue, it would still be difficult to fathom the scope of its application. Nevertheless, when examined closely, it cannot be said that there is no gain or loss.
Had that monk been a person of true caliber at that time, upon seeing him ask such a question, he would have simply—"
Turning toward the Way, one passes through the Iron Ring Mountains at the third watch; how could this not be "illuminating what precedes and severing what follows"? Striking the whisk, he says:
"The bamboo staff has transformed into a dragon and departed; the deluded person continues to bail out the night pond."
Jingshan said to Zishao, "You only know the principle of 'investigating things' (*gewu*), but you do not know 'things being investigated' (*wuge*.
Zishao then asked, "What is 'things being investigated'? Jingshan replied, "Have you not heard the story of Emperor Ming of Tang beheading the Governor of Lang?

Zishao attained realization thereupon and said, "Zishao investigates things; Miaoxi has things investigated. If you wish to recognize the 'one thread' (*yiguan*), it is simply two five-hundred [coins]."

Baoshou Fang said: "Although Miaoxi Zishao’s discourse was as lively as the wind and rarely encountered throughout the ages, he only knew how to copy a gourd by following the original pattern. Here it is not so. If someone were to ask, 'What is the realization of things?
I would say to him: 'This jade ruyi [scepter] was sent by Minister Tao. Do you understand? The red sun—[one]"
The night outside the wheel-mountain ends at dawn; fools all gaze into the mist. (A shout. Guangxiang Daoyun said:
"Stirring the boiling water in the cauldron is not as good as removing the firewood from the hearth. Only those with true discernment can do this;
the Elder Miaoxi was certainly one such hand. Zishao immediately knew his way home—how clever he was!
Examining this closely, it is much like a shrimp leaping but unable to get out of its basket.
Jingshan asked a monk, "How do you understand the story of Xiangyan climbing the tree? The monk replied, "It is like singing a *zhègū* [partridge] song in the spring breeze.
Jingshan said, "The Venerable Houtou said: 'I do not ask about being on the tree; tell me a phrase for being under the tree.'"
"Come forward. [The monk] asked, "And how about this? The monk said, "I have already told the Master just now. Dongsan said, "It is like singing a *zhègū* (partridge) song in the spring breeze;
is it a cry from atop the tree or from beneath the tree? As the monk was about to respond, Dongsan struck him.
Dazhu said: "What a pity this monk is—dragon-headed but snake-tailed. To delight in singing the *zhègū* [partridge] song in the spring breeze is merely 'tree-top talk' and 'tree-bottom talk.
It would have been enough simply to say, 'If you doubt, seek another teacher. I dare guarantee that at Mount Jing, the ice will melt and the tiles will crumble."
Chan Master Shouxun Foding of Heshan in Anji Prefecture (the fifteenth in the lineage of Taiping Qinqing, South) had already attained realization upon meeting Fojian.
That evening, he called out to the assembly with a stern voice, "Tonight, Senior Monk Xun will sleep soundly.
When Yuanwu heard this, he suspected it was not yet the case and wished to test him. He summoned him to his presence and, while wandering the mountains together, they happened to arrive at—
There was a pond of water. Wuzhuo then pushed his lamp into the water and suddenly asked, "When Niutou had not yet met the Fourth Patriarch, what was it like?
Dazhen replied, "The pond is deep and the fish gather. Wuzhuo asked, "After he had seen him, what was it like? Dazhen replied, "The tree is high and it beckons the wind.
Wuzhuo asked, "What is it like when one has seen and when one has not yet seen? Dazhen replied, "Stretching out the feet is within drawing them back. Wuzhuo then praised him.
Nantang Yu said: "Which mountain could possibly avoid being 'dragging water and trailing mud'?

Yuanwu’s heights are indeed high, yet how can he help it that he still employs the mind and puts his actions into practice? Nevertheless, without entering the startling waves, it is difficult to encounter the fish that satisfies one's heart."
Baiyan Fu said: "If one does not probe water with a staff, one will not know its depth; if one does not test gold with fire, one will not know its authenticity.

Since Mount He has already been tested and probed by Zhaojue, were it seen by a great master of the Dharma, he would surely spit out his food in laughter. Why? Because they are born from the same root. (The text ends here.)
"Why are you frying so urgently?

The lay practitioner Wu Juhou (a native of Nan'an, successor to Yuan Tong Min), who held the rank of Shumi (Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs), returned to Zhongling with his official insignia.

He went to visit Yuan Tong, saying: "Some time ago, when I was traveling to the provincial examinations, I passed through here. Crossing the Zhaozhou Barrier, I once questioned the former abbot, Elder Ne, regarding the matter of 'passing through.'"
"Regarding that matter of 'passing through the barrier,' what is it like? Nan said, "For now, go and serve as an official. Today, more than fifty years have passed unawares.
Tong asked, "Have you clearly understood the matter of passing through the barrier? Gong replied, "I have passed through it eight times;
I have always maintained this mindfulness, yet I have not yet reached a state of complete liberation. Tong handed him a fan and said, "Please use this fan. Gong immediately waved the fan. Tong said:
There was a point where he felt he had not yet attained liberation. Master Tong suddenly had an awakening and said, "I request one more final word.
As Tong waved his fan twice, the Master said, "Intimate! Intimate! Tong replied, "Ji-liao’s tongue reaches three thousand miles."
Yingshan Yun said: "If Yuantong had not spoken his later words, he would have been left stranded.
Master Wu merely flits about his spirit at the place where the fan was waved; what end can there be to this? As for saying, 'Ji lifts his tongue three thousand miles'—"
What is the intended meaning?
The lay practitioner (upāsaka) Shangshu Mo Jiang, courtesy name Shaohu (also known as Nan-shi-wu-da-sui-jing-si), was from Fengning in Hongzhou and served as an official in Western Shu.

He went to visit Nantang to inquire about resolving the essential point of his practice. Nantang instructed him to maintain mindfulness toward the "good place," but for a long time he made no progress.
Once, while rushing to the toilet, he was overcome by an urgent and foul odor; as he covered his nose with his hand, he suddenly attained thorough realization.

Seeing that Nantang had acted as his spiritual guide, he presented his understanding in a verse, saying: "From the beginning, my natural grace has always loved elegance; I have often laughed at those of this age who seek outwardly. Ten thousand..."
Separated by a thousand differences, there is no place to seek it; once attained, it has always been at the tip of the nose. [The Master] stamps his seal upon the hall.
Yingshan Yun said: "Although the Minister has reached this point through diligent effort, if one examines him closely, he still carries a trace of foul odor.
Why? Because he fell down right at the head of a latrine."

△ Chan Master Jiantang of Guoqing Temple in Taizhou, the Sixteenth Successor of the South (the successor of Hugu of the South), while presiding at Rishang Hall of Yuantong Temple in Jiangzhou, ascended the hall and addressed the assembly.
Yuantong does not open a pharmacy for the living; he sells nothing but the heads of dead cats.
Who knows which one lacks the wit to realize that, upon eating it, cold sweat flows down their entire body?
Panshan said, "In this place of Panshan, we neither open a pharmacy for life-giving medicines nor sell dead cats' heads.
We simply take a single unperforated flute and, facing the wind, blow it until the autumn of the Chu River is severed."
△ Southern Lineage 18:
Chan Master Songyuan Chongyue of Lingyin, Hangzhou (Southern Lineage 18; successor of Tiantong Jie). Addressing the assembly at the time of his death:
